overview: The work of billionaire tech CEO Donovan Chalmers is so valuable that he hires mercenaries to protect it, and a terrorist group kidnaps his daughter just to get it.
tagline: Take on a madman. Save the world.
title: Hard Kill
plot:
Hard Kill is a 2020 American action thriller film directed by Darin Moore and written by Darin Moore and Michael J. Martin. The movie stars Steven Seagal, John Dutton, and Krista Allen.

The main themes of Hard Kill include:

1. **Vigilantism**: The film explores the theme of vigilantism, where a former Marine (played by Steven Seagal) takes the law into his own hands to avenge his family's murder. This theme is central to the plot and raises questions about the morality of taking the law into one's own hands.

2. **Revenge**: Revenge is another dominant theme in Hard Kill. The protagonist, Colt (played by Steven Seagal), seeks revenge against those responsible for his family's death, which drives the plot forward and shapes the character's actions throughout the film.

3. **Family and Loyalty**: The movie highlights the importance of family and loyalty. Colt's motivation to avenge his family is rooted in his love and loyalty to them, which serves as a driving force behind his actions.

4. **Corruption and Injustice**: Hard Kill also touches on themes of corruption and injustice within law enforcement agencies. The film portrays a corrupt system that fails to protect its citizens, leading Colt to take matters into his own hands.

5. **Redemption**: Throughout the movie, Colt's character undergoes a transformation from a grieving father to a vengeful avenger. His journey towards redemption is a key aspect of the story, as he seeks to make amends for past mistakes and find closure.

Overall, Hard Kill explores complex themes that drive the plot forward and shape the characters' actions. The film's action-packed sequences and intense fight choreography add to its appeal, making it an entertaining watch for fans of the action-thriller genre.

overview: Carl Fredricksen spent his entire life dreaming of exploring the globe and experiencing life to its fullest. But at age 78, life seems to have passed him by, until a twist of fate (and a persistent 8-year old Wilderness Explorer named Russell) gives him a new lease on life.
title: Up
plot:
Up is a heartwarming animated adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and directed by Pete Docter. Released in 2009, the movie follows the story of Carl Fredricksen, an elderly widower who sets out to fulfill his lifelong dream of exploring South America.

The film begins with Carl (voiced by Edward Asner) living a mundane life in Paradise Falls, Peru, where he has lived for over 50 years. He is still grieving the loss of his wife, Ellie, who passed away five years ago. The two had shared a deep love for adventure and exploration, but their dreams were put on hold due to financial constraints.

As Carl's health begins to decline, he decides that it's time to fulfill his lifelong dream of exploring South America by tying thousands of balloons to his house and taking off into the sky. Unbeknownst to Carl, a young Wilderness Explorer named Russell (voiced by Jordan Nagai) is on his porch, trying to earn his final badge by assisting the elderly.

As the house soars into the air, Carl and Russell form an unlikely friendship, bonding over their shared love of adventure and exploration. Along the way, they encounter a series of obstacles, including treacherous storms, treacherous terrain, and a group of ruthless loggers who are determined to destroy Paradise Falls.

Throughout their journey, Carl and Russell learn valuable lessons about life, loss, and the importance of following your dreams. They also discover that Ellie's spirit is still with them, guiding them on their adventure.

As they near their destination, Carl and Russell face a final challenge: navigating the treacherous terrain of South America to reach Paradise Falls. In a thrilling climax, they successfully land in the falls, where Carl finally finds closure and a sense of fulfillment.

The film ends with Carl and Russell standing together, looking out at the breathtaking beauty of Paradise Falls. Carl has found a new sense of purpose and meaning in life, thanks to his adventure with Russell. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, as Carl and Ellie's love story is finally brought full circle.

Overall, Up is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, loss, and the power of following your dreams. With stunning animation, lovable characters, and a heartwarming story, it's no wonder that Up became one of Pixar's most beloved films.

overview: David, a robotic boy—the first of his kind programmed to love—is adopted as a test case by a Cybertronics employee and his wife. Though he gradually becomes their child, a series of unexpected circumstances make this life impossible for David. Without final acceptance by humans or machines, David embarks on a journey to discover where he truly belongs, uncovering a world in which the line between robot and machine is both vast and profoundly thin.
tagline: David is 11 years old. He weighs 60 pounds. He is 4 feet, 6 inches tall. He has brown hair. His love is real. But he is not.
title: A.I. Artificial Intelligence
plot: Steven Spielberg’s A.I. Artificial Intelligence, based on a concept by Stanley Kubrick, is a futuristic fairy tale that explores the emotional and existential consequences of artificial intelligence. Set in a distant future where climate change has drastically altered Earth and rising seas have submerged major cities, society relies heavily on humanoid robots known as Mechas.The story centers on David, a childlike robot played by Haley Joel Osment. David is a prototype created by the company Cybertronics. Unlike other robots, he is programmed to feel genuine, unconditional love. He is adopted by a couple, Monica and Henry Swinton, whose real son, Martin, is in cryogenic suspension due to illness. Monica activates David's emotional imprinting protocol, and he begins to love her as his true mother.When Martin unexpectedly recovers and returns home, tensions develop between him and David. After a series of incidents that put Martin in danger, the family views David as a threat. Monica, unable to return or deactivate David due to his emotional bond, abandons him in the woods rather than have him destroyed. This betrayal marks the beginning of David’s journey — a quest to become real, so Monica will love him again.David teams up with Gigolo Joe, a robot designed for adult companionship played by Jude Law. Together they navigate a world hostile to robots. They escape a violent event called the Flesh Fair, where obsolete robots are destroyed for entertainment, and search for the legendary Blue Fairy from the story of Pinocchio, whom David believes can turn him into a real boy.David eventually finds his creator, Professor Hobby, in the flooded ruins of Manhattan. However, he learns that he is not unique; many Davids have been made. Heartbroken but still determined, David continues his quest and ends up trapped underwater in front of a statue of the Blue Fairy. He remains there, silently praying to be made real, until his power runs out.Thousands of years later, advanced non-human AIs — evolved descendants of Mechas — resurrect David in a future where humanity is extinct. Using DNA from a lock of Monica’s hair, they recreate her for one final day. David spends that perfect day with her, finally experiencing the love he always longed for. At the end of the day, Monica dies, and David peacefully shuts down beside her.

overview: Chef who dreams of having own food trucks, agrees to pose as girlfriend of an attorney. Working together, they try to prove he's the ideal candidate to take over the family firm, but is complicated as real sparks begin to fly.
title: A Christmas Proposal
plot:
A Christmas Proposal is a 2021 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Martin Wood and produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America and Brad Krevoy Television for CBS. It stars Jessica Camacho as Maria Winters and Adam Rodriguez as Julian Diaz, with Luisa d'Oliveira as Maria's best friend Brooklyn, Bianca Caroca, Andres Soto, Claudia Ferri, Juan Chioran, Jaime M. Callica, Serge Houde, Shawn Hook, Malaika Jackson and Frank Crudele. Rodriguez, who also worked on the script to make the Latino family it portrays more authentic, described it as one of the first network Christmas films centred on an American family of Latin descent.

Maria is a struggling personal chef in Seattle who dreams of owning her own line of food trucks and drives for a ride-share app between cooking jobs. On her way to a singles Christmas party she picks up Julian, a wealthy, ambitious and rather cold attorney who pays her to drive him about 100 miles outside the city, where he plans to spend Christmas impressing his powerful father in the hope of being named his successor at the family law firm when he retires on Christmas Eve. Julian fears the job will instead go to his brother Bennett, who has a wife and children and seems more settled. When his parents meet Maria, they assume she is the surprise girlfriend Julian has hinted at, and he decides to run with the misunderstanding, while Maria agrees in return for an investment in her food truck. To keep their story straight without technically lying, the pair go on a crammed "power date" so they can describe their relationship truthfully. Maria cooks the family Christmas dinner, asks everyone to put their phones away at the table, and gradually draws the distracted Diaz family closer, but the business arrangement is complicated as real feelings develop between her and Julian, culminating at a Christmas Eve gala for children in need.

The film premiered on CBS on 12 December 2021. Brett White of Decider recommended it, presenting it as a revival of the major-network TV movie and praising its sleek, high-budget look, the lavish Diaz house, the chemistry between Camacho and Rodriguez and d'Oliveira's comic turn as the wisecracking best friend, and arguing that its inventive touches made an extremely familiar fake-relationship premise feel fresh.

original_title: The Monster at the End of This Story
overview: The Monster at the End of This Story is Sesame Street special on HBO Max.
title: The Monster at the End of This Story
plot:
The Monster at the End of This Story is a 2020 American animated musical television special produced by Sesame Workshop and directed by Mark Taylor, which premiered on the streaming service HBO Max on 29 October 2020. Running about half an hour and rated TV-Y, it adapts Sesame Street's best-selling 1971 picture book The Monster at the End of This Book, in which Grover discovers that a monster awaits him at the end of the book he is starring in. The Sesame Street puppeteers provide the voices of the animated characters, with Eric Jacobson, Ryan Dillon, Leslie Carrara-Rudolph, David Rudman and Carmen Osbahr in the cast and Stephanie D'Abruzzo voicing Grover's Mommy.

Grover learns that there will be a monster at the end of the story he is in, and, filled with dread, he tries everything he can to avoid meeting it. As in the book, he breaks the fourth wall, pleading with the viewer to stop watching and attempting to block the story's progress, for example by building a brick wall or tying up the screen with string. To fill out the longer format, he is joined by Elmo and by his friends Cookie Monster, Rosita and Abby Cadabby, who take his fear seriously while sharing their own experiences, such as Cookie Monster overcoming his fear of broccoli. Grover sings with Elmo about what fear feels like in the body, and Rosita, Cookie Monster and Abby sing about how courage helps you try new things, offering simple techniques such as taking a deep breath and telling yourself that you can do it. Grover also gets hold of a magical rewind control and travels back before the story began, revisiting moments in his own past when he overcame his fears, such as learning to ride a bicycle without training wheels with the support of his mother. Encouraged by his friends, he finally reaches the end of the story and, true to the book's twist, discovers that the monster was Grover himself all along, a revelation he celebrates with a musical number.

Reviews were mixed. Ashley Moulton of Common Sense Media named it a Common Sense Selection, finding that it exceeded expectations and praising its timely lessons about fear and courage. Matthew Soberman of ToughPigs called it a lovely, creative special with meta humor and an emotional core, though he was conflicted about the move from puppetry to animation. Nathan Rabin of Fatherly argued that the added friends, songs and time travel padded the story and diluted the lonely, existential power of the original book.

overview: The Invincible Iron Man and the Incredible Hulk must join forces to save the Earth from its greatest threat yet! When two Hydra scientists try to supercharge a Stark Arc Reactor with Hulk's Gamma Energy, they unleash a being of pure electricity called Zzzax - and he's hungry for destruction. Together, Iron Man and Hulk are the only force that stands in the way of the Zzzax's planetary blackout. But first, the super heroic duo will have to get through snarling Wendigos, deadly robots and the scaly powerhouse, Abomination.  Can two of Marvel's mightiest heroes find a way to work together without smashing each other before time runs out?
tagline: Iron Man and the Hulk team up in groundbreaking Marvel CG Animation.
title: Iron Man & Hulk: Heroes United
plot:
Iron Man & Hulk: Heroes United is an animated superhero film that explores the complex relationship between Tony Stark/Iron Man and Bruce Banner/Hulk, two iconic characters from the Marvel universe. The movie delves into the themes of friendship, sacrifice, and the blurred lines between heroism and villainy.

At its core, the film is a poignant exploration of the emotional toll that being a superhero takes on individuals. Both Tony Stark and Bruce Banner struggle with their own personal demons, which often lead to destructive outbursts. The movie highlights the difficulties of balancing one's ego with the need for selflessness and responsibility.

The story also touches upon the theme of redemption, as both characters grapple with past mistakes and seek a way to make amends. Tony Stark's character, in particular, is driven by a desire to prove himself as a hero and earn the respect of those around him. Meanwhile, Bruce Banner's struggles with his alter ego serve as a reminder that even the most well-intentioned individuals can be consumed by their darker impulses.

Furthermore, the film explores the idea of what it means to be a true hero. Is it about having incredible powers or abilities? Or is it about making sacrifices and putting the needs of others before one's own? The movie raises these questions through the characters' interactions and relationships, ultimately suggesting that true heroism lies in finding a balance between personal ambition and selflessness.

Overall, Iron Man & Hulk: Heroes United is a thought-provoking animated film that offers a nuanced exploration of complex themes and character dynamics.

overview: Edmond Dantés's life and plans to marry the beautiful Mercedes are shattered when his best friend, Fernand, deceives him. After spending 13 miserable years in prison, Dantés escapes with the help of a fellow inmate and plots his revenge, cleverly insinuating himself into the French nobility.
tagline: Prepare for adventure. Count on revenge.
title: The Count of Monte Cristo
plot:
The Count of Monte Cristo is a 2002 adventure drama film directed by Kevin Reynolds, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and based on the novel of the same name by Alexandre Dumas. The movie stars Jim Caviezel as Edmond Dantès, Richard Harris as Abbé Faria, Michael Wincott as Fernand Mondego, Guy Pearce as Villefort, Dagmara Domińczyk as Mercédès, and Henry Cavill as Albert de Morcerf.

The film begins in 1815, where we meet Edmond Dantès (Jim Caviezel), a young and successful sailor who is about to be promoted to captain. However, his life takes a dramatic turn when he is falsely accused of treason by his so-called friends, Fernand Mondego (Michael Wincott) and Villefort (Guy Pearce). The accusations are fueled by the jealousy of Mondego, who had been in love with Mercédès (Dagmara Domińczyk), Dantès' fiancée.

After being imprisoned for many years, Dantès befriends Abbé Faria (Richard Harris), a wise and kind priest who helps him escape. Faria teaches Dantès the secrets of wealth and power, which he uses to create a new identity for himself as the wealthy and mysterious Count of Monte Cristo.

As the Count, Dantès sets out to exact revenge on those who wronged him, using his newfound wealth and power to manipulate and deceive them. He becomes a master of disguise and deception, using his intelligence and cunning to outwit his enemies.

Meanwhile, Mondego and Villefort are struggling with their own personal demons, as they become increasingly entangled in the Count's web of deceit. Mercédès is torn between her love for Dantès and her loyalty to her husband, Albert de Morcerf (Henry Cavill), who is unaware of his father's true identity.

As the story unfolds, the Count's plan becomes more complex, involving a series of clever disguises, double-crosses, and betrayals. In the end, the Count's revenge is finally exacted, but at a great personal cost to himself.

The film ends with the Count's fate unknown, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of his identity and the consequences of his actions. The final shot of the film shows the Count standing alone on a cliff, looking out at the sea, as the sound of waves crashing in the background creates a sense of melancholy and introspection.

Overall, the 2002 adaptation of The Count of Monte Cristo is a thrilling and engaging tale of revenge, betrayal, and redemption. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and stunning visuals, it's a must-see for fans of adventure dramas.

overview: Canadian folk artist Maud Lewis falls in love with a fishmonger while working for him as a live-in housekeeper.
tagline: Triumph epitomizes adversity
title: Maudie
plot:
Maudie is a 2016 Canadian biographical drama film directed by Aneil Karsana and written by Ben Kettles. The movie tells the story of Maud Lewis, a talented but struggling artist who finds love and inspiration in her life.

The main theme of Maudie revolves around the struggle for artistic expression and independence. Maud's journey is marked by her perseverance in the face of adversity, as she navigates the challenges of being a single mother and an artist in a male-dominated world. Despite facing numerous setbacks, including poverty, illness, and personal loss, Maud finds solace in her art, which becomes her voice and her escape.

The film also explores themes of love, acceptance, and the power of human connection. Maud's relationship with her husband, Everett, is portrayed as a source of comfort and support, allowing her to pursue her artistic dreams. The movie highlights the importance of finding one's true partner in life, someone who understands and encourages your passions.

Furthermore, Maudie touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Maud navigates her life, she grapples with her own sense of purpose and belonging. Her art becomes a means to express herself and find her place in the world, allowing her to transcend her circumstances and create something beautiful from adversity.

Overall, Maudie is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the power of art, love, and human connection to overcome even the most daunting challenges.

overview: An ex-marine enforcer must battle his conscience and code of honor when he is forced to do things for the mob.
tagline: Live by a code. Die by a bullet.
title: White Elephant
plot:
White Elephant is a 2022 American action crime thriller directed by Jesse V. Johnson, who wrote the screenplay with Erik Martinez from his own story. Michael Rooker stars as Gabriel Tancredi, with Bruce Willis as Arnold Solomon, Olga Kurylenko as Vanessa Flynn and John Malkovich as the lawyer Glen Follett, alongside Vadhir Derbez, Michael Rose, Lauren Buglioli and Louie Ski Carr. It was produced by Corey Large through 308 Enterprises and BondIt Media Capital, with music by Sean Murray and cinematography by Jonathan Hall.

Gabriel is a widowed former Marine who has spent years as an enforcer for his friend, the mob boss Arnold Solomon, and is now mentoring a brash young protégé, Carlos Garcia (Derbez). Still mourning his wife, a wildlife activist, and regularly visiting her resting place, he dreams of leaving the life behind and using his skills to protect elephants in Africa, as she always wanted. When Solomon orders a hit on a Mexican gangster, Carlos botches the job and blows up a building, and the attack is witnessed by two police officers, Vanessa Flynn and her partner Walter Koschek (Rose). To protect himself, Solomon orders Gabriel to eliminate both witnesses.

Koschek is quickly killed, but Vanessa, an ex-soldier haunted by the violence she has seen on the job, proves far harder to catch, evading one kill squad after another. As Solomon's increasingly reckless decisions trigger more bloodshed and rival gangs move in, Gabriel finds himself drawn to Vanessa, discovering that she shares a birthday with his late wife. Torn between loyalty and his own code of honor, he decides for the first time in years to do the right thing, turning against Solomon to protect her. The conflict culminates at Gabriel's country house, where he and Vanessa fight off the remaining gunmen of Solomon's organization.

Filmed in Georgia beginning in April 2021, White Elephant is one of the last films Willis made before retiring from acting due to illness; crew members later described him as confused on set, and Johnson said he would not work with him again under such circumstances. The film was released in select US theaters by RLJE Films and on AMC+ on 3 June 2022. Reviews were mostly negative, with critics calling the script thin and repetitive, though Rooker's warm, commanding performance and the violent finale drew praise.

overview: Cancer-terminal tycoon Peter Murdoch's secret Wexel Hall Pharmaceuticals lab has developed a blood orchid extract cure. To examine why it works optimally in snakes, they also bread a super-anaconda strain. But the original pair escapes, leaving a bloody trail of corpses. Murdoch runs, instructing his staff to clean up. They keep failing and being eaten like unsuspecting locals, some alive, even after enlisting ruthless big game hunter Hammett. The fast-growing pregnant monster sheds its skin, thus disabling the only tracking device.
tagline: They Can Taste Your Fear
title: Anaconda 3: Offspring
plot:
Anaconda 3: Offspring is a 2008 adventure horror television film directed by Don E. FauntLeRoy, the third installment in the Anaconda series and a sequel to Anacondas: The Hunt for the Blood Orchid (2004). It stars David Hasselhoff as the hunter Stephen Hammett, Crystal Allen as Dr. Amanda Hayes and John Rhys-Davies as the industrialist Peter "J.D." Murdoch. Shot in Romania back-to-back with its sequel, Anacondas: Trail of Blood (2009), it premiered on Sci Fi on July 26, 2008.

After Hammett's team captures an anaconda in the Amazon, the snake is taken to a genetic research facility in Romania, where Professor Eric Kane is developing a serum from the Blood Orchid. The project, led by Amanda and funded by Murdoch, has caused the snake to grow to an enormous size. When Murdoch provokes it during a visit, the anaconda breaks out of its enclosure, killing a scientist and many lab workers, freeing a queen anaconda and devouring Kane. Murdoch calls in Hammett to recapture both snakes, and his team, joined by Amanda and Murdoch's assistant Pinkus, sets out into the countryside, where a farmer has already been eaten.

In the first confrontation, the snake kills two hunters, Grozny and Dragosh, with its razor-sharp tail and jaws. Hammett arrives and lectures the team on how to kill it. During another attack, the snake spits acidic venom at Victor, causing a crash, and devours Sofia, before Hammett rescues Amanda. Amanda then admits that the queen is pregnant and will give birth to genetically enhanced offspring within 24 hours, but Hammett refuses to involve the military and threatens her with prison for her part in creating the creatures. After Pinkus is killed, Amanda and the hunter Nick track the snakes into an old factory to plant explosives, and Nick kills the male anaconda and himself with a grenade. When Hammett and the last hunter, Andrei, arrive, Hammett kills Andrei and reveals that he is working for Murdoch, who wants a live baby snake. As the queen gives birth, Amanda wounds Hammett, sets the timer and escapes; the explosion kills Hammett, the queen and her brood. Afterward, Murdoch's man Peter Reysner retrieves one surviving baby snake for Murdoch, while Amanda burns her research notes.

Like many made-for-television sequels, the film received poor reviews, criticized for its weak connection to the earlier films, poor acting and lack of special effects.

overview: A wooden puppet embarks on a thrilling adventure to become a real boy.
tagline: The timeless classic.
title: Pinocchio
plot:
Pinocchio is a 2022 American musical fantasy film directed by Robert Zemeckis, who wrote it with Chris Weitz, a live-action remake of Walt Disney's 1940 animated film based on the 1883 book The Adventures of Pinocchio. Tom Hanks stars as Geppetto, with Cynthia Erivo, Giuseppe Battiston and Luke Evans, and the voices of Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Pinocchio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Jiminy Cricket, Keegan-Michael Key as Honest John and Lorraine Bracco.

In a small Italian village in the 19th century, the wandering cricket Jiminy enters the home of Geppetto, a widowed woodcarver who has just finished a puppet modeled on his late son, which he names Pinocchio. Geppetto wishes on a star, and that night the puppet comes to life. The Blue Fairy tells Pinocchio that if he proves himself brave, truthful and unselfish he can become a real boy, and appoints Jiminy as his conscience. Overjoyed, Geppetto sends Pinocchio to school, but the con-artist fox Honest John and his cat Gideon lure him toward fame on the stage, intending to sell him to the puppet master Stromboli. Thrown out of school for being a puppet, Pinocchio goes to Stromboli's theater, where he befriends the puppeteer Fabiana, but Stromboli locks him in a cage. He escapes with Jiminy's help, using lies that make his nose grow, only to be carried off by the Coachman to Pleasure Island, where children are encouraged to misbehave.

There, Pinocchio befriends the unruly Lampwick but discovers that the children are turned into donkeys and sold to the salt mines. Sprouting donkey ears and a tail, he escapes with Jiminy and returns home to find that Geppetto has sold his clocks to buy a boat and search for him. Fabiana, who has taken over the puppet show after Stromboli's arrest, invites Pinocchio to join her, but he chooses to rescue his father, and his donkey features disappear. Guided by a seagull named Sofia, he finds Geppetto at sea just before both are swallowed by the sea monster Monstro. Pinocchio lights a fire to make the monster sneeze them out, but in the escape Geppetto seems to die, until Pinocchio's tear revives him. Geppetto tells him that he is already a real boy at heart.

Initially planned for theaters, the film was moved to Disney+ because of the COVID-19 pandemic and released on September 8, 2022, for Disney+ Day. It received negative reviews, with 27% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and is regarded as among the weakest of Disney's live-action remakes.

overview: When Hilda wakes up in the body of a troll, she must use her wits and courage to get back home, become human again — and save the city of Trolberg.
title: Hilda and the Mountain King
plot:
Hilda and the Mountain King, marketed as Hilda: The Mountain King, is a 2021 animated fantasy adventure directed by Andy Coyle and written by Luke Pearson. It adapts Pearson's graphic novel of the same name and continues the season-two finale of the animated series Hilda. Bella Ramsey, Ameerah Falzon-Ojo, Oliver Nelson and Daisy Haggard lead the voice cast. It was produced by Silvergate Media and Mercury Filmworks.

At the end of the series' second season, a changeling spell has swapped Hilda with Baba, a young troll. Now a troll herself, Hilda runs away from her troll mother, Trylla, and turns to stone in the sunlight. In Trolberg, her mother Johanna finds Baba in Hilda's place and sets off to find her daughter. Meanwhile, Erik Ahlberg imposes a curfew and forms a Safety Patrol to deal with the rise in troll activity. Each night, Hilda turns back from stone, but the city's bells keep her out. She finds a huge cave where an imprisoned giant troll, Trundle, promises to make her human again if she does several tasks for him. She brings him troll mead, silences the bells that hold him and finally retrieves a red orb from the ruins of the legendary Mountain King's castle. When she touches the orb, she sees a giant creature looming over Trolberg's walls.

Johanna reaches the Stone Forest with Ahlberg's grudging help, and she and Hilda are reunited. When Trylla is reunited with Baba, the spell is broken. Trundle then puts the orb back in, revealing it as his missing eye, declares himself the Mountain King and leads the trolls against Trolberg. Hilda realizes what the vision meant: Amma, mother of all trolls, lies beneath the city and will rise to defend her children if they are attacked. Ahlberg destroys Trundle anyway, and Amma begins to wake. Hilda throws the eye at Ahlberg so that he sees the vision too, and he calls off the attack.

The trolls gather peacefully around Amma. Ahlberg resigns, and his deputy Gerda Gustav sets up an annual "Night of the Trolls" when trolls may visit their mother. Hilda's family stays in touch with Baba's.

Production wrapped in July 2021, and Netflix released the film on December 30, 2021. It is dedicated to two members of the animation crew who died during production. Reviews were positive: Polygon noted its darker tone, Variety praised its emotional wisdom and Screen Rant praised its visuals and music.

overview: Tov Matheson is a war veteran with PTSD who perceives that the apocalypse is coming. After starting a relationship with a dubious Messiah, he leaves his normal life and begins the construction of a shelter underground, training himself, in an extreme way, at the cost of losing everything and making people believe he is insane. When he also believes it, something extraordinary happens.
tagline: Are you ready to survive?
title: The Last Man
plot:
The Last Man (Spanish: El último hombre) is a 2019 Argentine-Canadian science fiction film co-written and directed by Rodrigo H. Vila. Set in a bleak, storm-ravaged future, it stars Hayden Christensen as Kurt, a war veteran suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder, Harvey Keitel as Noe, a street prophet who predicts an imminent catastrophe, and Liz Solari as Jessica, a woman who shares his belief, with Marco Leonardi and Rafael Spregelburd.

Kurt lives in an unnamed city plagued by constant storms, a world that collapsed during a 30-day crisis known as "the Black Month." Haunted by nightmares of a wounded soldier begging to be killed, he sleeps under his bed clutching a weapon. At a black market he crosses paths with a neo-Nazi gang extorting money from shopkeepers, and he hears Noe preach that a devastating electrical storm is coming. When Kurt returns a faulty gas mask to a shop run by Noe's followers, the prophet gives him a survival book, and Kurt is beaten by the gang. He takes a job at a security company run by Jessica's father, who values his combat experience, and is warned by the boss's enforcer, Gomez, to stay away from Jessica. He also sees the ghost of his friend Johnny, the soldier from his nightmare, whom Kurt shot, and a strange boy who calls him a ghost.

Kurt prepares for the apocalypse by building a secret bunker and grows close to Jessica, who wants to join him. When the gang returns to rob Noe's departing followers, Kurt kills several of them and lets the group escape. Gomez, who has been stealing money from the company and framing Kurt, uses Jessica as bait to capture him, and Kurt is locked in an asylum, where he is told that Noe is a convicted fraudster and that the world is not ending. Noe, disguised as Kurt's lawyer, arranges his escape. Before confronting Gomez, Kurt realizes the mysterious boy is his own younger self. At the security office, he plays a recording proving Gomez's guilt; Gomez shoots Kurt, who survives thanks to a protective vest, and kills Jessica's father before Kurt kills him. As the storms return worse than ever, Kurt fights his way back to his bunker and finds Jessica waiting for him.

The film was released in theaters and on video on demand on January 18, 2019, grossing only about $12,000. Reviews were negative, criticizing the plot and Christensen's performance; Christy Lemire of RogerEbert.com called it thoroughly unpleasant, though Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times praised its gloomy atmosphere.

overview: At the turning point of the Iran-Contra affair, Elena McMahon, a fearless investigative journalist covering the 1984 US presidential campaign, puts herself in danger when she abandons her assigned task in order to fulfill the last wish of her ailing father, a mysterious man whose past activities she barely knows.
title: The Last Thing He Wanted
plot:
The Last Thing He Wanted is a 2020 political thriller directed by Dee Rees, who adapted Joan Didion's 1996 novel of the same name with Marco Villalobos. Anne Hathaway stars as the journalist Elena McMahon, with Ben Affleck as Treat Morrison, Rosie Perez as Alma Guerrero, Willem Dafoe as her father Dick McMahon, Edi Gathegi as Jones, Mel Rodriguez as Barry Sedlow and Toby Jones as Paul Schuster.

Elena, a reporter for the Atlantic Post, was forced to flee the paper's Central American bureau in El Salvador during the civil war. Years later she wants it reopened, but her editor reveals that Congress is quietly pressing the paper to scale back its coverage of the region and assigns her instead to Ronald Reagan's re-election campaign. Elena reluctantly visits her long-absent father, Dick, and finds him still dealing in contraband but slipping into dementia. On the campaign trail, a general identifies her surveillance photos of shipping containers as surplus National Guard arms.

When Dick is hospitalised, Elena hands her assignment to her friend Alma and goes to Florida to care for him. He begs her to complete a deal he has arranged with his associate Barry Sedlow, and she agrees, seeing a chance to investigate the story from the inside. Following Sedlow's instructions, she delivers a large arms shipment to Costa Rica, where the buyer, Jones, underpays her and partly pays in cocaine. Stranded when her pilot leaves, she takes Jones's gun and vehicle, then discovers that her passport bears the name Elise Meyer. She reaches Antigua, learns that her father has died, and finds the embassy closed for the Fourth of July. Treat Morrison, an ambassador-at-large who has been investigating her, finds her at her hotel, and they sleep together. When gunmen attack her by the pool, Jones rescues her and explains that the deal was a trap to draw her father out of hiding. Morrison places her with Paul Schuster and promises to get her home to break the story of the arms deals, but a gunman kills Paul and his staff, and Elena turns to find it is Morrison, who shoots her dead and later claims self-defence. Jones, an agent of French intelligence, reports that he had been trying to protect her, and Alma uses Elena's notes to publish the story of the Iran–Contra affair.

The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 27, 2020, and was released on Netflix in February. It was panned, with only 5% positive reviews on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35.

overview: A woman struggles to survive on her own in the wake of a mysterious epidemic, which has decimated society and forced her deep into the unforgiving wild.
tagline: Those who stay die
title: Here Alone
plot:
Here Alone is a 2016 American post-apocalyptic horror drama film directed by Rod Blackhurst and written by David Ebeltoft. Lucy Walters stars as Ann, a woman trying to survive alone in the wilderness after a devastating epidemic, with Adam David Thompson as Chris, Gina Piersanti as his teenage stepdaughter, Olivia, and Shane West as Ann's husband, Jason. The film premiered at the 2016 Tribeca Film Festival, where it won the audience award for narrative features, and was released theatrically in March 2017.

Some time after a mysterious infection has turned much of the world's population into violent, zombie-like creatures, Ann lives in a makeshift camp deep in the woods. Resources are scarce, and she survives by foraging and living off the land, venturing only cautiously into abandoned houses, which tend to attract the infected. She clings to remnants of the world she has lost, listening to a hand-cranked radio that broadcasts an emergency message in French, a language she does not understand. Through flashbacks, the film gradually reveals what happened to her husband, Jason, and their infant daughter.

Returning from a scavenging trip, Ann comes across Chris, who has been injured, and Olivia. She takes them in and nurses Chris back to health, but she struggles to trust them, having grown used to depending only on herself. When a storm arrives just as the pair are about to move on, Ann allows them to stay longer, and over time she and Chris become romantically involved, to Olivia's resentment. The flashbacks reveal that Jason was killed by the infected after leaving at night to find supplies, leaving Ann to protect their baby alone in a world where any sound could draw the creatures to them. As tensions rise among the three survivors and Ann's buried guilt over the fate of her daughter comes to the surface, the group must decide whether to remain in the woods or seek out other survivors, a choice that forces Ann to confront the painful decisions she has made to stay alive.

Here Alone was praised for its restrained, character-driven approach to the zombie genre, which emphasizes isolation, grief and survival over action and gore, and for Walters's understated central performance. Its quiet, slow-burning style placed it among a wave of low-budget independent films using the post-apocalyptic setting for intimate drama.

overview: A group of Muslim men living in Sheffield hatch an inept plan to become suicide bombers.
tagline: We are four Lions.
title: Four Lions
plot:
Four Lions is a darkly comedic film that explores the complexities of radicalization and the nuances of British Muslim identity. The story revolves around four friends - Omar, Waj, Faisal, and Barry - who are all aspiring terrorists planning to carry out a bombing attack on the London Marathon.

At its core, Four Lions delves into the theme of identity crisis, particularly among young Muslims growing up in Britain. The film portrays how these characters struggle with their own sense of belonging, cultural heritage, and societal expectations. They grapple with the notion of what it means to be a Muslim in a predominantly Western society, often feeling caught between two worlds.

The movie also touches on the theme of toxic masculinity, as the characters' attempts to assert their virility and dominance are constantly thwarted by their own ineptitude and lack of direction. This is particularly evident in Barry's character, who is desperate to prove himself as a terrorist but ultimately ends up being more of a bumbling fool.

Furthermore, Four Lions critiques the notion of radicalization and the simplistic stereotypes often associated with it. The film humanizes its characters, revealing their vulnerabilities, fears, and insecurities, which are far removed from the typical portrayal of terrorists in media. This nuanced approach challenges the audience to reevaluate their assumptions about extremism and the complexities of the human experience.

Ultimately, Four Lions is a thought-provoking comedy that uses satire to explore some of the most pressing issues of our time, including identity, masculinity, and radicalization. The film's clever writing and strong performances bring these themes to life in a way that is both humorous and poignant.

overview: Seoul, South Korea, 1997. When the young but extremely anxious student Jin-seok, his parents and his successful older brother Yoo-seok move to a new home, mysterious and frightening events begin to happen around them, unexplained events that threaten to ruin their seemingly happy lives. Unable to understand what is happening, Jin-seok wonders if he is losing his mind.
tagline: Locked. Erased. Controlled. Isolated. Blurred.
title: Forgotten
plot:
Forgotten (Korean: 기억의 밤, literally "Night of Memory") is a 2017 South Korean mystery thriller film written and directed by Jang Hang-jun. It stars Kang Ha-neul as Jin-seok and Kim Mu-yeol as his older brother, Yoo-seok, and was released in South Korea on November 29, 2017, before becoming available worldwide on Netflix.

Jin-seok moves into a new house with his parents and his brother Yoo-seok, and they are told never to enter one locked room said to hold the previous owner's belongings. One rainy night, Jin-seok watches Yoo-seok being abducted and dragged into a car. Nineteen days later Yoo-seok returns with no memory of what happened, but Jin-seok notices disturbing changes in his personality and in his parents' behavior. Convinced something is wrong, he flees to a police station, where officers tell him it is not 1997, as he believes, but 2017, and that he is 41 years old, not 21. Returning home, he enters the forbidden room and finds a re-created murder scene.

Yoo-seok, whose real name is Choi, reveals the truth: twenty years earlier a woman and her teenage daughter were murdered in that room, and the victims' family, having found Jin-seok and identified him as the killer, abducted him to extract a confession. Because he remembered nothing, a hired psychiatrist concluded he suffered from dissociative amnesia and, posing as his father alongside an actress playing his mother, hypnotized him back to 1997 so that a reenactment of the crime might unlock his memory. Jin-seok escapes, and both he and the pursuing Choi are injured in road accidents. In hospital, Jin-seok's memories return. In 1997, after a car crash killed his parents and left his real brother dying, he could not afford the surgery during the Asian financial crisis and accepted an anonymous offer to kill a woman while sparing her children. Losing control when she and her daughter screamed, he killed them both, spared a little boy, and discovered that the man who hired him was his brother's doctor, the victims' husband and father, who had insured his wife's life; the doctor fell to his death in their struggle. Choi reveals that he is the boy Jin-seok spared, raised in an orphanage after relatives took the money. Jin-seok takes full blame and poisons himself, and Choi leaps from the hospital window. A final flashback shows Jin-seok at a river in 1997, smiling as the doctor's happy family walks past.

overview: Paul, a teenager in Arizona, tries to repair his relationships before moving to Oregon at the end of the summer.
tagline: Movin’ on
title: Saguaro
plot: Paul, a teenager in Arizona, tries to repair his relationships before moving to Oregon at the end of the summer.

overview: Maynard, a beloved local businessman is mistaken for the legendary Bigfoot during an inebriated romp through town in a makeshift gorilla costume. The sightings set off an international Bigfoot media spectacle and a windfall of tourism dollars for a simple American town hit by hard times. When Brock Masterson, reality TV’s “Monster Hunter,” arrives to hunt the beast, Maynard agonizes over whether to come clean, destroying the rebirth of his beloved town, or perpetuate the inadvertent hoax.
tagline: It's a magical life
title: Pottersville
plot:
Pottersville is a 2017 American fantasy comedy film directed by Michael Landon Jr. and written by Michael Landon Jr., Brian Smith, and Michael Landon Jr.'s mother, Linda Landon.

The main themes of Pottersville include:

1. **Redemption**: The story revolves around the idea of redemption, as the protagonist, John (played by Sam Jaeger), is given a chance to relive his life in an alternate universe where he made different choices.
2. **Personal growth and self-discovery**: As John navigates this new world, he learns valuable lessons about himself, his relationships, and what truly matters in life.
3. **The power of love and relationships**: The film highlights the importance of love, friendship, and family in shaping who we are and helping us grow as individuals.
4. **Choice and consequence**: Pottersville explores the idea that every choice we make has consequences, and that it's never too late to change our path and try again.

The story follows John, a man who is unhappy with his life, including his marriage and job. He is given a chance to relive his life in an alternate universe called Pottersville, where he made different choices. In this world, John finds success and happiness, but also learns that true fulfillment comes from within.

Throughout the film, John's experiences in Pottersville serve as a catalyst for personal growth and self-discovery. He must confront his past mistakes and learn to appreciate the present moment. Ultimately, John returns to his own universe, wiser and more grateful for the life he has.

Overall, Pottersville is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores themes of redemption, personal growth, love, and choice.

overview: Lexington, Kentucky, 2004. Four young men attempt to execute one of the most audacious art heists in the history of the United States.
tagline: You don't know where the line is until you cross it.
title: American Animals
plot:
American Animals is a 2018 docudrama heist film written and directed by Bart Layton, recounting the 2004 theft of rare books from the library of Transylvania University in Lexington, Kentucky. It stars Barry Keoghan as Spencer Reinhard, Evan Peters as Warren Lipka, Blake Jenner as Chas Allen and Jared Abrahamson as Eric Borsuk, with Ann Dowd as the librarian Betty Jean Gooch and Udo Kier. The film intercuts dramatized scenes with interviews of the real people involved, including the four culprits and Gooch.

Spencer, an art student who longs for some life-changing experience to inspire his work, tours the university library's special collections and is struck by a rare first edition of John James Audubon's The Birds of America. He and his friend Warren, a rebellious University of Kentucky student on an athletic scholarship, start to imagine stealing it along with other rare books. Noting that the collection is watched over by a single librarian, they plan to overpower her and escape through the staff elevator. Warren claims to have traveled to Amsterdam to meet black-market buyers, telling Spencer they could make millions, and they recruit two friends: Eric to handle logistics and Chas as the getaway driver.

On the day of the heist, the four arrive disguised as elderly men for an appointment to view the collection, but abort when they find several librarians present. Warren persuades the reluctant Spencer to try again the next day. This time Warren and Eric enter without disguises, clumsily subdue the librarian with a stun gun and tie her up, then drop The Birds of America during their chaotic escape, getting away with only two books. In New York, they seek a valuation at Christie's, which Warren says the buyers require, and Spencer carelessly leaves his own phone number. Back in Lexington, they realize that the email address used to book the appointments can be traced; the FBI tracks them down and they are arrested. In interviews years after their release from prison, the real men express regret, and Spencer wonders whether Warren ever really went to Amsterdam.

American Animals premiered at the 2018 Sundance Film Festival, where The Orchard and MoviePass Ventures bought it for $3 million, and opened in the United States on June 1, 2018. It received favorable reviews for its screenplay, acting and unconventional structure built around unreliable narrators; Rotten Tomatoes reported 88% approval and Metacritic a score of 68.

overview: For centuries, a small but powerful force of warriors called the Green Lantern Corps has sworn to keep intergalactic order. Each Green Lantern wears a ring that grants him superpowers. But when a new enemy called Parallax threatens to destroy the balance of power in the Universe, their fate and the fate of Earth lie in the hands of the first human ever recruited.
tagline: In our darkest hour, there will be light.
title: Green Lantern
plot:
Green Lantern is a 2011 superhero science fiction film directed by Ryan Reynolds, who also stars as the titular character. The movie is based on the DC Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with Hal Jordan (Ryan Reynolds), a test pilot and former Air Force pilot who is recruited by the InterGalactic Police Force to become a Green Lantern. The Green Lantern Corps is an intergalactic police force that uses power rings to protect the universe from threats. To become a Green Lantern, Hal must first be chosen by a power ring, which requires him to demonstrate his worthiness.

Hal's journey begins with a series of tests and challenges designed to assess his character and abilities. He eventually passes the test and becomes the 283rd member of the Green Lantern Corps. As he embarks on his new role, Hal is introduced to his fellow Green Lanterns, including John Stewart (Blu Huntley), Carol Ferris (Julia Stiles), and Tom Kalmaku (Ngoc Le).

As Hal navigates his new life as a Green Lantern, he also becomes romantically involved with Carol Ferris. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that Carol's father, Senator Hammond Ferris (Clancy Brown), is a powerful politician who opposes the Green Lantern Corps.

Meanwhile, a villainous character named Parallax emerges, who was once a Green Lantern but became corrupted by his own power ring. Parallax seeks to destroy the Green Lantern Corps and take over the universe for himself. Hal soon discovers that he has a personal connection to Parallax, as they were both test pilots in the Air Force.

As the story unfolds, Hal's relationships with his fellow Green Lanterns are put to the test when they face off against Parallax and his minions. The final battle takes place on the planet Oa, where Hal must confront his own demons and make a choice between saving the universe or saving himself.

In the end, Hal is able to defeat Parallax and save the universe, but not before he is forced to confront the darkness within himself. The movie ends with Hal reflecting on his journey and the lessons he has learned as a Green Lantern.

Overall, Green Lantern is an action-packed sci-fi adventure that explores themes of identity, duty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has its fans and remains a beloved entry in the DC Comics universe.

overview: With no means for defeating Godzilla Earth, mankind watches as King Ghidorah, clad in a golden light, descends on the planet. The heavens and earth shake once again as the war moves to a higher dimension.
tagline: Bow down and worship the golden demise.
title: Godzilla: The Planet Eater
plot:
Godzilla: The Planet Eater is a Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Kōbun Shizuno and Hiroyuki Seshita, produced by Polygon Pictures. The movie takes place in an alternate timeline where Godzilla has been awakened every 100 years to fight against the "Shin Godzilla" (the current iteration of Godzilla) that has been terrorizing Japan.

The story begins with a flashback of the events leading up to the awakening of the new Godzilla. In the past, humanity had discovered a way to harness the power of the Earth's core to create an infinite source of energy. However, this process also awakened the "Shin Godzilla," which was initially thought to be a monster created by humans.

As the years went by, the Shin Godzilla continued to grow in power and size, eventually becoming the dominant force on the planet. The world's top scientists and military leaders formed an alliance to stop the Shin Godzilla, but their efforts were unsuccessful.

The movie then jumps forward in time to the present day, where a new generation of humans has taken over the fight against the Shin Godzilla. A team of scientists, led by Dr. Niko Tatsumi (voiced by Takuya Ishida), discovers that the only way to defeat the Shin Godzilla is to use its own atomic breath against it.

The team develops a plan to create a massive spaceship that can harness the power of the Earth's core and channel it into the Shin Godzilla. The ship, called the "Godzilla Project," is launched into space and begins to orbit the planet.

As the Godzilla Project orbits the Earth, it begins to emit a powerful energy signal that resonates with the Shin Godzilla's atomic breath. The two energies begin to interact, causing the Shin Godzilla to become unstable and eventually break apart into smaller fragments.

The final battle takes place on the surface of the Earth, where the remaining fragments of the Shin Godzilla are fighting against each other. The team from the Godzilla Project uses their technology to amplify the energy signal, causing the fragments to collide with each other and ultimately destroying them.

With the Shin Godzilla defeated, humanity is finally able to take control of its own destiny. The movie ends with a shot of the Earth's core being harnessed for energy, symbolizing a new era of peace and prosperity for humanity.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that are explored, including the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control and the importance of working together to achieve a common goal. The film also features stunning animation and action sequences, making it a thrilling ride for fans of the Godzilla franchise.

overview: When an overconfident teen alien gets behind the controls of a spaceship, he must attempt to abduct a slumbering farmer under the watchful eye of a critical instructor. But abducting humans requires precision and a gentle touch, and within a few missteps it's painfully clear why more humans don't go missing every year.
tagline: Failure is an option.
title: Lifted
plot:
Lifted is a 2006 American computer-animated science fiction short written and directed by Gary Rydstrom for Pixar Animation Studios. It was the directing debut of Rydstrom, an Academy Award-winning sound designer, editor and mixer. It was also the first Pixar film produced by Katherine Sarafian, who later produced Brave in 2012. The short was inspired by the 1927 film Metropolis.

The story takes place aboard a spacecraft hovering over a farmhouse at night. Stu, a young green alien, is sitting a test in alien abduction while his examiner, Mr. B, watches silently and takes notes. Stu's task is to beam up Ernie, a farmer sound asleep in bed. The ship's controls are a huge board of thousands of identical, unlabeled toggle switches, and Mr. B's blank expression gives no hint which ones to use. Stu's nervous first tries send the sleeping Ernie into the walls. Growing frustrated, he starts flipping whole rows of switches, and Ernie bounces around the bedroom like a pinball, knocking things over without ever waking up.

Stu finally finds the right switch and guides Ernie towards a half-open window, where he briefly gets stuck, along with a nearby tree. As Ernie floats up towards the ship, Stu switches off the tractor beam too early, and the farmer drops to the ground until Mr. B turns it back on. Mr. B then pushes the trainee aside, takes over, puts Ernie back in bed and cleans up the damage. Stu begins to cry. With a sigh, Mr. B lets him fly the ship home, but Stu's joyful steering lands the ship on the farmhouse and crushes it. The ship leaves a vast crater, with Ernie still asleep on top of a single column of earth. During the credits he wakes up and is heard screaming as he falls.

Production ran from mid-2005 to summer 2006. Rydstrom based the story on his own work as a sound mixer: running a huge, complex console with many people watching and taking notes. The film used no major new technology, apart from a new program called Jiggle that let animators control the secondary jiggle of chosen body parts. The short premiered on October 12, 2006, at the 42nd Chicago International Film Festival. It was shown in the 2006 Animation Show of Shows and released in theaters with Ratatouille on June 29, 2007. It was nominated for Best Animated Short Film at the 79th Academy Awards and later appeared on the Ratatouille home release and in Pixar Short Films Collection, Volume 1.

overview: Set between the events of Halo 4 and Halo 5: Guardians… Halo: Nightfall tells the dramatic story of legendary man hunter and Naval Intelligence Officer Jameson Locke and his team as they are caught in a horrific biological attack while investigating terrorist activity on the distant colony world of Sedra. As they unravel a plot that draws them to an ancient, hellish artifact, they will be forced to fight for their survival, question everything and ultimately choose between their loyalty and their lives.
tagline: Survival Is A Choice
title: Halo: Nightfall
plot:
Halo: Nightfall is a 2014 American military science fiction production set in the universe of the Halo video game franchise, released both as a five-episode web series and as a feature-length film. Directed by Sergio Mimica-Gezzan from a script by Paul Scheuring, the creator of Prison Break, under the supervision of 343 Industries, it was produced by Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions with Xbox Entertainment Studios. Taking place between Halo 4 and Halo 5: Guardians, it introduces the Naval Intelligence agent Jameson Locke, played by Mike Colter, who later became a lead character in Halo 5.

Years after humanity's war with the alien alliance known as the Covenant, a fragile peace holds. Locke and his Office of Naval Intelligence team are sent to the colony world of Sedra to track a possible Covenant infiltration. Following an alien smuggler, they confront a Sangheili zealot who detonates a device in a crowded shopping center, releasing a mysterious element that attacks only human DNA and kills many people, including the daughter of Colonel Randall Aiken (Steven Waddington). Locke learns that the substance comes from Alpha Halo, a fragment of the ring world destroyed years earlier, now orbiting a star so closely that its surface becomes lethally hot by day,.

Locke and Aiken lead a joint team to the fragment to gather proof that the Covenant has broken the treaty and to destroy the source with a HAVOK nuclear warhead before sunrise. After they capture two smugglers, their dropship is brought down by swarms of Lekgolo worms drawn to active technology, and the survivors must cross the hostile terrain in darkness. As members are devoured one by one and the smugglers' two-seat ship becomes the only way off, the group fractures. Horrigan and Ramos mutiny and try to flee with a smuggler, and both are killed. Locke, Aiken and Private Talitha Macer reach the dropship and retrieve the bomb, which must be triggered by hand, and they draw lots to decide who stays behind. Aiken secretly rigs the draw, sacrifices himself to lure away the worms, and Locke and Macer escape as the fragment is destroyed at dawn.

Filmed in Iceland and Northern Ireland, Nightfall premiered weekly from 11 November to 10 December 2014 for owners of Halo: The Master Chief Collection on Xbox before a wider release in 2015. It won a Golden Reel Award for sound editing, though some critics called it cheap-looking and its soldiers interchangeable.

overview: A young woman dealing with anorexia meets an unconventional doctor who challenges her to face her condition and embrace life.
tagline: Don't fade away
title: To the Bone
plot:
To the Bone is a 2017 American drama film directed by Marti Noxon, written by Marti Noxon, and produced by Mockingbird Pictures.

The main themes of To the Bone revolve around eating disorders, mental health, body image, trauma, and recovery. The film follows Ellen, a 20-year-old woman struggling with anorexia nervosa, as she navigates her way through treatment at a residential facility.

Throughout the movie, the theme of body image is explored in depth, highlighting the societal pressures that contribute to eating disorders. Ellen's struggles with her weight and appearance are deeply intertwined with her mental health, leading to a complex exploration of the relationship between self-perception and self-worth.

The film also delves into the theme of trauma, revealing the underlying causes of Ellen's eating disorder. Her past experiences, including emotional abuse and neglect, are slowly revealed throughout the movie, shedding light on the long-term effects of trauma on mental health.

Recovery is a central theme in To the Bone, as Ellen navigates her way through treatment and begins to confront her demons. The film offers a nuanced portrayal of recovery, highlighting both the challenges and the triumphs that come with it.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity, as Ellen struggles to find herself outside of her eating disorder. Her relationships with others, particularly her therapist and her fellow patients, serve as catalysts for growth and self-discovery.

Overall, To the Bone is a powerful exploration of complex themes, offering a thought-provoking and emotionally charged portrayal of mental health, recovery, and the human experience.

overview: A pair of former high school sweethearts reunite after many years when they return to visit their small hometown.
tagline: You never forget your first love.
title: The Best of Me
plot:
The Best of Me is a 2014 American romantic drama film directed by Michael Hoffman and written by James L. White. The movie is based on Nicholas Sparks' 2011 novel of the same name.

The story begins with Dawson Cole (James Marsden), a successful businessman, who receives an invitation to his high school reunion in Beaufort, North Carolina. Dawson has been living in New York City and has built a life for himself, but he is struggling to connect with others due to a painful past.

Upon returning to his hometown, Dawson meets Amanda Collier (Michelle Monaghan), the love of his life from their high school days. They had a whirlwind romance before parting ways after graduation. However, Amanda's family disapproved of their relationship, and she eventually left town to pursue her dreams in New York City.

As Dawson and Amanda reconnect, they reminisce about their past and the choices they made that led them apart. The film then flashes back to their high school days, where we see their blossoming romance and the events that drove them apart.

Throughout the movie, Dawson and Amanda's relationship is rekindled, but it becomes clear that their past experiences have left emotional scars. They must confront the choices they made and the reasons why they drifted apart.

As the story unfolds, Dawson and Amanda face various challenges, including infidelity, family secrets, and personal struggles. The film takes a non-linear approach, jumping back and forth between the present day and their high school days.

Ultimately, Dawson and Amanda are forced to confront the reality of their past and make amends with each other. In a poignant and emotional climax, they come to terms with their feelings and find closure.

The Best of Me explores themes of love, loss, and redemption, highlighting the complexities of human relationships and the power of true love to overcome adversity. The film features strong performances from James Marsden and Michelle Monaghan, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, The Best of Me is a heartwarming and emotional romance that explores the complexities of love and relationships. With its non-linear storytelling and poignant performances, it's a must-see for fans of romantic dramas.

overview: When a driven doctor doesn't get the prestigious position she planned for, she unexpectedly finds herself moving to a remote Alaskan town. While she meets the locals and even starts a new romance, she has to learn to let the life she planned for give way to a love she never could have imagined, and finds this festive small town is hiding one big holiday secret.
title: Christmas Under Wraps
plot:
Christmas Under Wraps is a 2014 Hallmark Channel original movie starring Lacey Chabert and Paul Greene.

The main theme of Christmas Under Wraps revolves around the idea of second chances, forgiveness, and the power of love. The story follows Dr. Sophie Ellis, a successful surgeon who returns to her small hometown in Alaska after a personal tragedy. There, she reconnects with an old flame, Jake, and together they work on saving his family's struggling lodge.

Throughout the movie, Sophie learns to let go of her past and forgive herself and others. She also discovers that true love can be found again, even when you least expect it. The film showcases the beauty of small-town life, the importance of community, and the magic of Christmas.

The plot development is driven by Sophie's journey from a high-stress city life to a more relaxed, peaceful existence in her hometown. As she reconnects with Jake and his family, she begins to heal and find herself again. The movie features a heartwarming romance, stunning Alaskan landscapes, and a healthy dose of holiday cheer.

The ending is a feel-good, sentimental conclusion that leaves the audience with a sense of hope and renewal. Sophie and Jake's love story is a beautiful reminder that it's never too late to take a chance on love again, and that forgiveness and second chances can lead to happiness and fulfillment.

overview: Viktor Navorski is a man without a country; his plane took off just as a coup d'etat exploded in his homeland, leaving it in shambles, and now he's stranded at Kennedy Airport, where he's holding a passport that nobody recognizes. While quarantined in the transit lounge until authorities can figure out what to do with him, Viktor simply goes on living – and courts romance with a beautiful flight attendant.
tagline: Life is waiting.
title: The Terminal
plot:
The Terminal is a romantic drama film directed by Steven Spielberg, released in 2004 by DreamWorks Pictures.

The movie tells the story of Viktor Navorski (played by Tom Hanks), a traveler from Eastern Europe who becomes stranded at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City after his country experiences a coup d'état. The U.S. government refuses to let him enter the United States, and Viktor is forced to take up residence in the airport's terminal building.

As Viktor navigates his new life in the airport, he befriends a kind-hearted flight attendant named Amelia Warren (played by Catherine Zeta-Jones) and her colleagues. Despite being stuck in limbo, Viktor finds solace in his relationships with the airport staff and begins to rebuild his life.

However, Viktor's situation becomes increasingly complicated when he discovers that his country is still in turmoil, and he may be needed back home to help with the crisis. As Viktor struggles to decide whether to return or stay in the United States, he must also confront his own feelings for Amelia, who has grown close to him during their time together.

Throughout the film, Spielberg explores themes of identity, community, and the human spirit's ability to find hope and connection in even the most difficult circumstances. The movie features a strong supporting cast, including Stanley Tucci as Viktor's friend and confidant, Zeljko, and Diego Luna as a fellow traveler who becomes a source of support for Viktor.

As the story unfolds, Viktor must make a choice between his loyalty to his country and his growing feelings for Amelia. In the end, Viktor decides to stay in the United States with Amelia, and the two share a romantic moment as the airport's terminal building is transformed into a symbol of hope and new beginnings.

The Terminal received widespread critical acclaim upon its release, with many praising Tom Hanks' performance and Spielberg's direction. The film was also a commercial success, grossing over $216 million worldwide. Overall, The Terminal is a heartwarming and thought-provoking drama that explores the complexities of identity, community, and love in the face of uncertainty.

overview: Two families attempt a daredevil plan to escape the GDR with a homemade hot air balloon, but it crashes just before the border. The Stasi finds traces of this attempt to escape and immediately starts investigations, while the two families are forced to build a new escape balloon. With each passing day the Stasi is closer on their heels – a nerve-wracking race against time begins.
tagline: One of the most daring escapes of the Cold War.
title: Balloon
plot:
Balloon (German: Ballon) is a 2018 German thriller drama film directed by Michael Herbig about the 1979 escape of the Strelzyk and Wetzel families from East Germany to the West in a homemade hot-air balloon. The two families, including four children, flew from Pößneck in Thuringia to Naila in Bavaria, reaching an altitude of about 2,500 metres. Herbig spent six years preparing the film, met Günter Wetzel and was allowed to study the Stasi's thick file on the flight. The cast includes Friedrich Mücke, Karoline Schuch, David Kross, Alicia von Rittberg and Jonas Holdenrieder.

In the summer of 1979 in Pößneck, the families plan to flee the GDR by balloon. With ideal winds, Günter Wetzel decides the balloon is too small for eight people, and his wife Petra fears for their two young children, so Peter and Doris Strelzyk attempt the escape alone with their sons, Frank and Andreas, nicknamed "Fitscher." Frank, who is in love with Klara, the daughter of their neighbour Erik Baumann, a Stasi officer, nearly leaves behind a farewell letter to her. Hidden by clouds, the balloon rises, but the gas lines freeze, and it comes down just short of the border. The family escapes unhurt and destroys the evidence, but the Stasi finds the balloon, and Lieutenant Colonel Seidel launches a major investigation, steadily narrowing the circle of suspects.

Doris lost her medication at the landing site, and the investigators trace the pills to the local pharmacy. After a failed attempt to seek help at the US Embassy in East Berlin, Peter persuades Günter to build a new balloon. To avoid suspicion they buy fabric in small amounts in different towns, and Günter sews night after night, moving the work to the Strelzyks' cellar when neighbours notice the noise. When Frank learns that the Stasi is closing in and the wind turns south, the families leave that night, just before the Stasi breaks into their homes. The launch is rough, and when the gas runs out after about half an hour they land in a forest, uncertain where they are, until a police patrol tells them they are in Upper Franconia, in the West. Seidel must answer to Stasi chief Erich Mielke, and Erik Baumann is interrogated.

Around 936,000 people saw the film in German cinemas, and it was preselected for the 2019 German Film Award. Critics found it a solidly made and gripping thriller, though some felt it lacked historical depth; Rotten Tomatoes reported 70% approval. Disney had filmed the same escape in 1982.

overview: In 1666, a colonial town is gripped by a hysterical witch-hunt that has deadly consequences for centuries to come, and it's up to teenagers in 1994 to finally put an end to their town's curse, before it's too late.
tagline: End the curse.
title: Fear Street: 1666
plot:
Fear Street Part Three: 1666 is a 2021 American supernatural period horror film directed by Leigh Janiak, who wrote it with Phil Graziadei and Kate Trefry, the final chapter of the trilogy based on R. L. Stine's book series, after Part One: 1994 and Part Two: 1978. It stars Kiana Madeira, Ashley Zukerman, Gillian Jacobs, Olivia Scott Welch, Benjamin Flores Jr. and Darrell Britt-Gibson, and its two halves reveal the origin of the curse on the town of Shadyside and its defeat in 1994.

After reuniting Sarah Fier's severed hand with her remains, Deena experiences the events of 1666 through Sarah's eyes in Union, the settlement that would later split into Shadyside and Sunnyvale. Sarah and her friends gather berries from a reclusive widow, where Sarah notices a book of black magic, and at a party she and Hannah Miller kiss, unaware they are being watched. Soon the food and water are poisoned, and pastor Cyrus Miller, acting strangely, murders twelve children, including Sarah's brother, before Solomon Goode kills him. Accused of witchcraft, Hannah is captured while Sarah escapes. Seeking the widow's book to save Hannah, Sarah finds the widow murdered and the book beneath Solomon's house, where he admits that after losing his wife and child he made a pact with the Devil, offering Cyrus for possession in exchange for wealth and power. In their struggle her hand is severed, and she is captured, but at the execution she saves Hannah by declaring herself the witch and swears vengeance on Solomon before she is hanged.

Back in 1994, Deena understands that the Goodes have prospered by repeating the ritual in every generation, dooming Shadyside while Sunnyvale thrives. With Josh, Ziggy and the mall janitor, Martin, she lures Sheriff Nick Goode to the shopping mall and covers him with her blood so that the Shadyside killers turn on him. In the tunnels below, Deena frees the possessed Sam from the curse's grip, and when Nick is overwhelmed by visions of the curse's victims, Deena, guided by Sarah, stabs him in the eye, ending the curse. Life in Shadyside improves, and Deena and Sam picnic at Sarah's grave, though someone steals the widow's book from the tunnels.

It premiered on July 14, 2021, and was released by Netflix on July 16, a week after Part Two. Critics responded favorably, with 89% on Rotten Tomatoes and 68 on Metacritic.

overview: Seventeen-year-old Stella spends most of her time in the hospital as a cystic fibrosis patient. Her life is full of routines, boundaries and self-control — all of which get put to the test when she meets Will, an impossibly charming teen who has the same illness. There's an instant flirtation, though restrictions dictate that they must maintain a safe distance between them. As their connection intensifies, so does the temptation to throw the rules out the window and embrace that attraction.
tagline: When Life Keeps You Apart, Fight For Every Inch.
title: Five Feet Apart
plot:
Five Feet Apart is a 2019 American romantic drama film directed by Justin Baldoni and written by Mikki Daughtry and Toby Kebbell. The movie stars Haley Lu Richardson, Cole Sprouse, and Graham Verchere.

The story takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where cystic fibrosis patients are dying off due to the lack of a cure. The film follows the lives of two teenagers, Stella (Haley Lu Richardson) and Will (Cole Sprouse), who meet at a support group for CF patients.

Stella is a 17-year-old girl who has been living with CF since she was born. She is determined to live life to the fullest despite her illness. Will, on the other hand, is a 18-year-old boy who has just received his diagnosis and is struggling to come to terms with it.

The two teenagers meet at a support group meeting, where they are both told by their doctor that they have only five feet of lung capacity left due to the disease. This sets them off on a journey of self-discovery and exploration as they try to make the most of the time they have left.

As Stella and Will spend more time together, they develop strong feelings for each other. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that they are both CF patients who need to maintain social distancing in order to prevent the spread of the disease.

Despite this, the two teenagers find ways to be together, often sneaking around and finding creative ways to spend time with each other. They also become close friends with Will's sister, Meredith (Molly Gordon), who is also a CF patient.

As the story progresses, Stella and Will face numerous challenges, including hospitalizations, medication side effects, and the emotional toll of living with a terminal illness. Through it all, they find ways to support each other and make the most of their time together.

One of the central themes of the movie is the importance of human connection in the face of adversity. Despite the many obstacles that Stella and Will face, they are able to find joy and love in each other's company.

The film also explores the complexities of grief and loss. As Stella and Will navigate their relationships with each other and those around them, they must confront the reality of their own mortality.

Ultimately, Five Feet Apart is a heart-wrenching but ultimately uplifting film that celebrates the power of human connection and love in the face of adversity. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Stella and Will finding ways to make the most of their time together despite the challenges they face.

Overall, Five Feet Apart is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of love, loss, and resilience in the face of adversity. With outstanding performances from its cast, including Haley Lu Richardson and Cole Sprouse, the movie is sure to leave audiences moved and inspired.

overview: A young man seeking a father he has never met, through no fault of his own, ends up barricaded in a liquor store with five other people on Christmas Eve in the fictitious town of El Camino, NV.
tagline: Bullets, beer, holiday cheer.
title: El Camino Christmas
plot:
El Camino Christmas is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the complexities of family relationships and the true meaning of Christmas. The movie follows the story of a man who sets out to find his estranged father, only to discover that he's not what he expected.

At its core, El Camino Christmas is a story about redemption and forgiveness. The main character's journey is one of self-discovery, as he navigates his complicated past and confronts the mistakes of his family members. Through his experiences, he comes to understand the importance of letting go of grudges and embracing the love that's always been there.

The film also delves into themes of identity and belonging. The main character's search for his father is a metaphor for finding one's place in the world and understanding where you come from. As he travels along the El Camino, he encounters various characters who challenge his perceptions and force him to confront his own sense of self.

Furthermore, El Camino Christmas touches on the idea that family is not just about blood ties, but also about the people who show up for us when we need them most. The movie highlights the importance of human connection and community during the holiday season, when people often come together to support one another.
