Overall, El Camino Christmas is a feel-good film that celebrates the complexities of family relationships and the power of love and forgiveness to heal old wounds.

overview: A former American G.I. joins a yakuza family after his release from prison in post-World War II Osaka.
title: The Outsider
plot:
The Outsider is a 2018 action thriller directed by Martin Zandvliet from a screenplay by Andrew Baldwin. The Japanese-American production stars Jared Leto, Tadanobu Asano, Kippei Shiina, Shioli Kutsuna and Emile Hirsch, with Rory Cochrane.

The film opens in Osaka in 1954, nine years after the Pacific War. Former U.S. Marine captain Nick Lowell is the only foreigner in a prison full of tattooed yakuza. After he saves a gangster named Kiyoshi from being hanged, Kiyoshi's clan, the Shiromatsu-ikka, arranges Nick's early release and gives him a job. His first assignment is to win back Anthony Panetti, a bigoted American businessman who has chosen to deal with the rival Seizu-kai because they sent an American. Nick bludgeons Panetti with a typewriter, and Panetti changes his mind. Kiyoshi grows fond of the newcomer, giving him an apartment and asking him to look after his younger sister Miyu. Nick and Miyu begin an affair, and he gets a tattoo on his back to match hers.

When a weapons deal at the harbor turns out to be a Seizu-kai ambush, Nick kills two attackers but brings the clan to the brink of war. To make amends, Nick and Kiyoshi each cut off a fingertip as an apology to the Seizu-kai boss, and Nick is formally initiated into the clan. Lieutenant Paulie Bowers, a Marine who once served under Nick, recognizes him and tries to blackmail him, but Nick kills him and Kiyoshi helps him bury the body. After Miyu reveals that she is pregnant, Kiyoshi entrusts her safety to Nick. Soon afterwards, the Seizu-kai ambush the Shiromatsu boss at a tailor's shop, and Kiyoshi is shot dead as the group escapes.

Miyu's former lover Orochi and a fifth of the clan defect to the rivals. At peace talks on the harbor, Orochi stabs the Shiromatsu patriarch to death, a sniper wounds Nick, and the police burn down the clan's club. Nick goes to the Seizu-kai dojo with Kiyoshi's sword and confronts Orochi, who mocks him as a gaijin, an outsider who can never be yakuza. Nick cuts his throat. Back in hiding with Miyu, the surviving members bow to him as the new head of the clan.

Michael Fassbender was considered for the lead when Daniel Espinosa was in talks to direct, and Takashi Miike was later set to direct Tom Hardy before both left; Leto joined in 2016. Netflix released the film on March 9, 2018, to largely negative reviews. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called Leto disengaged and the film full of gangster clichés, and Variety's Andrew Barker called it a clueless misfire.

overview: A successful, single businesswoman who dreams of having a baby discovers she is infertile and hires a working class woman to be her unlikely surrogate.
tagline: Would you put your eggs...in this basket?
title: Baby Mama
plot:
Baby Mama is a 2008 American buddy comedy written and directed by Michael McCullers, who made his directing debut with it. Tina Fey and Amy Poehler lead a cast that includes Greg Kinnear, Dax Shepard, Romany Malco, Maura Tierney, Holland Taylor, Steve Martin and Sigourney Weaver. Relativity Media produced it and Universal Pictures released it.

Kate Holbrook is a successful single executive in Philadelphia who has put her career first. At 37 she decides she wants a child, but doctors tell her she has a T-shaped uterus that makes pregnancy unlikely. Adoption falls through, so she turns to a surrogacy agency run by the steely Chaffee Bicknell. The agency pairs her with Angie Ostrowski, a woman from South Philadelphia. When Angie is reported pregnant, Kate prepares in her usual driven way, reading parenting books, baby-proofing her apartment and researching the best preschools. Her plans fall apart when Angie, thrown out by her common-law husband Carl, moves in with her. The two clash constantly, and Kate also starts dating Rob Ackerman, the owner of a local juice bar.

What Kate does not know is that the implantation failed and Angie is faking the pregnancy to collect the money. Angie feels increasingly guilty but keeps putting off the truth, until an ultrasound shows she really is pregnant, with Carl's child. Carl exposes the lie at Kate's baby shower. Kate argues that the baby might still be hers, but a court rules that it is Angie's, and Angie apologizes. Right after the hearing, Angie goes into labor. Kate rushes her to the hospital, faints during the delivery and wakes to learn that she herself is two months pregnant by Rob. Kate forgives Angie, who names her daughter Stef after Gwen Stefani, and the two become close friends. A year later, at Stef's first birthday, Kate and Rob are engaged and have a daughter, and Carl is an involved father. The film ends with Kate and Angie watching Tom and Jerry cartoons with their girls.

The film opened on April 25, 2008, at number one in the United States and Canada, taking $17.4 million from 2,543 theaters. It went on to gross about $64.2 million against a $30 million budget. Reviews were mixed to moderately positive. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it a lightweight, predictable comedy carried by its performers. Variety's Todd McCarthy said its contents were easy to guess, while Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian called it enjoyable and amiable despite its romantic comedy clichés.

overview: Eight women gather to celebrate Christmas in a snowbound cottage, only to find the family patriarch dead with a knife in his back. Trapped in the house, every woman becomes a suspect, each having her own motive and secret.
tagline: Living in a house full of women can be murder
title: 8 Women
plot:
"8 Women" is a French comedy film released in 2002, directed by François Ozon. The movie revolves around the lives of eight sisters who are brought together at their family's estate after their father's death.

The main theme of "8 Women" explores the complexities and intricacies of female relationships, particularly among sisters. As the eight women navigate their individual personalities, desires, and conflicts, they reveal a deep-seated sense of vulnerability, insecurity, and competition that arises from their intertwined lives.

Throughout the film, Ozon masterfully weaves together themes of love, lust, and identity, as each sister struggles to find her place in the world. The movie also touches on the idea of female empowerment, as the women confront societal expectations and norms that have shaped their lives.

One of the most striking aspects of "8 Women" is its portrayal of the complexities of female desire and relationships. Ozon skillfully captures the nuances of human intimacy, revealing the intricate web of emotions, desires, and conflicts that exist between women.

Ultimately, "8 Women" is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the intricacies of female experience and the ways in which women navigate their lives, relationships, and identities.

overview: Three generations of the rowdy Cutler family live as outlaws in some of Britain's richest countryside – hunting hares, ram-raiding stately homes, and taunting the police. Struggling to retain a way of life fast becoming extinct, Chad Cutler ends up caught between his father's archaic principles and trying to do right by his kids, whilst the full force of the law is finally catching up with him.
tagline: Blood is a brutal bond.
title: Trespass Against Us
plot:
Trespass Against Us is a 2016 American crime drama film directed by Adam Wingard. The movie follows the story of Chad Cutler, a young man who struggles with his family's dark past and the cyclical nature of violence that has haunted them for generations.

At its core, Trespass Against Us explores themes of trauma, addiction, and the long-lasting effects of childhood experiences on adult life. The film delves into how Chad's upbringing within a dysfunctional family, marked by poverty, crime, and abuse, shapes his worldview and informs his relationships with others.

The movie also examines the concept of inherited trauma, where the experiences of past generations can be passed down through family lines, influencing the actions and decisions of those who come after. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, as Chad grapples with the legacy of his father's violent behavior and the ways in which it has impacted his own life.

Furthermore, Trespass Against Us touches on the idea of redemption and personal growth, as Chad seeks to break free from the patterns of behavior that have defined his family for so long. The film offers a nuanced portrayal of this journey, highlighting both the challenges and the potential for transformation that come with confronting one's past and working towards a better future.

Overall, Trespass Against Us is a powerful exploration of the complex interplay between trauma, family dynamics, and personal identity, offering a thought-provoking commentary on the cyclical nature of violence and the human capacity for growth and redemption.

original_title: A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song
overview: In this modern telling of the classic tale, aspiring singer Katie Gibbs falls for the new boy at her performing arts high school. But Katie's wicked stepmother and stepsister are scheming to crush her dream before she can sing her way into his heart.
tagline: Can the girl with a dream voice sing happily ever after?
title: A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song
plot:
A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song is a 2011 American musical teen comedy film directed by Damon Santostefano, a standalone sequel to Another Cinderella Story (2008) and the third installment in the A Cinderella Story series. Lucy Hale stars as Katie Gibbs, an aspiring singer, with Freddie Stroma as Luke Morgan, Missi Pyle as her stepmother, Gail, Megan Park as her stepsister, Bev, and Matthew Lintz as her stepbrother, Victor. It was released on DVD and digital platforms in September 2011 and premiered on ABC Family in January 2012.

Katie, an orphaned teenager with a beautiful voice, lives with her adoptive family, the Van Ravensways, who treat her as a servant: the shallow Gail, the spoiled Bev and the mischievous Victor. She accepts their mistreatment without complaint, fearing that Gail will send her back to foster care. Gail is the headmistress of the Wellesley Academy of the Arts, where Guy Morgan, the English head of Kensington Records, enrolls his son, Luke. Hoping to change her life, Katie slips her demo CD into Guy's briefcase. Guy asks Luke to produce an upcoming showcase at the academy, though Luke is reluctant to follow in his father's footsteps.

Bev, a terrible singer, is determined to win a recording contract with Guy. When Guy calls to say that he loves the demo, Gail claims that it belongs to Bev and that Katie stole it. Gail, Bev and Victor then scheme to use Katie's voice while Bev lip-syncs, with Victor using his technical skills to manipulate the audio. Meanwhile, Katie and Luke bond over their shared love of music, though Luke does not know that she is the voice he has been searching for. In a nod to the classic fairy tale, Katie attends a costume party in disguise and catches Luke's attention before slipping away, and with the help of her friends, including Victor, who eventually turns against his family's deceit, Katie must find the courage to reveal the truth and claim her voice at the showcase.

The film received negative reviews from the few critics who covered it. Mike McGranaghan of The Aisle Seat gave it one and a half stars out of four, likening it to a feature-length version of tween television shows such as iCarly and Victorious, while The DVD Sleuth rated it one out of two. It was followed by A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits in 2016.

overview: Mary Poppins returns to the Banks family and helps them evade grave dangers by taking them on magical, musical adventures.
tagline: Magic Always Returns.
title: Mary Poppins Returns
plot:
Mary Poppins Returns is a 2018 musical fantasy film directed by Rob Marshall and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1964 original film, Mary Poppins, and continues the story of the beloved nanny.

The film takes place 25 years after the events of the original. Michael Banks (Ben Whishaw), now an adult, is struggling to cope with the loss of his father, George Banks (David Tomlinson). The family's life has become dull and grey, lacking the magic and wonder that Mary Poppins brought into their lives.

When the children begin to act out and rebel against their parents' strict rules, Michael realizes that he needs help. He turns to an old friend, Jack (Lin-Manuel Miranda), who is now a struggling artist and musician. Jack introduces Michael to his cousin, Topsy Kettering (Emily Blunt), a wealthy and eccentric woman who claims to be the long-lost sister of Mary Poppins.

Topsy reveals that she has been keeping an eye on the Banks children from afar and believes that they need Mary Poppins' unique brand of magic in their lives. Michael is skeptical at first, but eventually agrees to let Topsy find Mary Poppins for him.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Mary Poppins (Emily Blunt) returning to London after a long absence. She is still as magical and mysterious as ever, with a newfound sense of purpose and determination. With the help of her trusty umbrella, Mary Poppins sets out to bring joy and wonder back into the lives of the Banks children.

Throughout the film, Mary Poppins uses her unique brand of magic to teach the children valuable lessons about love, loss, and the importance of family. Along the way, she also helps Michael come to terms with his own grief and find a new sense of purpose in life.

As the story reaches its climax, Mary Poppins reveals that she has been searching for a special place where the magic can be shared with others. She takes the children on a fantastical journey through London, using her umbrella to transport them to different locations around the city.

In the end, Mary Poppins helps the Banks family find closure and healing, and Michael comes to terms with his own emotions. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the entire family coming together to celebrate the magic of life and the power of love and connection.

Overall, Mary Poppins Returns is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that pays tribute to the original while also introducing new characters and themes. With its memorable songs, impressive choreography, and Emily Blunt's iconic performance as Mary Poppins, this movie is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: Jordan Sanders, a take-no-prisoners tech mogul, wakes up one morning in the body of her 13-year-old self right before a do-or-die presentation. Her beleaguered assistant April is the only one in on the secret that her daily tormentor is now trapped in an awkward tween body, just as everything is on the line.
tagline: She woke up like this
title: Little
plot:
Little (2019) is a fantasy comedy film directed by Tina Gordon, written by Tracy Oliver, and produced by Will Packer and Marc E. Platt.

The movie takes place on March 8th, which is International Women's Day, and follows the story of Maureen "Ma" Johnson (played by Regina Hall), a successful businesswoman who has just been passed over for a promotion at her company. Feeling frustrated and underappreciated, Ma decides to take revenge on her sexist boss, James King (played by Dan Aykroyd).

As she walks out of the office building, Ma is suddenly transported back in time to March 8th, 1982, when she was just a teenager. She finds herself reliving memories from her past, including her high school days and her relationships with her friends and family.

In this alternate timeline, Ma discovers that she has the ability to see and interact with the inner thoughts of women throughout history, including Frida Kahlo (played by Patricia Arquette), Rosa Parks (played by Regina King), and Susan B. Anthony (played by Danielle Brooks). These powerful women become her allies and mentors, guiding her on a journey of self-discovery and empowerment.

As Ma navigates this new reality, she also meets a young version of herself, played by Storm Reid, who is struggling to find her place in the world. Through her interactions with her past and present selves, Ma learns valuable lessons about feminism, identity, and the importance of supporting women.

Throughout the movie, Little features a talented ensemble cast, including Lyriq Bent, Marsai Martin, and Brian Tyree Henry. The film's humor is witty and relatable, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

As Ma continues to explore her past and present selves, she begins to realize that her experiences are not just about personal growth but also about the collective progress of women throughout history. In the end, Ma returns to her own time, armed with a newfound sense of confidence and purpose.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Ma embracing her inner strength and using it to inspire others. The final shot is of Ma walking out of the office building, ready to take on the world as a powerful and empowered woman.

Overall, Little (2019) is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates women's empowerment and the importance of female friendships. With its talented cast, witty humor, and inspiring message, it's a must-watch for anyone looking for a feel-good movie experience.

overview: Reunited witch twins Camryn and Alex adjust to their new life as supernatural beings while at the same time trying to maintain a normal existence in this sequel to the magical Disney Channel original movie Twitches. But they soon find themselves going head to head with the forces of darkness that threaten to destroy their world. Luckily, their birth mother, the powerful Miranda, is on hand to help out.
title: Twitches Too
plot: Reunited witch twins Camryn and Alex adjust to their new life as supernatural beings while at the same time trying to maintain a normal existence in this sequel to the magical Disney Channel original movie Twitches. But they soon find themselves going head to head with the forces of darkness that threaten to destroy their world. Luckily, their birth mother, the powerful Miranda, is on hand to help out.

overview: Big money artists and mega-collectors pay a high price when art collides with commerce. After a series of paintings by an unknown artist are discovered, a supernatural force enacts revenge on those who have allowed their greed to get in the way of art.
tagline: All Art Is Dangerous
title: Velvet Buzzsaw
plot:
Velvet Buzzsaw is a 2019 American satirical black comedy and supernatural horror film written and directed by Dan Gilroy. Jake Gyllenhaal, Rene Russo and Zawe Ashton lead an ensemble that includes Toni Collette, Daveed Diggs, Tom Sturridge, Natalia Dyer, Billy Magnussen and John Malkovich.

Los Angeles art critic Morf Vandewalt begins an affair with Josephina, who works for gallery owner Rhodora Haze, once a member of the punk band Velvet Buzzsaw. Josephina finds that a reclusive neighbor, Vetril Dease, has died, leaving behind a large collection of paintings, some partly destroyed. She takes them, and Rhodora shows them to great acclaim, deliberately keeping them scarce. Morf finds out that Dease had a violent childhood, killed his abusive father and was subjected to experiments in a psychiatric hospital. He later learns that Dease mixed blood into his paint.

The paintings then begin to kill the people who profit from them. Gallery worker Bryson is dragged into a painting at a deserted gas station. Rival dealer Jon Dondon is strangled with his own scarf by a hand that reaches out of the dark. Morf starts seeing figures move in the canvases. Gretchen, an art adviser who arranged a Dease show, is killed when an interactive sculpture called Sphere cuts off her arm. Each death only raises demand. Morf begs Rhodora to stop selling the work, but she rushes to sell it for tens of millions. Josephina is swallowed by a wall of graffiti. Hoboman, a robotic piece Morf once panned, comes to life and kills him. Rhodora's buzz saw tattoo starts spinning and cuts her throat. Coco, the assistant who kept finding the bodies, leaves for Michigan and passes a street vendor selling Dease paintings for five dollars each. Meanwhile, the painter Piers draws patterns in the sand at the edge of the waves.

Gilroy said he conceived the film after the cancellation of Superman Lives, a project he had worked on. He settled his frustration on a beach, which inspired the final scene. Netflix produced the film, and shooting began in Los Angeles in March 2018. Marco Beltrami and Buck Sanders scored it. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 27, 2019, and was released by Netflix on February 1. Reviews were mixed to favorable. Rotten Tomatoes rated it 61%, and RogerEbert.com called it wildly inconsistent but ambitious, with unforgettable images and an excellent ensemble.

overview: When a fisherman leaves to fight with the Greek army during World War II, his fiancée falls in love with the local Italian commander.
title: Captain Corelli's Mandolin
plot:
Captain Corelli's Mandolin is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature during wartime. The movie delves into the intricate relationships between characters, particularly the bond between Captain Antonio Corelli, an Italian officer, and Dr. Iannis, a Greek doctor.

At its core, the film grapples with the theme of love and loss in the face of war and occupation. The story is set on the island of Cephallonia during World War II, where Italy has occupied Greece. The narrative weaves together the lives of various characters, including Captain Corelli, Dr. Iannis, and his daughter Pelagia, as they navigate the challenges of living under foreign rule.

One of the primary themes of the film is the power of human connection in the face of adversity. Despite the animosity between the Italian and Greek populations, the characters form unexpected bonds with one another, which serve as a testament to the resilience of the human spirit. The relationship between Captain Corelli and Dr. Iannis, in particular, is a poignant exploration of how two individuals from different backgrounds can find common ground and develop a deep understanding of each other.

The film also touches on the theme of cultural identity and the struggle for self-preservation in the face of oppression. As the Italian occupation tightens its grip on Cephallonia, the characters must confront their own identities and the consequences of living under foreign rule.

Furthermore, Captain Corelli's Mandolin is a powerful exploration of the human cost of war and the impact it has on individuals and communities. The film's portrayal of the brutality and destruction caused by war serves as a stark reminder of the devastating effects of conflict on human lives.

Overall, Captain Corelli's Mandolin is a moving and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature during wartime, highlighting the power of love, connection, and resilience in the face of adversity.

original_title: Conquest of the Planet of the Apes
overview: In a futuristic world that has embraced ape slavery, a chimpanzee named Caesar resurfaces after almost twenty years of hiding from the authorities, and prepares for a revolt against humanity.
tagline: All new! The revolt of the apes. The most awesome spectacle in the annals of science fiction!
title: Conquest of the Planet of the Apes
plot:
Conquest of the Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking science fiction film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond our control. The movie delves into the theme of power struggles, as a group of intelligent apes, led by Caesar, rise up against their human oppressors in a bid for freedom and dominance.

At its core, Conquest of the Planet of the Apes is a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the devastating consequences of exploiting and manipulating others for one's own gain. The film highlights the inherent cruelty and ruthlessness that can exist within human society, as embodied by the sinister forces that seek to maintain their grip on power.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and what it means to be human. As Caesar and his apes navigate their newfound freedom, they are forced to confront the complexities of their own existence and the nature of their relationship with humans. This introspection raises questions about the boundaries between species and whether it is possible for intelligent beings from different worlds to coexist in harmony.

Furthermore, Conquest of the Planet of the Apes touches on the theme of revolution and social change. The apes' struggle for power serves as a metaphor for the human experience of fighting against oppressive systems and seeking a better future. The film's portrayal of a world where humans are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and limitations serves as a powerful commentary on the cyclical nature of history and the importance of empathy and understanding in shaping a more just society.

Overall, Conquest of the Planet of the Apes is a gripping and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider the complexities of human nature and our place within the natural world.

overview: France, 1914, during World War I. On Christmas Eve, an extraordinary event takes place in the bloody no man's land that the French and the Scots dispute with the Germans…
tagline: Without an enemy there can be no war.
title: Joyeux Noel
plot:
"Joyeux Noel" (also known as "Christmas in the Trenches") is a 2005 French war drama film directed by Christian Carion, produced by Canal+, and released by Wild Bunch. The main themes of this movie are:

1. **The Human Cost of War**: The film highlights the devastating effects of war on soldiers, particularly those from different countries who find themselves in the trenches together. It shows how quickly friendships can form and how quickly they can be destroyed.

2. **Compassion and Empathy**: The story revolves around the Christmas Truce of 1914, where Allied and German soldiers laid down their arms and celebrated Christmas together. This act of kindness and humanity serves as a powerful reminder that even in the midst of conflict, there is always room for compassion and understanding.

3. **The Power of Human Connection**: The film emphasizes the importance of human relationships and connections in breaking down barriers between enemies. Through the characters' experiences, we see how shared moments of joy, laughter, and camaraderie can transcend nationalities and ideologies.

4. **War's Disruption of Normal Life**: "Joyeux Noel" portrays the disruption that war causes to soldiers' lives, including their relationships with family and friends back home. The film also explores the emotional toll of war on individuals, particularly those who are forced to confront the harsh realities of conflict.

5. **A Glimmer of Hope in a Dark Time**: Set against the backdrop of one of the darkest periods in human history, "Joyeux Noel" offers a message of hope and resilience. The film suggests that even in the midst of chaos and destruction, there is always room for kindness, compassion, and humanity.

Overall, "Joyeux Noel" is a powerful and poignant film that sheds light on a pivotal moment in history while exploring universal themes that continue to resonate with audiences today.

original_title: The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl
overview: Everyone always knew that Max had a wild imagination, but no one believed that his wildest creations -- a boy raised by watchful great white sharks and a girl with the force of a volcano -- were real. Now, these two pint-sized action masters will show Max that even an ordinary kid has what it takes to be extraordinary.
tagline: Smaller heroes. Just as super.
title: The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl
plot:
The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl (marketed as The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl in 3-D) is a 2005 American superhero film co-written, edited, shot and directed by Robert Rodriguez. It stars Cayden Boyd as Max and Taylor Lautner as Sharkboy, with Taylor Dooley, David Arquette, Kristin Davis and George Lopez. Many of its ideas came from Rodriguez's children, especially his son Racer Max.

Max is a lonely ten-year-old in suburban Austin who records his dreams of an imaginary world called Planet Drool in a journal. Among his creations are two young superheroes, Sharkboy and Lavagirl. In real life, Max is bullied by his classmate Linus and worried by his parents' troubled marriage. After Linus steals and defaces his dream journal, Sharkboy and Lavagirl suddenly appear in his classroom and take him to Planet Drool, which is being corrupted by Mr. Electric, a villain based on Max's eccentric teacher, Mr. Electricidad.

On their journey to save Drool, the trio bond but are trapped by Mr. Electric in the Dream Graveyard, where forgotten dreams lie. Guided by Tobor, a robot toy Max abandoned, they set out to obtain the Crystal Heart, held by Lavagirl's rival the Ice Princess, which can freeze time and halt the spreading darkness. They are captured by Minus, the mastermind behind Mr. Electric, who turns out to be Linus, having entered Drool through Max's journal and filled it with his own dark dreams. After escaping and securing the Crystal Heart, the heroes are ambushed again, and Lavagirl sacrifices herself to save Sharkboy. Setting aside his selfish dreams, Max becomes the all-powerful Daydreamer, sends Sharkboy to revive Lavagirl, defeats Linus and offers to build a better dream world with him. Linus agrees, but Mr. Electric flees to Earth to kill Max in his sleep, attacking the school with an artificial tornado. While Sharkboy and Lavagirl rescue Max's parents, who reconcile, Max gives the Crystal Heart to his classmate Marissa, the model for the Ice Princess, who freezes and destroys Mr. Electric. Sharkboy becomes King of the Ocean and Lavagirl Queen of Earth's volcanoes, while Max, now friends with Marissa and Linus, urges everyone to dream a better dream and work to make it real.

Released by Dimension Films on June 10, 2005, the film opened fifth at the box office and grossed about $72 million worldwide. Critics were largely negative, judging the 3-D conversion a miscalculation; Rotten Tomatoes reported 19% approval and Metacritic a score of 38.

belongs_to_collection.name: Creature From The Black Lagoon Collection

overview: When scientists exploring the Amazon River stumble on a “missing link” connecting humans and fish, they plan to capture it for later study. But the Creature has plans of his own, and has set his sights on the lead scientist's beautiful fiancée, Kay.
tagline: From the Amazon's forbidden depths came the Creature from the Black Lagoon
title: Creature from the Black Lagoon
plot:
"Creature from the Black Lagoon" (1954) is a classic science fiction horror film directed by Jack Arnold, produced by Walter Wanger, and released by Universal International Pictures. The movie's main themes include:

1. **The Dangers of Scientific Hubris**: The film explores the consequences of playing with nature and tampering with forces beyond human control. The scientists' attempts to capture and study the creature lead to disastrous results, highlighting the importance of respecting the natural world.
2. **Environmentalism and Conservation**: The movie serves as a warning about the importance of preserving our environment and the delicate balance of ecosystems. The Black Lagoon's unique ecosystem is disrupted by human activities, leading to catastrophic consequences for both humans and the creature.
3. **Fear of the Unknown**: The film taps into the audience's fear of the unknown, using the mysterious and terrifying creature as a metaphor for the unexplored and uncontrollable aspects of nature. This theme is particularly relevant in the context of 1950s America, where scientific advancements were rapidly changing the world.
4. **The Power of Nature**: The movie showcases the awe-inspiring power of nature, highlighting the creature's incredible strength, speed, and adaptability. This theme serves as a reminder of our place within the natural world and the importance of respecting its boundaries.
5. **Romanticism and Adventure**: The film also features elements of romance and adventure, with the two female leads, Kay Lawrence and Julie Adams, navigating the dangers of the Amazonian jungle in search of their missing colleague.

These themes are woven throughout the movie's narrative, which follows a team of scientists and explorers as they venture into the Black Lagoon to capture the legendary creature. The film's blend of science fiction, horror, and adventure elements has made it a beloved classic among fans of the genre.

original_title: โปรเจกต์ลับ หลับ เป็น ตาย
overview: Four insomniac med school students are lured into a neuroscience experiment that spirals out of control and must find a way out before it’s too late.
title: Deep
plot:
Deep (Thai: โปรเจกต์ลับ หลับ เป็น ตาย, roughly "Secret Project: Sleep, Live, Die") is a 2021 Thai mystery thriller film produced by Transformation Films and released on Netflix. It was written and directed by a team of students from Bangkok University, with directing credits shared by Sita Likitvanichkul, Jetarin Ratanaserikiat, Apirak Samudkidpisan, Thanabodee Uawithya and Adirek Wattaleela. Panisara Rikulsurakan stars as Jane, with Kay Lertsittichai as Win, Supanaree Sutavijitvong as Cin, Krit Jeerapattananuwong as Peach, Warisara Jitpreedasakul as June and Dujdao Vadhanapakorn as Professor Nichcha.

Jane, a medical student, lives with her delinquent younger sister June and cares for their grandmother. Overwhelmed by studying, housework and debt, she has become an insomniac. Her professor, Nichcha, suggests that she join a study run by a German pharmaceutical company. Its head scientist, Hans Miller, explains that the experiment, called Deep, has three levels and aims to harvest Qratonin, a brain chemical that keeps people awake, through a microchip implanted in the subject's neck. Promised generous rewards, Jane signs a non-disclosure agreement and receives the implant and a watch to monitor her Qratonin level, along with a warning: if she falls asleep for more than 60 seconds before reaching 100 percent, the chip will stop her heart.

Jane meets fellow subjects Win, a partygoer, Peach, a gaming nerd, and Cin, a popular student, and the four, calling themselves Non-Non, complete the first two levels as their sleep deprivation causes vivid hallucinations. When Cin discovers that Peach is the stalker she has been afraid of, she collapses and nearly dies, and the group quits and drifts apart. After Jane sees a student die because of Deep and her grandmother suffers a stroke, she learns that June has joined the experiment too; Hans warns that June's third level has begun and that the chip will not be removed unless Jane brings her friends back. The reunited group enters the final level, but by the sixth day chaos erupts. Jane discovers that the company is a front, Hans is an actor and Nichcha is the mastermind, harvesting Qratonin to revive her comatose lover, Jed, who fell from a building through lack of sleep. Nichcha locks them up, but the friends fake Win's death to trick her and overpower her. She is arrested, the chips are removed and the friends mend their lives.

overview: A businessman, on his daily commute home, gets unwittingly caught up in a criminal conspiracy that threatens not only his life but the lives of those around him.
tagline: Lives are on the line
title: The Commuter
plot:
The Commuter is a 2018 action thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra, in his fourth collaboration with Liam Neeson, and written by Byron Willinger, Philip de Blasi and Ryan Engle. Neeson stars as a former policeman drawn into a murder conspiracy on his daily train ride, alongside Vera Farmiga, Patrick Wilson, Jonathan Banks, Florence Pugh and Sam Neill.

Michael MacCauley, a former NYPD officer turned insurance salesman, rides the same Hudson Line train between Tarrytown and Grand Central every day. Suddenly laid off and afraid to tell his wife, he confides in his former partner, Murphy, who is still on the force. On the ride home, a mysterious woman named Joanna offers him a "hypothetical" deal: find a passenger known as "Prynne," who has something that does not belong to them, for $100,000, starting with $25,000 hidden in the bathroom. Michael takes the money, but when he tries to get off, he is handed his wife's wedding ring as a warning. A commuter he asks for help is pushed under a bus, and Joanna reveals that his family is being held and that he must plant a GPS tracker on Prynne.

Michael's attempts to identify Prynne go wrong: the man he tags turns out to be an FBI agent, found dead soon after. Murphy tells him that Prynne is a key witness to the supposed suicide of city official Enrique Mendez, and Michael realizes that Prynne is to be killed and that he is being framed. He forces the passengers into the last car and kills another passenger, Oliver, who had been hired to murder Prynne. Prynne turns out to be Sofia, a teenage girl holding evidence against powerful people, who was being escorted to witness protection. When Michael refuses to kill her, Joanna detonates explosives to derail the train, but Michael uncouples the final car and saves most of the passengers. Police surround the car, believing he has taken hostages, and Murphy is sent in to negotiate, inadvertently revealing that he is the corrupt cop who killed Mendez. Michael removes Murphy's identifying tag, and snipers shoot Murphy. Sofia testifies, Michael's family is rescued, and he is offered his old job back. Later, he confronts Joanna on a train and prepares to arrest her.

Released by Lionsgate in the United States on January 12, 2018, The Commuter grossed $119.9 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with critics comparing it to Non-Stop but praising Neeson's performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 55% approval and Metacritic a score of 56.

overview: An ex-mercenary turned smuggler. A Mende fisherman. Amid the explosive civil war overtaking 1999 Sierra Leone, these men join for two desperate missions: recovering a rare pink diamond of immense value and rescuing the fisherman's son, conscripted as a child soldier into the brutal rebel forces ripping a swath of torture and bloodshed countrywide.
production_companies: Lonely Film Productions GmbH & Co. KG.
tagline: It will cost you everything.
title: Blood Diamond
plot:
Blood Diamond is a 2006 adventure drama film directed by Edward Zwick and starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Djimon Hounsou, Jennifer Connelly, and Arnold Vosloo.

The movie takes place during the Sierra Leone Civil War (1991-2002) and follows the story of Solomon Vandy (Djimon Hounsou), a fisherman who is forced to join the rebel army after his family is killed by the government. Solomon becomes embroiled in the diamond trade, which has become a lucrative business for those involved in the conflict.

Solomon meets Danny Archer (Leonardo DiCaprio), an American diamond smuggler who is searching for a rare pink diamond called the "Heart of Fire." The diamond is said to be cursed, and many people have died trying to find it. Solomon agrees to help Danny in exchange for his freedom and the promise that he will be able to return home.

As they journey through the war-torn country, Solomon and Danny encounter various characters, including Maddy Bowen (Jennifer Connelly), a diamond buyer who is working with Danny's company. The group faces numerous challenges, including government soldiers, rebel fighters, and treacherous terrain.

Throughout their journey, Solomon begins to question his involvement in the diamond trade and the morality of his actions. He also starts to develop feelings for Maddy, which complicates his relationship with Danny. Meanwhile, Danny becomes increasingly obsessed with finding the Heart of Fire, which he believes will make him rich and secure his future.

As they near their destination, Solomon and Danny are ambushed by government soldiers, who are also after the diamond. In a tense confrontation, Solomon is forced to choose between his loyalty to Danny and his desire to protect Maddy. He ultimately decides to betray Danny and escape with Maddy.

The movie culminates in a dramatic showdown between Solomon and Danny, who has become increasingly ruthless in his pursuit of the diamond. Solomon emerges victorious, but not without scars. He is finally able to return home to his family, who have been waiting for him.

Throughout the film, Zwick explores themes of greed, power, and redemption. The movie raises questions about the morality of the diamond trade and the impact it has on individuals and communities. The title "Blood Diamond" refers to the fact that many diamonds are mined using forced labor and inhumane conditions, resulting in the deaths of thousands of people.

The film features strong performances from its leads, particularly Djimon Hounsou, who won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his portrayal of Solomon Vandy. The movie also received critical acclaim for its cinematography, editing, and score.

Overall, Blood Diamond is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature and the consequences of our actions.

overview: Merab has been training since a young age at the National Georgian Ensemble with his dance partner Mary. His world is suddenly turned upside down when the charismatic and carefree Irakli arrives and becomes both his strongest rival and desire. In this conservative setting Merab finds himself having to break free and risk it all.
title: And Then We Danced
plot:
And Then We Danced is a poignant and powerful film that delves into the complexities of love, identity, and societal expectations in a small Estonian town. The movie tells the story of two young men, Kalju and Meri, who are forced to confront their feelings for each other when they're paired together as dance partners at the annual national ballet competition.

At its core, And Then We Danced is a film about the struggle for self-expression and acceptance in a society that often prioritizes conformity over individuality. The movie shines a light on the restrictive nature of traditional Estonian culture, where same-sex relationships are stigmatized and same-gender couples are shunned by their families and communities.

Through Kalju's character, the film explores the pain and vulnerability of being forced to hide one's true self in order to fit into societal norms. The movie also delves into the complexities of love and desire, as Kalju and Meri navigate their feelings for each other amidst the pressures of competition and expectation.

The film is a powerful exploration of the human need for connection and acceptance, and it raises important questions about the nature of identity, community, and what it means to be true to oneself. The movie's portrayal of the Estonian ballet world is also noteworthy, offering a nuanced critique of the cultural institution that often prioritizes discipline over passion and creativity.

Overall, And Then We Danced is a moving and thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to confront their own biases and assumptions about identity, love, and acceptance.

overview: Marlo, a mother of three, including a newborn, is gifted a night nanny by her brother. Hesitant at first, she quickly forms a bond with the thoughtful, surprising, and sometimes challenging nanny named Tully.
tagline: See how the mother half lives.
title: Tully
plot:
Tully is a 2018 American comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of motherhood, identity, and the struggles of modern womanhood.

At its core, Tully delves into the theme of exhaustion and burnout, particularly in the context of motherhood. The protagonist, Marlo (played by Charlize Theron), is a devoted but overwhelmed mother of three young children, struggling to balance her own desires and needs with the demands of caring for her family.

As the story unfolds, Tully also examines the societal expectations placed on women, particularly in terms of their roles as caregivers and nurturers. Marlo's life is marked by a sense of disconnection and isolation, as she feels suffocated by the responsibilities of motherhood and the lack of personal fulfillment in her own life.

The film also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery, as Marlo embarks on a journey of introspection and growth. Through her experiences with a night nanny (played by Mackenzie Davis), Marlo begins to re-evaluate her priorities and redefine what it means to be a mother and a woman in today's society.

Ultimately, Tully presents a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of the challenges faced by modern women, particularly those navigating the complexities of motherhood. The film offers a powerful commentary on the societal pressures that can lead to feelings of exhaustion, disconnection, and disillusionment, while also celebrating the resilience and strength of women in the face of adversity.

overview: A teenager struggles to keep her scandal-ridden past and a big secret from getting out when she strikes up an unlikely romance with the crown prince.
title: Royalteen
plot:
Royalteen (Norwegian: Royalteen: Arvingen, "The Heir") is a 2022 Norwegian teen romantic drama directed by Per-Olav Sørensen and Emilie Beck for Netflix, based on the young-adult novel series by Randi Fuglehaug and Anne Gunn Halvorsen. Co-written by Ester Schartum-Hansen, it stars Ines Høysæter Asserson as Lena and Mathias Storhøi as Crown Prince Karl Johan, known as Kalle, with Elli Rhiannon Müller Osborne as his twin sister Margrethe and Veslemøy Mørkrid and Petter Width Kristiansen as Lena's parents. The film runs 107 minutes and was conceived as the first installment of a franchise.

Lena is a teenager whose parents have uprooted their lives and found new jobs so that the family can move to Oslo and give her a fresh start after a scandal in her previous town, the reasons for which are not revealed at first. At her new school, which the royal twins attend, she strikes up a friendly conversation with Kalle on her first day. The prince, who is trying to shake off his party-boy image and is weary of people who see only his public persona, takes a liking to her, and the two slowly begin a romance through a series of ups and downs, including surprise visits to her home and the pressures of life in the public eye. Lena, who seems unimpressed that she is dating a royal, is not completely honest with Kalle about why she moved, and the secret she carries keeps haunting her; she devotedly cares for a baby she introduces to classmates as her little brother, though the child's real connection to her is more complicated. Her past catches up with her through old friends she treated badly, while the protective Margrethe, determined to preserve the royal status quo, makes biting remarks about Lena's ordinary background and opposes the relationship. As the truth threatens to come out, Lena must decide what she is willing to reveal to keep her love.

Royalteen was released on Netflix on 17 August 2022. Reviews were mixed. Decider's Radhika Menon advised skipping it, finding the romance clunky, Lena's secret obvious from the first act and the ending confusing, though she praised the strong chemistry between Asserson and Storhøi and the parents' grounded performances. On High on Films, Akash Deshpande considered the premise a reiteration of familiar teen tropes with surface-level class commentary, but found it consistently engaging thanks to unhurried direction and committed acting. Norwegian newspaper VG was more enthusiastic.

overview: Trapped in a remote tavern, a group of strangers must band together for survival. Outside the bar, a horde of ravenous, flesh-eating monsters are trying to break in and dine on the frightened humans inside.
tagline: They're Hungry. You're Dinner.
title: Feast
plot:
Feast is a 2005 American action horror comedy film directed by John Gulager and written by Patrick Melton and Marcus Dunstan, produced as the winning project of the third season of the filmmaking contest and documentary series Project Greenlight. Balthazar Getty, Henry Rollins, Navi Rawat, Judah Friedlander, Jenny Wade, Krista Allen, Clu Gulager, the director's father, Josh Zuckerman and Jason Mewes star. Ben Affleck, Matt Damon and Wes Craven were among its executive producers.

Patrons are drinking at an isolated bar in the Nevada desert when a blood-soaked man, identified on screen only as "Hero," bursts in to warn them of impending danger, displaying the severed head of a hideous creature as proof. Moments later he is dragged through a window and decapitated. His wife, "Heroine," arrives soon afterwards, and the survivors begin boarding up the bar as a family of monstrous creatures lays siege to it. Characters are introduced with on-screen captions giving their nicknames, occupations and life expectancies, and the film delights in subverting expectations about who will survive.

Despite the patrons' efforts, a young monster breaks in, killing one man and severing the leg of a woman, before a shotgun blast drives it into a freezer, where it is trapped. During a brief respite, the survivors discover that the bar's only phone has been destroyed and that they are cut off from help. As the creatures, which reproduce at an alarming rate and devour everything in their path, keep up their attack, the group, including a tough waitress, a cocky bartender, a motivational speaker and a single mother, argue over how to escape. Their increasingly desperate plans, from fighting back with makeshift weapons to attempting to reach a vehicle, lead to a series of gory deaths and grim reversals, as the band of strangers is whittled down by the monsters before dawn.

Feast received mixed reviews, with a 57 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes; the consensus noted that Gulager made the most of his material, offering some surprisingly tasty if far from nourishing morsels. It received a limited theatrical release in 2006 before finding a cult audience on home video, and was followed by two sequels, Feast II: Sloppy Seconds and Feast III: The Happy Finish.

overview: All the rules are broken as a sect of lawless marauders decides that the annual Purge does not stop at daybreak and instead should never end as they chase a group of immigrants who they want to punish because of their harsh historical past.
tagline: The rules are broken.
title: The Forever Purge
plot:
The Forever Purge is a 2021 American horror film directed by Everardo Gout and written by Rafe Judkins. It is the fifth installment in The Purge franchise, which is based on the concept of James Wan's 2007 film The Conjuring.

The movie takes place four years after the events of The Forever Purge: Eternal Summer (2021). The story begins with a flashback to the aftermath of the previous purge, where we see the aftermath of the violence and destruction caused by the masked figures known as the "Purged." We also meet our protagonist, Naya (played by Ana de la Reguera), who is struggling to cope with the trauma she experienced during the previous purge.

The story then shifts to the present day, where we are introduced to a new family, the Garcias, who are preparing for their own home invasion. The family consists of parents, Alejandro and Marisol (played by Tenoch Huerta and Eva Longoria), and their two children, Carlos and Sofia (played by Jorge Lendeborg Jr. and Angélica Celaya). They are unaware that the government has announced a new policy: if you survive four purges, you will be granted immunity from future invasions.

As the family prepares for their own home invasion, they begin to realize that something is off. The Purged seem more organized and ruthless than ever before, and the Garcias soon find themselves trapped in their own home with no escape. As the night wears on, the family must fight for survival against the increasingly violent and relentless Purged.

Throughout the movie, we see flashbacks of Naya's past experiences during the previous purges, which serve as a reminder of the trauma that the characters are facing. We also see glimpses of the government's true intentions behind the new policy: they want to create a class system where those who survive multiple purges become the ruling elite.

As the night reaches its climax, the Garcias must confront their own demons and work together to take down the Purged. In a shocking twist, we discover that Naya is actually one of the leaders of the Purged, and she has been manipulating events from behind the scenes.

The movie ends with a sense of hopelessness and despair, as the Garcias are forced to confront the reality of their situation. The final shot is of Naya, standing alone in the darkness, her mask still on, as we realize that the cycle of violence and trauma will continue forever.

Overall, The Forever Purge is a thought-provoking and intense horror film that explores themes of class, privilege, and the cyclical nature of violence. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and atmospheric tension, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and horror enthusiasts alike.

overview: To get revenge on her ex-boyfriend, an influencer attempts to transform an unpopular classmate into prom king.
tagline: It's his turn for a makeover.
title: He's All That
plot:
He's All That is a 2021 American teen romantic comedy film directed by Mark Waters and written by R. Lee Fleming Jr., a gender-swapped remake of the 1999 film She's All That, which was itself a modern take on George Bernard Shaw's Pygmalion. Social media personality Addison Rae makes her film debut as Padgett Sawyer, with Tanner Buchanan as Cameron Kweller, Madison Pettis, Peyton Meyer, and Rachael Leigh Cook and Matthew Lillard, stars of the original film, in new roles. It was released on Netflix on 27 August 2021.

Padgett is a popular high school senior and lifestyle influencer who lives with her divorced mother, a nurse, and hides her modest circumstances from her followers and sponsors by pretending to live in an upscale home. When she catches her boyfriend, the influencer and aspiring rapper Jordan Van Draanen, cheating on her with a backup dancer, her furious reaction is broadcast in a live stream, and she loses followers and sponsorship deals.

To restore her reputation, Padgett accepts a bet from her friend Alden to turn Cameron, an antisocial photographer and the school's least popular boy, into prom king. Cameron is indifferent to her, but she learns about him from his younger sister, Brin, and persuades him to give her horse-riding lessons. As she works to change his appearance and social life, Padgett grows close to Cameron, learning that he and Brin lost their mother in a plane crash and live with their grandmother while their father works abroad. Cameron, in turn, begins to see the real person behind Padgett's online persona. But as their feelings deepen and prom approaches, Jordan tries to win Padgett back, and the revelation of the bet threatens to destroy the trust between them, forcing Padgett to decide what matters more to her: her image or her authenticity.

He's All That received negative reviews, with a 28 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes; the consensus faulted the lack of chemistry between its stars and its failure to improve on the original. Rae's performance was widely criticized, and she received a Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Actress, although the film attracted large viewership on Netflix.

overview: The Planet Express crew return from cancellation, only to be robbed blind by hideous "sprunging" scam artists.  Things go from bad to worse when the scammers hack Bender, start traveling through time, and take Earth over entirely!  Will the crew be able to save the day, or will Bender's larcenous tendencies and their general incompetence doom them all?
tagline: Just when you thought it was safe to watch something else!
title: Futurama: Bender's Big Score
plot:
Futurama: Bender's Big Score is a direct-to-video film that serves as a pilot for the series, released in 2007. The movie follows the story of Bender, a bending unit who gets caught up in a plot to steal a valuable artifact.

The main themes of Futurama: Bender's Big Score include:

1. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The movie explores Bender's struggle with his own identity as a bending unit. He is torn between his loyalty to his friends and his desire for independence, leading him to question his purpose in life.
2. **Loyalty and Friendship**: The film highlights the strong bond between Bender and his friends, particularly Fry, Leela, and Professor Farnsworth. Despite their differences, they work together to overcome challenges and protect each other.
3. **Power and Corruption**: The plot revolves around a powerful artifact that could grant immense power to its owner. This theme serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the corrupting influence of power.
4. **Nostalgia and Retro-Futurism**: The movie pays homage to classic science fiction films from the 1950s and 1960s, such as Flash Gordon and Buck Rogers in the 25th Century. This retro-futuristic aesthetic adds to the film's humor and charm.

The story begins with Bender getting caught up in a plot by his nemesis, Kif Kroker, who is working for an alien named Zapp Brannigan. The artifact, known as the "Big Score," has the power to grant immense wealth and power to its owner. As Bender navigates this complex web of intrigue, he must confront his own identity and loyalties.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various challenges and obstacles, including a showdown with Zapp Brannigan's rival, Professor Hubert J. Farnsworth. In the end, Bender and his friends successfully retrieve the Big Score, but not before it is revealed that Kif was working for Zapp all along.

The ending of the movie sets the stage for the rest of the series, as Fry, Leela, and Bender return to their normal lives in New New York City. However, the experience has left a lasting impact on Bender, who begins to question his place in the world and his relationships with those around him.

Overall, Futurama: Bender's Big Score is a humorous and action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, loyalty, power, and nostalgia.

original_title: ゴジラ ファイナルウォーズ
overview: Humanity final rids themselves of Godzilla, in-prisoning him in an icy tomb at the South Pole. All is peaceful until various monsters emerge to lay waste to Earth's cities. Overwhelmed, humanity is seemingly saved by a race of benevolent aliens known as  Xiliens. But not all is what it seems with these bizarre visitors. If humanity wishes to survive they must reluctantly resurrect their most hated enemy, Godzilla.
tagline: Farewell, Godzilla.
title: Godzilla: Final Wars
plot:
Godzilla: Final Wars is a 2004 Japanese science fiction kaiju film directed by Ryuhei Kitamura and produced by Toho. The movie serves as the final installment in the Heisei series, concluding the story arc of the Godzilla franchise.

The main theme of Godzilla: Final Wars revolves around the consequences of humanity's reckless pursuit of technological advancement and its disregard for nature. The film depicts a future where humans have colonized other planets, but their actions ultimately lead to the destruction of the Earth. The movie portrays a world where corporations and governments prioritize profits over environmental concerns, leading to catastrophic consequences.

The story also explores the theme of existentialism, as humanity is forced to confront its own mortality and the fragility of life on Earth. The film's portrayal of an apocalyptic future serves as a warning about the dangers of unchecked technological progress and the importance of living in harmony with nature.

Furthermore, Godzilla: Final Wars can be seen as a commentary on the human condition, particularly in regards to war and conflict. The movie depicts a world where nations and corporations engage in destructive wars, leading to devastating consequences for humanity and the planet. This serves as a critique of the destructive nature of human conflict and the importance of finding peaceful solutions to resolve disputes.

Overall, Godzilla: Final Wars is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas, leaving viewers with a lasting impression of the consequences of humanity's actions.

overview: The true story about legendary explorer Thor Heyerdahl and his epic crossing of the Pacific on a balsa wood raft in 1947, in an effort to prove it was possible for South Americans to settle in Polynesia in pre-Columbian times.
title: Kon-Tiki
plot:
Kon-Tiki is an adventure drama film that tells the story of Thor Heyerdahl's historic 1947 expedition to sail a raft from South America to Polynesia. The movie explores several themes, primarily centered around human resilience, determination, and the power of nature.

At its core, Kon-Tiki is a testament to the human spirit's ability to overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges. The film follows Thor Heyerdahl, played by Pål Sverre Hagen, as he embarks on an incredible journey with his crew, facing treacherous seas, scorching sun, and personal conflicts along the way.

One of the primary themes is the relationship between humans and nature. As the crew navigates the vast Pacific Ocean, they are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities in the face of the unforgiving environment. The film highlights the delicate balance between human ingenuity and the natural world, showcasing both the beauty and brutality of the ocean.

The movie also delves into themes of exploration, discovery, and cultural exchange. Heyerdahl's expedition was not just a scientific endeavor but also a journey of self-discovery and cultural curiosity. As he encounters various island cultures, he is struck by their similarities to his own Norwegian heritage, sparking questions about identity, belonging, and the shared human experience.

Furthermore, Kon-Tiki touches on the idea of perseverance and the importance of teamwork. The crew faces numerous setbacks and disagreements, but ultimately, they come together to overcome their differences and achieve a common goal. This camaraderie is forged in the face of adversity, demonstrating that even in the most challenging situations, human connection can be a powerful force for survival.

Overall, Kon-Tiki is a film about the human condition, exploring our capacity for resilience, adaptability, and connection with the world around us.

original_title: LEGO Marvel Super Heroes: Black Panther - Trouble in Wakanda
overview: After speaking at the Wakanda Embassy, Black Panther fights Thanos and fends him off with the help of fellow Avengers Captain America, Thor, Iron Man, Hulk, and Black Widow. After regaining conscious, Thanos is approached by Erik Killmonger and Ulysses Klaue in a plot where they will obtain the Vibranium in Wakanda to empower Thanos. When Black Panther discovers this plot, he must work with Shuri, Okoye, and the Avengers to defeat them.
title: LEGO Marvel Super Heroes: Black Panther - Trouble in Wakanda
plot:
LEGO Marvel Super Heroes: Black Panther – Trouble in Wakanda is a 2018 American animated superhero special produced by Lego and Marvel Entertainment, with animation by Pure Imagination Studios. Directed by Michael Black and written by Mark Hoffmeier, with Stan Lee among its producers, it is a playful Lego reimagining of Black Panther and Avengers: Infinity War. The voice cast features James C. Mathis III as T'Challa / Black Panther, Keston John as Erik Killmonger, Daisy Lightfoot as Shuri, Yvette Nicole Brown as Okoye, Trevor Devall as Ulysses Klaue and Isaac C. Singleton Jr. as Thanos, with Mick Wingert as Iron Man, Travis Willingham as Thor, Roger Craig Smith as Captain America, Laura Bailey as Black Widow, Fred Tatasciore as Hulk and Liam O'Brien as Doctor Strange.

Being king of Wakanda is hard work, especially when the king is also the Black Panther. After T'Challa gives a speech at the Wakanda Embassy, Thanos arrives from outer space threatening to destroy Earth, and Black Panther leaps into action, driving off the Mad Titan with the help of fellow Avengers Captain America, Thor, Iron Man, Hulk and Black Widow. The weakened Thanos regains consciousness only to be approached by the rogue villains Killmonger and Klaue, who propose a plan to seize the vibranium hidden in Wakanda and use it to restore his power. To reach it, Klaue kidnaps T'Challa's sister Shuri, and Black Panther teams up with his loyal bodyguard Okoye to rescue her by braving Wakanda's dangerous Maze of Tal-Recs. Sneaking into the vibranium mine, the pair discover that Killmonger and Klaue have already used the precious metal to recharge Thanos, who is now stronger than ever. With his homeland in danger, Black Panther must join forces with Shuri, Okoye and the Avengers to defeat the villains before Wakanda is destroyed.

The special was made up of five shorts, "Speeches & Sandwiches", "Something Strange", "The Maze of Tal-Recs", "Mining Mayhem" and "Vibranium Vengeance", which were released one by one on Marvel's YouTube channel Marvel HQ in May and June 2018. The complete 22-minute compilation premiered on Disney XD in early June 2018.

overview: Hondo Harrelson recruits Jim Street to join an elite unit of the Los Angeles Police Department. Together they seek out more members, including tough Deke Kay and single mom Chris Sanchez. The team's first big assignment is to escort crime boss Alex Montel to prison. It seems routine, but when Montel offers a huge reward to anyone who can break him free, criminals of various stripes step up for the prize.
tagline: You're either S.W.A.T. or you're not.
title: S.W.A.T.
plot:
S.W.A.T. is a 2003 American action film directed by Tony Scott, starring Keanu Reeves, Samuel L. Jackson, and Lindsay Lohan.

The movie begins with the introduction of Chris Sanders (Keanu Reeves), a former Marine who joins the Los Angeles Police Department's Special Weapons and Tactics team, also known as S.W.A.T. The team is led by Lieutenant Dan 'Hondo' Harrelson (Samuel L. Jackson), a seasoned veteran with a no-nonsense attitude.

The story takes a turn when Chris is paired with rookie officer Trudy Shaw (Lindsay Lohan) and the two begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their budding relationship is put to the test as they face various challenges on the job.

One of the main plot points revolves around a wealthy businessman named Robert Hawkins (Owen Wilson), who has been kidnapped by a group of terrorists led by Captain Dan 'Mac' MacDougall (Robert Patrick). The team must navigate through the city's streets and buildings to rescue Hawkins, while also dealing with their own personal demons.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Hawkins is not just any ordinary hostage. He possesses information about a deadly virus that could potentially wipe out millions of people. The terrorists plan to use this information to hold the world hostage and demand a massive ransom in exchange for Hawkins' safe return.

The S.W.A.T. team must work together to stop the terrorists and prevent the spread of the virus. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, rival law enforcement agencies, and personal conflicts within the team.

As the stakes grow higher, Chris and Trudy find themselves in a cat-and-mouse game with Mac and his accomplices. The action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with intense shootouts, car chases, and hand-to-hand combat sequences.

In the end, the S.W.A.T. team manages to rescue Hawkins and prevent the virus from being released. However, not before several characters meet their demise, including Mac, who sacrifices himself to save his teammates.

The movie concludes with Chris and Trudy sharing a moment of triumph and intimacy, as they reflect on the events that have transpired. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the S.W.A.T. team standing together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way next.

Overall, S.W.A.T. is an action-packed thrill ride that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, the film has since developed a cult following and remains a beloved entry in the action genre.

overview: Every year, thousands of Antarctica's emperor penguins make an astonishing journey to breed their young. They walk, marching day and night in single file 70 miles into the darkest, driest and coldest continent on Earth.  This amazing, true-life tale is touched with humour and alive with thrills. Breathtaking photography captures the transcendent beauty and staggering drama of devoted parent penguins who, in the fierce polar winter, take turns guarding their egg and trekking to the ocean in search of food. Predators hunt them, storms lash them. But the safety of their adorable chicks makes it all worthwhile. So follow the leader... to adventure!!
production_companies: Buena Vista International Film Production France
tagline: In the harshest place on Earth, love finds a way.
title: March of the Penguins
plot:
March of the Penguins (French: La Marche de l'empereur) is a 2005 French nature documentary written and directed by Luc Jacquet, following the yearly breeding cycle of the emperor penguins of Antarctica. It was filmed over roughly a year by cinematographers Laurent Chalet and Jérôme Maison near the French research station Dumont d'Urville in Adélie Land, and was produced by Bonne Pioche with the participation of National Geographic Films, Wild Bunch, Canal+ and the French polar institute Paul-Émile Victor.

The film opens at the close of the Antarctic summer, when every penguin of breeding age leaves the ocean and walks inland, single file, to an ancestral breeding ground on solid, year-round ice. By the end of winter that site lies more than 100 kilometres from open water. After courtship, each female lays a single egg and passes it to her mate's feet with as little exposure to the cold as possible, then sets off back to the sea to feed, having lost a third of her body weight. The males, who by then have gone two months without food, huddle together through the polar winter to incubate the eggs in temperatures nearing −62 °C, drinking only fallen snow.

When the chicks hatch, the fathers can offer only a small meal secreted from a throat sac, and they must abandon their young if the mothers fail to return. The returning females recognise their families by their calls and take over feeding, while the starving males make the long trek to the ocean. Storms kill some chicks, a grieving mother tries to steal another's young, and predators such as leopard seals and giant petrels take their toll on adults and chicks alike. As spring advances and the ice melts, the trips grow shorter, until the parents finally leave the chicks to fend for themselves.

The original French version is narrated in the first person by Charles Berling and Romane Bohringer as the parent penguins and Jules Sitruk as their chick, with an electronic score by Émilie Simon. The English-language release, acquired at Sundance by National Geographic Films and distributed by Warner Independent Pictures, replaced this with a single third-person narration by Morgan Freeman and a score by Alex Wurman. Made on a budget of about $3.3 million, the film grossed over $127 million worldwide, becoming one of the most successful documentaries ever released in North America and France, and won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature. A sequel, March of the Penguins 2: The Next Step, followed in 2017.

keywords.name: based on song, poem or rhyme

overview: In year 1250 B.C. during the late Bronze age, two emerging nations begin to clash. Paris, the Trojan prince, convinces Helen, Queen of Sparta, to leave her husband Menelaus, and sail with him back to Troy. After Menelaus finds out that his wife was taken by the Trojans, he asks his brother Agamemnom to help him get her back. Agamemnon sees this as an opportunity for power. So they set off with 1,000 ships holding 50,000 Greeks to Troy. With the help of Achilles, the Greeks are able to fight the never before defeated Trojans.
tagline: For passion. For honor. For destiny. For victory. For love.
title: Troy
plot:
Troy is a 2004 epic historical drama film directed by Wolfgang Petersen, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and based on Homer's ancient Greek epic poem, the Iliad. The movie stars Brad Pitt as Achilles, Eric Bana as Hector, and Orlando Bloom as Prince Odysseus.

The film begins with King Agamemnon (Brian Cox), the leader of the Greeks, who is determined to reclaim Helen (Diane Kruger), the wife of King Menelaus (Brendan Gleeson). The Greeks assemble a massive army, led by Achilles, the greatest warrior in Greece. However, their plans are threatened when Agamemnon takes Achilles' war prize, Briseis (Saffron Burrows), as his own concubine.

Achilles is outraged and refuses to fight alongside the Greeks, leading to a rift between him and his comrades. Meanwhile, Prince Odysseus, who has been tasked with infiltrating Troy by disguising himself as a Trojan prince, becomes embroiled in the conflict when he falls in love with Helen.

As the war rages on, Achilles' rage grows, and he seeks revenge against Agamemnon. He kills Agamemnon's brother, King Diomedes (Peter O'Toole), and then sets his sights on Agamemnon himself. However, just as Achilles is about to kill Agamemnon, the god Apollo intervenes, sparing the king's life.

The Trojans, led by Hector, launch a counterattack against the Greeks, and the two armies clash in a series of intense battles. Meanwhile, Odysseus and his men devise a plan to infiltrate Troy by hiding inside a giant wooden horse.

As the war reaches its climax, Achilles' rage is finally satiated when he kills Hector, but not before the Trojan prince's father, King Priam (Boris Kodjoe), comes to Achilles' camp to beg for his son's body. The scene is a poignant moment in the film, as it highlights the humanity of both sides and the devastating consequences of war.

In the end, the Greeks emerge victorious, but at great cost. Odysseus and his men enter Troy by hiding inside the wooden horse, which is then set on fire, allowing them to escape. Achilles' body is taken back to Greece, where he is mourned as a hero.

The film ends with Prince Paris (David Thewlis), who had sparked the war by abducting Helen, being killed by Philoctetes (Dominic West), a Greek warrior. The final shot of the film shows Odysseus standing alone on the beach, reflecting on the cost of war and the futility of human conflict.

Overall, Troy is a visually stunning film that brings to life the epic story of the Trojan War. While it takes some creative liberties with Homer's original tale, the film remains faithful to the spirit of the ancient Greek poem.

overview: David, an orderly at a hospital, tells his horrific story of being kidnapped and forced to play a vile game of survival.
title: Saw
plot: David, an orderly at a hospital, tells his horrific story of being kidnapped and forced to play a vile game of survival.

overview: A look at the life of legendary American pilot Amelia Earhart, who disappeared while flying over the Pacific Ocean in 1937 in an attempt to make a flight around the world.
title: Amelia
plot:
Amelia is a 2009 biographical drama film that tells the story of Amelia Earhart, a pioneering American aviator who disappeared during a record attempt to fly around the world in 1937. The movie delves into the themes of female empowerment, independence, and the struggle for recognition in a male-dominated field.

The film portrays Amelia as a strong-willed and determined individual who defies societal norms to pursue her passion for flying. Her journey is marked by both triumphs and setbacks, including personal losses and professional challenges. As she pushes boundaries and breaks records, Amelia must also navigate the complexities of her own identity and the expectations placed upon her.

One of the central themes of the movie is the tension between freedom and responsibility. Amelia's desire for independence and autonomy often puts her at odds with those around her, including her husband George Putnam, who struggles to balance his own ambitions with his love for Amelia. This conflict serves as a backdrop for exploring the complexities of relationships and the sacrifices that must be made in order to pursue one's dreams.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Amelia navigates the challenges of her career, she must confront her own limitations and vulnerabilities, learning to reconcile her sense of self with the demands placed upon her by others. This journey is marked by moments of introspection and self-doubt, as Amelia grapples with the consequences of her choices and the true cost of her ambitions.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced portrayal of Amelia Earhart as a complex and multifaceted individual, driven by both a desire for adventure and a need for recognition. Through its exploration of these themes, the film offers a powerful tribute to a pioneering figure who continues to inspire generations with her courage and determination.

overview: Whitney Alder owns interior design firm Marietta Designs, which she runs with her friend Andi in the small town of Marietta, Montana. Whitney is designing Santa’s float for the annual Marietta Christmas Parade when a potential job opportunity comes her way: the full redesign of a landmark home by Christmas Eve.
title: A Christmas Miracle for Daisy
plot:
A Christmas Miracle for Daisy is a 2021 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Mike Rohl from a teleplay by J.B. White, adapted from Jane Porter's 2015 novel of the same name, the fifth book in her Taming of the Sheenans series published by Tule. Produced by Brad Krevoy Television and the Motion Picture Corporation of America, with Jill Wagner among its executive producers, it stars Wagner and Nick Bateman, with Tegan Moss, Rubi Tupper, Joe Costa, Andrew Francis, Heather-Claire Nortey and Terence Kelly in supporting roles. Announced in October 2021 as part of GAC Family's Great American Christmas line-up, it premiered on the network on 11 December 2021 and was later distributed on Peacock. It runs 85 minutes.

Whitney Alder (Wagner) owns the interior design firm Marietta Designs, which she runs with her friend Andi (Moss) in the small town of Marietta, Montana. While she is designing Santa's float for the town's annual Christmas parade, a tempting opportunity arrives: the complete redesign of a landmark home, to be finished by Christmas Eve. Despite the tight deadline, Whitney and Andi take the job, only to discover that the house's new owner is Whitney's former boyfriend, Connor Sheenan (Bateman), who has moved to Marietta from Los Angeles with his bright-eyed young daughter, Daisy (Tupper). Connor never intended to become a family man, but when his goddaughter was orphaned he adopted her and committed himself to being a devoted single father.
