Working together in the house brings back a trove of forgotten memories for Whitney and Connor, while Daisy, whose greatest wish is for a mother to complete her family, decides that Whitney is the perfect candidate, leaving it to the season of miracles to bring the former couple a second chance.

Reviews from holiday-film writers were generally warm. Rissi JC of RissiWrites found the film charming, sweet and better than expected, with a fun spin on a familiar trope; she noted that its production values were not quite equal to those of rival networks and praised Wagner while being less convinced by her co-star. Christiana of My Movie Views gave it 7.5 out of 10, calling it an ordinary but enjoyable Christmas film. In Porter's novel the hero is media mogul Cormac Sheenan, and four-year-old Daisy befriends Marietta's seasonal Santa Claus, whom she believes to be the real one.

overview: Trying to reverse a family curse, brothers Jimmy and Clyde Logan set out to execute an elaborate robbery during the legendary Coca-Cola 600 race at the Charlotte Motor Speedway.
tagline: See how the other half steals.
title: Logan Lucky
plot:
Logan Lucky is a 2017 American heist comedy film directed by Steven Soderbergh, marking his return from a self-declared retirement from filmmaking, from a screenplay credited to Rebecca Blunt. Channing Tatum and Adam Driver star as Jimmy and Clyde Logan, brothers from West Virginia, with Riley Keough as their sister, Mellie, Daniel Craig as the safecracker Joe Bang, Katie Holmes, Seth MacFarlane, Katherine Waterston, Hilary Swank, Sebastian Stan and Dwight Yoakam. Soderbergh distributed the film independently through his company Fingerprint Releasing, in partnership with Bleecker Street.

Jimmy, a former high school football star whose career was ended by a knee injury, is fired from his construction job in the tunnels beneath the Charlotte Motor Speedway because his old injury was not disclosed. He dotes on his young daughter, Sadie, who competes in beauty pageants and lives with his ex-wife, Bobbie Jo, and her wealthy new husband, who are planning to move away. Jimmy's brother, Clyde, an Iraq War veteran who lost part of his arm, tends a local bar, and the family is said to be cursed by bad luck. After a confrontation with an obnoxious NASCAR team owner, Max Chilblain, Jimmy reveals his plan to rob the speedway by exploiting what he knows about the pneumatic tube system used to move cash to its vault.

The Logans recruit Mellie and Joe Bang, an imprisoned explosives expert, along with his dim-witted brothers, Sam and Fish. Their scheme requires breaking Joe out of prison and returning him before anyone notices, so Clyde deliberately gets himself sent to the same prison. On the day of the Coca-Cola 600, one of the busiest races of the year, the gang carries out the heist, improvising around obstacles that include a prison riot staged as a diversion. Weeks later, the FBI agent Sarah Grayson investigates the robbery, but the case appears to have been solved, and the twists of the Logans' plan gradually come to light.

Logan Lucky received positive reviews for its humor, performances and clever plotting, with critics likening it to a rural counterpart of Soderbergh's Ocean's Eleven. It grossed about $48 million worldwide. Speculation that "Rebecca Blunt" was a pseudonym, possibly for Soderbergh's wife, Jules Asner, persisted after release.

overview: Corporate downsizing expert Ryan Bingham spends his life in planes, airports, and hotels, but just as he’s about to reach a milestone of ten million frequent flyer miles, he meets a woman who causes him to rethink his transient life.
tagline: The story of a man ready to make a connection.
title: Up in the Air
plot:
Up in the Air is a 2009 American comedy-drama film directed by Jason Reitman, produced by Gary Goetzman and Steven Haft, and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

The main themes of Up in the Air revolve around:

1. **Existentialism and Meaning**: The protagonist, Ryan Bingham (played by George Clooney), is a corporate downsizer who travels the country firing people for a living. As he navigates his job and personal life, he begins to question the meaning of his existence and the purpose of his actions.

2. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Ryan's character is portrayed as a loner, who has given up on relationships and intimacy. His interactions with others are often superficial, and he struggles to form genuine connections with people.

3. **The American Dream**: The film critiques the idea of the American Dream, which promises success, happiness, and fulfillment through hard work and material possessions. Ryan's character is a product of this system, but he begins to realize that it may not be as fulfilling as he thought.

4. **Mortality and Impermanence**: As Ryan travels from city to city, he encounters people who are facing their own mortality, whether due to illness, job loss, or personal struggles. This theme serves as a reminder of the impermanence of life and the importance of living in the present.

5. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Through his relationships with Natalie (played by Vera Farmiga) and Alex (played by Anna Kendrick), Ryan begins to develop empathy and understanding for others, which challenges his initial cynicism and loneliness.

The film's themes are expertly woven throughout the narrative, creating a complex and thought-provoking story that explores the human condition.

overview: A terminally ill mother invites her family to their country house for one final gathering, but tensions quickly boil over between her two daughters.
title: Blackbird
plot:
Blackbird is a 2019 American thriller film directed by Moraiz Guedes. The movie revolves around a young woman named Maya who discovers that her mother, a former CIA operative, has been hiding secrets about their family's past and the true nature of her work.

The main theme of Blackbird is the exploration of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between truth and deception. As Maya delves deeper into her mother's past, she uncovers a complex web of lies and half-truths that challenge everything she thought she knew about herself and her family. The film raises questions about the nature of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and the stories we tell ourselves.

Throughout the movie, the theme of loyalty is also explored, particularly in the context of Maya's relationship with her mother. As Maya navigates the truth about her mother's past, she must confront the consequences of her own loyalty to her family and the moral compromises that come with it.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. Maya's journey is marked by a series of revelations that force her to confront the dark secrets of her family's past and the emotional scars that have been passed down through generations.

Overall, Blackbird is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes of identity, loyalty, and truth, raising questions about the nature of reality and the power of storytelling.

original_title: The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines
overview: After retrieving the Crystal Skull in Utah, Flynn Carsen receives a map in the mail with the secret location of King Solomon's Mines. When the scroll is stolen, Judson explains the power of the Key of Solomon's book and assigns Flynn to retrieve the map. The map is useless without the legend piece to decipher it, which is located in Volubilis near the Roman ruins in Morocco. Flynn heads to Casablanca to the ruins where he is chased by a group of mercenaries leaded by General Samir. They too want to find the location of King Solomon's mines. Flynn teams-up with Professor Emily Davenport working in the dig and they escape from General Samir and his men. While traveling to Gedi, they save the local Jomo from death and the trio faces a dangerous journey through the wild Africa.
title: The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines
plot:
The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines is an action-adventure film that delves into the realm of ancient mythology and treasure hunting. At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and the unrelenting pursuit of knowledge and power.

The protagonist, Flynn Carsen (played by Noah Wyle), is a modern-day librarian who finds himself entangled in a world of adventure and danger. His quest for the legendary mines of King Solomon becomes an all-consuming passion that drives him to risk everything. As he navigates treacherous landscapes and battles formidable foes, Flynn's obsession with uncovering the secrets of the mines serves as a catalyst for his personal growth.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. Throughout his journey, Flynn is forced to confront his own limitations and vulnerabilities, ultimately emerging stronger and more confident. His experiences in the mines serve as a metaphor for the transformative power of knowledge and the importance of embracing one's true nature.

Furthermore, the movie alludes to the idea that power and knowledge can be corrupting forces when left unchecked. The villainous character, Dr. Julia Jones (played by Rebecca Romijn), represents the dangers of ambition and the exploitation of ancient wisdom for personal gain. Her character serves as a foil to Flynn's more noble motivations, highlighting the importance of using one's discoveries for the greater good.

Overall, The Librarian: Return to King Solomon's Mines is a thrilling adventure that explores the complexities of human nature, the allure of power and knowledge, and the transformative potential of self-discovery.

overview: A suburban family is torn apart when fourteen-year-old Annie meets her first boyfriend online. After months of communicating via online chat and phone, Annie discovers her friend is not who he originally claimed to be. Shocked into disbelief, her parents are shattered by their daughter's actions and struggle to support her as she comes to terms with what has happened to her once innocent life.
tagline: What took her family years to build, a stranger stole in an instant.
title: Trust
plot:
Trust (stylised as trust_) is a 2010 American drama thriller directed by David Schwimmer and written by Andy Bellin and Robert Festinger from an uncredited story by Schwimmer. Liana Liberato plays Annie Cameron, with Clive Owen and Catherine Keener as her parents, Will and Lynn, Viola Davis as the counsellor Gail Friedman and Jason Clarke as the FBI agent Doug Tate.

For her fourteenth birthday Annie receives a laptop and soon begins chatting with "Charlie", who first says he is sixteen, then admits to being twenty and later twenty-five. Despite her unease she comes to believe they are in love, and after two months he arranges to meet her at a shopping mall, where she discovers he is a man in his late thirties. Though upset, she lets him persuade her to go to a motel, where he rapes her and films the assault. Her best friend Brittany, who saw them at the mall, alerts the school, and police remove Annie in front of her classmates.

Tate leads the investigation, but when Annie calls Charlie he sees through the trap and cuts contact before he can be traced, and private investigators hired by Will find only a masked address that appears to be in the Czech Republic. Will becomes consumed by the hunt, suffers nightmares about the attack and questions his advertising work, which uses provocative images of teenagers. Annie insists to her counsellor that Charlie loves her. Only when DNA evidence links Charlie to the abuse of several other young girls, and she sees their photographs, does she break down and acknowledge that she was raped. At a school volleyball match, Will attacks a father taking photographs, wrongly believing him to be a registered sex offender, and a humiliated Annie accuses him of ruining her life. After discovering that classmates have been mocking her online with doctored pornographic images and posting her number and address, she tries to kill herself with pills, but Will finds her in time. Brittany stays the night, repairing their friendship, and Will begs Annie's forgiveness for failing to protect her, and she embraces him. A post-credits scene reveals that "Charlie" is a married high school physics teacher named Graham Weston.

Shot in Michigan, it premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2010 and opened in limited release in the United States on April 1, 2011. It received positive reviews, with 79% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Liberato won the Silver Hugo for Best Actress at the Chicago International Film Festival.

overview: Kristen, a troubled young woman, is captured by the police after burning down a farmhouse and is locked in the North Bend Psychiatric Hospital. Soon, she begins to suspect that the place has a dark secret at its core and she's determined to find out what it is.
tagline: Only Sanity Can Keep You Alive!
title: The Ward
plot:
The Ward is a 2010 supernatural horror film that revolves around a young woman's struggle with her dark past and the evil forces that haunt her.

At its core, The Ward explores the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. The protagonist, Amber (played by Lindsay Lohan), is forced to confront her troubled history when she returns to her family's old mansion, only to discover that it holds a malevolent presence that threatens to consume her.

The film delves into the idea of how past experiences can shape our present and future, often in ways we're not aware of. Amber's journey is a metaphor for the struggle to overcome one's demons and break free from the shackles of trauma. As she navigates the treacherous world of ghosts and supernatural entities, she must also confront her own inner demons and learn to face her fears.

The Ward also touches on the theme of isolation and loneliness, highlighting how these emotions can be both a source of strength and weakness. Amber's experiences in the mansion serve as a reminder that even in the most isolated environments, we're never truly alone, and that our past can come back to haunt us at any moment.

Furthermore, the film explores the idea of female empowerment and the struggle for independence. As Amber navigates her way through the supernatural world, she must also assert her own agency and make difficult choices about her future. The Ward suggests that true strength lies in embracing one's vulnerabilities and learning to control one's fears, rather than letting them consume us.

Overall, The Ward is a thought-provoking horror film that explores complex themes of trauma, isolation, and female empowerment, making it a compelling watch for fans of the genre.

overview: When alien invaders capture Earth's superheroes, their kids must learn to work together to save their parents - and the planet.
tagline: Power comes in all sizes.
title: We Can Be Heroes
plot:
We Can Be Heroes is a 2020 American superhero film directed by Robert Rodriguez and written by Carlos Gallardo. The movie takes place after the events of Avengers: Endgame and follows a group of young superheroes as they try to save the world from an alien invasion.

The story begins with a flashback of Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson) explaining that aliens have been monitoring Earth's children for years, looking for one who can be their savior. The chosen child is Alex Owens (Yara Shahidi), a 12-year-old girl who possesses unique abilities. However, she is not the only one; other kids around the world also possess special powers.

The movie then shifts to the present day, where we meet our main characters: Alex's friends and fellow superheroes, including Marcus (Jacob Vargas), Ella (Viola Davis), and Sam (Gael García Bernal). They are all brought together by a mysterious figure known as "The Director" (Rami Malek) who claims to be the leader of an organization called "The Department of Youth."

As The Director explains, the aliens have returned, and their spaceship is heading straight for Earth. However, they need human help to defeat the alien threat. The kids are tasked with stopping the aliens' ship from reaching its destination.

The plot thickens as we learn that each child has a unique power that can be used against the aliens. Alex's power allows her to create force fields, Marcus can turn invisible, Ella can control plants, and Sam can manipulate technology. However, they soon realize that their powers are not enough to defeat the aliens alone.

The kids embark on a journey across the globe, visiting different countries and meeting new allies along the way. They also discover that The Director's true intentions may not be entirely pure, and that he has his own agenda for the children.

As the stakes rise, the kids face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to stop the alien invasion. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, trust, and believing in themselves.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the kids and the aliens. Using their combined powers, they manage to defeat the aliens and save the world. However, not without some sacrifices and unexpected twists along the way.

In the end, The Director's true identity is revealed, and it turns out that he was once a superhero himself who had been thought to be dead. He has been searching for a new generation of heroes to carry on his legacy.

The movie concludes with Alex and her friends being hailed as heroes, but also realizing that their journey is far from over. They have saved the world, but there are still many challenges ahead, and they must continue to work together to protect it.

Overall, We Can Be Heroes is a heartwarming and action-packed film that celebrates the power of teamwork, friendship, and believing in oneself.

overview: The "Academy Island Incident" in which four "kings" cross paths... Since then, Silver Clansmen Kuroh Yatogami and Neko have been searching for their master, Shiro. Without finding any clues to Shiro's whereabouts, the two became disheartened. However, one day, they see HOMRA members Rikio Kamamoto and Anna Kushina being chased by someone.
title: K: Missing Kings
plot:
K: Missing Kings is a 2014 Japanese animated urban fantasy film directed by Shingo Suzuki, a sequel to the television anime K created by the writing collective GoRA. Set around a year after the events of the series, it bridges the first season and the second, K: Return of Kings. The Japanese voice cast includes Daisuke Namikawa, Daisuke Ono, Tomokazu Sugita, Mikako Komatsu, Kenjiro Tsuda, Takahiro Sakurai and Yui Horie, who voices the young girl Anna and also sings the insert song "Flames of Red". The music is by Mikio Endo.

The world of K is governed by seven Kings, each leading a clan of followers with supernatural powers. Almost a year has passed since the so-called Academy Island Incident, in which four of the Kings crossed paths and Mikoto Suoh, the Red King, was killed. His clan, HOMRA, has fallen into disarray, with several members gone their separate ways and Yata unable to let go of the past. Kuroh Yatogami and Neko, followers of the Silver King, have spent months searching without success for their missing master, Shiro, and are losing heart.

One day the two see HOMRA's Rikio Kamamoto and Anna Kushina being chased. The pursuers belong to the Green Clan, whose King sees the Silver King as the greatest threat to his plans and wants to kidnap Anna, believing that her gift for locating people will reveal whether Shiro is still alive and where he is. Defending her, Kuroh discovers that one of the Green Clan's most dangerous fighters, the flamboyant swordsman Yukari, was a fellow disciple of his former master, a man he once looked up to as an older brother. While Kuroh, Neko and Yata fight to rescue Anna, the Blue King's organisation, Scepter 4, mobilises around the domain of the absent Gold King. Captured and grieving, Anna finally accepts her destiny and awakens as the new Red King, uniting what remains of HOMRA, and a meeting with the Blue King brings Mikoto's story to a close.

The film premiered in July 2014 at Anime Expo in Los Angeles and Japan Expo in Paris before opening in Japanese cinemas on 12 July, and grossed about $826,000. Viz Media later released it in North America with an English dub that brought back the voice cast of the series. Reviews were mixed: Anime News Network praised Anna's awakening and the dynamic action scenes but found the plot thin, the Village Voice judged it a film for diehard fans, and the Los Angeles Times called it a hot mess.

overview: Before being extradited to Africa to stand trial, a notorious Belgian criminal is entrusted to the Marseilles police department for less than 24 hours. But the wily crook convinces bumbling policeman Emilien he's a lowly Belgian embassy employee who got railroaded by the brilliant master criminal.
title: Taxi 4
plot:
Taxi 4, stylized T4XI, is a 2007 French action comedy directed by Gérard Krawczyk from a screenplay by producer Luc Besson, the fourth installment of the Taxi series after Taxi 3 (2003). Samy Naceri returns as Marseille taxi driver Daniel Morales, now driving a Peugeot 407, alongside Frédéric Diefenthal as hapless policeman Émilien Coutant-Kerbalec, Bernard Farcy as Commissioner Gibert, Emma Sjöberg as Petra and Jean-Christophe Bouvet as General Bertineau, with footballer Djibril Cissé as himself.

With all of Marseille obsessed with football, Daniel races the newly signed Cissé to the stadium. Soon after, Gibert's squad is assigned to hold a notorious Belgian bank robber wanted by Interpol, Albert Van den Bosch, for a few hours before his transfer to the Congo to stand trial. Their bungling begins at once: they arrive late at the airport and wreck their own convoy. Meanwhile Daniel leaves his son, Léo, and Émilien's son, Maxime, at the station, where the boys unwittingly help one of the robber's accomplices alter his file on Gibert's computer. During the prisoner's processing, Gibert knocks himself out with a tranquilizer dart meant for bears, and Émilien, fooled by the doctored wanted notice and a phone call to a gang member, releases the Belgian, who promptly hails Daniel's taxi.

Fired by Gibert, Émilien turns to Daniel, who remembers where he dropped off his passenger. They follow the gang to Monaco, where the Belgian robs a bank after taking the place of his timid twin brother, Édouard, and they discover that Petra, Émilien's wife, has infiltrated the gang undercover to retrieve compromising documents from one of the vaults. Gibert's men arrest the innocent twin instead, while the real robber escapes toward Cannes to the lavish villa of a Colombian former associate. Émilien is captured sneaking in, and Petra must stall for time until Gibert's assault team storms the villa. Launched over the wall, the commissioner lands in a pile of cocaine and goes on a deranged shooting spree with assault rifles and a rocket launcher, before Daniel drives his taxi into the living room, locks the robber in the trunk and rescues the couple. Petra's mission succeeds, and a still-intoxicated Gibert ends up on the pitch at a Marseille match.

Released in France in February 2007, the film drew more than 4.5 million admissions there. Critics and audiences panned it, faulting its thin plot, slack pacing and lack of the car chases that had defined the earlier films.

overview: An assassin is shot by her ruthless employer, Bill, and other members of their assassination circle – but she lives to plot her vengeance.
tagline: A roaring rampage of revenge.
title: Kill Bill: Vol. 1
plot:
Kill Bill: Vol. 1 is a 2003 martial arts film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. The movie follows the story of Beatrix "Black Mamba" Kiddo (Uma Thurman), a former assassin who seeks revenge against her former boss, Bill (David Carradine), and his team of assassins.

The film begins with Kiddo, once a member of Bill's Deadly Viper Assassination Squad (DVAS), being betrayed by Bill and left for dead after their mission in Mexico. She is found by a group of people who are trying to help her recover from her injuries, but she eventually escapes and sets out on a journey to track down Bill and his team.

As Kiddo navigates through the world of assassins, she encounters various characters who aid or hinder her progress. One such character is O-Ren Ishii (Lucy Liu), a former DVAS member who has become a powerful crime lord in Tokyo. Kiddo seeks revenge against O-Ren for killing her lover, Vernita Green (Vivica A. Fox).

Kiddo's journey takes her to various locations, including Tokyo and Hanoi, where she faces off against O-Ren's henchmen and eventually confronts O-Ren herself. The two engage in a fierce battle, but Kiddo ultimately emerges victorious.

Meanwhile, Bill is also dealing with his own demons as he tries to come to terms with his past actions. He is haunted by the memories of his time with Kiddo and the events that led to her betrayal. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Bill's motivations for betraying Kiddo were not entirely malicious, but rather a result of his own emotional turmoil.

Throughout the film, Tarantino pays homage to classic martial arts movies and anime, incorporating references to Hong Kong cinema and Japanese culture into the narrative. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, with Kiddo showcasing her impressive fighting skills.

The movie ends on a cliffhanger, setting up the events of Kill Bill: Vol. 2. Kiddo is left for dead once again, but this time she is found by a mysterious figure who seems to be working against her interests. The stage is set for the final confrontation between Kiddo and Bill, which will determine the fate of both characters.

Overall, Kill Bill: Vol. 1 is a stylish and action-packed film that explores themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption. With its intricate plot and memorable characters, it has become a cult classic among fans of martial arts cinema.

overview: Mater, the rusty but trusty tow truck from Cars, spends a day in Radiator Springs playing scary pranks on his fellow townsfolk. That night at Flo's V8 Café, the Sheriff tells the story of the legend of the Ghostlight, and as everyone races home Mater is left alone primed for a good old-fashioned scare.
title: Mater and the Ghostlight
plot:
Mater and the Ghostlight is a 2006 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and directed by John Lasseter and Dan Scanlon. Set in the world of Cars, it stars Larry the Cable Guy as the tow truck Mater, with Owen Wilson as Lightning McQueen, Bonnie Hunt as Sally, Paul Newman as Doc Hudson and Michael Wallis as the Sheriff. It was released as a special feature on the DVD of Cars in November 2006 and became a forerunner of the Cars Toons series of shorts centered on Mater.

Some time after the events of Cars, Mater has been playing pranks on the residents of Radiator Springs, among them moving Red's flowers, leaping out from a stack of tires to startle Guido and Luigi, dressing up as a traffic-cone vampire to frighten Sally, and hiding behind a pile of cans to scare Lightning, who is fooled by one of Mater's signs. Pleased with himself, Mater teases Lightning as if he had seen the Ghostlight, a legendary spirit said to haunt the area.

The Sheriff scolds Mater for making fun of the legend. Mater dismisses the Ghostlight as a myth, but the Sheriff gathers the townsfolk and solemnly tells the tale of a young couple who vanished after encountering the glowing blue orb, leaving nothing behind but two out-of-state license plates. He adds that the Ghostlight hates the sound of clanking metal. Terrified, Mater realizes that he himself clanks with every movement and cannot stop. As the residents say good night and switch off their lights, Mater is left alone in the darkness, jumping at every sound. When a blue light appears behind him, he flees in a frantic chase through the desert, unaware that his friends have hung a lantern on his tow hook to get him back for his pranks. The town gathers to laugh at Mater's panic, but in the closing moments, a mysterious blue light appears in the desert, suggesting that the legend may be true after all.

The short was well received as a playful, spooky addition to the Cars franchise, drawing on Route 66 folklore and the friendship between Mater and Lightning that was central to the feature film.

overview: Constructed from over 500 hours of never-before-seen footage, this documentary centers on the personal life and career of the controversial football player Diego Maradona who played for SSC Napoli and Argentina in the 1980s.
tagline: Rebel. Hero. Hustler. God.
title: Diego Maradona
plot:
Diego Maradona is a 2019 biographical drama film directed by Asif Kapadia, produced by Film4 Productions, and starring Édgar Ramírez as Diego Maradona. 

The main themes of the movie are:

1. The struggle with addiction: The film portrays Maradona's struggles with cocaine addiction, which had a significant impact on his life and career.
2. Family dynamics: The movie explores Maradona's complicated relationship with his father, Diego Sr., who was also his coach, and his mother, Dalma.
3. Football as a source of identity: The film highlights how football became Maradona's escape from his troubled past and a means to prove himself on the international stage.
4. Personal demons vs. professional success: As Maradona's career soared, he struggled with personal issues that threatened to derail his life, including addiction and family problems.

The movie follows Maradona's journey from his early days as a young footballer in Argentina to his rise to fame as one of the greatest players of all time, culminating in his infamous handball goal against England in the 1986 World Cup.

overview: In a countryside town bordering on a magical land, a young man makes a promise to his beloved that he'll retrieve a fallen star by venturing into the magical realm. His journey takes him into a world beyond his wildest dreams and reveals his true identity.
tagline: This Summer A Star Falls. The Chase Begins.
title: Stardust
plot:
Stardust is a 2007 fantasy adventure film directed by Matthew Vaughn, produced by Paramount Pictures, and based on the novel of the same name by Neil Gaiman.

The main themes of Stardust include:

1. **Love and Sacrifice**: The story revolves around Tristan (played by Charlie Cox), who sets out to retrieve a fallen star for his beloved, Victoria (played by Claire Danes). His journey is motivated by his love for her and his willingness to risk everything to be with her.
2. **Self-Discovery**: As Tristan navigates the magical world of Faerie, he encounters various characters who challenge his perceptions and force him to confront his own identity. He learns valuable lessons about courage, loyalty, and the importance of staying true to oneself.
3. **Good vs. Evil**: The film features a clear distinction between good and evil, with Tristan's quest representing the struggle between light and darkness. The villainous King Zed (played by Jason Flemyng) embodies the forces of darkness, while the benevolent characters, such as Captain Shakespeare (played by Robert De Niro), represent the power of good.
4. **Coming of Age**: Stardust can be seen as a classic coming-of-age story, where Tristan transitions from adolescence to adulthood. His journey is marked by trials and tribulations that test his resolve and help him grow into a confident, self-assured individual.

The film's themes are woven throughout the narrative, creating a rich tapestry of emotions, action, and adventure. The movie's success lies in its ability to balance lighthearted humor with deeper emotional resonance, making it a beloved classic among fantasy fans.

overview: A former professional dancer volunteers to teach dance in the New York public school system and, while his background first clashes with his students' tastes, together they create a completely new style of dance. Based on the story of ballroom dancer, Pierre Dulane.
tagline: Never Follow
title: Take the Lead
plot:
Take the Lead is a 2006 American romantic drama film directed by Elizabeth Chase and starring Antonio Banderas, Rob Brown, and Yaya DaCosta.

The main themes of Take the Lead revolve around:

1. **Self-discovery**: The movie follows the journey of Pierre Dulaine (Antonio Banderas), a dance instructor who is hired to teach dance at an underprivileged high school in Harlem. As he works with his students, particularly Mauro (Rob Brown), he discovers his own passion for teaching and finds a new sense of purpose.

2. **Empowerment**: The film highlights the transformative power of dance as a means of self-expression and empowerment. Through dance, the characters are able to overcome their personal struggles, build confidence, and find their voice.

3. **Cultural exchange**: Take the Lead celebrates the beauty of different cultures through dance. Pierre Dulaine introduces his students to various styles of dance, including salsa, tango, and contemporary, which helps them appreciate the diversity of music and movement from around the world.

4. **Mentorship**: The movie explores the mentorship between Pierre Dulaine and Mauro, as well as other characters in the school. Their relationships serve as a catalyst for growth, learning, and personal development.

5. **Overcoming adversity**: The film tackles issues such as poverty, racism, and social inequality, highlighting the challenges faced by the students at the high school. Through Pierre's guidance and their collective efforts, they learn to overcome these obstacles and find hope in their lives.

Overall, Take the Lead is a heartwarming story about self-discovery, empowerment, and the transformative power of dance and mentorship.

overview: Hotel night clerk Bart Bromley is a highly intelligent young man on the Autism spectrum. When a woman is murdered during his shift, Bart becomes the prime suspect. As the police investigation closes in, Bart makes a personal connection with a beautiful guest named Andrea, but soon realises he must stop the real murderer before she becomes the next victim.
tagline: Someone's always watching.
title: The Night Clerk
plot:
The Night Clerk is a 2020 American crime drama film written and directed by Michael Cristofer. It stars Tye Sheridan as Bart Bromley, a hotel night clerk who becomes the center of a murder investigation, with Ana de Armas as Andrea Rivera, John Leguizamo as Detective Espada, Helen Hunt as Bart's mother Ethel and Johnathon Schaech as Detective Nick Perretti.

Bart, a young man with Asperger syndrome who lives with his mother, works the night shift at a hotel, where he secretly places cameras in a guest room and studies the recordings to imitate the speech and mannerisms of the guests and overcome his social awkwardness. One night, after his shift, he watches from home as a new guest, Karen, lets a man into her room, argues with him and is beaten. Seeing a gun fall from her purse, Bart races back to the hotel. Soon after, his co-worker Jack hears a gunshot and finds Karen dead with Bart sitting on the bed. While Jack calls 911, Bart removes his cameras but leaves behind a storage card. Questioned by Detective Espada, Bart claims he returned to the hotel for his forgotten wallet, a lie Espada sees through because Bart had just bought ice cream. Reviewing his recording, Bart notices that the killer had a bird tattoo on his arm.

Reassigned to another hotel, Bart meets Andrea Rivera, a guest who recognizes his condition and flirts with him. He hides cameras in her room, and they share a kiss by the pool. Smitten, he gets a haircut, a new suit and a new car, but then sees Andrea in bed with the man with the bird tattoo. The police seize his equipment, though Bart has kept a hidden copy of the recording of Karen's room. The man is Karen's husband, Nick, a detective having an affair with Andrea, who wants her to get rid of Bart. When Bart sees Nick beating Andrea on camera, he rushes to help and shows her the recording proving that Nick killed Karen. She weeps and falls asleep in his bed, but the next morning she is gone with the hard drive, leaving behind Karen's gun. As Andrea and Nick drive out of town, the police find that Bart has left the gun, the camera storage cards and a note for Espada, and the couple are pulled over. Bart walks through a mall, practising the conversational skills he has learned from his recordings.

Saban Films released The Night Clerk on February 21, 2020, and it reached Netflix's Top Ten after arriving on the service in June. Reviews were unfavorable, with 34% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44.

overview: Leonard is an English tailor who used to craft suits on London’s world-famous Savile Row. After a personal tragedy, he’s ended up in Chicago, operating a small tailor shop in a rough part of town where he makes beautiful clothes for the only people around who can afford them: a family of vicious gangsters.
tagline: Everyone has something up their sleeve.
title: The Outfit
plot:
The Outfit is a 2022 American crime thriller and the directing debut of Graham Moore, who wrote it with Johnathan McClain. Mark Rylance stars as an English tailor whose shop serves Chicago gangsters, with Zoey Deutch, Johnny Flynn, Dylan O'Brien, Nikki Amuka-Bird and Simon Russell Beale in supporting roles.

In Chicago in 1956, Leonard Burling, a bespoke cutter who once had a shop on Savile Row, works in a neighborhood run by Irish mob boss Roy Boyle. Roy's son Richie and his enforcer Francis use the shop as a drop for cash and messages, and Leonard puts up with it because the gangsters are his best customers. His receptionist, Mable, with whom he shares a complicated bond, is Richie's girlfriend. One night Francis brings in Richie, shot in a clash with the rival LaFontaine family, and forces Leonard to stitch him up and hide a case holding an FBI surveillance tape. The tape came from the Outfit, the national crime syndicate, and Richie believes it will expose the informant in their ranks.

Over one long night, Leonard sets the gangsters against each other. He nudges Richie to suspect Francis, who then kills Richie. Leonard and Francis lie to Roy about where his son is, and Leonard distracts the boss with the story of how his wife and daughter died in a fire in London. Mable is the real informant, and Leonard persuades Francis to betray Roy to LaFontaine so he can take over. When LaFontaine turns out to be a woman, Violet, Leonard warns her and her guards shoot Francis. She leaves with a tape that is a decoy. Leonard reveals that he planted fake Outfit messages and that the real FBI recorder in the shop captured the whole night. He gives the recording to Mable to deliver and tells her to keep the money. As he sets fire to the shop, a wounded Francis attacks him. Leonard admits he was once an enforcer himself, whose old gang killed his family, and kills Francis with his shears before walking away in a new suit.

The film was shot in March and April 2021 at the Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre near London, with cinematographer Dick Pope, editor William Goldenberg and composer Alexandre Desplat. It premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival on February 14, 2022, and Focus Features released it on March 18. It opened to $1.5 million but was widely praised. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it an old-school thriller made by a solid story and Rylance's "tightly tailored performance".

overview: Hinako is a surf-loving college student who has just moved to a small seaside town. When a sudden fire breaks out at her apartment building, she is rescued by Minato, a handsome firefighter, and the two soon fall in love. Just as they become inseparable, Minato loses his life in an accident at sea. Hinako is so distraught that she can no longer even look at the ocean, but one day she sings a song that reminds her of their time together, and Minato appears in the water. From then on, she can summon him in any watery surface as soon as she sings their song, but can the two really remain together forever? And what is the real reason for Minato's sudden reappearance?
tagline: Ride Your Own Wave.
title: Ride Your Wave
plot:
Ride Your Wave is a 2019 Japanese romantic drama film directed by Keishi Ōtomo and produced by Toho. The movie tells the story of two young women, Akira and Hinata, who meet at an all-girls surf competition.

The film begins with Akira (played by Fumi Nikaido), a talented surfer from Hokkaido, competing in a surfing tournament. She is determined to win, but her competitive spirit also makes her come across as arrogant and dismissive of others. After the competition, Akira meets Hinata (played by Kanna Hashimoto), a free-spirited young woman who has just moved to Tokyo from Hokkaido.

Despite their initial differences, the two women form an unlikely bond over their shared love of surfing. As they spend more time together, Akira begins to open up and show her vulnerable side to Hinata. The two women start dating, and their relationship blossoms as they explore the city and the ocean together.

However, their happiness is short-lived, as Akira's competitive spirit soon gets the better of her. She becomes increasingly obsessed with winning, causing tension in her relationship with Hinata. Meanwhile, Hinata struggles to find her place in Tokyo and feels like she doesn't quite fit in.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that both women are struggling with their own personal demons. Akira's competitive nature is rooted in a deep-seated insecurity, while Hinata's free-spirited nature hides a fear of commitment. Through their relationship, they learn to support and understand each other, but ultimately, their differences prove too great.

The film's climax features an intense surfing competition, where Akira faces off against her rival, a talented surfer named Yui (played by Rina Sasaki). The competition is fierce, but in the end, Akira emerges victorious. However, as she stands on the podium, basking in the glory of her win, she realizes that it's not just about winning – it's about finding happiness and fulfillment.

The film ends with Akira and Hinata standing together on the beach, watching the sunset over the ocean. They share a tender moment, and it becomes clear that their relationship has been transformed by their experiences. Akira has learned to balance her competitive spirit with her love for Hinata, while Hinata has found a sense of belonging and purpose.

Throughout the film, Ōtomo explores themes of identity, competition, and relationships. The movie is a poignant portrayal of two women navigating their lives and finding happiness in each other's company. Ride Your Wave is a beautiful and uplifting film that celebrates the power of love and self-discovery.

overview: In New York, former convict Pete Koslow, related to the Polish mafia, must deal with both Klimek the General, his ruthless boss, and the twisted ambitions of two federal agents, as he tries to survive and protect the lives of his loved ones.
tagline: Choose your enemies wisely
title: The Informer
plot:
The Informer is a 2019 crime thriller film directed by Andrea Di Stefano and written by Matt Nix. The movie stars Joel Kinnaman, Rosamund Pike, Clive Owen, and Common.

The story follows Rick Ford (Joel Kinnaman), an undercover cop who infiltrates the Irish mob in Boston. Rick is a former Marine who has been working as an informant for the FBI, providing them with information about the mob's activities in exchange for protection and a chance to start a new life.

However, things take a turn when Rick's cover is blown by his partner, Danny Patterson (Common), who is also an undercover cop. As a result, Rick is forced to go on the run from both the Irish mob and the FBI, who are now after him for his betrayal.

Rick teams up with Shannon Mullins (Rosamund Pike), a tough-as-nails Boston bartender who becomes his unlikely ally. Together, they try to stay one step ahead of their pursuers while also trying to take down the Irish mob from within.

As Rick navigates this treacherous world, he is forced to confront his own demons and make difficult choices in order to survive. Along the way, he also discovers that Danny's betrayal was not just a simple mistake, but rather a calculated move to protect himself and others.

The Informer explores themes of loyalty, deception, and redemption, as Rick struggles to come to terms with his past mistakes and find a way to make amends. The movie features a tense and suspenseful plot, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

Throughout the film, Kinnaman delivers a strong performance as Rick Ford, bringing depth and nuance to a complex character. Pike is also excellent as Shannon Mullins, bringing a sense of toughness and vulnerability to her role.

Overall, The Informer is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the darker side of human nature. With its strong performances, tense plot, and thought-provoking themes, it's a must-see for fans of crime dramas.

original_title: The Minute You Wake Up Dead
overview: A stockbroker in a small southern town gets embroiled in an insurance scam with a next-door neighbor that leads to multiple murders when a host of other people want in on the plot. Sheriff Thurmond Fowler, the by-the-book town sheriff for over four decades, works earnestly to try and unravel the town’s mystery and winds up getting more than he bargained for.
tagline: Don't trust a soul.
title: The Minute You Wake Up Dead
plot:
The Minute You Wake Up Dead is a 2022 American noir thriller directed by Michael Mailer. Cole Hauser plays the stockbroker Russ Potter, Jaimie Alexander the waitress Delaine Moore and Morgan Freeman Sheriff Thurmond Fowler, with Darren Mann as Lucius McFalls, Tony DeMil as the loan shark Jody, Benjamin Vandermey as Deputy Kane and Liann Pattison as Purnie Cannon.

Russ, a stockbroker, has moved back to his childhood home of Bare Hollow, Mississippi. Locals have profited from his tips, but his latest advice on a merger goes wrong and wipes out the savings of many residents. He rents the house next door to Delaine, a waitress he fancied in high school, and they begin an affair. Meanwhile Lucius, a small-time crook, murders Delaine's father, who is dying of cancer. Delaine pretends to grieve, but she had seduced Lucius and persuaded him to carry out the killing so that she could collect $550,000 in life insurance. When Sheriff Fowler's inquiries quickly point to Lucius, Delaine kills him too.

Lucius had meant to use his cut to repay the loan shark Jody, and after Jody's henchman Mace cut off one of his toes he told Jody everything. With Lucius dead, Jody demands that Delaine settle the debt. Lucius's body then disappears, and Delaine discovers that Russ has taken it. Russ explains that he learned of the crime and hid the corpse to shield her, intending to become her partner in the insurance money, and admits that he has killed Fowler, who was getting too close to the truth. Delaine reveals that her terminally ill father, knowing that suicide would void his policy, had arranged his own murder with her to defraud the insurer. She then kills Russ and dumps both bodies in the swamp. When they are found, Deputy Kane tells Delaine he suspects her and will prove it. Purnie, Russ's secretary, then claims that Russ told her everything and demands a share of the money. Delaine has Purnie kill Jody and Mace that night and murders Purnie the next morning, bringing the death toll of her scheme to seven. Later that day Kane arrests her, and to his astonishment she confesses everything, ignoring his advice to remain silent.

Filming began in Mississippi in February 2022, and Grindstone Entertainment acquired North American distribution. Released mainly on home video, with a very limited theatrical run that earned about $35,000, the film was panned by critics; none of the nine reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes were positive, and The Guardian gave it one star.

original_title: Monster High: Escape from Skull Shores
overview: It's officially Spring Break at Monster High, and Lagoona takes her gilfriends across the sea to the Great Barrier Reef, but they are ship wrecked and end up on a mysterious skull shaped island. Here they enjoy the local hospitality until they realize that they are being used by a slippery showman named Farnum to lure the rarest, most mysterious monster of them all, "the Beast" into a trap. Frankie is taken by the Beast but tables turn and she ends up rescuing him and returning with him to Monster High. The story goes to high voltage when they realize that Frankie has inadvertently led Farnum to the location of the greatest gathering of monsters anywhere...Monster High.
title: Monster High: Escape from Skull Shores
plot:
Monster High: Escape from Skull Shores is a 2012 animated adventure fantasy television special produced by Nerd Corps Entertainment for Mattel, the fourth special based on the Monster High doll line. It premiered on Nickelodeon in the United States in April 2012 and was tied to a dedicated Skull Shores line of dolls. Kate Higgins, Laura Bailey, Salli Saffioti, Debi Derryberry and Evan Smith are among the voice cast. It was later released on Blu-ray alongside Monster High: Fright On! as part of a double feature.

For spring break, Lagoona Blue invites her friends to the Great Scarrier Reef. On the way, their ship is destroyed by a kraken, leaving the students adrift on a raft made from their luggage. They are rescued by Bartleby Farnum, an eccentric human showman, and his assistant, Kipling, who wears a sack over his head, and taken to an island called Skull Shores, where they are welcomed by the local Tiki tribe.

Suspicious, Lagoona and her boyfriend, Gil, search Farnum's boat and find a recording about the Beast of Skull Shores, a creature that Farnum is obsessed with capturing, and about an explorer who befriended it and who looks like Frankie Stein. They realize that Farnum plans to use Frankie as bait. That night, the beast appears and carries Frankie off; she is frightened at first, but soon realizes that he means her no harm. Farnum and the Tiki give chase, trapping Ghoulia Yelps and Abbey Bominable in a pit, while Clawdeen Wolf, Draculaura and Cleo de Nile escape. The next morning, Frankie meets Andy, a friendly monster who reveals that he and the beast are the same creature, and the friends must work together to rescue their captured classmates, protect Andy from Farnum and find a way to escape from the island. Along the way, the story explores friendship and acceptance, as the ghouls stand up for a misunderstood creature, and Andy eventually joins them as a new student at Monster High.

Grace Montgomery of Common Sense Media found its monsters more silly than sinister and praised its strong message about tolerance, but felt that the message was partly undermined by the revealing outfits and heavy makeup of the female characters, who she otherwise considered decent role models.

overview: Two veterans of the Bosnian War, one American, one Serbian, clash in the remote Smoky Mountain wilderness.
tagline: The purest form of war is one on one.
title: Killing Season
plot:
Killing Season is an action thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie follows two former Special Forces operatives, Cody (Robert De Niro) and Dushkov (Jason Statham), who find themselves on a violent and deadly game of cat and mouse in the woods of Montana.

At its core, Killing Season explores the theme of revenge and the destructive power it can have on individuals. Both Cody and Dushkov are driven by a desire for retribution against those who wronged them in the past, and their actions become increasingly brutal and merciless as the story unfolds. This toxic cycle of revenge is expertly woven throughout the narrative, highlighting the devastating consequences of allowing hatred and anger to consume us.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption, albeit in a somewhat ambiguous manner. As Cody and Dushkov engage in their deadly game, it becomes clear that neither character is capable of true redemption. Their actions are driven by a deep-seated need for revenge, rather than any desire to make amends or find forgiveness.

Furthermore, Killing Season critiques the notion of masculinity and the societal expectations placed upon men. Cody and Dushkov embody two different sides of toxic masculinity – one that is rooted in honor and loyalty, while the other is driven by a primal urge for violence and domination. The film raises questions about what it means to be a man and whether these traditional masculine ideals are worth sacrificing one's humanity.

Overall, Killing Season is a gripping and intense thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of revenge, redemption, and toxic masculinity in a thought-provoking and unsettling manner.

overview: The harrowing true story of two elite US Navy fighter pilots during the Korean War. Their heroic sacrifices would ultimately make them the Navy's most celebrated wingmen.
tagline: In America’s forgotten war, they made history.
title: Devotion
plot:
Devotion is a 2022 American biographical war film directed by J. D. Dillard and written by Jake Crane and Jonathan Stewart, based on Adam Makos's book about the friendship between naval aviators Jesse L. Brown and Tom Hudner during the Korean War. It stars Jonathan Majors as Brown and Glen Powell as Hudner, with Christina Jackson, Joe Jonas and Thomas Sadoski.

In early 1950, Lieutenant Tom Hudner joins Fighter Squadron 32, where Ensign Jesse Brown is the only Black pilot. The unit flies the powerful but dangerous F4U Corsair. Hudner begins giving Brown rides and meets his wife Daisy and their daughter Pam, and he learns that Brown privately shouts racist abuse at himself in the mirror to steel himself before missions. Before the squadron deploys on the USS Leyte to the Mediterranean, Daisy makes Hudner promise to be there for Jesse. When a squadron mate dies in a landing crash after ignoring instructions, Brown explains that had he always done as he was told, racist superiors would have ended his career long ago. On shore leave in Cannes, Brown charms Elizabeth Taylor into inviting the squadron to a casino, and after Hudner fights a Marine who harassed Brown, Brown tells him not to fight his battles but simply to stand by him.

When war breaks out in Korea, the Leyte is redeployed, and in November 1950 the squadron is ordered to destroy bridges on the Yalu River while firing only on the Korean side. Brown disobeys Hudner's order to retreat and destroys the last bridge alone; Hudner's report notes the disobedience, which Brown fears will cost him promotions. While supporting Marines at the Battle of Chosin Reservoir, Brown's plane is hit and he crash-lands in the mountains. Seeing that he is alive but trapped, Hudner deliberately crash-lands beside him, but he cannot free Brown, who dies shortly after a rescue helicopter arrives. With recovery judged too risky, the squadron destroys the wreckage with Brown's body inside. Months later, President Harry S. Truman awards Hudner the Medal of Honor, and Daisy tells him that she only asked him to be there for Jesse, not to save him. A closing note says that Brown's remains have never been recovered and that the families remain close.

Devotion premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 12, 2022, and was released by Sony Pictures on November 23. Despite positive reviews (81% on Rotten Tomatoes), it grossed only about $21.7 million against a $90 million budget.

overview: When political turmoil forces a British-Caribbean dictator to flee his island nation, he seeks refuge and hides with a rebellious teenage girl in suburban America, and ends up teaching the young teen how to start a revolution and overthrow the "mean girls" in her high school.
tagline: She thought she was a rebel... Until she met a real one
title: Dear Dictator
plot:
Dear Dictator is a 2018 American satirical comedy film written and directed by Lisa Addario and Joe Syracuse. It stars Michael Caine as Anton Vincent, the deposed dictator of a Caribbean island nation, and Odeya Rush as Tatiana Mills, the American teenager who becomes his pen pal, with Katie Holmes, Seth Green and Jason Biggs. The script appeared on the 2006 Black List of unproduced screenplays, and Alfred Molina, Robert De Niro and Anthony Hopkins were at various times attached to the title role before Caine was cast in 2016.

Sixteen-year-old Tatiana lives a chaotic life with her single mother, Darlene, who is involved with her married boss, Dr. Charles, a dentist with a foot fetish. For a letter-writing assignment from her social studies teacher, Mr. Spines, Tatiana becomes the pen pal of Anton Vincent, a notorious strongman who rules an island nation. When his people rise up against his violent, oppressive regime and overthrow him, Vincent vanishes, and Tatiana worries about his safety. A few days later he turns up unexpectedly in the United States and hides in her family's suburban garage.

There, Anton forms a grandfatherly bond with Tatiana and her struggling mother, making himself useful around the house while secretly coordinating with loyalist forces back home to plot his return to power. He also turns his attention to Tatiana's troubles at high school, where she is bullied by a clique of popular girls. Making her a dictator-in-training, he teaches her to seize power at school using the same methods that brought him to power in the Caribbean. His schemes eventually go too far, turning Tatiana against him, and the security services, having intercepted Anton's messages to his loyalists, suspect that she is involved in terrorism. The police question Tatiana and Darlene and search their home without realizing that the old man living with them is the missing dictator. No evidence is found and they are released, but Tatiana then tells the police who he is, and Anton is arrested pending extradition.

Screened at several festivals under its working title, Coup d'Etat, the film was released in North America by Cinedigm in theaters and on video on demand on March 16, 2018. Reviews were negative, although Caine's and Rush's performances were praised; Rotten Tomatoes reported 16% approval, with critics finding that it squandered its wildly silly premise and talented cast.

overview: A haunted doll teaches one little girl why children shouldn't play with undead things.
title: Finders Keepers
plot:
Finders Keepers is a 2014 American supernatural horror television film directed by Alexander Yellen. Written by Peter Sullivan from a story by Jeffrey Schenck and Sullivan, it was produced by HFD Productions and Hybrid, with a score by Matthew Janszen, and premiered on the Syfy channel on 18 October 2014 before being distributed on home video by Lionsgate. It runs about 85 minutes and stars Jaime Pressly, Kylie Rogers, Patrick Muldoon and Tobin Bell, its premise summed up by the warning that children should not play with undead things.

The film opens with two police officers entering a house where a family has been murdered; inside, they are attacked and killed by the family's knife-wielding son, Zachary. Five years later, newly separated from her husband Jonathan (Muldoon), Alyson Simon (Pressly) moves into the large old house in the countryside with her nine-year-old daughter Claire (Rogers). The estate agent has kept the killings secret, and Alyson only learns of them after the move. Exploring the house, Claire finds a doll left behind by the previous occupants and soon develops a dangerous obsession with it.

Claire's behaviour grows increasingly disturbing, and deaths begin to pile up, starting with the apparent suicide of Jonathan's new girlfriend during one of Claire's visits. Alyson visits Zachary in a psychiatric institution in search of answers, learning nothing before he later escapes. Every attempt to get rid of the doll fails, as it keeps returning to Claire, and a voodoo-like bond forms between them, so that whatever happens to one happens to the other. Claire's therapist, Dr. Freeman (Bell), mistakes the injuries she suffers when her parents try to destroy the toy for signs of abuse, but is killed after realising she lied. Alyson's friend Elena Carranza (Justina Machado), a professor who studies the paranormal, takes the doll to her laboratory and suggests that removing its eyes will break the connection, but she too falls victim to the possessed girl. In a final struggle at the house, Jonathan gouges out the doll's eyes and breaks the curse, and the reconciled parents decide to sell the house and give their marriage another chance.

The cast also includes Marina Sirtis, Mark DeCarlo and Joey Luthman as the adult Zachary. German-language reviews found the film lacking in suspense and derivative of Sinister and Child's Play, praising the performances of Rogers and Bell but less impressed by Pressly and the dialogue.

overview: A social worker is coming to Gru's house to check if it's suitable for children. Margo, Edith, Agnes and the Minions must take care of the situation.
title: Minions: Home Makeover
plot:
Minions: Home Makeover, released simply as Home Makeover, is a 2010 American computer-animated comedy short produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures as a follow-up to the feature Despicable Me. Directed by Kyle Balda and Samuel Tourneux and written by Brett Hoffman, it runs between four and five minutes. It was released in December 2010 as one of three new shorts, together with Orientation Day and Banana, included with the home-video release of Despicable Me, appearing among the bonus features of the Blu-ray and in the Minion Madness collection.

Set after the events of the film, the short opens in Gru's house while the supervillain is out on an errand. Margo answers an unexpected telephone call from Miss Hattie's Home for Girls, the orphanage the three sisters came from, and, pretending to be Gru, learns that a social worker is on the way to inspect whether the house is safe and suitable for children. If it is not, the girls will be sent back to the orphanage. With little time to spare, Margo, Edith and Agnes enlist the Minions to give the lair a rapid child-friendly makeover.

The comedy comes from the gap between a villain's home and a family home, and from the inventive, chaotic solutions the girls and the Minions devise. Tennis balls are stuck over the spikes inside a coffin, the pins are pulled from a voodoo doll, a clown nose is placed on a skull in the dining room, Gru's own shrink ray is used to make the weapons smaller, and a paint-filled bazooka turns the walls pink. To complete the illusion, the Minions stand in for the master of the house with a makeshift "Mr. Gru". The inspector seems satisfied with the result until the real Gru comes home: the disguise falls apart, the startled social worker faints, and Gru, taking in his newly "girly" lair, passes out as well.

The voice cast reunites the girls of the feature, with Miranda Cosgrove as Margo, Dana Gaier as Edith and Elsie Fisher as Agnes, while Pierre Coffin voices both the Minions and the social worker. The short was later collected among Illumination's short films on streaming and television platforms, where it carries a TV-Y7 rating.

overview: A Democratic political consultant helps a retired Marine colonel run for mayor in a small, conservative Wisconsin town.
tagline: Send in the clowns.
title: Irresistible
plot:
Irresistible is a satirical comedy film that delves into the darker aspects of American politics and society. The movie follows a Democratic campaign manager, Gary Clements, who is sent to a small town in Pennsylvania to help a local candidate win an election. However, things take a turn when he discovers that the town's residents are being manipulated by a wealthy corporate executive, Jack Morris, who is using his influence to sway the outcome of the election.

Through this narrative, the film critiques the corrupting influence of money in politics and the ways in which special interests can manipulate public opinion. The movie also explores themes of class struggle, as Gary's character represents the values of the working class, while Jack's character embodies the power and privilege of the wealthy elite.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Irresistible is not just a comedy about politics, but also a commentary on the erosion of civic engagement and the decline of community. The film highlights how politicians and corporate interests often prioritize their own interests over those of the people they claim to represent.

Ultimately, the movie presents a bleak vision of American politics, where money and power are seen as the primary drivers of decision-making, rather than the needs and values of the citizens being represented.

overview: A gang of thieves plan a heist during a hurricane and encounter trouble when a disgraced cop tries to force everyone in the building to evacuate.
tagline: When the perfect crime meets the perfect storm.
title: Force of Nature
plot:
Force of Nature is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Ben Wheatley, not Ingenious Media. The movie stars Michelle Dockery, Luke Evans, and Hannah John-Kamen.

The main themes of Force of Nature revolve around the cat-and-mouse game between two women, played by Michelle Dockery and Hannah John-Kamen, who are on a plane that is being hijacked by a man, played by Luke Evans. The film explores several key ideas:

1. **Survival vs. Humanity**: As the story unfolds, the characters must confront their own humanity in the face of extreme circumstances. They must decide whether to prioritize their own survival or try to find ways to escape and reclaim control.
2. **Power Dynamics**: The film examines the power struggles between the characters, particularly between the two women. Their interactions are tense and complex, revealing a deep-seated desire for control and agency in a situation where they feel powerless.
3. **Trauma and PTSD**: Both female leads have experienced trauma in their pasts, which is slowly revealed throughout the film. This backstory informs their actions and decisions, adding depth to their characters and motivations.
4. **Deception and Misdirection**: The movie's plot is full of twists and turns, keeping the audience guessing about the true intentions of each character. This theme highlights the complexity of human nature and the ease with which people can deceive others.

Overall, Force of Nature is a gripping thriller that explores the darker aspects of human psychology, power struggles, and survival in the face of adversity.

overview: Retired cop James Lasombra is asked by a friend to investigate the disappearance of her daughter, who seemingly packed in the night and left an ominous message on the bathroom mirror - "The Empty Man Made Me Do It." As he investigates this mysterious figure further, James begins to see and hear strange things, and is forced to come to terms with his past and what it means for his future.
tagline: The first night you hear him. The second night you see him. The third night he finds you.
title: The Empty Man
plot:
The Empty Man is a 2020 American supernatural horror film directed by David Prior and written by C. Robert Cargill. The movie follows the story of James Lasombra, a former FBI agent who is investigating a series of bizarre occurrences in a small town.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the main theme of the movie revolves around the concept of identity and the blurring of lines between reality and madness. The protagonist, James Lasombra, is a complex character whose past is shrouded in mystery, and as he delves deeper into the mystery, his own sanity begins to unravel.

The film also explores the idea of possession and the supernatural, as James encounters a mysterious figure known as "The Empty Man," who seems to be manipulating events from behind the scenes. The Empty Man is a symbol of the void or the abyss, representing the unknown and the unknowable.

Throughout the movie, the themes of identity, reality, and madness are intertwined, creating a sense of unease and uncertainty in the viewer. The film's use of atmospheric tension and unsettling visuals adds to the overall sense of unease, making it difficult for the protagonist (and the audience) to distinguish between what is real and what is just a product of his own paranoia.

Ultimately, the movie builds towards a climactic confrontation between James and the Empty Man, which serves as a metaphor for the struggle to maintain one's identity in the face of overwhelming uncertainty. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the viewer to ponder the nature of reality and the true meaning of the Empty Man.

Overall, The Empty Man is a thought-provoking horror film that explores complex themes and ideas, making it a compelling watch for fans of supernatural horror.

overview: During an emergency landing on a deserted island suddenly traumatized by antiauthoritarian education Lena Schneider (Josefine Preuss) together with the Turkish Super Macho Cem Öztürk (Elyas M'Barek) must fight for survival. After initially Cem macho repulsive acts on Lena, a jellyfish in the water and sand in a bikini, she recognizes the time the romantic core behind his cool facade. Meanwhile, meet also their parents, who obdurate psychologist Doris (Anna Stieblich) and Metin Öztürk (Adnan Maral) to work together to find their missing children. So both generations take an involuntary Turkish Basic Course for beginners.
title: Turkish for Beginners
plot:
Turkish for Beginners (Türkisch für Anfänger) is a 2012 German comedy written and directed by Bora Dagtekin, who created the ARD television series of the same name and made his feature directing debut with this film. Rather than continuing the show, it retells from scratch how the Schneider and Öztürk families meet. Almost the entire television cast returned, led by Josefine Preuß as Lena Schneider, Elyas M'Barek as Cem Öztürk, Anna Stieblich as Doris, Adnan Maral as Metin, Pegah Ferydoni as Yağmur and Arnel Tači as Costa, with Katja Riemann, Günther Kaufmann and Frederick Lau in supporting roles. It was produced by Rat Pack Filmproduktion with Constantin Film, ARD Degeto and several regional broadcasters.

Raised by Doris, a free-spirited therapist of the 1968 generation, Lena has become her opposite: controlled, rule-bound and wary of emotion. For her graduation, mother and daughter fly to Thailand, sitting next to the Öztürks, a widowed police detective, Metin, and his children, the macho would-be rapper Cem and his sister Yağmur. When an ash cloud forces the plane to ditch in the Indian Ocean, most passengers are rescued, but Lena drifts ashore on a deserted island in a life raft with Cem, Yağmur and Costa, a stuttering Greek. Their radio contact with their parents reveals that the raft's beacon is too weak to be located.

As the castaways struggle to get by, Lena and Cem constantly clash. After Lena steps on a sea urchin and suffers an allergic reaction, Cem carries her to a village of supposed cannibals, who turn out to speak fluent German and are hosting a researcher who treats her. At a celebration, Lena believes she slept with Cem while intoxicated and later overhears that he had made a bet about it. Meanwhile, Doris and Metin fall in love at the resort. Once reunited with her mother, the hurt Lena drives the Öztürks away by making Metin believe that the mafia clan that put the family in witness protection has found them. When she later watches her camcorder footage and sees that Cem only watched over her while she slept, she confesses everything. She and Doris catch up with the Öztürks on the plane as they leave with new identities, and both couples are reunited.

Shot over 37 days in 2011 in Munich, Berlin and Thailand, whose islands Ko Kut and Ko Chang stood in for the Andaman Islands, the film premiered in Munich on 6 March 2012 and opened in German cinemas on 15 March 2012.

overview: An atheist goes through a near-death experience in an auto accident before converting to Christianity.
title: Let There Be Light
plot:
Let There Be Light is a 2017 American drama film directed by Jeremy Goldberg and written by Jeremy Goldberg and Michael McEvoy. The movie stars Steven Yeun, Samm Levine, and Janina Gavankar.

The main themes of Let There Be Light revolve around mental health, specifically bipolar disorder, and the struggles of living with a stigmatized condition. The film follows the story of John (played by Steven Yeun), a successful businessman who is diagnosed with bipolar disorder after experiencing a severe manic episode.

Throughout the movie, the theme of mental illness is portrayed as a complex and multifaceted issue that affects not only the individual but also their loved ones. The film explores the challenges of managing symptoms, maintaining relationships, and finding treatment options in a society that often stigmatizes mental health issues.

Another significant theme present in Let There Be Light is the importance of community and support. John's journey is marked by his struggles to find acceptance and understanding from those around him, particularly his family and friends. The film highlights the need for empathy, education, and open conversation about mental health to break down stigmas and promote a culture of understanding.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, self-discovery, and personal growth. As John navigates his diagnosis and treatment, he is forced to confront his own strengths, weaknesses, and values, ultimately leading to a deeper understanding of himself and the world around him.

Overall, Let There Be Light offers a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of mental health, community, and personal growth, shedding light on the complexities of living with bipolar disorder and promoting greater awareness and understanding.

overview: Talented rookie race-car driver Jimmy Bly has started losing his focus and begins to slip in the race rankings. It's no wonder, with the immense pressure being shoveled on him by his overly ambitious promoter brother as well as Bly's romance with his arch rival's girlfriend Sophia. With much riding on Bly, car owner Carl Henry brings former racing star Joe Tanto on board to help Bly. To drive Bly back to the top of the rankings, Tanto must first deal with the emotional scars left over from a tragic racing accident which nearly took his life.
tagline: Get ready for the race of your life.
title: Driven
plot:
Driven is a 2001 American sports action film directed by Renny Harlin and written and produced by Sylvester Stallone, who also stars. Set in the CART FedEx Championship Series, it follows a young driver's attempt to win the title. Kip Pardue plays the rookie Jimmy Bly and Stallone the veteran Joe Tanto, with Burt Reynolds as the team owner Carl Henry, Til Schweiger as Beau Brandenburg, Estella Warren as Sophia Simone, Gina Gershon as Cathy, Cristián de la Fuente as Memo Moreno and Robert Sean Leonard as Jimmy's brother Demille.

Halfway through the season, the rookie Jimmy has already won five races, angering the reigning champion Beau, who blames his own slump on his fiancée Sophia and breaks off their engagement, after which his form returns. Carl, Jimmy's wheelchair-using team owner, notices his driver making more mistakes and talks his former champion Joe out of retirement to mentor him, replacing Memo, who is now married to Joe's ex-wife Cathy. Jimmy and Sophia grow close. In Canada, Carl holds Joe in the pits so that he can rejoin just in time to block Beau and hand Jimmy the win, while Demille resents Joe's influence. Distracted by Sophia, Jimmy crashes in Japan, and when she reconciles with Beau at a party in Chicago, Jimmy steals one of the new prototype cars and tears through the city streets until Joe chases him down and calms him.

Carl reinstates Memo and moves Joe to the pit lane. In a rain-soaked race in Germany, Memo, urged on by Cathy, goes for the win instead of protecting Jimmy and crashes, ending up in a lake; Jimmy and Beau dive in and pull him out just before the car explodes. Furious that Jimmy has sacrificed his title hopes, Carl arranges to replace him with Beau through Demille, but Beau tears up the contract and Sophia punches Demille. Jimmy, cleared to race despite an injured foot, goes into the Detroit finale with Joe back as his teammate. Joe damages his suspension avoiding a crash, and on the last lap Jimmy edges past Beau by inches to win the championship, celebrating with Joe and Beau as Demille watches proudly.

Driven was a commercial failure, grossing $32 million against a $72 million budget, though it was Stallone's first number-one opening since Cop Land. Critics panned it, with 14% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it received seven Golden Raspberry nominations; Warren won Worst Supporting Actress for this film and Planet of the Apes.

overview: When Shaun decides to take the day off and have some fun, he gets a little more action than he bargained for. A mix up with the Farmer, a caravan and a very steep hill lead them all to the Big City and it's up to Shaun and the flock to return everyone safely to the green grass of home.
tagline: Moving on to Pastures New.
title: Shaun the Sheep Movie
plot:
Shaun the Sheep Movie is a heartwarming and hilarious animated film that explores several endearing themes. At its core, the movie is a celebration of friendship, loyalty, and the power of imagination.

The story follows Shaun, a clever and resourceful sheep who dreams of exploring the big city beyond his farm. As he navigates this new world, Shaun must confront his own limitations and learn to rely on his friends for support. The film showcases the strong bonds between Shaun and his flock, particularly Timmy, who becomes his trusted companion in the city.

One of the main themes of the movie is the importance of taking risks and embracing uncertainty. Shaun's desire to explore the city leads him down a path of discovery, where he learns to adapt to new situations and trust his instincts. This theme is beautifully illustrated through Shaun's interactions with various characters, including a wise-cracking pigeon who becomes his guide.

The film also explores the idea of finding one's true identity and purpose. As Shaun navigates the city, he begins to realize that there's more to life than just following the rules on the farm. He discovers a sense of freedom and joy in exploring new places and meeting new people, which ultimately helps him find his place in the world.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of perseverance and determination. Shaun faces numerous challenges as he tries to achieve his goals, but he never gives up. With the help of his friends, he finds creative solutions to overcome obstacles and stay true to himself.

Overall, Shaun the Sheep Movie is a charming film that celebrates the power of friendship, imagination, and self-discovery. Its lighthearted tone and lovable characters make it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Sent into a drunken tailspin when his entire unit is killed by a gang of thrill-seeking punks, disgraced Hong Kong police inspector Wing needs help from his new rookie partner, with a troubled past of his own, to climb out of the bottle and track down the gang and its ruthless leader.
tagline: Failures and suffering make a real hero.
title: New Police Story
