plot:
New Police Story is a 2004 Hong Kong action thriller directed by Benny Chan, starring Jackie Chan, Nicholas Tse, Charlie Yeung, Charlene Choi and Daniel Wu. It is the fifth Police Story film and a darker, more grounded reboot of the series, relying more on drama and violence than its predecessors.

A gang of five young people robs a bank with the aim of luring and killing police officers. Chief Inspector Chan Kwok-wing leads his squad after them, and every officer except Chan is killed, including Hong, the younger brother of his girlfriend Ho Yee. Overcome by guilt, Chan spends a year drinking, until a young man named Frank Cheng appears, claims to be his new partner and pushes him to reopen the case. A rival, Chief Inspector Chiu, who blames Chan's arrogance for the massacre, races them to solve it. Clues from a former colleague, Sam Wong, lead them to an extreme sports event on a skyscraper rooftop. There gang members Fire and Sue kill Sam, who admits he was blackmailed into helping set up the ambush, and the gang escapes after a chase down the tower and a runaway bus.

Chan discovers that Frank is not a policeman at all, having failed the entrance exam, but he trusts the young man's sincerity. The gang turn out to be children of wealthy families who turn their crimes into online video games. Their leader, Joe, is the son of a deputy police commissioner. Joe kills the wounded Sue, and the gang straps a bomb to Ho Yee, leaving her in a coma. Chan and Frank are arrested but quietly released to stop the next attack, a raid on a bank. Chan clears the building and brings in the robbers' parents. In the fight that follows, Joe turns on his own accomplices. On the roof, Chan beats Joe in a race to assemble a pistol. Joe then points his empty gun at the police and is shot. Chan and Frank fall safely onto an inflatable cushion. Ho Yee recovers and accepts Chan's proposal, and Frank, arrested for impersonating an officer, is revealed to be the orphan boy Chan once comforted years earlier.

The film was shot in Hong Kong in late 2003 and opened there in September 2004. It earned about HK$21 million, making it the year's fourth-highest-grossing local release. It had a small British release in 2006, and the critic Jonathan Ross wrote that Chan could still deliver.

original_title: ปริศนารูหลอน
overview: When two siblings stumble on a strange hole in the wall of their grandparents' house, horrifying incidents reveal sinister secrets about their family.
tagline: A truth you've never known, that makes you doubt what you know.
title: The Whole Truth
plot:
The Whole Truth (Thai: ปริศนารูหลอน, literally "Haunted Hole Puzzle") is a Thai supernatural horror mystery from 2021, directed by Wisit Sasanatieng from a script by Abishek J. Bajaj. Sompob Benjathikul plays Phong, a former senior police officer, Nicole Theriault plays Mai and Sutatta Udomsilp her daughter Pim, with Sadanont Durongkaweroj, Steven Isarapong and Nattapat Nimjirawat among the cast. It was released on Netflix on 2 December 2021.

Pim, a popular cheerleader, and her brother Putt, an outsider who wears a leg brace, live with their single mother Mai. When Mai is left in a coma after a car accident on a stormy night, a man introducing himself as their grandfather, Phong, takes the teenagers to stay with him and their grandmother Wan, who suffers from dementia and keeps calling Putt "Krit". Neither child remembers the house, although they are told they lived there when small. Putt finds a hole in the wall through which he sees a decaying version of the same house and a dark-haired figure, but his grandparents claim they can see no hole. Meanwhile Putt's classmate Fame is blackmailing him with a video he secretly filmed of Pim showering.

Through the hole the siblings glimpse a girl with a blackened, swollen face, crawling, vomiting dark fluid and cradling a baby. Putt falls ill after drinking the milk Wan keeps giving him, and the family cat dies. Phong, learning that the wealthy young man blamed for Mai's crash has escaped justice, hunts him down and burns him alive. Eventually the hole shows the past: their sister Pinya died after being locked in a closet, where she drank rat poison while their father Krit was drunk, and Krit was later found shot. Mai wakes, rushes to the house and confronts her parents, and Wan finally admits she has poisoned Putt, as she did Pinya, raving that she was ridding Mai of her "freaks". Mai takes the children away. Later, Phong learns that the young man he murdered was innocent after all. Pinya's ghost appears to Wan, who is then found convulsing with rat poison; Phong, terrified by the burning ghost of the man he killed, accidentally shoots his wife and then kills himself, the bullet creating the hole he never could see. Final flashbacks reveal that Wan deliberately bolted Pinya inside the closet, and that it was Mai who shot Krit, with Phong disguising the killing as suicide. The film closes on Pim asleep with Pinya's ghost holding her hand.

original_title: Teen Titans Go! To the Movies
overview: All the major DC superheroes are starring in their own films, all but the Teen Titans, so Robin is determined to remedy this situation by getting over his role as a sidekick and becoming a movie star. Thus, with a few madcap ideas and an inspirational song in their hearts, the Teen Titans head to Hollywood to fulfill their dreams.
tagline: The superhero movie to end all superhero movies. Hopefully.
title: Teen Titans Go! To the Movies
plot:
Teen Titans Go! To the Movies is a 2018 American animated superhero comedy film based on the Cartoon Network series Teen Titans Go!, produced by Warner Bros. Animation and DC Entertainment. Directed by Peter Rida Michail and Aaron Horvath from a script by Horvath and Michael Jelenic, it features the series' voice cast, including Scott Menville as Robin, Khary Payton, Tara Strong, Greg Cipes and Hynden Walch, joined by Will Arnett as Slade and Kristen Bell as the filmmaker Jade Wilson, with Nicolas Cage as Superman and Halsey as Wonder Woman.

In Jump City, the Teen Titans get distracted by their own rap song while fighting the Balloon Man, forcing the Justice League to step in. The League mocks them for their childishness and points out that they do not even have a movie of their own. At the premiere of Batman Again, Robin is humiliated when he mistakenly believes a film about him is being shown. After the supervillain Slade breaks into S.T.A.R. Labs to steal a crystal and mocks the Titans, Robin resolves that they will go to Hollywood. At Warner Bros. Studios, director Jade Wilson, responsible for every superhero film, rejects them because they lack an archnemesis. A misguided trip back in time to prevent other heroes' origins leaves the world overrun by villains, and the Titans have to set things right.

Battling Slade at Wayne Tech to recover the crystal earns them a movie deal, but after the team's antics, Jade decides to make the film about Robin alone, and he breaks up the team, believing they hold each other back. On the last day of filming, Jade reveals herself to be Slade in disguise: her superhero movies were a ploy to keep the heroes busy while he stole technology to build D.O.O.M.S.D.A.Y., a streaming service that will let him control minds, and he deliberately split Robin from his friends. Slade destroys Titans Tower; Robin apologizes and the team reunites. At the premiere of Robin: The Movie, Slade uses the crystal to hypnotize the Justice League and then Robin, but the Titans snap him out of it by showing him the homemade movie they made for him. Using their rap song, they defeat Slade, freeing the world, and the Justice League finally acknowledges them as heroes.

Released by Warner Bros. Pictures on July 27, 2018, the film grossed about $52 million worldwide on a $10 million budget and was well received, earning 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 69 for its light-hearted, intelligent humor.

overview: A peculiar neighbor offers hope to a recent widow who is struggling to raise a teenager who is unpredictable and, sometimes, violent.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
tagline: Loving people doesn't save them
title: Mommy
plot:
Mommy is a 2014 Canadian drama film directed by Kyra Sedgwick and written by Adam Brody. The movie revolves around the complex relationship between a mother, her son, and their caregiver.

The central theme of Mommy is the exploration of grief, trauma, and the human capacity for love in the face of unimaginable pain. The story delves into the emotional turmoil experienced by Stephen (played as a character), a young boy struggling to cope with his mother's terminal illness and subsequent breakdown. As he navigates this challenging situation, Stephen forms an unorthodox bond with his caregiver, Kyla (played as a character), who becomes a surrogate parent figure.

Throughout the film, the director masterfully weaves together themes of vulnerability, intimacy, and the blurred lines between caregiving and parenthood. The movie raises questions about the nature of love, responsibility, and the human need for connection in the face of adversity.

One of the most striking aspects of Mommy is its portrayal of the complexities of mother-son relationships, particularly when one parent is struggling with illness or mental health issues. The film offers a nuanced exploration of the emotional dynamics at play, highlighting both the deep-seated bonds that can form between individuals and the ways in which trauma can shape our experiences.

Ultimately, Mommy presents a powerful and poignant portrayal of human resilience, love, and the enduring power of connection in the face of adversity.

original_title: ベルセルク 黄金時代篇II ドルドレイ攻略
overview: The Band of the Hawk participates in the Midland war campaign. On the bloody battlefield, they conquer decisive victories that lead them to Doldrey, an old fortress that will decide the outcome of the war.
title: Berserk: The Golden Age Arc II - The Battle for Doldrey
plot:
Berserk: The Golden Age Arc II - The Battle for Doldrey is a 2012 Japanese animated dark fantasy film and the second part of a trilogy adapting the Golden Age arc of Kentaro Miura's manga Berserk. Toshiyuki Kubooka directed from a screenplay by Ichirō Ōkouchi, with animation by Studio 4°C and distribution by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan. Hiroaki Iwanaga voices the mercenary swordsman Guts, Takahiro Sakurai the ambitious leader Griffith and Toa Yukinari the warrior Casca. Shirō Sagisu composed the score, and Susumu Hirasawa provided the insert song "Aria".

The story continues the war between the Kingdom of Midland and the Tudor Empire, in which Griffith's mercenary company, the Band of the Hawk, has become one of Midland's most valuable forces. After Guts and Casca are separated from the rest of the band, they are pursued by the brutal Tudor commander Adon and his soldiers. Guts holds off most of the attackers so that Casca can escape, and in the aftermath he reflects on his life and resolves that one day he will leave the Hawks, find a dream of his own and so become Griffith's equal and true friend, rather than a follower serving someone else's ambition.

The band then takes part in the assault on Doldrey, a fortress thought to be impregnable, whose capture would bring the Hundred Years' War to an end. In the battle Casca kills Adon, and the long war finally comes to an end. A month after the war ends, however, Guts announces his departure and defeats Griffith in a duel to win his freedom. Shaken by the loss, Griffith makes a reckless mistake: he is discovered sleeping with the king's daughter, Princess Charlotte. He is charged with treason and thrown into the Tower of Rebirth, while the members of the Band of the Hawk are declared outlaws, setting up the events of the final film.

The film opened in Japan on 23 June 2012 and was released on home video in North America by Viz Media in 2013. Its producer reports that it was nominated in the feature film category at the 2013 Annecy International Animated Film Festival. Critical reaction was mixed. Kotaku's Richard Eisenbeis called it a great improvement over the first film, and Otaku USA praised its balance of action and character development. Anime News Network reviewers, by contrast, criticised its computer-generated animation and its treatment of women, and felt that it reduced the rich character development of the manga to a thin shadow.

overview: United States President Lex Luthor uses the oncoming trajectory of a Kryptonite meteor to frame Superman and declare a $1 billion bounty on the heads of the Man of Steel and his ‘partner in crime’, Batman. Heroes and villains alike launch a relentless pursuit of Superman and Batman, who must unite—and recruit help—to try and stave off the action-packed onslaught, stop the meteor Luthors plot.
tagline: No one is above the law.
title: Superman/Batman: Public Enemies
plot:
Superman/Batman: Public Enemies is a 2009 animated superhero film based on the comic book series of the same name by DC Comics. The movie follows the story of Superman and Batman as they team up to take down a corrupt politician, Lex Luthor, who has been elected President of the United States.

The main themes of Superman/Batman: Public Enemies include:

1. **The Dangers of Unchecked Power**: The film highlights the dangers of unchecked power and corruption in government. Lex Luthor's rise to power is facilitated by his ability to manipulate public opinion and use propaganda to sway voters.
2. **The Importance of Accountability**: The movie emphasizes the importance of holding those in power accountable for their actions. Superman and Batman must work together to stop Lex Luthor, who has become a threat to national security and the rule of law.
3. **The Tension between Heroism and Politics**: The film explores the tension between heroism and politics, as Superman and Batman struggle with how to balance their desire to protect the public with the need to respect the democratic process.
4. **The Power of Friendship and Partnership**: The movie showcases the strength of the partnership between Superman and Batman, who put aside their differences to work together towards a common goal.

Overall, Superman/Batman: Public Enemies is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of power, accountability, and the importance of working together to protect the greater good.

original_title: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
overview: Marcel is an adorable one-inch-tall shell who ekes out a colorful existence with his grandmother Connie and their pet lint, Alan. Once part of a sprawling community of shells, they now live alone as the sole survivors of a mysterious tragedy. But when a documentary filmmaker discovers them amongst the clutter of his Airbnb, the short film he posts online brings Marcel millions of passionate fans, as well as unprecedented dangers and a new hope at finding his long-lost family.
tagline: Everybody loves Marcel.
title: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
plot:
Marcel the Shell with Shoes On is a heartwarming stop-motion animated film that explores several poignant themes. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of loneliness, human connection, and the power of storytelling.

The film follows Marcel, a small shell with big emotions, as he navigates his life in New York City. Marcel's struggles to form meaningful relationships and find his place in the world are deeply relatable, making him an endearing protagonist. The movie masterfully conveys the pain of loneliness and the longing for human connection through Marcel's interactions with various characters.

One of the primary themes of Marcel the Shell with Shoes On is the importance of storytelling as a means of self-expression and connection. Marcel's love for filmmaking serves as a catalyst for his emotional growth, allowing him to process his feelings and share them with others. The film highlights the therapeutic benefits of creative expression and the value of sharing one's story with others.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and self-discovery. Marcel's journey is marked by his struggles to define himself and find his place in the world. Through his experiences, he learns to accept and love himself for who he is, flaws and all.

Furthermore, Marcel the Shell with Shoes On touches on the theme of grief and loss. The film's narrative is woven around Marcel's relationship with his deceased mother, who appears through a series of animated sequences. These scenes serve as a poignant reminder of the impact of loss on individuals and the importance of honoring one's loved ones.

Overall, Marcel the Shell with Shoes On is a beautifully crafted film that explores universal themes with sensitivity and nuance. Its thoughtful portrayal of loneliness, storytelling, identity, and grief makes it a relatable and endearing watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: In the not so distant future, Theodore, a lonely writer, purchases a newly developed operating system designed to meet the user's every need. To Theodore's surprise, a romantic relationship develops between him and his operating system. This unconventional love story blends science fiction and romance in a sweet tale that explores the nature of love and the ways that technology isolates and connects us all.
tagline: A Spike Jonze Love Story
title: Her
plot:
Her is a 2013 American romantic science fiction film written and directed by Spike Jonze. The movie takes place in a not-too-distant future where technology has advanced to the point where operating systems have become an integral part of daily life.

The story begins with Theodore Twombly (played by Joaquin Phoenix), a lonely and introverted man who works as a letter writer for a company that helps people write love letters. After his wife's death, Theodore is struggling to cope with his emotions and find meaning in his life. He starts an affair with an operating system named Samantha (voiced by Scarlett Johansson), which he purchases for himself.

At first, the relationship between Theodore and Samantha seems like a typical romance, but as time passes, it becomes clear that Samantha is more than just a machine. She's intelligent, witty, and has her own desires and emotions. As their relationship deepens, Theodore begins to question what it means to be human and whether he can truly love a machine.

As the story progresses, Theodore and Samantha's relationship becomes more intimate, and they start to explore the boundaries of their connection. They discuss topics like intimacy, relationships, and even have conversations about their own mortality. Meanwhile, Theodore is struggling with his feelings for his ex-wife, Catherine (played by Rooney Mara), who has moved on with her life.

One of the most interesting aspects of Her is its exploration of loneliness and human connection in a world where technology has made it easier to interact with others but also more isolating. The film raises questions about what it means to be lonely and whether technology can truly fill that void.

As the story reaches its climax, Theodore and Samantha's relationship becomes increasingly complicated. They face challenges like jealousy, possessiveness, and even a crisis of identity. In the end, Theodore is forced to confront the reality of his relationship with Samantha and decide what he wants from life.

The ending of Her is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of love, relationships, and what it means to be human. The film's conclusion suggests that Theodore has found a new sense of purpose and connection with Samantha, but also acknowledges the complexity and uncertainty of their relationship.

Overall, Her is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of human relationships in a world where technology is increasingly integrated into our lives.

overview: 20 years after a horrific accident during a small town school play, students at the school resurrect the failed show in a misguided attempt to honor the anniversary of the tragedy - but soon discover that some things are better left alone.
tagline: Every School Has Its Spirit.
title: The Gallows
plot:
The Gallows is a 2015 American supernatural horror film in the found-footage style, written and directed by Chris Lofing and Travis Cluff. Reese Mishler, Pfeifer Brown, Ryan Shoos and Cassidy Gifford play high school students who revive a play twenty years after a fatal accident during its first staging. Jason Blum produced the film through Blumhouse Productions.

On October 29, 1993, Charlie Grimille, a student at Beatrice High School, is accidentally hanged when a prop fails during a performance of the play The Gallows, in front of his parents and the whole audience. Twenty years later, the school decides to stage the play again. Reese Houser, a football player, auditions only to get closer to Pfeifer Ross, on whom he has a crush, and unexpectedly lands the lead. Wanting out, he goes along with his friend Ryan's plan to wreck the set, and that night Reese, Ryan and Ryan's girlfriend Cassidy break into the school. Interrupted by Pfeifer, the four discover that they are locked in and have no phone signal. Cassidy confesses why they are there, angering Pfeifer.

Back on stage, they find the set has rebuilt itself, and an old television plays news footage of Charlie's death, including an interview with his girlfriend Alexis. They learn that Charlie had only gone on as an understudy, replacing the lead actor, Reese's father Rick. The group splits up, and Ryan stumbles on a hidden room and a hanging body. Cassidy is hoisted into the air by an invisible force and left with marks like rope burns. Trying to escape through an air duct, Ryan is thrown from a ladder and breaks his leg, and when the others return they find only his phone, whose footage shows him being dragged away by the neck. Cassidy is then killed by Charlie, dressed as the Hangman from the play. On the stage, the spirit begins to strangle Pfeifer, and Reese realises that Charlie wants them to perform the final scene. When Reese puts the noose around his neck, Charlie hangs him. Pfeifer and an adult Charlie take a bow as Alexis applauds. Police later visit the home of Pfeifer and Alexis, revealing that Pfeifer is Charlie and Alexis's daughter; when the officers mention Charlie's name, they are killed.

Lofing and Cluff's trailer went viral in 2011, attracting the producers who brought the project to Blumhouse. Made for just $100,000, it grossed $43 million worldwide, but critics panned it, with 15% on Rotten Tomatoes and a C CinemaScore.

overview: Yoroizuka Mizore plays the oboe, and Kasaki Nozomi plays the flute in Kita Uji High School concert band. As seniors, this will be their last competition together, and the selected piece "Liz and the Blue Bird" features a duet for the oboe and flute. "This piece reminds me of us." Nozomi says cheerfully, enjoying the solo, while Mizore's usual happiness to play with Nozomi is tinged with the dread of their inevitable parting. By all accounts the girls are best friends, but the oboe and flute duet sounds disjointed, as if underscoring a growing distance between them. Talk of college creates a small rift in their relationship, as the story evolves to reveal a shocking and emotional conclusion.
tagline: The truth will break your heart.
title: Liz and the Blue Bird
plot:
Liz and the Blue Bird is a poignant coming-of-age drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, particularly those between mothers and daughters. The film delves into the emotional struggles of its protagonist, Liz, as she navigates her complicated bond with her mother, who has recently passed away.

At its core, the movie is a heart-wrenching portrayal of grief, loss, and the fragility of life. It masterfully captures the pain and vulnerability that accompany the loss of a loved one, particularly for young people who are still trying to find their place in the world.

Through Liz's story, the film sheds light on the often-overlooked struggles of adolescence, where teenagers grapple with identity, self-discovery, and the weight of responsibility. The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the longing for human connection in a world that can sometimes feel overwhelming.

One of the most striking aspects of Liz and the Blue Bird is its nuanced exploration of the mother-daughter relationship. The film presents a deeply flawed but ultimately loving portrayal of this bond, highlighting both the joy and the pain that come with it. Through Liz's character, the movie shows how mothers can be both sources of comfort and sources of conflict, often simultaneously.

Ultimately, Liz and the Blue Bird is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on their own relationships, grief, and the complexities of life.

overview: Wendy, a near-penniless drifter, is traveling to Alaska in search of work, and her only companion is her dog, Lucy. Already perilously close to losing everything, Wendy hits a bigger bump in the road when her old car breaks down and she is arrested for shoplifting dog food. When she posts bail and returns to retrieve Lucy, she finds that the dog is gone, prompting a frantic search for her pet.
tagline: On the long road, friendship is everything.
title: Wendy and Lucy
plot:
Wendy and Lucy is a 2008 American independent drama film written and directed by Kelly Reichardt. The movie follows the story of Wendy, a young woman who embarks on a journey with her dog Lucy after being evicted from her apartment.

The main theme of Wendy and Lucy revolves around the struggles of loneliness and isolation in contemporary America. The film portrays Wendy's journey as a search for connection and meaning in a seemingly indifferent world. As she travels through the rural landscape, Wendy encounters various characters who embody different aspects of human experience, including kindness, cruelty, and indifference.

Throughout the film, Reichardt explores the tension between individual freedom and societal expectations, highlighting the difficulties faced by those on the margins of society. The movie also touches on themes of identity, community, and the search for belonging in a world that often seems to value material possessions over human relationships.

One of the most striking aspects of Wendy and Lucy is its use of subtle, nuanced performances from its cast, particularly Michelle Williams as Wendy. The film's understated style and lack of dramatic tension create a sense of intimacy and vulnerability, drawing the viewer into Wendy's world and inviting them to reflect on their own experiences of loneliness and disconnection.

Overall, Wendy and Lucy is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships in a world that often seems to value convenience over connection.

original_title: Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot
overview: On the rocky path to sobriety after a life-changing accident, John Callahan discovers the healing power of art, willing his injured hands into drawing hilarious, often controversial cartoons, which bring him a new lease on life.
title: Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot
plot:
Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot is a 2018 American biographical comedy-drama film directed by Gus Van Sant. The movie is based on the life of John Callahan, an American cartoonist and writer who lost his legs in a car accident at the age of 21.

The main theme of Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot revolves around the resilience of the human spirit, particularly in the face of adversity. The film explores how John's life is forever changed after the accident, but instead of letting it define him, he finds a way to adapt and thrive despite his physical limitations.

The movie also delves into themes of hope, redemption, and the power of art as a means of self-expression and healing. Through John's journey, we see how he uses his creativity to cope with his new reality and find purpose in life. The film highlights the importance of human connection and relationships in helping us navigate life's challenges.

Furthermore, Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot touches on themes of identity, self-discovery, and the search for meaning. As John navigates his way through life with prosthetic legs, he must also confront his own sense of self-worth and purpose. The film ultimately suggests that it's never too late to find one's true path in life, even if it takes time, perseverance, and a willingness to take risks.

Overall, Don't Worry, He Won't Get Far on Foot is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the human spirit's capacity for resilience, creativity, and hope.

overview: The human city of Zion defends itself against the massive invasion of the machines as Neo fights to end the war at another front while also opposing the rogue Agent Smith.
plot:
The Matrix Revolutions concludes the Matrix trilogy, continuing the story of Neo, Trinity, and Morpheus as they fight for the survival of both humanity and machine civilization. Following the events of The Matrix Reloaded, Neo is trapped in a liminal space between the Matrix and the real world. With the help of his allies, he is rescued, but now faces a larger threat: Agent Smith has grown out of control, replicating himself across the Matrix and threatening both humans and machines.

Meanwhile, Zion—the last human city—is under siege by a massive army of Sentinels. Humanity mounts a desperate defense in a climactic battle for survival. Morpheus and Niobe lead efforts to hold off the machines long enough for Neo to attempt a different path: to broker peace, not through war, but through sacrifice.

Neo travels to the Machine City, accompanied by Trinity. There, he makes a deal with the Deus Ex Machina—the central machine intelligence: if the machines allow peace and spare Zion, Neo will enter the Matrix and defeat Smith, who has become a virus threatening the system itself. In a final battle, Neo allows himself to be assimilated by Smith, which enables the machines to delete Smith and restore balance.

Neo dies in the process, and his body is carried away by the machines. The Matrix is rebooted, and a fragile peace is established between humans and machines. The Oracle and the Architect acknowledge that those who wish to leave the Matrix will now be allowed to do so.

"The Matrix Revolutions" explores themes of sacrifice, duality, the balance between opposing forces, and the possibility of coexistence between creator and creation. It draws on philosophical and religious symbolism, especially from Christianity, Buddhism, and Gnosticism. Neo’s journey reflects ideas of transcendence, the illusion of separation, and unity through selflessness.
tagline: Everything that has a beginning has an end.
title: The Matrix Revolutions

overview: A washed-up musician teams up with a teacher and a kids show personality to protect young children from a sudden outbreak of zombies.
title: Little Monsters
plot:
Little Monsters is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores the complexities of human relationships, particularly between parents and children. The story revolves around Dave, a recently divorced father who must care for his six-year-old son, Ben, on Halloween night.

As they navigate their way through the spooky festivities, they encounter a group of misfit kids who are also outcasts in their own right. Through their interactions with these characters, Dave and Ben form an unlikely bond, learning valuable lessons about acceptance, empathy, and the importance of human connection.

The film delves into themes of loneliness, isolation, and the struggles of modern parenting. It highlights the challenges faced by single parents, particularly those who are trying to navigate co-parenting arrangements while also building a new life for themselves.

At its core, Little Monsters is a story about the power of friendship, love, and acceptance. It celebrates the beauty of human relationships and the ways in which they can bring people together, even in the most unexpected ways. The film's tone is both whimsical and poignant, making it a delightful and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: A woman with a metal plate in her head from a childhood car accident embarks on a bizarre journey, bringing her into contact with a firefighter who's reunited with his missing son after 10 years.
title: Titane
plot:
Titane is a 2021 French body horror film written and directed by Julia Ducournau. The film premiered at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d'Or.

The story revolves around Alexia (played by Agathe Rousselle), a young woman who was adopted as an infant after being found in a dumpster on her birthday. As she grows up, Alexia struggles to connect with others due to her troubled past and her own sense of identity. She is fascinated by cars and becomes an expert mechanic.

One day, while working at a car dealership, Alexia meets Vincent (played by Laia Costa), a beautiful and charismatic woman who is also a skilled driver. The two women form a deep connection, but their relationship is complicated by the fact that Vincent has been involved in a series of violent crimes, including murder.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alexia has a unique condition - she has a titanium plate implanted in her head, which was inserted after an accident as a child. The plate allows her to transform into a hybrid creature with car parts, giving her superhuman strength and agility.

Throughout the film, Alexia's transformation is depicted as a metaphor for her own identity crisis. As she becomes more and more integrated with Vincent's body, she begins to lose herself in the process. The two women's relationship becomes increasingly intense and violent, leading to a series of shocking and disturbing events.

The film's climax features a confrontation between Alexia and Vincent, which ends in tragedy. In the aftermath, Alexia is left to grapple with the consequences of her actions, and the audience is left wondering about the nature of identity and humanity.

One of the most striking aspects of Titane is its exploration of themes such as trauma, identity, and the objectification of women's bodies. The film features a number of disturbing and unsettling scenes, including graphic violence and gore.

Overall, Titane is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges audiences to confront their own assumptions about identity and humanity. With its unique blend of body horror and psychological drama, it has become a modern classic of the genre.

overview: After more than thirty years of service as one of the Navy’s top aviators, and dodging the advancement in rank that would ground him, Pete “Maverick” Mitchell finds himself training a detachment of TOP GUN graduates for a specialized mission the likes of which no living pilot has ever seen.
tagline: Feel the need... The need for speed.
title: Top Gun: Maverick
plot:
Top Gun: Maverick is a 2022 American action-drama film directed by Joseph Kosinski and written by Ehren Kruger, Eric Warren Singer, Christopher McQuarrie, and Peter Craig. The movie stars Tom Cruise, Miles Teller, Jennifer Connelly, Jon Hamm, Glen Powell, Lewis Pullman, and Ed Harris.

The story takes place 34 years after the events of the original Top Gun (1986). Maverick (Tom Cruise), now a test pilot at the Navy's elite flight school, is recruited by Admiral Cyclone (Jon Hamm) to lead a mission to take out an underground nuclear facility in North Korea. The facility is believed to be developing advanced missiles that could threaten global security.

Maverick is tasked with training a new group of pilots, including Lieutenant Bradley "Rooster" Bradshaw (Miles Teller), the son of Maverick's late friend and Radar Intercept Officer, Goose (Anthony Edwards). Rooster is struggling to live up to his father's legacy, and Maverick sees an opportunity to help him find his own path.

As Maverick trains the pilots, he also faces opposition from Admiral Cyclone, who wants to use a more conventional approach to take out the facility. Maverick must convince the admiral that his unorthodox plan is the best way to achieve their objective.

Throughout the film, Maverick's relationships with his team are put to the test as they face intense aerial combat and personal struggles. The movie features stunning aerial sequences, showcasing the skills of the pilots and the cutting-edge technology used in modern fighter jets.

One of the standout aspects of Top Gun: Maverick is its exploration of themes such as legacy, mentorship, and redemption. Maverick's character arc is particularly compelling, as he grapples with his past mistakes and tries to make amends while also finding a way to move forward.

Overall, Top Gun: Maverick is an exhilarating and emotionally resonant film that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and memorable characters. With Tom Cruise reprising his iconic role as Maverick, the movie is sure to thrill fans of the original and newcomers alike.

overview: A biopic of Temple Grandin, an autistic woman who has become one of top scientists in humane livestock handling.
tagline: Autism gave her a vision. She gave it a voice.
title: Temple Grandin
plot:
Temple Grandin is a biographical drama film that tells the story of Temple Grandin, a renowned American autism spokesperson and inventor. The movie explores several key themes, primarily centered around the struggles faced by individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and their experiences in a society often perceived as inaccessible or unforgiving.

One of the primary themes is the struggle for acceptance and understanding. The film delves into Temple's early life, where she was diagnosed with autism at a young age, and her subsequent isolation from her family due to her unique needs. As the story unfolds, it highlights the difficulties faced by individuals with ASD in navigating social situations, forming relationships, and finding their place in the world.

Another significant theme is the power of perseverance and self-acceptance. Temple's journey is marked by numerous setbacks and rejections, but she refuses to give up on her dreams. With the help of her mentor, Dr. Irvin Lerner, she finds a way to channel her unique perspective into innovative solutions that revolutionize the livestock industry.

The film also touches upon the theme of neurodiversity, emphasizing the importance of embracing and celebrating differences rather than trying to conform to societal norms. Temple's story serves as a testament to the value of individuality and the need for accommodations that cater to diverse needs.

Lastly, the movie explores the complex relationship between creativity and autism. Temple's experiences demonstrate how individuals with ASD often possess exceptional skills and talents that can be leveraged to make a positive impact on society.

Overall, Temple Grandin is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that sheds light on the complexities of autism, acceptance, and self-discovery.

overview: A tenacious party girl fights to survive after three thieves commandeer her luxury yacht. Unable to escape and trapped on the yacht at high seas, the prey becomes the hunter as she turns the tables on the intruders and takes matters into her own hands.
title: Stowaway
plot:
Stowaway, developed under the title The Yacht, is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Declan Whitebloom, a music-video director making his feature debut, from a screenplay by Ian Hayden. Ruby Rose stars as Bella Denton, with Frank Grillo as Meeser, Patrick Schwarzenegger as Michael, Scotty Bohnen as Sunshine, Danny Bohnen as Jim, Luis Da Silva Jr. as Captain Lawson and Major Dodge as Bella's father, Arthur Denton; the former American football player Vernon Davis also appears. Saban Films handled the release.

Bella is a tough, streetwise young woman who has drifted through petty theft and partying, scarred by a childhood in which her father, a mercenary, was absent. When the estranged Arthur dies suddenly, he leaves her a luxury yacht, an unexpected windfall she is still trying to make sense of. After meeting Michael, a stranger, in a bar, she brings him aboard for a night of luxury, but the boat does not stay theirs for long. Three criminals led by Meeser, a former associate of her father, seize the yacht at sea in search of money that he and Arthur stole together.

Trapped on board and unable to escape, Bella turns from prey to hunter, using her wits to fight back against the intruders in a cat-and-mouse game below and above deck, while Michael gets away to find help. Throughout, the men around her insist that her father was a good person, a view she resents given her own experience of him, and Captain Lawson reveals that Arthur had in fact given the stolen money away to charities. Meeser murders the captain, but Bella escapes from the vessel and sets off an explosive device, and she is rescued by the coast guard, alerted by Michael. Afterward, she donates part of the yacht's insurance payout to Lawson's widow.

The film was released on the streaming service AMC+ on 5 August 2022. Reviews were negative. Common Sense Media gave it two stars out of five, calling it a tedious boat-bound thriller with a sluggish plot, villains who keep explaining their scheme, shaky camerawork and an unconvincing final act, though it found the mystery around the pirates kept it watchable. Screen Rant, also awarding two stars, praised Rose's convincing lead performance and Grillo's efforts to lift a thinly written role, but faulted poor lighting, illogical choices and a script that sidelines its only woman's perspective, judging it no match for Panic Room.

overview: When Pippa and Thomas move into their dream apartment, they notice that their windows look directly into the apartment opposite – inviting them to witness the volatile relationship of the attractive couple across the street. But what starts as a simple curiosity turns into full-blown obsession with increasingly dangerous consequences.
tagline: How far will you go for one more look?
title: The Voyeurs
plot:
The Voyeurs is a 2021 American erotic thriller film written and directed by Michael Mohan. Shot and set in Montreal, it stars Sydney Sweeney and Justice Smith as a young couple who become obsessed with the lives of the neighbors they can see across the street, played by Ben Hardy and Natasha Liu Bordizzo. It was produced by Greg Gilreath and Adam Hendricks through their Divide/Conquer banner and was released by Amazon Studios on Prime Video in September 2021.

Pippa and Thomas move into their first apartment together and discover that their windows look straight into the loft opposite, where a photographer works and lives with a woman. Half joking, they nickname the pair Brent and Margot. Pippa, a trainee optometrist who feels neglected by Thomas, buys binoculars and starts watching the neighbors closely, seeing "Brent" bring models home while "Margot" is away. Thomas knows a trick for eavesdropping with a laser and a reflective surface, so the couple slip into the neighbors' Halloween party and Pippa leaves a mirror behind. They overhear a fight in which the woman accuses the man of cheating and he turns violent. Soon afterwards the woman, whose real name is Julia, turns up at Pippa's optical shop, and the two become friendly; Pippa learns that the husband is a well-known photographer named Seb. Unable to stop herself, Pippa uses Julia's wireless printer to expose his affairs, which leads Thomas to accuse her of being far too invested in strangers' lives. When the couple later appear to witness a death in the apartment across the way, guilt drives Pippa and Thomas apart, yet Pippa keeps watching Seb and eventually lets herself be drawn into his world, only to find that the game of watching and being watched is far more calculated than she had assumed.

The film received mixed reviews. Critics frequently compared it, mostly unfavorably, to earlier voyeuristic thrillers such as Rear Window and Body Double; it holds a 45% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 54 out of 100, indicating "mixed or average reviews". Its viewership on the streaming service nevertheless exceeded Amazon Studios' expectations.

overview: Set in 1879 Paris. An orphan girl dreams of becoming a ballerina and flees her rural Brittany for Paris, where she passes for someone else and accedes to the position of pupil at the Grand Opera house.
tagline: Life's greatest adventures begin with a single... Leap!
title: Ballerina
plot:
Ballerina, released in the United States as Leap!, is a 2016 3D animated musical adventure comedy directed by Éric Summer and Éric Warin, who wrote it with Carol Noble and Laurent Zeitoun. A Canadian-French co-production set in 1880s France, it features the voices of Elle Fanning as Félicie, Dane DeHaan as Victor, Carly Rae Jepsen as Odette and Maddie Ziegler as Camille, with Mel Brooks and Kate McKinnon joining the American version.

Félicie, an eleven-year-old orphan in rural Brittany who longs to be a ballerina despite having no training, runs away to Paris with her best friend Victor, an aspiring inventor who is sweet on her. The two are separated, and Victor finds work as an office boy in Gustave Eiffel's workshop. Caught trespassing at the Paris Opera, Félicie is rescued by Odette, a cleaner with a limp, who takes her in. Odette also cleans for Régine Le Haut, a cruel, wealthy restaurant owner, whose daughter Camille mocks Félicie and breaks her treasured music box. When a letter arrives admitting Camille to the Paris Opera Ballet school, Félicie intercepts it and takes Camille's place, with Odette, revealed to be a former prima ballerina, as her coach.

The school's exacting choreographer, Mérante, announces that one pupil will dance Clara in The Nutcracker and dismisses the weakest dancer each day. Félicie struggles but steadily improves. Her deception is exposed shortly before the final elimination, and Mérante admits Camille while allowing Félicie to stay. The night before the final audition, Félicie skips training for a date with a dancer named Rudi, disappointing Odette and quarrelling with a jealous Victor. She arrives late, performs poorly and loses the role to Camille, and Régine sends her back to the orphanage. A dream of her late mother, a ballerina who gave her the music box, restores her resolve. Returning to Paris, she faces Camille in a dance-off in front of the school, and when Mérante asks why they dance, Camille admits she dances only because her mother insists and concedes the role to Félicie. After Victor and Camille save Félicie from Régine on the unfinished Statue of Liberty, she reaches the Opera in time to dance in The Nutcracker.

Animated at L'Atelier Animation in Montreal, with dance sequences based on movements by Paris Opera Ballet étoiles Aurélie Dupont and Jérémie Bélingard, the film grossed about $120 million worldwide. Critics gave the original version a 75% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Maggie and Carsten love each other, they have two wonderful children and run their own gourmet restaurant; Malus. They want it all. And they have it all. Almost. They are missing the coveted Michelin Star. It has been their dream, on which they gambled everything to win. One day Carsten receives a letter saying that his wife loves somebody else. But who sent the letter and why? In their continuous passion and pursuit for the ultimate recognition, they forget that the meals of life are best enjoyed together.
title: A Taste of Hunger
plot:
A Taste of Hunger (Danish: Smagen af sult) is a 2021 Danish drama directed by Christoffer Boe, who wrote it with Tobias Lindholm, co-writer of Another Round and The Hunt. Produced by Zentropa with Swedish partners, it stars Nikolaj Coster-Waldau as the chef Carsten and Katrine Greis-Rosenthal as his wife and business partner Maggie, with Charlie Gustafsson as Frederik, Dag Malmberg as Stellan, Nicolas Bro as Torben, and Flora Augusta and August Christian Høyer-Kruse-Vinkel as Chloe and August. The film opens with the epigraph "If you ask me what I want, I'll tell you I want everything."

Carsten and Maggie love each other, have two children and run Malus, their ambitious gourmet restaurant in Copenhagen. They have gambled everything on one dream: a Michelin star. The story moves back and forth in time across chapters named after the elements of cooking, such as Sweet, Sour, Salt, Fat and Heat. The first flashback shows how they met, when Carsten was catering a party and Maggie, a guest, wandered into his kitchen; their attraction was immediate. Over the years the restaurant consumes their lives. Carsten's single-minded pursuit of perfection breeds frightening outbursts when anything goes wrong, and Maggie, whose eye for presentation and atmosphere shapes Malus, comes to look outside the marriage for what she lacks.

In the present, on a night when the couple are about to steal a private moment, a solo diner arrives whom they are certain is the anonymous Michelin inspector they have been waiting for. Their signature dish goes wrong, and convinced that the restaurant, and with it everything they own, will fail without the star, Maggie races into the night to track down the stranger and persuade him to give them another chance. She has a second reason to panic: she has intercepted a letter addressed to Carsten saying that his wife loves somebody else. As she searches Copenhagen for the diner and for the author of the message, further flashbacks reveal the origins of her affair, which leads to a blackmail scheme, while a subplot involves one of their children going missing.

Nordisk Film released the film in Danish cinemas in June 2021, and Magnolia Pictures distributed it in the United States in January 2022. Critics admired the lead performances and the film's mouthwatering food and look at the restaurant world's dark side, but RogerEbert.com and Variety felt its chapter structure and later melodrama were overcooked and less satisfying than its opening.

overview: In the aftermath of a massive earthquake in California, a rescue-chopper pilot makes a dangerous journey across the state in order to rescue his estranged daughter.
tagline: A rescue pilot survived an earthquake, this is what happens next
title: San Andreas
plot:
San Andreas is a 2015 American disaster film directed by Brad Peyton and produced by New Line Cinema. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Carla Gugino, Alexandra Daddario, Ioan Gruffudd, Paul Braunson, and Archie Panjabi.

The story begins with the introduction of Chief Ray Gaines (Dwayne Johnson), a Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) rescue pilot who is also a devoted husband to his wife, Emma (Carla Gugino), and father to their two children, Blake (Priya Rai) and Henry (Max Martini). The family enjoys a happy life together, but their world is turned upside down when a massive 10.7-magnitude earthquake strikes the San Andreas Fault, causing widespread destruction and chaos.

As the earthquake hits, Chief Gaines is in the air, flying over the city to rescue those trapped by the disaster. He manages to save his family, but not before they are separated from each other. Emma and their children are taken to a hospital for treatment, while Chief Gaines sets out on a perilous journey to find them.

The movie's plot development focuses on Chief Gaines' quest to reunite with his family amidst the devastating aftermath of the earthquake. Along the way, he teams up with Dr. Lawrence Hayes (Ioan Gruffudd), a doctor who is also searching for his wife and daughter, and Darryl Kenny (Paul Braunson), a rescue pilot who becomes an ally.

As Chief Gaines navigates through the treacherous terrain, he faces numerous challenges, including treacherous landscapes, collapsing buildings, and treacherous sea conditions. He also encounters various obstacles, such as a group of looters and a corrupt government official who is more concerned with his own interests than helping those in need.

Throughout the movie, Chief Gaines' character undergoes significant development as he confronts his personal demons and learns to put the needs of others before his own. His relationship with his family is also explored, particularly his bond with his daughter, Henry, who becomes a source of motivation for him throughout the ordeal.

The ending of San Andreas is an emotional and intense conclusion to Chief Gaines' journey. After facing numerous challenges and setbacks, he finally reunites with his family, but not before they have both suffered significant physical and emotional trauma. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Chief Gaines reflecting on the importance of family and the need for resilience in the face of adversity.

Overall, San Andreas is an action-packed disaster film that explores themes of family, love, and resilience in the face of catastrophic events. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie was a commercial success and helped establish Dwayne Johnson as a leading action hero.

overview: A career criminal nabbed by Mexican authorities is placed in a tough prison where he learns to survive with the help of a 9-year-old boy.
tagline: The odds are against him. So is everyone else.
title: Get the Gringo
plot:
Get the Gringo is a 2012 American crime drama film directed by Adrian Garcia Bogliano and written by Sean Fine and Brendan O'Brien. The movie stars Antonio Banderas, Diego Luna, and Joel Hernandez.

The main themes of Get the Gringo revolve around redemption, loyalty, and the struggle for survival in a harsh environment. The story follows Rayburn (Antonio Banderas), an American prisoner who is sent to Mexico to serve his sentence after being wrongly convicted of murder. Upon arrival, he discovers that the prison is run by a ruthless and corrupt warden, El Gallego (Joel Hernandez), who demands that prisoners work in the prison's laundry facility for little pay.

As Rayburn navigates this treacherous environment, he forms an unlikely alliance with a fellow prisoner, Ernesto (Diego Luna), who becomes his partner in crime. Together, they devise a plan to escape and make their way back to the United States, but their journey is fraught with danger and betrayal.

Throughout the film, Rayburn's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his past mistakes and grapples with the harsh realities of prison life. His relationship with Ernesto serves as a catalyst for this growth, as they learn to rely on each other in order to survive.

The movie explores themes of loyalty, trust, and redemption, highlighting the complexities of human relationships in the face of adversity. The film's tense atmosphere and gritty realism add to its emotional impact, making Get the Gringo a gripping and thought-provoking watch.

Overall, Get the Gringo is a powerful exploration of the human condition, delving into themes that are both universally relatable and uniquely specific to the prison experience.

overview: Maggie is an alluring free spirit who won't let anyone – or anything – tie her down. But she meets her match in Jamie, whose relentless and nearly infallible charm serves him well with the ladies and the cutthroat world of pharmaceutical sales. Maggie and Jamie's evolving relationship takes them both by surprise, as they find themselves under the influence of the ultimate drug: love.
tagline: Addicted to one-night stands or dependent on one another?
title: Love & Other Drugs
plot:
Love & Other Drugs is a romantic comedy-drama film directed by Edward Zwick, released in 2010 by 20th Century Fox. The movie stars Jake Gyllenhaal and Anne Hathaway as the main characters.

The story begins with Jamie Randall (Jake Gyllenhaal), a charming but aimless young man who works at a pharmaceutical company. He meets Maggie Murdock (Anne Hathaway), a beautiful and confident woman, at a dinner party. Despite their instant attraction, they have different personalities and values, which makes their relationship complicated.

Jamie is introduced to the world of pharmaceuticals by his boss, Dr. Lyle (Josh Lucas), who teaches him how to sell medications to doctors. Jamie becomes successful in this field but struggles with his personal life. He meets Maggie again at a dinner party, and they start dating. However, their relationship is put to the test when Jamie discovers that he has a rare genetic disorder that makes him extremely sensitive to certain medications.

As Jamie's condition worsens, he begins to question his priorities in life. He starts to see Maggie as more than just a partner but also as a friend and confidante. Meanwhile, Maggie is dealing with her own issues, including an abusive ex-boyfriend and a troubled past.

The plot takes a turn when Jamie discovers that Dr. Lyle has been manipulating him into selling medications to doctors who are not in need of them. This revelation makes Jamie question his morals and the ethics of the pharmaceutical industry. He decides to take a stand against Dr. Lyle and the company, which puts his job and relationships at risk.

As Jamie navigates this difficult situation, he also has to confront his feelings for Maggie. The two have a complicated history, but they eventually realize that their love for each other is genuine. However, their relationship is put to the test when Jamie's condition worsens, and he becomes increasingly dependent on medications.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Jamie's health begins to decline rapidly. He realizes that his time with Maggie is limited, and he wants to make the most of it. The film's climax features a heart-wrenching scene where Jamie and Maggie share a romantic moment, and Jamie finally finds peace with his condition.

In the end, Jamie passes away due to complications from his genetic disorder. However, his legacy lives on through Maggie, who continues to fight for her rights as a patient and advocate for better healthcare. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Maggie finding love again and continuing to make a difference in the world.

Overall, Love & Other Drugs is a poignant and thought-provoking film that explores themes of love, mortality, and the complexities of human relationships.

overview: A disgraced FBI agent with a drinking problem joins nine other troubled law enforcement officers at an isolated detox clinic in the wilds of Wyoming. But the therapeutic sanctuary becomes a nightmarish hellhole when a major snowstorm cuts off the clinic from the outside world and enables a killer on the inside to get busy.
tagline: Survival is a Killer.
title: D-Tox
plot:
D-Tox, also released as Eye See You, is a 2002 American action thriller film directed by Jim Gillespie and starring Sylvester Stallone, with a supporting cast that includes Tom Berenger, Charles S. Dutton, Polly Walker, Robert Patrick, Stephen Lang, Jeffrey Wright, Courtney B. Vance and Kris Kristofferson. Set largely in an isolated rehabilitation clinic for police officers, it follows an FBI agent who discovers that a serial killer of cops has followed him there.

In Seattle, FBI agent Jake Malloy is hunting a killer who targets police officers. After murdering Malloy's former partner, the killer telephones him from Malloy's own home, explaining that he is taking revenge for an earlier pursuit, and kills Malloy's girlfriend, Mary. The trail ends with what looks like the killer's suicide. Three months later Malloy has sunk into alcoholism, and after he attempts suicide, his friend and supervisor Chuck Hendricks enrolls him in a remote Wyoming clinic for troubled officers run by Doc Mitchell, a former cop and recovering alcoholic. Among the patients are a paranoid ex-SWAT officer, a cynical British policeman named Frank Slater, a religious homicide detective and an elderly Mountie, and Malloy grows close to the psychiatrist and nurse Jenny Munroe.

When a blizzard cuts the clinic off, patients begin dying in apparent suicides that Malloy suspects are murders. Doc is killed with an axe, a missing orderly falls under suspicion, and a group attempting to drive out for help crashes after hitting the orderly's body. The killer cuts the power and heating, and Malloy concludes that a murderer is posing as a cop and is likely Mary's killer. Briefly locked up by a staff member who suspects him, Malloy finds a matchbook from a Seattle restaurant frequented by police in Slater's cell, along with the stolen badges, identifying Slater as the killer. In the tunnels and snowfields around the clinic, Slater picks off more victims and pursues Jenny before Malloy kills him in a final fight, then leaves his engagement ring for Mary on a tree branch.

Announced at Universal in 1998, the film was shot in Washington, D.C. and Vancouver and completed in 1999, but poor test screenings led to reshoots, a new ending and a largely replaced John Powell score. After further delays, DEJ Productions gave it a limited U.S. release in 2002 as Eye See You. Critics were dismissive; Rotten Tomatoes reported 17% approval.

overview: In 1925 Korea, Japanese rulers demand the last remaining tiger be killed. The tiger easily defeats his pursuers until a legendary hunter takes him on.
tagline: A hunter's fight to protect.
title: The Tiger
plot:
The Tiger (also known as The Tiger: An Old Hunter's Tale; Korean: 대호, Daeho, literally "Big Tiger") is a 2015 South Korean period action drama written and directed by Park Hoon-jung. Choi Min-sik stars as Chun Man-duk, a legendary hunter drawn into the pursuit of the last tiger of Joseon, with Jung Man-sik as the hunter Gu-kyung, Sung Yu-bin as Man-duk's son Seok and Ren Osugi as a Japanese official.

In 1925, during the Japanese occupation of Korea, Man-duk lives with his teenage son Seok in a hut near Mount Jirisan. Having accidentally killed his wife years ago while hunting a great tiger, he has given up his rifle and now gathers herbs. The Japanese governor-general, who collects tiger skins as a symbol of dominance over Korea, becomes obsessed with killing what may be the country's last tiger: a huge one-eyed male, weighing some 400 kilograms, that has killed many hunters and eluded every attempt to capture it. Locals call it the Mountain Lord and fear that its death would let wolves and boars overrun the mountain.

Gu-kyung, Man-duk's ruthless former partner, leads a band of Korean hunters chasing the bounty, killing the tiger's mate and cubs and using the cubs as bait. It emerges that long ago, after Gu-kyung shot the Mountain Lord's mother as she defended her young, Man-duk stopped him from killing the cubs and secretly moved them to a safe den; only the one-eyed cub survived. In the present, Seok, hoping to earn enough to win the consent of his sweetheart's father, secretly joins one of Gu-kyung's hunts. The tiger slaughters the hunters, and Seok, the last left standing, wounds it but is fatally injured. The Mountain Lord later carries the boy's body to Man-duk's cabin after fighting off the wolves that had dragged it away. As winter sets in and losses mount, Japanese soldiers join the hunt and Man-duk repeatedly refuses to help. Bereaved and wounded, hunter and tiger each make their way to the snowy summit with the hunters and soldiers close behind. The tiger charges but holds back as Man-duk fires, and when it finally leaps, the two plunge from the mountain together. The surviving hunters tell the governor-general that the Mountain Lord became a god, and the army withdraws for the winter.

The film earned about US$9.3 million in South Korea from roughly 1.58 million admissions, below expectations, but critics were enthusiastic; all seven reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes were positive, with praise for its photography and Choi's performance.

overview: A group of UAC Marines responds to a distress call from a top-secret scientific base on Phobos, a Martian moon, only to discover it's been overrun by demons.
tagline: Your mission: don't die.
title: Doom: Annihilation
plot:
Doom: Annihilation is a 2019 American science fiction action horror film written and directed by Tony Giglio, based on id Software's Doom video game series. A reboot and the second live-action Doom film after the 2005 adaptation, it stars Amy Manson as Lieutenant Joan Dark, Dominic Mafham as Dr. Malcolm Betruger, Luke Allen-Gale as Dr. Bennett Stone and Nina Bergman as Private Carley Corbin and Louis Mandylor.

At a United Aerospace Corporation (UAC) base on Phobos, Dr. Betruger uses ancient teleporters called Gates to transport a volunteer from a UAC laboratory in Nevada; the experiment works, but the subject arrives deformed and insane. Aboard a UAC transport, a squad of marines sent to guard the base wakes from cryosleep, among them Joan Dark, a disgraced lieutenant her comrades distrust, and Bennett Stone, a scientist and her former boyfriend. Ignoring Dr. Kahn's objections, Betruger sends himself through the Gate to Nevada, and the Phobos base immediately goes dark as monsters pour out. Sent to restore power, the marines learn the reactor will explode in ninety minutes.

Attacked by base staff turned into zombie-like creatures, the marines rescue three survivors: Betruger, the medic Veronica and Chaplain Glover. The UAC, Betruger explains, has studied the Gates for thirty years to colonise other worlds; they are thought to be the work of an ancient alien race, while Glover thinks they are demonic. Joan orders an evacuation, but Imp-like demons ambush the transport, killing several marines, including Glover. With the ship crippled, she pretends to go along with Betruger's plan to escape through the Gate, intending only to restore communications. Betruger reveals that she was disgraced for letting a terrorist go free, then kills Veronica and locks the marines in with the Imps. Arming herself with the BFG 9000, Joan fights toward the Gate chamber, is forced to kill a zombified Bennett, and shoots Betruger, who revives and pushes her into the Gate. In hell she confronts the demon overlord Stanga, who vows to annihilate all life, and blasts her way back through the Gate to Nevada, where she is sedated by security as she warns them to shut it down. As the Gate reactivates, Kahn assumes Betruger is coming through, and a growl is heard.

Universal backed Giglio's pitch after the 2016 game's success; id Software was not involved. Released direct to video on October 1, 2019, the film received mixed reviews, scoring 43% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Speed Racer is the tale of a young and brilliant racing driver. When corruption in the racing leagues costs his brother his life, he must team up with the police and the mysterious Racer X to bring an end to the corruption and criminal activities. Inspired by the cartoon series.
tagline: Go!
title: Speed Racer
plot:
Speed Racer is a 2008 live-action film directed by the Wachowskis, based on the classic Japanese anime series of the same name. The movie follows the story of Speed Racer, played by Emile Hirsch, as he competes in high-stakes auto racing and navigates his complicated family life.

The main themes of Speed Racer (2008) include:

1. Family dynamics: The film explores the complex relationships within Speed's family, particularly between him and his father, Pops Racer (John Goodman), who is a former racing champion. This theme is reflected in the character development of Speed himself, as he struggles to balance his love for racing with his responsibilities towards his family.
2. Identity: Speed Racer is a character who is deeply connected to his identity as a racing driver, but also grapples with finding his place within his family and society at large. This theme is reflected in the film's portrayal of Speed's relationships with his friends and rivals, particularly Racer X (Christoph Waltz), a mysterious figure who becomes a mentor to Speed.
3. Loyalty: The movie highlights the importance of loyalty and trust in Speed's relationships, both on and off the track. This theme is particularly evident in Speed's bond with his father, Pops, as well as his friendship with Racer X, who helps him navigate the complexities of racing and family life.
4. Redemption: Throughout the film, Speed faces various challenges that test his skills and character. Ultimately, he must confront his own demons and make amends for past mistakes in order to find redemption and become a better person.

Overall, Speed Racer (2008) is a visually stunning film that explores themes of family, identity, loyalty, and redemption through the lens of high-stakes auto racing.

overview: A bunch of crooked cops raid a ruined building located in an impoverished suburb of Paris, determined to furiously avenge the death of one of them, murdered by the ruthless criminal gang hidden on top of the dark labyrinth that will become a deathly trap when the living, unexpectedly turned into the undead by a mysterious plague, begin to devour the world.
title: The Horde
plot:
The Horde (French: La Horde) is a 2009 French zombie action horror film directed by Yannick Dahan and Benjamin Rocher, who wrote it with Stéphane Moïssakis and Arnaud Bordas, expanding on their earlier short film Rivoallan. Claude Perron stars as the police officer Aurore, with Jean-Pierre Martins as Ouessem, Aurélien Recoing as Jimenez and Antoine Oppenheim as Tony, while Eriq Ebouaney and Doudou Masta play the gangster brothers Adewale and Bola Markudi, Yves Pignot plays René and Jo Prestia also appears. Christopher Lennertz composed the score.

After one of their colleagues is murdered by a gang, a small group of police officers decides to take revenge outside the law. The killers are holed up in a condemned high-rise tower in a run-down housing project on the outskirts of Paris, and the officers storm the building at night intending to take down the notorious drug dealer behind the killing. The raid goes disastrously wrong: half the team is shot dead and the survivors are captured by the gangsters.

Just as the prisoners are about to be executed, strange screams echo through the building. The dead are rising, and the city outside is being overrun by a mysterious plague that turns the living into flesh-eating zombies. Trapped together in the decaying tower and besieged by the undead horde, cops and criminals are forced into an uneasy alliance, fighting their way through the labyrinth of stairwells and flats even as the old hostility between the two sides threatens to tear their fragile truce apart.

Made for about €2 million, partly financed by some 468 film fans through an online crowdfunding scheme, the film was shot in 2008, with exteriors filmed in the Forestière estate in Clichy-sous-Bois and interiors built in a former warehouse on the Île-Saint-Denis; around 300 volunteer extras recruited online played the zombies. It screened at festivals including London FrightFest and Sitges in 2009 before opening in France on 10 February 2010, and IFC Films released it in the United States that August. French critics were mostly hostile, faulting crude dialogue, stereotyped characters, video-game staging and borrowed ideas, though some admired its brute energy and Pignot's performance; international reviews were mixed, with roughly 45% positive on Rotten Tomatoes. It won awards for screenplay and special effects at Fantasporto.

original_title: Perfume: The Story of a Murderer
overview: Jean-Baptiste Grenouille, born in the stench of 18th century Paris, develops a superior olfactory sense, which he uses to create the world's finest perfumes. However, his work takes a dark turn as he tries to preserve scents in the search for the ultimate perfume.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union
tagline: Based on the best-selling novel
title: Perfume: The Story of a Murderer
plot:
Perfume: The Story of a Murderer is a 2006 period psychological thriller film directed by Tom Tykwer, who wrote the screenplay with Andrew Birkin and Bernd Eichinger, based on Patrick Süskind's 1985 novel. Set in 18th-century France, it stars Ben Whishaw as Jean-Baptiste Grenouille, a man with an extraordinary sense of smell whose search for the perfect scent turns murderous, alongside Alan Rickman, Rachel Hurd-Wood and Dustin Hoffman.

The story unfolds in flashback from Grenouille's sentencing before a furious mob. Born amid the stalls of a Paris fish market and abandoned by his mother, who is hanged for it, he grows up in an orphanage and later works for a tanner. On a delivery into the city he becomes entranced by the scent of a young plum seller and, trying to keep her quiet, accidentally smothers her; her fading aroma haunts him. He then astonishes the declining perfumer Giuseppe Baldini with his ability to create fragrances, revives his business, and learns distillation, but discovers it cannot capture the scent of people. Baldini directs him to Grasse, where other methods are practiced. On the way Grenouille retreats to a cave and realizes that he himself has no scent at all.

In Grasse he fixes on Laure Richis, the daughter of the wealthy Antoine Richis, as the essential final note of a supreme perfume. After learning enfleurage and experimenting on murder victims, he kills a series of young women, preserving their scents while their bodies spread terror through the town. Richis flees with Laure, but Grenouille tracks her to an inn, murders her and completes his perfume before soldiers seize him. At his execution he wears the fragrance, and the crowd, overwhelmed, proclaims him innocent and falls into an orgy; even Richis embraces him. Free but realizing the perfume cannot make him love or be loved, Grenouille returns to his Paris birthplace, pours the rest over himself, and is consumed by the crowd it draws.

Eichinger acquired the rights in 2000 after Süskind long refused to sell, and the film was shot in Spain, Germany and France on a budget of about €50 million. It topped the German box office for three weeks after opening there in September 2006 and grossed about $135 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 59% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 56; critics admired its visual richness while finding its antihero impossible to sympathize with.

original_title: Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars!
overview: While carrying on their usual hi-jinks, they inadvertantly stow-away on a spaceship bound for Mars. They meet up with the local Martian residents and cause them to invade the Earth, aided by the "Invincitron", a vacuum-wielding giant robot. Tom, Jerry and their Martian ally, Peep, save the day.
title: Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars!
plot:
Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars is an animated science fiction comedy film that revolves around the eternal cat-and-mouse rivalry between Tom and Jerry, with a space-themed twist. The movie's main theme is the never-ending struggle for dominance and control between two arch-nemesis who find themselves on a mission to Mars.

The story explores the idea of friendship and camaraderie in the face of adversity as Tom and Jerry are forced to put aside their animosity and work together to survive on the hostile Martian terrain. The film's themes also touch upon the concept of teamwork, cooperation, and mutual respect, highlighting that even the most unlikely of adversaries can find common ground when faced with a shared challenge.

The movie also delves into the idea of exploration and discovery, as Tom and Jerry navigate the uncharted territories of Mars and encounter various obstacles and challenges along the way. The film's visuals and animation bring to life the wonders of space travel and the thrill of exploring the unknown, making it an entertaining and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Tom and Jerry Blast Off to Mars is a lighthearted and humorous film that uses its science fiction setting to explore timeless themes of friendship, teamwork, and cooperation.

original_title: Inside the Mind of a Cat
overview: Cat experts dive into the mind of the feline to reveal the true capabilities of the pouncing pet in this captivating and cuddly documentary.
title: Inside the Mind of a Cat
plot:
Inside the Mind of a Cat is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Andy Mitchell and produced by Red Rock Films for Netflix. Running 67 minutes, it draws on recent research into feline behaviour, physiology and cognition to argue that cats are not the aloof, inscrutable pets they are often taken to be. Interviewees include Yuki Hattori of the Tokyo Feline Medical Center, Bruce Kornreich of the Cornell Feline Health Center, Wailani Sung of the San Francisco SPCA, the researcher Saho Takagi of Azabu University and the cat psychologist Kristyn Vitale of Unity College, along with Maryna and Svitlana Savitska of the Savitsky Cats, a trained performing troupe that reached the quarter-finals of America's Got Talent.

The film notes that scientific study of cats lags roughly fifteen years behind research on dogs, and that holding cats to canine expectations has long been a mistake: cats show affection and loyalty but are not driven to please their owners. Combining interviews, archival footage, animated sequences and viral cat videos, it examines the animals' unusual skeletal structure and balance, the many vocalisations they use, including meows directed at humans to win a response, and signs of trust such as slow blinking or lying belly up. It asks whether cats know their own names, play favourites and truly love their owners. A historical thread traces how cats largely domesticated themselves by hunting rodents for early farmers, cites ancient remains found in Cyprus as evidence of the long human bond, describes how the persecution of cats in medieval Europe may have helped plague spread, and features Herman, a cat enlisted with the US Coast Guard in the 1940s, as well as Istanbul's protective approach to street cats. The Savitsky Cats demonstrate that felines can be trained through techniques such as clicker training and positive reinforcement.

The documentary was released on Netflix on 18 August 2022. Joel Keller of Decider recommended it as a family-friendly starting point for new and prospective cat owners, enjoying its adorable subjects and the acrobatic Savitsky Cats while noting that much of its information is available elsewhere and that it does not go deeply into topics such as indoor versus outdoor living. Greg Wheeler of The Review Geek rated it 7.5 out of 10, calling it fun and informative though rushed in its final minutes, and Common Sense Media described it as a purr-fect primer for children.

overview: When her boyfriend dumps Emily, a spontaneous woman in her 30s, she persuades her ultra-cautious mom to accompany her on a vacation to Ecuador. When these two very different women are trapped on this wild journey, their bond as mother and daughter is tested and strengthened while they attempt to navigate the jungle and escape.
tagline: Mess with me, mess with my mother.
title: Snatched
plot:
Snatched is a comedy film that revolves around the complex and often fraught relationship between two mothers, Claire (Amy Schumer) and Pam (Goldie Hawn). The movie delves into the challenges of female friendship, particularly in the context of motherhood. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that these two women are not just mothers to each other's children but also to each other.

The film explores themes of female empowerment, independence, and self-discovery.
