Claire, a single mother, is forced to embark on an adventure with her daughter and Pam, who has recently become a grandmother, in search of the latter's missing granddaughter. Along the way, they confront their own personal demons, insecurities, and fears.

One of the primary themes of Snatched is the idea that women are not always defined by their roles as mothers or caregivers. The movie showcases the strength and resilience of these characters as they navigate uncharted territory, pushing past their comfort zones and embracing new experiences.

The film also touches on the theme of midlife crises and the challenges of aging. As Claire and Pam face various obstacles, they are forced to confront their own mortality and the impermanence of life. This introspection serves as a catalyst for growth, self-reflection, and ultimately, a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

Ultimately, Snatched is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of female friendship, motherhood, and personal growth, showcasing the complexities and nuances of relationships between women across different stages of life.

overview: A father coming to grips with his daughter’s upcoming wedding through the prism of multiple relationships within a big, sprawling Cuban-American family.
tagline: Love is simple. Family is not.
title: Father of the Bride
plot:
Father of the Bride is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Gaz Alazraki and written by Matt Lopez, based on Edward Streeter's 1949 novel. A reimagining of the 1950 and 1991 films and the third screen version of the story, it relocates the tale to a Cuban-American family in Miami and stars Andy García, Gloria Estefan, Adria Arjona, Isabela Merced, Diego Boneta and Chloe Fineman. Produced by Plan B Entertainment, it premiered on HBO Max.

Guillermo "Billy" Herrera is a successful, stubborn Miami architect married to Ingrid. At a counseling session, Ingrid tells him she is tired of his workaholism and wants a divorce, and they plan to tell their daughters: Sofia, a newly graduated lawyer, and Cora, a rebellious aspiring fashion designer. Before they can, Sofia arrives home and announces that she is engaged to a fellow lawyer, Adan Castillo, that they plan to marry within a month, and that they intend to move to Mexico to work for a non-profit. Billy and Ingrid agree to keep the divorce secret until after the wedding. Billy wants a big traditional Cuban celebration while the couple prefer something small, and Sofia asks Cora to design her gown, irritating the eccentric wedding planner Natalie Vance.

Adan's wealthy father, Hernan, arrives with his family and clashes repeatedly with Billy over the cost and scale of the event, offending him by offering to cover anything he cannot afford, throwing an extravagant engagement party on his yacht and proposing his island mansion as the venue. Billy eventually admits that he dislikes Adan and his family, then makes peace with Sofia and confides the divorce to Adan at the bachelor party. At the rehearsal, with a storm approaching, Cora overhears the secret and blurts it out to the guests. Sofia is hurt that her parents and fiancé hid it from her but reconciles with her father. The storm wrecks the decorations and knocks out the only bridge to the venue, so the two families pool their resources to hold the wedding at the Herrera home, with Natalie officiating. Sofia and Adan marry with Billy's blessing, and he and Ingrid rekindle their romance.

The project was announced in 2020 at Warner Bros., and principal photography began in Atlanta in June 2021. Released on HBO Max in June 2022, the film earned 80% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 65, with critics noting that it diverged smartly from its predecessors while keeping the story's timeless charm.

overview: A photographer is tasked to take a photo of a rare flower thriving in the mountain, but he discovers women trapped in a hidden brothel for illegal loggers.
title: Virgin Forest
plot:
Virgin Forest is a 2022 Filipino erotic thriller directed by Brillante Mendoza and produced and distributed by Viva Films with Center Stage Productions. It stars Sid Lucero as Francis and Angeli Khang as Angela, with Vince Rillon as Roger, Kat Dovey as Karla, Rob Guinto as Gina, Alma Moreno as Minda, Allan Paule as Mang Canor and Micaella Raz as the leader of the forest spirits, or diwata.

Francis, a photojournalist and father of two, is hired by the mayor of the town of Dolores to photograph the giant rafflesia, the flower with the largest blooms in the world, which grows deep in the mountains. He sets off into the jungle with a local guide, Roger. When they stop in Roger's village, Francis sees a resident accuse Roger of abducting his daughter, a charge Roger denies. In the forest they meet Gina, a naked, terrified woman who seeks Roger's protection; he rebuffs her and tells Francis she is mad. At night Francis repeatedly dreams of erotic encounters with diwata who beg him to save them. The next morning they find the bloody body of a hunter they had met, then stumble upon illegal loggers and a desperate young woman, Angela, who pleads with Roger for help. Instead, he drags her back to a hidden compound in the jungle, a tavern and brothel run by Minda, and the loggers decide that Francis, who now knows their secret, must be eliminated. Locked up with Francis, Angela tells him that Roger promised her and her sister Karla jobs but sold them as sex slaves, the same fate that befell his former girlfriend Gina. With Gina's help, they escape and free Karla, but the loggers pursue them through the forest, and Karla is shot. The hunters meet their own deaths in a fall and in snake attacks, and Roger is later killed by the father of one of the girls he trafficked. Back in Dolores, Angela confronts her grandmother, who sold the sisters, and Francis and his journalist wife expose the trafficking and illegal logging, leading to the arrest of the mayor and his accomplices. The film suggests that a forest spirit was behind the men's deaths.

Principal photography took place in 2022 in Batangas, Bukidnon and Quezon. A teaser was released on 30 May 2022, and the film premiered on the streaming service Vivamax on 24 June 2022. It was later released on home video in Germany by Busch Media Group.

overview: A story about bravery, self-sacrifice and human dignity put on trial by the merciless power of nature. A young pilot is fired from military air force after disobeying an absurd order. He gets a job as a co-pilot with a civil airline. Being brutally honest and direct, he is not on best terms with his new colleagues. During a flight to Asia his crew receives a distress message from a volcanic island and makes a decision to attempt a rescue mission. Will it be a success? Will they survive the disaster? They have a single chance to find that out: by being a team and sticking up for one another.
tagline: A mid air rescue mission
title: Flight Crew
plot:
Flight Crew (Russian: Экипаж, Ekipazh) is a 2016 Russian disaster film directed by Nikolai Lebedev and produced by the Russia-1 channel, starring Danila Kozlovsky, Vladimir Mashkov and Agnė Grudytė. A remake of the 1979 Soviet film Air Crew, it was shot with digital 3D cameras and became the second Russian film released in IMAX, after Stalingrad.

Alexey Gushchin, a gifted young military pilot, is grounded after he jettisons a car being carried for a general from a charity flight to get through a storm. Seeking work with a passenger airline, he fails a simulator test overseen by veteran captain Leonid Zinchenko, but when Zinchenko himself fails the same scenario, he takes Alexey on as a trainee co-pilot on a Tu-204. Zinchenko is estranged from his son Valera, who has dropped out of school, while Alexey begins a relationship with fellow pilot Alexandra Kuzmina. The two pilots clash after Zinchenko refuses to let locals board an evacuation flight from an African country in revolution, and Alexey is fired after a fight with a wealthy passenger who ignores safety rules. Zinchenko, valuing his skill, brings him back for a flight to Southeast Asia, taking Valera along.

Sent to the volcanic island of Kanwoo after an eruption, the crew begins evacuating survivors when an earthquake wrecks the airport. While Alexey, Valera and attendant Andrey drive out to rescue a group of trapped people, the advancing lava forces Zinchenko and Alexandra to leave in an An-26, leaving the Tu-204 behind. The rescuers return on foot, and Alexey takes off from a shorter runway covered in burning oil and flies out through the ash cloud. Learning that the An-26 is losing fuel, the crew follows a plan devised by Alexey's father Igor, an aircraft engineer, to transfer its passengers mid-air in a cage on a cable. Alexandra is saved, but the cage's ropes snap on its third trip, killing eleven people, and Zinchenko escapes along the cable before the An-26 falls into the ocean. Defying orders, Alexey lands the crippled jet in a storm at Elizovo and everyone aboard survives. Fired for disobedience, the pilots are taken on by Aeroflot.

Filmed from September 2014 to February 2015 in Moscow and Crimea, the film premiered on April 21, 2016, through Central Partnership. Critics praised its effects and tension, and it was the highest-grossing Russian film of 2016, receiving 11 nominations at the 2017 Golden Eagle Awards.

overview: After experiencing a traumatic misfortune, Jasmine French, a wealthy woman from New York, moves to San Francisco to live with her foster sister Ginger and the firm purpose of getting a new life, but she will be haunted by anxiety and memories of the past.
title: Blue Jasmine
plot:
Blue Jasmine is a 2013 American drama film directed by Woody Allen, produced by Gravier Productions, and released by Sony Pictures Classics.

The main themes of Blue Jasmine include:

1. Mental Illness: The film explores the theme of mental illness, particularly depression and anxiety, through the character of Jasmine (played by Cate Blanchett). Her struggles with her past and present life are portrayed as a manifestation of her inner turmoil.
2. Identity Crisis: Jasmine's identity crisis is a central theme in the film. She struggles to come to terms with her past mistakes and find a new sense of purpose in her life. This theme is also reflected in her relationship with her sister, Ginger (played by Sally Hawkins), who represents a more stable and secure identity.
3. Class and Social Status: The film critiques the social status of wealthy Americans, particularly those who have made their fortunes through questionable means. Jasmine's family, represented by her father (played by Bobby Cannavale) and stepmother (played by Mary Steenburgen), embody this theme.
4. Trauma and Guilt: Jasmine's past traumas and guilt are slowly revealed throughout the film, highlighting the long-term effects of these experiences on her mental health and relationships.
5. Redemption and Self-Discovery: The film ultimately suggests that redemption and self-discovery are possible through confronting one's past mistakes and finding a new sense of purpose.

The plot development of Blue Jasmine follows Jasmine as she leaves her wealthy life in San Francisco to move in with her working-class sister Ginger in New York City. As Jasmine navigates this new environment, she begins to confront her past and find a new sense of identity.

The ending of the film is bittersweet, with Jasmine finally finding some semblance of peace and acceptance, but also acknowledging that she will always carry the scars of her past with her. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that Jasmine has taken the first steps towards healing and redemption.

Overall, Blue Jasmine is a thought-provoking exploration of mental illness, identity crisis, class, trauma, and redemption, all woven together by Woody Allen's signature wit and insight into the human condition.

overview: Deliveryman Jongsu is out on a job when he runs into Haemi, a girl who once lived in his neighborhood. She asks if he'd mind looking after her cat while she's away on a trip to Africa. On her return she introduces to Jongsu an enigmatic young man named Ben, who she met during her trip. And one day Ben tells Jongsu about his most unusual hobby...
tagline: The truth is all in your head.
title: Burning
plot:
Burning is a 2018 South Korean psychological thriller film directed by Lee Chang-dong, not Pinehouse Film.

The main themes of Burning include:

1. Class struggle and social inequality: The film explores the contrast between the wealthy and the poor in South Korea, highlighting the economic disparities and the struggles of the working class.
2. Obsession and fixation: The protagonist, Jongsu (played by Yoo Ah-in), becomes fixated on his childhood friend, Saebyok (played by Kim Tae-ri), who has moved to a wealthy neighborhood, leading to a complex web of relationships and desires.
3. Identity and belonging: As the story unfolds, the characters' identities are called into question, and they struggle to find their place in society. Jongsu's feelings for Saebyok are complicated by his own sense of identity and belonging.
4. Power dynamics and manipulation: The film explores how power is exercised and manipulated in relationships, particularly between the wealthy and the poor. The characters' actions are driven by a desire for control and status.

The plot follows Jongsu, who reconnects with Saebyok after she returns to Seoul from abroad. He becomes embroiled in her life when he meets her employer, Ben (played by Steven Yeun), a wealthy American businessman. As the story unfolds, Jongsu's relationships with both women become increasingly complicated, leading to a tragic confrontation.

Overall, Burning is a thought-provoking and atmospheric film that explores themes of class struggle, obsession, identity, and power dynamics in contemporary South Korea.

overview: After being bitten by a genetically altered spider at Oscorp, nerdy but endearing high school student Peter Parker is endowed with amazing powers to become the superhero known as Spider-Man.
tagline: With great power comes great responsibility.
title: Spider-Man
plot:
Spider-Man is a 2002 American superhero film adapted from the Marvel Comics hero by screenwriter David Koepp and director Sam Raimi. The first instalment of Raimi's trilogy, it stars Tobey Maguire as Peter Parker, with Willem Dafoe as Norman Osborn, Kirsten Dunst as Mary Jane Watson, James Franco as Harry Osborn, Cliff Robertson and Rosemary Harris.

On a school trip to a Columbia University genetics lab, the shy teenager Peter is bitten by a genetically engineered spider. At the same time, Norman Osborn, founder of Oscorp and father of Peter's best friend Harry, tests an experimental performance enhancer on himself to win a military contract; it gives him superhuman strength but drives him mad, and he kills one of his scientists. Peter wakes with heightened strength and senses, the ability to cling to walls and shoot organic webs, and perfect eyesight. Hoping to buy a car to impress his crush, Mary Jane, he wins an underground wrestling match but is cheated of the prize, and in resentment he lets a thief rob the promoter. The same thief then kills his Uncle Ben; Peter tracks him down, and the man falls to his death.

Now Spider-Man, Peter fights crime and sells photos of himself to J. Jonah Jameson of the Daily Bugle. Norman, who has attacked a rival's product test, murders Oscorp's board at the Unity Day festival after they vote to oust him, and Spider-Man saves Mary Jane from the attack. Jameson dubs the killer the Green Goblin. The Goblin offers Spider-Man a partnership and wounds him when he refuses; at Thanksgiving dinner Norman notices Peter's injury and realises who he is, then attacks Aunt May. Learning from Harry that Peter loves Mary Jane, the Goblin captures her and a tram car full of children and drops both from the Queensboro Bridge, forcing Peter to choose; he saves them all. In the fight that follows, Norman unmasks and pleads for forgiveness while steering his glider toward Peter, who dodges, and the glider impales Norman. Dying, Norman asks Peter to keep his secret from Harry. At the funeral, Harry swears vengeance on Spider-Man, and Peter, wanting to protect Mary Jane, tells her they can only be friends, remembering Ben's words that great power brings great responsibility.

Released in May 2002 after decades of stalled development, it set a record with a $114.8 million opening weekend and grossed $825.8 million worldwide. Critics praised it, with 90% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it was nominated for two Academy Awards. Two sequels followed.

overview: After suffering a personal tragedy, and desperate for justice, Jacob Kanon, a veteran New York City police detective, embarks on the search for a twisted killer who is leaving a bloody trail of elaborate murders across Europe.
title: The Postcard Killings
plot:
The Postcard Killings is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of trauma. The film follows a detective who becomes obsessed with solving a series of murders, all linked to postcards sent to his office.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and how it can consume individuals, leading them down a path of destruction. The protagonist's fixation on the case is portrayed as an all-consuming force that drives him to question his own sanity and morality.

The film also touches on the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. The victims' backstories and the circumstances surrounding their deaths serve as a reminder of the devastating effects of violence and abuse. Through these narratives, the movie sheds light on the long-term consequences of trauma on both the survivors and those who perpetrate it.

Furthermore, The Postcard Killings critiques the societal expectations placed on men, particularly in regards to masculinity and emotional expression. The protagonist's struggles with his own emotions and the pressure to conform to traditional masculine norms serve as a commentary on the toxic masculinity that can lead individuals down a path of violence and destruction.

Overall, The Postcard Killings is a gripping thriller that delves into the complexities of human psychology, exploring themes of obsession, trauma, and the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: Stranded at a summer camp when aliens attack the planet, four teens with nothing in common embark on a perilous mission to save the world.
tagline: Saving the world is alien to them
title: Rim of the World
plot:
Rim of the World is a 2019 science fiction adventure film directed by Jonathan Liebesman and written by Mark Fergus, Hawk Ostby, and Michael Mitchell. The movie stars Jack Black, Marlon Wayans, and Adam DeVine.

The story begins with three friends, Scott (Jack Black), Oscar (Marlon Wayans), and Ethan (Adam DeVine), who are on a road trip to attend their friend's wedding in Las Vegas. However, their plans are disrupted when they stumble upon an alien spacecraft that has crash-landed in the desert.

As they explore the ship, they discover that it is a reconnaissance vessel from an advanced alien civilization known as the "Xenomorphs." The Xenomorphs have been monitoring Earth for decades and have developed a plan to invade the planet. The three friends soon realize that they are now at the center of this invasion.

The aliens begin to hunt them down, using their advanced technology to track and eliminate any human who gets in their way. Scott, Oscar, and Ethan must use their wits and whatever resources they can find to survive against the Xenomorphs' relentless attacks.

As the stakes grow higher, the three friends discover that the Xenomorphs are not just mindless killers but also have a complex social hierarchy with different castes and roles. They also learn that the aliens have been studying human behavior and psychology, making them even more formidable opponents.

Throughout their journey, Scott, Oscar, and Ethan face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to evade capture and find a way to stop the Xenomorph invasion. Along the way, they encounter other humans who are fighting back against the alien threat, including a group of rebels led by a mysterious figure known only as "The Architect."

As the battle between humans and Xenomorphs reaches its climax, Scott, Oscar, and Ethan discover that the aliens' ultimate goal is to harvest human DNA for their own purposes. The three friends must use all their skills and resources to outsmart the Xenomorphs and prevent a catastrophic invasion of Earth.

In the end, Scott, Oscar, and Ethan manage to defeat the Xenomorphs and save humanity from extinction. However, not before they realize that the aliens' technology has left behind a mysterious artifact that could potentially be used for good or evil in the future.

Overall, Rim of the World is an action-packed sci-fi adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the human condition in the face of overwhelming odds.

overview: The inhabitants of the British Isles have lost their battle against the onslaught of disease, as the deadly rage virus has killed every citizen there. Six months later, a group of Americans dare to set foot on the isles, convinced the danger has come and gone. But it soon becomes all too clear that the scourge continues to live, waiting to pounce on its next victims.
tagline: When days turn to weeks... the horror returns.
title: 28 Weeks Later
plot:
28 Weeks Later is a 2007 British post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Juan Carlos Fresnadillo and written by Rowan Joffe, Jesús Olmo, and Diego Sanjuán. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2002 film 28 Days Later.

The story takes place six months after the events of the first film. The UK government has established a quarantine zone in London, where a small group of survivors lives under strict military rule. The city remains in a state of lockdown, with a curfew and strict controls on movement.

The movie begins with Don (Robert Carlyle), a survivor who has been living in the quarantine zone, trying to rebuild his life. He is visited by his friend, Jim (Clemence Poesy), who brings news that her sister, Scarlet (Imogen Poots), has gone missing. Scarlet was one of the few people allowed to leave the quarantine zone for a medical experiment.

As Don and Jim search for Scarlet, they discover that she has been infected with the rage virus, which caused the initial outbreak in London. The virus is highly contagious and turns its victims into violent, zombie-like creatures.

The group soon realizes that the virus has mutated, making it even more deadly and aggressive. They also learn that a new strain of the virus has emerged, which can be transmitted through casual contact, rather than just through bites or scratches.

As the situation spirals out of control, Don and Jim must navigate the treacherous landscape of London to find Scarlet and prevent the spread of the virus. Along the way, they encounter other survivors who are struggling to cope with the new reality.

The movie's plot is driven by a sense of urgency and desperation, as the characters try to survive in a world that has been turned upside down. The film's climax features an intense and violent confrontation between Don and Scarlet, which ultimately leads to her downfall.

Throughout the movie, there are themes of grief, loss, and redemption. Don's character is particularly well-developed, as he grapples with the guilt of surviving while others have died. His relationship with Jim adds a human element to the story, and their bond helps to drive the plot forward.

Overall, 28 Weeks Later is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores the consequences of a global pandemic. The movie's use of practical effects and its focus on character development make it a standout in the horror genre.

overview: Bacurau, a small town in the Brazilian sertão, mourns the loss of its matriarch, Carmelita, who lived to be 94. Days later, its inhabitants notice that their community has vanished from most maps.
title: Bacurau
plot:
Bacurau is a 2019 Brazilian Western film directed by Kleber Mendonça Filho and Juliano Dornelles, produced by ARTE France Cinéma. The movie's narrative revolves around the residents of the small town of Bacurau, who band together to fight against an alien invasion.

At its core, Bacurau is a powerful exploration of community, resilience, and the human spirit in the face of overwhelming odds. The film delves into the themes of colonialism, imperialism, and the exploitation of indigenous cultures, as the aliens' presence serves as a metaphor for the historical and ongoing struggles faced by marginalized communities.

Through its unique blend of Western and Brazilian folklore, Bacurau critiques the notion of "civilization" and the ways in which it is often imposed upon indigenous populations. The film's portrayal of the town's residents, who must draw upon their traditional knowledge and resourcefulness to survive, serves as a powerful statement about the importance of preserving cultural heritage and resisting external influences.

Ultimately, Bacurau is a triumphant celebration of community, solidarity, and the human capacity for resistance and survival in the face of adversity. The film's vibrant visuals, coupled with its thought-provoking narrative, make it a must-see for anyone interested in exploring themes of identity, culture, and social justice.

overview: The rise of Aretha Franklin’s career from a child singing in her father’s church’s choir to her international superstardom.
tagline: The queen arrives.
title: Respect
plot:
Respect is a 2021 biographical drama film directed by Jay Roach, written by Jonathan Herman and Will Berson, and produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The movie tells the story of Aretha Franklin's life, focusing on her rise to fame as the "Queen of Soul" and her struggles with sexism, racism, and personal relationships.

The main themes of Respect include:

1. Empowerment: The film showcases Aretha Franklin's journey from a young girl with a powerful voice to a confident woman who takes control of her life and career.
2. Feminism: The movie highlights the challenges faced by women in the music industry during the 1960s and 1970s, particularly in terms of sexism and objectification.
3. Racism: Respect explores the racial tensions and injustices that Aretha Franklin faced throughout her life, including her experiences with racism in the music industry and her involvement in the Civil Rights Movement.
4. Personal relationships: The film delves into Aretha's complex relationships with her family members, particularly her father Clarence Franklin, who played a significant role in shaping her early career.
5. Identity: Respect explores Aretha's struggles to balance her personal identity with her public persona as "The Queen of Soul," highlighting the tension between her desire for authenticity and the pressures of fame.

Overall, Respect is a powerful tribute to Aretha Franklin's life and legacy, offering a nuanced exploration of the challenges she faced as a black woman in a male-dominated industry.

overview: Unscrupulous boxing promoters, violent bookmakers, a Russian gangster, incompetent amateur robbers and supposedly Jewish jewelers fight to track down a priceless stolen diamond.
tagline: Stealin' stones and breakin' bones.
title: Snatch
plot:
Snatch is a 2000 crime comedy film written and directed by Guy Ritchie and produced by Matthew Vaughn. Set in the London criminal underworld, it has an ensemble cast including Jason Statham, Stephen Graham, Dennis Farina, Brad Pitt, Alan Ford, Benicio del Toro, Lennie James, Rade Šerbedžija, Jason Flemyng and Vinnie Jones. Its two intertwined storylines follow the pursuit of a stolen diamond and a small-time boxing promoter, played by Statham, who becomes entangled with a sadistic gangster played by Ford.

In Antwerp, robbers disguised as Orthodox Jews steal an 84-carat diamond. Their leader, Franky Four-Fingers, travels to London to fence it through the dealer Doug the Head for the American crime figure Cousin Avi. One of the robbers steers Franky toward Boris the Blade, an ex-KGB arms dealer, and secretly urges Boris, his brother, to steal the stone. Meanwhile, unlicensed promoter Turkish and his partner Tommy are drawn into a fight for crime boss Brick Top, but their boxer, Gorgeous George, is knocked out by Mickey O'Neil, a bare-knuckle champion among the Irish Travellers who had just swindled Tommy over a caravan. Turkish recruits Mickey as a replacement in return for a new caravan for his mother, and Brick Top orders that Mickey throw the fight.

Exploiting Franky's gambling habit, Boris sends him to a bookmaker and hires small-time crooks Sol, Vinny and Tyrone to rob it and grab Franky. The robbery fails, but Franky is abducted and killed by Boris, who takes the diamond. Avi hires the bounty hunter Bullet Tooth Tony, setting off a chain of chases and shootouts in which Boris dies and the stone passes to Sol and Vinny, whose dog then swallows it and escapes. Avi accidentally shoots Tony while aiming at the dog and goes home. Brick Top's men burn down Mickey's mother's caravan, killing her, but in the fixed fight Mickey gets up and knocks out his opponent, having bet on himself, and the Travellers massacre Brick Top and his crew. Turkish and Tommy find the dog, have a vet remove the diamond, and sell it through Doug, bringing Avi back to London.

Shot in London and Buckinghamshire in late 1999, the film opened in the United Kingdom on 1 September 2000, setting an opening record for an 18-certificate film, and grossed $83.6 million worldwide on a $10 million budget. Critics found it perhaps style over substance but praised its snappy dialogue and dark comedy, giving it 74% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; it has gained a cult following.

overview: When the Valley of Peace is threatened, lazy Po the panda discovers his destiny as the "chosen one" and trains to become a kung fu hero, but transforming the unsleek slacker into a brave warrior won't be easy. It's up to Master Shifu and the Furious Five -- Tigress, Crane, Mantis, Viper and Monkey -- to give it a try.
tagline: Prepare for awesomeness.
title: Kung Fu Panda
plot:
Kung Fu Panda is a 2008 computer-animated action comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Po, a lazy and overweight panda who dreams of becoming a kung fu master.

The film begins with Po (voiced by Jack Black) living in the Valley of Peace, a serene and idyllic valley inhabited by various animals. Po is a food enthusiast and spends most of his days eating and lounging around. However, his life takes an unexpected turn when he is unexpectedly chosen by Master Oogway (voiced by Randall Duk Kim), a wise old tortoise, to be the Dragon Warrior.

According to legend, the Dragon Warrior is destined to bring balance to the Valley of Peace and defeat the evil snow leopard, Tai Lung. Po is initially hesitant and uninterested in taking on the challenge, but Master Oogway convinces him that he has what it takes to become a kung fu master.

Po begins his training with Master Shifu (voiced by Dustin Hoffman), a strict and demanding kung fu master who teaches him the ways of kung fu. However, Po struggles to keep up with the other students, including Tigress (voiced by Angelina Jolie), Monkey (voiced by Jackie Chan), Viper (voiced by Lucy Liu), and Crane (voiced by David Cross).

As Po's training progresses, he faces numerous challenges and setbacks, including a series of humiliating defeats at the hands of Tai Lung. Despite his struggles, Po perseveres and eventually discovers his own unique kung fu style, which combines humor, wit, and heart.

Meanwhile, Tai Lung escapes from prison and begins to wreak havoc on the Valley of Peace, threatening its inhabitants and destroying its harmony. Po must confront his fears and doubts in order to face Tai Lung and save the valley.

The final battle between Po and Tai Lung is an epic showdown that showcases Po's growth and development as a kung fu master. With the help of his friends and Master Shifu, Po defeats Tai Lung and brings balance back to the Valley of Peace.

Throughout the film, Kung Fu Panda explores themes of identity, perseverance, and self-acceptance. Po's journey is a metaphor for finding one's true purpose and embracing one's uniqueness. The movie also features stunning animation, witty humor, and memorable characters that have become iconic in modern animation.

Overall, Kung Fu Panda is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of friendship, teamwork, and believing in oneself.

overview: 70-year-old widower Ben Whittaker has discovered that retirement isn't all it's cracked up to be. Seizing an opportunity to get back in the game, he becomes a senior intern at an online fashion site, founded and run by Jules Ostin.
tagline: Experience never gets old
title: The Intern
plot:
The Intern is a 2013 American comedy-drama film directed by Nancy Meyers, not 2015, but I'll provide you with the details.

The movie follows Ben Whittaker (played by Robert De Niro), a retired executive who decides to pursue his long-held passion for gardening. He moves to New York City and applies for an internship at a fashion startup called Second Act, founded by Jules Ostin (played by Anne Hathaway). Despite being 70 years old, Ben is hired as the company's first intern.

Initially, Ben struggles to adapt to the fast-paced world of tech startups, but he quickly wins over his colleagues with his wit and kindness. He befriends Jules, who becomes a mentor to him, and helps her navigate the challenges of running a business. As they spend more time together, Ben and Jules develop an unlikely friendship.

Ben's presence at Second Act also brings about positive changes in the workplace. He encourages his colleagues to take breaks, have fun, and prioritize work-life balance. His unconventional approach inspires them to rethink their priorities and values.

Meanwhile, Jules faces numerous challenges as a young entrepreneur. She struggles to manage her company's growth, deal with difficult employees, and maintain her own identity. Ben's guidance helps her stay grounded and focused on what matters most – creating a positive work environment for her team.

As the story unfolds, Ben and Jules grow closer, and their friendship deepens. They share stories about their past, support each other through tough times, and learn from each other's experiences. Through their bond, they find common ground and discover that age is just a number.

The film explores themes of friendship, mentorship, and the importance of human connection in a rapidly changing world. It highlights the value of intergenerational relationships and challenges societal norms around work, aging, and identity.

Ultimately, The Intern is a heartwarming story about finding purpose, belonging, and happiness at any age. Ben and Jules's unlikely friendship becomes a source of inspiration for those around them, reminding us that it's never too late to pursue our passions and make a positive impact on the world.

original_title: Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Across the 2nd Dimension
overview: Phineas and Ferb get trapped in an alternate dimension where the evil Doofenshmirtz rules the tri-state area. They must find a way back home with the help of their pet platypus named Perry, who they discover is a secret agent.
tagline: An adventure so big, one dimension isn't enough.
title: Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Across the 2nd Dimension
plot:
Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Across the 2nd Dimension is a 2011 animated film produced by Disney Television Animation. The movie follows Phineas Flynn and his stepbrother Ferb Fletcher as they travel through a portal into a parallel universe, where they encounter their evil doppelgangers, Isabella's twin sisters Candace and Vanessa.

The main themes of the movie can be broken down into several key areas:

1. **Friendship and Sibling Bonding**: The film highlights the strong bond between Phineas and Ferb, as well as their relationships with their friends and family members. Despite being stepbrothers, they work together to overcome challenges and have fun.
2. **Imagination and Creativity**: The movie celebrates the power of imagination and creativity, showcasing the duo's inventive ideas and projects that bring joy to those around them.
3. **Deception and Identity**: The parallel universe introduces a new level of complexity, as Phineas and Ferb must navigate their doppelgangers' evil plans while maintaining their own identities. This theme explores the consequences of deception and the importance of staying true to oneself.
4. **Family and Love**: The film emphasizes the value of family and love, demonstrating how Phineas and Ferb's relationships with their stepmother Linda and Isabella help them overcome obstacles and find happiness.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a story that is both entertaining and heartwarming. The film's lighthearted tone and humor make it an enjoyable experience for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Across the 2nd Dimension is a fun and imaginative adventure that explores themes of friendship, creativity, deception, and family, making it a great addition to the beloved animated series.

overview: It has been nine years since we last met Jesse and Celine, the French-American couple who once met on a train in Vienna. Now, live in Paris with twin daughters, but have spent a summer in Greece on the invitation of an author colleague of Jesse's. When the vacation is over and Jesse must send his teenage son off to the States, he begins to question his life decisions, and his relationship with Celine is at risk.
tagline: Everything's better with maturity.
title: Before Midnight
plot:
Before Midnight is a 2013 romantic drama directed by Richard Linklater, who wrote the screenplay with his stars Ethan Hawke and Julie Delpy. It follows Before Sunrise (1995) and Before Sunset (2004) and concludes the Before trilogy. Like the earlier films, it has a minimal plot and is built around long conversations.

Nine years after their reunion in Paris, Jesse and Céline are a couple with twin daughters. They are ending a summer stay in Greece's Peloponnese. Jesse, now a successful novelist, sees his teenage son Hank off to Chicago, where the boy lives with his mother, and feels guilty about missing so much of his life. Céline is at a crossroads in her career: her NGO's wind farm project has collapsed, and she is considering a government job working for someone she dislikes. On the long drive back, they joke about their parenting, and Céline warns that the question of Hank could be the beginning of the end. At dinner with the friends who invited them, the group compares how men and women see love, aging and relationships.

Their friends have booked them a hotel room for a night alone. On the walk there, Jesse and Céline remember their younger selves and wonder whether they would fall for each other if they met now. Jesse mentions that his grandmother has died after more than seventy years with his late grandfather. At the hotel, a phone call from Hank interrupts them as they begin to make love, and a quarrel follows. It becomes a long, bitter argument about moving to Chicago, Céline's career and the strains of family life, with accusations of past affairs. Céline walks out more than once and finally says she no longer loves him. Jesse finds her at the hotel's outdoor restaurant and replays the time-traveler game from the night they met, reading a letter supposedly from her 82-year-old self. Céline at first resists, saying fantasy can never match reality, but Jesse says that their imperfect love is real. She joins the game, and they reconcile.

The three filmmakers wrote the film to keep the nine-year gap between installments. It was shot in about 15 days in Greece in 2012 for under $3 million and premiered at Sundance in January 2013. Sony Pictures Classics released it, and it grossed $23 million, the most in the trilogy. It was widely acclaimed and earned the writers an Academy Award nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay.

overview: Set during the occupation of Iraq, a squad of U.S. soldiers try to protect a small village.
tagline: Home is a war away
title: Sand Castle
plot:
Sand Castle is a 2017 American war drama film directed by Fernando Coimbra from a screenplay by Chris Roessner, who drew on his own experience as a soldier in the Iraq War. It stars Nicholas Hoult, Logan Marshall-Green, Henry Cavill, Glen Powell, Tommy Flanagan, Beau Knapp and Neil Brown Jr., and centers on a young American soldier assigned to restore the water supply of an Iraqi village. The film was released on Netflix on April 21, 2017.

Private Matt Ocre joined the Army Reserve in 2001 to pay for college, and when the 2003 invasion of Iraq begins he is so reluctant to fight that he deliberately slams his hand in a Humvee door in the hope of being sent home. The ploy fails, and once his cast is removed he is deployed to Baghdad. After the initial fighting, his civil affairs squad, led by Staff Sergeant Harper, is sent to the dangerous village of Baqubah, where a Special Forces unit under Captain Syverson, whom Ocre comes to admire, explains the mission: the squad must fill a tanker at a damaged pump station and carry water back to the villagers every day while army engineers repair the system. The engineers warn that the work will take weeks unless local men can be hired, but nobody from the village turns up, so the soldiers are forced to do much of the labor themselves. The daily water runs expose them to ambushes, and in one firefight Sergeant Chutsky is killed. Progress finally comes when Kadeer, the administrator of the local school, agrees to help, but the cooperation comes at a terrible price, as the insurgents retaliate against anyone who works with the Americans. Each step forward is matched by fresh violence, and Ocre is left to question what the occupation is achieving and what his own part in it means.

Sand Castle received mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes it has an approval rating of 47% based on 17 reviews, with an average rating of 5.3/10, while Metacritic assigned it a score of 45 out of 100 based on seven critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews". Principal photography began in November 2015, and Netflix acquired the distribution rights in May 2016.

overview: Prima ballerina, Dominika Egorova faces a bleak and uncertain future after she suffers an injury that ends her career. She soon turns to Sparrow School, a secret intelligence service that trains exceptional young people to use their minds and bodies as weapons. Dominika emerges as the most dangerous Sparrow after completing the sadistic training process. As she comes to terms with her new abilities, she meets a CIA agent who tries to convince her that he is the only person she can trust.
tagline: Seduce. Deceive. Repeat.
title: Red Sparrow
plot:
Red Sparrow is a 2018 spy thriller film directed by Francis Lawrence, based on the 2013 novel of the same name by Jason Matthews. The movie stars Jennifer Lawrence as Dominika Egorova, a Russian ballerina turned CIA operative.

The story begins with Dominika (Jennifer Lawrence) performing at the Bolshoi Ballet in Moscow. She is a talented and beautiful dancer, but her life takes a dramatic turn when she is approached by her uncle, Pavlov (Matthias Schoenaerts), who works for the Russian intelligence agency SVR. Pavlov reveals that he has been watching Dominika's performances and believes she has the potential to become a spy.

Dominika is recruited by Pavlov and undergoes rigorous training, learning how to use her charm and beauty to manipulate men and gather information. She becomes a skilled operative, using her talents to infiltrate the CIA's Moscow station and gather intelligence on their operations.

Meanwhile, Nate Nash (Joe Alwyn), a CIA officer, is tasked with recruiting Dominika as a double agent. He believes that she can provide valuable insight into Russian espionage methods and help the CIA stay one step ahead of their enemies.

As Dominika navigates her new role, she must balance her loyalty to Pavlov and the SVR with her growing feelings for Nate. However, her allegiances are tested when she is sent on a mission to infiltrate a high-stakes poker game in Macau, where she encounters a wealthy businessman named Konstantin (Tom Wlaschiha).

Dominika's mission becomes complicated when she discovers that Konstantin is involved in a plot to sell nuclear technology to the highest bidder. She must use her skills and resources to gather evidence and prevent the sale from happening.

As the story unfolds, Dominika finds herself caught between her loyalty to Pavlov and Nate, as well as her own moral code. She must make difficult choices and confront the consequences of her actions in order to protect herself and those she cares about.

The film's climax features a tense showdown between Dominika and Konstantin, with Nate and his team trying to prevent the sale from happening. In the end, Dominika emerges victorious, but not without scars. She has been forced to confront the harsh realities of her profession and make difficult choices in order to survive.

Throughout the film, Jennifer Lawrence delivers a powerful performance as Dominika, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Matthias Schoenaerts and Joe Alwyn, also deliver strong performances that add to the film's tension and suspense.

Overall, Red Sparrow is a gripping spy thriller that explores the complexities of loyalty, morality, and identity. With its talented cast and intricate plot, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

original_title: るろうに剣心 最終章 The Final
overview: In 1879, Kenshin and his allies face their strongest enemy yet: his former brother-in-law Enishi Yukishiro and his minions, who've vowed their revenge.
title: Rurouni Kenshin: The Final
plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: The Final is a 2021 Japanese jidaigeki action film written and directed by Keishi Ōtomo, based on Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga Rurouni Kenshin. The fourth installment of the live-action film series, following Rurouni Kenshin: The Legend Ends (2014), it adapts the manga's final arc with some changes. Takeru Satoh returns as Himura Kenshin, with Emi Takei as Kamiya Kaoru, Mackenyu as Yukishiro Enishi, Kasumi Arimura as Yukishiro Tomoe, Munetaka Aoki as Sagara Sanosuke and Yū Aoi as Takani Megumi.

Yukishiro Enishi, head of the Shanghai mafia, arrives in Tokyo seeking revenge on Kenshin, a former government assassin. He and allies who all hold grudges against Kenshin launch attacks across the city, firing a cannon into the Akabeko restaurant and targeting the Maekawa Dojo and the home of the police chief, leaving behind notes reading jinchū, or "human judgment". Confronting Kenshin, Enishi declares that he wants him to suffer as he did when Kenshin killed his sister. Kenshin then tells his friends of his past: fifteen years earlier, while serving the Imperialists, he fell in love with and married Tomoe, a Shogunate spy who had originally meant to avenge her fiancé, whom Kenshin had killed. When assassins ambushed him, Tomoe stepped between them and was accidentally killed by Kenshin, leaving him the second scar that forms the cross on his cheek.

Allies including Shinomori Aoshi and Makimachi Misao arrive with Tomoe's diary, while Saitō Hajime and his troops are lured into a trap by Sawagejō Chō, who is revealed to be working with the mafia. As bombings spread through Tokyo, Enishi beats Sanosuke and kidnaps Kaoru but cannot bring himself to kill her because she reminds him of his sister. Aided by Misao, Saitō and the police, and by his former enemy Seta Sōjirō, Kenshin storms Enishi's mansion. In their duel he lets Enishi stab him and apologizes. When Woo Heishin fires at Kenshin, Enishi shields Kaoru and takes a bullet. Arrested, Enishi reads Tomoe's diary and understands that she gave her life to stop Kenshin from killing; Kenshin bids farewell to Tomoe at her grave.

Released in Japan by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan on April 23, 2021, and later internationally on Netflix, the film had the year's biggest opening weekend for a live-action film despite pandemic closures and grossed about 4.34 billion yen. Reviews were positive, praising its fight sequences and its conclusion to Kenshin's story.

overview: After a young man's premonition of a deadly race-car crash helps saves the lives of his peers, Death sets out to collect those who evaded their end.
tagline: Rest In Pieces.
title: The Final Destination
plot:
The Final Destination is a supernatural horror film directed by James Wong, released in 2009 by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with four high school friends - Nick O'Bannon (Shawn Ashmore), Chase Sanford (Mykelti Williamson), Justin Conner (Jon Abrahams), and Peter Fountaine (Emile Hirsch) - who are all seated together on a plane that is taking off from New York to Los Angeles. As the plane reaches cruising altitude, Nick has a premonition of a catastrophic event occurring at the end of the flight.

Despite his friends' skepticism, Nick convinces them to disembark the plane and take a different flight, which they do. However, unbeknownst to them, their decision is actually a result of Nick's premonition, and the original flight has indeed crashed into a school bus carrying students on their way home from a field trip.

The group soon discovers that whenever someone dies in a specific sequence of events, death follows them. They start to experience a series of bizarre and gruesome deaths, which seem to be connected to their own premonitions. As the bodies pile up, they realize that Nick's initial warning was actually a warning from the future, trying to prevent them from dying.

The group tries to figure out who will die next and how to avoid it, but each time they think they've found a way to escape death, another member of their group meets an untimely demise. The deaths become increasingly gruesome and violent, with the victims being killed in creative and terrifying ways.

As the body count rises, Nick becomes more and more convinced that he is the only one who can prevent the deaths from occurring. He tries to find a way to change the course of events, but it seems like fate has other plans for him and his friends.

In the end, it's revealed that the group's deaths were all connected to their own premonitions, which were actually messages from the future trying to warn them of their impending doom. The movie ends with Nick being the only survivor, who is left to ponder the meaning of his premonition and whether he was able to change the course of events.

Throughout the movie, there are several twists and turns that keep the audience guessing, as well as some clever plot reveals that add to the tension and suspense. The Final Destination is a classic horror film that relies on its clever plot and gruesome deaths to create a thrilling and terrifying experience for viewers.

original_title: 映画犬夜叉 天下覇道の剣
overview: Inuyasha and his brother, Sesshomaru, each inherited a sword from their father after his death. However, their father had a third sword, named Sounga, that he sealed away. Seven hundreds years after his death, Sounga awakens and threatens mankind's very existence. How will the children of the Great Dog Demon stop this unimaginable power?
tagline: The Three Swords of the Fang collide in an epic battle!
title: Inuyasha the Movie 3: Swords of an Honorable Ruler
plot:
Inuyasha the Movie 3: Swords of an Honorable Ruler (Japanese: 映画犬夜叉 天下覇道の剣) is a 2003 Japanese animated fantasy adventure film based on Rumiko Takahashi's manga series Inuyasha. Produced by Sunrise, it was directed by Toshiya Shinohara and written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, and is the third Inuyasha film, following The Castle Beyond the Looking Glass and preceding Fire on the Mystic Island. Its voice cast includes Kappei Yamaguchi, Satsuki Yukino and Koji Tsujitani. The story has the half-brothers Inuyasha and Sesshomaru reluctantly joining forces against So'unga, their late father's third sword.

Two hundred years earlier, the great dog demon Tōga refuses to give his elder son Sesshomaru his swords Tessaiga and So'unga. He then rescues his human wife, Lady Izayoi, from the samurai leader Takemaru of Setsuna, who loves her and has stabbed her and set fire to the mansion where she is giving birth. Reviving her with his sword Tenseiga, Tōga lets her escape with their newborn son, Inuyasha, and dies fighting Takemaru as the mansion collapses on them.

In the present, Kagome Higurashi's family finds an ancient sword among their shrine's treasures; it is So'unga, and the spirit of its sheath, Saya, warns that Inuyasha must master it before it destroys the modern world. When Inuyasha grasps it, the sword possesses him and turns him into his demon form. Back in the feudal era it drives him against Sesshomaru until Kagome breaks the spell with the command of his subjugation beads. The swordsmith Totosai explains that So'unga harbors an ancient evil demon. The sword then revives Takemaru, who seizes a castle, raises its slain soldiers as an undead army and opens a portal to the netherworld. Inuyasha, Kagome, Miroku, Sango, Shippo and Kirara fight alongside Sesshomaru, and Miroku risks his life using his Wind Tunnel against the army. Inuyasha kills Takemaru, forcing So'unga to take a body of its own, and after failing separately the brothers combine Tessaiga's Backlash Wave and the Dragon Strike of Sesshomaru's Tōkijin to send the sword into the netherworld, as Tōga's spirit declares his pride in his sons.

Toho released the film in Japan on December 20, 2003; it opened at number three behind Finding Nemo and The Last Samurai. Its theme song, "Four Seasons", was performed by Namie Amuro, and Viz Media issued it on DVD in 2005. Reviewers praised its action and its expanded family backstory while criticizing its pacing and some corny moments.

overview: In a massive, mysterious chamber, fifty strangers awaken to find themselves trapped with no memory of how they got there.  Organized in an inward-facing circle and unable to move, they quickly learn that every two minutes, one of them must die…executed by a strange device in the center of the room.
tagline: In here…everything gets you killed.
title: Circle
plot:
Circle is a 2015 American science fiction psychological thriller film written and directed by Aaron Hann and Mario Miscione. Inspired by the 1957 courtroom drama 12 Angry Men, it features an ensemble cast that includes Carter Jenkins, Lawrence Kao, Allegra Masters, Michael Nardelli, Julie Benz, Mercy Malick, Lisa Pelikan and Cesar Garcia. Shot in 2014, it premiered at the Seattle International Film Festival on May 28, 2015, and was released on video on demand in October of that year.

Fifty strangers wake up in a dark room, standing on platforms arranged in two concentric circles around a black dome. Anyone who steps away from their spot or touches another person is killed by a beam from the dome, and every two minutes the device kills someone else. The captives soon work out that they are voting, through small hand gestures, on who dies next, and that refusing to vote simply leaves the choice to chance. To buy time, they agree to eliminate the oldest among them first while they try to understand where they are; several remember fleeing Los Angeles and being pulled into the sky, and one elderly man insists he saw aliens, but the group refuses to listen. As the rounds continue, the debate turns ugly. People confess to affairs and violence, accusations of racism, homophobia and hypocrisy are traded, and each prejudice becomes a reason to target someone. A few volunteers sacrifice themselves to give the others more time. Eventually the survivors realize that only one person can be left standing, and they split into factions: one wants to protect a pregnant woman and a little girl at all costs, while the other argues that no one deserves special treatment. Alliances shift, lies are exposed, and the ever-shrinking circle is forced to decide who, if anyone, deserves to survive.

The film received a mixed response. On Rotten Tomatoes, four of seven critics' reviews are positive. John DeFore of The Hollywood Reporter described it as a "Twilight Zone-y drama" that works better than expected, and Tony Kay of City Arts praised the way it engineers suspense and the puzzle-box appeal of piecing together what is going on as each execution approaches.

overview: A ne er-do-well thirty-something attempts to appease her family by kidnapping herself an attractive boyfriend for the family Christmas. Despite unlikely odds and dysfunctional family moments, the two fall in love and share a magical Christmas.
title: Holiday in Handcuffs
plot:
Holiday in Handcuffs is a 2007 American romantic comedy film directed by John Murlowski and starring Christina Milian and Carlos PenaVega.

The movie follows the story of Natalie (Christina Milian), a young woman who is forced to pretend to be engaged to her boyfriend, Mike (Carlos PenaVega), in order to impress her wealthy and influential family. However, things take a turn when they are actually handcuffed together for the entire holiday season.

The main themes of Holiday in Handcuffs include:

1. Love and relationships: The movie explores the complexities of love and relationships, particularly in the context of arranged marriages and societal expectations.
2. Identity and self-discovery: Natalie's journey is also one of self-discovery as she navigates her own desires and aspirations amidst the pressures of family and social obligations.
3. Family dynamics: The film highlights the challenges and complexities of family relationships, particularly when it comes to intergenerational conflicts and generational differences.
4. Social class and status: The movie touches on issues of social class and status, as Natalie navigates her way through high-society events and tries to fit in with her wealthy family's expectations.

Overall, Holiday in Handcuffs is a lighthearted and entertaining romantic comedy that explores themes of love, identity, and family dynamics.

overview: Life's a beach for surfers Brady and McKenzie – until a rogue wave magically transports them inside the classic '60s beach party flick, "Wet Side Story," where a full-blown rivalry between bikers and surfers threatens to erupt. There, amidst a sea of surfing, singing and dancing, Brady and Mack accidentally change the storyline, and the film’s dreamy hero and heroine fall for them instead of for each other!
tagline: Getting trapped in a movie... is no day at the beach.
title: Teen Beach Movie
plot:
Teen Beach Movie is a 2013 American musical comedy film directed by Steven Antin and produced by Rainforest Productions.

The movie follows the story of three high school friends, Micki, Brady, and Lela, who are transported into a 1960s beach party-themed musical. The main themes of Teen Beach Movie include:

1. Friendship: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and loyalty among the three main characters. Despite their differences, they come together to overcome challenges and have fun.
2. Self-discovery: As Micki navigates her feelings for Brady, she learns to be true to herself and find her own identity. This theme is also reflected in Lela's journey as she discovers her passion for music and performance.
3. Nostalgia: The film pays homage to the classic beach party movies of the 1960s, incorporating elements of that era into its storyline. This nostalgia serves as a backdrop for the characters' adventures and helps them learn valuable lessons about life.
4. Empowerment: Teen Beach Movie promotes female empowerment, particularly through Lela's character. She takes center stage and showcases her talents, inspiring others to do the same.

The movie features a range of musical numbers, including "Surfside", "Me Too", and "Seaside Lullaby". The film's lighthearted tone, colorful characters, and catchy music make it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: A former U.S. soldier returns to his hometown to find it overrun by crime and corruption, which prompts him to clean house.
tagline: One man will stand up for what's right.
title: Walking Tall
plot:
Walking Tall is a 2004 American action film directed by Kevin Jarre and starring The Rock as Chris Vaughn. The movie is loosely based on the 1973 film of the same name, which was inspired by the real-life story of Buford Pusser.

The film begins with Chris Vaughn (Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson), a former Army Ranger who has retired to a small town in Tennessee called Sugar Hill. Chris is married to his wife, Tricia (Kayla Ewell), and they have two young daughters together. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when the local sheriff, Ray Owens (Neal McDonough), announces that he will not be seeking re-election due to a lack of funds.

As the town's problems escalate, Chris becomes increasingly frustrated with the corruption and lawlessness in Sugar Hill. He decides to take matters into his own hands and runs for sheriff himself, despite having no prior experience in law enforcement. Despite initial skepticism from the townspeople, Chris's charisma and military background quickly win them over, and he is elected as the new sheriff.

As Chris settles into his new role, he discovers that the town is plagued by a range of problems, including poverty, crime, and corruption. He vows to clean up the town and restore order, but faces opposition from the local crime lord, Floyd (Jason Flemyng), who has been exploiting the townspeople for years.

As Chris delves deeper into the world of law enforcement, he must confront his own demons and learn to balance his desire for justice with his need to protect his family. Along the way, he forms alliances with some of the town's residents, including a local mechanic, Ray's brother-in-law, and a young woman named Tricia (Kayla Ewell), who becomes his love interest.

As Chris's campaign against Floyd gains momentum, the stakes become increasingly high. The crime lord will stop at nothing to maintain his grip on Sugar Hill, and Chris must use all of his skills and resources to take him down. In a thrilling showdown, Chris confronts Floyd in an abandoned warehouse, where he ultimately emerges victorious.

Throughout the film, Chris's character undergoes significant development as he transforms from a quiet, reserved man into a confident and determined leader. His military background proves invaluable as he uses his combat skills to take down Floyd's henchmen and restore order to Sugar Hill.

Ultimately, Chris's efforts pay off, and he is hailed as a hero by the townspeople. However, the film ends on a bittersweet note, with Chris realizing that his work is far from over and that there will always be new challenges to face in Sugar Hill.

Overall, Walking Tall is an action-packed thrill ride that explores themes of justice, redemption, and community. The film's success can be attributed to Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson's charismatic performance as Chris Vaughn, who brings a sense of gravitas and authenticity to the role.

overview: When a renowned architecture scholar falls suddenly ill during a speaking tour, his son Jin finds himself stranded in Columbus, Indiana - a small Midwestern city celebrated for its many significant modernist buildings. Jin strikes up a friendship with Casey, a young architecture enthusiast who works at the local library.
tagline: In the middle of all the mess... there was this.
title: Columbus
plot:
Columbus is a poignant and contemplative film that explores the complexities of loneliness, human connection, and the search for meaning. The movie delves into the life of Adi, a shy and introverted man who has been living in New York City for over 40 years, struggling to form meaningful relationships due to his social anxiety.

As Adi navigates his mundane routine, he becomes fixated on finding the perfect person to share his life with. His quest is driven by a deep-seated desire for companionship and understanding, which has led him to become increasingly isolated from the world around him.

Through Adi's story, the film sheds light on the struggles of introversion and the challenges of forming connections in a society that often values extroversion and social interaction. The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, highlighting the ways in which people can become disconnected from others despite being surrounded by them.

Ultimately, Columbus is a powerful exploration of the human need for connection and understanding, and the film's thoughtful pacing and nuanced character study make it a deeply moving and thought-provoking viewing experience.

overview: Officially, Apollo 17 was the last manned mission to the moon. But a year later in 1973, three American astronauts were sent on a secret mission to the moon funded by the US Department of Defense. What you are about to see is the actual footage which the astronauts captured on that mission. While NASA denies its authenticity, others say it's the real reason we've never gone back to the moon.
tagline: There's a reason we've never gone back to the moon.
title: Apollo 18
plot:
Apollo 18 is a science fiction film directed by Gonzalo López-Gallego and produced by Bazelevs Production, not just Bazelevs Production. The movie was released in 2011.

The main themes of Apollo 18 include:

1. **Doubt and Paranoia**: The film explores the theme of doubt and paranoia as the astronauts begin to question their mission and the true nature of their encounter with an alien species.
2. **Isolation and Confined Spaces**: The movie takes place in a confined environment, the lunar module, where the astronauts are trapped and forced to confront their fears and the unknown.
3. **The Unknown and the Unseen**: Apollo 18 taps into our deep-seated fear of the unknown and the unseen, leaving audiences with a sense of unease and uncertainty.
4. **Militarization and Secrecy**: The film critiques the militarization of space exploration and the secrecy surrounding government projects, highlighting the tension between scientific discovery and national security interests.

The plot follows three astronauts, Sam Bell (Warren Christensen), Joe Aguilar (Lance Henriksen), and Jack Crowther (John Cusack), who are sent on a mission to the Moon in search of evidence of extraterrestrial life. However, they soon discover that their presence on the Moon has awakened an alien species, which begins to hunt them down.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving audiences with more questions than answers, adding to the sense of unease and uncertainty that pervades the film.

Overall, Apollo 18 is a tense, suspenseful thriller that explores themes of doubt, paranoia, isolation, and the unknown, making it a compelling watch for fans of science fiction.

original_title: 映画ドラえもん のび太の月面探査記
overview: During a Japanese robotic exploration to find life on the other side of the moon, Nobita is watching from Earth and sees the moon turn yellow. With the help of Doraemon, the pair travel to the moon and create bunnies that will build their own colony. After he returns, Nobita tells his class about their adventure but no one will believe him. That is until a new student and his sister arrive who appear to come from a very far away place...
title: Doraemon: Nobita's Chronicle of the Moon Exploration
plot:
Doraemon: Nobita's Chronicle of the Moon Exploration is a 2019 Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Tsutomu Shibayama. The movie follows Nobita Nobi, a young boy who travels back in time to the age of dinosaurs with his robotic cat Doraemon.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Friendship and camaraderie: Throughout the adventure, Nobita learns valuable lessons about friendship and teamwork from his friends, including Shizuka, Suneo, and Rikizo.
2. Exploration and discovery: The film celebrates the thrill of exploration and discovery as Nobita and Doraemon venture into the unknown, encountering new species and experiencing the wonders of prehistoric times.
3. Environmentalism and conservation: The movie highlights the importance of preserving our planet's natural resources and protecting endangered species, as seen in the dinosaurs' struggle to survive in a changing environment.
4. Time travel and its consequences: The film explores the concept of time travel and its potential consequences, as Nobita navigates the challenges of interacting with his past self and altering the course of history.

The movie also features some comedic elements, showcasing Doraemon's signature wit and resourcefulness as he helps Nobita overcome obstacles and find creative solutions to problems.

Overall, Doraemon: Nobita's Chronicle of the Moon Exploration is a heartwarming and entertaining adventure that promotes valuable life lessons and encourages viewers to appreciate the wonders of science, nature, and friendship.

overview: A geologist races against time to save his estranged wife and two children when a devastating earthquake strikes Oslo, Norway.
tagline: The Wave Was Only The Beginning
title: The Quake
plot:
The Quake (Norwegian: Skjelvet) is a 2018 Norwegian disaster film directed by John Andreas Andersen and the sequel to the 2015 film The Wave. Kristoffer Joner returns as geologist Kristian Eikjord, with Ane Dahl Torp, Jonas Hoff Oftebro, Edith Haagenrud-Sande and Kathrine Thorborg Johansen in the main cast. It was released in Norwegian cinemas on 31 August 2018.

Three years after he was hailed as a hero for his actions during the Geiranger tsunami, Kristian is a broken man. He blames himself for the 250 people who died, keeps a hidden room devoted to the disaster, and has become estranged from his wife Idun, who is divorcing him, and their children Sondre and Julia, who have moved to Oslo, where Idun works at the Radisson Blu Plaza Hotel. When a fellow geologist, Konrad Lindblom, is killed in a collapse in the Oslofjord Tunnel, Kristian travels to the capital to find out why. Konrad's supervisor, Johannes Løberg, assures him that the tremors Konrad had been monitoring were nothing more than construction blasting, but Kristian, working with Konrad's daughter Marit, finds core samples, maps of alarming seismic activity and video of laboratory rats killed by gas escaping from the ground. Kristian concludes that a massive earthquake, as strong as 8.5 on the Richter scale, is about to strike Oslo. A smaller rift that damages the Oslo Opera House during Julia's ballet recital proves he is right, but no one in authority will listen. As the city goes about its business, Kristian races to warn his family, calling in a fake bomb threat to clear Sondre's university and hurrying to Idun's office high in the hotel tower. The earthquake hits while they are still inside, devastating the city and leaving Kristian, Idun, Julia and Marit fighting to survive in the collapsing skyscraper.

The Quake was well received by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an 85% approval rating based on 40 reviews, with a consensus describing it as a satisfyingly smart action thriller that delivers nail-biting tension without sacrificing character development or common sense, and on Metacritic it has a score of 70 out of 100, indicating "generally favorable reviews".

overview: A lifelong love of flight inspires Japanese aviation engineer Jiro Horikoshi, whose storied career includes the creation of the A-6M World War II fighter plane.
tagline: We must live.
title: The Wind Rises
plot:
The Wind Rises (Japanese: Kaze Tachinu) is a 2013 Japanese animated historical drama film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, based on his own 2009 manga. Produced by Studio Ghibli and distributed by Toho, it features the voices of Hideaki Anno, Miori Takimoto, Hidetoshi Nishijima, Masahiko Nishimura and Nomura Mansai, and offers a fictionalized account of the life of aeronautical engineer Jiro Horikoshi, the designer of Japanese fighter aircraft before and during the Second World War.

As a nearsighted boy in 1918, Jiro realizes he can never be a pilot, but in recurring dreams the Italian aircraft designer Giovanni Battista Caproni tells him that building airplanes is better than flying them. Years later, while studying aeronautical engineering in Tokyo, Jiro is on a train when the Great Kantō earthquake strikes, and he helps a young girl, Nahoko Satomi, and her injured maid reach safety before parting without learning each other's names. After graduating, he and his friend Honjo join Mitsubishi, where their first fighter design breaks apart during testing. The company sends them to Germany to study the work of Hugo Junkers, and the visit shows them how far Japan lags behind. Back home, Jiro's next design also fails, and he takes a holiday at a resort in Karuizawa, where he meets the now grown-up Nahoko again. They fall in love, but she is suffering from tuberculosis. A German guest at the resort, critical of the Nazi regime, warns Jiro about the war to come, and his remarks later bring Jiro to the attention of the secret police, forcing him into hiding at the home of his supervisor, Kurokawa. Determined to share whatever time she has, Nahoko leaves a mountain sanatorium to marry Jiro, and the couple live together while he pours himself into a new fighter design for the Imperial Navy, torn between his beautiful dream of flight and the knowledge of what his machines will be used for.

The Wind Rises was met with critical acclaim, although it also provoked some political controversy and criticism in Asia. It won the Japan Academy Prize for Animation of the Year and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film. It was originally intended to be Miyazaki's final feature film, before he reversed that decision and went on to direct The Boy and the Heron.

overview: A rebellious young graffiti artist, who targets the homes of the wealthy elite, discovers a shocking secret that leads him on a journey endangering himself and those closest to him.
title: I Came By
plot:
I Came By is a 2022 British crime thriller written, co-produced and directed by British-Iranian filmmaker Babak Anvari. It stars George MacKay, Percelle Ascott, Kelly Macdonald and Hugh Bonneville.

Toby Nealey is a 23-year-old graffiti artist with strong political views. He breaks into the homes of the upper classes and leaves the tag "I CAME BY" on their walls. His next target is Sir Hector Blake, a retired High Court judge whom Toby considers a hypocrite despite his liberal public image. Inside, Toby finds a pottery studio and a man held captive in the basement. His former partner-in-crime Jay, preoccupied with his pregnant girlfriend Naz, does not take him seriously, and an anonymous tip leads police to search the house without finding anything. After a row with his widowed mother, Lizzie, Toby goes back to free the prisoner. Blake kills him with a cricket bat, burns the body in his kiln and flushes the ashes away.

Jay plants a letter pointing to Blake in Toby's room. Police find the hidden cell, which Blake claims is a panic room, but his connections get him released quickly. Lizzie begins following him herself. She watches him bring home Omid, a gay Iranian asylum seeker he has promised to help. Flashbacks show Blake's history: his father's affair with an Indo-Persian man, his mother's suicide and his teenage attack on his father's lover. Omid escapes but is afraid to go to the police, and Blake later hunts him down and kills him. Jay refuses to help Lizzie, so she breaks into Blake's house alone and is murdered too. Wracked with guilt, Jay drifts away from Naz. Some time later, he follows Blake from an anniversary celebration at Birlstone School to a country estate. He overpowers him, finds and frees another captive, calls the police and leaves the judge tied up beneath a fresh "I CAME BY" tag.

The film opened in British cinemas on August 19, 2022, and began streaming on Netflix on August 31. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said the film fell short of its Hitchcockian ambitions but benefited greatly from Bonneville's excellent performance against type. Empire praised Bonneville but found the political messaging blunt and the result messy. The Los Angeles Times said the shifts between characters kept the story unpredictable, but at some cost to tension. RogerEbert.com said it crammed a TV season's worth of ideas into one film.

overview: When he starts dating drop-dead gorgeous Molly, insecure airport security agent Kirk can't believe it. As his friends and family share their doubts about the relationship lasting, Kirk does everything he can to avoid losing Molly forever.
tagline: When she's this hot, You get one shot.
title: She's Out of My League
plot:
She's Out of My League is a romantic comedy film released in 2010 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of Moe Flinders (played by Jay Baruchel), a shy and awkward hockey player who works as a flight attendant for a small airline.

Moe lives with his mother, Nora (played by Wendy Crewson), and his best friend, Stu (played by Craig Robinson). Despite his unassuming nature, Moe has a secret crush on Lauren Reynolds (played by Alice Eve), a beautiful and charming flight attendant who works at the same airline. However, he is too shy to approach her.

One day, Lauren transfers to Moe's airline, and he sees an opportunity to get close to her. He enlists the help of his friend Stu, who has a more outgoing personality, to help him woo Lauren. Stu agrees to pretend to be Moe's girlfriend in order to impress Lauren and make Moe jealous.

As the story progresses, Moe becomes increasingly frustrated with Stu's antics, which only seem to drive Lauren further away from him. Meanwhile, Lauren starts to develop feelings for Moe, but she is hesitant to express them due to her fear of rejection.

The plot takes a turn when Lauren suffers an injury and is forced to take time off work. During this period, Moe has the opportunity to get close to her and win her heart. However, he struggles with his own insecurities and fears of rejection, which causes him to make mistakes and lose Lauren's trust.

In the end, Moe realizes that he needs to be true to himself and take a chance on love. He confesses his feelings to Lauren, and they share a romantic moment together. The movie ends with Moe and Lauren flying off into the sunset, symbolizing their newfound love and happiness.

Throughout the movie, the supporting characters add comedic relief and depth to the story. Stu's antics provide much of the humor, while Nora's motherly instincts and advice offer a heartwarming contrast to the more lighthearted moments.

Overall, She's Out of My League is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, vulnerability, and self-discovery. The movie features a talented cast, witty dialogue, and a relatable protagonist who will resonate with audiences.

overview: In Manhattan, a bike messenger picks up an envelope that attracts the interest of a dirty cop, who pursues the cyclist throughout the city.
tagline: Ride Like Hell
title: Premium Rush
plot:
Premium Rush is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by David Koepp and starring Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Michael Shannon, and Emma Stone.
