But not everyone at Avalon High is who they appear to be, not even Ellie herself. Eventually, it becomes apparent that Avalon High is a situation where the ancient Arthurian legend is repeating itself. Will, Jennifer, Lance, Marco, and Mr. Morton all correspond to King Arthur, Queen Guinevere, Knight Lancelot, Mordred, and Merlin, respectively.
title: Avalon High
plot:
Avalon High is a supernatural teen comedy-drama film that revolves around Evan Treborn, a shy and awkward teenager who transfers to Avalon High School. As he navigates his new school, Evan discovers that it's inhabited by ghosts of former students who died under mysterious circumstances.

The main theme of Avalon High is the struggle for identity and self-discovery. Evan, as an outsider, must find his place in a new environment while dealing with the pressures of high school social hierarchy and the supernatural forces that surround him. As he delves deeper into the mysteries of Avalon High, Evan uncovers secrets about his own past and the dark history of the school.

Throughout the film, themes of friendship, loyalty, and acceptance are also explored. Evan forms connections with a group of students who accept him for who he is, despite his awkwardness and outsider status. Together, they work to uncover the truth behind the ghostly apparitions and find a way to put them to rest.

Ultimately, Avalon High is a story about embracing one's uniqueness and finding one's place in the world. Evan's journey is a metaphor for the challenges of adolescence, where self-discovery and acceptance are key to navigating the complexities of growing up.

overview: An American nanny is shocked that her new English family's boy is actually a life-sized doll. After she violates a list of strict rules, disturbing events make her believe that the doll is really alive.
tagline: Every child needs to feel loved.
title: The Boy
plot:
The Boy is a 2016 horror film directed by William Brent Bell and written by Stacey Menear. It stars Lauren Cohan and Rupert Evans alongside Jim Norton, Diana Hardcastle and James Russell. An international co-production between China and the United States, it was filmed in Victoria, British Columbia, beginning in March 2015, and was released by STXfilms on January 22, 2016. A sequel, Brahms: The Boy II, followed in 2020.

Greta Evans, an American travelling in the United Kingdom whose abusive ex-boyfriend Cole has been trying to find out where she is, takes a job as a nanny for the elderly Heelshires at their remote English house. Her charge turns out to be Brahms, a doll that the couple treat as their real son. Before leaving on holiday, they give Greta a strict list of rules for looking after him, which she promptly ignores. From Malcolm, the young man who delivers the family's groceries, she learns that the real Brahms died in a fire twenty years earlier, on his eighth birthday, and that he was considered an odd child. Soon unsettling things begin to happen: her clothes and jewelry disappear, she is trapped in the attic, the doll seems to move when she is not in the room, and a child's voice promises to be good. Greta begins to follow the rules carefully and comes to believe that Brahms's spirit inhabits the doll. Malcolm then tells her that a girl who played with Brahms was found dead in the forest before the fire, and he urges Greta to leave, but she feels bound to stay. Matters reach a crisis when Cole tracks her down and arrives at the house, demanding that she return to America with him, and the secret that the Heelshires have been hiding behind the walls of their home finally comes to light.

The Boy received mixed to negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has a 31% approval rating, with a consensus that it settles for routine jump scares within a pedestrian plot, and Metacritic gives it a score of 42 out of 100. Commercially it was a success, grossing about $73.9 million worldwide against a production budget of $10 million.

keywords.name: based on magazine, newspaper or article

overview: The tragic and controversial story of Cameron Todd Willingham, who was executed in Texas for killing his three children after scientific evidence and expert testimony that bolstered his claims of innocence were suppressed.
tagline: Stand for what's right. Fight for what's true.
title: Trial by Fire
plot:
Trial by Fire is a 2018 American biographical drama directed by Edward Zwick. It is based on David Grann's 2009 New Yorker article of the same name about Cameron Todd Willingham, a Texas man executed for the deaths of his three daughters. Jack O'Connell stars as Willingham, with Laura Dern, Emily Meade, Jeff Perry and Jade Pettyjohn.

On December 23, 1991, Willingham wakes up to find his house on fire and cannot save his three young daughters. At trial, prosecutor John Jackson argues the fire was arson, citing a pentagram-shaped pattern of accelerant and a refrigerator supposedly moved to block a door. Witnesses describe Willingham as violent, and jailhouse informant Johnny Webb testifies that he confessed. Despite his and his wife Stacy's protests that he is innocent, Willingham is sentenced to death. On death row he is beaten and harassed, sent to solitary confinement and tormented by memories of his stormy marriage. Stacy stops writing at her grandmother's urging. Over time he learns to cope, improves his writing with the help of fellow inmate Ponchai James, who is later executed, and slowly wins over a hostile guard named Daniels.

Years later, one of his letters reaches playwright Elizabeth Gilbert. Despite her family's doubts, she visits him and is struck by his calm, and they bond over their love for their children. Gilbert finds that witnesses lied and confronts Webb, who reacts with threats. Fire scientist Dr. Hurst concludes the fire was not arson and that the refrigerator was never moved, but his report is ignored, Webb's recantation is buried and Stacy is pressured into saying Willingham confessed to her. As the execution approaches, Gilbert is badly injured in a car crash and cannot attend. Willingham gives a moving final statement and asks for his ashes to be scattered over his daughters' graves. Daniels, now doubtful of his guilt, has to carry out the lethal injection. Later, Gilbert, paralyzed from the crash, scatters the ashes with her children. An epilogue shows Governor Rick Perry rejecting criticism of the execution.

Trial by Fire premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on August 31, 2018, and was released by Roadside Attractions on May 17, 2019. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said the film had a worthy and heartbreaking story and strong performances but was undermined by an aggressively manipulative approach. On Metacritic it scored 51 out of 100.

overview: The Queen is an intimate behind the scenes glimpse at the interaction between HM Elizabeth II and Prime Minister Tony Blair during their struggle, following the death of Diana, to reach a compromise between what was a private tragedy for the Royal family and the public's demand for an overt display of mourning.
tagline: Our Leaders. Ourselves.
title: The Queen
plot:
The Queen is a 2006 docudrama directed by Stephen Frears and written by Peter Morgan, depicting the aftermath of the death of Diana, Princess of Wales, in 1997. While the royal family treats Diana's death as a private matter, the new prime minister Tony Blair and Prince Charles side with a public demanding an official display of grief. Helen Mirren stars as Queen Elizabeth II and Michael Sheen as Blair, with James Cromwell as Prince Philip, Helen McCrory as Cherie Blair, Alex Jennings as Prince Charles, Sylvia Syms and Roger Allam.

In 1997 Blair and the Labour Party sweep to power promising reform and modernisation, and the Queen wonders whether he intends to modernise the monarchy too. Less than four months later, Diana is killed in a car crash in a Paris tunnel, raising the question of how to honour a future king's mother who is no longer a royal. The Spencer family asks for a private funeral, and the Queen, determined to shield her grieving grandsons, stays on at Balmoral, making no public gesture. When Blair calls Diana the "People's Princess", the phrase is taken up by the press, and the nation's mourning swells into vast floral tributes outside Buckingham and Kensington Palaces.

As the royal family's popularity collapses, Blair's soars. His attempts to steer the Queen are rebuffed as giving in to hysteria, and Philip shares her disdain for the public displays of sympathy, but the private secretaries to both the Queen and Prince Charles quietly encourage Blair to keep trying. Finally he tells the Queen that seventy per cent of the country thinks her conduct is damaging the monarchy and that one in four people favour abolishing it, and urges her to fly a flag at half-mast over Buckingham Palace, pay her respects in person and address the nation. Shaken, she accepts that the country has changed during her reign and returns to London with Philip. Her live televised tribute to Diana helps calm the public mood, and the family attends the funeral at Westminster Abbey. At their next meeting, the Queen reflects with Blair on what has passed and warns him that public opinion may one day turn on him just as abruptly.

The film exceeded expectations at the box office, earning $56.4 million in the United States and Canada on a $15 million budget. Critics acclaimed it, with 97% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 91, and Mirren swept the major acting prizes, winning the Academy Award, BAFTA, Golden Globe and Screen Actors Guild Award for Best Actress.

overview: A hardened CIA operative finds himself at the mercy of a precocious 9-year-old girl, having been sent undercover to surveil her family.
tagline: Almost Totally in Control
title: My Spy
plot:
My Spy is a 2020 American action comedy film produced and directed by Peter Segal from a screenplay by Jon and Erich Hoeber. It stars Dave Bautista as a CIA operative who falls under the control of a precocious nine-year-old girl, played by Chloe Coleman in her film debut, with Kristen Schaal, Parisa Fitz-Henley and Ken Jeong in supporting roles. Released in Australian cinemas by STX Entertainment in January 2020, it was bought by Amazon Studios after the COVID-19 pandemic closed theaters and premiered on Prime Video in June 2020.

JJ, a former Army Ranger recently recruited by the CIA, wrecks his first big assignment in Pripyat, a plutonium deal between the Russian mafia and a terrorist named Hassan, through sheer lack of subtlety. Even so, his boss David Kim sends him with Bobbi, an eager tech operator who idolizes him, to watch the family of Victor Marquez, a French arms dealer who wants to sell plans for a miniaturized nuclear bomb to Hassan. Victor lost the plans to his brother David, who hid them before Victor murdered him, and the CIA suspects that David's American widow Kate and their daughter Sophie, who have moved back to Wicker Park in Chicago, may unknowingly have them. JJ and Bobbi set up a surveillance post in the family's apartment building, but Sophie quickly finds one of their hidden cameras, traces the signal and confronts them. She blackmails JJ into spending time with her, helping her navigate life at her new school and teaching her the basics of espionage as she struggles to fit in, and she works to bring him and her mother together. The unlikely friendship grows into something like a family, until Kim discovers that JJ has become personally involved with his targets and pulls him off the case, Kate learns the truth about him, and Victor arrives in Chicago to take back the plans, putting Sophie in danger and forcing JJ to prove himself.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has a 49% approval rating based on 127 reviews, with a consensus that it plugs Bautista into the "charismatic action star meets cute kid" formula with generally painless but mediocre results, and Metacritic gives it a score of 46 out of 100. A sequel, The Eternal City, was released in July 2024.

overview: Captain William Stanaforth is on a one-way solo mission to take the first steps in colonising Mars. Like all pioneers throughout history, Stanaforth will face insurmountable odds and life and death decisions as he rockets bravely through space.
title: Approaching the Unknown
plot:
Approaching the Unknown is a thought-provoking science fiction film that delves into the complexities of human existence and our understanding of the universe. The movie follows an astronaut who, after being presumed dead for years, returns to Earth with a mysterious presence on his spaceship.

At its core, Approaching the Unknown explores the theme of identity and what it means to be human. As the protagonist struggles to reintegrate into society, he begins to question the nature of his own existence and the reality of his experiences in space. The film raises questions about the blurred lines between reality and fantasy, leaving the audience to ponder the true essence of humanity.

The movie also touches on the theme of isolation and loneliness, as the protagonist's prolonged absence from human connection takes its toll on his mental state. His return to Earth serves as a catalyst for self-discovery, forcing him to confront the consequences of his time in space and the impact it has had on his sense of identity.

Furthermore, Approaching the Unknown delves into the idea of the unknown and the unexplained, leaving room for interpretation and speculation about the mysterious presence on the spaceship. This theme serves as a metaphor for the mysteries of the universe and our place within it, inviting the audience to contemplate the vastness of existence and our limited understanding of it.

Overall, Approaching the Unknown is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront their own assumptions about identity, reality, and humanity's place in the universe.

overview: A teenage girl living with schizophrenia begins to suspect her neighbor has kidnapped a child. Her parents try desperately to help her live a normal life, without exposing their own tragic secrets, and the only person who believes her is Caleb – a boy she isn’t even sure exists.
tagline: Some voices you can't outrun.
title: Fear of Rain
plot:
Fear of Rain is a 2021 American science fiction thriller film directed by Castore Segura and written by Castore Segura and Josh Boone. The movie stars Kaya Scodelario, Iain de Caestecker, and Will Poulter.

The main themes of Fear of Rain include:

1. **Trauma and PTSD**: The film explores the psychological effects of trauma on its characters, particularly Maya (Kaya Scodelario), who has experienced a traumatic event in her past. As she navigates the post-apocalyptic world, she struggles to cope with her emotions and confront her demons.
2. **Survival and Adaptation**: In a world ravaged by climate change and nuclear war, the characters must adapt to survive. The movie highlights their resourcefulness, resilience, and determination to stay alive in a harsh environment.
3. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Despite the dire circumstances, the film emphasizes the importance of human connection and empathy. Maya forms bonds with her companions, including Wolf (Iain de Caestecker) and Sam (Will Poulter), which help her cope with her trauma and find hope in a desolate world.
4. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Throughout the movie, the characters face challenges that force them to confront their past mistakes and make amends. Maya, in particular, undergoes significant personal growth as she learns to forgive herself and others.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, creating a complex and thought-provoking story that explores the human condition in the face of catastrophic events.

overview: Having lived through traumatizing events during WWII, Father Lankester Merrin takes a sabbatical from the Church to conduct archaeological excavations in British-administered East Africa. Merrin unearths an ancient Byzantine church believed have been built and then immediately buried to keep down evil from the crypt below. The natives are convinced that uncovering the church has unleashed a demon, and begin to violently clash with the British military troops. As the village rapidly disintegrates into chaos and war, Merrin must face-off with the demon which has taken possession of somebody close to him.
tagline: Go back to where the horror began.
title: Exorcist: The Beginning
plot:
Exorcist: The Beginning is a 2004 American supernatural horror film directed by Renny Harlin. A prequel to The Exorcist (1973) and the fourth installment in the series, it stars Stellan Skarsgård as the young Father Lankester Merrin, alongside Izabella Scorupco and James D'Arcy. The film was retooled from Paul Schrader's nearly finished Dominion: Prequel to the Exorcist after Morgan Creek Productions decided that version would not succeed, and the new production was designed to feature more scares and gore. Warner Bros. Pictures released it on August 20, 2004.

In Cairo in 1949, Merrin is working as an archaeologist, his faith shattered by an atrocity in the occupied Netherlands during the Second World War, when a sadistic SS officer forced him, as the village priest, to take part in arbitrary executions to save the rest of the villagers. A collector of antiquities named Semelier asks him to join a British excavation in the Turkana region of colonial Kenya, where a Byzantine church dating from around 500 AD has been found, centuries before Christianity reached that part of Africa, and to recover an ancient demonic relic believed to be inside it. Merrin travels to the site with the young Father Francis and meets the chief excavator Jefferies and the camp doctor, Sarah Novak. The church turns out to be perfectly preserved, as though it had been buried right after it was built, and its angel statues point their spears downward as if restraining something beneath the floor. Local workers are deserting the dig, believing the place is cursed, and Merrin learns that the lead archaeologist, Bession, went mad weeks earlier. When Merrin visits him at an asylum in Nairobi, Bession speaks in the voice of the Nazi officer who tormented Merrin and then takes his own life. Back at the camp, violence and strange occurrences multiply, a local boy is attacked, and Merrin, despite his loss of faith, is forced to confront the evil that has been awakened.

The film received negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 11% of 132 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus calling it a mediocre, gory horror film nowhere near the quality of the 1973 original, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 30 out of 100. It nevertheless grossed about $78 million worldwide against a $50 million budget, and Schrader's Dominion was released the following year.

overview: While exploring the neighboring woods, 13-year-old John discovers an unfinished bunker — a deep hole in the ground. Seemingly without provocation, he drugs his affluent parents and older sister and drags their unconscious bodies into the bunker, where he holds them captive. As they anxiously wait for John to free them from the hole, the boy returns home, where he can finally do what he wants.
title: John and the Hole
plot:
John and the Hole is a psychological drama film that delves into the complexities of human relationships, particularly those between parents and children. The movie revolves around a young boy named John, who forms an unlikely bond with his mother's new boyfriend, played by Charlie Plummer.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this relationship is not as innocent as it seems. The film expertly weaves together themes of trauma, manipulation, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The main character, John, struggles to distinguish between what is real and what is a product of his own imagination, which serves as a coping mechanism for the emotional pain he's experiencing.

The movie also explores the theme of toxic relationships, where one person seeks control over another through manipulation and coercion. This dynamic is particularly evident in the relationship between John and his mother's boyfriend, who uses guilt and emotional blackmail to exert power over John.

Furthermore, the film touches on the idea of childhood trauma and its lasting impact on a person's life. John's experiences serve as a catalyst for him to confront the dark secrets and emotions that have been buried beneath the surface.

Overall, John and the Hole is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that delves into the complexities of human relationships, trauma, and the fragility of childhood innocence.

overview: On the day of his retirement, a veteran CIA agent learns that his former protégé has been arrested in China, is sentenced to die the next morning in Beijing, and that the CIA is considering letting that happen to avoid an international scandal.
tagline: It's not how you play the game. It's how the game plays you.
title: Spy Game
plot:
Spy Game is a 2001 action-thriller film directed by Tony Scott. The movie revolves around the story of two men, Robert Dean (Robert Redford) and Aaron Cross (Brad Pitt), who form an unlikely bond over their shared passion for espionage.

At its core, Spy Game explores themes of loyalty, redemption, and the complexities of human relationships. The film delves into the emotional toll that a life of espionage takes on individuals, particularly those who are forced to abandon their personal lives in pursuit of their duty. Robert Dean's character, in particular, is driven by a sense of guilt and regret over his past mistakes, which he hopes to make amends for through his relationship with Aaron.

The movie also touches on the theme of mentorship and the passing of knowledge from one generation to another. As Aaron navigates the treacherous world of espionage, he learns valuable lessons from Robert Dean, who serves as a surrogate father figure to him. This dynamic highlights the importance of guidance, trust, and support in helping individuals navigate the challenges of their profession.

Furthermore, Spy Game explores the moral gray areas that often accompany a life of espionage. The film raises questions about the nature of right and wrong, highlighting the complexities of making difficult choices in high-pressure situations. Through Aaron's character, the movie humanizes the spy genre, revealing the personal costs and emotional consequences of living a life of secrecy and deception.

Overall, Spy Game is a gripping thriller that delves into the intricate world of espionage, exploring themes of loyalty, redemption, mentorship, and the complexities of human relationships in the process.

original_title: Professor Marston and the Wonder Women
overview: The unconventional life of Dr. William Marston, the Harvard psychologist and inventor who helped invent the modern lie detector test and created Wonder Woman in 1941.
tagline: Ever wonder?
title: Professor Marston and the Wonder Women
plot:
Professor Marston and the Wonder Woman is a 2017 biographical drama film directed by Patty Jenkins, produced by DC Entertainment, New Line Cinema, and Atlas Entertainment. The movie is based on the life of William Moulton Marston, the creator of the iconic superhero Wonder Woman.

The main themes of Professor Marston and the Wonder Woman are:

1. **Love and Relationships**: The film explores the complex relationships between William Moulton Marston (played by Luke Evans), his wife Elizabeth (played by Rebecca Hall), and their lover Olive Byrne (played by Bella Heathcote). The movie delves into the societal norms of the time, highlighting the double standards faced by women in relationships.
2. **Feminism and Empowerment**: Wonder Woman is a symbol of female empowerment, and the film showcases Marston's vision for a strong, independent woman. The movie also explores the struggles faced by women in the early 20th century, particularly in the context of marriage, work, and personal freedom.
3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: As Marston navigates his relationships and creative pursuits, he grapples with his own identity and sense of purpose. The film highlights the tension between his desire for artistic expression and the societal expectations placed upon him as a husband and father.
4. **The Power of Imagination**: The movie celebrates the power of imagination and creativity, showcasing Marston's innovative approach to comic book storytelling. Wonder Woman becomes a symbol of hope and inspiration for women around the world, reflecting Marston's vision for a more inclusive and empowering society.

Overall, Professor Marston and the Wonder Woman is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of love, relationships, feminism, identity, and self-discovery, all set against the backdrop of a fascinating true story.

overview: A rare mutation has occurred within the vampire community - The Reaper. A vampire so consumed with an insatiable bloodlust that they prey on vampires as well as humans, transforming victims who are unlucky enough to survive into Reapers themselves. Blade is asked by the Vampire Nation for his help in preventing a nightmare plague that would wipe out both humans and vampires.
tagline: Faster. Sharper. Deadlier.
title: Blade II
plot:
Blade II is a 2002 American superhero horror film directed by Guillermo del Toro and written by David S. Goyer. The movie is the sequel to the 1998 film Blade, starring Wesley Snipes as the titular character.

The story takes place two years after the events of the first film. Blade (Wesley Snipes) has been tracking a series of mysterious murders in Los Angeles, which seem to be connected to an ancient vampire virus that is spreading rapidly across the city. The virus, known as the "Virus," is created by the Reapers, a group of vampires who have been infected with the virus and are now seeking to destroy humanity.

Blade soon discovers that the source of the Virus is a powerful and ancient vampire named Bloodsucker (Ron Perlman), who has been awakened from his centuries-long slumber. Bloodsucker is revealed to be an extremely powerful and nearly indestructible vampire, with abilities that make him almost invulnerable to conventional attacks.

As Blade delves deeper into the mystery of the Virus, he teams up with a group of scientists, including Dr. Karen Jenson (Leigh Whannell), who are working on a cure for the virus. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Bloodsucker and his minions from spreading the Virus further.

Meanwhile, Blade also encounters a new ally in the form of Nyssa (Jessica Biel), a vampire hunter who is determined to help him defeat Bloodsucker. As they work together, Blade begins to question whether he can truly trust Nyssa, as she seems to be hiding secrets about her own past.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between Blade and Bloodsucker, with the two engaging in a fierce and intense fight that takes them across the city. In the end, Blade emerges victorious, but not before realizing that the Virus has already spread too far, and that humanity is now at risk of being wiped out.

Throughout the movie, del Toro's direction brings a dark and gothic atmosphere to the film, with a focus on practical effects and makeup to create the vampires. The action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, making for an exciting and thrilling ride.

Overall, Blade II is a gripping and entertaining sequel that expands on the world of the first film while introducing new characters and plot twists. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

overview: Nina and Allen split everything in their lives 50/50 after their break-up to avoid any drama—everything, that is, except for their favorite local bar. Nina and Allen must compete in a ridiculous, tavern-style custody battle for their prized watering hole, in which lines will be drawn, sides will be chosen, and beers will be drunken.
tagline: Time to settle the score one drink at a time.
title: Bar Fight
plot:
Bar Fight! is a 2022 American romantic comedy written and directed by Jim Mahoney and released by IFC Films. Melissa Fumero and Luka Jones star as Nina and Allen, a Los Angeles couple who have just broken up, with Rachel Bloom as Nina's best friend Chelsea, Julian Gant as Allen's business partner Milan, Vik Sahay as the bar's manager Dick, Dot-Marie Jones as the cook Elena, Daniel Dorr and Shontae Saldana as bartenders, Patrick Byas as the bouncer and Hope Lauren as a new waitress, Autumn.

After five years together, Nina and Allen, a laid-back furniture maker, are going through the most amicable of separations, set during the holiday season. When we first meet them they are cheerfully running a yard sale in Venice, and they divide everything, from the furniture to the giant television, fifty-fifty without a single argument. The one thing they cannot split is their favorite local hangout, the Martinez Bar & Lounge. On their first night out as singles, Allen arrives with Milan and Nina with Chelsea, a married mother of two who lives vicariously through her newly unattached friend, and the two exes realise they cannot both remain regulars.

With the staff's loyalties divided, a tavern-style custody battle is devised: Nina and Allen must face each other in a series of bar challenges, and the loser will be banned from the Martinez for good. The contests include a tricycle race through the bar, blindfolded darts, human bowling and a race to collect the most phone numbers from strangers before closing time. Around the competition the film sketches the bar's regulars and employees: a pushover manager who cannot stop an older woman from stealing the copper Moscow Mule mugs, a charming bartender with no ambition, a fearsome cook and a customer who pretends to be an agent to cadge free drinks. In a more wistful final stretch, Allen's settled, stuck-in-place nature and Nina's restlessness come to the surface as the couple confront why they split.

The film was released in theaters, on demand and on AMC+ on 11 November 2022. Reviews were mostly negative, with under a fifth of critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes. The Guardian found the premise nifty but the challenges dull and the main characters underwritten, while Movie Nation felt the comedy ran out of steam after half an hour and that Bloom's manic sidekick was its funniest element; several critics noted the chemistry between Fumero and Jones.

original_title: ポケモン・ザ・ムービーXY 破壊の繭とディアンシー
overview: In the underground Diamond Domain, where many Carbink live, the Mythical Pokémon Diancie serves as ruler. The Heart Diamond that sustains the land is beginning to fall apart, and Diancie is not yet strong enough to create a new one. While seeking help from the Legendary Pokémon Xerneas, Diancie encounters a group of thieves who want to take control of its diamond-producing power–and who awaken the Legendary Pokémon Yveltal from its cocoon in the process! Can Ash and his friends help Diancie discover its true power, stop Yveltal’s rampage, and save the Diamond Domain?
tagline: When destruction rises, can life prevail?
title: Pokémon the Movie: Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction
plot:
Pokémon the Movie: Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction is a 2014 Japanese animated science fantasy adventure film produced by OLM, Inc. (not Production I.G) and directed by Kunihiko Yuyama.

The main themes of Pokémon the Movie: Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction include:

1. Environmentalism: The movie highlights the importance of preserving nature and the consequences of human actions on the environment. The film's antagonist, Diancie, is a Pokémon that has been awakened by human greed and destruction of its natural habitat.
2. Greed vs. Responsibility: The story explores the theme of greed versus responsibility, as the main characters struggle with the consequences of their own actions. Team Flare's leader, Lysandre, is driven by his desire for wealth and power, while Diancie's awakening serves as a warning about the dangers of unchecked ambition.
3. Friendship and Unity: The movie emphasizes the importance of friendship and unity in overcoming challenges. The main characters, including Ash Ketchum, Iris, and Mairax, work together to stop Team Flare and save Diancie from destruction.

The film's plot follows Ash and his friends as they travel to the Alola region to participate in the Pokémon World Tournament. However, their journey is disrupted by the awakening of Diancie, a powerful Pokémon that has been sealed away for centuries. As the story unfolds, the characters must navigate the consequences of human actions on the environment and work together to stop Team Flare's destructive plans.

Overall, Pokémon the Movie: Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of environmentalism, greed, and responsibility, while also emphasizing the importance of friendship and unity.

original_title: Ed, Edd n Eddy's Big Picture Show
overview: When a scam goes horribly wrong and leaves the neighborhood kids furious, the Eds embark on a journey to find Eddy's brother in the "Ed, Edd, n Eddy" series finale.
tagline: One Failed Scam Gone Bad!
title: Ed, Edd n Eddy's Big Picture Show
plot:
Ed, Edd n Eddy's Big Picture Show is an animated film that explores the complexities of childhood friendships and the consequences of one's actions. The movie delves into the themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption as the trio navigates their relationships with each other and the people around them.

At its core, the film is a coming-of-age story that examines the challenges of growing up and the difficulties of maintaining friendships in the face of changing circumstances. The characters' experiences are marked by a sense of nostalgia and longing for a simpler time, highlighting the bittersweet nature of childhood and adolescence.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity, as each character struggles to find their place within the group and define themselves outside of their relationships with Edd and Ed. This exploration of self-discovery is intertwined with the consequences of the characters' actions, which serve as a catalyst for growth and change.

Ultimately, Ed, Edd n Eddy's Big Picture Show presents a nuanced portrayal of childhood friendships, one that acknowledges both the joys and the difficulties of these relationships. The film's themes are relatable and endearing, making it a heartwarming and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Jane is a beautiful but troubled American girl backpacking through Japan, when her raw street fighting skills draw the attention of Oshima, Japanese karate champion, who recruits and trains her to fight in the vicious, all-female, underground martial arts tournament known as "The Kumite". After months of rigorous preparation, Jane is ready to face off against the deadliest female fighters in the world, including Ling, the Chinese apprentice of Oshima's nemesis. But other nefarious forces lie in the shadows, and Jane and Ling will have to unite on a journey that will take them from the gritty underworld of Hong Kong to the glitz of Macao, before deciding who really is the best female fighter on the planet.
tagline: Fight for your life
title: Lady Bloodfight
plot:
Lady Bloodfight is a 2016 martial arts action film directed by Chris Nahon, best known for Kiss of the Dragon, from a screenplay by Bey Logan and Judd Bloch. An all-female reworking of Jean-Claude Van Damme's 1988 cult film Bloodsport and a standalone entry in that series, it stars the stuntwoman Amy Johnston as Jane Jones, with Muriel Hofmann as her teacher Shu, Kathy Wu as Shu's rival Wai, Jenny Wu as Wai's pupil Ling, Jet Tranter as the Australian fighter Cassidy, Mayling Ng as the Russian Svietta Chekhov and Kirt Kishita as the gambler Mr. Sang. Voltage Productions produced it.

Jane, a tough but troubled young American, shows her temper early when she deals with a rude customer at the diner where she works. Hoping to help her mother, who has sunk into heavy drinking, she leaves her small-town life and goes backpacking in Hong Kong, where her father vanished years earlier after taking part in a fighting tournament there. When three thugs try to mug her on the street, she fights them off with a ferocity that impresses Shu, a wise expert in the Wudang martial arts, who takes her on as a student and trains her for the Kumite, a brutal underground tournament for women fighters that carries a large cash prize.

Shu has reasons of her own: she needs a champion to face the pupil of her friend turned enemy, Wai, who teaches Shaolin with a far more lethal outlook and has recruited Ling, a scrappy street thief. After months of training, Jane and Ling must survive round after round against some of the deadliest fighters in the world before they can settle their teachers' feud. Fighters sometimes die in the Kumite, and disturbing events lead Jane to doubt her physical and emotional strength, while she keeps searching for the truth about her father. Mr. Sang, who watches the contest with great interest, eventually proves even more villainous than he first appears.

Vertical Entertainment released the film in the United States on 5 May 2017. Critics enjoyed its fight scenes but little else. The Hollywood Reporter found the action fast and suitably bloody and praised Johnston's physicality, while calling the script overcomplicated and noting how often the camera dwells on scantily clad women. Film Inquiry thought the dialogue clichéd and the father subplot sentimental but enjoyed the brutal fights as B-movie fun, and the Los Angeles Times advised skipping the plot and enjoying the action.

overview: Lewis is an outwardly ordinary guy, but in reality he is hiding an obsession – revenge – against Cathy. Lewis kidnaps Cathy in broad daylight and takes her to his home, where he locks her in a soundproof cell and attempts to extract a dark secret from her past.
tagline: There are some secrets we cannot escape
title: 10x10
plot:
10x10 is a 2018 psychological thriller directed by Suzi Ewing and written by Noel Clarke, who produced it through his company Unstoppable Entertainment and also appears as Dennis. Luke Evans stars as Robert Lewis and Kelly Reilly as Cathy, with Olivia Chenery as Lewis's late wife Alana, Skye Lucia Degruttola as his young daughter Summer, Jill Winternitz as Jen, Jason Maza and Stacy Hall as police officers and Norma Dixit as the housekeeper Alondra.

Cathy, a woman who listens to Christian radio and is about to open a new business, has coffee in town and drives to her gym, unaware that she is being watched and followed. In the parking lot, Lewis pulls a gun on her, ties her up, gags her and locks her in the trunk of his car. At his secluded modernist house, he shuts her in a padded ten-by-ten-foot room whose thick walls absorb every sound and asks her one question: what is her name. He wants neither sex nor money, only an admission.

Lewis is an ordinary man rather than a seasoned criminal, and Cathy repeatedly manages to break out before he overpowers her and returns her to the cell. Meanwhile he follows television reports about the Charleston Three, patients who died in mysterious circumstances at a hospital, where the nurses tried for the deaths were eventually cleared. Under pressure, Cathy confesses that she is really Natalie-Ann Stevens and that Cathy was her twin sister, who killed herself after their father's affair brought shame on the family in their strict religious community. As a nurse, Natalie appointed herself judge of patients who confided their sins, and she admits that she killed Alana, one of the three victims, for having cheated on Lewis. She even suggests that Summer is not his child. Escaping again, she seizes Summer, who bites her and gets away; the housekeeper is shot. As Lewis prepares to take recordings of her confession to the police, Cathy attacks him in the garage, and after he knocks her down, the falling door crashes onto her. Lewis tells Summer that he loves her and that she is his daughter.

The film was released in April 2018, with shooting having taken place in London and Atlanta. Critics were divided: the Los Angeles Times called it an effective thriller with smart performances and twists, while RogerEbert.com disliked its abduction premise and the misogynist trope behind its reversal, though it credited Ewing's command of suspense. In July 2023 it became the most-watched film on Netflix in the UK.

overview: Seven years since the Monsterpocalypse began, Joel Dawson has been living underground in order to survive. But after reconnecting over radio with his high school girlfriend Aimee, Joel decides to venture out to reunite with her, despite all the dangerous monsters that stand in his way.
tagline: An apocalyptic love story.
title: Love and Monsters
plot:
Love and Monsters is a 2020 American post-apocalyptic romantic comedy film directed by Michael Matthews and written by Matthew Robinson. The movie stars Dylan O'Brien, Jessica Henwick, and Mike Epps.

In the beginning of the story, we see a world that has been devastated by an alien invasion known as "The Monster". This event occurred about 20 years ago, when a massive spaceship descended upon Earth, destroying most of the planet's cities. The aliens, who are referred to as "Monsters", have taken over and are now living among humans.

The story follows Joel (played by Dylan O'Brien), a young man who has grown up in this new world. He is a survivor who lives on his own terms, scavenging for food and supplies in the ruins of civilization. Joel's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Aimee (played by Jessica Henwick), a strong-willed and independent woman who shares his desire to survive.

As they navigate this treacherous world together, Joel and Aimee develop feelings for each other. However, their budding romance is put to the test when Joel discovers that Aimee has been hiding a secret: she is pregnant with a child. This revelation sets off a chain of events as Joel must confront his own fears and insecurities about becoming a father in this harsh new world.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as "The Monster" (played by Mike Epps) emerges from the shadows. The Monster is an alien who has been living among humans for years, disguising himself as one of them. He becomes a key player in Joel's journey, offering guidance and support as he navigates his new role as a father.

As the story unfolds, Joel and Aimee must confront the dangers of their world head-on. They face off against hostile creatures, including giant spiders and other monstrous beings that roam the ruins of civilization. Along the way, they discover hidden strengths and weaknesses within themselves, learning to rely on each other in order to survive.

In the end, Joel and Aimee's love becomes a beacon of hope in a world that has been ravaged by destruction. They find a way to build a new life together, one that is filled with love, laughter, and a sense of purpose. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest of times, there is always the possibility for redemption and renewal.

Overall, Love and Monsters is a heartwarming and action-packed romantic comedy that explores themes of love, survival, and self-discovery. With its talented cast and engaging storyline, it's a must-see for fans of post-apocalyptic fiction and romance.

overview: A series of mysterious events changes the life of a blind pianist who now must report a crime that was actually never witnessed by him.
tagline: Every artist has a secret.
title: Andhadhun
plot:
Andhadhun is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human emotions, particularly those related to love, loss, and deception. The film's narrative revolves around the character of Aditya Shrivastava, a blind pianist who becomes embroiled in a murder mystery.

At its core, Andhadhun explores the theme of obsession, which is expertly woven throughout the story. Aditya's all-consuming passion for music and his desire to reconnect with his lost love, Supriya, drive him to make choices that ultimately lead to chaos. The film also delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing a world where people are willing to go to great lengths to achieve their goals.

The movie also touches upon the theme of identity, as Aditya navigates his way through a complex web of relationships and deception. His blindness serves as a metaphor for his emotional blindness, which allows him to see the world in a unique and distorted way. Through Aditya's character, the film raises questions about how our perceptions shape us and influence our actions.

Furthermore, Andhadhun is a commentary on the societal pressures that can lead people down a path of destruction. The film highlights the consequences of allowing obsession and desire to consume us, ultimately leading to devastating outcomes.

Overall, Andhadhun is a gripping thriller that masterfully explores the complexities of human emotions, revealing a world where nothing is as it seems, and the lines between good and evil are constantly blurred.

overview: Balto and the other sled dogs are feeling dejected because the mail that used to be delivered by dogsled is now being delivered by airplanes. But when a mail plane crashes in the mountains, the dogs come to the rescue.
title: Balto III: Wings of Change
plot:
Balto III: Wings of Change is an animated adventure film that explores several themes, primarily centered around the idea of perseverance and self-discovery.

The movie follows Balto's son, Kodi, as he sets out to find his father and learn about his legendary heroics. Along the way, Kodi faces various challenges and obstacles that test his courage and determination. Through these experiences, Kodi comes to understand the true meaning of being a hero and finds his own path in life.

One of the main themes of Balto III: Wings of Change is the importance of embracing one's heritage and legacy. Kodi struggles with living up to his father's reputation and finding his own identity, which serves as a metaphor for the challenges many people face when trying to live up to others' expectations.

The film also touches on the theme of letting go and moving forward. As Kodi navigates his journey, he learns to release his attachment to the past and focus on building a brighter future. This is particularly evident in his relationship with his mother, who encourages him to forge his own path and find his own sense of purpose.

Furthermore, Balto III: Wings of Change explores the idea of community and the power of working together towards a common goal. The film highlights the importance of supporting one another and celebrating individual strengths and weaknesses.

Overall, Balto III: Wings of Change is a heartwarming story that celebrates the values of perseverance, self-discovery, and community, making it an inspiring tale for audiences of all ages.

overview: A teenager who's lived a sheltered life because she's allergic to everything, falls for the boy who moves in next door.
tagline: Risk everything... for love.
title: Everything, Everything
plot:
Everything, Everything is a 2017 American romantic fantasy film directed by Stella Meghie and written by J. Mills Goodloe. The movie stars Amandla Stenberg as Madeline Whittier, a young girl who has a rare genetic disorder that makes her immune to everything outside of her house.

The main themes of the movie are:

1. **Isolation vs. Connection**: The film explores the tension between Madeline's need for isolation due to her condition and her desire for human connection. As she falls in love with Olly, played by Nick Robinson, she must navigate the risks of leaving her house and interacting with the outside world.
2. **Love Conquers All**: Despite the obstacles in their path, Madeline and Olly's love becomes a powerful force that helps them overcome their differences and find a way to be together.
3. **Self-Discovery**: Throughout the movie, Madeline undergoes significant personal growth as she learns to accept herself and her condition. She discovers new things about herself and finds ways to cope with her isolation.
4. **The Power of Human Connection**: The film highlights the importance of human relationships in our lives. Madeline's interactions with Olly and other characters show that even small connections can have a profound impact on our well-being.

Overall, Everything, Everything is a heartwarming and thought-provoking movie that explores themes of love, self-discovery, and the power of human connection.

belongs_to_collection.name: The Fast and the Furious Collection

overview: Dominic Toretto and his crew battle the most skilled assassin and high-performance driver they've ever encountered: his forsaken brother.
tagline: Justice is coming.
title: F9
plot:
F9: The Fast Saga is a 2021 action film directed by Justin Lin and written by Daniel Casey, Chris Morgan, and Justin Lin. The movie is the ninth installment in the Fast and Furious franchise.

The story begins with Dominic Toretto (Vin Diesel) being pursued by the authorities after a heist goes wrong. He is forced to go into hiding, but his brother Jakob (John Cena), who was thought to be dead, appears out of nowhere and reveals that he has been working for the government to take down Dom.

As Jakob's true intentions become clear, Dom realizes that his brother has been manipulating him all along. The two brothers engage in an intense battle, but their fight is interrupted by a group of mercenaries led by Cipher (Charlize Theron), who has returned from the previous film.

Cipher reveals that she has stolen a powerful device known as "Project 9," which can control and manipulate the world's energy supply. She plans to use it to hold the world hostage and demands that Dom hand over his brother in exchange for sparing humanity.

Dom, however, refuses to give up on Jakob and sets out to stop Cipher and her team. Along the way, he is joined by his family, including Letty (Michelle Rodriguez), Roman (Tyrese Gibson), Tej (Chris "Ludacris" Bridges), and Mia (Jordana Brewster).

As the story unfolds, Dom's team faces off against Cipher's mercenaries in a series of high-stakes action sequences. The movie features plenty of car chases, stunts, and explosive set pieces.

Throughout the film, Dom struggles with his complicated past and his relationship with Jakob. He also grapples with the consequences of his actions as a high-stakes thief and the toll it takes on those around him.

Ultimately, Dom and his team manage to outsmart Cipher and destroy Project 9, saving the world from her sinister plans. The movie concludes with Dom reflecting on the sacrifices he has made for his family and the lessons he has learned about loyalty and redemption.

Overall, F9: The Fast Saga is a thrilling action film that delivers on its promise of high-octane excitement and heart-pumping suspense. While it may not be as emotionally resonant as some of the previous films in the franchise, it remains a fun and entertaining ride from start to finish.

overview: A lab accident gives a hound named Shoeshine some serious superpowers -- a secret that the dog eventually shares with the young boy who becomes his owner and friend.
tagline: ONE NATION... UNDER DOG
title: Underdog
plot:
Underdog is a 2007 animated superhero comedy film that tells the story of a lovable and underappreciated dog named Underdog who dreams of becoming a hero. The movie explores several themes, including the importance of believing in oneself and one's abilities.

At its core, Underdog is a tale about self-discovery and empowerment. The main character, Underdog, is an ordinary dog with extraordinary potential, but he lacks confidence and recognition from those around him. As he navigates his way through various challenges and obstacles, Underdog learns to trust himself and his unique abilities, ultimately discovering that being different is not a weakness, but a strength.

The film also touches on the theme of friendship and loyalty. Underdog's relationships with his owner, Polly Purebred, and other characters in the story serve as a reminder of the importance of having supportive friends by your side. Through their interactions, the movie shows how these bonds can help us overcome adversity and achieve our goals.

Furthermore, Underdog pokes fun at societal expectations and the pressures to conform. The character of Sweet Polly Purebred, for instance, is a perfect example of this theme. She's a beautiful, high-society dog who struggles with her own identity and sense of purpose, highlighting the tension between being true to oneself and meeting the expectations of others.

Overall, Underdog is a heartwarming story about embracing one's individuality, finding confidence in oneself, and the power of friendship and loyalty.

overview: A Texas cop battles ex-navy seals who are trying to traffic drugs from Mexico into the USA.
tagline: Welcome To Mexico
title: The Shepherd: Border Patrol
plot:
The Shepherd: Border Patrol, also known as The Shepherd, is a 2008 American action film directed by Isaac Florentine. It stars Jean-Claude Van Damme as Jack Robideaux, a former New Orleans police officer who joins the U.S. Border Patrol, with a supporting cast including Natalie J. Robb, Stephen Lord, Gary McDonald, Scott Adkins and Van Damme's daughter Bianca Van Varenberg.

Jack arrives in Columbus, New Mexico, with a pet rabbit to take up a post with the border patrol under Captain Ramona García, played by Robb. The patrol is struggling against a dangerous smuggling operation that moves illegal immigrants and heroin across the porous border between Mexico and the United States, sometimes strapping explosive vests onto migrants so that any agent who intervenes risks being blown up. The smugglers turn out to be a rogue special forces unit led by Benjamin Meyers, played by Lord, and his right-hand man Karp, played by Adkins, who have taken over the region's trade by killing the major drug lords. Jack and his partner Billy Pawnell, played by McDonald, set out to bring the operation down.

When Meyers's men rig a missionary bus to carry drugs, Jack and Billy chase it across the border, beyond their jurisdiction, and Jack is arrested by Mexican police on Meyers's payroll and taken to the gang's compound. There he discovers that Billy is in league with Meyers, who has also kidnapped Ramona and her uncle Emile and kills Emile by throwing him into electrified water. Jack's crusade is personal: three months earlier his sixteen-year-old daughter, Kassie, played by Van Varenberg, died because of Meyers's drugs, and the rabbit he carries was hers. He swore at her grave to destroy whatever drug operation he could find. Jack and Ramona break free and kill Billy, and Ramona calls the Mexican police before being knocked out in a car crash while looking for a getaway vehicle. Jack fights the martial arts expert Karp, survives a brutal kick to the head and beats him to death. Abandoned by his would-be investors, Meyers prepares to shoot Jack, but Jack throws an explosive collar at him and detonates it. Afterward, Ramona advises Jack to return to New Orleans and his wife.

The film was shot over 47 days in Bulgaria between February and March 2007. It was released direct-to-DVD by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment in the United States on March 4, 2008, and in the United Kingdom that July.

overview: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is a remarkably talented young Viennese composer who unwittingly finds a fierce rival in the disciplined and determined Antonio Salieri. Resenting Mozart for both his hedonistic lifestyle and his undeniable talent, the highly religious Salieri is gradually consumed by his jealousy and becomes obsessed with Mozart's downfall, leading to a devious scheme that has dire consequences for both men.
tagline: Everything you've heard is true...
title: Amadeus
plot:
Amadeus is a 1984 period drama film directed by Miloš Forman, written by Peter Shaffer, and starring F. Murray Abraham as Antonio Salieri and Tom Hulce as Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.

The film begins with an elderly Antonio Salieri, who has grown old and bitter, recounting his life story to a reporter. According to Salieri, he was a struggling composer in 18th-century Vienna, where he worked for the powerful Archbishop of Salzburg, Cardinal Joseph II. Salieri's life is marked by jealousy and resentment towards Mozart, whom he perceives as a genius and a threat to his own artistic success.

As the story unfolds, we see Salieri's early days as a composer, where he meets Mozart, a young prodigy from Salzburg who has come to Vienna to study music. The two men are introduced by Cardinal II, who sees potential in Mozart and commissions him to compose music for the court. Salieri is envious of Mozart's talent and feels overshadowed by his success.

Throughout the film, we witness the rise of Mozart's fame, as he becomes a celebrated composer and performer in Vienna. Meanwhile, Salieri's own work is met with indifference and criticism from the public and the critics. He becomes increasingly bitter and resentful towards Mozart, whom he believes has stolen his ideas and taken credit for his genius.

As the years pass, Mozart's popularity grows, while Salieri's career stagnates. The two men engage in a series of intellectual and artistic competitions, with Mozart emerging as the clear winner. Salieri's jealousy and resentment boil over into hatred towards Mozart, whom he sees as a rival and a threat to his own existence.

The film reaches its climax when Mozart dies suddenly at the age of 35, leaving behind a legacy of music that will be remembered for centuries. Salieri is devastated by Mozart's death, but also relieved that he no longer has to compete with him. In a final twist, it is revealed that Salieri had actually poisoned Mozart, not out of jealousy or resentment, but out of a desire to eliminate the competition and secure his own place in history.

The film ends with an elderly Salieri, who has grown old and content, reflecting on his life and his relationship with Mozart. He realizes that he was wrong to hate Mozart and that his genius was not a threat to him, but rather a source of inspiration. The final shot is of Salieri's music, which is revealed to be inferior to Mozart's, but still worthy of recognition.

Overall, Amadeus is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human nature, creativity, and jealousy. It is a testament to the enduring legacy of Mozart's music and a reminder that true greatness can only be achieved through hard work, dedication, and a willingness to learn from others.

original_title: Portrait de la jeune fille en feu
overview: On an isolated island in Brittany at the end of the eighteenth century, a female painter is obliged to paint a wedding portrait of a young woman.
tagline: Don't regret. Remember.
title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
plot:
Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a 2019 historical drama film written and directed by Céline Sciamma. The film premiered at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival and received critical acclaim for its beautiful cinematography, nuanced performances, and thoughtful exploration of themes such as love, identity, and female desire.

The story takes place in 18th-century France, during the reign of King Louis XV. The film follows the relationship between Marianne (played by Adèle Haenel), a young and talented portrait painter, and Héloïse (played by Noémie Merlant), a beautiful and wealthy noblewoman who is engaged to be married.

The film begins with Marianne's arrival at Héloïse's family estate, where she is tasked with painting her portrait. As Marianne works on the painting, she becomes increasingly fascinated with Héloïse, and their mutual attraction grows stronger. Despite the societal norms that prohibit women from expressing romantic feelings towards each other, Marianne and Héloïse begin a secret affair.

As the story unfolds, we see the development of their relationship through a series of tender and intimate moments. Marianne's paintings become more expressive and sensual, reflecting her growing connection with Héloïse. The film also explores the societal constraints that women faced during this time period, including the limited options available to them for education, employment, and personal fulfillment.

Throughout the film, Sciamma masterfully captures the beauty of 18th-century France, from the lush landscapes to the opulent interiors of Héloïse's estate. The cinematography is stunning, with a focus on warm colors and soft lighting that creates a sense of intimacy and vulnerability.

As the story reaches its climax, Marianne and Héloïse must navigate the complexities of their relationship in the face of societal expectations. In a poignant and powerful finale, the two women find a way to express their love for each other, despite the obstacles that stand in their way.

One of the standout aspects of Portrait of a Lady on Fire is its thoughtful exploration of themes such as female desire and identity. The film raises important questions about the ways in which women have been marginalized and silenced throughout history, and how they can reclaim their agency and express themselves authentically.

Overall, Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a beautiful and powerful film that celebrates the beauty of human connection and the resilience of the human spirit. With its stunning cinematography, nuanced performances, and thoughtful exploration of themes, it is a must-see for anyone who loves great storytelling and compelling characters.

overview: Jerry Welbach, a reluctant bagman, has been given two ultimatums: The first is from his mob boss to travel to Mexico and retrieve a priceless antique pistol, known as "the Mexican"... or suffer the consequences. The second is from his girlfriend Samantha to end his association with the mob. Jerry figures alive and in trouble with Samantha is better than the more permanent alternative, so he heads south of the border.
tagline: Love with the safety off.
title: The Mexican
plot:
The Mexican is a 2001 American romantic comedy film directed by Gore Verbinski. The story revolves around Carlos O'Connell (played by Antonio Banderas), an American lawyer who travels to Mexico to retrieve his friend's body, only to find himself caught up in a complicated web of love and loyalty.

At its core, the movie explores themes of identity, cultural heritage, and the complexities of human relationships. Carlos, as an outsider navigating Mexican culture, must confront his own sense of belonging and purpose. His journey is marked by humorous misunderstandings and poignant moments of self-discovery.

The film also delves into the tension between tradition and modernity, as embodied by the contrasting worlds of Carlos's American upbringing and the vibrant, traditional Mexican culture he encounters. This clash sparks a romantic connection with Frida Berdansky (played by Salma Hayek), a beautiful and strong-willed woman who challenges Carlos to reevaluate his priorities.

Ultimately, The Mexican is a heartwarming tale about finding one's place in the world, embracing cultural differences, and learning to love unconditionally. Through its lighthearted humor and poignant moments, the movie celebrates the beauty of human connection and the power of love to transcend borders and boundaries.

overview: The Egyptian Queen Cleopatra bets against the Roman Emperor, Julius Caesar, that her people are still great, even if the times of the Pharaohs has long passed. She vows (against all logic) to build a new palace for Caesar within three months. Since all her architects are either busy otherwise or too conservative in style, this ambivalent honor falls to Edifis. He is to build the palace and be covered in gold or, if not, his fate is to be eaten by crocodiles. Edifis calls upon an old friend to help him out: The fabulous Druid Getafix from Gaul, who brews a fantastic potion that gives supernatural strength. In order to help and protect the old Druid, Asterix and Obelix accompany him on his journey to Egypt. When Julius Caesar gets wind of the project succeeding, he has the building site attacked by his troops in order to win the bet and not lose face. But just like the local pirates, he hasn't counted on Asterix and Obelix.
tagline: The funniest film in ancient history!
title: Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra
plot:
Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra is a 2002 French-Italian comedy film directed by Robert Guédiguian, produced by Renn Productions, and written by Robert Guédiguian. The movie is the fourth installment in the Asterix series, based on the comic book characters created by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo.

The story begins with Asterix (Gérard Depardieu) and Obelix (Christian Clavier), two ancient Celtic warriors who live in the village of Indomiti. The villagers are preparing for a grand festival to celebrate their victory over the Romans, but they soon discover that Cleopatra (Monica Bellucci), the last pharaoh of Ancient Egypt, has arrived in their village.

Cleopatra is on a mission to find the legendary Golden Egg, which she believes will grant her immense power and help her reclaim her throne. However, she is being pursued by Julius Caesar's (Gérard Depardieu) nephew, Octavius (Vincent Cassel), who seeks to capture Cleopatra and claim the Golden Egg for himself.

Asterix and Obelix are recruited by a group of Egyptian warriors to help Cleopatra on her quest. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious beasts, and Octavius's henchmen. The duo also befriends a young Egyptian warrior named Irini (Monica Bellucci), who becomes Obelix's love interest.

As the journey progresses, Asterix and Obelix face numerous challenges, from navigating treacherous tombs to battling giant spiders. Meanwhile, Cleopatra's true intentions are revealed, and it is discovered that she has been using her charm and beauty to manipulate those around her in order to achieve her goals.

In the end, Asterix and Obelix successfully retrieve the Golden Egg, but not before Octavius and his men arrive on the scene. A fierce battle ensues, with Asterix and Obelix fighting valiantly to protect Cleopatra and the Golden Egg. In the heat of the battle, Irini sacrifices herself to save Obelix, and Cleopatra is forced to flee.

The movie ends with Asterix and Obelix returning to their village, where they are greeted as heroes. However, the film's final scene reveals that Octavius has survived and is planning his revenge against Asterix and Obelix.

Overall, Asterix & Obelix: Mission Cleopatra is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that combines action, adventure, and humor. The movie features impressive stunts, witty dialogue, and memorable characters, making it a fun watch for fans of the Asterix series.

overview: In 2027, in a chaotic world in which humans can no longer procreate, a former activist agrees to help transport a miraculously pregnant woman to a sanctuary at sea, where her child's birth may help scientists save the future of humankind.
tagline: The future's a thing of the past.
title: Children of Men
plot:
Children of Men is a thought-provoking science fiction film directed by Alfonso Cuarón, released in 2006 by Universal Pictures. The movie takes place in a dystopian England where humans have lost the ability to procreate.

The story begins on December 28, 2021, with Theo Faron (Clive Owen), a former activist and now a taxi driver, who is struggling to cope with his own feelings of hopelessness and despair. He is haunted by the memory of his wife, Julia, who died in childbirth. The world has become a bleak and barren place, where people live in fear of their government's strict control over every aspect of life.

The plot thickens when Theo is approached by Kee (Clare-Hope Ashitey), an 18-year-old refugee from Africa, who claims to be pregnant. Theo agrees to help her, but soon realizes that the world has become so hostile towards people with children that even a pregnancy is seen as a threat.

As they embark on their perilous journey across England, they are pursued by the authorities and a ruthless gang leader named Harriet (Peta Wilson). Along the way, they meet Jimmy (Michael Caine), an elderly activist who was once a key figure in the anti-immigrant movement. He is now a broken man, struggling to come to terms with his own past actions.

As Theo and Kee navigate the treacherous landscape, they begin to realize that their journey may be more than just a simple escape from danger. They may hold the key to humanity's survival. The government has outlawed all forms of reproduction, fearing that it will lead to chaos and anarchy.

Throughout their journey, Theo and Kee form a bond, which becomes a source of hope in a world devoid of it. However, as they near their destination, they are met with unexpected challenges and revelations about the true nature of the world they live in.

The film's climax takes place at Harriet's hideout, where Theo and Kee finally find safety. However, the government has one last trick up its sleeve - a plan to "re-educate" people who have children, forcing them to abandon their offspring. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Jimmy had been working with the authorities all along, using his knowledge of the anti-immigrant movement to further their agenda.

In the end, Theo and Kee escape, but not without scars. The film ends on a hopeful note, as they look towards a future where humanity may have a chance to rebuild and start anew. The final shot is of Kee, who has given birth to a baby boy, symbolizing the possibility of a new beginning.

Children of Men is a powerful commentary on themes such as hope, despair, and redemption in a world that seems to have lost its way. The film's thought-provoking storyline, coupled with its stunning visuals and strong performances, make it a must-see for fans of science fiction and drama alike.

original_title: 劇場版 STEINS;GATE 負荷領域のデジャヴ
overview: One year after the events of the anime, Rintarou begins to feel the repercussions of extensive time travel, and eventually completely fades from reality. Kurisu, being the only companion to remember him, now must find a way to bring him back.
tagline: No one knows what the future holds. That’s why its potential is infinite.
title: Steins;Gate: The Movie - Load Region of Déjà Vu
plot:
Steins;Gate: The Movie - Load Region of Déjà Vu is a 2013 Japanese animated science fiction film based on the visual novel of the same name. The movie follows Rintarou Okabe, a self-proclaimed mad scientist who has created a device called the D-Mail, which allows him to send messages into the past.

The main themes of Steins;Gate: The Movie - Load Region of Déjà Vu include:

1. **Predestination vs. Free Will**: The movie explores the concept of predestination versus free will, as Okabe's actions in the past start to alter the present and future. This theme is central to the story, as Okabe struggles with the consequences of his decisions.
2. **The Butterfly Effect**: The film illustrates the butterfly effect, where small changes in the past have significant effects on the present and future. This theme highlights the unpredictable nature of time travel and the potential consequences of altering historical events.
3. **Friendship and Sacrifice**: Throughout the movie, Okabe's relationships with his friends and allies are put to the test as he navigates the complexities of time travel. The film showcases the importance of friendship and sacrifice in the face of adversity.
4. **The Dangers of Playing God**: The movie serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of playing god and tampering with the fabric of reality. Okabe's actions demonstrate the risks of scientific hubris and the unintended consequences of meddling with forces beyond human control.

Overall, Steins;Gate: The Movie - Load Region of Déjà Vu is a thought-provoking exploration of complex themes, featuring a gripping narrative that keeps viewers engaged until the very end.

overview: Lt. Wakes is a vengeful police detective determined to solve the murders of his partner and an informant, and joins forces with a witness injured during the shootings. After the killers pursue the witness across the abandoned floor of a hospital, she confirms Wakes's worst fears.
tagline: The enemy is closer than you think
title: Trauma Center
plot:
Trauma Center is a 2019 American action thriller directed by Matt Eskandari from a screenplay by Paul Da Silva. Nicky Whelan stars as Madison Taylor, a young woman hunted through a hospital by two corrupt police officers, with Bruce Willis as the police lieutenant assigned to protect her. The supporting cast includes Tito Ortiz, Texas Battle, Catherine Davis, Tyler Jon Olson, Lala Kent and Steve Guttenberg. The film was produced by Randall Emmett and George Furla's Emmett/Furla Oasis Films, among others, and released by Lionsgate's Grindstone Entertainment Group.

The story is set in San Juan, Puerto Rico. Detective Pierce and Sergeant Tull, two crooked cops, murder an accomplice in a warehouse because his phone holds evidence against them. Madison, who has moved to Puerto Rico and works long hours to support her teenage sister Emily after their mother's death, finishes a shift at the coffee shop where she works and stumbles on the body of Tony Martin, the partner of Lieutenant Steve Wakes, who had been investigating the warehouse killing. Caught in the crossfire, she is wounded, and the bullet that remains lodged in her leg becomes the only piece of evidence that can tie the two killers to the murder.

Madison wakes up in hospital, where Wakes asks her to help his investigation and, for her own safety, has her moved to an isolation ward in an empty wing of the building. Pierce and Tull realize she is the key to tracing the crime back to them and come to finish the job. Trapped overnight in the locked-down ward, Madison desperately calls Wakes for help, but with the lieutenant mostly failing to keep her safe she must use the meagre resources of the under-stocked unit to evade and fight off the two men in a long game of cat and mouse if she is to get out of the hospital alive.

Trauma Center received a limited theatrical release in the United States on December 6, 2019. Reviews were largely negative. Writing in the Los Angeles Times, Noel Murray described it as essentially Die Hard in a hospital and praised Whelan's Willis-worthy performance, but felt that Willis's few scenes were a distraction and that the confined setting was a cost-saving measure rather than a creative opportunity. Blu-ray.com called it short but hopelessly bland, while Film Threat considered it an undemanding piece of fun for fans of the star. On Rotten Tomatoes, only a small minority of critics' reviews are positive.

overview: Nine-year-old Frankie and his single mum Lizzie have been on the move ever since Frankie can remember, most recently arriving in a seaside Scottish town. Wanting to protect her deaf son from the truth that they've run away from his father, Lizzie has invented a story that he is away at sea on the HMS Accra. Every few weeks, Lizzie writes Frankie a make-believe letter from his father, telling of his adventures in exotic lands. As Frankie tracks the ship's progress around the globe, he discovers that it is due to dock in his hometown. With the real HMS Accra arriving in only a fortnight, Lizzie must choose between telling Frankie the truth or finding the perfect stranger to play Frankie's father for just one day...
title: Dear Frankie
plot:
Dear Frankie is a heartwarming and poignant film that explores the complexities of family relationships, love, and acceptance. The story revolves around Frankie, a young girl who writes letters to her absent father, pretending he's still alive after his death in World War II.

The main theme of Dear Frankie is the power of imagination and creativity as a coping mechanism for dealing with loss and grief. Frankie's letters serve as a way for her to hold onto memories of her father and maintain a sense of connection with him, even though he's no longer physically present. This theme is beautifully woven throughout the film, highlighting the importance of holding onto hope and finding ways to keep loved ones alive in our minds.

The film also delves into the complexities of family dynamics, particularly the relationships between mothers, daughters, and siblings. The mother-daughter bond is a central focus, as Frankie's mother struggles to balance her own grief with the need to care for her daughter. This theme is expertly handled, conveying the depth of love and sacrifice that exists within these relationships.

Furthermore, Dear Frankie touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Frankie navigates her way through adolescence, she begins to question her place in the world and her relationship with her family. The film encourages viewers to consider the importance of embracing one's individuality and finding one's own path in life.

Overall, Dear Frankie is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, and loss. Its themes are both poignant and uplifting, making it a truly memorable viewing experience.

overview: A group of astronauts living in the haunting emptiness of deep space struggle to cope after Earth suffers an extinction-level event.
tagline: Mankind's last hope.
plot:
3022 is a 2019 American science fiction film directed by John Suits and starring Omar Epps, Kate Walsh, Miranda Cosgrove and Angus Macfadyen, with Jorja Fox also in the cast. Set aboard a space station in the distant future, it follows a crew that suffers severe psychological strain and considers abandoning its mission after witnessing what appears to be the destruction of Earth. The story is told through a series of flashbacks and flash-forwards.

In 2190, the space station Pangea serves as a refueling stop for ships heading to Europa One, humanity's first space colony, and is staffed by crews serving ten-year shifts. Four American astronauts begin their term: Captain John Laine, engineer Jackie Miller, doctor Richard Valin and Lisa Brown. At first they get along well, and Laine and Miller fall in love, but as the years pass the isolation wears them down; by the fifth year Laine suffers night terrors and Valin is ready to declare the crew mentally unfit to continue. Then a massive explosion sends shockwaves through the station. Brown is gravely injured and later dies, repeated attempts to contact Earth go unanswered, and the station's instruments find only an asteroid field where the planet used to be. Miller, desperate to find her daughter, tries to leave in the station's escape pod, but the pod is lost in the attempt, and the survivors are left with failing life support and dwindling hope. Months later, as Laine and Miller plan a way to stretch their oxygen and Valin sinks into despair, a shuttle drifts past carrying three unconscious astronauts from the International Space Station, led by Captain Diane Ures, played by Fox, with two French crewmates. Their arrival at first renews everyone's spirits, but the extra mouths mean Pangea's resources will run out within a month, and the newcomers carry dark secrets about what they saw and what they did to survive, setting the two crews on a collision course.
