A member of the South Korean intelligence service frames Dong-cheol for the murder, and a massive manhunt is launched, led by Min Se-hoon, an NIS operative who was demoted to drill sergeant after a failed mission in which Dong-cheol spared his life, and by Kim Seok-ho, a corrupt NIS director. With the help of Choi Kyung-hee, a documentary filmmaker making a film about North Korean defectors who comes to sympathize with his past, Dong-cheol must evade his pursuers while trying to recover the top-secret materials his dying employer wanted him to find and settle his score with the man who destroyed his family.

The Suspect opened in South Korea on December 24, 2013, and became a box office hit with 4.1 million admissions; its distribution rights were sold to seven territories. It holds a 75% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 63 out of 100, and the Los Angeles Times praised its "inspired and teeth-grittingly determined" set pieces.

overview: A young girl from London moves to Africa with her parents where she befriends a lion cub.
tagline: Friendship is the wildest adventure of all
title: Mia and the White Lion
plot:
Mia and the White Lion is a 2018 South African drama film directed by Oliver Hermanus. The movie tells the story of Mia, a young girl who forms an unlikely bond with a white lion at a wildlife sanctuary in South Africa.

The main themes of Mia and the White Lion include:

1. **Conservation and Wildlife Preservation**: The film highlights the importance of conservation efforts and the impact of human activities on the environment. The movie showcases the struggles faced by the wildlife sanctuary, where Mia finds refuge with the white lion.
2. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Mia's backstory reveals a troubled past, marked by loneliness and abandonment. Her relationship with the white lion serves as a source of comfort and companionship, illustrating the healing power of connection and love.
3. **Empowerment and Self-Discovery**: Through her interactions with the white lion, Mia begins to find her own strength and sense of purpose. The film suggests that even in difficult circumstances, individuals can discover their inner resilience and potential for growth.
4. **Human-Animal Bonding**: The movie explores the deep emotional connection between humans and animals, highlighting the ways in which these relationships can transform our lives. Mia's bond with the white lion serves as a catalyst for her personal growth and healing.

Overall, Mia and the White Lion is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores themes of conservation, loneliness, empowerment, and human-animal bonding.

overview: A trio of female soul singers cross over to the pop charts in the early 1960s, facing their own personal struggles along the way.
tagline: All you have to do is dream.
title: Dreamgirls
plot:
Dreamgirls is a 2006 musical drama film that explores the highs and lows of fame, friendship, and the sacrifices one must make for success in the entertainment industry.

At its core, the movie delves into the theme of the American Dream, which is both alluring and elusive. The story follows three women - Deena Jones (played by Beyoncé), Lorrell Robinson (played by Anika Noni Rose), and Effie White (played by Jennifer Hudson) - who rise to fame in the 1960s as part of a Motown girl group, The Dreams.

As they navigate the cutthroat music industry, the film examines the tension between artistic expression and commercial success. The characters must confront the harsh realities of their newfound fame, including the pressures of maintaining a public image, dealing with personal demons, and making sacrifices for the sake of their careers.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by external forces. Deena, in particular, struggles to reconcile her desire for stardom with her own sense of self-worth, leading to a complex exploration of what it means to be authentic in the public eye.

Furthermore, Dreamgirls touches on the issue of female empowerment and the challenges women face in a male-dominated industry. The film highlights the ways in which women are often pitted against each other, both within their own group and with external forces that seek to exploit their talents for personal gain.

Ultimately, Dreamgirls is a powerful exploration of the human cost of fame and the sacrifices one must make to achieve success. Through its complex characters and themes, the movie offers a nuanced commentary on the music industry and the societal pressures that shape our lives.

overview: An aspiring dancer moves to New York City and becomes caught up in a whirlwind of flighty fair-weather friends, diminishing fortunes and career setbacks.
title: Frances Ha
plot:
Frances Ha is a 2012 American comedy-drama film directed by Noah Baumbach and written by Baumbach and Greta Gerwig, who also stars as Frances, a struggling 27-year-old dancer whose career and social life fall apart just as her best friend's life takes off. Mickey Sumner, Adam Driver, Michael Zegen and Michael Esper co-star. Shot in black and white, the film premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on September 1, 2012, and was released in the United States by IFC Films on May 17, 2013.

After graduating from Vassar College, best friends Frances and Sophie moved to Brooklyn with dreams of creative success. Frances is an apprentice with a dance company, waiting for a place in the permanent troupe, while Sophie works in publishing. At 27, Frances is still scraping by when she breaks up with her boyfriend, and soon afterwards Sophie announces that she is moving to a nicer apartment in Tribeca with another friend. Hurt, Frances rents a room in Chinatown with Lev and Benji, two affluent young men whose parents help with their rent. As Sophie grows closer to her boyfriend Patch, a well-paid Goldman Sachs employee, the two friends drift apart. Frances's boss, Colleen, begins easing her out of the company and denies her a Christmas show she needs to pay her rent, so Frances moves out, spends the holidays with her family in Sacramento, and then bounces from one temporary arrangement to another. When she learns that Sophie is leaving to follow Patch to Tokyo without having told her, Frances impulsively flies to Paris for a poorly planned weekend that brings her little comfort. Too proud to accept Colleen's offer of an office job, she returns to Vassar to work as a waitress and summer resident assistant, where an unexpected encounter with Sophie forces both women to confront what their friendship means. Gradually Frances learns to let go of the life she imagined and begins to find her own path, choreography included.

Frances Ha was widely acclaimed. It holds a 92% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a consensus that Baumbach's sensitive direction and Gerwig's endearing performance make its narrative drift easy to forgive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 82 out of 100, indicating "universal acclaim".

overview: When real estate developer Dan Sanders finalizes plans to level a swath of pristine Oregon forest to make way for a soulless housing subdivision, a band of woodland creatures rises up to throw a monkey wrench into the greedy scheme. Just how much mischief from the furry critters can the businessman take before he calls it quits?
tagline: He came. He saw. They conquered.
title: Furry Vengeance
plot:
Furry Vengeance is a 2010 American comedy film directed by Roger Kumble. The movie revolves around a wealthy businessman who moves his family to a rural area, only to discover that the community is being terrorized by a group of vicious and aggressive raccoons.

The main theme of Furry Vengeance is the clash between nature and human development. The film portrays the natural world as a force to be reckoned with, and the consequences of disrupting it. The raccoons in the movie serve as a symbol of the untamed power of nature, which ultimately proves to be more powerful than human ingenuity.

The film also explores the theme of community and the importance of living in harmony with one's surroundings. The residents of the rural area are initially portrayed as being at odds with each other, but they eventually come together to fight against the common enemy - the raccoons. This serves as a metaphor for the power of unity and cooperation in the face of adversity.

Furthermore, Furry Vengeance can be seen as a commentary on the human tendency to underestimate nature and the consequences of our actions. The film's protagonist is initially dismissive of the raccoons' threat, but ultimately learns a valuable lesson about respecting and appreciating the natural world.

Overall, Furry Vengeance is a lighthearted and entertaining film that uses humor and satire to explore themes of nature, community, and the importance of living in harmony with our surroundings.

overview: The captivating crime-fighting trio who are masters of disguise, espionage and martial arts are back! When a devious mastermind embroils them in a plot to destroy individual privacy, the Angels, aided by their loyal sidekick Bosley, set out to bring down the bad guys. But when a terrible secret is revealed, it makes the Angels targets for assassination.
tagline: Get some action.
title: Charlie's Angels
plot:
Charlie's Angels is a 2000 action-comedy film directed by McG and written by John Brancato, Michael Ferris, and Shane Black. The movie is a remake of the 1976 television series of the same name.

The story begins with Charlie Townsend (played by John Forsythe), a wealthy businessman who employs three women, known as Angels, to carry out various missions for him. The Angels are: Dylan Sanders (played by Drew Barrymore), a tough and confident operative; Natalie Cook (played by Cameron Diaz), a sweet and innocent-looking but deadly Angel; and Alex Munday (played by Lucy Liu), a quiet and reserved but highly skilled Angel.

The movie opens with the Angels on a mission to stop a group of terrorists who are planning to steal a valuable diamond. The Angels successfully complete their mission, but not before they are ambushed by the terrorists' leader, Warren Stiles (played by Crispin Glover).

After the mission, Charlie reveals that he has been watching the Angels from afar and is impressed with their skills. He decides to take them on as his personal agents, giving them a team of experts to help them complete their missions.

As the story progresses, the Angels are tasked with stopping a group of rogue agents who have stolen a valuable diamond. The Angels soon discover that the diamond is actually a fake, and they must track down the real one before it falls into the wrong hands.

Along the way, the Angels encounter various obstacles and challenges, including a villainous character named Warren Stiles, who is revealed to be working for a wealthy businessman named James Dalton (played by Robert Patrick). The Angels also discover that Charlie's true intentions are not entirely pure, and they begin to question their loyalty to him.

In the end, the Angels successfully complete their mission and stop the villains. However, the movie ends with a twist: Charlie is revealed to be working for a secret organization known as "The Syndicate," which has been manipulating world events from behind the scenes.

Throughout the movie, the Angels are portrayed as strong and independent women who can hold their own in any situation. The film features plenty of action, humor, and style, making it an entertaining watch for audiences.

Overall, Charlie's Angels is a fun and action-packed movie that pays homage to the original television series while also offering something new and exciting.

overview: When two bus crash survivors awake to discover that they are the only people left in their small town, they must form an unlikely alliance in a race to unravel the truth behind their isolation. As strange events begin to unfold, they start to question whether the town they know so well is really what it seems.
title: After
plot:
After is a 2012 fantasy horror film written and directed by Ryan Smith (also known as Ryan Whitaker). Steven Strait and Karolina Wydra star, with Sandra Lafferty as Aunt Lu and Madison Lintz and Chase Presley as the young versions of the leads. It premiered at the Nashville Film Festival on April 19, 2012.

Ana, a nurse who once wanted to write horror stories, meets Freddy, a graphic novelist, on a bus and finds that they live on the same street in the small town of Pearl. Then the bus crashes. Ana wakes at home in a strange, permanent twilight to find the town deserted. She joins Freddy, and they find that every means of communication is dead and that a towering wall of black fog, the Darkness, surrounds Pearl and is closing in. The town center keeps shifting back to August 23, 1992, when they watch themselves as children: Ana with her beloved Aunt Lu, who raised her, and Freddy with his kind stepfather Phil. A recording at the hospital reveals that Ana has been in a coma for two months, and that her living will means life support will be switched off in three days. That is exactly when the fog will reach the center of town.

Freddy suspects that the Darkness reflects Ana's dying brain. Inside it they find a locked door surrounded by thousands of keys. It is the same image Freddy once drew in his childhood comic Behind the Veil. They are pursued by a toothed monster from a play young Ana wrote, and it carries the key in its chest. Reliving the day of the 1992 carnival, they see their younger selves catch each other's eye. Ana explains that Aunt Lu was fatally injured that night. Freddy goes off to face the monster alone and is dragged away. Ana then sees the truth: Freddy's bullying friends pushed him into the vandalism that caused the fire that left Lu in a fatal coma. When the beaten Freddy returns and apologizes, Ana kills the monster, takes the key and pulls him through the door. She wakes up in hospital and finds that Freddy, already discharged, has partial amnesia. Using his sketchbook, she helps him remember.

Smith and producer Brandon Gregory spent three years on the film. It was shot in Alabama but otherwise made in Nashville. Strait joined after a friend showed him the script, which he praised as original, intelligent and heartfelt. Canadian distributor Mongrel Media acquired North American rights in 2013. Reviews were mixed to positive, with horror sites especially enthusiastic, while Exclaim! found the leads' conversations lacking nuance.

overview: Successful author Veronica finds herself trapped in a horrifying reality and must uncover the mind-bending mystery before it's too late.
tagline: If it chooses you, nothing can save you.
title: Antebellum
plot:
Antebellum is a 2020 American horror film written and directed by Gerard Bush and Christopher Renz. The movie stars Janelle Monáe, Eric Lange, and Jena Malone.

The main themes of Antebellum revolve around the horrors of slavery, racism, and the cyclical nature of oppression. The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping between two timelines: 1903, where the story takes place during the Jim Crow era, and 2020, where the protagonist, Veronica Henley (Janelle Monáe), finds herself trapped in a nightmarish world that mirrors her own reality.

Throughout the film, Bush and Renz explore themes of systemic racism, oppression, and the ways in which historical trauma continues to affect marginalized communities. The movie also delves into the concept of "double consciousness," coined by W.E.B. Du Bois, which refers to the experience of living with two conflicting identities: one that is imposed upon you by society, and another that is authentic and true to yourself.

The film's use of horror elements serves as a metaphor for the terror and trauma experienced by enslaved people and those who continue to face systemic racism today. By presenting these themes in a thought-provoking and unsettling manner, Antebellum encourages viewers to confront the dark history of America and its ongoing impact on contemporary society.

Ultimately, the film's ending suggests that true freedom and liberation can only be achieved through self-awareness, resistance, and collective action. The movie serves as a powerful commentary on the need for ongoing dialogue and activism in the face of systemic oppression, and it challenges viewers to consider their own complicity in perpetuating or challenging these systems.

Overall, Antebellum is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores some of the most pressing issues facing America today. Its non-linear narrative and use of horror elements make for a compelling and unforgettable viewing experience.

overview: Three magazine employees head out on an assignment to interview a guy who placed a classified ad seeking a companion for time travel.
tagline: What would you go back for?
title: Safety Not Guaranteed
plot:
Safety Not Guaranteed is a 2012 American independent comedy-drama film directed by Colin Trevorrow and written by Derek Connolly. The movie follows Darius, a young man who answers a mysterious classified ad placed by Kenneth, a charismatic but troubled individual, to join him on a road trip across the country.

The main theme of Safety Not Guaranteed is the exploration of existentialism and the search for meaning in life. The film delves into the idea that people often go through the motions of daily life without questioning their purpose or values. Darius's journey with Kenneth forces him to confront his own sense of identity and the emptiness of modern society.

Throughout the movie, Trevorrow also explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and human connection. The film highlights the complexities of relationships and how people often struggle to form meaningful connections in a world that seems to value superficiality over substance. The title "Safety Not Guaranteed" serves as a metaphor for the uncertainty and unpredictability of life, emphasizing the importance of embracing the unknown and taking risks.

The movie also touches on the idea of nostalgia and the longing for a simpler time. Kenneth's character is a nostalgic figure who embodies a bygone era, and his presence in Darius's life sparks a sense of wonder and curiosity about the past. However, this nostalgia is tempered by the harsh realities of the present, highlighting the tension between yearning for something lost and accepting the imperfections of the world we live in.

Ultimately, Safety Not Guaranteed is a thought-provoking film that encourages viewers to reevaluate their priorities and values in life. It's a story about finding meaning in the mundane and embracing the complexities of human experience.

overview: Uta — the most beloved singer in the world. Her voice, which she sings with while concealing her true identity, has been described as “otherworldly.” She will appear in public for the first time at a live concert. As the venue fills with all kinds of Uta fans — excited pirates, the Navy watching closely, and the Straw Hats led by Luffy who simply came to enjoy her sonorous performance — the voice that the whole world has been waiting for is about to resound.
tagline: An almighty voice. With fiery red locks.
title: One Piece Film Red
plot:
One Piece Film Red is a 2022 Japanese animated adventure film directed by Goro Taniguchi, produced by Toei Animation, and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures and Toho.

The film takes place after the Wano Country arc of the One Piece manga and anime series. The story follows Monkey D. Luffy and his crew, the Straw Hat Pirates, as they search for a mysterious island called "Red Island" (also known as "Red Land"). According to legend, Red Island is said to be the birthplace of the legendary pirate Shanks, who is considered one of the most powerful pirates in the world.

Upon arrival at Red Island, Luffy and his crew discover that it's actually a massive, ancient temple filled with treasures and mysterious artifacts. However, they soon realize that they're not alone on the island, as they encounter a group of powerful warriors known as the "Red Pirates," who are also searching for the legendary treasure.

As Luffy and his crew navigate through the island, they uncover the secrets behind Red Island's ancient history and the true nature of the Red Pirates. Along the way, they face off against various formidable foes, including the enigmatic and powerful "Pirate King" of Red Island.

Throughout the film, Taniguchi explores themes of friendship, camaraderie, and the power of unity among pirates. The animation is stunning, with vibrant colors and intricate details that bring the world of One Piece to life in a way that's both faithful to the original manga and anime series and visually stunning in its own right.

One Piece Film Red features an all-star voice cast, including Ichiro Okamoto as Monkey D. Luffy, Akemi Okamura as Roronoa Zoro, and Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji. The film also includes cameos from other One Piece characters, adding to the excitement and nostalgia for fans of the series.

Overall, One Piece Film Red is a thrilling adventure that's sure to delight both longtime fans of the One Piece franchise and newcomers alike. With its stunning animation, engaging storyline, and memorable characters, it's a must-see for anyone who loves action-packed adventures with a dash of humor and heart.

overview: The star of a team of teenage crime fighters falls for the alluring villainess she must bring to justice.
tagline: Evil is so totally busted!
title: D.E.B.S.
plot:
D.E.B.S. is a 2004 American action comedy film directed by Peter Sollett. The movie follows the story of Jill Johnson (played by Sara Paxton), a high school student who is recruited into an elite spy training program called D.E.B.S. (Defense, Espionage, and Stealth Bureau).

The main themes of D.E.B.S. include:

1. Female empowerment: The film explores the idea of women taking control of their lives and pursuing careers that are traditionally male-dominated. Jill and her fellow trainees are encouraged to be confident, assertive, and independent, which serves as a powerful message for young women.
2. Identity formation: As Jill navigates the D.E.B.S. program, she must confront her own identity and figure out who she is outside of her relationships with others. The film explores themes of self-discovery and growth.
3. Friendship and camaraderie: Despite their differences, the trainees form strong bonds with each other, which becomes a source of strength and support throughout the story.
4. Coming-of-age: D.E.B.S. can be seen as a coming-of-age story for Jill, who is transitioning from adolescence to adulthood. The film explores her growth and development as she faces challenges and learns valuable lessons.

Overall, D.E.B.S. is a fun and entertaining film that offers a fresh take on the spy genre while also exploring important themes about identity, empowerment, and friendship.

overview: The story revolves around a top-secret resort for retired U.S. intelligence officers. A group of criminals led by Balzary breach the compound, hellbent on revenge on Robert, forcing the retired officer and his son to save the day.
tagline: This prison has no bars.
title: Fortress
plot:
Fortress is a 2021 American action thriller directed by James Cullen Bressack from a screenplay by Alan Horsnail, based on a story by Emile Hirsch and Randall Emmett. Jesse Metcalfe stars as Paul, with Bruce Willis as his father Robert, Chad Michael Murray as the villain Frederick Balzary, Kelly Greyson as Kate, the director of the facility, Shannen Doherty as its security chief Dobbs, alongside Ser'Darius Blain. It was the first of two films shot back to back in Puerto Rico in 2021, followed by Fortress: Sniper's Eye.

Robert, a retired CIA officer, lives at Forge Mountain, a secluded, top-secret resort that shelters former U.S. intelligence operatives after they leave government service. His son Paul, who runs a cryptocurrency company, has not seen or heard from him in three years, since around the time Paul's mother died, but now tracks him down out of necessity: the business is close to bankruptcy, and Paul needs $5 million to make it cash positive, which means persuading Robert to sign a document releasing money from his mother's estate. Paul is unaware that his father has been quietly following his life and career.

The awkward reunion is cut short when a team of mercenaries led by Balzary breaks into the resort. Balzary, who once worked alongside Robert, has a score to settle and knows about his old colleague's history with dark money. Robert hurries his son into the Fortress, a high-tech underground bunker with steel walls and an arsenal, but the attackers kill the guards, follow them inside and tie them up. Balzary explains that Russians have kidnapped his wife, Sasha, and that he needs the money Robert stole from him to pay her ransom; Robert has invested it in cryptocurrency, and he makes Paul memorise the access code exactly, telling him it could save his life. Learning for the first time about his father's past, Paul must fight alongside Robert, Kate and Dobbs to survive, discovering along the way that he can stand up for himself.

Lionsgate released the film in select theaters and on demand on 17 December 2021. Reviews were mostly negative, with only one of five critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes; The New York Times dismissed it as one of Bressack's cheap thrillers, while Film Threat and Cinema Daily US praised its pace, action and production values. Willis was nominated for a special Golden Raspberry category devoted to his 2021 performances, later rescinded after his retirement because of aphasia.

overview: Set in the futuristic Metro City, Astro Boy (Atom) is a young robot with incredible powers created by a brilliant scientist in the image of the son he had lost. Unable to fulfill his creator's expectations, Astro embarks on a journey in search of acceptance, experiencing betrayal and a netherworld of robot gladiators, before returning to save Metro City and reconcile with the father who rejected him.
tagline: Have a blast.
title: Astro Boy
plot:
Astro Boy is a 2009 animated superhero film loosely based on Osamu Tezuka's manga series. Produced by the Hong Kong company Imagi Studios, it was directed by David Bowers, who co-wrote it with Timothy Hyde Harris. Freddie Highmore voices Toby Tenma and his robot double Astro, with Kristen Bell as Cora, Nicolas Cage as Dr. Tenma, Donald Sutherland as President Stone, Bill Nighy as Dr. Elefun, Samuel L. Jackson as Zog and Nathan Lane as Hamegg, alongside Matt Lucas, Eugene Levy and Charlize Theron.

In the 22nd century, Toby lives in Metro City, which floats high above the polluted Earth. His father, Dr. Tenma, and Dr. Elefun of the Ministry of Science have built the Peacekeeper, a defence robot for President Stone, who is seeking re-election, powered by two cores from a star fragment: a positive blue one and a negative red one. Against their warnings, Stone loads the red core, and the robot runs amok, killing Toby. The grieving Tenma builds a robot with his son's memories, the power of flight and other defences, powered by the blue core, but soon rejects him as no true replacement. Hunted by Stone, who wants the blue core, the boy is blasted off the edge of the city.

He lands in a vast junkyard of discarded robots, where he meets orphans led by Cora, the robot dog Trashcan and the bumbling Robot Revolutionary Front, who rename him "Astro". The children's guardian, Hamegg, a former head of the Ministry of Science, takes him in, and Astro revives an old construction robot, Zog, with some of his core's energy. Cora admits that she ran away from Metro City and misses her parents. Discovering that Astro is a robot, Hamegg forces him to fight in his Robot Games, but Astro and Zog refuse to fight each other, and Astro saves Hamegg when Zog turns on him. Astro then surrenders to Stone's forces. Back in Metro City, Tenma realises he loves Astro as much as Toby and sets him free. Stone powers the Peacekeeper with the red core, but it absorbs him and swells to enormous size. Astro saves the falling city, then sacrifices himself by flying into the Peacekeeper's red core, destroying it. Stone is arrested, Zog revives Astro, Cora returns to her parents, and Astro springs into action when an alien monster attacks the city.

Released in Hong Kong on October 8, 2009, and in the United States later that month, Astro Boy received mixed reviews, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned well short of its $65 million budget, and Imagi Studios closed in February 2010.

overview: Yearning for an evening without their kids, some friends plan a night out. But to do this, their husbands need to watch the kids. What can go wrong?
tagline: What could go wrong?
title: Moms' Night Out
plot:
Moms' Night Out is a 2014 American comedy film directed by Kirk Jones. The movie revolves around three mothers - Mary (Sandra Bullock), Jules (Tina Fey), and Gwendolyn (Maya Rudolph) - who are struggling to balance their domestic lives with their own desires for freedom and friendship.

The main theme of the movie is the importance of female friendships and the need for women to reconnect with each other, especially in a society that often pressures them to prioritize family over personal interests. The film explores how these three mothers, despite their different backgrounds and personalities, come together to rediscover themselves and find joy in their lives.

Through the characters' experiences, the movie highlights the challenges of motherhood, including the pressure to be perfect, the loss of identity, and the struggle to maintain relationships outside of family. The film ultimately suggests that women can find empowerment and happiness by embracing their individuality and nurturing their friendships.

The movie also touches on themes of suburban ennui, social expectations, and the search for meaning in a seemingly ordinary life. As the characters let loose and have fun, they begin to see themselves in a new light, and the film becomes a heartwarming exploration of female friendship and personal growth.

overview: After her mom's death, Casey pulls away from everyone in her life, including her emotionally distant dad. With help from a magic spell, she tries to bring her mother back from the dead; instead, Casey's words accidentally awaken one of her least favorite toys: a statuesque Barbie clone named Eve. Things get worse when Casey's dad develops a crush on his daughter's living doll.
tagline: She was a perfect doll. Now she's the real thing.
title: Life-Size
plot:
Life-Size is a 2000 American fantasy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie revolves around Casey Stuart, a teenage girl who accidentally brings her doll, Eve, to life. As Eve navigates the complexities of human life, she learns valuable lessons about friendship, love, and growing up.

One of the primary themes of Life-Size is the importance of empathy and understanding in relationships. Through Eve's experiences, the film highlights the need for people to put themselves in others' shoes and appreciate their unique perspectives. Casey and Eve's unlikely friendship serves as a catalyst for this theme, demonstrating how two individuals from different worlds can come together and form a strong bond.

Another significant theme present in Life-Size is the concept of identity and self-discovery. As Eve navigates her new surroundings, she struggles to reconcile her doll-like existence with her newfound human experiences. This internal conflict serves as a metaphor for Casey's own journey towards self-discovery, as she learns to let go of her insecurities and embrace her individuality.

The film also explores the theme of responsibility and accountability. As Eve becomes more confident in her abilities, she begins to take on more responsibilities, including helping Casey with her problems. However, this newfound sense of agency also brings its own set of challenges, forcing Eve to confront the consequences of her actions.

Lastly, Life-Size touches on the idea of love and acceptance. Through Casey's relationships with Eve and her family, the film shows that love can take many forms, including unconditional acceptance and support. The movie ultimately conveys a heartwarming message about the importance of embracing those who may be different from us, and finding common ground in our shared humanity.

Overall, Life-Size is a lighthearted yet thought-provoking film that explores themes of empathy, identity, responsibility, and love, making it a delightful watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Firemen brothers Brian and Stephen McCaffrey battle each other over past slights while trying to stop an arsonist with a diabolical agenda from torching Chicago.
tagline: Silently behind a door, it waits.
title: Backdraft
plot:
Backdraft is a 1991 American drama film directed by Ron Howard, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and distributed by Touchstone Pictures.

The movie follows two brothers, Stephen "Bull" McCaffrey (played by Kurt Russell) and Brian McCaffrey (played by William Baldwin), who are both firefighters in Chicago. The story revolves around their personal and professional struggles as they navigate the challenges of their job, family relationships, and personal demons.

Some of the main themes present in Backdraft include:

1. Family dynamics: The movie explores the complex relationships between the McCaffrey brothers, particularly their father's influence on their lives and careers.
2. Identity crisis: Both Bull and Brian struggle with finding their place in the world, whether it's as firefighters or as individuals. This theme is reflected in their differing approaches to life and their respective career choices.
3. Loyalty and brotherhood: The film highlights the strong bond between the McCaffrey brothers, who rely on each other for support and protection both on and off the job.
4. Personal growth and redemption: Throughout the movie, Bull and Brian face various challenges that force them to confront their personal flaws and weaknesses, ultimately leading to a path of self-discovery and redemption.

The film's climax features an intense fire scene, which serves as a metaphor for the characters' inner struggles and the need for transformation. The ending is particularly poignant, as both brothers come to terms with their past mistakes and find a way to move forward, united in their pursuit of personal growth and healing.

Overall, Backdraft is a powerful exploration of family, identity, loyalty, and redemption, set against the backdrop of the high-stakes world of firefighting.

overview: The story of Michael Oher, a homeless and traumatized boy who became an All American football player and first round NFL draft pick with the help of a caring woman and her family.
tagline: Based on the extraordinary true story
title: The Blind Side
plot:
The Blind Side is a biographical sports drama film directed by John Lee Hancock, released in 2009 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie is based on the life of Michael Oher, an American football player who was adopted by a wealthy family.

The story begins with Michael Oher (played by Quinton Aaron), a homeless and traumatized teenager living in Memphis, Tennessee. He is forced to live in foster care after his mother's death due to HIV/AIDS. Despite his difficult circumstances, Michael shows exceptional athletic talent, particularly in football.

Enter the Tuohy family - Sean (Tim McGraw), Leigh Anne (Sandra Bullock), and their two children, S.J. (Jae Head) and Collin (Taylor John Smith). The family is wealthy and influential, but they are also kind-hearted and open to helping those in need. When Michael's foster care case comes up for review, the Tuohys decide to take him in.

Initially, Michael struggles to adjust to his new life with the Tuohys. He faces cultural and social challenges as an outsider in their affluent household. However, Leigh Anne, a devoted mother, takes it upon herself to help Michael overcome his emotional scars and develop into a confident individual.

As Michael settles into his new home, he begins to flourish under the Tuohys' care. Sean, a successful businessman, becomes a mentor to Michael, teaching him valuable life lessons about responsibility and hard work. Meanwhile, Leigh Anne forms a close bond with Michael, helping him to heal from his traumatic past.

Throughout the movie, Michael's football talent is showcased, as he joins the Briarcrest Christian School team under Coach Cotton (Ray McKinnon). With the Tuohys' support, Michael becomes an exceptional player, earning college scholarships and eventually being drafted by the Baltimore Ravens in 2009.

The Blind Side explores themes of family, love, and redemption. The movie highlights the transformative power of the Tuohy family's kindness and generosity towards Michael Oher, who was once a lost soul. As Michael navigates his new life, he finds solace in the Tuohys' unwavering support and guidance.

The film culminates with Michael's successful NFL career, as well as his adoption by the Tuohy family. The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, showcasing the strong bond between Michael and the Tuohys, who have become like a second family to him.

Overall, The Blind Side is an inspiring true story of hope, resilience, and the impact one family can have on another's life.

overview: A young woman's penchant for sensational Gothic novels leads to misunderstandings in the matters of the heart.
title: Northanger Abbey
plot:
Northanger Abbey is a 2007 film adaptation of Jane Austen's novel of the same name, produced by WGBH Boston. The movie explores several timeless and thought-provoking themes that continue to resonate with audiences today.

At its core, Northanger Abbey is a commentary on the societal pressures and expectations placed on women during the late 18th century. The protagonist, Catherine Morland, embodies the ideal of a young woman navigating the complexities of high society, where appearances can be deceiving and social standing is everything. As Catherine navigates this treacherous landscape, she must confront her own desires, values, and sense of identity.

One of the primary themes of Northanger Abbey is the tension between reality and fantasy. Catherine's imagination often gets the better of her, leading her to misinterpret the world around her. This blurs the lines between what is real and what is imagined, highlighting the fragility of perception and the ease with which our understanding can be distorted.

The film also delves into the theme of social class and its impact on relationships. The contrast between Catherine's humble upbringing and the aristocratic world she enters serves as a backdrop for exploring issues of status, privilege, and the constraints placed on individuals by their social position.

Furthermore, Northanger Abbey touches upon the idea of female empowerment and independence. As Catherine navigates her way through various relationships and experiences, she begins to assert her own agency and develop a sense of self-worth that is not solely defined by her social standing.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both humorous and poignant. Through its thoughtful portrayal of complex themes, Northanger Abbey offers a rich and engaging commentary on the societal norms and expectations that shape our lives.

overview: When Travis, the mouthy son of a criminal, disappears in the Amazon in search of a treasured artifact, his father sends in Beck, who becomes Travis's rival for the affections of Mariana, a mysterious Brazilian woman. With his steely disposition, Beck is a man of few words -- but it takes him all the discipline he can muster to work with Travis to nab a tyrant who's after the same treasure.
tagline: Bulls, guns, whips, gold and one sacred cat
title: The Rundown
plot:
The Rundown is a 2003 action comedy film directed by Peter Howitt and starring Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, Seann William Scott, and Christopher Walken.

The movie begins with Beck (Seann William Scott), a young and ambitious journalist who lands an interview with the infamous mercenary, Beck Owen (Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson). However, during the interview, Beck is kidnapped by Owen's employer, Verona (Rosario Dawson), and taken to the jungle. Owen rescues Beck, but not before she reveals that he has a long-lost brother, Wade (John Billingsley), who is also being held captive.

Owen agrees to rescue Wade in exchange for his freedom, and they set off on a perilous journey through the jungle. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and Owen's rival mercenaries. As they navigate the jungle, Owen and Beck develop a close bond, and Beck begins to see Owen as more than just a mercenary.

As they near Wade's location, Owen and Beck discover that Verona has ulterior motives for keeping Wade captive. She plans to use him as leverage to get revenge on Owen, who she believes wronged her in the past. Owen and Beck must fight their way through Verona's henchmen to reach Wade before it's too late.

The action-packed climax features an intense showdown between Owen and Verona's mercenaries. In the end, Owen emerges victorious, but not without some unexpected surprises. As Owen and Beck part ways, they share a romantic moment, leaving the audience wondering if their relationship might be more than just a coincidence.

Throughout the movie, The Rock Johnson delivers his signature charm and charisma, making Owen a lovable and relatable protagonist. Seann William Scott provides comedic relief as the bumbling but endearing Beck, while Christopher Walken brings his signature gravitas to the role of Verona's ruthless leader.

Overall, The Rundown is an action-packed adventure with plenty of humor and heart. While it may not be a critically acclaimed film, it has become a cult classic among fans of 80s and 90s action movies.

overview: Noreno, a half-Roman, is entrusted with the mission of crossing the snowy mountains of Armenia, swarming with Parthian patrols, to seek help for his slowly dying men.
title: The Legion
plot:
The Legion is a 2020 Spanish-American historical action adventure film and the directorial debut of the veteran Spanish producer José Magán, from a screenplay by Pedro Santamaria and Carmen Ballesteros. Inspired by the war between Rome and the Parthian Empire over Armenia in the years 58 to 63 AD, it stars Lee Partridge as Noreno, a half-Roman soldier, with Mickey Rourke as General Corbulo, Bai Ling as Amirah, Joaquim de Almeida as General Paetus and Vladimir Kulich as Marcus.

Opening titles set the story in Syria in 62 AD. Two Roman legions have become trapped in the snowy mountains of Armenia during the campaign against Parthia; surrounded by enemy patrols, the soldiers are slowly dying of cold and hunger. The main Roman army in Syria is still two weeks away on foot, and the passes between are infested with hostile forces. Noreno is chosen for a perilous mission across the frozen mountains, carrying an urgent message on which the fate of his besieged comrades depends, because he is an expert runner, even though he deeply resents Rome and everything its empire stands for. Meanwhile, Corbulo frets over the crisis in front of a bust of the Emperor Nero, and Amirah, in a single scene, urges him to accept martyrdom.

Noreno, who also narrates the film, sets off alone and spends much of his journey running through the wintry landscape, periodically stopping to fight Parthian soldiers who cross his path. Along the way he faces harsh weather and his own inner conflicts, rescues a young woman from being raped, is briefly captured by a bounty hunter, and is saved by an older man, an early Christian, with whom he has a long philosophical discussion. By the end of the mission the trek has become a journey of personal growth for Noreno, who finds that he has felt free for the first time.

Produced by Magol Films, Carbara Films and Equo Entertainment, the film was released in the United States by Saban Films on May 8, 2020, on video on demand and digital platforms. Reviews were negative. Tara McNamara of Common Sense Media gave it one star out of five. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter compared its premise to 1917, noted that the billed stars Rourke and Bai Ling have only brief roles, found the repeated running scenes monotonous, and wrote that Magán showed no flair for action, partly owing to budget limits, nor for drama, singling out an anguished monologue by Rourke that nearly erased memories of his work in Diner and The Wrestler.

overview: On Anna's birthday, Elsa and Kristoff are determined to give her the best celebration ever, but Elsa's icy powers may put more than just the party at risk.
title: Frozen Fever
plot:
Frozen Fever is a 2015 animated short film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. It serves as a sequel to the 2013 film Frozen and was released on February 13, 2015.

The story begins with Anna (voiced by Kristen Bell) waking up on her birthday, only to find that she has come down with a bad cold. She is worried because she had planned a big celebration for Elsa's (Idina Menzel) coronation as the queen of Arendelle. However, Elsa's powers are still unpredictable and Anna fears that Elsa might accidentally plunge the kingdom into eternal winter.

Anna decides to take matters into her own hands and sets out on a mission to find Elsa, who has gone into seclusion after her coronation. Along the way, she meets Olaf (Josh Gad), who is excited about Anna's birthday and wants to help her celebrate. However, his enthusiasm is short-lived as he soon falls ill with a cold of his own.

As Anna searches for Elsa, she encounters various obstacles, including a group of snowmen who are trying to take over the kingdom. She also meets Kristoff (Jonathan Groff) and Sven, his reindeer companion, who offer their assistance in finding Elsa.

Meanwhile, Elsa is struggling with her powers, which are becoming increasingly difficult to control. She becomes convinced that she is the cause of Anna's illness and feels guilty for putting her sister in harm's way.

In the end, Anna finds Elsa and convinces her to come out of seclusion. With Elsa's help, they work together to create a magical snowflake that will cure Anna's cold and bring warmth back to Arendelle. The film ends with Anna and Elsa celebrating Anna's birthday in style, surrounded by their friends and family.

Frozen Fever is a heartwarming and humorous short film that explores the themes of sisterly love, friendship, and the importance of embracing one's unique qualities. The film features stunning animation, catchy music, and lovable characters that will delight audiences of all ages.

overview: Join Barbie “Brooklyn” Roberts, Barbie “Malibu” Roberts, and her sisters Skipper, Stacie, and Chelsea on an underwater adventure as they transform into mermaids to help save the world of Pacifica! In Barbie Mermaid Power™, Barbie and Barbie are summoned by Isla (from Dolphin Magic) to compete to be the underwater Power Keeper in a series of challenges designed to find their inner powers. Through these competitions, they discover whether they are mermaids of Earth, Air, Water, or Fire, all while making new animal and mermaid friends. In this fish-tale of friendship, adventure, and bravery, Barbie, Barbie, and family experience first-hand what it’s like to balance the worlds above and below the sea and learn a lesson in finding their inner powers along the way.
tagline: Join Brooklyn Barbie and Malibu Barbie on an underwater adventure.
title: Barbie: Mermaid Power
plot:
Barbie: Mermaid Power is a 2022 computer-animated musical adventure for children, directed by Ron Myrick and written by Ann Austen, and the fortieth entry in the Barbie film series. America Young voices Barbie "Malibu" Roberts and Tatiana Varria her friend Barbie "Brooklyn" Roberts, with Kirsten Day, Cassandra Lee Morris and Natalie Lashkari as Malibu's sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea, Madelyn Kratzer as the young mermaid Aquaryah, Vivian Lu as Isla, Melanie Minichino as Marlo and Johnny Yong Bosch as Finn. It debuted on Australian television in August 2022, reached Netflix worldwide on 1 September and later played in cinemas in Britain, Ireland and parts of Europe and the Middle East.

The two Barbies and Malibu's sisters are cleaning trash from the ocean when Malibu's mermaid friend Isla, from Barbie: Dolphin Magic, summons them to the undersea kingdom of Pacifica. Using the magic pearl necklace Isla once gave Malibu, they all become mermaids, a first for Brooklyn, who must accept that the legends are real. It is time for the Ceremony of the Mermaid Moon, held once every hundred years, when chosen mermaids learn to wield the powers of earth, air, water and fire and compete to see who will become the Power Keeper, able to command all four. Some contestants, led by the haughty Talleigha and Sareena, resent the "land dwellers," and they also bully Aquaryah, a spirited girl born without a working tail fin who swims with one her father made. Chelsea quickly befriends her.

On land, the self-styled marine biologist Marlo, who has lost her funding, is determined to prove mermaids exist and sets out to capture evidence during the Mermaid Moon, at one point netting Chelsea and Aquaryah, who escape. Meanwhile a vast floating island of garbage threatens Pacifica. When Marlo's vessel floods, Malibu shares her magic to save them both, turning Marlo into a mermaid; Marlo in turn helps awaken Malibu's water power. As the merfolk fail to clear the trash, Malibu declares that the brave and kind Aquaryah should be the Power Keeper, and with everyone's powers channeled through her, Aquaryah wipes out the trash island.

Common Sense Media called it a sweet musical promoting friendship and acceptance and praised its diverse cast and disability representation, though another reviewer found the story predictable and slow.

overview: An imperial guard searches for the truth behind a conspiracy that framed him and his partners. The proof of his innocence lies with a wanted woman named Bei Zhai... but will she reveal what she knows? In this intense prequel to BROTHERHOOD OF BLADES, the only thing he can truly trust is his sword.
production_companies: 东阳坏猴子影视文化传播有限公司
title: Brotherhood of Blades II: The Infernal Battlefield
plot:
Brotherhood of Blades II: The Infernal Battlefield is a 2017 Chinese martial arts film directed by Tsui Hark. The movie is set in the Qing dynasty and follows the story of a group of assassins, led by a young woman named Yu Shu Lien, as they navigate a complex web of loyalty, honor, and betrayal.

At its core, the film explores themes of identity, duty, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The protagonist, Yu Shu Lien, is a complex character who must confront her own moral compass as she navigates the treacherous world of assassins and imperial politics. Throughout the film, Tsui Hark masterfully weaves together elements of Chinese history, mythology, and philosophy to create a rich tapestry of themes that are both timely and timeless.

One of the primary concerns of the film is the tension between personal loyalty and national duty. The characters must navigate a treacherous landscape of intrigue and deception, where allegiances are constantly shifting and the lines between friend and foe are blurred. This tension is reflected in the character of Yu Shu Lien herself, who must balance her own sense of justice with the demands of her position as an imperial assassin.

The film also explores the theme of identity through the character of a young assassin named Xue Wuyan, who is struggling to find his place within the Brotherhood of Blades. As he navigates the complexities of his own morality and the expectations placed upon him by his mentors, Xue Wuyan must confront the darker aspects of his own nature and the true cost of his loyalty.

Ultimately, Brotherhood of Blades II: The Infernal Battlefield is a film about the human condition, with all its attendant complexities and contradictions. Through its richly detailed world-building and complex characters, Tsui Hark creates a movie that is both a thrilling action-adventure and a profound exploration of the human heart.

overview: After the collapse of Earth's ecosystem, Vesper, a 13-year-old girl struggling to survive with her paralyzed Father, meets a mysterious Woman with a secret that forces Vesper to use her wits, strength and bio-hacking abilities to fight for the possibility of a future.
tagline: One seed can change everything.
title: Vesper
plot:
Vesper, released in France as Vesper Chronicles, is a 2022 science fiction film directed and written by Kristina Buožytė and Bruno Samper. Raffiella Chapman stars as Vesper, with Eddie Marsan as her uncle Jonas, Rosy McEwen as Camellia and Richard Brake as her father Darius.

Humanity's gamble on genetic engineering to avert ecological collapse has failed, and escaped organisms have destroyed edible plants, animals and much of humanity. A wealthy elite lives in sealed cities called citadels, while everyone else scrapes by outside, dependent on citadel seeds designed to produce only a single harvest. Fourteen-year-old Vesper, a gifted biohacker, lives in a forest house with Darius, who is paralyzed and follows her everywhere through a floating drone. Her mother left a year earlier to join the wandering scavengers known as the Pilgrims. Nearby, Darius's brother Jonas runs a camp where he sells children's blood to the citadel and uses engineered slaves called Jugs.

When a citadel ship crashes nearby, Vesper rescues a young woman, Camellia, who promises to take her and her father to the citadel if they can find her companion Elias. Jonas finds Elias first and kills him. Vesper realizes that Camellia, who grieves deeply for Elias, is not human: she is an advanced, sentient Jug created by Elias, a forbidden creation, which is why they fled. Working with seeds stolen from Jonas and samples from Camellia, Vesper discovers a way to unlock the citadel seeds so they can reproduce. After the two women overpower Jonas, he betrays Camellia to the citadel and is killed by its soldiers. Darius sacrifices himself to hold off the soldiers, and Camellia surrenders so that Vesper can escape with the seeds. Vesper buries some of them at her ruined home, takes in four of Jonas's children and heads south. At the top of a tower built by the Pilgrims, she looks out over the forest and scatters the remaining seeds to the wind.

The directors, who made Vanishing Waves (2012), spent six years on the film and shot it in English. Shot around Vilnius, Lithuania, it used no green screen, and cinematographer Feliksas Abrukauskas drew on the light in Vermeer and Rembrandt paintings. Vesper premiered at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival on July 2, 2022, and opened in France on August 18. Reviews were positive; Rotten Tomatoes said that, though more visually impressive than narratively engaging, it rewards patient viewers with immersive world-building and intelligent ideas.

overview: An investigation of how Hollywood's fabled stories have deeply influenced how Americans feel about transgender people, and how transgender people have been taught to feel about themselves.
tagline: Trans lives on screen
title: Disclosure
plot:
Disclosure, originally subtitled Trans Lives on Screen, is a 2020 American documentary directed by Sam Feder, who produced it with Amy Scholder. It examines how Hollywood film and television have depicted transgender people and how those depictions have shaped both trans people's understanding of themselves and the wider public's view of them. Laverne Cox served as an executive producer and is one of the central interviewees.

Every person interviewed in the film is transgender. Alongside Cox, the participants include Jen Richards, Susan Stryker, Alexandra Billings, Jamie Clayton, Chaz Bono, Yance Ford, Trace Lysette, Mj Rodriguez, Angelica Ross, Candis Cayne, Lilly Wachowski and Leo Sheng. Combining their testimony with hundreds of clips, the documentary traces gender-nonconforming characters back to silent films such as D. W. Griffith's Judith of Bethulia and follows them up to series such as Pose. It notes that, according to GLAAD, most Americans say they do not personally know a trans person, so their ideas come largely from the media. The interviewees discuss recurring patterns: trans characters played for laughs in sitcoms and cross-dressing comedies such as Tootsie; trans women cast as psychopathic killers in Psycho, Dressed to Kill and The Silence of the Lambs; scenes of characters vomiting on discovering a trans person's body, as in The Crying Game and Ace Ventura: Pet Detective; and the trope of the shocking "disclosure" that frames trans people as deceivers. They also criticize the casting of cisgender male stars as trans women, the scarcity of trans men on screen, the frequent casting of trans women as sex workers or murder victims, and the erasure of Black trans people. The film contrasts these images with portrayals the participants found affirming, from Yentl to Bugs Bunny, and with the recent rise of trans actors in shows such as Orange Is the New Black, Sense8 and Pose, while stressing that visibility alone has not ended discrimination.

Feder, inspired by The Celluloid Closet, compiled hundreds of film and television titles with Cox's input, and editor Stacy Goldate shaped the material thematically rather than chronologically. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020 and was released on Netflix on June 19, 2020. It was acclaimed by critics in outlets including Variety, the Los Angeles Times and Sight and Sound, holds a 98% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and won the GLAAD Media Award for Outstanding Documentary.

original_title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
overview: A teenager finds himself transported to an island where he must help protect a group of orphans with special powers from creatures intent on destroying them.
tagline: Stay peculiar.
title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
plot:
Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children is a 2016 American fantasy adventure film directed by Tim Burton, based on the 2011 novel of the same name by Ransom Riggs. The movie stars Asa Butterfield, Eva Green, and Terence Stamp.

The story begins with Jake Portman (Asa Butterfield), an orphan who lives with his cruel and neglectful foster parents, Mr. and Mrs. Bugg. On his 16th birthday, Jake receives a letter from a lawyer's office informing him that he is the sole beneficiary of a mysterious inheritance: a large sum of money and a peculiar mansion in Wales.

Jake travels to Wales, where he discovers the mansion, which turns out to be the home of Miss Peregrine (Eva Green), a mysterious and enigmatic caretaker. She reveals to Jake that his grandfather, Abraham Portman, was a famous photographer who discovered a magical island called Cairnholm Island, where children with extraordinary abilities, known as "peculiarities," live.

Miss Peregrine explains that these children are being hunted by monstrous creatures known as the Hollows, which feed on human flesh. The peculiarity Jake possesses is his ability to see and communicate with the dead. He also discovers that he has a special connection to his grandfather's past and the mysterious island.

As Jake spends more time at the mansion, he learns about the history of the peculiaries and their struggles against the Hollows. He also meets other peculiar children, including Emma Bloom (Maddie Harris), a fire-starting girl; Olive Llewellyn (Lora Akinley), a shape-shifting boy; and Horace Burroughs (Samson Kayo), a boy with superhuman strength.

However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Jake discovers that the Hollows are closing in on the island. He also learns that his grandfather's death was not an accident but a deliberate act to protect him from the Hollows.

As the story unfolds, Jake and Miss Peregrine embark on a perilous journey to Cairnholm Island, where they must confront the monstrous creatures and uncover the secrets of the peculiaries' past. Along the way, Jake discovers more about his grandfather's life and the mysterious island, which holds many secrets and surprises.

The movie culminates in an action-packed sequence as Jake and Miss Peregrine face off against the Hollows on the island. In a thrilling finale, Jake uses his newfound understanding of the peculiaries' abilities to defeat the monsters and save the children.

In the end, Jake returns home with a newfound appreciation for his grandfather's legacy and the peculiar children who have become like family to him. The movie concludes with Jake reflecting on the lessons he has learned about acceptance, love, and the power of being different.

Overall, Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children is a visually stunning and imaginative film that explores themes of identity, community, and self-acceptance. With its unique blend of fantasy and adventure, it has become a beloved classic among fans of Tim Burton's films.

overview: Thirty years after defeating the Galactic Empire, Han Solo and his allies face a new threat from the evil Kylo Ren and his army of Stormtroopers.
tagline: Every generation has a story.
title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
plot:
Star Wars: The Force Awakens is a 2015 science fiction film directed by J.J. Abrams, written by Abrams and Lawrence Kasdan, and produced by Lucasfilm Ltd.

The film takes place thirty years after the events of Return of the Jedi (1983). In a galaxy far, far away...

The story begins on the planet Jakku, where we meet our protagonist, Rey (Daisy Ridley), a scavenger who lives in a desert wasteland. She discovers a droid, BB-8, which contains a map that leads to the location of Luke Skywalker's (Mark Hamill) missing lightsaber.

Rey is pursued by the First Order, a new evil force risen from the ashes of the Empire, led by Kylo Ren (Adam Driver), a dark warrior with a personal connection to Rey. The First Order is searching for Luke, who has gone into exile after the fall of the Empire.

Meanwhile, we are introduced to Finn (John Boyega), a former Stormtrooper who defects from the First Order and joins the Resistance, led by General Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher). Finn becomes embroiled in the search for Luke, who is believed to be hiding on Jakku.

As Rey navigates her way through the desert, she encounters Han Solo (Harrison Ford), a smuggler with a heart of gold, and his co-pilot Chewbacca. Together, they help Rey find Luke's lightsaber, which becomes a crucial piece in the battle against the First Order.

The film's plot thickens as Kylo Ren, who is struggling with his own identity and loyalties, confronts Han Solo, leading to a thrilling space battle between the Resistance and the First Order. The battle culminates in the destruction of the Starkiller Base, a planet-sized weapon that can destroy entire star systems.

As the story unfolds, we learn more about Rey's past and her connection to Kylo Ren, who is revealed to be Ben Solo, the son of Han and Leia. The film's climax features an epic confrontation between Rey and Kylo Ren, which ultimately leads to a dramatic showdown with Luke Skywalker.

In the end, Rey discovers that she has a strong connection to the Force, which makes her a powerful Jedi in her own right. With the help of Finn, Han, and Chewbacca, Rey defeats Kylo Ren and helps bring balance to the Force.

The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as the Resistance is reinvigorated and a new generation of heroes emerges. The stage is set for the next installment in the Star Wars saga, as we await the adventures of Rey, Finn, and their allies in the fight against the First Order.

Overall, Star Wars: The Force Awakens is an exciting and action-packed film that pays homage to the original trilogy while introducing new characters and storylines. It sets the stage for a thrilling sequel series, which has captivated audiences worldwide.

overview: While working a job at an exclusive ski resort to support her Dad, Kim learns to snowboard and is so good at it that she enters a competition with a huge cash prize. She has to dig deep to overcome her fears, but her life gets more complicated through her spoken-for boss, Jonny.
tagline: How to marry a billionaire.
title: Chalet Girl
plot:
Chalet Girl is a 2011 British romantic comedy-drama film that explores the theme of self-discovery and empowerment through the lens of a young woman's journey to find her place in the world. The movie follows the story of Kim Matthews, a teenager from a troubled home who finds solace and confidence while working as a ski instructor at a chalet resort.

As Kim navigates her relationships with her colleagues and clients, she begins to shed her insecurities and assert herself, discovering a sense of purpose and belonging. Through her experiences, the film highlights the importance of female friendship, support, and camaraderie in helping women overcome their personal struggles and find their voice.

The movie also touches on themes of class and social status, as Kim's working-class background is contrasted with the more affluent clientele she encounters at the chalet resort. This dichotomy serves to underscore the film's exploration of identity, class, and privilege, raising questions about how these factors shape our experiences and relationships.

Ultimately, Chalet Girl is a heartwarming and uplifting film that celebrates the power of female friendship, self-discovery, and personal growth, offering a relatable and inspiring portrayal of a young woman's journey towards empowerment and independence.

overview: A young boy wanders Eastern Europe during World War II.
tagline: Light is visible only in the dark
title: The Painted Bird
plot:
The Painted Bird (Nabarvené ptáče) is a 2019 Czech war drama written, directed and produced by Václav Marhoul. It adapts Jerzy Kosiński's novel of the same name. Petr Kotlár plays the boy, with a supporting cast including Udo Kier, Stellan Skarsgård, Harvey Keitel, Julian Sands and Barry Pepper. It is the first film to use the constructed Interslavic language. Marhoul chose it so that no Slavic nation would be identified with the brutal villagers.

During the Second World War, somewhere in German-occupied Eastern Europe, a young Jewish boy has been left in the care of his elderly aunt. When she dies, he accidentally burns down her house and sets out alone. His journey becomes a series of horrific encounters with superstition, cruelty and abuse. An old healer buys him, but villagers blame him for bad luck and throw him into a river. A miller gouges out the eyes of a young man he suspects of desiring his wife. A kindly bird catcher, Lekh, hangs himself after village women brutally attack his lover. Handed to the Germans, the boy is spared by the soldier ordered to shoot him and later escapes execution again. A priest takes him in but places him with Garbos, who sexually abuses him, and the boy causes Garbos's death. He is driven out after the priest dies and is then sexually exploited by a widow, Labina, before fleeing.

When the Red Army arrives, a Soviet sniper, Mitka, briefly looks after him, and the boy watches him kill villagers in revenge for an attack on Soviet soldiers. Sent to an orphanage, the now-mute boy keeps trying to run away and kills a shopkeeper who beat him. Finally, a man named Nikodém arrives and tearfully claims him as his son. On the bus home, the boy notices a number tattooed on his father's arm and, with his finger, writes his name, Joska, on the misted window.

Marhoul secured the rights in 2012. Shooting took place over 16 months between 2017 and 2018 in Ukraine, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, with Vladimír Smutný as cinematographer. The film competed at the 76th Venice International Film Festival, where some viewers walked out over its violence, but it also received long ovations, and it later played at Toronto and London. It was the Czech submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film and made the shortlist. It won nine Czech Lions, including Best Film. The Guardian gave it five stars, calling it a savage three-hour tour of hell.

original_title: 名探偵コナン 天空の難破船（ロスト・シップ）
overview: A terrorist group invades a laboratory containing a deadly bacteria and destroys the lab with an explosion. They later announce via the internet they have gained possession of the bacteria and declare themselves to be the Red Siamese Cats, a terrorist group that was eradicated a decade ago.
title: Detective Conan: The Lost Ship in the Sky
plot:
Detective Conan: The Lost Ship in the Sky is an animated mystery film that revolves around Shinichi Kudo's adventures with his alter ego, Conan Edogawa. The movie delves into themes of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The story explores the idea of identity through Shinichi's dual existence as both Conan and Shinichi. This dichotomy raises questions about the nature of self and how our identities are shaped by our experiences and relationships. As Conan navigates his way through a complex web of clues and conspiracies, he must also confront the consequences of his own identity and the impact it has on those around him.

The film also touches on the theme of loyalty, particularly in the context of Shinichi's relationships with his friends and allies. His bond with Ran Mori, in particular, is put to the test as he struggles to reconcile his dual identities and protect those he cares about.

Furthermore, the movie explores the idea of reality vs. fantasy, as Conan navigates a world where nothing seems quite as it appears. The film's use of clever plot twists and red herrings keeps the audience guessing, mirroring Conan's own efforts to uncover the truth behind a mysterious ship that has been lost at sea.

Overall, Detective Conan: The Lost Ship in the Sky is a thought-provoking mystery that delves into complex themes and ideas, keeping viewers engaged and invested in the story until its satisfying conclusion.

overview: As a collection of history's worst tyrants and criminal masterminds gather to plot a war to wipe out millions, one man must race against time to stop them.
tagline: Witness the bloody origin.
title: The King's Man
plot:
The King's Man is a 2021 spy action film directed by Matthew Vaughn, produced by Marv Films, and written by Karl Gajdusek. The movie serves as a prequel to the Kingsman franchise.

The story takes place during World War I and follows the early life of Orlando Oxford (Harris Dickinson), a young man from a wealthy family who is struggling to find his place in society. After his mother's death, Orlando discovers that he has inherited a vast fortune and becomes embroiled in a world of espionage and intrigue.

Orlando meets Phoenix (Ralph Fiennes), the Duke of Oxford, who recognizes his potential as a spy and begins training him in the art of espionage. As Orlando navigates this new world, he befriends a group of young spies, including Conrad Oxford (Rhys Ifans) and Charlotte (Hannah Rae).

The story takes a dark turn when Orlando discovers that his family's business is secretly funding the war effort, and that they are involved in a plot to assassinate Kaiser Wilhelm II. As Orlando delves deeper into the conspiracy, he must confront his own demons and make difficult choices to protect himself and those he cares about.

Throughout the film, Vaughn pays homage to the original Kingsman franchise while introducing new characters and themes. The movie features a blend of action, humor, and style, with a nod to classic spy films from the 1960s and 1970s.

One of the standout aspects of The King's Man is its exploration of the complexities of class and privilege in the early 20th century. Orlando's journey from an outsider to a member of the aristocracy serves as a commentary on the social hierarchies of the time, while also highlighting the moral ambiguities of those who wield power.

Overall, The King's Man is a thrilling and entertaining film that expands the Kingsman universe in exciting ways. With its stylish visuals, witty dialogue, and strong performances, it is a must-see for fans of the franchise and action-adventure movies in general.

original_title: ブレードランナー ブラックアウト 2022
overview: This animated short revolves around the events causing an electrical systems failure on the west coast of the US. According to Blade Runner 2049’s official timeline, this failure leads to cities shutting down, financial and trade markets being thrown into chaos, and food supplies dwindling. There’s no proof as to what caused the blackouts, but Replicants — the bio-engineered robots featured in the original Blade Runner, are blamed.
title: Blade Runner: Black Out 2022
plot:
Blade Runner Black Out 2022 (Japanese: Burēdoran'nā Burakkuauto 2022) is a 2017 Japanese cyberpunk tech-noir anime short film directed by Shinichiro Watanabe and animated by CygamesPictures. It is one of three short films, together with 2036: Nexus Dawn and 2048: Nowhere to Run, made as prequels to the live-action feature Blade Runner 2049, and it bridges the years between the original Blade Runner and its sequel. The voice cast includes Jovan Jackson as Iggy Cygnus, Luci Christian as Trixie, Bryson Baugus as Ren and Edward James Olmos, who returns as Gaff. The short debuted on Crunchyroll on 27 September 2017.

Three years after the events of Blade Runner, the Tyrell Corporation has introduced a new line of replicants, the Nexus-8, whose lifespans are open-ended like those of humans, and growing tension between people and replicants leads to unrest. When a replicant named Trixie is attacked by a gang of human thugs, she is rescued by Iggy, a replicant soldier who deserted after discovering that the enemy he was fighting were replicants too. Iggy recruits Trixie into an underground replicant freedom movement whose goal is to wipe out the Tyrell Corporation's database and tracking records so that replicants can no longer be easily identified and hunted. Trixie befriends Ren, a sympathetic human technician who is in charge of launching nuclear missiles, and he agrees to redirect a test missile so that it detonates over Los Angeles, where its electromagnetic pulse will plunge the city into darkness and erase electronic data. While the missile is on its way, Trixie and Iggy set out to physically destroy the Tyrell servers themselves, a mission that comes at a heavy cost. The resulting blackout triggers a global collapse in which replicant production is halted and Tyrell goes bankrupt, paving the way for the Wallace Corporation to take over the company and revive replicant manufacturing a decade later, setting the stage for the world of Blade Runner 2049.

The short was well received by viewers, earning user ratings of 7.3 on IMDb and 4.4 out of 5 on Crunchyroll. Writing for Forbes, Ollie Barder praised it as "expertly done", wishing there had been more of it, and noted that it combines elements of Watanabe's Cowboy Bebop with some of the bleakness of the anime Armor Hunter Mellowlink, on which Watanabe also worked.

overview: Jackie Moon is the owner, promoter, coach, and star player of the Flint Michigan Tropics of the American Basketball Association (ABA). In 1976 before the ABA collapses, the National Basketball Association (NBA) plans to merge with the best teams of the ABA at the end of the season. Only the top four teams will make the move and the worst teams will fold. The Tropics are the worst team in the league and if they want to make it to the NBA, Jackie Moon must rally his team and start winning. The only problem is the fact that Jackie Moon is not really the coach and star basketball player he thinks he is. To keep his team from oblivion and leave his mark in the city, Jackie Moon must inspire his team to win fourth place in the playoffs.
tagline: Putting the funk into the dunk.
title: Semi-Pro
plot:
Semi-Pro is a sports comedy film that explores the themes of perseverance, teamwork, and redemption. The movie follows the story of Jackie Moon, a former basketball player who becomes the coach of the American Basketball Association's (ABA) Flint Tropics.

At its core, Semi-Pro is a film about finding one's purpose in life and making amends for past mistakes. Jackie Moon, played by Will Ferrell, is a complex character who has never quite found his place in the world. He's a wannabe entrepreneur, a failed musician, and an unfulfilled athlete, all rolled into one. When he gets the chance to coach the Tropics, he sees it as an opportunity to redeem himself and prove that he still has what it takes.

Throughout the film, Moon's character is driven by a desire to prove himself and earn the respect of his players. He's a demanding coach who pushes his team to be their best, but he also shows a softer side when it comes to his players' personal struggles. As the season progresses, Moon becomes more than just a coach - he becomes a mentor and a father figure to his players.

The film also explores the theme of redemption through the character of Norman Dale, played by Woody Harrelson. Dale is a former college basketball coach who has lost his way in life after a scandalous incident. He's hired as the Tropics' coach, but he struggles to connect with his players and find his footing on the court.

As the season progresses, both Moon and Dale learn valuable lessons about leadership, teamwork, and the importance of following your heart. The film culminates in an exciting championship game that showcases the team's growth and development throughout the season.

Overall, Semi-Pro is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of perseverance, redemption, and the power of sports to bring people together.

overview: A young NASA JPL scientist is abducted by extraterrestrials but when no one believes his story he becomes obsessed with finding proof which leads him on a journey of discovery.
tagline: They have arrived.
title: Proximity
plot:
Proximity is a 2020 American science fiction drama film written and directed by Eric Demeusy in his directorial debut. It stars Ryan Masson as Isaac, Highdee Kuan as Sara, Christian Prentice as Zed, Shaw Jones as Agent Graves and Don Scribner as Carl. The film was released on demand on May 15, 2020.

In 1979, Carl, a lumberjack working in Alaska, is abducted by aliens. In the present day, Isaac, a young computer engineer who has started keeping a video diary, goes hiking in the woods and encounters a flying saucer and an alien. He wakes up three days later by the water and begins suffering hallucinations, and a doctor finds that one of his bones has been broken with a strangely precise cut. Because his camera recorded the abduction, Isaac uploads the footage to the internet, where it goes viral, drawing questions from the news media and the government. Convinced that signs of alien life have been left throughout history, Isaac finds an online post by Sara, a young woman with a similar story, and the two meet at a diner. After Isaac passes a lie detector test, the pair are seized by a group of men in black led by Agent Graves, who discover that both of them carry alien tracking devices in their arms. Refusing to cooperate, Isaac escapes with Sara, pursued by androids, and they realize they have been taken to Costa Rica.
