Suspecting that Cheol-ryung is really seeking revenge, South Korean officials assign the Seoul detective Jin-tae to watch him closely.

The two meet at the airport and set off after one of Ki-seong's associates, Park Myung-ho, but Cheol-ryung slips away after discovering Jin-tae's assignment. Ordered to keep him under surveillance, Jin-tae brings him home to stay with his family, while Cheol-ryung removes the tracking SIM card Jin-tae has planted in his phone and secretly bugs Jin-tae's phone instead. Tracing Park to a restaurant, they find him meeting one of Ki-seong's accomplices, who kills Park for planning to settle in the South. Learning of Cheol-ryung's past, Jin-tae resolves to help him. At a meeting where Ki-seong plans to sell the plates, Ki-seong kills the buyer, and when Cheol-ryung is about to shoot him, Jin-tae intervenes, allowing Ki-seong to flee while Cheol-ryung secures the plates. Ki-seong retaliates by kidnapping Jin-tae's family and demanding the plates. Cheol-ryung brings them to the exchange, Jin-tae gets his family to safety, and the two men kill Ki-seong in the ensuing battle. A year later, they are given a new joint mission.

Confidential Assignment opened in second place in South Korea on January 18, 2017, and rose to first in its second week. It drew 7.8 million admissions, the most for a Korean film in the first half of 2017, and was sold to 42 territories. A sequel, Confidential Assignment 2: International, was released in 2022.

overview: In a future society in the era of indefinite eugenics, humans are set on a life course depending on their DNA. Young Vincent Freeman is born with a condition that would prevent him from space travel, yet is determined to infiltrate the GATTACA space program.
tagline: There is no gene for the human spirit.
title: Gattaca
plot:
Gattaca is a thought-provoking science fiction film directed by Andrew Niccol, released in 1997 by Columbia Pictures. The movie takes place in a future where genetic engineering has become a dominant force in society.

The story begins with Vincent Freeman (played by Ethan Hawke), an "invalid" who was born naturally without any genetic enhancements. In this world, people can choose to enhance their genes to achieve perfection, and those who do are considered superior. The main character's father, Maurice (played by James Cromwell), is a former test pilot who died in a tragic accident.

Vincent dreams of becoming an astronaut, but his "invalid" status makes it impossible for him to join the prestigious Gattaca Corporation's space program. He decides to impersonate a genetically perfect individual named Eugene Morrow (played by Jude Law) and applies for a job at Gattaca. Vincent uses advanced technology to create a fake identity and genetic profile, which he hopes will fool the corporation's sophisticated DNA testing system.

As Vincent navigates his new life as Eugene, he meets Irene Cassini (played by Uma Thurman), a beautiful and intelligent woman who is also an employee of Gattaca. The two begin a romantic relationship, but their love is threatened when Vincent's true identity is discovered by the corporation's security team.

Meanwhile, the story unfolds through a series of flashbacks, which reveal the tragic events that led to Maurice's death. It is revealed that he was involved in a conspiracy to sabotage the space program and prevent genetically enhanced individuals from taking over. The truth behind his death is slowly uncovered throughout the film, adding depth to Vincent's character.

As the story progresses, Vincent becomes embroiled in a complex web of intrigue and deception. He must confront the consequences of his actions and decide whether to continue living as Eugene or reveal his true identity. In the end, Vincent chooses to come clean about his past, but not before he has a profound impact on Irene's life.

The film explores themes of identity, free will, and what it means to be human in a world where genetic engineering has become the norm. The title "Gattaca" refers to the corporation's motto, which reads: "Genetic testing is mandatory." Throughout the movie, Vincent struggles with the idea that his existence is defined by his genetic code, rather than his own choices and actions.

Ultimately, Gattaca is a thought-provoking commentary on the consequences of playing God with human genetics. The film raises important questions about the ethics of genetic engineering and the importance of individual freedom in a world where technology seems to be controlling every aspect of our lives.

overview: A sorority moves in next door to the home of Mac and Kelly Radner who have a young child. The Radner's enlist their former nemeses from the fraternity to help battle the raucous sisters.
tagline: New neighbors.
title: Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising
plot:
Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising (titled Bad Neighbours 2 in some markets) is an American comedy of 2016 from director Nicholas Stoller, who wrote it with Andrew J. Cohen, Brendan O'Brien, Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg. Following Neighbors (2014), it stars Seth Rogen and Rose Byrne as Mac and Kelly Radner, Zac Efron as Teddy Sanders and Chloë Grace Moretz as Shelby, with Dave Franco, Ike Barinholtz, Kiersey Clemons and Beanie Feldstein.

Expecting their second child, Mac and Kelly agree to sell their house to the Baier family, but the deal is in escrow for thirty days. Meanwhile, the college freshmen Shelby, Beth and Nora, appalled by sexist fraternity parties and by a rule barring sororities from hosting their own, found an independent sorority, Kappa Nu. Teddy, from the first film, is adrift: his friends have moved on to careers, while his criminal record keeps him out of decent work, and when his best friend Pete gets engaged to his boyfriend Darren, Pete asks him to move out. Teddy wanders back to his old fraternity house next to the Radners, where he finds the girls hoping to rent it, and offers to teach them how to throw parties to pay the rent.

The Radners ask Shelby to hold off, but she refuses, and appeals to the dean and her father fail. A prank war follows: Mac, Kelly and their friends Jimmy and Paula infest the house with bed bugs, while the girls plan to sell marijuana at a tailgate party. Disgusted by their pranks, Teddy is thrown out of the sorority and joins forces with the Radners, distracting the girls while Mac steals their stash. The sorority hits back by tricking Mac into flying to Australia and ransacking the Radners' house, and the Baiers threaten to back out unless the girls are evicted. Facing eviction, Shelby reluctantly stages a raunchy, fraternity-style party, but after Beth and Nora accuse her of betraying their ideals, Kelly urges the girls not to give up on themselves. They throw a party on their own terms and are flooded with new recruits from other sororities, earning enough to keep the house. The Radners rent their own home to Kappa Nu rather than sell it, Teddy reconciles with Pete and becomes a wedding planner, and both couples welcome their babies.

Neighbors 2 premiered in Berlin on April 26, 2016, and was released by Universal Pictures in the United States on May 20. It grossed $108.8 million worldwide on a $35 million budget and received mostly positive reviews, with 65% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: An entry-level employee at a powerful corporation finds himself occupying a corner office, but at a dangerous price—he must spy on his boss's old mentor to secure for him a multi-billion dollar advantage.
tagline: In a war between kings even a pawn can change the game.
title: Paranoia
plot:
Paranoia is a 2013 American techno-thriller directed by Robert Luketic. Barry L. Levy and Jason Hall wrote the screenplay, loosely based on Joseph Finder's 2004 novel of the same name. Liam Hemsworth stars as Adam Cassidy, with Gary Oldman as Nicholas Wyatt, Amber Heard as Emma Jennings and Harrison Ford as Jock Goddard. Lucas Till, Julian McMahon and Richard Dreyfuss co-star.

Adam is a low-level inventor at Wyatt's company. After he is fired for insubordination, he uses a company credit card to treat his friends at an expensive nightclub. Wyatt and his enforcer, Miles Meachum, then blackmail him: unless he becomes Wyatt's corporate spy, he will be prosecuted for fraud. Coached by Dr. Judith Bolton, Adam is placed inside the company of Goddard, Wyatt's former mentor and bitter rival, who stole some of Wyatt's ideas. He wins Goddard's favor and begins a relationship with Emma, Goddard's marketing director, whom he had met at the club, partly to get access to confidential files. FBI Agent Gamble warns him that three other Wyatt employees who moved to Goddard's company have turned up dead, but Adam ignores him.

The pressure grows when Wyatt threatens Adam's father, Frank, and orders him to steal Occura, Goddard's revolutionary prototype phone. Adam finds cameras in his apartment and destroys them, and Meachum retaliates by running down his friend Kevin with a car. Given 48 hours, Adam uses Emma's fingerprint, lifted from a spoon, to break into the vault, only to be caught by Goddard. Goddard reveals that he knows Adam is Wyatt's spy and plans to use him to take over Wyatt's company, and Emma realizes she has been used. With Kevin's help, Adam turns the tables. At a meeting between the two tycoons, where it emerges that Bolton has been working for Goddard, Adam secretly records both men discussing their crimes and sends the recording to the FBI. Wyatt, Goddard, Bolton and Meachum are arrested. Adam starts a small company in Brooklyn with his friends and reconciles with Emma.

Filming took place in Philadelphia in 2012, and Junkie XL wrote the score. Relativity Media released the film on August 16, 2013. It opened 13th with $3.5 million and grossed just $17.1 million worldwide against a $35 million budget, and Variety listed it among the year's biggest flops. Reviews were very negative: Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it a clichéd, unoriginal techno-thriller with indifferent performances and few thrills.

overview: Chinese narco-cops take their mission to the Golden Triangle following the Mekong River massacre of innocent fishermen by the region's drug lord.
title: Operation Mekong
plot:
Operation Mekong is a 2016 Thai action thriller film directed by Banjong Pisanthanakun. The movie follows the story of a group of Thai and Cambodian fishermen who team up to take down a human trafficking ring that has been operating in the Mekong River.

The main themes of Operation Mekong include:

1. Human Trafficking: The film highlights the issue of human trafficking, particularly in Southeast Asia, where thousands of people are trafficked every year. The movie sheds light on the brutal treatment of victims and the need for action to combat this crime.
2. Corruption: The film also explores the theme of corruption, as the authorities are often complicit in or turn a blind eye to human trafficking. This highlights the need for stronger laws and enforcement to tackle this issue.
3. Friendship and Unity: Despite their differences, the fishermen from both Thailand and Cambodia come together to fight against the traffickers, demonstrating the power of unity and friendship in the face of adversity.
4. Revenge: The protagonist, a Thai fisherman named Pakpao, seeks revenge against the human traffickers who killed his brother, driving the plot forward with a sense of urgency and motivation.

The movie features a mix of action, suspense, and drama, as the characters navigate the treacherous waters of the Mekong River. With its gripping storyline and strong performances, Operation Mekong is a thrilling ride that sheds light on an important social issue.

original_title: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
overview: On a mission to make Christmas unforgettable for Quill, the Guardians head to Earth in search of the perfect present.
tagline: The perfect present is a galaxy away.
title: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
plot:
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special is a 2022 American Christmas special television film directed by Louis Leterrier and written by David Houseer. The story takes place after the events of Avengers: Endgame.

The special follows Peter Quill (Star-Lord), Gamora, Drax, Rocket Raccoon, and Groot as they embark on a mission to find a rare and powerful artifact known as the "Orb". This Orb has the power to grant wishes, but it's also extremely difficult to locate. The Guardians are hired by a wealthy client to retrieve the Orb for him.

However, things take a turn when they discover that the Orb is actually a Christmas-themed gift from an unknown benefactor. As they try to figure out who sent the gift and what their intentions are, they begin to experience strange visions of Christmas past, present, and future.

Throughout the special, we see flashbacks of Peter's childhood on Morag, where he was raised by his mother Yondu (who is also a key character in the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise). We also see glimpses of Gamora's troubled past and her complicated relationship with her father Thanos.

As the story unfolds, the Guardians begin to realize that the true meaning of Christmas is not about material gifts or power, but about family, friendship, and giving. They come together to help each other and find a way to make the most of their holiday season.

The special features many Easter eggs and references to the larger Marvel Cinematic Universe, including cameos from characters like Mantis and Nebula. The story is full of humor, heart, and action, making it a fun and festive addition to the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise.

Overall, The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special is a delightful and entertaining holiday special that explores themes of family, friendship, and the true meaning of Christmas. It's a must-watch for fans of the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise and anyone looking for a fun and festive holiday treat.

overview: When Zoe tires of looking for Mr. Right, she decides to have a baby on her own. But on the day she's artificially inseminated, she meets Stan, who seems to be just who she's been searching for all her life. Now, Zoe has to figure out how to make her two life's dreams fit with each other.
tagline: Fall in love, get married, have a baby. Not necessarily in that order.
title: The Back-Up Plan
plot:
The Back-up Plan, previously known as Plan B, is a 2010 American romantic comedy film directed by Alan Poul in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Kate Angelo. It stars Jennifer Lopez, in her first film in three years, alongside Alex O'Loughlin, Eric Christian Olsen, Anthony Anderson and Linda Lavin, and it was the last film featuring Tom Bosley before his death. Shot in Los Angeles beginning in May 2009, it was released in the United States by CBS Films on April 23, 2010.

Having given up on finding the man of her dreams, Zoe decides to become a single mother and undergoes artificial insemination. That same day she meets Stan when they both try to hail the same taxi, and after running into him twice more, at a farmers market and at a book signing, she agrees to go on a no-strings date with him. Unsure whether she is pregnant, and whether she should tell him, Zoe keeps seeing Stan, enduring a disastrous romantic dinner in a garden before learning that the insemination has worked just as he invites her to spend the weekend at his farm. When she finally tells him the truth, Stan is confused and angry, but he soon decides that he still wants to be with her. A visit to the doctor reveals that Zoe is carrying twins, and the couple must learn to navigate an unusual relationship in which the pregnancy comes before the romance. Stan, overwhelmed, finds a sympathetic friend at a children's playground, while Zoe finds little support from her single mothers' group once its members learn that she is no longer single. As the pregnancy progresses through a series of comic mishaps and misunderstandings, Zoe struggles to trust that Stan is really prepared to raise children who are not biologically his, and a chance encounter with his ex-girlfriend threatens to drive them apart just as the babies' arrival draws near, at the same time as her grandmother prepares for her own wedding.

The Back-up Plan received negative reviews; critics generally praised Lopez's performance but faulted the generic script. On Rotten Tomatoes, 17% of 150 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 34 out of 100. It was nevertheless a commercial success, grossing about $77 million worldwide against a $35 million budget and becoming CBS Films' highest-grossing film at the time.

overview: Royal Air Force pilot Lt. Kate Sinclair is on her final flight mission when her jet is shot down over one of the most dangerous rebel strongholds in Afghanistan. She finds refuge in an abandoned underground bunker where deadly man-made creatures known as Ravagers — half-human, half-alien, and hungry for human flesh — are awakened.
tagline: Unlocked. Unleashed.
title: The Lair
plot:
The Lair is a 2022 British action horror film directed by Neil Marshall, who co-wrote it with Charlotte Kirk. Kirk stars as Royal Air Force pilot Kate Sinclair, alongside Jonathan Howard, Jamie Bamber and Leon Ockenden.

In 2017, Sinclair and her weapons systems officer, Terry Johnson, are shot down over Afghanistan. Insurgents kill Johnson, and Sinclair, with no way to call for help, takes refuge in an abandoned Soviet bunker. Her pursuers follow her inside and accidentally wake clawed humanoid creatures from stasis. The monsters slaughter the insurgents while the wounded Sinclair escapes. U.S. soldiers in a Humvee pick her up and takes her to a small outpost, where she tells Major Roy Finch what she saw. That night, the creatures attack the outpost, kill several soldiers and carry off the bodies, and Finch is knocked unconscious. The survivors wait out the attack in the armory. An older local man, Kabir, remembers that a star fell from the sky just before the Soviet invasion in 1979, and that villagers, including his father, disappeared for years until the Soviets withdrew.

The team examines a creature left behind and finds human organs under its tough hide. When Finch wakes up, he explains what his superiors told him. The Soviets invaded Afghanistan to recover a crashed alien spacecraft and then spliced alien DNA with human subjects at a secret site the Americans were never able to locate. The supposedly dead creature revives, reads Sinclair's mind through tentacles in its head, and Finch kills it with a grenade, sacrificing himself. The survivors return to the bunker to destroy it with explosives, and when a soldier named Hook is dragged underground, Sinclair leads a rescue. The creatures have set a trap, and the military has learned the location and will drop a bunker-buster bomb in 20 minutes. Kabir recognizes his transformed father among the monsters before he dies. Only Sinclair, Hook and Wilks, who stayed on the surface, make it out. They rescue Wilks from insurgents and escape in a stolen vehicle just before the bomb destroys the site. Later, an American black ops team searches the outpost for a specimen but finds nothing.

The Lair received mixed reviews. Variety called it more hectic than scary but praised Marshall's brisk staging of bloody action, and the Los Angeles Times considered it a good genre picture, though not a great one. RogerEbert.com praised its practical creature effects. It grossed about $157,000 worldwide.

overview: Dean and Sal are the portrait of the Beat Generation. Their search for "It" results in a fast paced, energetic roller coaster ride with highs and lows throughout the U.S.
tagline: The best teacher is experience.
title: On the Road
plot:
On the Road is a 2012 film that explores the themes of freedom, nonconformity, and the search for meaning in post-war America. The movie delves into the lives of its characters as they embark on a journey across the country, seeking adventure, love, and connection.

At its core, On the Road is a film about the allure of the open road and the sense of liberation that comes with it. The characters are drawn to the freedom and spontaneity that travel offers, and their journeys become a metaphor for the search for identity and purpose in life. As they move from place to place, they encounter various experiences, people, and landscapes that shape their perspectives and inform their values.

The film also explores the tension between individualism and conformity, as embodied by the characters' desire for independence and nonconformity versus the societal expectations of the time. The characters are drawn to the Beats, a literary and cultural movement that celebrated creativity, spontaneity, and nonconformity, but they also struggle with the constraints of mainstream society.

Furthermore, On the Road touches on the theme of love and relationships in a way that is both intimate and ephemeral. The film's portrayal of romantic relationships is marked by a sense of longing and impermanence, reflecting the characters' desire for connection and community in a world that often seems hostile to their values.

Ultimately, On the Road presents a vision of America as a land of possibility and promise, where individuals can come together to create something new and meaningful. The film's characters are drawn to this vision, but they also grapple with its elusiveness, reflecting the complexities and challenges of finding one's place in the world.

It is worth noting that the movie adaptation took some creative liberties with the original novel by Jack Kerouac, so while it captures the essence of the book, it may not be a direct representation of the author's vision.

overview: During a space voyage, four scientists are altered by cosmic rays: Reed Richards gains the ability to stretch his body; Sue Storm can become invisible; Johnny Storm controls fire; and Ben Grimm is turned into a super-strong … thing. Together, these "Fantastic Four" must now thwart the evil plans of Dr. Doom and save the world from certain destruction.
production_companies: Kumar Mobiliengesellschaft mbH & Co. Projekt Nr. 3 KG
tagline: 4 times the action. 4 times the adventure. 4 times the fantastic.
title: Fantastic Four
plot:
Fantastic Four is a 2005 superhero film based on the Marvel Comics team created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. Directed by Tim Story and written by Mark Frost and Michael France, it stars Ioan Gruffudd as Reed Richards, Jessica Alba as Susan Storm, Chris Evans as Johnny Storm, Michael Chiklis as Ben Grimm and Julian McMahon as Victor von Doom, with Kerry Washington. It tells the origin story of the team, who must learn to live with the extraordinary abilities they gain after being exposed to cosmic rays in space. It was the second live-action Fantastic Four film to be produced, after an unreleased version produced by Roger Corman.

Scientist Reed Richards and his friend Ben Grimm persuade Victor von Doom, the head of Von Doom Industries, to give them access to his space station so that Reed can study the effects of a cosmic energy cloud on living samples. Victor brings along his chief geneticist, Susan Storm, who is Reed's former girlfriend, and her reckless brother Johnny. The cloud arrives ahead of schedule, and while Reed, Susan and Johnny rush to help Ben, who is outside on a spacewalk, Victor seals himself behind the station's shields. The storm strikes them all. Back on Earth, the four develop strange powers: Reed can stretch his body like rubber, Susan can turn invisible and project force fields, Johnny can engulf himself in fire, and Ben is transformed into a massive, rock-skinned creature of tremendous strength. After they use their abilities to avert a disaster on the Brooklyn Bridge, the media dubs them the Fantastic Four. Johnny revels in the fame, but Ben is devastated when his fiancée leaves him, and Reed vows to find a cure. Working from his laboratory in the Baxter Building, Reed tries to build a machine that can reverse the changes, while Victor, ruined by the mission's failure and blaming Reed, discovers that the storm has also changed him, turning his body into living metal able to generate electricity. Calling himself Doom, he sets out to drive the team apart and take his revenge, forcing the four to decide whether they can work together as a family.

The film received generally mixed reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes, 28% of 213 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus faulting its goofy attempts at wit, subpar acting and bland storytelling, and Metacritic gave it a score of 40 out of 100. It was nonetheless a commercial success, grossing $333.5 million worldwide, and was followed by the sequel Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer.

overview: For more than a decade, parents Andy and Vicky have been on the run, desperate to hide their daughter Charlie from a shadowy federal agency that wants to harness her unprecedented gift for creating fire into a weapon of mass destruction. Andy has taught Charlie how to defuse her power, which is triggered by anger or pain. But as Charlie turns 11, the fire becomes harder and harder to control. After an incident reveals the family's location, a mysterious operative is deployed to hunt down the family and seize Charlie once and for all. Charlie has other plans.
tagline: Never play with fire.
title: Firestarter
plot:
Firestarter is a 2022 American science fiction horror thriller film directed by Keith Thomas from a screenplay by Scott Teems. Based on Stephen King's novel and a remake of the 1984 film of the same name, it stars Zac Efron, Ryan Kiera Armstrong, Sydney Lemmon, Kurtwood Smith, Michael Greyeyes and Gloria Reuben, with John Beasley in his final film role. Produced by Jason Blum and Akiva Goldsman through Blumhouse Productions and Weed Road Pictures, it was released by Universal Pictures on May 13, 2022, simultaneously in theaters and on Peacock.

Years ago, Andy McGee and his girlfriend Vicky took part in a clinical trial of an experimental drug called Lot-6, which secretly gave them supernatural abilities: Andy gained a telepathic power of suggestion he calls "the push", while Vicky became telekinetic. Their daughter, Charlie, was born with the even more dangerous gift of pyrokinesis, and her parents struggle to keep the family's secret. Now a young girl, Charlie is struggling to contain powers that grow more unstable whenever she is angry or frightened, and after an outburst at school in which she causes an explosion in a bathroom, her thermal signature is detected by Captain Jane Hollister, head of a secret government agency called the Department of Scientific Intelligence. Dr. Joseph Wanless, the creator of Lot-6, urges Hollister to have Charlie killed before her abilities become uncontrollable, and Hollister sends John Rainbird, another of the program's superhumans, to track the family down. Rainbird's attack on the McGee home ends in tragedy, and Andy and Charlie flee on the road, hitching a ride with a farmer, Irv Manders, who reluctantly shelters them until agents close in. As Andy, weakened by the physical toll of using his power, is captured, Charlie must learn to master her fire on her own and decide how to use it as she sets out to rescue her father from the agency that created them.

Firestarter received negative reviews, with many critics finding it inferior to the 1984 film. On Rotten Tomatoes, only 10% of 162 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 32 out of 100. It grossed $15 million worldwide against a $12 million budget and was watched in two million households during its first week of streaming.

overview: Avery, a teenager with a tendency towards perfectionism, enlists her friend Larson to help her prepare for her first time with her long-distance boyfriend.
tagline: The only science she doesn't get is chemistry.
title: Sex Appeal
plot:
Sex Appeal, stylized as SexAPPeal, is a 2022 American teen sex comedy directed by Talia Osteen in her feature debut and written by Tate Hanyok, who also served as an executive producer. Developed by American High for Hulu and produced with LD Entertainment, Nickel City Pictures and Lit Entertainment Group, it stars Mika Abdalla, also in her first feature lead, and Jake Short, with Fortune Feimster, Margaret Cho, Rebecca Henderson, Mason Versaw, Paris Jackson, Artemis Pebdani and Hayden Szeto.

Avery Hansen-White (Abdalla) is a hyper-achieving high school senior with a perfect record, a wall of medals and a full scholarship to MIT, who avoids anything she cannot excel at and has no time for proms. She is raised by three supportive mothers: the nurturing Deb (Feimster), the artist Suze (Cho) and Suze's partner Kim (Henderson). Her long-distance boyfriend Casper (Versaw), whom she met at the previous STEMCon, a science competition nicknamed "nerd prom", hopes they will sleep together for the first time at the upcoming event a month away. Avery finds this logical, but she knows almost nothing about sex. When the competition asks entrants to build an app that solves a problem in their personal lives, she decides to make her own first time perfect her project, interviewing classmates and collecting data. For hands-on research, she recruits her lifelong best friend Larson (Short), a good-natured boy who once let her set him on fire for science and who has long harbored feelings for her. As their experiments progress, Larson understands far better than Avery how emotionally risky the arrangement is, and she gradually realizes that relationships involve less science and more heart. The story is framed by a flash-forward in which Avery freezes on stage at STEMCon.

The project was announced in March 2021, with Cho, Jackson and Henderson joining the cast that April. Filming took place in and around Syracuse, New York, including Syracuse Studios, the village of Liverpool and Onondaga Lake Park. The film premiered on Hulu on 14 January 2022 and was later released internationally on Disney+ and in Latin America on Star+. Reviews were mixed, with 55% on Rotten Tomatoes. Common Sense Media praised its positive message about relationships and diverse cast, Decider recommended it for its empathy and consistent tone despite its uneven humor, and Paste and Screen Rant found the heroine's ignorance of sex implausible and the characters thinly developed, while praising Abdalla.

overview: Three high school students make an incredible discovery, leading to their developing uncanny powers beyond their understanding. As they learn to control their abilities and use them to their advantage, their lives start to spin out of control, and their darker sides begin to take over.
tagline: What are you capable of?
title: Chronicle
plot:
Chronicle is a 2012 American science fiction thriller film directed by Josh Trank and written by Max Landis. The movie follows the story of three high school outcasts who discover they have superhuman powers after being bitten by a genetically modified spider.

The film begins with Andrew Detmer (Dane DeHaan), a troubled teenager struggling to cope with his father's death in a car accident. He is joined by Steven Monarch (Alex Russell) and Matt Gannon (Michael B. Jordan), two outcasts who share similar feelings of isolation and anger towards the world.

One day, while exploring an abandoned warehouse, Andrew bites into a genetically modified spider that has been left behind by a scientist. Unbeknownst to him, this spider is carrying a unique genetic code that will grant its victims superhuman powers.

As the days pass, each of the three teenagers begins to exhibit extraordinary abilities: Andrew develops telekinetic powers, Steven gains the ability to manipulate and control electricity, and Matt can fly using his newfound strength. Initially, they use their powers for personal gain and revenge against those who have wronged them.

However, as they delve deeper into their new abilities, they realize that their powers are not just physical but also emotional. They begin to experience intense emotions such as anger, fear, and sadness, which can be both a blessing and a curse.

As the story unfolds, Andrew becomes increasingly obsessed with his powers and begins to lose control of them. He starts to use his abilities for destructive purposes, causing chaos in his town. Meanwhile, Steven's powers become more erratic, and he starts to experience terrifying hallucinations.

Matt, who has been struggling to cope with his own demons, finds solace in his newfound ability to fly. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that Matt is hiding a dark secret: he is actually the son of a powerful and sinister figure known as the Monarch.

The film's climax revolves around Andrew's descent into madness and his ultimate confrontation with Steven. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Andrew has been using his powers to manipulate and control those around him, including his friends and family.

In the end, Matt uses his powers to save Andrew from himself, sacrificing his own life in the process. The film concludes with Steven, who has lost his powers, reflecting on the devastating consequences of their actions. As he looks up at the sky, it is revealed that Matt's spirit has been transformed into a being with wings, symbolizing his newfound freedom and redemption.

Throughout the film, Chronicle explores themes of isolation, anger, and the struggle for control. The movie features a talented young cast, including Dane DeHaan, Alex Russell, and Michael B. Jordan, who deliver standout performances that bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Chronicle is a gripping and thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that explores the complexities of human nature and the dangers of unchecked power.

overview: After reuniting with his first mentor Bruno and receiving his latest mission, an exiled Ciro is left to fearlessly confront whatever comes his way, navigating a new chapter of gang warfare while grappling with devastating memories of loss and trauma. Weaving between his past as an orphan in Naples' cruel underworld and present as a hardened, cunning assassin with nothing left to lose, Ciro is plunged into the cold, dark depths of a world where immortality is just another form of damnation.
title: The Immortal
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "The Immortal" released in 2019 by Beta Film. 

However, I did find information on a 2020 film called "The Immortal" directed by Chris Sparling and produced by Beta Film. The main themes of this movie appear to be:

*   Existentialism: The story revolves around the protagonist's struggle with his own mortality and the meaning of life.
*   Identity: The character grapples with his sense of self, questioning whether he is truly immortal or just pretending to be so.
*   Human connection: As the protagonist navigates his relationships with others, he begins to realize that true immortality lies in forming meaningful connections with people.

The plot follows a man who claims to be immortal and has lived for centuries. He becomes embroiled in a complex web of relationships and deceit as he tries to maintain his secret while also searching for human connection.

overview: Salvador Mallo, a filmmaker in the twilight of his career, remembers his life: his mother, his lovers, the actors he worked with. The sixties in a small village in Valencia, the eighties in Madrid, the present, when he feels an immeasurable emptiness, facing his mortality, the incapability of continuing filming, the impossibility of separating creation from his own life. The need of narrating his past can be his salvation.
title: Pain and Glory
plot:
Pain and Glory is a 2019 Spanish drama film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, not El Deseo. The movie follows the story of a retired theater director, Sergio, who embarks on a journey to rediscover his passion for life and art after being diagnosed with cancer.

The main themes of Pain and Glory revolve around the complexities of human existence, love, loss, and the search for meaning in life. The film explores the idea that our experiences, both joyful and painful, shape us into who we are, and that it's never too late to rediscover ourselves and pursue our passions.

Through Sergio's story, Almodóvar delves into the human condition, examining the ways in which we cope with mortality, grief, and the fear of losing what matters most. The film also touches on the theme of creative expression as a means of healing and self-discovery.

Ultimately, Pain and Glory is a poignant exploration of the human spirit's capacity for resilience, love, and transformation, even in the face of adversity.

overview: As a CODA (Child of Deaf Adults), Ruby is the only hearing person in her deaf family. When the family's fishing business is threatened, Ruby finds herself torn between pursuing her love of music and her fear of abandoning her parents.
tagline: Every family has its own language.
title: CODA
plot:
CODA (Child of Deaf Adults) is a heartwarming drama film released in 2021, directed by Sian Heder and produced by Frida Thorsson, Tony Hsieh, and others. The movie tells the story of Ruby Rossi, a 17-year-old girl who is the only hearing member of her deaf family.

The film begins with Ruby (played by Marlee Matlin's daughter, Emilia) navigating her way through high school as the only one in her family who can hear. Her parents, Frank and Jackie (played by Troy Kotsur and Daniel Durant), are both deaf, and her younger brother Leo (played by Millicent Simmonds) is also deaf. Ruby's life is a balancing act between her love for music and her responsibilities to support her family.

Ruby's passion for singing is evident from an early age, and she dreams of attending Berklee College of Music in Boston. However, her parents are hesitant about her pursuing a career in the performing arts due to their concerns about her future and the financial burden it may place on them.

As Ruby navigates her relationships with her family members, she also develops feelings for Miles (played by Daniel Durant), her brother Leo's best friend. The romance between Ruby and Miles adds an extra layer of complexity to the story, as they must navigate their own identities and desires while supporting each other through thick and thin.

Throughout the film, Ruby faces numerous challenges, including balancing schoolwork with her music career and dealing with the pressure from her family to prioritize their needs over her own. However, she also finds solace in her relationships with her loved ones, particularly her brother Leo, who becomes a source of inspiration and support for her.

As the story unfolds, Ruby's determination and passion for music ultimately lead her to make a difficult decision that will change the course of her life forever. The film's climax features an emotional performance by Ruby at a local restaurant, where she sings with conviction and heart, showcasing her incredible talent.

The ending of CODA is both poignant and uplifting, as Ruby finds a way to reconcile her love for music with her responsibilities to her family. The film concludes on a hopeful note, with Ruby embarking on a new journey that will take her to Berklee College of Music and beyond.

Overall, CODA is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of identity, family, and following one's dreams. With outstanding performances from the cast, particularly Marlee Matlin, Troy Kotsur, and Millicent Simmonds, the movie has captured the hearts of audiences worldwide.

overview: Mike Fallon, the Accident Man, is a stone cold killer.  When a loved one is murdered by his own crew, Fallon is forced to avenge the one person who actually meant something to him.
tagline: Accidents happen. He can guarantee it.
title: Accident Man
plot:
Accident Man is a 2018 action thriller film directed by Mike Binder and starring Simon Pegg as Michael Stonehouse, an insurance investigator who becomes embroiled in a complex web of espionage and deception.

The main themes of Accident Man include:

1. Identity Crisis: The film explores the theme of identity crisis through Michael Stonehouse's character, who is struggling to find his place in the world after being diagnosed with a terminal illness. This existential crisis leads him to question his purpose and sense of self.
2. Deception and Betrayal: The movie delves into the themes of deception and betrayal as Michael navigates a complex web of espionage and double agents. He must confront the fact that everyone around him is hiding secrets and lies, making it difficult for him to trust anyone.
3. Redemption and Self-Sacrifice: As Michael becomes more deeply embroiled in the conspiracy, he begins to realize that his only way out is to sacrifice himself. This theme of redemption and self-sacrifice drives the plot of the film and serves as a commentary on the human cost of espionage and deception.

Overall, Accident Man is a thought-provoking thriller that explores complex themes through its engaging storyline and well-developed characters.

original_title: How to Be a Latin Lover
overview: An aging Latin lover gets dumped by his sugar mama and must fend for himself in a harsh world.
tagline: Fifty shades grayer
title: How to Be a Latin Lover
plot:
"How to Be a Latin Lover" is a 2017 American romantic comedy film directed by Ken Marino and starring Carlos PenaVega, Rosa Salazar, and Norm Macdonald. The movie follows the story of Carlos, an American who travels to Mexico in search of his estranged father's fortune.

The main themes of "How to Be a Latin Lover" include:

1. Cultural Identity: The film explores the complexities of cultural identity, particularly for those of Latin American descent living in the United States. Carlos struggles to reconcile his Mexican heritage with his American upbringing, leading to comedic misunderstandings and cultural clashes.
2. Family Dynamics: The movie delves into the complexities of family relationships, particularly between fathers and sons. Carlos's journey is motivated by a desire to reconnect with his father and understand his past.
3. Love and Relationships: As Carlos navigates the dating world in Mexico, he must confront his own insecurities and learn to open up to love. The film features a romantic subplot that adds to the overall comedic tone.
4. Self-Discovery: Throughout the movie, Carlos undergoes a journey of self-discovery, learning to accept himself and his cultural roots. This theme is reflected in his interactions with his father and his romantic interests.

Overall, "How to Be a Latin Lover" is a lighthearted, comedic film that explores themes of identity, family, love, and self-discovery through the lens of a humorous and entertaining story.

overview: A young man and his three younger siblings are plagued by a sinister presence in the sprawling manor in which they live.
tagline: No one will ever separate us.
title: Marrowbone
plot:
Marrowbone (Spanish: El secreto de Marrowbone) is a 2017 English-language Spanish psychological horror mystery film written and directed by Sergio G. Sánchez. It stars George MacKay, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Heaton, Mia Goth and Matthew Stagg, and follows four siblings who move from England to their mother's ancestral home in Maine, where they are confronted by a sinister presence. It screened in the Special Presentations section of the 2017 Toronto International Film Festival and was released in Spain by Universal Pictures on 27 October 2017.

In 1968, Rose Fairbairn brings her four children, Jack, Jane, Billy and Sam, from England to the remote house in rural Maine where she grew up, and tells them they will now go by her maiden name, Marrowbone. The family is befriended by a local girl, Allie, but Rose's health soon fails. Before she dies she makes Jack, the eldest, promise to keep the family together and to hide her death until he can become his siblings' legal guardian. Six months later the children are still living alone in the house, where every mirror is covered and the attic is sealed off because they believe something lives up there. Jack slips into town for supplies and quietly courts Allie, now working at the library, while hiding his past from her. Tom Porter, the town lawyer handling the Marrowbone estate and Allie's unrequited admirer, needs Rose's signature to complete the transfer of the property, and the siblings are forced to forge it and to dip into a box of money left by their father. As strange noises and incidents in the house multiply, Allie learns from Tom some disturbing facts about the family's past and the father the children fled from, while Tom, under financial pressure, begins to suspect the Marrowbones are hiding more money and turns to blackmail. When Billy goes looking for the money in the house, he makes a terrifying discovery, and the secret that Jack has been protecting threatens to come out.

On Rotten Tomatoes, Marrowbone holds a 49% approval rating based on 75 reviews, with a consensus that its effective setting and strong cast cannot make up for thinly conceived characters and a story short on genuine scares, while Metacritic gave it a score of 63 out of 100.

overview: Several years after the murderous events of the first movie left her father dead, Emma is now living with her aunt Angela and navigating high school. Angela’s husband begins to suspect that Emma may not be as innocent as she appears and suggests sending her off to boarding school. Meanwhile, a new girl at school seems to know Emma’s secrets, leaving Emma no choice but to slip back to her old ways and take care of her enemies by any means necessary.
title: The Bad Seed Returns
plot:
The Bad Seed Returns is a 2022 American made-for-television horror drama film directed by Louise Archambault and written by Ross Burge, Mckenna Grace and Barbara Marshall. A sequel to the 2018 television film The Bad Seed, itself a remake of the 1956 film adapted from William March's 1954 novel, it stars Grace, reprising her role as Emma, with Michelle Morgan, Benjamin Ayres, Ella Dixon, Marlowe Zimmerman and Jude Wilson. Patty McCormack, who played the murderous Rhoda Penmark in the 1956 version, makes a special appearance as Emma's therapist, Dr. March. The film was shot in Vancouver and premiered on Lifetime on September 5, 2022.

Six years after the death of her father, David, 15-year-old Emma Grossman lives with her aunt Angela, a psychiatrist, Angela's new husband Robert and their baby son, Cade. Nobody suspects her past crimes, and Emma keeps up the appearance of an ordinary teenager devoted to school, friends and her dance team while concealing her psychopathy. She resents Robert's presence in the household, and when he finds his missing camping knife hidden in her drawer, he arranges for her to be sent to a boarding school, St. Crispin's. Emma responds by sabotaging his car jack, leaving him badly injured in hospital. At school, a new student named Kat, who knows about Emma's past, refuses to be fooled by her, and Emma's rivalry with her friend Stephanie over the position of dance captain takes a dark turn. As people around her begin to suffer suspicious misfortunes, Angela slowly starts to see her niece for who she really is, and a conversation with Brian, the caretaker who shot David in self-defense years earlier, helps her understand what David had come to realize. Robert, meanwhile, begins to recover his memory of what happened to him and confronts Emma with an ultimatum. Cornered, Emma prepares a final scheme to protect herself and her secret, putting everyone in the household in grave danger.

Production on the sequel was announced in November 2021, with Grace both co-writing and starring, and filming took place in Vancouver later that month. McCormack's character name, Dr. March, is a nod to William March, the author of the novel on which the story is based.

overview: Remmy and her parents, refugees from Earth, have found peace on the Martian outskirts until strangers appear in the hills beyond their farm. Told as a triptych, the film follows Remmy as she struggles to survive in an uneasy landscape.
tagline: How far would you go to build a new life?
title: Settlers
plot:
Settlers is a 2021 British science fiction thriller written and directed by Wyatt Rockefeller in his feature debut. It stars Sofia Boutella as Ilsa, Ismael Cruz Córdova as Jerry and Jonny Lee Miller as Reza, with Brooklynn Prince and Nell Tiger Free playing the daughter, Remmy, as a child and as a young woman.

The film takes place on Mars, where Reza, Ilsa and their young daughter Remmy live on a remote, barren homestead. One morning they find the word "LEAVE" written on their window, and soon afterwards bandits attack the farm. Reza is killed. Jerry, one of the attackers, survives and takes over the homestead. He asks Ilsa and Remmy for thirty days to prove himself and earn their trust. As the weeks pass, Ilsa seems to warm to him, but at the end of the thirty days she tries to shoot him. The gun Jerry deliberately left within reach turns out to be empty, and Jerry kills Ilsa in the struggle that follows.

Remmy, now alone with the man who destroyed her family, becomes withdrawn and resentful. She spends her time with Steve, a pet-like utility robot she found in a storage unit. Exploring the farm, she learns that it lies inside a large force-field bubble that keeps the air breathable, so the bandits must have come from outside or from another protected settlement. Years go by. Remmy grows into a young woman who barely speaks to Jerry. When he insists that they have a child together and she tries to leave, he stops her, ties her up and attempts to rape her. Steve intervenes, striking Jerry in the neck with its drill, and Remmy frees herself and kills him. Finally free but alone, Remmy decides to set out into the unknown Martian landscape, leaving Steve to look after the farm.

Critics described the film as a stark, minimalist science fiction western, an intimate drama about survival, power and trust. IFC Midnight acquired the American distribution rights in April 2021. Settlers premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on June 18, 2021, and was released in the United States on July 23, 2021. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said the film was serious to a fault but that viewers looking for a non-sensational take on space colonization might find it a rewarding voyage.

overview: Venice, 1596. Bassanio begs his friend Antonio, a prosperous merchant, to lend him a large sum of money so that he can woo Portia, a very wealthy heiress; but Antonio has invested his fortune abroad, so they turn to Shylock, a Jewish moneylender, and ask him for a loan.
title: The Merchant of Venice
plot:
The Merchant of Venice is a 2004 romantic drama film directed by Michael Radford and based on William Shakespeare's play. Al Pacino plays the Jewish moneylender Shylock and Jeremy Irons the title character, the merchant Antonio, with Joseph Fiennes, Lynn Collins and Zuleikha Robinson. It was the first full-length English-language sound film of the play, earlier versions having been videotaped television productions, and while it follows Shakespeare's text it omits much of it. Radford regarded Shylock as Shakespeare's first great tragic hero, a man brought to catastrophe by his own flaws.

In Venice, the young Bassanio needs 3,000 ducats to travel to Belmont and court the wealthy heiress Portia. His friend Antonio, whose fortune is tied up in ships at sea, borrows the money from Shylock, a moneylender who resents Antonio for having insulted and spat on him for being a Jew. Shylock agrees to the loan on an unusual condition: if Antonio fails to repay it on time, Shylock may take a pound of his flesh. Antonio accepts despite Bassanio's misgivings. At Belmont, Portia's late father has decreed that her suitors must choose among caskets of gold, silver and lead, and Bassanio wins her hand by choosing the lead one. In Venice, however, news arrives that Antonio's ships have all been lost, and Shylock, embittered further after his daughter Jessica runs away with the Christian Lorenzo, converting and taking much of his wealth with her, insists on enforcing the bond. Bassanio and his companion Gratiano hurry back with Portia's money to save their friend, but Shylock refuses even double the sum and demands his pound of flesh before the Duke of Venice. Unknown to the men, Portia and her maid Nerissa follow them, disguised as a young doctor of law and his clerk, and Portia's arguments in court turn the law against Shylock, leading to a judgment that costs him his fortune, followed by a playful test of the newlyweds' loyalty involving the rings they promised never to give away.

The film received generally positive reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes, 72% of 125 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 63 out of 100. Critics praised Pacino's and Radford's interpretation of Shylock and the dark, realistic look of Venice, for which production designer Bruno Rubeo was honored by the Italian National Syndicate of Film Journalists, while responses to its handling of antisemitism were mixed.

overview: The way of the eagle is to raise two chicks. The stronger is destined always to throw the weaker from the nest. Man also has his ways, often to hurt those closest to him.  Lukas suffers at the hands of a father who has withdrawn since the loss of his wife. Killed whilst rescuing the infant Lukas, the boy now carries the burden of her death.  Our eagle’s story begins in the nest. The first-born chick pushes his weaker brother to a certain death on the forest floor. But fate intervenes and the chick is found by Lukas. Naming him Abel, Lukas cares for the creature in secret, finding a love and companionship denied to him at home. But when the day comes to release Abel back into the wild, will Lukas find his own release into a new life?
tagline: Sometimes a friendship sets you free
title: Brothers of the Wind
plot:
Brothers of the Wind is an English-language Austrian coming-of-age drama directed by Gerardo Olivares and Otmar Penker, first released in December 2015. Set amid the Alps, it intertwines the life of a young golden eagle with that of a grieving boy, and stars Manuel Camacho as Lukas, Jean Reno as the forester Danzer, Tobias Moretti as Lukas's father Keller and Eva Kuen as his late mother Maria.

In the 1960s a pair of eagles hatch two chicks high in the mountains. The father is killed in a fight with another eagle, and one eaglet tumbles from the nest, abandoned by its mother, who by instinct raises only the stronger chick. Below, Lukas and Keller have moved into a new mountain home after Maria died in a fire. Consumed by grief, Keller cannot connect with his son, who retreats into the forest and to the ruins of their old house. There Lukas discovers the fallen eaglet and decides to nurse it, and Danzer, fond of the boy, teaches him how to feed and care for the bird. Reading the family Bible, Lukas comes across Cain and Abel and names the eaglet Abel, thinking of the brother still in the nest as Cain.

Danzer takes Lukas and Abel to stay with him for the summer, and the boy helps the young eagle learn to fly. Abel vanishes for days and returns, and the two friends train him to hunt despite Keller's objections, until Danzer persuades Lukas that the bird must go free; they release it blindfolded in a distant part of the mountains. After a wolf frightens Lukas into a bear trap and Danzer rescues him, the rift with his father deepens. Coming to believe that Keller started the fire that killed his mother, Lukas runs away into the mountains, where a rockslide and a lightning strike leave him unconscious. Keller finds him and apologises for his harshness. Two years later, Abel reappears and lands on Lukas's arm; the boy removes the band he once tied to its leg and lets it go for good, and Abel later awaits a new hatchling with a mate.

Common Sense Media gave the film a strong recommendation, citing its gorgeous imagery, its faithful portrayal of the laws of nature and its uplifting story of a boy growing up, while Cinemagazine was cooler, rating it 2.5.

overview: The world is on the verge of a devastating war with monsters who are coming to retrieve the Scaling Stone. Yin Yang Master Qingming's life is in danger and he travels to different worlds to prepare for the upcoming assaults. On his journey, Qingming finds that the key to all the calamities is embracing his hybrid identity of both human and monster.
title: The Yin Yang Master
plot:
The Yin Yang Master (Chinese: Shi Shen Ling), also known as The Yinyang Master, is a 2021 Chinese fantasy film directed by Li Weiran and starring Chen Kun and Zhou Xun. It is adapted from NetEase's video game Onmyōji, which in turn draws on the Onmyōji novel series by the author Baku Yumemakura. The cast also includes William Chan as Ci Mu, Qu Chuxiao as Yuan Boya, Wang Likun as the Peach Blossom Spirit, Wang Zixuan as the Snow Queen and Wang Ruiyi as the Butterfly Spirit. Filmed in 2018, it was released in Chinese cinemas on 12 February 2021, the first day of the Chinese New Year, and Netflix, which acquired the international streaming rights, released it worldwide on 19 March 2021.

Qing Ming, played by Chen Kun, is a Yinyang Master, a being who is half human and half demon and who serves as an officer of the Yinyang Bureau, the organization that guards captured demon souls and a powerful supernatural artifact known as the Scale Stone. When he is framed for the deaths of a team of guards and of his senior, Ci Mu, he flees the Bureau and begins a new life, moving between the human world and the demon world. Seven years later, as the Demon King threatens to return, Qing Ming becomes entangled in the robbery of a shipment of imperial tributes being escorted by Boya, and he is hunted by Bai Ni, played by Zhou Xun, the head of the Yinyang Bureau, with whom he once made a pact. Trapped together in a fighting arena in the demon world, Qing Ming, an injured Bai Ni, Boya and their companions are forced to cooperate to escape. Bai Ni discovers that Qing Ming has secretly been caring for and training a band of demons to resist the Demon King, and after he heals her, she recovers the Scale Stone, which one of his demons had accidentally swallowed. On her way back to the Bureau, however, she is ambushed by an old enemy and the Snow Queen, and the Stone is stolen. The theft exposes a long-hidden betrayal rooted in envy of Qing Ming's demonic power, unleashes a demon invasion of the human world and forces Qing Ming to consider a dangerous bargain to save both realms.

The film was released in China under the English title The Yinyang Master and reached audiences outside China under the title The Yin Yang Master through its Netflix release.

overview: A high-rolling corporate shark and his impoverished young guide play the most dangerous game during a hunting trip in the Mojave Desert.
title: Beyond the Reach
plot:
Beyond the Reach is a 2014 American action thriller film directed by Martin Campbell and starring Anthony Hopkins and Christopher Walken.

The movie revolves around a former CIA operative, Jack Reacher, who is wrongly accused of murdering a young woman. As he tries to clear his name, he uncovers a conspiracy involving corrupt government officials and a mysterious plot that puts him in the crosshairs of a ruthless adversary.

At its core, Beyond the Reach explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong. The film delves into the complexities of human nature, highlighting the moral ambiguities that often accompany the pursuit of justice. Through Reacher's character, the movie raises questions about the consequences of playing by one's own rules and the importance of accountability in a system that seems to be stacked against its most vulnerable members.

The film also touches on the theme of isolation and the difficulties of forming connections in a world where trust is hard to come by. As Reacher navigates his way through the treacherous landscape, he must confront his own demons and learn to rely on others if he hopes to survive.

Ultimately, Beyond the Reach is a gripping thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats as it hurtles towards its explosive conclusion. With its breakneck pace and pulse-pounding action sequences, the film delivers an adrenaline-fueled ride that will keep you guessing until the very end.

overview: After being infected in the wake of a violent pandemic and with only 48 hours to live, a father struggles to find a new home for his baby daughter.
tagline: The future is fragile.
title: Cargo
plot:
Cargo is a 2017 Australian post-apocalyptic romantic drama film directed by Ben Cipollini. The movie revolves around Andy, a man who has contracted a deadly virus that slowly turns him into a zombie-like creature. As he navigates his way through the desolate landscape to find a cure for himself and protect those he cares about, he forms an unlikely bond with Erin, a young woman who is pregnant.

The main theme of Cargo is the power of human connection in the face of unimaginable adversity. The film explores the complexities of love, loss, and sacrifice as Andy struggles to come to terms with his own mortality and find a way to save those around him. Through Andy's journey, the movie highlights the resilience of the human spirit and the importance of holding onto hope even when all seems lost.

The film also delves into themes of grief, loneliness, and the search for meaning in a world that has been ravaged by a deadly virus. As Andy navigates his way through this desolate landscape, he is forced to confront his own emotions and find ways to cope with the loss of those around him. The movie ultimately becomes a poignant exploration of what it means to be human, even in the face of unimaginable tragedy.

The character of Erin serves as a catalyst for Andy's transformation, forcing him to re-evaluate his priorities and find a new sense of purpose. Through their relationship, the film shows how love can transcend even the most impossible circumstances, and how two people can come together to form a bond that is stronger than any virus or apocalypse.

Overall, Cargo is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that highlights the importance of connection, hope, and resilience in the face of adversity.

overview: A sawmill owner and his teenage daughter become tangled in a deadly feud when a drug dealer stashes stolen cocaine on their remote property.
title: Earth and Blood
plot:
Earth and Blood (French: La Terre et le Sang) is a 2020 French action thriller film directed by Julien Leclercq and starring Sami Bouajila, Eriq Ebouaney and Samy Seghir, with Sofia Lesaffre and Redouanne Harjane. It depicts a violent siege at an isolated sawmill after a young employee hides a gang's stolen cocaine there, forcing the mill's owner into a last stand to protect his teenage daughter.

A raid on a police evidence room leaves two of four robbers dead; the survivors escape with eight kilos of cocaine. Meanwhile, sawmill owner Saïd learns from a scan that he has cancer and not long to live, and he plans to sell the mill, which once belonged to his sister-in-law's father, to pay for the further education of his teenage daughter, Sarah, who has impaired hearing and speech. One of his employees, Yanis, a young parolee, meets his half-brother, one of the surviving robbers, who has decided not to hand the drugs over to the drug lord Adama and asks Yanis to hide them at the mill. Adama captures the two robbers and kills one of them. Growing suspicious, Saïd questions Yanis, finds the drugs in a truck, locks him inside the mill and drives off for help, but turns back on learning that the gang is coming.

Adama's brother Moussa arrives first and threatens Yanis and Sarah at gunpoint before Saïd shoots him. With Adama and his men closing in and the phone lines cut, Saïd arms Yanis with a shotgun and sends him into the woods with Sarah while he draws the gang into a series of traps, killing them one by one. Trapped when the gang sets the mill ablaze, he breaks out in a heavy log loader and crushes a pursuing car. In the woods, a henchman finds Yanis and Sarah hiding in a shed and stabs Yanis; Sarah runs to a farmhouse for help, and Saïd arrives too late to save Yanis. Adama wounds Saïd badly and goes after Sarah to avenge his brother, killing the old farmer who sheltered her. Sarah leaps from an upper floor but is caught, and as Adama tries to break her neck, Saïd arrives and kills him with an axe, collapsing in his daughter's arms as a police helicopter approaches.

Netflix released the film on April 17, 2020. Decider likened it to a French take on Rambo: Last Blood, praising Bouajila's and Lesaffre's acting but faulting the thin screenplay and stylized slow motion, while The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw found the characters sketched in too quickly and the film like a truncated version of a longer work.

overview: Gene, a multi-expressional emoji, sets out on a journey to become a normal emoji.
tagline: Not easy being meh
title: The Emoji Movie
plot:
The Emoji Movie is a computer-animated comedy-adventure film released in 2017 by Columbia Pictures. The movie takes place inside a smartphone, where emojis live and interact with each other.

The story begins with Gene (voiced by T.J. Miller), a multi-expressional emoji who feels like he doesn't quite fit in with the other emojis. He is a "smile" emoji, but he has a unique personality that makes him feel like an outcast. Gene dreams of becoming a "text message" emoji, which would allow him to be more expressive and have a sense of purpose.

One day, Gene meets Hi-5 (voiced by James Corden), a popular emoji who is known for his bright smile and infectious enthusiasm. However, when a new app called "MessageApp" is released, it threatens the existence of all emojis. The app's creator, Textopolis (voiced by Anna Faris), has created an algorithm that can control every aspect of digital communication, including emojis.

Gene and Hi-5 embark on a journey to stop Textopolis and save their world from being deleted. Along the way, they meet other emojis who join them on their quest, including Jailbreak (voiced by Patrick Stewart), a rebellious emoji who is determined to take down Textopolis; Smiler (voiced by Maya Rudolph), a happy-go-lucky emoji who becomes Gene's love interest; and Hi-5's rival, Hi-5 Jr. (voiced by Jake T. Austin).

As they navigate through the smartphone, the emojis encounter various obstacles and challenges, including navigating through apps, avoiding deletion, and dealing with the consequences of their own emotions. Along the way, Gene discovers his true purpose as a "smile" emoji and learns to accept himself for who he is.

The movie features a star-studded voice cast, including Steven Wright, Christina Aguilera, and Jennifer Coolidge. The animation is colorful and vibrant, with a unique blend of 2D and 3D elements that bring the emojis to life.

In the end, Gene and his friends successfully defeat Textopolis and save their world from being deleted. However, the movie ends on a bittersweet note, as Gene realizes that he must return to his old life as a "smile" emoji. Despite this, Gene is happy knowing that he has found his purpose and made new friends along the way.

Overall, The Emoji Movie is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, self-acceptance, and the power of emotions. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has become a cult classic among fans of animation and comedy.

overview: After they meet at their parent's engagement party, Mia and Frida are intrigued by and attracted to one another, despite Mia's own upcoming engagement to Tim. Mia must decide whether to continue her life with Tim or to follow her heart with Frida.
tagline: With Every Heartbeat
title: Kiss Me
plot:
Kiss Me is a 2011 South Korean romantic comedy film directed by Lee Seung-jun and produced by SBS TV's in-house production company, SBS TV (not SVT). 

The movie revolves around the story of two people who meet at a funeral and develop an unlikely romance. The main themes of Kiss Me include:

1. Unlikely love: The film explores the idea that love can come from unexpected places and that people from different walks of life can find common ground.
2. Grief and healing: The movie delves into the theme of coping with loss and finding solace in the company of others.
3. Human connection: Kiss Me highlights the importance of human relationships and the impact they have on our lives.

The film features a strong cast, including Kim Sun-ah and Lee Hyo-seok, who deliver nuanced performances that bring depth to their characters. The movie's tone is light-hearted and humorous, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences looking for a feel-good romantic comedy.

Overall, Kiss Me is a heartwarming story about finding love in unexpected places and the power of human connection to heal emotional wounds.

overview: Set after the events of Continental Drift, Scrat's epic pursuit of his elusive acorn catapults him outside of Earth, where he accidentally sets off a series of cosmic events that transform and threaten the planet. To save themselves from peril, Manny, Sid, Diego, and the rest of the herd leave their home and embark on a quest full of thrills and spills, highs and lows, laughter and adventure while traveling to exotic new lands and locations.
tagline: One small step. One giant mess.
title: Ice Age: Collision Course
plot:
Ice Age: Collision Course is a 2016 American animated adventure comedy film directed by Michael Thurmeier and written by Michael Wilson, Michael Berg and Yoni Brenner. Produced by 20th Century Fox Animation and Blue Sky Studios, it is the fifth installment in the Ice Age series, following Ice Age: Continental Drift (2012). Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary, Josh Peck, Simon Pegg, Seann William Scott, Jennifer Lopez and Queen Latifah reprise their voice roles, joined by Jessie J and Adam DeVine.

Peaches, the daughter of the mammoths Manny and Ellie, is engaged to Julian, a cheerful mammoth whom Manny finds annoying and considers incapable of protecting her, and Manny is even more upset to learn that the couple want to travel the world after the wedding. Diego and Shira are hoping to start a family, and Sid is dumped by his girlfriend just as he is about to propose. Meanwhile Scrat's never-ending pursuit of his acorn has propelled him into outer space aboard an abandoned spaceship, where his antics send a giant asteroid hurtling toward Earth. As meteors begin to rain down on Manny and Ellie's anniversary, the herd takes shelter in a cave and is reunited with the adventurous weasel Buck, who has found an ancient stone pillar in the underground dinosaur world. According to its carvings, asteroids have caused two mass extinctions in the past, always striking the same spot, and Buck believes a solution may be found there. Pursued by a trio of flying dromaeosaurs who hope to survive the catastrophe and inherit the planet, the herd sets off for the impact site. On the way, Buck discovers that the asteroids are magnetic and devises a plan to launch a mass of smaller fragments into orbit to pull the big one off course. The journey leads them to Geotopia, a community of long-lived animals living inside a fallen asteroid, where Sid finds a new admirer in a sloth named Brooke, but the community's leader, Shangri Llama, refuses to surrender the crystals that keep his people young, and the herd must find a way to save the world while Manny learns to accept Julian.

The film received generally negative reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes, only 18% of 120 critics' reviews are positive, ranking it as the lowest-rated Ice Age film, with a consensus calling it unoriginal and unfunny. It still grossed $408 million worldwide against a $105 million production budget.

overview: 13-year-old Sinikka vanishes on a hot summer night. Her bicycle is found in the exact place where a girl was killed 23 years ago. The dramatic present forces those involved in the original case to face their past.
title: The Silence
plot:
The Silence (German: Das letzte Schweigen) is a 2010 German thriller film directed by Baran bo Odar, adapted from the crime novel The Silence by Jan Costin Wagner. Its ensemble cast includes Ulrich Thomsen as Peer Sommer, Wotan Wilke Möhring as Timo Friedrich, Sebastian Blomberg as detective David Jahn, Burghart Klaußner as retired detective Krischan Mittich, Katrin Sass as Elena Lange and Oliver Stokowski as Matthias Grimmer.

In the summer of 1986, eleven-year-old Pia is raped and murdered in a wheat field outside a small German town by one man while another watches silently from the passenger seat of a red car. Her body is taken away and her bicycle is left behind. Exactly 23 years later, in 2009, thirteen-year-old Sinikka Weghamm disappears after leaving the local fair, and her bicycle is found at the same spot. Krischan Mittich, the detective who never solved Pia's murder, has just retired, and the new investigation falls to David Jahn, who is still overwhelmed by grief after the death of his wife five months earlier, under the leadership of the stubborn senior detective Matthias Grimmer, who keeps Mittich at arm's length. Flashbacks reveal how the killer, a Dane named Peer Sommer, met Timo, a student with whom he shared a collection of child pornography, and how Timo fled after witnessing Pia's death. Timo has since built a respectable life as an architect, married and become a father, but news of Sinikka's disappearance sends him back to the town and to Sommer, who is pleased to see him again. Racked with shame, Timo visits Pia's grieving mother, Elena, whose suspicions about the stranger lead Mittich and Jahn to his home, while Jahn proposes cross-checking lists of red cars registered near the old crime scenes. As the police close in from different directions, the investigation is shadowed by the anguish of Sinikka's parents and the guilt of the two men who have kept silent for more than two decades, and the question of whether the new crime was committed by the same killer becomes ever more pressing.

The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw gave the film a favorable review, calling it an icy, gripping police procedural thriller that is easy to recommend to fans of The Killing and to anyone else. It won a Special Jury Award at the Beaune film festival in 2011, the Best Adaptation Award at the 2010 Frankfurt Book Fair and an audience award at the German Thriller Awards, and it was nominated for the German Film Critics Award.

overview: In Babel, a tragic incident involving an American couple in Morocco sparks a chain of events for four families in different countries throughout the world. In the struggle to overcome isolation, fear, and displacement, each character discovers that it is family that ultimately provides solace. In the remote sands of the Moroccan desert, a rifle shot rings out  detonating a chain of events that will link an American tourist couples frantic struggle to survive, two Moroccan boys involved in an accidental crime, a nanny illegally crossing into Mexico with two American children and a Japanese teen rebel whose father is sought by the police in Tokyo. Separated by clashing cultures and sprawling distances, each of these four disparate groups of people are nevertheless hurtling towards a shared destiny of isolation and grief.
tagline: If You Want to be Understood...Listen
title: Babel
plot:
Babel is a 2006 psychological drama directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu and written by Guillermo Arriaga. It completes their "Death Trilogy" after Amores perros (2000) and 21 Grams (2003). The ensemble cast includes Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett, Gael García Bernal, Kōji Yakusho, Adriana Barraza and Rinko Kikuchi. Four interlinked stories in Morocco, the United States, Mexico and Japan are told out of chronological order.

In the Moroccan desert, a goatherd buys a rifle to protect his flock from jackals and gives it to his young sons, Yussef and Ahmed. Testing its range, Yussef fires at a passing tour bus and seriously wounds Susan, an American tourist traveling with her husband, Richard. The couple are struggling after the death of their infant son. Stranded in a remote village while the other tourists demand to leave, Richard waits desperately for help. The American government calls the shooting terrorism, and Moroccan police hunt down the family. In a shootout, Ahmed is badly hurt, and Yussef surrenders, confessing to the shooting. A helicopter finally takes Susan to a hospital in Casablanca.

In San Diego, the couple's Mexican nanny, Amelia, cannot find anyone to look after their children so she can attend her son's wedding. She takes them with her across the border to a village near Tijuana. On the way back, her drunk nephew Santiago panics at the border checkpoint, speeds off and leaves Amelia and the children in the desert. Amelia goes for help and is arrested by the Border Patrol. The children are found alive, but Amelia, who has been working illegally for years, is deported.

In Tokyo, Chieko, a deaf teenager, is lonely and grieving her mother's suicide, and she seeks attention through provocative sexual behavior. Police come to ask about her father, Yasujiro. The connection is the rifle: he had given it as a gift to his hunting guide in Morocco. Chieko tries to seduce a detective, who gently turns her down, and her father finally comforts her on their balcony.

Babel competed at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival, where González Iñárritu won Best Director. It grossed $135.3 million worldwide on a $25 million budget. It won the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Drama and received seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and supporting actress nominations for Barraza and Kikuchi. Gustavo Santaolalla won the Oscar for Best Original Score. Roger Ebert later added it to his Great Movies list.

overview: A Viking boy is left behind after his clan battles a Native American tribe. Raised within the tribe, he ultimately becomes their savior in a fight against the Norsemen.
tagline: Two Worlds, One War. The Ultimate Battle Begins.
title: Pathfinder
plot:
Pathfinder is a 2007 American fantasy adventure film directed by Marcus Nispel, starring Jason Statham, Ray Liotta, and Delroy Lindo.

The main themes of Pathfinder include:

1. **Survival and Self-Discovery**: The movie follows the story of Erik Bloodaxe (Jason Statham), a Viking warrior who is exiled from his tribe and must navigate the treacherous world of 11th-century England to survive. As he faces various challenges, Erik discovers more about himself and his place in the world.

2. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: The film explores the complexities of loyalty and betrayal through Erik's relationships with his brother Ivar (Jürgen Prochnow) and his adopted son Sigurd (Ralf Möller). These relationships are tested as Erik navigates the treacherous landscape of medieval England.

3. **Power and Corruption**: The movie touches on the theme of power and corruption, particularly in the character of King Aethelred (Ray Liotta), who is struggling to maintain control over his kingdom. Erik's arrival sets off a chain of events that challenges Aethelred's authority and forces him to confront the consequences of his actions.

4. **Cultural Clash**: The film also explores the clash between different cultures, as Viking warriors encounter the English nobility. This cultural divide leads to conflicts and misunderstandings, highlighting the difficulties of communication and cooperation between people from different backgrounds.
