Overall, Pathfinder is a thrilling adventure film that delves into themes of survival, loyalty, power, and cultural clash, set against the backdrop of 11th-century England.

overview: An undercover cop in a not-too-distant future becomes involved with a dangerous new drug and begins to lose his own identity as a result.
tagline: Everything is not going to be OK
title: A Scanner Darkly
plot:
A Scanner Darkly is indeed a 2006 film directed by Richard Linklater, not produced by Section Eight.

The main theme of A Scanner Darkly revolves around the blurred lines between reality and paranoia. The story follows an undercover cop, Bob Arctor, who becomes deeply entrenched in his own paranoid delusions as he navigates a complex web of addiction, corporate espionage, and government surveillance. As the film progresses, it becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish what is real and what is just a product of Arctor's own fractured mind.

The movie explores the darker aspects of human nature, particularly the destructive power of addiction and the ways in which it can consume individuals. The film also delves into themes of identity, loyalty, and the erosion of personal boundaries in a world where technology and societal pressures are constantly monitoring and manipulating our thoughts and actions.

Through Arctor's character, the film critiques the notion of a "free" individual in a society that is increasingly controlled by corporate interests and government agencies. The movie ultimately presents a bleak vision of a future where paranoia and mistrust have become the norm, leaving individuals feeling isolated and disconnected from one another.

Overall, A Scanner Darkly is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions in a world that is rapidly becoming more surveillance-driven.

overview: A family gets trapped in their storm flooded vacation rental, tries to escape from a hungry shark that made it's way into the house.
tagline: If you can't run...
title: Swim
plot:
Swim is a 2021 American shark horror film produced by The Asylum and directed by Jared Cohn, from a script credited to Anthony C. Ferrante, the director of the Sharknado franchise. Its cast includes Jennifer Field, Joey Lawrence, Andy Lauer, Brett Hargrave, Daniel Grogan, Rib Hillis, Addison Bowman, David Hutchison and Trevor B. Nagle. Like several of the studio's titles, it reworks the premise of a recent hit, in this case the survival thriller Crawl, moving the confined-space threat from alligators to a shark.

Lacey Samon (Field) heads to a beach rental house for a week by the sea with her two teenage children, played by Hargrave and Grogan, continuing a family tradition begun by her father Noah (Lauer), an ailing man who relies on an oxygen tank and joins them on the trip. Her husband (Lawrence) is supposed to follow by car from San Francisco. On arrival the family discovers that badly needed repairs on the house were never finished, leaving the basement flooded just as a powerful storm rolls in. What begins as a relaxing getaway turns into a nightmare when the rising floodwater carries a hungry shark into the house. Trapped by the storm, with the water climbing and injuries slowing them down, the family must fend off the predator inside the flooded rooms, improvising weapons from household objects while trying to stay above the waterline. Noah makes a sacrifice to protect the others, and the father finally arrives late in the film to join the fight for survival.

Swim premiered on the free streaming service Tubi on 13 August 2021. Much of it was filmed in a pool and on built sets, and it was shot in a widescreen 2.39:1 format that gave it a slightly more polished look than many comparable low-budget productions. Reviews were largely negative. Knockout Horror gave it one and a half stars out of five, acknowledging the cast's commitment under waterlogged shooting conditions and the film's relatively expensive appearance but criticizing its thin script, implausible casting of family members' ages, shark effects that kept changing scale, poor lighting and visible continuity errors. Cinematic Diversions was more forgiving, rating it six out of ten as an entertaining if clumsy entry in the genre, with decent shark effects and a story that was serviceable by the standards of shark movies, though it mocked the late appearance of top-billed Lawrence.

overview: In a small town in Maine, seven children known as The Losers Club come face to face with life problems, bullies and a monster that takes the shape of a clown called Pennywise.
tagline: Your fears are unleashed
title: It
plot:
It is a 2017 American horror film directed by Andy Muschietti, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The story takes place in Derry, Maine, where a group of young outcasts must face their fears and battle an ancient evil that preys on their town every 27 years.

The film begins with a prologue set in 1958, where we see a young Bill Denbrough (Jaeden Lieberher) witnessing the murder of his younger brother, Georgie (Jack Dylan Grazer), by the monstrous entity known as Pennywise (Bill Skarsgård). This traumatic event sets the tone for the rest of the story.

The main plot follows a group of young friends who call themselves "The Losers Club": Bill, Ben Hanscom (Jeremy Ray Taylor), Beverly Marsh (Sophia Lillis), Richie Tozier (Finn Wolfhard), Mike Hanlon (Chosen Jacobs), and Eddie Kaspbrak (Jack London). They are all outsiders in their own way, struggling with personal issues and family problems.

As the story unfolds, The Losers Club discovers that Pennywise is an ancient entity that feeds on fear and terrorizes Derry every 27 years. The group decides to face their fears and work together to defeat Pennywise, who takes the form of a clown to lure its victims into his lair.

Throughout the film, each member of The Losers Club shares their personal struggles and fears with the group, which helps them bond and understand each other's strengths and weaknesses. They also uncover the dark history of Derry and the origins of Pennywise, who was once a human named Thaddeus Bowditch.

As the story progresses, The Losers Club faces various challenges and obstacles, including encounters with Pennywise in different forms. They also discover that Mike is the only member of the group who still lives in Derry as an adult, and he serves as the keeper of the group's memories and the link to their past.

The climax of the film takes place at the old sewers beneath Derry, where The Losers Club confronts Pennywise in a final showdown. Bill, who has been struggling with his own guilt and responsibility for Georgie's death, must face his fears and lead the group in a desperate bid to defeat Pennywise.

In the end, The Losers Club emerges victorious, but not without scars. They have faced their fears and overcome their personal struggles, and they have formed a bond that will last a lifetime. As the story concludes, we see Mike returning to Derry as an adult, ready to face his own demons and continue the fight against Pennywise.

The film ends on a hopeful note, with The Losers Club reunited in adulthood, ready to face whatever challenges come their way. However, it also leaves room for speculation about the future of the story, as we see Mike's son, Ben, who is now a young boy, being watched by an unseen presence - hinting that Pennywise may still be lurking in the shadows, waiting for its next victim.

Overall, It is a thrilling and emotional ride that explores themes of friendship, trauma, and the power of facing one's fears. The film features outstanding performances from the cast, particularly Bill Skarsgård as the iconic and terrifying Pennywise.

overview: A thriller set in New York City during the winter of 1981, statistically one of the most violent years in the city's history, and centered on the lives of an immigrant and his family trying to expand their business and capitalize on opportunities as the rampant violence, decay, and corruption of the day drag them in and threaten to destroy all they have built.
tagline: The result is never in question. Just the path you take to get there.
title: A Most Violent Year
plot:
A Most Violent Year is a 2014 American crime drama film directed by J.C. Chandor and written by Chuck MacLean, J.C. Chandor, and Zach Staggs. The film stars Oscar Isaac as Abel Morales, a Mexican immigrant who becomes embroiled in the world of New York City's underworld.

The film begins with Abel Morales (Oscar Isaac), a successful oil distributor who has built his business from scratch through hard work and determination. However, Abel's success is threatened when he is forced to pay a hefty sum of money to a local crime lord, Danny Nunis (David Dastmalchian), in order to maintain his business.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that Abel is not just a simple businessman, but also a complex and nuanced individual who is driven by a desire to provide for his family. He is married to Anna (Jessica Chastain), a strong-willed and independent woman who is struggling to balance her own ambitions with her role as a mother.

Abel's situation becomes increasingly precarious when he is forced to deal with the machinations of Danny Nunis, who is determined to take control of Abel's business. Meanwhile, Abel also finds himself drawn into a world of violence and corruption, where he must navigate a complex web of alliances and rivalries in order to protect his family and his business.

As the plot thickens, it becomes clear that Abel is not just fighting for survival, but also for his dignity and self-respect. He is a man who has been forced to confront the harsh realities of the world around him, and he will stop at nothing to protect himself and those he loves.

Throughout the film, Oscar Isaac delivers a powerful performance as Abel Morales, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and multifaceted character. The supporting cast, including Jessica Chastain and David Dastmalchian, also deliver strong performances that add to the overall tension and suspense of the film.

The film's climax is both intense and emotionally resonant, as Abel finds himself facing off against Danny Nunis in a violent confrontation that will determine the fate of his business and his family. In the end, Abel emerges victorious, but not without scars - both physical and emotional.

Overall, A Most Violent Year is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, community, and the human condition. With its strong performances, tense plot, and nuanced characters, it is a must-see for fans of crime dramas and anyone interested in exploring the complexities of the human experience.

overview: A criminal subculture operates among U.S. soldiers stationed in West Germany just before the fall of the Berlin wall.
tagline: War is hell... but peace is f*#!%!! boring.
title: Buffalo Soldiers
plot:
Buffalo Soldiers is a 2002 American drama film directed by Gregor Jordan. The movie explores the complex and often fraught relationship between African-American soldiers from the United States and their Mexican counterparts during the early 20th century.

At its core, Buffalo Soldiers delves into themes of racism, prejudice, and cultural clashes. The story is set against the backdrop of a tumultuous period in American history, where racial tensions were running high, both within the US military and between the US and Mexico. The film sheds light on the often-overlooked experiences of African-American soldiers who served alongside their Mexican counterparts, highlighting the difficulties they faced due to racism and xenophobia.

The movie also touches upon themes of identity, loyalty, and belonging. As the characters navigate their respective cultures and allegiances, they are forced to confront their own sense of self and where they belong in the world. The film's portrayal of these struggles is nuanced and thought-provoking, inviting viewers to consider the complexities of cultural identity and the human experience.

Furthermore, Buffalo Soldiers explores the theme of camaraderie and brotherhood among soldiers from different backgrounds, who are united by their shared experiences and challenges. Despite the tensions and conflicts that arise, the film suggests that these bonds can be powerful and transformative, allowing individuals to find a sense of belonging and purpose in the midst of adversity.

Overall, Buffalo Soldiers is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on a lesser-known chapter in American history, while also exploring universal themes of identity, loyalty, and human connection.

overview: Werner Herzog's documentary film about the "Grizzly Man" Timothy Treadwell and what the thirteen summers in a National Park in Alaska were like in one man's attempt to protect the grizzly bears. The film is full of unique images and a look into the spirit of a man who sacrificed himself for nature.
tagline: In nature, there are boundaries. One man spent the last 13 years of his life crossing them.
title: Grizzly Man
plot:
Grizzly Man is a documentary film that delves into the life of Timothy Treadwell, an American bear enthusiast who spent 13 summers in Alaska's Katmai National Park and Preserve. The film explores the complexities of human nature, particularly through the lens of Treadwell's obsession with bears.

At its core, Grizzly Man is a thought-provoking examination of the blurred lines between fascination and fixation. Treadwell's all-consuming passion for bears leads him to take risks that ultimately prove fatal. The documentary raises questions about the ethics of human-bear interactions and the consequences of playing with nature.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for meaning. Treadwell's decision to leave behind a life in civilization to live among the bears can be seen as a quest for connection and understanding with the natural world. However, this pursuit ultimately leads him down a path of self-destruction.

Furthermore, Grizzly Man is a commentary on the human tendency to romanticize and idealize nature. Treadwell's portrayal of himself as a bear whisperer and his claims of being able to communicate with the animals are both captivating and disturbing. The documentary suggests that this kind of anthropomorphism can be both alluring and destructive, highlighting the need for a more nuanced understanding of our place within the natural world.

Ultimately, Grizzly Man is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own relationship with nature and the consequences of our actions.

overview: The Simpsons host a Disney+ Day party and everyone is on the list… except Homer. With friends from across the service and music fit for a Disney Princess, Plusaversary is Springfield's event of the year.
title: The Simpsons in Plusaversary
plot:
The Simpsons in Plusaversary, or simply Plusaversary, is a 2021 American animated short film based on the television series The Simpsons, produced by Gracie Films and 20th Television Animation and directed by David Silverman. Made to celebrate the second anniversary of the streaming service Disney+, it was released on November 12, 2021, Disney+ Day, as the fifth short film in the Simpsons franchise and the third promotional short produced for the service. The story concerns a Disney+ party at Moe's Tavern to which everyone is invited except Homer.

Dan Castellaneta voices Homer Simpson along with Donald Duck, Barney Gumble and the dwarfs Happy and Grumpy, among others. Nancy Cartwright voices Bart, Yeardley Smith voices Lisa, Hank Azaria voices Moe, Goofy and Buzz Lightyear, and Tress MacNeille voices Maleficent. Dozens of characters from Disney, Pixar, Marvel and Star Wars make silent cameo appearances, among them Cinderella, Cruella de Vil, Elsa, Olaf, Mulan, Woody, WALL-E, Loki, Ant-Man, Darth Vader, BB-8 and the Mandalorian.

A crowd of characters from across these franchises queues outside Moe's Tavern, where Maleficent checks names against the guest list. Homer protests that he has been left off it, but when Goofy arrives, Homer forces Goofy to take him in as his plus-one. Inside, Darth Vader drinks a beer, Doctor Strange plays pool with Carl and Lenny, and Elsa conjures ice into a bucket being filled with beer by an enchanted broom from Fantasia. Buzz Lightyear loses an arm-wrestling match to the Mandalorian, and when Moe thinks Donald Duck is choking, Barney attempts the Heimlich maneuver on him. At a table Homer and Goofy talk while Happy grumbles that the party stinks and turns his complaints on Grumpy. Lisa arrives to take Homer home, BB-8 knocks his beer away, and Lisa lifts the mood with a song about Disney+. Afterward, the shadow of Mickey Mouse falls across the door, and the guests are thrilled that the boss has arrived, but it is only Bart in a Mickey costume, who orders everyone back to work and drags Goofy off while Barney hauls Homer away.

Reviews were mixed to positive. CinemaBlend ranked it first among the Simpsons shorts made for Disney+, praising its gags and its satire of Disney and its characters, and LaughingPlace.com enjoyed seeing the Simpsons run amok with familiar characters, while Bubbleblabber gave it five out of ten, finding it the most hands-off of the shorts.

overview: Two teen rival babysitters, Jenny and Lola, team up to hunt down one of their kids who accidentally ran away into the big city without any supervision.
title: Adventures in Babysitting
plot:
Adventures in Babysitting is a 2016 American adventure comedy television film directed by John Schultz and starring Sabrina Carpenter and Sofia Carson. A remake of the 1987 film of the same name, it premiered on Disney Channel in the United States and Canada on June 24, 2016, and holds the distinction of being the 100th Disney Channel Original Movie. The supporting cast includes Nikki Hahn, Mallory James Mahoney, Max Gecowets, Jet Jurgensmeyer, Madison Horcher and Kevin Quinn.

Jenny Parker and Lola Perez are both nineteen and share a passion for photography, but their personalities are very different, and Lola is by far the more impulsive of the two. They meet as finalists for the same photography internship and accidentally swap phones at the interview. When a professor, Helen Anderson, calls Jenny's phone in search of a last-minute babysitter, Lola takes the job, and that night Jenny looks after Emily and Katy Cooper while Lola watches the three Anderson children, Trey, Bobby and AJ. After realizing they have each other's phones, Jenny sets out to find Lola, only to discover that fourteen-year-old Trey has sneaked out to a concert. The two babysitters and the remaining children head into the city to bring him back, and a stop at a shady pawn shop goes wrong when Bobby accidentally releases a rare ferret, Lola snaps a photo of the chaos, and the owners, Tiny and Scalper, who are trafficking the animal illegally, give chase to get rid of the evidence. As the night spirals out of control, the group must find the money to recover their towed car before midnight, Lola lands in a police station for scalping a concert ticket, Jenny clashes with rebellious thirteen-year-old Emily, who has secretly dyed her hair and gotten a tattoo, and young AJ meets her roller derby idol. All the while, the two sitters must get every child home before the parents return from their party, learning to rely on each other along the way, while Jenny wonders whether she has missed her chance with her crush, Zac.

Carpenter plays Jenny and Carson plays Lola, with Kevin Quinn as Zac Chase, Gillian Vigman as Helen Anderson, Gabrielle Miller as Donna Cooper, and Michael Northey and Ken Lawson as the pawn shop crooks Tiny and Scalper. Hahn and Mahoney play the Cooper sisters, while Gecowets, Jurgensmeyer and Horcher play the Anderson siblings.

overview: An LA girl, unlucky in love, falls for an East Coast guy on a dating app and decides to surprise him for Christmas, only to discover that she's been catfished. But the object of her affection actually lives in the same town, and the guy who duped her offers to set them up if she pretends to be his own girlfriend for the holidays.
tagline: A romantic comedy about the lies we tell for love.
title: Love Hard
plot:
Love Hard is a 2021 American romantic comedy film directed by Daniel Barnz and written by Aaron Lohr. The movie stars Nina Dobrev, Jimmy O. Yang, and Damon Wayans Jr.

The main themes of Love Hard include:

1. **Self-discovery**: The protagonist, Natalie, played by Nina Dobrev, is on a journey to discover herself and figure out what she wants in life. She's recently gone through a breakup and is trying to move on, but her plans are disrupted when she meets Graham, the man she was set up with.

2. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of love, relationships, and communication. Natalie and Graham have an instant connection, but their relationship is put to the test as they navigate their differences and confront their own emotional baggage.

3. **Identity and belonging**: As Natalie travels to meet Graham in person, she's forced to confront her own identity and sense of belonging. She's struggling to find her place in the world after a recent breakup, and meeting Graham makes her question whether she's ready for love again.

4. **Friendship and support**: The movie highlights the importance of friendship and support in navigating life's challenges. Natalie's friends back home provide her with emotional support and encouragement as she navigates her relationship with Graham.

5. **Embracing imperfection**: Love Hard celebrates the beauty of imperfection and the idea that nobody is perfect. Natalie and Graham are both flawed characters who learn to accept and love each other for who they are, flaws and all.

Overall, Love Hard is a heartwarming romantic comedy that explores themes of self-discovery, love, relationships, identity, friendship, and embracing imperfection.

overview: A high school senior, Alex Lainey, has an encounter with mysterious lights that appear over her small town. She soon develops dangerous, supernatural abilities and turns to her childhood friend Sean Terrel. The authorities target them and a chase ensues as officials try to discover the truth behind Alex's transformation.
tagline: We called, they answered,  she's the proof
title: At First Light
plot:
At First Light, also titled First Light, is a 2018 Canadian science fiction thriller drama film written and directed by Jason Stone. It stars Stefanie Scott as Alex and Théodore Pellerin as Sean, with Saïd Taghmaoui as Cal, Kate Burton, James Wotherspoon and Percy Hynes White. The film premiered at South by Southwest in 2018, and after Gravitas Ventures acquired its distribution rights for the United States, Australia and New Zealand, it was released in theaters and on demand on September 28, 2018.

Seventeen-year-old Sean looks after his catatonic grandmother and his little brother. At a party he reconnects with Alex, an old friend he has long had a crush on, and writes his number on her arm. Later that night Alex goes swimming with her boyfriend and drowns, but as she sinks, mysterious lights fill the sky and the water around her. She is next seen wandering along a road, confused and unable to remember anything, and calls Sean, who takes her home, assuming she is on drugs. The next day, strange things begin to happen around her: lights flicker, knives float in the air and Sean's grandmother suddenly becomes lively and lucid again. When Sean tries to take Alex home, where her stepmother has reported her missing, she pushes him out of a second-story window and then halts their fall with her new powers. On the run together, they meet Cal, a former scientist who has tracked Alex through the electromagnetic energy she gives off. He tells them that the organization he once worked for has been sending messages into space for years and that someone, or something, has finally answered. He also warns Sean that staying close to Alex is exposing him to radiation that will eventually kill him. Torn between her feelings for Sean and the harm she is causing him, Alex sets off alone toward a vast circle of solar panels in the desert, while agents from Cal's former organization, who have discovered that she has survived far longer than anyone like her before, close in on both of them.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 50% of 14 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 49 out of 100. Chris Knight of the National Post felt that the drab screenplay did the capable actors no favors, while Kevin Crust of the Los Angeles Times gave it a positive review, praising Pellerin and Scott.

overview: Snow White's mother dies during childbirth, leaving baby Snow and father John for dead on an icy field, who then receives a visit from one of Satan's representatives, granting him three wishes.
tagline: Deception never looked so sweet
title: Snow White: The Fairest of Them All
plot:
Snow White: The Fairest of Them All is a 2001 television film that offers a unique take on the classic fairy tale, focusing on the emotional and psychological aspects of its characters. At its core, the movie explores the theme of toxic relationships and the dangers of allowing others to define one's self-worth.

The story delves into the complexities of Snow White's character, portraying her as a strong-willed and independent individual who is driven by a desire for love and acceptance. However, she also struggles with feelings of insecurity and low self-esteem, which are exacerbated by the manipulative and controlling behavior of those around her, particularly Queen Grimhilde.

The film highlights the devastating consequences of allowing others to dictate one's emotions and actions, as Snow White becomes increasingly isolated and vulnerable to the queen's schemes. This serves as a cautionary tale about the importance of self-awareness, emotional intelligence, and healthy boundaries in relationships.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of female empowerment, showcasing Snow White's growth from a timid and uncertain individual to a confident and determined heroine who ultimately finds her own path to happiness. The film suggests that true beauty and worth come from within, and that one should not rely on external validation or the opinions of others to define their self-worth.

Overall, Snow White: The Fairest of Them All is a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant retelling of the classic fairy tale, offering a nuanced exploration of complex themes and characters.

overview: A former actress trying to break into directing tests her skills with a town’s annual Christmas Eve courtroom production in which the true authorship of the famous poem “A Visit from St. Nick” is debated.
tagline: Raise the curtain. Lift your spirits.
title: 'Twas the Night Before Christmas
plot:
'Twas the Night Before Christmas is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Gary Yates, who co-wrote the screenplay with C. Jay Cox. Produced by Muse Entertainment, it stars Torrey DeVitto and Zane Holtz, with Shawn Ahmed, Amanda Barker, Tanisha Thammavongsa, Richard Waugh, Shaun Austin-Olsen, Sophie Bastelle and Jennie Esnard in supporting roles. The film premiered on the Hallmark Channel on 17 December 2022 as part of its Countdown to Christmas season, and runs 84 minutes.

Madison Rush (DeVitto), an actress eager to reinvent herself and move into directing, especially in the theatre, has co-written a play for a town's annual Christmas Eve production: a mock courtroom trial to decide the true authorship of the famous poem "A Visit from St. Nicholas", better known as "'Twas the Night Before Christmas", which is traditionally credited to Clement Clarke Moore (Austin-Olsen) but also claimed for Major Henry Livingston Jr. (Waugh). To draw audiences she recruits her friend and former co-star Connor Avery (Holtz), a charming actor who trained as a lawyer, acts to pay the bills and is a devoted father to his daughter, and who soon talks his way into the bed and breakfast where she is staying. Madison insists she does not date actors, but Connor keeps hinting that she was his favourite on-screen kiss. As the producer keeps throwing her curveballs, her co-writer has to leave for Los Angeles and the ghosts of Livingston and Moore turn up to argue their cases, Madison, who believes returning to the stage is what her late father would have wanted, struggles to hold the show together. When the troublesome lead actress, Lena (Bastelle), drops out the night before the performance, Connor and her friends help Madison see that she should play the lead herself, realising that she does not have to choose between acting and directing, and that she can date an actor after all.

TheWrap ranked it 10th of Hallmark's 43 new Christmas films of 2022, saying that although it tried to embrace many ideas, it somehow came together thanks mainly to the chemistry between DeVitto and Holtz. Erin E. Gross of Fangirlish also praised the leads' great on-screen chemistry and Madison's growth. Cassandra Morgan found it neither terrible nor good, arguing that it failed to make viewers care about the couple, the lead actress or the authorship mystery, which ended without a real resolution.

overview: Chasing his dream to join an elite K-9 unit, a state trooper partners with a fellow underdog: clever but naughty shelter pup Ruby. Based on a true story.
title: Rescued by Ruby
plot:

overview: Ruka is a young girl whose parents are separated and whose father works in an aquarium. When two boys, Umi and Sora, who were raised in the sea by dugongs, are brought to the aquarium, Ruka feels drawn to them and begins to realize that she has the same sort of supernatural connection to the ocean that they do. Umi and Sora's special power seems to be connected to strange events that have been occurring more and more frequently, such as the appearance of sea creatures far from their home territory and the disappearance of aquarium animals around the world. However, the exact nature of the boys' power and of the abnormal events is unknown, and Ruka gets drawn into investigating the mystery that surrounds her new friends.
title: Children of the Sea
plot:
Children of the Sea is a 2019 Japanese science fiction film directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi. The movie tells the story of a widowed father, Taka, who takes his young daughter, Mirai, on a journey to the ocean to help her cope with the loss of her mother.

The main theme of Children of the Sea is the healing power of nature and the importance of human connection in the face of grief. The film explores the complex emotions of Taka as he navigates his own grief while trying to support Mirai through hers. Through their journey, the movie highlights the transformative impact of shared experiences and the ocean's ability to evoke feelings of wonder, awe, and introspection.

The film also delves into the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Taka's relationship with his daughter serves as a catalyst for him to re-examine his own sense of self and find new meaning in life after the loss of his partner. The movie suggests that it is through these connections with others, particularly those who are vulnerable and dependent on us, that we can discover our true purpose and find healing.

Furthermore, Children of the Sea touches on the idea of letting go and embracing change. As Taka and Mirai navigate their journey, they must confront the reality of Mirai's mother passing away and come to terms with the fact that she will never return. The film encourages viewers to accept this loss and find a way to move forward, even in the face of uncertainty.

Overall, Children of the Sea is a poignant and contemplative film that explores the complexities of human emotions and relationships through the lens of nature's transformative power.

overview: France, 17th century, under the reign of Louis XIII. Dogtanian is an impetuous and innocent peasant from Gascony, as well as a skilled swordsman, who travels to Paris with the purpose of making his dream come true: to join the Corps of Muskehounds of the Royal Guard.
tagline: One for all and all for one!
title: Dogtanian and the Three Muskehounds
plot:
Dogtanian and the Three Muskehounds (Spanish: D'Artacán y los tres mosqueperros), released in North America as The Dog Knight, is a 2021 Spanish-Indian animated adventure comedy film directed by Toni García and written by Doug Langdale. It is based on the 1981 Spanish-Japanese television series of the same name, itself adapted from Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel about d'Artagnan and the Three Musketeers, and was produced by Apolo Films, the cinema studio of BRB Internacional, together with the Indian company Cosmos Maya. The original Spanish voice cast includes Miguel Ángel Pérez as Dogtanian, Ana Esther Alborg as Juliette, Ana María Marí as Milady de Winter, Luis Bajo as Count Rochefort and Carlos Kaniowsky as Treville.

Dogtanian, a young and eager swordsman, travels to Paris dreaming of joining the legendary Muskehounds. At their headquarters, Monsieur de Treville tells him that his father was framed by Cardinal Richelieu and judges him unfit to become a Muskehound. Shortly afterwards Dogtanian accidentally runs into each of the three Muskehounds in turn and ends up challenged to duels with all of them, but when the Cardinal's guards interrupt and a fight breaks out, his courage wins the three over. One night he rescues Juliette, a young lady he has met, from the Cardinal's men, and she reveals that Richelieu is plotting to start a war between France and England so that he can seize power across Europe. Queen Anne of Austria plans to send a letter to the King of England to secure peace, together with a diamond necklace given to her by King Louis, and if the Cardinal's agents steal the necklace, war could follow. Remembering a conversation he overheard between Richelieu's spy, Count Rochefort, and the cunning Milady de Winter, Dogtanian joins the Muskehounds in a race to Calais to stop Milady before she can escape across the Channel. Along the way he enlists the help of a pirate, Captain Bloodhound, and must prove his skill with the sword while also seeking the truth about the plot that disgraced his father.

On Rotten Tomatoes, four of seven critics' reviews of the film are positive. A television series continuing the story after the events of the film, titled Dogtanian, The Hero, was reported to be in development, though no further news about it has emerged.

overview: Two boys find a fugitive hiding out on an island in the Mississippi River and form a pact to help him reunite with his lover and escape.
tagline: Running from his past. Hiding from the law. Only one way out.
title: Mud
plot:
Mud is a 2012 American drama film directed by Jeff Nichols, not 2013. It was released on April 19, 2012.

The main themes of Mud are:

1. **Coming of Age**: The story revolves around two young boys, Ellis and Neckbone, who embark on an adventure to find the mysterious and charismatic figure known as "Mud." As they navigate their way through the challenges of growing up, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and the complexities of human relationships.
2. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Mud is a character who has been left behind by society, living on a remote island in the Mississippi River. His story highlights the struggles of those who feel disconnected from the world around them, and the difficulties of forming meaningful connections with others.
3. **Redemption and Forgiveness**: Throughout the film, Ellis and Neckbone grapple with their own personal demons, including family conflicts and past traumas. As they try to find Mud, they also confront their own emotional baggage and learn to forgive themselves and others.
4. **The Power of Human Connection**: Despite being a recluse, Mud forms strong bonds with the two boys, teaching them about the importance of human connection and the value of relationships in our lives.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, creating a poignant and thought-provoking story that explores the complexities of human nature and the challenges of growing up.

overview: After a series of tragedies including the death of his father-in-law, Robert and his wife Maia leave their home in London to move back to her childhood home. But when Robert discovers an old portrait in the attic of a man who is his spitting image, he goes down a rabbit hole to discover the identity of this mysterious doppelganger known only as the visitor. It isn’t long until he realizes – where the visitor goes, death follows.
tagline: Where he goes, death follows.
title: The Visitor
plot:
The Visitor is a 2022 American psychological horror film directed by Justin P. Lange from a screenplay by Adam Mason and Simon Boyes. Finn Jones stars as Robert Burrows, an Englishman who moves to the American South with his wife, Maia, played by Jessica McNamee, and the cast also includes Dane Rhodes as Joseph Ellis, Donna Biscoe as Margaret Delacroix and Thomas Francis Murphy as Maxwell Braun. It was produced for television through a deal between Blumhouse Television and Epix, with Jason Blum as an executive producer.

Robert, an affable, polite and somewhat oblivious Londoner, travels with Maia to her childhood home in a small Southern town, where the couple hope to settle down and start a family. When Maia takes him to a local bar in her old stomping ground, the residents gravitate toward him and greet him with unusual warmth, almost as though they have been waiting years for his arrival. Robert cannot tell whether the welcome is simply sentimental or hides a darker purpose.

More alarming is a discovery in the house: an old portrait, found in the attic, of a man sitting in an armchair who bears an uncanny resemblance to Robert. Disturbed by the likeness and by frightening dreams, including one in which a blind ghostly figure screams in his face, he sets out to learn the true identity of his mysterious doppelgänger. His search takes him down a frightening rabbit hole into the history of Maia's family and the town, with small clues scattered along the way, until he realizes that every family has its own terrifying secrets and uncovers how he is connected to the man in the painting.

The project was announced in October 2021 as part of Blumhouse Television and Epix's slate of television films. The film, which runs about 80 minutes, was released digitally in the United States by Epix and Paramount Home Entertainment on October 7, 2022. Reviews were largely negative, and the film holds a low rating on Rotten Tomatoes, where only a small minority of critics' reviews are positive. Andy Crump of Paste praised Jones as an unexpectedly believable everyman, as well as Lange's careful, sometimes painterly craftsmanship and an effectively staged early dream sequence, but felt that the screenplay arrived at a thuddingly routine destination and that the late revelation of the mystery was a letdown. Other critics similarly found it atmospheric but generic, relying on familiar small-town horror tropes and a twist that comes too late.

overview: After narrowly surviving a massive heart attack, Randal enlists his old friend Dante to help him make a movie immortalizing their youthful days at the little convenience store that started it all.
tagline: They're too old for this shift.
title: Clerks III
plot:
Clerks III is a 2022 American comedy film directed by Kevin Smith and written by Jeff Anderson and Kevin Smith. The movie takes place 20 years after the events of Clerks II.

The story begins with Dante Hicks (Brian O'Halloran), who has just been fired from his job at the Quick Stop convenience store, which is now owned by Randal Graves (Jeff Anderson). Dante is struggling to find a new job and is feeling unfulfilled in life. He decides to take a road trip with his friend Jay (Jason Mewes) to visit their old friend Silent Bob (Kevin Smith), who has just been released from prison.

Upon arrival, they discover that Silent Bob has become a successful businessman and is now the owner of a chain of convenience stores called "Silent Bob's." However, things take a turn when Dante discovers that Randal has been embezzling money from the Quick Stop and has used it to fund his own business ventures.

As Dante navigates this new reality, he also reconnects with other old friends, including Mallory (Jennifer Schwalbach Smith), who is now married to Jay. The group spends their days hanging out at Silent Bob's convenience store, discussing life, love, and everything in between.

Throughout the movie, Kevin Smith pays homage to his previous films, including Clerks II and Mallrats. He also explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and finding one's purpose in life. The film features a mix of humor, heart, and pop culture references that are characteristic of Smith's style.

One of the standout aspects of Clerks III is its cast, which includes many familiar faces from Smith's previous films. The chemistry between the actors is undeniable, and their performances bring depth and nuance to the story.

The movie also features a number of cameos, including appearances by Jason Lee, Ben Affleck, and Marilyn Manson, among others. These cameos add to the film's humor and charm, and help to reinforce its connection to Smith's previous work.

Ultimately, Clerks III is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of friendship and finding one's place in the world. The movie is full of laughs, pop culture references, and memorable moments that will leave audiences smiling long after the credits roll.

overview: Before Alice went to Wonderland, and before Peter became Pan, they were brother and sister. When their eldest brother dies in a tragic accident, they each seek to save their parents from their downward spirals of despair until finally they are forced to choose between home and imagination, setting the stage for their iconic journeys into Wonderland and Neverland.
tagline: A story about courage, wonder and never growing old.
title: Come Away
plot:
Come Away is a 2020 fantasy drama film that tells the story of the origins of Peter Pan and the Darling children. The movie delves into the complexities of family dynamics, particularly the relationships between parents and children.

At its core, Come Away explores the theme of the struggle for power and control within families. The character of Mother (played by Nicole Kidman) is a complex figure who embodies both nurturing and authoritarian qualities, reflecting the push-and-pull nature of motherhood. Her relationship with her children, particularly Peter (played by Harris Dickinson), is fraught with tension as she navigates the challenges of raising them in a world that seems determined to hold them back.

The film also touches on the theme of imagination and its role in shaping our experiences and perceptions of reality. The Darling children's adventures in Neverland serve as a metaphor for the power of imagination to transcend the mundane and tap into the magic of childhood. Through their journey, the characters learn to harness the transformative potential of imagination, finding freedom and empowerment in the process.

Furthermore, Come Away grapples with the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Peter's struggles to find his place within his family and society serve as a catalyst for his growth and self-discovery. His journey is one of self-actualization, as he learns to navigate the complexities of adulthood while holding onto the essence of his childhood imagination.

Overall, Come Away offers a nuanced exploration of the human experience, delving into the intricate web of relationships that shape our lives and the power of imagination to transform and transcend them.

overview: Barents Sea, August 12th, 2000. During a Russian naval exercise, and after suffering a serious accident, the K-141 Kursk submarine sinks with 118 crew members on board. While the few sailors who are still alive barely manage to survive, their families push for accurate information and a British officer struggles to obtain from the Russian government a permit to attempt a rescue before it is late. But general incompetence are against all their efforts.
tagline: Together till the end
title: Kursk
plot:
Kursk is a 2018 war drama film directed by Thomas Vinterberg, not produced by Belga Productions. The movie is based on the true story of the Russian submarine K-141 Kursk that sank in 2000 during a naval exercise.

The main themes of Kursk revolve around the psychological and emotional toll of war on its characters, particularly the crew members who are trapped inside the sinking submarine. The film explores the claustrophobic and desperate situation of the sailors as they struggle to survive against all odds.

As the story unfolds, the audience is taken through a journey of human emotions, from fear and panic to despair and ultimately, hope. The characters' relationships with each other become crucial in their survival, as they rely on each other for support and comfort in the face of unimaginable danger.

The film also delves into the themes of sacrifice, duty, and loyalty, highlighting the bravery and selflessness of the sailors who risked their lives to save others. The movie's portrayal of these themes is both poignant and powerful, making it a gripping and emotional watch.

Overall, Kursk is a thought-provoking film that sheds light on the human side of war, emphasizing the importance of camaraderie, resilience, and the unbreakable bonds between people in the face of adversity.

overview: Laura and Massimo are back and hotter than ever. But the reunited couple's new beginning is complicated by Massimo’s family ties and a mysterious man who enters Laura’s life to win her heart and trust, at any cost.
tagline: Oh Yes.
title: 365 Days: This Day
plot:
365 Days: This Day (Polish: 365 dni: Ten dzień) is a Polish erotic drama of 2022 directed by Barbara Białowąs and Tomasz Mandes. The sequel to 365 Days, it adapts This Day, the second novel in Blanka Lipińska's trilogy, and stars Anna-Maria Sieklucka as Laura, Michele Morrone in the dual role of the mafia boss Massimo Torricelli and his twin brother Adriano, Simone Susinna as Nacho, Magdalena Lamparska as Olga and Otar Saralidze as Domenico.

The story opens with Laura marrying Massimo. Having lost their baby in the accident at the end of the previous film, she confides the miscarriage only to her best friend Olga, the only person from her side invited to the Italian wedding, since Massimo fears that her family would discover his criminal life. On returning from their honeymoon the couple catch Olga with Massimo's right-hand man Domenico. Married life soon turns sour: Laura is bored and lonely with nothing to do while Massimo is busy with his business, the two argue daily, and she grows drawn to Nacho, the gardener. At a party she believes she sees Massimo having sex with his former lover Anna, and in her heartbreak she flees with Nacho to an island, where she begins to enjoy a new life while Massimo hunts for her.

Nacho eventually reveals that his father leads a mafia family that rivals Massimo's, and the old man favours Adriano, Massimo's unstable and estranged twin, to take over the Sicilian clan. Laura learns that the man she saw with Anna was in fact Adriano, who now holds her captive. Massimo and Nacho, long rivals, join forces to rescue her, but she is shot by Anna and Adriano before the two men kill them, and the film ends with Laura in Massimo's arms, her fate unresolved.

Principal photography took place in Italy and Poland in 2021 after pandemic delays. Released on Netflix on 27 April 2022, the film was savaged by critics, scoring 0% on Rotten Tomatoes and 8 out of 100 on Metacritic; Variety's Jessica Kiang called it piping hot trash. A further sequel, The Next 365 Days, followed in August 2022.

overview: A parolee becomes the target of a massive police manhunt after inadvertently picking up a rental car with a female whistleblower tied up in the trunk. Now, as the police attempt to silence the woman before she can testify about the city's rampant corruption, the ex-con who just regained his freedom must defend her life, and clear his own name.
tagline: Wrong place. Wrong time. Wrong car.
title: Vehicle 19
plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "Vehicle 19" released in 2013 or produced by K5 International. 

However, I found that there is a 2014 film called "Vehicle 19" directed by David Hackl and produced by K5 Entertainment (not K5 International).

overview: Two young women terrorized by a group of small town psychos seek revenge on their tormentors.
tagline: Revenge can be a bitch.
title: Even Lambs Have Teeth
plot:
Even Lambs Have Teeth is a Canadian-French rape-and-revenge thriller of 2015 written and directed by Terry Miles. It stars Kirsten Prout as Sloan and Tiera Skovbye as Katie, two young women who strike back at the trafficking ring that abducted them, with Garrett Black, Jameson Parker, Darren Mann, Michael Karl Richards, Patrick Gilmore as Boris and Craig March as the local sheriff.

Fresh out of college, Katie and Sloan plan to spend a month working on a rural organic farm before a trip to New York City. Katie's uncle, an FBI agent, sees them off at the bus station and asks for a coded text message each day to prove they are safe. While they wait, two charming young men, Lucas and Jed, offer them a lift to the farm; Sloan talks a reluctant Katie into accepting. Instead the boys detour to Jed's family home, where their mother serves the girls drugged food. They wake in their underwear, chained inside storage containers in the woods, prisoners of a sex-exploitation ring run by Boris, and are assaulted by the sheriff and other local men. Boris uses Katie's phone to send a reassuring message, unaware that the code must change daily.

Sensing that something is wrong, the uncle drives to the town. The sheriff tries to calm him and then warns Boris, who orders Jed to get rid of the girls. A restaurant worker, however, remembers seeing them leave in a blue truck, and the uncle traces it to Boris. Meanwhile Katie kills one of their abusers by biting into his throat, takes his keys and frees Sloan, and the pair escape in the sheriff's own patrol car. After arming themselves at a hardware store, they ambush Boris at home, force him to name his accomplices and kill him, then hunt down the rest of the ring one by one in increasingly inventive ways. Later, as the friends finally leave for New York, the uncle assures Katie's mother that they will be fine, while at the airport a stranger with an organic-farm sign greets a new pair of young travellers.

The film premiered at the Mile High Horror Film Festival in October 2015 and was later released on DVD and on demand. Bloody Disgusting's Patrick Cooper praised its balance of human horror, dark comedy and violent revenge.

overview: Found inside a shining stalk of bamboo by an old bamboo cutter and his wife, a tiny girl grows rapidly into an exquisite young lady. The mysterious young princess enthrals all who encounter her. But, ultimately, she must confront her fate, the punishment for her crime.
tagline: A princess's crime and punishment.
title: The Tale of The Princess Kaguya
plot:
The Tale of The Princess Kaguya is a 2013 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Isao Takahata, produced by Studio Ghibli and Toho. 

The main themes of The Tale of The Princess Kaguya revolve around the complexities of human relationships, the struggle for identity, and the consequences of one's actions.

At its core, the story revolves around the life of Princess Kaguya, a young girl discovered as a baby inside a bamboo stalk. As she grows up in the imperial palace, she is surrounded by luxury and privilege but struggles to find her place within the strict rules and expectations of court life. Her journey is marked by a series of events that test her resolve and force her to confront the harsh realities of adulthood.

One of the primary themes explored in The Tale of The Princess Kaguya is the struggle for identity. As Kaguya navigates her new surroundings, she grapples with the conflicting desires of her own heart and the expectations placed upon her by others. Her relationships with those around her, particularly Prince Ayakashi and the Emperor, serve as catalysts for her growth and self-discovery.

Another significant theme is the consequences of one's actions. Throughout the film, Kaguya faces numerous challenges that force her to make difficult choices and confront the repercussions of her decisions. These events shape her into a strong-willed and compassionate individual who ultimately finds her own path in life.

The film also touches on the idea of the human condition, exploring universal themes such as love, loss, and the search for belonging. The Tale of The Princess Kaguya is a poignant and thought-provoking tale that invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences and emotions.

Overall, The Tale of The Princess Kaguya is a beautifully crafted film that explores complex themes with nuance and sensitivity. Its rich storytelling and memorable characters make it a timeless classic in the world of animation.

overview: Isabella runs her own salon and isn’t afraid to speak her mind, while Prince Thomas runs his own country and is about to marry for duty rather than love. When Izzy and her fellow stylists get the opportunity of a lifetime to do the hair for the royal wedding, she and Prince Thomas learn that taking control of their own destiny requires following their hearts.
title: The Royal Treatment
plot:
The Royal Treatment is a 2022 American romance film directed by Rick Jacobson and written by Holly Hester. It stars Laura Marano and Mena Massoud, and apart from them and a few other actors, most of the cast is from New Zealand, where it was filmed. Released on Netflix on January 20, 2022, it became the streaming service's most-watched film that week.

Isabella, known as Izzy, is a hairdresser who runs a salon in Manhattan. When a fire caused by a faulty microwave damages the salon, the landlord's assistant, Doug, insists that she pay for the repairs, and Izzy has to give up the money she had been saving to travel the world. Meanwhile Prince Thomas of the kingdom of Lavania, visiting New York, asks his assistant Walter to book him a haircut, and Walter mistakenly calls Izzy's salon. Izzy agrees to cut the prince's hair for $500, but she walks out halfway through after seeing how badly a housekeeper is treated. Intrigued, Thomas comes to the salon to have his haircut finished, and the two spend a fun night together walking through the city. Soon afterwards, Thomas's fiancée Lauren and her mother hire Izzy and her coworkers to do hair and makeup for the royal wedding, and the team travels to Lavania for a $50,000 fee. At the castle, a strict royal assistant, Madam Fabre, tests the team's skills, and Izzy impresses her by transforming a manservant. She explores the kingdom with Thomas, including a poor district the royal family considers dangerous, and inspires local people to donate gifts for underprivileged children, encouraging Thomas to do more for his people. As their friendship deepens, Lauren's mother notices that the two are growing too close, and Thomas learns that his arranged marriage is tied to the royal family's financial troubles, leaving him to decide between duty and love.

The Royal Treatment received negative reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, 35% of 17 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 36 out of 100, although Courtney Howard of Variety gave it a positive review, writing that it infuses expected genre trappings with unexpected delights.

overview: An ex-cop turned con threatens to jump to his death from a Manhattan hotel rooftop. The NYPD dispatch a female police psychologist to talk him down. However, unbeknownst to the police on the scene, the suicide attempt is a cover for the biggest diamond heist ever pulled.
tagline: You can only push an innocent man so far
title: Man on a Ledge
plot:
Man on a Ledge is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by Chris Cayille and starring Sam Worthington, Elizabeth Banks, and Anthony Mackie. The movie follows the story of Nick Cassidy (Worthington), a former FBI hostage negotiator who has lost his job after being involved in a scandal.

The plot begins with Nick Cassidy, who is now working as a security consultant for a private company called "The Company". He is hired to guard a high-rise building in New York City. However, things take a turn when Nick's estranged brother, Pete (Mackie), calls him and tells him that their father has been murdered by the same people who killed their mother.

Nick's brother Pete is being held captive by the same group of terrorists who killed their family, and he wants Nick to rescue him. However, Nick knows that if he tries to escape from his job at The Company, he will be arrested and charged with treason. He also knows that the FBI has been monitoring his activities, and they are not going to let him go.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Company is actually a front for a group of terrorists who are planning to take over the United States government. Nick's brother Pete is being held captive in a high-rise building in New York City, and Nick must use his skills as a hostage negotiator to rescue him without getting caught.

The plot thickens when it becomes clear that The Company has infiltrated the FBI, and Nick's former boss, Agent Harris (Anthony Mackie), is actually working for them. This creates a moral dilemma for Nick, who must decide whether to follow his orders or do what he thinks is right.

As the story reaches its climax, Nick uses his skills as a hostage negotiator to rescue his brother Pete from the high-rise building. However, in doing so, he also puts himself at risk of being caught by The Company and the FBI. In the end, Nick manages to escape from The Company's clutches and clear his name.

The movie ends with Nick reflecting on the events that have transpired, and realizing that he has been given a second chance to make things right. He is seen walking away from the high-rise building, symbolizing his newfound freedom and determination to start anew.

Overall, Man on a Ledge is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption. The movie features impressive stunts and suspenseful plot twists, making it a thrilling ride for audiences.

overview: In this grisly remake of the 2002 horror hit, five college chums rent an isolated woodland cabin for a party. But their fun quickly ends when the group is exposed to a hideous flesh-eating virus, and survival becomes the name of the game.
tagline: You can't run from what's inside.
title: Cabin Fever
plot:
Cabin Fever (2016) is a horror-comedy film that explores several themes, including social isolation, paranoia, and the breakdown of human relationships under pressure.

The movie takes place in a remote cabin where a group of friends, all with different personalities and quirks, are brought together by their mutual desire for a relaxing getaway. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each character has their own secrets and insecurities, which slowly start to surface, leading to a descent into chaos.

As the characters' behavior becomes increasingly erratic and paranoid, the film highlights the dangers of unchecked emotions and the devastating consequences of allowing personal demons to consume one's relationships. The movie also touches on the theme of social hierarchy, as the characters' initial camaraderie gives way to a struggle for dominance and power.

Throughout the film, the tension builds as the characters' behavior becomes more erratic, leading to a climax that is both shocking and thought-provoking. Ultimately, Cabin Fever (2016) is a commentary on how quickly social norms can break down in the face of adversity, revealing the darker aspects of human nature.

The film's tone is often described as darkly comedic, with a touch of satire, which adds to its unique charm and makes it a standout in the horror-comedy genre.

overview: Dave Skylark and his producer Aaron Rapaport run the celebrity tabloid show "Skylark Tonight". When they land an interview with a surprise fan, North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un, they are recruited by the CIA to turn their trip to Pyongyang into an assassination mission.
tagline: The Film Hackers Tried To Get Banned
title: The Interview
plot:
The Interview is a 2014 American action comedy film directed by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg, starring Seth Rogen, James Franco, Randall Park, and Diana Krall. The movie was released on December 25, 2014.

In the beginning of the film, we are introduced to two friends, Dave (Seth Rogen) and his friend Cheech (James Franco), who work as freelance journalists in New York City. They receive an offer from a South Korean news organization to interview the country's leader, Kim Jong-un (Randall Park). The story takes a turn when they learn that the North Korean government has discovered their true intentions - to write a scathing review of Kim Jong-un.

Dave and Cheech are recruited by the CIA to assassinate Kim Jong-un. They are given a special mission: to infiltrate North Korea, find Kim's location, and kill him using a virus that will make his computer system crash. The plan is to do this while pretending to be a pair of tourists visiting Pyongyang.

The plot development begins as Dave and Cheech travel to North Korea, where they encounter various obstacles, including the country's strict laws and surveillance. They are forced to wear ridiculous disguises and pretend to be enthusiastic fans of Kim Jong-un's regime. However, things take a turn when they meet Hana (Diana Krall), a beautiful and charming North Korean singer who becomes Dave's love interest.

As Dave and Cheech navigate the complexities of North Korea, they begin to question their mission and the true intentions of the CIA. They also start to develop feelings for each other, which adds an extra layer of complexity to their relationship.

The climax of the film takes place when Dave and Cheech finally reach Kim Jong-un's location, but things don't go as planned. The virus they were given doesn't work, and they are forced to improvise a plan to assassinate Kim. In the end, they succeed in killing him, but not before he reveals that he has been playing them all along.

The ending of the film is a commentary on the absurdity of war and politics. Dave and Cheech's mission was never about actually killing Kim Jong-un, but rather about exposing his regime to the world. The film ends with the two friends returning home, where they are greeted as heroes for their bravery. However, the audience knows that the true hero is Hana, who has been working behind the scenes to undermine Kim's regime.

Overall, The Interview is a satirical comedy that pokes fun at politics and war. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it was a commercial success and has become a cult classic among fans of action comedies.

overview: A con man and a would-be filmmaking crew force themselves into the lives of two grief-scarred young women. But nothing is as it seems.
tagline: Is it love or is it a lie?
title: The Forest of Love
plot:
The Forest of Love (Japanese: 愛なき森で叫べ, Ainaki Mori de Sakebe) is a Japanese crime thriller written and directed by Sion Sono, inspired by the murders, torture and extortion carried out in Kyushu from the mid-1990s by the serial killer Futoshi Matsunaga. It stars Kippei Shiina as the con man Joe Murata, Shinnosuke Mitsushima as Shin, Eri Kamataki as Mitsuko, Kyoko Hinami as Taeko, Young Dais as Jay and Yuzuka Nakaya as Mitsuko's sister Ami.

Two aspiring filmmakers, Jay and Fukami, befriend the shy Shin and introduce him to Taeko, who sets him up with her sheltered classmate Mitsuko. Years earlier the two women had been part of a group of schoolgirls who, after a friend named Eiko died in a car accident, jumped from their school roof; Mitsuko alone held back, while Taeko survived with a limp and a scar. Murata now resurfaces in Mitsuko's life, claiming he wants to repay fifty yen she once lent him, and woos her with a sports car. Mitsuko and Taeko recognise him as a swindler who once deceived Mitsuko's sister and Taeko's mother, yet he seduces Mitsuko, Ami and Taeko alike and leaves them scarred and burned.

Pretending to be rich, Murata offers to back the young men's film about his cons and then seizes control of it, revelling in cruelty. He coaches Mitsuko into strangling Jay on camera and has the body destroyed, and Taeko is shot dead by an unseen gunman while trying to escape. Using Jay's death, Murata blackmails and tortures Mitsuko's parents while Ami eagerly joins in, and a series of deaths engulfs the family. In a forest, Mitsuko confesses that she secretly hoped Murata and Shin would kill her sister, parents and Taeko. Shin shoots Mitsuko and Ami and reveals himself as the serial killer in the news; Murata escapes in a car driven by a woman resembling Eiko, while Shin pursues a vision of Eiko into the trees.

First screened in Tokyo in June 2019, the film was released on Netflix on 11 October 2019, followed in 2020 by a seven-episode extended cut, The Forest of Love: Deep Cut. Critics found it excessive and overlong but compelling; IndieWire's David Ehrlich praised Sono's feral energy, and Rotten Tomatoes reviews were positive.

overview: A bank robber tries to turn himself in because he's falling in love and wants to live an honest life...but when he realizes the Feds are more corrupt than him, he must fight back to clear his name.
tagline: Never steal a man's second chance.
title: Honest Thief
plot:
Honest Thief is a 2020 American action comedy film directed by Mark Williams Jardine and written by Chris Bremner. The movie stars Will Poulter, Lily Collins, and Damson Idris.

The story begins with Nick (Will Poulter), an ex-con who has just been released from prison after serving time for a string of high-profile art thefts. Despite his tough exterior, Nick is haunted by the memories of his past and struggles to find work or connect with people. He lives in a small apartment and spends most of his days sleeping on the couch.

One day, Nick receives an offer from a wealthy collector, Frank Cook (Damson Idris), who wants him to steal a valuable painting from a museum in Los Angeles. The catch is that the painting belongs to Frank's estranged father, and stealing it would be a betrayal of his family's trust.

Despite his reservations, Nick agrees to take on the job, hoping to earn enough money to pay off his debts and start fresh. As he plans the heist, Nick begins to develop feelings for Frank's sister, Emma (Lily Collins), who is working as a museum curator.

As the day of the heist approaches, Nick becomes increasingly anxious about the risks involved. He knows that if he gets caught, he'll be sent back to prison and lose his chance at redemption. Meanwhile, Frank becomes suspicious of Nick's intentions and starts to investigate him.

On the night of the heist, Nick successfully steals the painting, but things don't go according to plan. Emma discovers his true identity and confronts him about his past mistakes. Despite this, she chooses to believe in Nick and help him escape from the museum.

As they make their way through the city, Nick and Emma form a bond, and Nick begins to open up about his past traumas. Frank, however, is hot on their heels, determined to catch Nick and reclaim the stolen painting.

The movie culminates in an action-packed chase sequence as Nick, Emma, and Frank engage in a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. In the end, Nick manages to outsmart Frank and return the painting, but not before revealing his true identity and confessing his past mistakes.

As the dust settles, Nick and Emma share a moment of intimacy, suggesting that they may have found love amidst the chaos. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Nick finally finding redemption and a chance to start anew.

Overall, Honest Thief is a tense and entertaining thriller that explores themes of redemption, trust, and the power of human connection. Will Poulter delivers a standout performance as the complex and troubled Nick, while Lily Collins shines as the compassionate and understanding Emma.

overview: A bullied young boy befriends a young female vampire who lives in secrecy with her guardian.  A remake of the movie “Let The Right One In” which was an adaptation of a book.
tagline: Innocence dies. Abby doesn't.
title: Let Me In
plot:
Let Me In is a 2010 American vampire horror film directed by Matt Reeves, based on the Swedish novel of the same name by John Ajvide Lindqvist. The movie stars Chloe Moretz as Abby, a young girl who befriends a vampire named Vicky (played by Mia Wasikowska).

The main themes of Let Me In include:

1. **Isolation and Loneliness**: Both Abby and Vicky are outcasts in their respective communities, struggling to find acceptance and belonging. Their friendship serves as a source of comfort and companionship for each other.
2. **Vulnerability and Empowerment**: As the story progresses, Abby learns to assert herself and take control of her life, while Vicky's character evolves from a passive victim to a more proactive force in her own right.
3. **The Struggle between Human and Monster**: The film explores the tension between human nature and the monstrous aspects that can emerge within us all. Vicky's transformation serves as a metaphor for the darkness that can lurk beneath the surface of seemingly ordinary people.
4. **Coming-of-Age and Self-Discovery**: Through her relationship with Vicky, Abby navigates the challenges of adolescence, including first love, peer pressure, and self-discovery.
5. **The Dangers of Isolation and the Importance of Human Connection**: The movie highlights the risks of isolating oneself from others and the importance of forming meaningful relationships in order to find happiness and fulfillment.

Overall, Let Me In is a thought-provoking exploration of complex themes that resonate with audiences of all ages.

overview: Two lighthouse keepers try to maintain their sanity while living on a remote and mysterious New England island in the 1890s.
tagline: There is enchantment in the light.
title: The Lighthouse
plot:
The Lighthouse is a 2019 film directed and produced by Robert Eggers from a screenplay he wrote with his brother Max Eggers. It stars Robert Pattinson as a young lighthouse keeper calling himself Ephraim Winslow and Willem Dafoe as his superior, Thomas Wake, two tormented men stranded on a remote New England outpost by a violent storm. The project grew out of Max's script based on Edgar Allan Poe's unfinished story "The Light-House", and Eggers shaped the plot from a nineteenth-century legend about an accident at a Welsh lighthouse.

In the 1890s, Winslow arrives for a four-week stint as a "wickie" on an isolated island under Wake, a former sailor. He finds a small scrimshaw carving of a mermaid and keeps it. The domineering Wake assigns him the hardest labor while forbidding him to enter the lantern room, where Winslow sees him undress before the light each night. Winslow begins to have visions of sea creatures, is harassed by a one-eyed gull that Wake warns him not to harm, since gulls are said to hold the souls of dead sailors, and learns that his predecessor went mad. On the eve of his departure, he finds a dead gull fouling the cistern and beats the one-eyed gull to death. The wind turns, a fierce storm prevents the tender from relieving them, and the two men drink heavily as Winslow sees a mermaid on the shore.

Cut off for what Wake insists has been weeks, they veer between camaraderie and violence. Winslow fails to steal the lantern keys and glimpses the head of the previous keeper in a lobster trap. Drunk, he confesses that he is really Thomas Howard, who took the name of a cruel foreman he let drown during a log drive. Howard's attempt to flee in the dory ends when Wake smashes the boat with an axe, later blaming Howard. After the alcohol runs out, they drink turpentine. Reading Wake's logbook, which recommends he be dismissed without pay, Howard attacks him amid hallucinations, forces him into a grave, and takes the keys, then kills him when Wake strikes back. Climbing to the lamp, Howard stares into the lens, screams and tumbles down the stairs, and is last seen lying naked on the rocks as gulls devour him.

Shot in Nova Scotia in 2018, the film premiered at Cannes in the Directors' Fortnight in May 2019 and was released by A24 on October 18, 2019, grossing $18.3 million. Critics acclaimed Eggers's filmmaking and the two leads, giving it 90% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 83.

overview: Rhode Island State Trooper Charlie Baileygates has a multiple personality disorder. One personality is crazy and aggressive, while the other is more friendly and laid back. Both of these personalities fall in love with the same woman named Irene after Charlie loses his medication.
tagline: From gentle to mental.
title: Me, Myself & Irene
plot:
Me, Myself & Irene is a 2000 American black comedy film directed by the Farrelly brothers, written by Bobby Moresco and Peter Farrelly, and starring Jim Carrey. The movie was produced by 20th Century Fox.

The story revolves around Charlie McMillan (played by Jim Carrey), a state trooper who suffers from multiple personality disorder (MPD). He has two distinct personalities: Charlie McMillan, the mild-mannered and responsible police officer, and Hank Evans, a rough-around-the-edges, hot-headed, and violent individual.

The movie begins with Charlie's arrest for drunk driving. During his arrest, he is taken to a psychiatric hospital, where he meets Dr. Lillian Hurst (played by Renée Zellweger), a psychiatrist who specializes in treating MPD patients. She agrees to help Charlie manage his condition, and they begin therapy sessions together.

As the story progresses, we see glimpses of both personalities, with Hank's aggressive behavior causing trouble for Charlie at work and home. However, when a young woman named Irene (played by Renée Zellweger) is kidnapped by a group of armed robbers, Charlie must use his unique skills to track them down.

As the investigation unfolds, we see more of Charlie's dual personality, with Hank taking over in situations that require aggression and violence. Meanwhile, Dr. Hurst tries to help Charlie understand and control his condition, while also developing feelings for him.

The plot thickens when it is revealed that Irene is actually a woman who was kidnapped by the robbers, and she has been hiding out at a remote cabin. Charlie must use both personalities to infiltrate the robbers' hideout and rescue Irene.

In the climactic final scene, Charlie faces off against the leader of the robbers, a ruthless individual known as "The Kid" (played by George Segal). With Hank's help, Charlie is able to overpower The Kid and save Irene. However, in the process, he also loses control of his condition, leading to a chaotic and violent confrontation.

In the end, Charlie is able to reconcile with both personalities, and Dr. Hurst helps him find a way to manage his MPD. The movie concludes with Charlie and Irene sharing a romantic moment, as Charlie finally finds a sense of peace and stability in his life.

Throughout the movie, Jim Carrey delivers a standout performance, showcasing his impressive range as an actor. His portrayal of both Charlie and Hank is nuanced and convincing, making it easy to become invested in their story. The supporting cast, including Renée Zellweger and George Segal, also deliver memorable performances that add to the film's humor and charm.

Overall, Me, Myself & Irene is a hilarious and heartwarming movie that explores themes of identity, relationships, and personal growth. With its unique blend of comedy and drama, it has become a cult classic that continues to delight audiences to this day.

overview: A gang of South Korean thieves team up with a Hong Kong crew to steal a diamond necklace from a heavily-guarded casino safe in Macau. As the cops close in, old betrayals — and misunderstandings — resurface.
tagline: All For The Money. One For The Revenge. Every Man For Himself.
title: The Thieves
plot:
The Thieves is a 2012 South Korean heist film directed by Suk Kyung-chae. The movie revolves around a group of professional thieves who plan to steal a priceless artifact from a museum in Macau.

At its core, The Thieves explores the themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption. The characters are complex and multi-dimensional, with each one having their own motivations and backstories that drive their actions throughout the story. As the heist unfolds, alliances are tested, and old wounds are reopened, leading to a web of deceit and mistrust.

The film also delves into the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences and relationships. The characters are not one-dimensional figures, but rather nuanced individuals with their own strengths and weaknesses. As they navigate the complexities of their heist, they are forced to confront their own demons and question who they truly are.

Furthermore, The Thieves touches on the theme of obsession and the lengths people will go to achieve their goals. The characters' fixation on the artifact drives them to take risks and push themselves to the limit, often putting their relationships and even their lives at stake.

Overall, The Thieves is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores the human condition through its complex characters and intricate plot.

overview: A police chief tries to solve a kidnapping that involves a bank robber holding a young boy hostage.
tagline: When you only have one shot, don't miss.
title: First Kill
plot:
First Kill is a 2017 American romantic horror film directed by Christian Whitehead and written by Christian Whitehead. The movie follows the story of a young woman named Violet, who returns to her hometown in Louisiana after being away for several years.

The main theme of First Kill revolves around the struggle between tradition and modernity, as embodied by the contrast between Violet's old-fashioned values and the more progressive views of those around her. The film also explores the tension between desire and duty, particularly in the context of Violet's relationships with men.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the idea of female empowerment and independence, as Violet navigates a world where she is expected to conform to certain societal norms. Through Violet's journey, the film suggests that women must find their own path and make their own choices, even if it means challenging the status quo.

The film also delves into the theme of small-town secrets and the consequences of keeping them hidden. As Violet becomes embroiled in a mysterious plot involving a local legend, she begins to uncover dark secrets about her community that threaten to upend her life forever.

Overall, First Kill is a thought-provoking exploration of themes that are both timely and timeless, offering a nuanced portrayal of the complexities of human relationships and the challenges of growing up.
