overview: Each Christmas, Santa and his vast army of highly trained elves produce gifts and distribute them around the world in one night. However, when one of 600 million children to receive a gift from Santa on Christmas Eve is missed, it is deemed ‘acceptable’ to all but one—Arthur. Arthur Claus is Santa’s misfit son who executes an unauthorised rookie mission to get the last present half way around the globe before dawn on Christmas morning.
tagline: Ever wonder how 2 Billion presents get delivered all in 1 night?
title: Arthur Christmas
plot:
Arthur Christmas is a heartwarming animated comedy film released in 2011 by Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of Arthur, the eldest son of Santa Claus, who is struggling to live up to his father's expectations.

The film begins on Christmas Eve at the North Pole, where Santa and his wife, Mrs. Claus, are preparing for the big night. However, with the help of their elves, they manage to deliver all the presents in record time, thanks to a high-tech system that allows them to track every child's gift. The system is so efficient that it becomes redundant, and Arthur finds himself feeling unappreciated and overlooked.

As Christmas Eve comes to an end, Santa announces his retirement and names Arthur as his successor. However, Arthur is not interested in taking over the reins of the North Pole, and he spends most of his time trying to avoid his responsibilities. Meanwhile, a young girl named Sophie receives a gift that was left behind by Santa's high-tech system, which fails to deliver it on time.

Sophie teams up with Arthur's younger brother, Steve, who is more interested in playing video games than helping out at the North Pole. Together, they embark on a mission to find the missing gift and return it to its rightful owner. Along the way, they encounter a series of hilarious misadventures, including a run-in with a group of bumbling burglars.

As Arthur and Steve journey through the city, they begin to realize that Christmas is not just about presents, but about the joy and love that comes with giving and receiving. They also learn more about their father's legacy and the importance of following in his footsteps.

In the end, Arthur and Steve successfully deliver the gift, and Sophie returns home with a newfound appreciation for the magic of Christmas. Meanwhile, Santa is forced to come out of retirement and help his sons on their mission, proving that he still has what it takes to be a great Santa Claus.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of traditional and computer-generated imagery. The voice cast, including James McAvoy as Arthur, Hugh Laurie as Steve, and Bill Nighy as Santa, brings the characters to life in a way that is both humorous and heartwarming.

Overall, Arthur Christmas is a delightful holiday film that celebrates the spirit of giving and the importance of family. With its witty humor, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for families around the world.

overview: A group of cold-blooded killers find themselves trapped on an alien planet to be hunted by extraterrestrial Predators.
tagline: The hunt is on.
title: Predators
plot:
Predators is a 2010 science fiction action film directed by Nimród Antal and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as a reboot of the Predator franchise, ignoring the events of the previous films.

The story begins with Royce (Adrien Brody), a former Special Forces operative who has lost his way after a traumatic event in his past. He is hired by a wealthy client to lead an elite team of mercenaries on a mission to retrieve a valuable artifact from the remote jungles of South America. The team consists of Noland (Topher Grace), a skilled sniper; Stans (Lawrence Fishburne), a seasoned soldier; Mombasa (Alice Braga), a Brazilian mercenary; and Cuchillo (Danny Trejo), a Mexican fighter.

Upon arrival, the team discovers that they are not alone in the jungle. They soon realize that they are being hunted by a technologically advanced alien species known as the Yautja, also referred to as Predators. The Yautja are skilled warriors who have been hunting humans for sport and scientific study.

As the team tries to survive and escape the jungle, they discover that each member of their group has a unique skillset that makes them vulnerable to the Yautja's tactics. Noland is forced to confront his own demons when he discovers that one of his teammates is being hunted by the aliens. Meanwhile, Stans becomes increasingly paranoid and aggressive as the situation spirals out of control.

Throughout the film, Royce begins to realize that the team's only hope for survival lies in understanding the Yautja's motivations and weaknesses. He also starts to uncover clues about the artifact they were hired to retrieve, which may hold the key to their escape.

As the body count rises, the team is forced to work together to take down the Yautja. In a thrilling climax, Royce faces off against the leader of the Yautja, Isabelle (Alice Braga's character), who has been hunting him throughout the film. The final confrontation takes place in an ancient temple deep within the jungle, where Royce uses his wits and combat skills to outsmart the Yautja.

In the end, only a few members of the team manage to escape the jungle alive, including Royce and Stans. As they emerge from the jungle, they are met with a surprise: the artifact they were hired to retrieve is actually a device that can track and locate other Predators. The film ends on a cliffhanger, setting up the possibility for future adventures in the Predator franchise.

Overall, Predators offers a fresh take on the Predator franchise, exploring themes of survival, teamwork, and the psychological effects of being hunted by an alien species. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has developed a loyal fan base over the years, and its action-packed sequences and suspenseful plot have made it a staple of the sci-fi genre.

overview: When Nancy is surfing on a secluded beach, she finds herself on the feeding ground of a great white shark. Though she is stranded only 200 yards from shore, survival proves to be the ultimate test of wills, requiring all of Nancy's ingenuity, resourcefulness, and fortitude.
tagline: What was once in the deep is now in the shallows.
title: The Shallows
plot:
The Shallows is a 2016 American thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and starring Blake Lively, Brett Cullen, and Jay Ellis. The movie follows the story of Nancy Adams (Blake Lively), a surfer who finds herself trapped on a rock formation in the middle of the ocean.

Nancy, an experienced surfer, is out catching waves off the coast of Santa Cruz, California. She's been surfing since she was a teenager and has developed a deep respect for the ocean. As she paddles out to catch a particularly large wave, she notices a great white shark (Carcharodon carcharias) approaching her from beneath the surface.

The shark attacks Nancy, biting down on her leg and pulling her underwater. She manages to escape by grabbing onto a rock formation in the middle of the ocean, but not before the shark severely injures her leg. As she tries to catch her breath and assess her injuries, Nancy realizes that she's trapped - the shark has taken out its anger on her, and it won't let go.

As the days pass, Nancy becomes increasingly desperate to escape. She uses her knowledge of the ocean and her surfing skills to try and lure the shark away from her rock formation, but the shark proves to be a formidable opponent. Despite her best efforts, Nancy is forced to confront the reality that she may not survive this ordeal.

As the tension builds, Nancy begins to experience flashbacks to her past - memories of her relationship with her ex-boyfriend, Brian (Brett Cullen), and her struggles as a single mother. These flashbacks serve as a reminder of what's at stake for Nancy: her life, her freedom, and her future.

As the shark continues to circle her, Nancy becomes more and more desperate. She starts to use unconventional methods to try and distract the shark, including using a surfboard to create a diversion and even attempting to lure it away with bait. However, the shark proves to be relentless, and Nancy is forced to confront the possibility that she may never escape.

In the end, Nancy comes up with a plan to outsmart the shark once and for all. Using her knowledge of the ocean and her surfing skills, she creates a makeshift "trap" using a piece of driftwood and some seaweed. The shark takes the bait, and Nancy is finally able to escape from its deadly grasp.

As she swims away from the rock formation, Nancy reflects on the experience and realizes that it's changed her in profound ways. She's forced to confront her own mortality and the fragility of life, but she's also discovered a newfound appreciation for the ocean and its power. The movie ends with Nancy swimming off into the distance, free at last from the shark's deadly grasp.

Overall, The Shallows is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption. With its stunning ocean scenery and pulse-pounding action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: China is plunged into strife as feuding warlords try to expand their power by warring over neighboring lands. Fuelled by his success on the battlefield, young and arrogant Hao Jie sneers at Shaolin's masters when he beats one of them in a duel. But the pride comes before a fall. When his own family is wiped out by a rival warlord, Hao is forced to take refuge with the monks. As the civil unrest spreads and the people suffer, Hao and the Shaolin masters are forced to take a fiery stand against the evil warlords. They launch a daring plan or rescue and escape.
tagline: In a land torn by strife, the righteous monks of Shaolin stand as a beacon of hope for the oppressed masses.
title: Shaolin
plot:
Shaolin is a 2011 Hong Kong–Chinese martial arts film directed by Benny Chan. Andy Lau stars as the warlord Hou Jie, with Nicholas Tse as his treacherous lieutenant Cao Man, Jackie Chan as the temple cook Wudao and Fan Bingbing as Hou's wife, Yan Xi. Wu Jing, Yu Shaoqun and Xing Yu play Shaolin monks. The film is a loose remake of the 1982 Jet Li film Shaolin Temple, moved to a different historical period, and it was released in both Mandarin and Cantonese.

The story is set in early 20th-century China during the Warlord Era. Hou Jie, a ruthless warlord, defeats his rival Huo Long and takes control of Dengfeng. When Huo seeks refuge at the Shaolin Temple, Hou follows him there, kills him and mocks the monks. Hou then plans to murder his sworn brother, Song Hu, but his ambitious second-in-command, Cao Man, turns the trap against him and sends assassins after them all. Song is killed, and Hou's young daughter is gravely injured in a fall from a cliff. In desperation, Hou carries her to Shaolin and begs the monks to save her, but she dies. His wife blames him and leaves him, and in a single night Hou has lost his power and his family.

Wandering the temple grounds, Hou is taken in by Wudao, the kind-hearted cook, who gives him food and shelter. Full of remorse, Hou becomes a monk, and through study and martial arts he absorbs Shaolin's principles and finds peace. Meanwhile, Cao has seized Hou's army and is brutalizing innocent people, and Hou must confront his past to stop him. While he distracts Cao, the monks raid Cao's camp to free the laborers, and Hou escapes with his wife. As Cao's forces close in, the monks decide to evacuate. Wudao leads the refugees to safety while Hou and a group of monks stay behind to hold off the attackers. The temple is pounded by artillery, killing many monks and soldiers. Hou defeats Cao in combat but then saves him from a falling beam, sacrificing his own life. He dies peacefully in the palm of the great Buddha statue, leaving Cao overcome with guilt.

Filming began in October 2009 with a ceremony at the Shaolin Temple. To avoid damaging the real temple, the production built its own replica in Zhejiang for 10 million yuan. Released in mainland China on January 19, 2011, and in Hong Kong a week later, it opened at number one in Hong Kong, Thailand and Singapore and set a box office record in Malaysia. It holds a 74% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: There's trouble brewing in Bikini Bottom. Someone has stolen King Neptune's crown, and it looks like Mr. Krab, SpongeBob's boss, is the culprit. Though he's just been passed over for the promotion of his dreams, SpongeBob stands by his boss, and along with his best pal Patrick, sets out on a treacherous mission to Shell City to reclaim the crown and save Mr. Krab's life.
tagline: Bigger. Better. More absorbent.
title: The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie
plot:
The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie is a 2004 animated musical comedy film directed by Stephen Hillenburg, based on the popular Nickelodeon television series. The movie follows the adventures of SpongeBob SquarePants and his friends in Bikini Bottom.

The story begins with Plankton, the owner of the Chum Bucket restaurant, stealing King Neptune's crown, which gives him control over the ocean. As a result, King Neptune banishes Plankton to a distant island, but not before he orders SpongeBob to retrieve the crown and bring it back to Bikini Bottom.

SpongeBob sets off on his journey, accompanied by Patrick Star, his best friend and neighbor. Along the way, they face various obstacles, including the treacherous waters of the open ocean, the Fry Cook Museum, where they meet a group of retired fry cooks who are trying to break into the museum's vault, and the evil Dennis, a fish who is working for Plankton.

As SpongeBob and Patrick continue their journey, they encounter various characters from Bikini Bottom, including Sandy Cheeks, Squidward Tentacles, and Mr. Krabs. However, none of them are aware of the crown's location, and SpongeBob must rely on his own determination and resourcefulness to find it.

Meanwhile, Plankton is using the crown's power to take over the ocean, and King Neptune is trying to stop him. The two engage in an epic battle, with SpongeBob and Patrick eventually joining forces to help their king defeat Plankton.

In the end, SpongeBob and Patrick successfully retrieve the crown and return it to Bikini Bottom, where they are hailed as heroes. However, not before Plankton's plan is foiled, and he is banished back to his island.

The movie ends with a grand celebration in Bikini Bottom, featuring music, dancing, and a cameo appearance by Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy. The film concludes on a high note, with SpongeBob and his friends enjoying their victory and looking forward to their next adventure together.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the underwater world of Bikini Bottom to life in a way that is both visually stunning and endearing. The voice acting is also top-notch, with Tom Kenny reprising his role as SpongeBob SquarePants and Bill Fagerbakke returning as Patrick Star.

Overall, The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie is a fun, entertaining film that captures the spirit of the beloved television series. With its catchy musical numbers, lovable characters, and exciting adventure storyline, it's a must-see for fans of all ages.

belongs_to_collection.name: On the Other Side of the Tracks Collection

overview: Ousmane Diakité and François Monge are two cops with very different styles, backgrounds and careers. The unlikely pair are reunited once again for a new investigation that takes them across France. What seemed to be a simple drug deal turns out to be a much bigger criminal case wrapped in danger and unexpected comedy.
tagline: Two cops. One case. No clue.
title: The Takedown
plot:
The Takedown (Loin du périph) is a 2022 French action comedy directed by Louis Leterrier from a screenplay by Stéphane Kazandjian, based on characters created for David Charhon's 2012 film On the Other Side of the Tracks. Omar Sy and Laurent Lafitte return as the mismatched police partners Ousmane Diakité and François Monge, joined by Izïa Higelin as Alice Gauthier, Dimitri Storoge as Antoine Brunner, Stéphane Pezerat as Commissioner Mercier and Sabrina Ouazani as Yasmine.

A decade after their first case, Ousmane is a commander in the Paris criminal brigade, and after a viral video of him fighting a suspect he is pushed to front a national police recruitment campaign, while François, a captain in the 12th arrondissement, is criticized by colleagues for getting in the way of investigations. The two meet again by chance when François finds half of a corpse on a high-speed train. The victim, Kevin Marchal, came from Valergnes, a town in the Alps, and Ousmane travels there to escape the campaign, with François tagging along. With help from local officer Alice, they learn Kevin was shot off his motorbike onto the tracks and had been running a drug lab in his mother's house. A brawl in a strip club with a bouncer who seems immune to pain, and the man's sudden death, lead them to a security firm whose guards share the tattoo of a militia, the Sons of Clovis. Commissioner Mercier quickly closes the case, but Ousmane refuses to leave. A friend of Kevin's reveals that the victim feared the militia and had asked Mercier for protection.

Following Mercier, the duo is threatened by Brunner, the town's far-right mayor, and attacked on the road. In Brunner's basement they discover plans for coordinated attacks on mosques, synagogues and a migrant center, carried out by fighters taking pain-numbing methamphetamine. In the final showdown, François distracts the militia while Ousmane sabotages their weapons and fights Alice, who turns out to be Brunner's ally. The pair stop a bomb at the migrant center and arrest Brunner and Alice, and François ends up as the face of the recruitment campaign.

Filmed in spring 2021 in Paris and the Alps, the film was released on Netflix on 6 May 2022 and logged more than 78 million hours viewed in its first 28 days. French reviews were mixed: Ouest-France praised the chemistry of Sy and Lafitte, while Les Inrockuptibles felt its political satire and action scenes were less successful than its comedy.

overview: A young woman encounters a malevolent supernatural force while searching for her missing sister in Tokyo, a mean high school prank goes horribly wrong, and strange things begin happening in a Chicago apartment building.
tagline: What Was Once Trapped, Will Now Be Unleashed
title: The Grudge 2
plot:
The Grudge 2 is a supernatural horror film directed by Takashi Shimizu, released in 2006 by Columbia Pictures.

The main theme of The Grudge 2 revolves around the concept of cursed bloodlines and the consequences of meddling with forces beyond human control. The story follows Karen Davis (played by Sarah Michelle Gellar), an American nurse who travels to Japan to visit her friend, but soon finds herself entangled in a web of vengeful spirits.

The film explores the idea that certain families or individuals can be cursed for generations, and that these curses can be passed down through bloodlines. The main antagonist, Kayako Saeki (played by Takako Fuji), is a vengeful spirit who seeks revenge on those who disturb her family's rest.

Throughout the movie, Shimizu delves into themes of:

1. Cursed Bloodlines: The film highlights the idea that certain families or individuals can be cursed for generations, and that these curses can have devastating consequences.
2. Revenge and Retribution: Kayako's relentless pursuit of revenge serves as a catalyst for the plot, exploring the destructive nature of unchecked anger and the cyclical nature of violence.
3. Cultural Heritage: The film touches on Japanese cultural traditions and the importance of respecting one's ancestors and heritage.
4. Trauma and Guilt: Karen's character is haunted by her past mistakes, which serves as a metaphor for the emotional baggage that can be passed down through generations.

The Grudge 2 received mixed reviews from critics but has since become a cult classic among horror fans, who appreciate its eerie atmosphere and supernatural themes.

overview: With the peak of his career long behind him, an actor clings to his past glory — until a sudden wake-up call forces him to face who he's become.
title: What Happened to Mr Cha?
plot:
Titled in Korean simply 차인표, after its star, What Happened to Mr. Cha? is a South Korean comedy from 2021 written and directed by Kim Dong-kyu, previously a co-writer of the thrillers Confession of Murder and Golden Job, in his feature directing debut, and released by Netflix. The veteran actor Cha In-pyo plays a fictionalised, somewhat haughtier version of himself, with Jo Dal-hwan as his manager A-ram, Song Jae-ryong, Ji Seung-hyun, Shin Shin-ae as Bok-soon, Jo Sang-gu as a hiker and Song Duk-ho; Cha's real-life wife, the actress Shin Ae-ra, plays his on-screen wife, and Ryu Seung-ryong appears as himself.

After 25 years in show business, Cha is still handsome, fit and fond of the signature finger wag his ageing fans remember, but his career is fading. Once the star of hit television dramas, he now poses for advertisements for mid-range casual sportswear while a young creative director rejects his leading-man looks and the makeup artist gets better offers than he does. He lives apart from his wife, from whom he has recently separated, and his young manager A-ram has not had the heart to tell him that the phone has stopped ringing.

Out on a hike with his tiny dog to clear his head, Cha is asked by passing seniors whether he has quit acting, and then tumbles into a mud puddle. Unwilling to be seen in such a state, he follows a stranger's advice to wash up at a nearby high school that is empty for the summer. While he is in the shower, the building's bumbling staff set off an explosion, and the school collapses on top of him. Naked, covered in dust and pinned in the rubble, Cha calls his manager, but he refuses any rescue that might humiliate him or ruin the image he has spent decades building, imagining live television footage of his blurred body being carried out. As A-ram tries to placate him and fend off the building's manager and the approaching excavator, Cha reflects on his past triumphs, seen in clips of his old roles, and as he grows delirious the film turns surreal, with Cha floating among the stars still encased in concrete and confronting his manager and versions of himself before accepting his new reality.

Netflix released the film on 1 January 2021. Critics admired Cha's willingness to mock his own persona. Decider recommended it, praising his wit and melancholy despite a sluggish middle section, while the South China Morning Post found that its sharp satire of celebrity culture gave way to more ordinary slapstick.

overview: In Monterrey, Mexico, a young street gang spends their days dancing to slowed-down cumbia and attending parties. After a mix-up with a local cartel, their leader is forced to migrate to the U.S. but quickly longs to return home.
title: I'm No Longer Here
plot:
I'm No Longer Here is a 2019 Mexican drama film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, not Panorama Global. The movie tells the story of two brothers, Carlos and Humberto, who are forced to flee their home in Colombia due to the country's civil war.

The main themes of I'm No Longer Here include:

1. **Trauma and its effects**: The film explores the long-lasting impact of trauma on individuals and families, particularly those affected by violence and conflict.
2. **Brotherly love and loyalty**: The relationship between Carlos and Humberto is central to the story, as they navigate their complicated past and present circumstances together.
3. **Identity and belonging**: As the brothers travel through Europe, they grapple with their identities, cultural backgrounds, and sense of belonging in a foreign land.
4. **Memory and nostalgia**: The film delves into the power of memory and nostalgia, highlighting how these emotions can both heal and haunt individuals.
5. **Human migration and displacement**: I'm No Longer Here sheds light on the experiences of migrants and refugees, who often face immense challenges and uncertainties in their journeys.

The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Gael García Bernal, Luis Guzmán, and Natalie Martinez, among others. Almodóvar's direction weaves together these themes with his signature style, creating a poignant and thought-provoking cinematic experience.

overview: Benjamin has lost his wife and, in a bid to start his life over, purchases a large house that has a zoo – welcome news for his daughter, but his son is not happy about it. The zoo is in need of renovation and Benjamin sets about the work with the head keeper and the rest of the staff, but, the zoo soon runs into financial trouble.
tagline: A True Zoo Story
title: We Bought a Zoo
plot:
We Bought a Zoo is a heartwarming drama film released in 2011, directed by Cameron Crowe and starring Matt Damon, Scarlett Johansson, and Thomas Haden Church. The movie is based on the memoir of the same name by Benjamin Mee.

The main themes of We Bought a Zoo revolve around family, love, loss, and redemption. Here's a brief overview:

**Beginning:** The film opens with the story of Benjamin Mee (Matt Damon), a widowed father who moves to England with his two children, Dylan (Mason Lee) and Rosie (Maggie Elizabeth Jones). After losing his wife in a tragic accident, Benjamin is struggling to cope with his grief. He decides to buy a dilapidated zoo in the countryside, which becomes an opportunity for him to start anew and provide a better life for his children.

**Plot Development:** As Benjamin navigates the challenges of running a zoo, he also faces personal struggles, including his relationship with his children and his own emotional healing process. The film explores themes of love, loss, and redemption as Benjamin works to restore the zoo to its former glory and create a sense of community among the animals and the people who work there.

**Ending:** Through his journey, Benjamin learns valuable lessons about the importance of family, friendship, and finding purpose in life. He also comes to terms with his past and finds a way to heal and move forward. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Benjamin's children thriving at the zoo and their father finally finding happiness again.

Throughout the movie, Cameron Crowe weaves together themes of hope, resilience, and the power of nature to heal emotional wounds. We Bought a Zoo is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the transformative power of love and loss.

overview: When Earth is attacked by a hostile alien force, a small town firefighter and a rogue SETI scientist team up to activate the only technology capable of defeating the invaders.
tagline: The battle for Earth begins
title: Independence Daysaster
plot:
Independence Daysaster is a 2013 Canadian science fiction action television film directed by W. D. Hogan and starring Ryan Merriman as firefighter Pete Garsette and Tom Everett Scott as his brother, President Sam Garsette, with Emily Holmes, Keenan Tracey, Andrea Brooks, Garwin Sanford, Michael Kopsa and Jill Teed. A mockbuster of the 1996 blockbuster Independence Day, it premiered on Syfy on June 27, 2013, and was released on DVD in May 2014.

In the small town of Moose Ridge, Oregon, teenager Andrew Garsette, his friends Nick and Eliza and his uncle Pete, a local firefighter, are preparing for the arrival of Andrew's father, President Sam Garsette, who is coming home for the Fourth of July. Before Marine One can land, it is diverted to the nearby Dixon Airbase, and SETI scientist Celia Leyman is told about a mysterious signal that is being sent out and answered. Moments later, alien machines begin drilling up through the ground while others attack from the sky in locations all over the world. Pete persuades Secret Service agents to take the children to safety while he helps the townspeople, and on the road he picks up Celia, whose car has broken down. Sam orders his staff not to engage the alien ships until more is known, but Marine One is shot down, and Vice President Dennis Brubaker, believing the president dead, escapes Washington with General Moore shortly before the capital is destroyed. At Dixon, Brubaker assumes the presidency and authorizes a counterattack, but the alien drones easily overwhelm the fighter jets. Pete and Celia discover that her experimental phonon-emitting device can bring down the drones by cutting their link to a vast mothership, and after reuniting with the children they set out to turn it into a weapon. Meanwhile Sam, who has survived the crash, teams up with a young computer genius named Todd to reestablish contact with the base. When a nuclear strike on the mothership near the Moon fails and Moore realizes that the drilling machines are releasing a gas that will make Earth's atmosphere unbreathable within days, the group must find a way to deliver the device to the mothership before it is too late.

Like the film it imitates, it sets its global alien invasion during the Fourth of July holiday, and it closes on an ominous note, with a larger alien fleet shown approaching Earth.

overview: When space galleon cabin boy Jim Hawkins discovers a map to an intergalactic "loot of a thousand worlds," a cyborg cook named John Silver teaches him to battle supernovas and space storms on their journey to find treasure.
tagline: Find your place in the universe.
title: Treasure Planet
plot:
Treasure Planet is a science fiction adventure film produced by Walt Disney Pictures, released in 2002. The movie is an adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson's classic novel "Treasure Island," set in a futuristic universe.

The story begins with Jim Hawkins (voiced by Joseph Gordon-Levitt), an orphan boy living on the planet Terra. Jim's life changes when he meets Billy Bones (voiced by David Hyde Pierce), an old pirate who has been injured and is dying. Before his death, Billy gives Jim a mysterious map that supposedly leads to the treasure of the infamous Captain Flint.

Jim sets out on a journey with Dr. Delbert Doppler (voiced by Brian Murray), a spaceship captain who claims to be taking him to find the treasure. However, upon arrival at the planet of Salacia, they are ambushed by Captain Flint's crew, led by the ruthless and cunning Long John Silver (voiced by Jack Davenport). Long John Silver is revealed to be Jim's biological father, and his true intentions for finding the treasure are not what they seem.

As Jim navigates this new world, he meets a group of space pirates known as the "Buccaneers," who are on a quest to find the legendary treasure. The crew includes John Mutt (voiced by Jason Lee), a young and skilled pirate; and B.E.N. (voiced by Patrick McGoohan), an old robot who becomes Jim's friend and ally.

Throughout their journey, Jim faces various challenges and obstacles as he tries to uncover the truth about his father's past and the treasure. Along the way, he learns valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

As the story unfolds, Long John Silver's true intentions are revealed: he plans to use the treasure to gain control over the entire planet. Jim and his friends must work together to stop him and save the day. In a thrilling finale, they engage in an epic space battle against Captain Flint's crew, with Jim ultimately discovering the truth about his father's past and finding the treasure.

The movie ends with Jim returning home, having grown into a confident and capable young man. He reflects on the lessons he learned during his journey and the friends he made along the way, knowing that their bond will last a lifetime.

Treasure Planet is a visually stunning film that combines traditional animation techniques with cutting-edge computer-generated imagery. The movie's unique blend of science fiction and classic adventure elements has made it a beloved favorite among audiences of all ages.

overview: Friends and fledgling entrepreneurs invent a device in their garage which reduces the apparent mass of any object placed inside it, but they discover that it has some highly unexpected capabilities - ones that could enable them to do and to have seemingly anything they want. Taking advantage of this unique opportunity is the first challenge they face. Dealing with the consequences is the next.
tagline: What happens if it actually works?
title: Primer
plot:
Primer is a 2004 science fiction film written, directed, edited, and scored by Shane Carruth. The movie follows two engineers, Aaron (Shane Carruth) and Abe (David Sullivan), who work for a company that specializes in developing technology related to time travel.

The story begins with Aaron and Abe working on a project to develop a device that can send information through time. They successfully test the device, but their excitement is short-lived as they soon realize the consequences of their actions. The device creates a closed timelike curve, allowing them to send messages to their past selves, which in turn causes a series of paradoxes and disruptions to their timeline.

As the story unfolds, Aaron and Abe try to navigate the complexities of time travel, but their attempts only lead to more problems. They start to experience strange occurrences, such as finding themselves in different locations at the same time, and encountering alternate versions of themselves. The two men become increasingly paranoid and isolated, struggling to maintain a sense of reality.

One of the most striking aspects of Primer is its exploration of the consequences of playing with time. Carruth raises questions about the nature of free will and the potential risks of tampering with the timeline. As Aaron and Abe try to fix their mistakes, they begin to realize that every decision they make has a ripple effect on the world around them.

Throughout the film, Carruth employs a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between different points in time. This creates a sense of disorientation and confusion, mirroring the characters' experiences as they try to navigate the complexities of their own timeline.

As the story reaches its climax, Aaron and Abe are forced to confront the consequences of their actions. They realize that their attempts to fix their mistakes have created a new reality, one in which they are no longer sure what is real and what is not. The film ends with a sense of ambiguity, leaving the audience wondering what will happen next.

Overall, Primer is a thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating film that challenges viewers to think critically about the nature of time and its consequences. With its complex narrative structure and exploration of philosophical themes, Primer has become a cult classic among fans of science fiction and independent cinema.

original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- ブラッド・プリズン
overview: After his capture for attempted assassination of the Raikage, leader of Kumogakure, as well as killing Jōnin from Kirigakure and Iwagakure, Naruto is imprisoned in Hōzukijou: A criminal containment facility known as the Blood Prison. Mui, the castle master, uses the ultimate imprisonment technique to steal power from the prisoners, which is when Naruto notices his life has been targeted. Thus begins the battle to uncover the truth behind the mysterious murders and prove Naruto's innocence.
title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: Blood Prison
plot:
Naruto Shippuden the Movie: Blood Prison (also titled Naruto the Movie: Blood Prison) is a 2011 Japanese animated action fantasy film based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and anime. Directed by Masahiko Murata for Studio Pierrot from a script by Akira Higashiyama, it is the eighth Naruto film and the fifth in the Shippuden era, and it sends its hero into a notorious prison after he is accused of an attempted assassination.

A hooded figure attacks the Fourth Raikage of the Hidden Cloud Village and, when unmasked, appears to be Naruto Uzumaki. Back in the Hidden Leaf, Tsunade announces that Naruto is wanted for the assassination attempt and for killing ninja of other villages, and despite his protests he is sent to Hōzuki Castle, the "Blood Prison" in the Hidden Grass Village. Its warden, Mui, places a seal on him that cripples his chakra, so every escape attempt and every challenge to Mui ends in agony and solitary confinement. Admired by the other inmates, Naruto tries again to flee by sea and is rescued from a whirlpool by Ryūzetsu, a Hidden Grass agent working undercover, who reveals that Mui framed him and sacrificed his own son Muku to the mysterious Box of Ultimate Bliss years earlier. Aided by the scheming inmate Maroi, the pair stage a riot, but Mui captures Naruto and uses his chakra to open the box, wishing for his son's return. A grown Muku emerges, stabs his father and transforms into the demon Satori, which can anticipate its enemies' attacks. Naruto, in Sage Mode, and the toad Gamabunta are overwhelmed until Killer B and Naruto's friends arrive, and Tsunade reveals that the arrest was a ruse to get Naruto inside to destroy the box. Realising Satori reads fears rather than thoughts, Naruto fights it on even terms and, with the dying Mui's help, defeats it with his Rasenshuriken. Muku ends both his father's life and his own, and Ryūzetsu gives her life to revive the mortally wounded Naruto. At her grave he ties on her headband and vows to cherish the life she gave him.

Junko Takeuchi voices Naruto, with Masaki Terasoma as Mui, Mie Sonozaki as Ryūzetsu and Yūichi Nakamura as Muku; the English dub stars Maile Flanagan, Matthew Mercer and Carrie Keranen. Distributed by Toho, it opened in Japan in July 2011 and grossed about ¥800 million. Yusuke Kamiji performed the theme song "Otakebi", and Viz Media released the film in North America on February 18, 2014.

overview: Composer Gustav von Aschenbach travels to Venice for health reasons. There, he becomes obsessed with the stunning beauty of an adolescent Polish boy named Tadzio who is staying with his family at the same Grand Hôtel des Bains on the Lido as Aschenbach.
tagline: The celebrated story of a man obsessed with ideal beauty.
title: Death in Venice
plot:
Death in Venice (Italian: Morte a Venezia) is a 1971 historical drama film directed and produced by Luchino Visconti, who adapted Thomas Mann's 1912 novella with Nicola Badalucco. It stars Dirk Bogarde as Gustav von Aschenbach and Björn Andrésen as Tadzio, with Mark Burns, Marisa Berenson and Silvana Mangano. Shot in Technicolor by Pasqualino De Santis, it uses music from Gustav Mahler's Third and Fifth Symphonies and is the second part of Visconti's "German Trilogy", between The Damned (1969) and Ludwig (1973).

In poor health, the composer Aschenbach travels to Venice to rest. As his ship arrives, a garishly made-up old man accosts him with suggestive remarks, and he turns away in disgust. Staying at the Grand Hotel des Bains on the Lido, he notices a Polish family and becomes captivated by their beautiful adolescent son, Tadzio. The boy's image recalls heated debates with his friend and pupil Alfred over whether beauty is created by art or exists in nature and is superior to it. Aschenbach watches Tadzio on the beach, and after an encounter in the hotel lift in which the boy seems to give him an inviting look, he resolves in agitation to leave. When his luggage is misdirected at the station, however, he is secretly glad to return, though he sees a man collapse at the station, and the hotel manager dismisses foreign press reports as exaggerated.

Aschenbach makes Tadzio his muse but cannot master his longing and drifts into daydreams about the unreachable boy, who notices his gaze and occasionally returns it, though they never speak. A travel clerk in Saint Mark's Square reluctantly admits that cholera is spreading through the city, and Aschenbach imagines warning Tadzio's mother. He follows the family to St Mark's Basilica, and a talkative barber dyes and paints him into a likeness of the old man from the ship. Trailing the family through the streets, he collapses by a well in pained laughter, and he dreams of a disastrous concert in Munich and Alfred's reproaches. Learning the family is departing, Aschenbach, now gravely ill, sits on the empty beach watching Tadzio wade into the sea to Mahler's Adagietto. The boy turns and points toward the horizon, and Aschenbach dies in his deck chair.

The film premiered in London on 1 March 1971 and competed at the 24th Cannes Film Festival. Critics have admired its sumptuous visuals, with Derek Malcolm of The Guardian calling it a slow, precise and beautiful achievement; Rotten Tomatoes reports 70% approval.

overview: A thriller that revolves around the key people at an investment bank over a 24-hour period during the early stages of the financial crisis.
tagline: Be first. Be smarter. Or cheat.
title: Margin Call
plot:
Margin Call is a 2011 American thriller film directed by J.C. Chandor, produced by Myriad Pictures, Cross Creek Pictures, and Sidney Kimmel Entertainment.

The main themes of Margin Call include:

1. **Financial Crisis**: The movie depicts the early stages of the 2008 financial crisis, highlighting the reckless behavior of Wall Street executives and the devastating consequences of their actions.
2. **Hubris and Greed**: The characters' excessive ambition and desire for wealth lead to their downfall, serving as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked greed.
3. **Accountability and Responsibility**: As the crisis unfolds, the characters are forced to confront their roles in the disaster and take responsibility for their actions, leading to a sense of accountability and redemption.
4. **Human Connection and Relationships**: Amidst the chaos, the film explores the personal relationships between the characters, highlighting the importance of human connections and empathy in times of crisis.
5. **Systemic Failure**: The movie critiques the flaws in the financial system, revealing how the pursuit of profit can lead to systemic failures that have far-reaching consequences.

The plot follows a group of investment bankers at a Wall Street firm as they navigate the unfolding financial crisis, facing difficult decisions and moral dilemmas along the way. As the situation spirals out of control, the characters must confront their own mortality and the true cost of their actions.

Overall, Margin Call is a thought-provoking thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of unchecked ambition in the financial world.

overview: Haunted by her past, a nurse travels from England to a remote Irish village in 1862 to investigate a young girl's supposedly miraculous fast.
title: The Wonder
plot:
The Wonder is a 2022 period psychological drama film directed by Sebastián Lelio from a screenplay by Emma Donoghue, Lelio and Alice Birch, based on Donoghue's 2016 novel of the same name. Florence Pugh leads an ensemble cast that includes Tom Burke, Niamh Algar, Elaine Cassidy, Toby Jones, Ciarán Hinds and Kíla Lord Cassidy. It premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on 2 September 2022, received a limited theatrical release on 2 November and began streaming on Netflix on 16 November 2022.

In 1862, not long after the Great Famine, Elizabeth "Lib" Wright, an English nurse who served in the Crimean War, is sent to a rural Irish village to observe Anna O'Donnell, a young girl whose devout family claims she has not eaten for four months. Working alongside a nun, Sister Michael, Lib is to report independently to a council of local dignitaries on whether the "fasting girl" is a miracle or a fraud. Many villagers, still scarred by the famine, distrust the English nurse. Anna appears healthy and says she lives on "manna from heaven". At her lodgings Lib meets William Byrne, a journalist for the Daily Telegraph who grew up in the area, lost his family in the famine and suspects the whole affair is a hoax, and the two begin a relationship. Lib, who is grieving the death of her only child and relies on laudanum to sleep, watches Anna closely and at first finds no sign of deception, until she notices the way Anna's mother kisses the girl goodnight and realizes how food is being secretly passed to her. Once the family is kept away from her, Anna's health begins to fail, and she confides the painful reasons behind her fast, which are bound up with her late brother and her family's faith. The council refuses to accept Lib's findings, the family will not intervene, and as Anna grows weaker, Lib must decide how far she is willing to go to save a child whom everyone else seems prepared to let die.

The Wonder received positive reviews, with critics praising its production design and its performances, particularly Pugh's. On Rotten Tomatoes, 85% of 171 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus that its atmosphere is absorbing and its story fascinating but that the true wonder lies in Pugh's remarkable performance, and Metacritic gave it a score of 71 out of 100.

overview: FBI agent Malcolm Turner goes back undercover as Big Momma, a slick-talking, slam-dunking Southern granny with attitude to spare! Now this granny must play nanny to three dysfunctional upper class kids in order to spy on their computer hacked dad.
tagline: The momma of all comedies is back.
title: Big Momma's House 2
plot:
Big Momma's House 2 is an American crime comedy of 2006 directed by John Whitesell, the second film in the Big Momma series. Martin Lawrence returns as FBI agent Malcolm Turner and his disguise as the formidable Hattie Mae "Big Momma" Pierce, with Nia Long as his wife Sherry, Mark Moses and Emily Procter as Tom and Leah Fuller, Zachary Levi as agent Kevin Keneally, Marisol Nichols as agent Liliana Morales, and Kat Dennings and Chloë Grace Moretz as the Fuller daughters.

Six years after the first film, Malcolm is married to Sherry, stepfather to her son Trent and working a desk job while they await their first baby. When his friend Doug Hudson is killed undercover in Orange County, Malcolm learns that Doug had been investigating Tom Fuller, a former military intelligence specialist working for a software company, who appears to be building a computer worm able to open a back door into government databases. Barred from the case, Malcolm tells Sherry he is off to an out-of-state conference, digs out his old disguise and, as Big Momma, beats the other candidates for the job of nanny to the Fullers.

Inside the household he finds a family under strain: Leah is a stern taskmaster, teenage Molly is trying to be someone she is not, Carrie struggles on her cheerleading squad, and toddler Andrew keeps leaping off high places. Sherry discovers the ruse and is furious, while Morales lets Malcolm stay on the case provided he keeps his cover and works with Kevin. With help from a young hacker, Stewart, the agents go after Tom's workstation, but when Malcolm rescues Molly from a nightclub, men working for the company's chief executive, Casal, take them both hostage to force Tom to finish a deal involving the worm. Malcolm frees himself and Molly, saves Tom from being killed and stops Casal before the FBI arrives, and Tom is cleared after explaining that he was coerced under threat to his family. Malcolm reconciles with Sherry, helps Carrie's squad win a championship, leaves a farewell letter from Big Momma and returns home to welcome a son he names Doug.

Released by 20th Century Fox in January 2006, the film opened at number one and earned roughly $140 million worldwide on a $40 million budget, despite scathing reviews and a 5% Rotten Tomatoes rating. A third film, Big Mommas: Like Father, Like Son, followed in 2011.

overview: An ambitious lobbyist faces off against the powerful gun lobby in an attempt to pass gun control legislation.
tagline: Make sure you surprise them.
title: Miss Sloane
plot:
Miss Sloane is a 2016 American drama film directed by John Madden, starring Jessica Chastain as Elizabeth Sloane, a ruthless and cunning lobbyist. The movie follows the story of Elizabeth Sloane, a top lobbyist who specializes in gun control legislation.

The film begins with Elizabeth Sloane (Jessica Chastain) delivering a speech at a gun lobby conference, where she is booed by the audience for her stance on stricter gun control laws. Despite this, she remains committed to her cause and decides to take on the National Rifle Association (NRA), led by Senator Richard Shelby's (Sam Elliott) aide, Jacobson (Giovanni Ribisi).

Elizabeth Sloane starts working with a group of grassroots activists, including her protégée, Shelly (Samantha Morton). Together, they develop a strategy to pass stricter gun control laws in the Senate. However, Elizabeth soon realizes that the NRA is well-funded and has significant influence over politicians.

As Elizabeth navigates the complex world of lobbying, she faces opposition from her colleagues and struggles with her own moral compass. She becomes increasingly ruthless in her tactics, using underhanded methods to manipulate politicians and sway public opinion. Her personal life also begins to suffer as she becomes more consumed by her work.

Meanwhile, Jacobson, who is initially Elizabeth's adversary, starts to question his allegiances to the NRA and develops a complicated relationship with Elizabeth. The two engage in a cat-and-mouse game of one-upmanship, each trying to outmaneuver the other.

As the story unfolds, Elizabeth faces setbacks and challenges, including a failed attempt to pass gun control legislation and a personal crisis that forces her to reevaluate her priorities. In the end, she makes a bold move that could potentially change the course of the debate on gun control.

The film culminates with Elizabeth delivering a powerful speech at a Senate hearing, where she presents a compelling argument for stricter gun control laws. The outcome is uncertain, leaving the audience wondering if Elizabeth's efforts will be successful.

Throughout the movie, Jessica Chastain delivers a tour-de-force performance as Elizabeth Sloane, bringing depth and nuance to her character. The supporting cast, including Sam Elliott and Giovanni Ribisi, add complexity to the story, exploring themes of power, morality, and the human cost of politics.

Overall, Miss Sloane is a gripping drama that explores the cutthroat world of lobbying and the personal costs of fighting for a cause. With its strong performances, timely subject matter, and thought-provoking themes, it's a movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

overview: A scientist discovers the bodies of three frozen genetically modified Russians buried in the Canadian North. Upon thawing them out he realizes he has unleashed a deadly threat to Western society and must stop them at all costs.
tagline: The Cold War Begins Again.
title: Ice Soldiers
plot:
Ice Soldiers is a 2013 Canadian action science fiction film directed by Sturla Gunnarsson. Dominic Purcell stars as scientist Andrew Malraux, with Adam Beach as T.C. Cardinal, Michael Ironside as Colonel Desmond Trump and Gabriel Hogan as the leader of three frozen Soviet super soldiers.

The film opens in 1962, during the Cuban Missile Crisis, when Canadian troops in the Arctic find a crashed aircraft carrying three Soviet soldiers with superhuman abilities. Taken to a base for study, they break free, kill many troops and vanish. Fifty years later, a team of Canadian soldiers and scientists, including Malraux and Dr. Lobokoff, finds the three soldiers frozen beneath the ice. Malraux explains that Soviet extremists, aided by a captured Nazi scientist, engineered them to attack New York and trigger a third world war. The bodies prove to be alive and regenerating. When the team cannot agree on what to do, Malraux tries to kill them by cutting off their life support and is locked up. His fears prove justified: the soldiers wake up and massacre most of the team, including Lobokoff.

Malraux escapes and pursues them across the frozen landscape with T.C., a troubled Cree ex-convict whose father survived the soldiers' first rampage in the 1960s. They track the soldiers to a small oil town, where the three have learned of a mine where they can steal explosives. Arriving too late, Malraux and T.C. are wrongly arrested for the theft and the murder of the miners. No one heeds Malraux's warning about the soldiers' preprogrammed mission. That night, the soldiers blow up the power plant and kill local officials and police. Malraux and T.C. escape and chase the soldiers' truck by snowmobile, tricking it into crashing into a mountainside. The explosion kills two of the soldiers. The third heads for a plane bound for New York, and Malraux drags him off and kills him after a brutal fight. As they cremate the body, Malraux reveals that his mother was a scientist who examined the soldiers in the 1960s and was raped by this man, making him the soldier's son. T.C. assures him that he is a good man, but Malraux remains unsure.

The film was shot in 2013 around Sudbury, Ontario. Gunnarsson, staging storms with wind machines and a snowmobile chase, called it a "big toybox". It premiered in Sudbury on February 28, 2014. Critics dismissed it as generic B-movie fare, and Canada.com called it a gleefully preposterous slice of B-movie cheese.

original_title: Astérix - Le Secret de la Potion Magique
overview: Following a fall during mistletoe picking, Druid Getafix decides that it is time to secure the future of the village. Accompanied by Asterix and Obelix, he undertakes to travel the Gallic world in search of a talented young druid to transmit the Secret of the Magic Potion.
title: Asterix: The Secret of the Magic Potion
plot:
Asterix: The Secret of the Magic Potion (French: Astérix: Le Secret de la Potion Magique) is a French animated adventure comedy of 2018 co-directed by Alexandre Astier and Louis Clichy, from a screenplay by Astier based on the characters of René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo. A sequel to Asterix: The Mansions of the Gods (2014), it was the first Asterix production without Roger Carel as the hero; Christian Clavier voices Asterix, with Guillaume Briat as Obelix, Bernard Alane as Getafix, Daniel Mesguich as the villain Sulfurix (Demonix in English), Lévanah Solomon as Pectine and Alex Lutz as Teleferix.

After falling from a tree and breaking his foot, the druid Getafix confronts his own mortality and resolves to pass the recipe for his strength-giving magic potion to a worthy successor. Escorted by Asterix and Obelix, with the inventive village girl Pectine stowed away in his cauldron, he attends a gathering of druids that is disrupted by his old rival Sulfurix, then tours Gaul to audition young candidates. The village men go along, leaving Cacofonix and the women behind with a reserve of potion to hold off the Romans.

Sulfurix offers the secret to Julius Caesar and, with the scheming Senator Tomcrus, plots to besiege the village until its potion runs out. He secretly coaches the gifted young druid Teleferix to impress Getafix, who duly chooses him, and burns the druids' sacred forest. As the village runs dry, Sulfurix steals the gathered ingredients and freezes Obelix with a spell. Lacking one ingredient, he boosts a flawed batch with his own fire magic, drinks it and attacks Gauls and Romans alike. Getafix reveals to Pectine that the missing element is a drop of earlier potion hidden in the handle of his golden sickle, and she brews a new batch. When Sulfurix becomes a giant, Gauls and Romans unite, and Getafix shapes the legionaries into a giant centaur steered by Obelix that defeats him. Teleferix is sent home to begin his training again, while Pectine cannot get the recipe out of her head, hinting that she may one day succeed Getafix.

Distributed in France by SND from 5 December 2018, the film took close to $7 million in its first five days.

overview: Disconnect interweaves multiple storylines about people searching for human connection in today’s wired world. Through poignant turns that are both harrowing and touching, the stories intersect with surprising twists that expose a shocking reality into our daily use of technology that mediates and defines our relationships and ultimately our lives.
tagline: Look up
title: Disconnect
plot:
Disconnect is a 2012 American drama film directed by Henry Alex Rubin and written by Justin Mark Sperber. The movie explores several themes that are relevant to our modern society.

One of the primary themes of Disconnect is the impact of technology on human relationships. The film delves into how social media, online harassment, and cyberbullying can affect people's lives, particularly in the context of teenagers and young adults. The story follows four main characters: a teenager who is bullied online, his mother who tries to protect him, a politician who uses her online presence to manipulate public opinion, and a lawyer who defends a client accused of hacking.

Another significant theme in Disconnect is the concept of identity and how it relates to technology. As people spend more time online, they often present a curated version of themselves, hiding their true selves behind a digital facade. This raises questions about authenticity, vulnerability, and the blurring of boundaries between the physical and digital worlds.

The film also touches on issues of social responsibility, accountability, and the consequences of our actions in the digital age. The characters' online behavior has real-world repercussions, highlighting the need for individuals to be mindful of their online presence and its impact on others.

Lastly, Disconnect explores the theme of family dynamics and the importance of human connection in a world where technology is increasingly prevalent. The movie shows how even in the midst of chaos and disconnection, there are moments of love, empathy, and understanding that can bring people together.

Overall, Disconnect offers a thought-provoking commentary on the complexities of modern life, encouraging viewers to think critically about their own relationships with technology and its effects on society.

overview: From a mountain peak in South Korea, a man plummets to his death. Did he jump, or was he pushed? When detective Hae-joon arrives on the scene, he begins to suspect the dead man’s wife Seo-rae. But as he digs deeper into the investigation, he finds himself trapped in a web of deception and desire.
tagline: The Closer You Look, The Harder You Fall.
title: Decision to Leave
plot:
Decision to Leave (Heeojil gyeolsim) is a 2022 South Korean neo-noir romantic mystery directed, co-written and produced by Park Chan-wook. Park Hae-il plays the married detective Jang Hae-jun, and Tang Wei plays Song Seo-rae, a Chinese immigrant whose husband's death brings them together.

Hae-jun, an insomniac Busan detective, sees his wife Jung-an, a nuclear plant manager in Ipo, only on weekends. He and his partner Soo-wan investigate the death of Ki Do-soo, a retired immigration officer found at the foot of a mountain he often climbed. Suspicion falls on Seo-rae, Ki's much younger widow and a caregiver for the elderly, because of her apparent lack of grief and the injuries on her body. During nightly stakeouts outside her apartment, Hae-jun becomes infatuated with her, and she notices him. An alibi and CCTV footage seem to clear her. She also reveals that she helped her terminally ill mother die in China, and that she came to Korea to climb a mountain left to her by her grandfather, an independence fighter. When letters suggest Ki killed himself, Hae-jun closes the case, and the two grow close. Then Hae-jun discovers that Seo-rae swapped phones with a client who has dementia, and that the phone's step count reveals she climbed the mountain on the day of the killing. He confronts her, calls himself "shattered", hides the evidence and tells her to throw the phone into the sea.

Thirteen months later, Hae-jun has moved to Ipo, depressed and sleepless, when he runs into Seo-rae with her new husband, Im Ho-shin, who is found dead in his pool the next day. A Chinese immigrant confesses to killing Ho-shin, but Hae-jun eventually realizes that Seo-rae set the killing in motion. Jung-an leaves him. Seo-rae tells him that Ho-shin had found a recording of Hae-jun telling her he loved her and that she began loving him the moment he stopped. She then buries herself in a pit on a beach as the tide rises, leaving behind the phone with Hae-jun's incriminating words. Hae-jun searches the shore in anguish, unaware that she lies beneath the sand.

Shooting began in October 2020. It premiered in competition at the 2022 Cannes Film Festival, where Park won Best Director, and opened in South Korea on June 29, 2022, at number one. Mubi released it in North America and later made it its most-streamed film. It was acclaimed by critics, scoring 85 on Metacritic, and it made the Oscar shortlist as South Korea's entry and received two BAFTA nominations.

overview: A young girl finds solace in her artist father and the ghost of her dead mother.
tagline: It won't let go.
title: Separation
plot:
Separation is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by William Brent Bell from a screenplay by Nick Amadeus and Josh Braun. It stars Rupert Friend, Mamie Gummer, Madeline Brewer, Violet McGraw, Simon Quarterman and Brian Cox, and follows a father caring for his young daughter after the sudden death of his estranged wife, as the two are tormented by mysterious spirits.

Jeff Vahn, a struggling illustrator, is divorced from his wife, Maggie, who is seeking sole custody of their daughter, Jenny. Shortly after a heated phone argument with Jeff, Maggie is killed in a hit-and-run. After the funeral, her father, Paul Rivers, prepares to sue for custody, while Jenny withdraws into depression and starts behaving strangely. Unable to reach her, Jeff takes a small job at a comic book company through an old friend, and Jenny's babysitter, Samantha Nally, begins looking after her full-time. The house is haunted: Jeff suffers recurring nightmares of spirits roaming the rooms and falls into trances in which he draws monstrous figures that the ghosts then bring to life. The spirits interact with Jenny, and Jeff becomes convinced that Maggie is controlling them in search of revenge from beyond the grave.

After Jenny survives a severe allergic reaction to her food, Jeff decides to move upstate to be near Paul, and the two men settle the custody dispute amicably, while Jeff earns a promotion at work. A private investigator then tells Paul that Maggie's killer was Samantha, who pushes Paul from the second floor of the house; Jeff calls for help and Paul survives. Samantha confesses that she is in love with Jeff and killed Maggie to protect him, and that she poisoned Jenny's food because the girl stood between them. Jeff realizes that Maggie's ghost has indeed returned for vengeance and leads the other spirits, but that her target is Samantha, not him. Maggie kills Samantha. When Jenny climbs into the attic to speak with her mother, she slips, and Jeff falls with her from the window as he tries to catch her. They wake unhurt on the ground, saved by Maggie, whose spirit finally departs as emergency services arrive.

Open Road Films and Briarcliff Entertainment acquired the film in March 2021 and released it on April 30, 2021, It opened fourth at the box office with $1.8 million. Reviews were overwhelmingly negative; Rotten Tomatoes reported 7% approval, calling it a lifeless divorce drama cosplaying as a horror film.

overview: Young princess Anna of Arendelle dreams about finding true love at her sister Elsa’s coronation. Fate takes her on a dangerous journey in an attempt to end the eternal winter that has fallen over the kingdom. She's accompanied by ice delivery man Kristoff, his reindeer Sven, and snowman Olaf. On an adventure where she will find out what friendship, courage, family, and true love really means.
tagline: Only the act of true love will thaw a frozen heart.
title: Frozen
plot:
Frozen is a 2013 animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie follows the story of two sisters, Elsa and Anna, who are princesses of the kingdom of Arendelle.

Elsa, played by Idina Menzel, has the magical power to create and control ice and snow. However, she has been keeping her powers hidden away for fear of hurting those she loves. On the day of Elsa's coronation as the queen of Arendelle, her powers are accidentally revealed, and she inadvertently plunges the kingdom into eternal winter.

Elsa becomes a recluse, fearing that her powers will harm Anna, who is determined to help her sister. Meanwhile, Prince Hans of the Southern Isles arrives in Arendelle, seeking an alliance with Elsa. However, his true intentions are soon revealed, and he betrays Anna's trust.

Anna sets out on a journey to find Elsa, teaming up with Kristoff, an ice harvester, and his loyal reindeer Sven. Along the way, they encounter Olaf, a snowman brought to life by Elsa's magic. Olaf becomes a source of comic relief and serves as a symbol of the joy and innocence that Elsa has lost.

As Anna and Kristoff near Elsa's ice palace, they face numerous obstacles, including Hans' attempts to capture Elsa and take advantage of her powers for his own gain. In the end, Anna's love and determination help Elsa to control her powers and reverse the curse that has been cast over Arendelle.

The movie features a range of memorable characters, including Olaf, who becomes a fan favorite due to his childlike innocence and humor. The film's soundtrack, featuring songs like "Let It Go" and "Do You Want to Build a Snowman?", was widely praised for its catchy melodies and empowering lyrics.

Overall, Frozen is a heartwarming story about the power of sisterly love, acceptance, and self-discovery. The movie's themes of embracing one's true nature and finding inner strength are conveyed through Elsa's journey, making it a beloved classic among audiences of all ages.

overview: Barbie and her best friends Teresa and Renee transform from hard-working gymnasts to undercover secret agents. When their amazing gymnastics skills catch the eye of a top-secret spy agency, the girls are soon following clues to a gem-stealing cat burglar, using high-tech gadgets, glam disguises and cute robo-pets to save the day.
title: Barbie: Spy Squad
plot:
Barbie: Spy Squad is a 2016 American computer-animated action comedy film and the 32nd entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Conrad Helten from a screenplay by Marsha Griffin and Kacey Arnold, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment and music by Gabriel Mann and Rebecca Kneubuhl. It opened in Polish cinemas on 15 January 2016, had limited cinema screenings in the United Kingdom alongside its DVD release there, and was released direct to video in North America by Universal in early 2016, later airing on Nickelodeon. It was the first film with Erica Lindbeck, replacing Kelly Sheridan, as Barbie's voice.

Barbie and her best friends Renee (Stephanie Sheh) and Teresa (Jenny Pellicer) are gymnasts preparing for a championship, though Barbie is shaken after losing focus during the team's pyramid. Renee's Aunt Zoe (Cathy Weseluck), a cat-loving knitter who never misses a meet, invites the girls to a picnic at the Hollywood sign, where a hidden door leads to the headquarters of a secret spy organisation, the International Intelligence and Innovation Agency. Zoe turns out to be its head, Agent Z. Impressed by the girls' agility and teamwork, she recruits them to stop a cat burglar stealing rare gems which, once assembled, could power a device able to shut down the agency's systems.

Trained by Agent Dunbar (Brian Dobson) and equipped by the young inventor Lazlo (Ian Hanlin) with gadgets disguised as make-up and fashion accessories, motorcycles and a robotic dog named Percy, the girls must keep their mission secret even from their sisters. Their inexperience costs them dearly: the thief, a superb gymnast, escapes with a gem at their first stakeout and again at a party where their kitchen disguises end in chaos, and they are dismissed from the agency. Applying Zoe's advice to visualise a move before making it, Barbie recognises the burglar's moves in their rival gymnast Patricia (Rebecca Husain). Following her into headquarters, the girls discover she has been working for Dunbar, who resents being passed over and plans to use the gems to cripple the agency, frame Zoe and take her place. With help from Zoe, their friends and the agency's robots, the girls foil the scheme, Barbie regains her confidence, and Patricia, realising her mistakes, makes friends with the trio.

The supporting cast includes Alyssya Swales as Barbie's younger sister Chelsea, Elizabeth Irving as Mila and Kathleen Barr as Violet.

overview: The Last Avatar is a mystical adventure film, a story of a young man who leaves Hollywood to find himself. What he finds is beyond his wildest imagination. Based on ancient prophecy, contemporary truth seeking and the future of humanity, The Last Avatar is a film that takes transformational themes and makes them relevant for audiences of all ages. Filled with love, magic, mystery, conspiracy, psychics, underground cities, secret societies, light bodies and much more, The Last Avatar tells the story of the emergence of Kalki Avatar- the final Avatar of our current Age of Chaos. Kalki is also a metaphor for the innate power and potential that lies within humanity to awaken and create a world of truth, harmony and possibility.
tagline: We are becoming conscious of our power to re-make the world
title: The Last Avatar
plot: A young man leaves Hollywood to find himself. What he finds is beyond his wildest imagination.

overview: Two corrupt cops in New Mexico set out to blackmail and frame every criminal unfortunate enough to cross their path. Things take a sinister turn, however, when they try to intimidate someone who is more dangerous than they are. Or is he?
tagline: They have the right to remain violent.
title: War on Everyone
plot:
War on Everyone is a dark comedy film that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly in the context of two mismatched hitmen. The movie explores the theme of toxic masculinity, where two men, played by Alexander Skarsgård and Michael Peña, engage in a series of violent and absurd heists, while also struggling with their own emotional vulnerabilities.

The film also touches on the idea of codependency, as the two hitmen form an unlikely bond, relying on each other for support and validation. This dynamic is often played for comedic effect, but it also serves to highlight the deeper psychological issues at play.

Furthermore, War on Everyone critiques the notion of heroism and the glorification of violence in popular culture. The film's portrayal of two anti-heroes who are more interested in their own self-preservation than in achieving any greater good, serves as a commentary on the societal pressures that can lead individuals to engage in destructive behavior.

Overall, War on Everyone is a satirical exploration of toxic masculinity, codependency, and the consequences of violence, presented through a darkly comedic lens.

overview: A 9th century woman of English extraction born in the German city of Ingelheim disguises herself as a man and rises through the Vatican ranks.
production_companies: UFA International Film & TV Production GmbH
title: Pope Joan
plot:
Pope Joan (German: Die Päpstin) is a 2009 epic historical drama film directed by Sönke Wortmann and produced by Bernd Eichinger, based on Donna Woolfolk Cross's novel about the legendary female pope. It stars Johanna Wokalek as Johanna, David Wenham as her lover, Count Gerold, and John Goodman as Pope Sergius II.

Shortly after Charlemagne's death, Johanna is born in Ingelheim am Rhein, the daughter of a harsh village priest. Studying the Bible behind her father's back, she proves far more gifted than her brother Johannes when the scholar Aesculapius visits, and he tutors her against her father's wishes. When a bishop's messenger comes for her, her father sends Johannes instead, but Johanna runs away, joins her brother and reaches the cathedral school at Dorestad, where a reluctant teacher accepts her. Count Gerold takes her into his household and falls in love with her. While he is away fighting for Lothair I, his jealous wife arranges Johanna's marriage, but Vikings attack during the wedding, killing Johannes. Disguised as a man, Johanna enters the Benedictine monastery at Fulda as Brother Johannes Anglicus. Her father, discovering her identity, dies of a stroke while trying to expose her, and when fever strikes the monastery, an old monk who knows her secret helps her avoid examination before she flees, finding shelter with Arn, whose daughter, Arnalda, she tutors.

Resuming her disguise, Johanna travels to Rome as a physician, cures Sergius II of gout and becomes his doctor and later his nomenclator. When Lothair marches on Rome, a hydraulic device swings the palace door shut as if by divine will, and his soldiers kneel. Gerold, in Lothair's army, recognizes Johanna, and she is torn between her two identities. After Lothair's ally Anastasius has Sergius murdered, the people acclaim Johanna as pope. She rules charitably, helping women and children, and makes Gerold head of the papal army, but she becomes pregnant. Gerold is killed by Anastasius's conspirators during the Easter procession, and Johanna dies in childbirth that day. Anastasius succeeds her but is soon deposed and exiled, and in revenge omits her from his history of the popes. Years later her story is revealed by Bishop Arnaldo, who is really Arnalda.

The film premiered in Berlin on 19 October 2009 and opened in Germany three days later. It reached the Italian box office top ten, but drew Vatican criticism, and the Italian bishops' newspaper Avvenire called it extremely limited in vision.

overview: A look at the life of Margaret Thatcher, the former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, with a focus on the price she paid for power.
tagline: Never Compromise.
title: The Iron Lady
plot:
The Iron Lady is a 2011 biographical drama about Margaret Thatcher, the longest-serving British prime minister of the 20th century and the first woman to hold the office. Phyllida Lloyd directed from a screenplay by Abi Morgan, loosely based on John Campbell's biography. Meryl Streep plays Thatcher, with Alexandra Roach as the young Margaret. Jim Broadbent and Harry Lloyd play her husband, Denis, and Anthony Head plays Geoffrey Howe.

In the present day, the elderly Thatcher, now suffering from dementia, keeps seeing and talking to Denis, who has died. Her memories take the story back through her life. As a girl, Margaret Roberts works in her family's grocery shop in Grantham and absorbs the political speeches of the father she idolizes, while her relationship with her mother is distant. She wins a place at Somerville College, Oxford, and later fights to break into a snobbish, male-dominated Conservative Party and win a seat in the House of Commons. She accepts Denis's proposal only after warning him that she will never be content as a housewife: "I don't want to die cleaning a teacup."

The flashbacks follow her through life as one of the few women in Parliament and as education secretary under Edward Heath. They show her friendship with Airey Neave, her run for party leader and her image makeover. As prime minister after the 1979 election, she pushes through monetarist policies and the austere 1981 budget over the doubts of the "wets" in her cabinet. She faces unemployment, riots, the miners' strike and the 1984 Brighton bombing. She sends a task force to recover the Falkland Islands from Argentina, forms an alliance with Ronald Reagan and presides over the late-1980s boom. By 1990, she has become imperious, berating her ministers, defending the poll tax amid riots and resisting European integration. Howe resigns after she humiliates him, Michael Heseltine challenges her and she is forced to resign after eleven years. In the present, Thatcher finally packs away Denis's belongings and tells him to go. As his ghost departs, he assures her that she will be fine on her own, and she washes a teacup alone in her kitchen.

Filming began on December 31, 2010. The film grossed $115 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, and Thatcher's children and biographer criticized its portrayal. Streep's performance was widely acclaimed and won her a third Academy Award, as well as a Golden Globe and a BAFTA. The film also won the Oscar for Best Makeup.

overview: The story of the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962—the nuclear standoff with the USSR sparked by the discovery by the Americans of missile bases established on the Soviet-allied island of Cuba.
tagline: You'll never believe how close we came
title: Thirteen Days
plot:
Thirteen Days is a 2000 historical drama film directed by Roger Donaldson, which tells the story of the Cuban Missile Crisis from the perspective of President John F. Kennedy's advisors.

The movie delves into the intense and suspenseful atmosphere that characterized this pivotal moment in history, as the world teetered on the brink of nuclear war. The main theme of Thirteen Days revolves around the concept of crisis management and decision-making under pressure. The film highlights the complexities and nuances of international diplomacy, showcasing the intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and interests that defined the Cold War era.

At its core, the movie explores the human side of politics, revealing the personal struggles, fears, and motivations of the key players involved in this high-stakes crisis. The characters are multidimensional and flawed, with their own strengths and weaknesses, which adds to the tension and drama of the story.

The film also touches on the theme of leadership and the weight of responsibility that comes with it. As President Kennedy navigates the treacherous waters of the Cuban Missile Crisis, he must balance his own instincts and values with the advice of his advisors, all while keeping the fate of humanity in the balance.

Ultimately, Thirteen Days is a gripping drama that captures the essence of this critical moment in history, offering a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, politics, and the complexities of decision-making under extreme pressure.

original_title: You Don't Mess with the Zohan
overview: An Israeli counterterrorism soldier with a secretly fabulous ambition to become a Manhattan hairstylist. Zohan's desire runs so deep that he'll do anything -- including faking his own death and going head-to-head with an Arab cab driver -- to make his dreams come true.
tagline: Lather. Rinse. Save the world.
title: You Don't Mess with the Zohan
plot:
You Don't Mess with the Zohan is a 2008 American action comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan, starring Adam Sandler as the main character. The movie follows the story of Zohan Dimski (Adam Sandler), an Israeli Mossad agent who fakes his own death to pursue his dream of becoming a hairstylist in New York City.

The film begins with Zohan working for the Mossad, where he is tasked with infiltrating and gathering intelligence on a terrorist organization. During a mission, Zohan kills several terrorists, but not before one of them shoots him in the head.
