The film premiered at BFI Southbank in London on October 28, 2019, and was released by Warner Bros. Pictures in the United Kingdom on November 8 and in the United States on November 15, 2019.

Roy Courtnay is an aging British swindler who uses a string of false identities to gain access to other people's money. In 2009 he sets his sights on Betty McLeish, a recently widowed woman with savings of more than £2 million. After a first date in London, he feigns a bad knee to get himself invited to stay at her house, and soon persuades her to open a joint offshore investment account with him. At the same time, Roy and his partner Vincent are running an elaborate investment scam using fake Russian investors, and when one of their victims discovers he has been robbed and follows Roy through London, Roy kills him at Charing Cross tube station, revealing how dangerous he can be. During a holiday in Berlin, Betty's grandson Stephen confronts him with evidence that the real Roy Courtnay, a young British Army officer, was killed in the city in 1948, and Roy is forced to spin an elaborate new account of his wartime past. Betty appears to accept his explanation, and the couple prepare to transfer their fortunes into the joint account, which Roy intends to empty, leaving her ruined as he has left so many others. But as the con approaches its climax, it becomes clear that Roy is not the only person in the relationship hiding the truth, and that the roots of the deception stretch back to Germany during the Second World War.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 64% of 165 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus that it is less than the sum of its prestigious parts but that McKellen and Mirren keep it consistently watchable, and Metacritic gave it a score of 55 out of 100. It grossed $33.4 million worldwide against a $10 million budget.

original_title: Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico
overview: A friend of Fred's, Alejo Otero, invites the Scooby gang to Veracruz, Mexico. There they find a monster, El Chupacabra, terrorizing the town.
title: Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico
plot:
Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico is a 2003 animated film that follows the Mystery Inc. gang as they travel to Mexico to solve a mystery surrounding a legendary monster said to be terrorizing a small town.

The main themes of Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico include:

1. Friendship: The movie highlights the strong bond between the members of the Mystery Inc. gang, particularly Shaggy and Scooby, who work together to help their friends and solve the mystery.
2. Cultural Exchange: The film showcases the rich cultural heritage of Mexico, introducing American viewers to traditional Mexican music, food, and customs.
3. Teamwork: The gang must put aside their differences and work together to uncover the truth behind the monster legend, demonstrating the importance of collaboration and communication in solving problems.
4. Skepticism vs. Belief: The movie pokes fun at the idea of believing in monsters and supernatural explanations, encouraging viewers to think critically about the evidence presented.

The plot development revolves around the gang's arrival in Mexico, where they meet a local girl named Lupita who is being terrorized by a legendary monster known as El Chupacabra. As the Mystery Inc. gang investigates, they uncover a series of clues and red herrings that lead them on a wild goose chase through the town.

In the end, the gang exposes the truth behind the monster legend, revealing it to be a human culprit in disguise. The movie concludes with the gang enjoying a festive celebration, highlighting the importance of friendship, teamwork, and cultural understanding.

Overall, Scooby-Doo! and the Monster of Mexico is a lighthearted, entertaining film that combines humor, mystery, and adventure, making it a fun watch for both kids and adults.

overview: Alex, a boy obsessed with scary stories, is trapped by a witch in her modern, magical New York City apartment. His original hair-raising tales are the only thing keeping him safe as he desperately tries to find a way out of this twisted place.
tagline: Write for your life.
title: Nightbooks
plot:
Nightbooks is a 2021 American dark fantasy film directed by David Yarovesky from a screenplay by Mikki Daughtry and Tobias Iaconis, based on J. A. White's 2018 children's book. It stars Winslow Fegley as Alex, Lidya Jewett as Yasmin and Krysten Ritter as the witch Natacha, and was released on Netflix on September 15, 2021.

Alex Mosher, a boy from Brooklyn who loves writing scary stories, overhears his parents worrying about his obsession and about how he is coping after a recent incident. Upset, he grabs his notebooks, which he calls his "nightbooks", and heads for the basement to burn them in the furnace, but the elevator stops on a dark floor where an open apartment door reveals a television playing his favorite film, The Lost Boys. Inside, he eats a slice of pumpkin pie and passes out. He wakes up as the prisoner of Natacha, a beautiful witch who lives in a magical apartment and who shows him a closet full of clothes belonging to children who were "not useful" to her. When she learns that he writes scary stories, she spares him on one condition: he must read her a new story every night, and each one must have an unhappy ending. Alex is put to work alongside Yasmin, another captive child who serves as housekeeper, while Natacha's sometimes-invisible cat, Lenore, keeps watch over them. The apartment travels around the world in search of new victims, and its doors open only with Natacha's keys. Searching her vast library for inspiration, Alex discovers notes left in the margins of books by a girl who seems to have been planning an escape, and he nicknames her "Unicorn Girl" after the necklace she describes. As Alex and Yasmin become friends and win over Lenore, they use the notes to plan their own escape, but the apartment holds dark secrets, and Natacha keeps asking Alex why he wanted to destroy his stories.

Nightbooks received positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has an 87% approval rating based on 25 reviews, with a consensus that, though busy and overly familiar, it offers a fun and genuinely scary gateway to horror for younger viewers, and Metacritic gave it a score of 65 out of 100.

overview: Two men get laid off and have to become stay-at-home dads when they can't find jobs, which inspires them to open their own day-care center.
tagline: Who's your daddy?
title: Daddy Day Care
plot:
"Daddy Day Care" is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Steve Carr and starring Eddie Murphy and Jeff Garlin.

The movie follows the story of Charlie Hinton (Eddie Murphy) and Phil Ryerson (Jeff Garlin), two unemployed fathers who start a daycare center in their home. As they navigate the challenges of childcare, they learn valuable lessons about fatherhood, friendship, and growing up.

Some of the main themes of "Daddy Day Care" include:

1. **Redemption and Second Chances**: Charlie and Phil are both struggling to provide for their families, but through their new venture, they find a way to redeem themselves and prove that they're capable parents.
2. **Friendship and Camaraderie**: The unlikely friendship between Charlie and Phil is at the heart of the movie. Despite their differences, they learn to work together and support each other in their endeavors.
3. **Growing Up and Maturity**: As Charlie and Phil navigate the challenges of childcare, they're forced to confront their own immaturity and learn to grow up. This theme is particularly evident in Charlie's character development throughout the movie.
4. **Family and Parenting**: The film explores the importance of family and parenting, highlighting the challenges and rewards that come with raising children.
5. **Self-Discovery and Empowerment**: Through their experiences as daycare providers, Charlie and Phil discover new aspects of themselves and find a sense of purpose and fulfillment.

Overall, "Daddy Day Care" is a heartwarming comedy that explores themes of redemption, friendship, growing up, family, and self-discovery.

overview: As the face of law enforcement in the United States for almost 50 years, J. Edgar Hoover was feared and admired, reviled and revered. But behind closed doors, he held secrets that would have destroyed his image, his career, and his life.
tagline: The most powerful man in the world.
title: J. Edgar
plot:
J. Edgar is a 2011 biographical drama film that delves into the life of J. Edgar Hoover, the infamous director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). The movie masterfully weaves together themes of power, corruption, and the blurred lines between loyalty and obsession.

At its core, J. Edgar explores the complexities of a man who rose to become one of the most powerful figures in American law enforcement, yet struggled with his own demons. Hoover's fixation on the communist threat during the Cold War serves as a backdrop for his personal struggles, including his repressed homosexuality and his all-consuming desire for control.

The film also delves into the theme of identity, as Hoover navigates the constraints of societal norms and expectations. His relationships with those around him, particularly his protégés and romantic interests, serve as a catalyst for his growth and downfall. Through these characters, the movie sheds light on the human cost of Hoover's actions, revealing a complex web of motivations that drive his decisions.

Furthermore, J. Edgar critiques the abuse of power and the dangers of unchecked authority. As Hoover's grip on the FBI tightens, he becomes increasingly isolated and paranoid, leading to a downward spiral of corruption and deceit. The film serves as a cautionary tale about the perils of allowing one individual to wield such immense power without accountability.

Ultimately, J. Edgar is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that raises important questions about the nature of power, loyalty, and identity. Through its nuanced portrayal of Hoover's life, the film offers a searing critique of the darker aspects of American history, leaving viewers to ponder the complexities of a man who both fascinated and repelled us.

overview: A plastic surgeon, romancing a much younger schoolteacher, enlists his loyal assistant to pretend to be his soon to be ex-wife, in order to cover up a careless lie. When more lies backfire, the assistant's kids become involved, and everyone heads off for a weekend in Hawaii that will change all their lives.  A remake of Cactus Flower (1969).
tagline: Sometimes a guy's best wingman... is a wingwoman
title: Just Go with It
plot:
Just Go with It is a 2011 American romantic comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and starring Adam Sandler, Jennifer Aniston, and Brooklyn Decker.

The movie begins with Danny Maccabee (Adam Sandler), a successful plastic surgeon who has been married to his high school sweetheart, Palmer Dodge (Brooklyn Decker), for three years. However, their marriage is on the rocks due to Palmer's lack of interest in sex and her desire to have children. Feeling suffocated by the situation, Danny decides to end the relationship.

One day, while working on a new face, Danny meets Katherine Murphy (Jennifer Aniston), his receptionist who has been secretly admiring him from afar. Katherine is a single mother with a young son, who is struggling to make ends meet after her husband's death. Despite their instant attraction, Danny tries to keep his distance, fearing that he will get hurt again.

However, when Palmer reveals that she is pregnant, Danny sees an opportunity to win her back and proposes a fake engagement to Katherine, claiming that they are having an affair. The plan works initially, but things start to get complicated as Katherine begins to develop real feelings for Danny.

As the story unfolds, Katherine's son, Gabe (Nathan Parsons), becomes a catalyst for change in Danny's life. Through his interactions with Gabe, Danny starts to see Katherine in a different light and realizes that he has fallen in love with her. Meanwhile, Palmer's pregnancy progresses, and she begins to realize that she is not ready to be a mother.

The plot thickens when Katherine discovers the truth about Danny's fake engagement and feels betrayed. However, instead of being angry, she decides to give it another chance and proposes a real relationship to Danny. The movie culminates with Danny and Katherine confessing their love for each other and starting a new life together.

Throughout the film, Adam Sandler delivers his signature comedic charm, while Jennifer Aniston brings warmth and depth to her character. Brooklyn Decker shines as Palmer, providing a perfect foil to the on-screen chemistry between Sandler and Aniston. The movie's lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and engaging storyline make it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Just Go with It is a heartwarming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, engaging plot, and uplifting message, this movie is sure to leave viewers feeling entertained and inspired.

overview: The tale of a workaholic dad-turned-dog who finds that being man's best friend shows him the most important job - being a great dad.
tagline: It's going to be a ruff day.
title: The Shaggy Dog
plot:
The Shaggy Dog is a family comedy film that revolves around the transformation of a man into a shaggy dog. On the surface, it appears to be a lighthearted and humorous tale, but upon closer examination, it explores themes of identity, responsibility, and the importance of human connection.

At its core, The Shaggy Dog is a story about a man who struggles to balance his personal life with his professional responsibilities. When he undergoes a magical transformation into a shaggy dog, he is forced to confront his own flaws and shortcomings. As he navigates this new reality, he learns valuable lessons about the importance of being present in the moment, letting go of his ego, and embracing his true nature.

The film also touches on the theme of family and relationships. The protagonist's transformation serves as a catalyst for him to re-evaluate his priorities and reconnect with those around him. Through his interactions with his wife and children, he comes to appreciate the beauty of simplicity and the importance of being there for the people who matter most.

Furthermore, The Shaggy Dog can be seen as a commentary on the human condition. It pokes fun at our insecurities and flaws, while also reminding us that we are all capable of growth and change. Ultimately, the film suggests that it's never too late to rediscover ourselves and find happiness in the simple things.

Overall, The Shaggy Dog is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, responsibility, and human connection with humor and wit.

overview: The Templeton brothers — Tim and his Boss Baby little bro Ted — have become adults and drifted away from each other. But a new boss baby with a cutting-edge approach and a can-do attitude is about to bring them together again … and inspire a new family business.
tagline: Playtime is over.
title: The Boss Baby: Family Business
plot:
The Boss Baby: Family Business is a 2021 American computer-animated comedy film directed by Tom McGrath, produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures. 

The movie takes place five years after the events of the first film. The Boss Baby (voiced by Alec Baldwin) has been working with his brother Tim (voiced by Miles Bakshi) to help their father, Ted (voiced by Steve Buscemi), who is now retired from being a boss. However, when a new villain emerges in the form of Francis Francisca (voiced by Marisa Tomei), the Boss Baby must team up with his brother and their mother, Janine (voiced by Amy Sedaris), to stop her and save the family business.

Throughout the film, Tim struggles to find his place in the world as a "boss" and prove himself to his father. Meanwhile, Francisca is determined to take over the family business and eliminate the Boss Baby once and for all. The movie features plenty of action, humor, and heartwarming moments as the characters navigate their relationships with each other.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its exploration of themes such as identity, family dynamics, and the challenges of growing up. The movie also expands on the world of the Boss Baby universe, introducing new characters and plotlines that add depth to the story.

Overall, The Boss Baby: Family Business is a fun and entertaining film that is sure to delight both children and adults. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and engaging storyline, it's a great addition to the Boss Baby franchise.

overview: In order to win the Street Dance Championships, a dance crew is forced to work with ballet dancers from the Royal Dance School in exchange for rehearsal space.
tagline: Teo Worlds. One Dream.
title: StreetDance 3D
plot:
StreetDance 3D is a 2010 British dance film that delves into the world of street dance and its cultural significance. At its core, the movie explores the theme of identity and self-expression through dance. The main character, Luke, played by Richard Madden, is a young dancer who finds his passion in street dance, which becomes an outlet for him to express himself and find his place in the world.

The film also touches on the idea of community and belonging. Luke's journey is not just about mastering his dance skills but also about finding a sense of belonging among his peers and mentors. The movie highlights the importance of support systems and the role that positive relationships can play in helping individuals overcome challenges and achieve their goals.

Furthermore, StreetDance 3D examines the tension between tradition and innovation. The film's protagonist is drawn to the raw energy and authenticity of street dance, which contrasts with the more formalized and structured world of competitive dance. This dichotomy serves as a metaphor for the struggle to balance individuality with conformity, highlighting the importance of staying true to oneself while still respecting the traditions that have come before.

Ultimately, StreetDance 3D is a movie about embracing one's passion and finding one's voice through self-expression. The film's themes of identity, community, and tradition are woven together to create a narrative that is both inspiring and thought-provoking.

original_title: Arthur et la vengeance de Maltazard
overview: Arthur answers a distress call from Princess Selenia, who is menaced by the nefarious Maltazard.
title: Arthur and the Revenge of Maltazard
plot:
Arthur and the Revenge of Maltazard is a 2009 French animated fantasy adventure film directed by Luc Besson and produced by Canal+. The movie is based on the first book in the "Asterix" spin-off series, "Astérix and Obelix: The Mansions of the Gods," but it has its own unique storyline.

The main themes of Arthur and the Revenge of Maltazard include:

1. Friendship and Loyalty: The film highlights the strong bond between Arthur and his friends, including Dogmatix, Betamorphous, and Selenia. Their loyalty to each other is tested as they face various challenges and obstacles.
2. Courage and Bravery: Arthur, being the brave and determined leader that he is, shows remarkable courage in the face of danger. He risks everything to protect his friends and the people of Dimwiddlee.
3. Power and Corruption: The character of Maltazard serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of power and corruption. His lust for power and control ultimately lead to his downfall.
4. Self-Discovery: Arthur's journey is also one of self-discovery, as he learns more about himself and his destiny. He must come to terms with his own strengths and weaknesses in order to save the day.

The movie follows Arthur, a young boy who lives in Dimwiddlee, as he discovers that he has magical powers. Maltazard, an evil sorcerer, seeks to exploit these powers for his own gain. With the help of his friends, Arthur must thwart Maltazard's plans and save the kingdom.

Throughout the film, there are many exciting action sequences, memorable characters, and heartwarming moments of friendship and growth. The movie is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of courage, loyalty, and self-discovery.

overview: Jack McCall is a fast-talking literary agent, who can close any deal, any time, any way. He has set his sights on New Age guru Dr. Sinja for his own selfish purposes. But Dr. Sinja is on to him, and Jack’s life comes unglued after a magical Bodhi tree mysteriously appears in his backyard. With every word Jack speaks, a leaf falls from the tree and he realizes that when the last leaf falls, both he and the tree are toast. Words have never failed Jack McCall, but now he’s got to stop talking and conjure up some outrageous ways to communicate or he’s a goner.
tagline: He only has 1000 words left to discover what matters the most.
title: A Thousand Words
plot:
A Thousand Words is a 2012 American fantasy comedy-drama film directed by Brian Robbins and starring Eddie Murphy.

The movie begins with Edward Lewis (Eddie Murphy), a wealthy and successful publishing executive who has lost touch with his roots. He is on the verge of losing his daughter, Michelle (Olivia Wilde), to her mother's neglect. One day, while walking in the woods, he stumbles upon a magical book that contains the words of wisdom from his late father.

As Edward reads the book, he discovers that it has the power to change his life and teach him valuable lessons about love, family, and friendship. The book's words are presented as a series of vignettes, each with its own unique story and message.

Throughout the film, Edward learns to appreciate the simple things in life and reconnects with Michelle, who is struggling to find her place in the world. He also befriends a young boy named Jimmy (Maxwell Haley), who teaches him about the importance of kindness, empathy, and understanding.

As the story unfolds, Edward's transformation from a selfish and materialistic person to someone more compassionate and genuine is remarkable. The film explores themes such as:

1. Redemption: Edward's journey is one of redemption, as he seeks to make amends for past mistakes and become a better person.
2. Family: The movie highlights the importance of family and the need to nurture relationships with loved ones.
3. Self-discovery: Through his experiences, Edward learns to find himself and discover what truly matters in life.
4. Kindness and empathy: The film emphasizes the value of treating others with kindness, compassion, and understanding.

The ending of the movie is heartwarming and uplifting, as Edward's transformation is complete, and he has formed meaningful connections with those around him. Overall, A Thousand Words is a feel-good film that explores themes of personal growth, redemption, and the importance of human relationships.

overview: Set in the southern USA, a racist white man, Hank, falls in love with a black woman named Leticia. Ironically, Hank is a prison guard working on Death Row who executed Leticia's husband. Hank and Leticia's inter-racial affair leads to confusion and new ideas for the two unlikely lovers.
tagline: A lifetime of change can happen in a single moment.
title: Monster's Ball
plot:
Monster's Ball is a 2001 American drama film directed by Marc Forster, produced by Scott Rudin, and written by Eric Roth. The movie stars Billy Bob Thornton, Halle Berry, and Heath Ledger.

The main themes of Monster's Ball revolve around the complex relationships between characters, particularly the exploration of racial tension, redemption, and the human condition. Here are some key themes:

1. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: The film follows the story of Percy Walker (Billy Bob Thornton), a death row supervisor who forms an unlikely bond with his inmate, Leticia Musgrove (Halle Berry). Through their interactions, Percy seeks redemption for past mistakes and learns to confront his own demons.
2. **Racial Tension and Prejudice**: The movie tackles the sensitive topic of racial tension in the American South during the 1970s. Percy's character is a product of this environment, and his relationships with Leticia and other characters are influenced by his upbringing and societal expectations.
3. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Both Percy and Leticia are isolated individuals who find solace in each other's company. Their bond serves as a catalyst for both characters to confront their emotional scars and begin the process of healing.
4. **Mortality and the Human Condition**: The film explores the theme of mortality through Leticia's impending execution. This serves as a reminder of the fragility of life and the importance of human connection in the face of death.
5. **Social Commentary**: Monster's Ball offers commentary on the social issues of its time, including racism, sexism, and the treatment of prisoners. The film challenges the audience to confront these issues and consider the complexities of human relationships.

Overall, Monster's Ball is a powerful drama that explores the intricacies of human relationships, redemption, and personal growth in the face of adversity.

overview: Cherry drifts from college dropout to army medic in Iraq - anchored only by his true love, Emily. But after returning from the war with PTSD, his life spirals into drugs and crime as he struggles to find his place in the world.
tagline: Life leaves a mark.
title: Cherry
plot:
Cherry is an American crime drama of 2021 from directors Anthony and Joe Russo, written by Angela Russo-Otstot and Jessica Goldberg and adapted from Nico Walker's semi-autobiographical novel of 2018. Tom Holland plays the title character, a college student who becomes an army medic and then a heroin-addicted bank robber, with Ciara Bravo as his wife Emily, Jack Reynor as the dealer known as Pills and Coke, Jeff Wahlberg as the soldier Jimenez, Forrest Goodluck as James Lightfoot and Michael Rispoli as Tommy.

Cherry falls for his classmate Emily at first sight, but when she announces that she is leaving to study in Montreal, he enlists in the Army as a medic to escape his heartbreak. Just before he ships out she admits she loves him too, and they marry before his deployment. Over two years of service he witnesses horrors, including the death of his friend Jimenez in a roadside bomb blast, and he returns home with post-traumatic stress. The OxyContin prescribed for his panic attacks becomes an addiction, Emily starts taking the pills herself, and both slide into heroin use.

After the couple consume the drugs stored in a safe they were keeping for Pills and Coke, they learn that the stash belonged to his boss, Black, who will kill them all. Cherry robs a bank to repay the debt and, driven by withdrawal, keeps robbing banks. Emily nearly dies of an overdose, her mother blames Cherry, and she leaves rehab to return to him, insisting she will use with or without him. Cherry recruits Pills and Coke and his friend Lightfoot for bigger robberies; when Pills and Coke bolts mid-heist, the others pick him up, find him shot, and, afraid to go to a hospital, let him die and dump his body. When Black comes to collect, Cherry says goodbye to Emily, pulls one last robbery in which he urges the teller to trip the alarm, pays Black, fires his gun in the air to draw police and gets high one final time before his arrest. He gets clean in prison and, paroled after fourteen years, walks out to find Emily waiting for him.

Apple acquired the film for about $40 million; it opened in select theatres on 26 February 2021 and streamed on Apple TV+ from 12 March. Critics praised Holland and Bravo but faulted the writing and direction, giving it 37% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Andy moves to New York to work in the fashion industry. Her boss is extremely demanding, cruel and won't let her succeed if she doesn't fit into the high class elegant look of their magazine.
tagline: Meet Andy Sachs. A million girls would kill to have her job. She's not one of them.
title: The Devil Wears Prada
plot:
The Devil Wears Prada is a 2006 American comedy-drama film directed by David Frankel, based on the novel of the same name by Lauren Weisberger. The movie stars Anne Hathaway as Andy Sachs, a young and aspiring journalist, and Meryl Streep as Miranda Priestly, the demanding editor-in-chief of Runway magazine.

The film begins with Andy Sachs (Anne Hathaway), a recent college graduate who lands an entry-level job at Runway magazine despite having no experience in fashion. She is hired by Miranda Priestly (Meryl Streep), who is notorious for being ruthless and demanding. Andy's new boss is not only a fashion icon but also a formidable figure who expects nothing but perfection from her employees.

As Andy navigates the challenges of working at Runway, she struggles to balance her job with her personal life. She moves into a small apartment in Manhattan and starts dating Nate Cooper (Adrian Grenier), a charming and laid-back journalist. However, their relationship is put to the test as Andy becomes increasingly consumed by her job.

Miranda Priestly's character is a complex and multifaceted one, with a backstory that is slowly revealed throughout the film. Despite her tough exterior, she has a vulnerable side that is exposed when Andy discovers a photo of her as a young woman, which shows her to be more relatable and human than initially thought.

As the story progresses, Andy becomes embroiled in Miranda's personal life, including her complicated relationship with her daughter Emily (Emily Blunt). The two women engage in a series of verbal sparring matches, with Miranda pushing Andy to her limits as she tries to prove herself worthy of working at Runway.

Throughout the film, there are several key plot developments that drive the story forward. One notable moment is when Andy discovers that Miranda has been using her personal assistant Emily to do her bidding, rather than hiring a professional assistant. This revelation sparks a chain reaction of events that ultimately leads to Andy's departure from Runway.

The film culminates with Andy leaving her job at Runway and moving back in with her mother. However, the experience has changed her, and she is now more confident and self-assured. The final scene shows Andy walking down the street, looking stylish and put-together, as if she has finally found her place in the world.

Overall, The Devil Wears Prada is a witty and engaging film that explores themes of identity, ambition, and the challenges of working in a demanding industry. Meryl Streep's performance as Miranda Priestly is particularly noteworthy, as she brings depth and nuance to a character who could have easily been one-dimensional.

original_title: The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor
overview: Archaeologist Rick O'Connell travels to China, pitting him against an emperor from the 2,000-year-old Han dynasty who's returned from the dead to pursue a quest for world domination. This time, O'Connell enlists the help of his wife and son to quash the so-called 'Dragon Emperor' and his abuse of supernatural power.
tagline: A New Evil Awakens.
title: The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor
plot:
The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor is a 2008 action-adventure film directed by Rob Cohen, starring Brendan Fraser, Maria Bello, and Jet Li. The movie is the third installment in the Mummy film series.

Beginning:
The film starts with an elderly Jonathan Carnahan (John Hannah), who has been searching for his father's lost treasure for years. He finally finds it, but it comes with a curse that slowly drives him mad. Meanwhile, Evelyn Carnahan (Maria Bello) and her brother Alex (Jake Abbot) are on a plane flying over the Himalayas when they encounter a mysterious dragon-shaped object in the sky.

Plot Development:
The story then shifts to 1935, where we meet our main characters: Evelyn Carnahan, an expert in ancient artifacts; Jonathan Carnahan, a treasure hunter; and Alex O'Connell (Jake Abbot), their nephew. They are on a mission to find the legendary tomb of Han, the first emperor of China, which is said to be hidden deep within the Himalayas.

As they journey through the treacherous mountains, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, they meet a mysterious warrior named Lin (Pei Pei), who joins their quest.

Upon reaching the tomb, they discover that it is guarded by an army of undead warriors, led by the powerful Scorpion King (Dwayne Johnson). The Scorpion King is revealed to be the reincarnation of Han's brother, and he seeks revenge against Evelyn for stealing his father's treasure.

As the group navigates the treacherous tomb, they uncover a series of booby traps and puzzles that must be solved in order to reach the heart of the tomb. Along the way, they also discover that Lin is actually the reincarnation of Han's daughter, who was killed by the Scorpion King.

Ending:
In the final showdown, Evelyn and her brother Alex face off against the Scorpion King, while Jonathan tries to escape with the treasure. However, the curse of the tomb ultimately catches up with him, and he is killed by the Scorpion King.

Evelyn and Alex manage to defeat the Scorpion King, but not before he reveals that he has been searching for a way to break the curse that has haunted his family for centuries. In the end, Evelyn and Alex escape the tomb, but not without realizing that they have been changed forever by their experiences.

Overall, The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor is an action-packed adventure film with plenty of twists and turns. While it may not be as well-received as its predecessors, it still delivers on its promise of excitement and thrills.

overview: It's the ultimate fairytale musical! Barbie stars as Alexa, a shy princess who discovers a secret door in her kingdom and enters a whimsical land filled with magical creatures and surprises. Inside, Alexa meets Romy and Nori, a mermaid and a fairy, who explain that a spoiled ruler named Malucia is trying to take all the magic in the land. To her surprise, Alexa has magical powers in this world, and her new friends are certain that only she can restore their magic. Discover what happens when Alexa finds the courage to stand up for what's right and learns that the power of friendship is far more precious than magic.
title: Barbie and the Secret Door
plot:
Barbie and the Secret Door is a computer-animated musical fantasy of 2014 directed by Karen Lloyd, the 28th entry in the Barbie film series. Kelly Sheridan voices Princess Alexa, with Brittany McDonald providing her singing voice, Ashleigh Ball as the fairy Nori, Chanelle Peloso as the mermaid Romy and Tabitha St. Germain as the villainous child princess Malucia; Christopher Gaze, Andrea Libman and Andrew Francis are also in the cast.

Alexa is the shy princess of a modern-day kingdom who shrinks from her royal duties. To encourage her, her grandmother gives her a storybook about a princess who discovers she has magic, and while reading it Alexa finds a hidden door in the palace gardens. Stepping through, she lands in the magical land of Zinnia, where her dress is transformed and a wand appears in her hair. She meets Nori, a fairy who has lost her wings, and Romy, a mermaid who has legs instead of a tail, both thrilled that a princess has arrived to fix their troubles.

Their realm is menaced by Malucia, a spoiled young princess born without magic, who seizes it by force from every creature she can catch and stores it in her sceptre. In a glade where fairies, mermaids and unicorns hide from her, Alexa slowly learns to use her wand but cannot restore her friends, whose magic is trapped in the sceptre. Hoping to protect the Queen Unicorn, the most magical being in the realm, the three set out to find her but unwittingly lead Malucia and her minions to her, and the queen is captured. Alexa finds the door home yet chooses to stay. At Malucia's palace the friends watch the villain drain the unicorns' magic, and Alexa challenges her to a magical duel over who is the true princess. Noticing that the overloaded sceptre is cracking, Alexa lets Malucia take all her magic, and the sceptre bursts, releasing every stolen power. Now able to work magic without a wand, Alexa returns it to its owners and goes home with new confidence, while Malucia's parents come back from holiday and scold her for her schemes.

The film features songs such as "If I Had Magic" and "I Want It All", with a soundtrack album released in August 2014. It was released on DVD on 16 September 2014, debuted on Nickelodeon that November, and grossed about $2 million in limited theatrical runs overseas.

original_title: Tom and Jerry Meet Sherlock Holmes
overview: Tom and Jerry need to learn to work together in order to help Sherlock Holmes with an investigation of a jewel theft. But still, they are cat and mouse!
title: Tom and Jerry Meet Sherlock Holmes
plot:
Tom and Jerry Meet Sherlock Holmes is an animated comedy film that brings together two beloved characters from different eras. The movie follows the adventures of Tom, Jerry, and their new ally, Sherlock Holmes, as they team up to solve a mystery in Victorian-era London.

At its core, the film explores the theme of friendship and unlikely alliances. Despite being natural enemies, Tom and Jerry put aside their differences to work together with Sherlock Holmes, who is initially perplexed by their antics but eventually warms up to them. This unlikely trio forms a strong bond, showcasing that even the most disparate individuals can come together to achieve a common goal.

The movie also delves into the theme of intelligence and wit. Sherlock Holmes, being the iconic detective, uses his extraordinary abilities to unravel the mystery, while Tom and Jerry employ their cunning and resourcefulness to outsmart their adversaries. The film highlights the importance of using one's unique skills and talents to overcome challenges.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the idea of adaptation and flexibility. As Tom and Jerry navigate the unfamiliar world of Victorian London, they must learn to adapt to new situations and environments. This theme is also reflected in Sherlock Holmes' ability to adjust his methods to suit the situation, demonstrating that being open-minded and willing to change can be a key factor in success.

Overall, Tom and Jerry Meet Sherlock Holmes is a lighthearted, entertaining film that celebrates the power of friendship, intelligence, and adaptability.

overview: A coming-of-age story centered around a small-town singer brokenhearted by the death of her brother in a car crash, who had secretly submitted her for a summer session at a performing arts academy in Los Angeles. In the academy, she experiences a whole new way of life in the big city, far from the small town lifestyle she's used to.
tagline: Don't Hold Back ...Don't Give Up.
title: Raise Your Voice
plot:
Raise Your Voice is a 2004 American drama film that revolves around the life of Terri Fletcher, a young and talented singer who returns to her hometown after being homeschooled by her mother. The movie explores themes of self-discovery, redemption, and the struggle for acceptance.

At its core, Raise Your Voice is a story about finding one's identity and purpose in life. Terri, played by Hilary Duff, has been isolated from the world due to her mother's overprotectiveness, but as she navigates her relationships with her peers and mentors, she begins to uncover her own passions and interests.

The film also delves into the theme of redemption, as Terri seeks to make amends for past mistakes and hurtful behavior. Her journey is marked by a series of challenges and setbacks, but ultimately, she emerges stronger and more resilient.

Furthermore, Raise Your Voice touches on the theme of acceptance and belonging. Terri's struggles to fit in with her peers serve as a metaphor for the difficulties many people face in finding their place in the world. The movie suggests that true acceptance comes from within, and that embracing one's individuality is essential to happiness and fulfillment.

Overall, Raise Your Voice is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores universal themes of self-discovery, redemption, and acceptance.

overview: James Bond is sent to investigate after a fellow “00” agent is found dead with a priceless Indian Fabergé egg. Bond follows the mystery and uncovers a smuggling scandal and a Russian General who wants to provoke a new World War.
tagline: James Bond's all time high.
title: Octopussy
plot:
Octopussy is a 1983 spy film produced by Eon Productions, starring Roger Moore as James Bond. The movie follows Bond's mission to stop a group of terrorists who plan to detonate a nuclear bomb during the annual Festival of India in London.

The story begins with Bond attending an exhibition of Indian artifacts at the London Museum, where he meets Octopussy (Maud Adams), a beautiful and mysterious woman who is also a member of a circus troupe. Unbeknownst to Bond, Octopussy is actually Kamal Khan's (Louis Jourdan) accomplice, working with him to steal a valuable Fabergé egg.

Kamal Khan, a wealthy businessman, has stolen the Fabergé egg and plans to sell it to General Orlov (Steven Berkoff), a Soviet general who intends to use its value to fund his country's nuclear program. Bond soon discovers that Octopussy is not what she seems, and he begins to unravel the mystery behind her true identity.

As Bond delves deeper into the plot, he encounters a group of terrorists led by Kamal Khan, who plan to detonate a nuclear bomb during the Festival of India in London. The bomb will be triggered by a device hidden inside a Fabergé egg, which will explode when the egg is opened.

Bond teams up with Octopussy, and together they embark on a mission to stop the terrorists and prevent the bombing. Along the way, Bond must navigate through a complex web of espionage, deception, and betrayal.

As the story unfolds, Bond discovers that General Orlov has been using Kamal Khan's stolen Fabergé egg as leverage to manipulate world events. The general plans to use the bomb to spark a global crisis, allowing him to gain control over the world's nuclear arsenals.

In the climactic final scene, Bond and Octopussy face off against Kamal Khan and General Orlov at the Festival of India. In a thrilling sequence of events, Bond uses his skills and gadgets to outwit the villains and prevent the bombing.

In the end, Bond and Octopussy succeed in stopping the terrorists, and the world is saved from a catastrophic nuclear disaster. As for Octopussy, her true identity as Kamal Khan's accomplice is revealed, but she has already fallen in love with Bond, and their relationship becomes a central theme of the film.

Overall, Octopussy is an entertaining and action-packed spy thriller that showcases Roger Moore's signature charm and wit as James Bond. The movie features stunning stunts, memorable characters, and a complex plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

overview: A mysterious woman recounts the rise and fall of Nikodem "Nikoś" Skotarczak, one of the biggest gangsters in Poland's history. Inspired by a true story.
title: How I Fell in Love with a Gangster
plot:
How I Fell in Love with a Gangster (Polish: Jak pokochałam gangstera) is a 2022 Polish crime drama directed by Maciej Kawulski, who co-wrote it with Krzysztof Gureczny. Inspired by the life of the real Gdańsk gangster Nikodem "Nikoś" Skotarczak and described as partly fictionalized, the film stars Tomasz Włosok as Nikoś, with Aleks Kurdzielewicz as the young Nikoś and Antoni Królikowski as his best friend, Komo. Agnieszka Grochowska, Magdalena Lamparska, Eryk Lubos and Sebastian Fabijański also appear.

The story is framed as an interview in which a mysterious woman, one of Nikoś's former lovers, recounts his life to an eager young journalist. Nikoś grows up in Gdańsk with a father who beats him. As a boy on the docks, he watches a man use currency exchange to swindle people and discovers his calling as a hustler. After teenage scams, he joins the criminal enterprise of the local crime lord Kleks and gathers his own circle of delinquents. With Komo at his side, Nikoś moves from petty crime to stealing cars in Germany and selling them in Poland, a hugely profitable trade that makes him the underworld ruler of the Polish coast, the "King of the Coast."

Charming and easygoing, Nikoś seems to succeed without effort. He marries twice and has children, opens an illegal casino frequented by both militiamen and criminals, buys a ranch for his family and even buys his hometown football team. Through every relationship, including those with Halina and Nikita, he stays bound to Milena, known as Czarna, perhaps the one person who truly understands him. By the 1980s, cocaine has entered his world, a German police inspector is pursuing him, and rivals such as the volatile Silvio are closing in. Arrests and prison feuds pile up as Nikoś sinks into addiction and grows haunted by visions of his younger self. Characters regularly break the fourth wall to dispute the story's details.

The roughly three-hour film was released on Netflix in January 2022. Critics noted the clear influence of Martin Scorsese and Goodfellas. Decider recommended it despite its length. Aurora Amidon of Paste found it stylish but derivative. Marc Miller of Ready Steady Cut dismissed it as a ridiculous Goodfellas imitation, and Barbara Jaros of Onet.pl criticized its romanticizing of criminal life and its passive female characters. Skotarczak's last wife sued Kawulski, Open Mind Production and Netflix, claiming the film violated her personal rights and the memory of her late husband.

original_title: Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers
overview: In Disney's take on the Alexander Dumas tale, Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck and Goofy want nothing more than to perform brave deeds on behalf of their queen (Minnie Mouse), but they're stymied by the head Musketeer, Pete. Pete secretly wants to get rid of the queen, so he appoints Mickey and his bumbling friends as guardians to Minnie, thinking such a maneuver will ensure his scheme's success. The score features songs based on familiar classical melodies.
tagline: All for fun and fun for all
title: Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers
plot:
Mickey, Donald, Goofy: The Three Musketeers is an American animated musical adventure of 2004 directed by Donovan Cook and produced by Walt Disney Pictures with the Australian unit of Disneytoon Studios. Loosely drawn from Alexandre Dumas's novel, it was the first feature-length film to star the three friends together. Wayne Allwine voices Mickey Mouse, Tony Anselmo Donald Duck and Bill Farmer both Goofy and Pluto, with Russi Taylor as Minnie, Tress MacNeille as Daisy, Jim Cummings as Pete, April Winchell as Clarabelle Cow and Rob Paulsen as the narrating Troubadour.

The Troubadour, a music-loving French tortoise, tells the tale from his comic book. In 17th-century France, the street urchins Mickey, Donald, Goofy and Pluto are rescued from the bullying Beagle Boys by royal musketeers, who give Mickey a hat and inspire the friends to become musketeers themselves. Years later they are merely janitors at musketeer headquarters, run by Captain Pete, who secretly plans to depose Princess Minnie and crown himself king. After the Beagle Boys, in Pete's pay, nearly assassinate her, Minnie demands musketeer bodyguards, and Pete appoints the three janitors, assuming they will be easy to dispose of.

On a carriage ride the Beagle Boys kidnap Minnie and her lady-in-waiting Daisy. Mickey and Goofy track them to a tower and defeat them while a frightened Donald hangs back, and Mickey and Minnie begin a romance. Pete then targets the heroes one by one: his lieutenant Clarabelle lures Goofy away and tries to drown him in the Seine, only to fall in love with him, while Mickey, warned by Donald of Pete's treachery, is locked in a flooding dungeon at Mont Saint-Michel. Scolded by the Troubadour for his cowardice, Donald joins Goofy and Pluto to free Mickey. At the opera, where a disguised Beagle Boy posing as Minnie proclaims Pete king, the musketeers battle the villains on stage and rescue the princess and Daisy, who declare their love for Mickey and Donald. Minnie then makes the three friends royal musketeers at last.

The songs set new comic lyrics to classical pieces and include a cover of "Three Is a Magic Number". After a limited screening at the El Capitan Theatre, the film was released on DVD and VHS on 17 August 2004, the first Disney DVD with the FastPlay feature. Reviews were mixed, praising the music and action, and it scored 42% on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: Ali Wong might be seven-months pregnant, but there’s not a fetus in the world that can stop this acerbic and savage train of comedy from delivering a masterful hour of stand-up.
title: Ali Wong: Baby Cobra
plot:
Ali Wong: Baby Cobra is a 2016 American comedy film that explores themes of motherhood, identity, and feminism through the lens of Ali Wong's personal experiences. The movie delves into the challenges of navigating modern life as a single Asian-American mother, tackling topics such as societal expectations, body image, and the struggles of balancing career ambitions with family responsibilities.

The film also touches on Wong's own experiences with racism, sexism, and cultural identity, offering a candid and humorous look at the complexities of being a woman of color in America. Through her storytelling, Wong sheds light on the often-overlooked realities faced by Asian-American mothers, who are frequently expected to conform to traditional roles while navigating their own desires and aspirations.

Ultimately, Baby Cobra is a powerful exploration of what it means to be a strong, independent woman in today's society, one that challenges societal norms and expectations while celebrating the beauty of imperfection and authenticity. The film features Wong's signature wit and humor, making it an entertaining and thought-provoking watch for audiences looking for a fresh take on motherhood and identity.

overview: Dr. Adrian Helmsley, part of a worldwide geophysical team investigating the effect on the earth of radiation from unprecedented solar storms, learns that the earth's core is heating up. He warns U.S. President Thomas Wilson that the crust of the earth is becoming unstable and that without proper preparations for saving a fraction of the world's population, the entire race is doomed. Meanwhile, writer Jackson Curtis stumbles on the same information. While the world's leaders race to build "arks" to escape the impending cataclysm, Curtis struggles to find a way to save his family. Meanwhile, volcanic eruptions and earthquakes of unprecedented strength wreak havoc around the world.
tagline: We Were Warned.
plot:
2012 is an American disaster film of 2009 directed by Roland Emmerich, who wrote it with Harald Kloser, inspired by the 2012 doomsday phenomenon. John Cusack stars as the struggling novelist Jackson Curtis and Chiwetel Ejiofor as the geologist Adrian Helmsley, with Amanda Peet as Jackson's former wife Kate, Oliver Platt as White House chief of staff Carl Anheuser, Thandie Newton as Laura Wilson, Danny Glover as President Thomas Wilson and Woody Harrelson as the conspiracy theorist Charlie Frost.

In 2009, Adrian learns from an astrophysicist in India that neutrinos from a solar flare are heating the Earth's core, and he warns the White House. The G8 and China begin building giant arks in Tibet, secretly funding them in part by selling places to the very rich for a billion euros each. By 2012, Jackson works as a limousine driver for the Russian billionaire Yuri Karpov. On a camping trip to Yellowstone with his children, Noah and Lilly, he finds the lake dried up and meets Charlie, a radio host who claims that the world is about to end and that governments are hiding it. Convinced after a string of warning signs, Jackson rents a small plane and rescues Kate, the children and her boyfriend Gordon just as a colossal earthquake sends California into the Pacific.

The group flies to Yellowstone to retrieve Charlie's map of the arks as the caldera erupts and kills him, then join the Karpovs aboard a huge Antonov cargo jet piloted by Sasha and Gordon. As the Earth's crust shifts, billions die, including President Wilson, who stayed in Washington. The Antonov crash-lands in the Himalayas, killing Sasha, and only the ticket-holding Karpovs are flown away. A Tibetan family helps the Curtises stow away on Ark 4. When a megatsunami approaches, Adrian persuades the world leaders to open the gates to the stranded crowds; Yuri dies saving his sons and Gordon is crushed. A tool jammed in the gate floods the ark and sends it drifting towards Mount Everest until Jackson and Noah dislodge it. Weeks later the arks head for the Cape of Good Hope, where the Drakensberg are now the world's highest mountains, and Jackson reconciles with Kate.

Shot in Vancouver in 2008, the film opened on 13 November 2009 and grossed $791.2 million worldwide against a $200 million budget, one of the top earners of the year. Critics praised the spectacle but not the script, giving it 40% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Roger Ebert awarded it three and a half stars.

original_title: Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call - New Orleans
overview: Terrence McDonagh is a New Orleans Police sergeant, who recieves a medal and a promotion to lieutenant for heroism during Hurricane Katrina. Due to his heroic act, McDonagh injures his back and becomes addicted to prescription pain medication. He then finds himself involved with a drug dealer who is suspected of murdering a family of African immigrants.
tagline: The only criminal he can't catch is himself.
title: Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call - New Orleans
plot:
Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call New Orleans is a 2009 American black comedy crime drama film directed by Werner Herzog and written by William Finkelstein. It stars Nicolas Cage in the title role as Terence McDonagh, a drug-addicted New Orleans detective, with Eva Mendes, Val Kilmer and Alvin "Xzibit" Joiner. Herzog described it as a spiritual successor to the 1992 film Bad Lieutenant rather than a remake.

In August 2005, during Hurricane Katrina, police sergeant McDonagh discovers that a prisoner has been left behind in a flooding jail. After mocking the man with his partner, Stevie Pruit, he jumps in and saves him, injuring his back. He is decorated for valor, promoted to lieutenant and prescribed Vicodin. Six months later he is addicted not only to painkillers but also to cocaine and other drugs, which he shares with his girlfriend, Frankie, a prostitute, and obtains from the evidence room or by bullying people. He is estranged from his father and stepmother.

McDonagh is assigned to investigate the murder of a family of five Senegalese immigrants who were killed for selling drugs in the territory of a gang leader, Big Fate. While the case unfolds, he roughs up and robs a well-connected client who beat Frankie, threatens an elderly nursing home resident to force the grandmother of a missing witness to reveal his whereabouts, and falls deep into debt with his bookie. After the client's associates demand $50,000 in compensation and McDonagh is placed on modified duty, he goes into partnership with Big Fate, feeding him police information. When the gangsters come for their money, Big Fate's crew kills them. McDonagh then persuades Big Fate to smoke from his "lucky crack pipe," plants it at the murder scene and has the gang arrested. When Stevie proposes killing Big Fate to steal his money, McDonagh refuses and makes the arrest by the book, and he is promoted to captain. A year later, he seems to have cleaned up, as have Frankie, now pregnant with his child, and his parents, but he is still using heroin. At the city's aquarium, he meets the prisoner he rescued, now sober, who offers to help him, and the two sit before a giant fish tank.

The film premiered at the 66th Venice International Film Festival in September 2009 and was released in the United States by First Look Studios on November 20, 2009, grossing $10.6 million worldwide. Critics praised Herzog's fearless direction and Cage's unhinged performance, with 86% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

overview: An accomplished headhunter risks everything to obtain a valuable painting owned by a former mercenary.
tagline: The hunt is on.
title: Headhunters
plot:
Headhunters is a 2011 Norwegian thriller film directed by Morten Tyldum. The movie revolves around Martin Bressau, a charming and cunning headhunter who becomes embroiled in a complex web of deceit and obsession.

At its core, Headhunters explores the theme of identity and how it can be both a source of strength and weakness. Martin's character is a master manipulator, using his charm and intelligence to get what he wants from people, but this also makes him vulnerable to being manipulated himself. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Martin's carefully constructed facade is fragile and easily pierced.

The film also delves into the theme of class and social status, highlighting the tensions between those who have power and influence, and those who are marginalized or oppressed. Martin's world is one of luxury and privilege, but this comes at a cost, as he is forced to navigate a complex web of relationships and alliances that ultimately threaten his very existence.

Furthermore, Headhunters touches on the theme of obsession and the destructive nature of unchecked desire. Martin's fixation on Gyda, a beautiful and alluring woman, drives much of the plot, but it also leads him down a path of self-destruction. The film suggests that when we become too fixated on something or someone, we can lose sight of what is truly important and become trapped in our own desires.

Overall, Headhunters is a gripping thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the complexities and flaws that make us who we are.

overview: A man steps out of a park fountain in Ho Chi Minh City with no recollection of who he is or where he came from. As he wanders through the city, piecing together clues to his past, he is relentlessly pursued by mysterious figures.
title: Abduction
plot:
Abduction, also known as Twilight Zodiac, is a 2019 science fiction action film directed by Ernie Barbarash and written by Mike MacLean, with cinematography by Phil Parmet and music by Marc Vanocur. A China-backed production made by Ace Films, Beijing iQIYI Technology, Pandora Culture & Media and Red Sea Media, with Roger Corman among its producers, it was shot in Vietnam and China and released on 20 March 2019. It stars Scott Adkins as Andrew Quinn, Andy On as Connor and Truong Ngoc Anh as Dr. Anna Pham, with Lily Ji, Aki Aleong, Daniel Whyte, Mike Leeder, Tom Caserto, Brahim Achabbakhe and Jai Day. Tim Man choreographed the fights, and it runs 98 minutes.

Quinn pulls himself out of a park fountain in Ho Chi Minh City, soaking wet and with no clear memory of who he is, only fragmented visions of a rotting labyrinth, cloaked figures who can bend reality and his missing daughter Lucy. He discovers that three days earlier, by his own reckoning, he was in England in 1985, but it is now 2018. Struggling to speak through a severe stammer, he wanders the city and is pursued by mysterious figures. Meanwhile Connor, a former military man working as an assassin for a local Chinese gang boss, wakes to find his wife gone; dismissing what seemed a dream of aliens taking her, he blames a rival gang and goes on the warpath. The psychiatrist Dr. Pham, who treats Quinn, brings the two men together, and they learn that an invisible alien race stationed above the fountain is abducting people with especially strong qi, the life force it needs to return home. The drones serving the aliens can only be stopped by pulling a small robotic spider from their necks. Together the trio set out to rescue the abducted and stop a portal to the aliens' world from opening.

The Blu-ray release included both a director's cut and a producer's cut. Reviews were mixed to positive. Justin Harrison of Birth.Movies.Death. called it shaky but enjoyable, praising Adkins for playing against type as a vulnerable, disoriented hero and the film's eerie atmosphere, while faulting its blunt exposition and familiar characters. Paul Bramhall of City on Fire rated it 7 out of 10, enjoying its goofy premise, Adkins's rare comedic turn, his reunion with On and the fight choreography.

overview: After moving from their home to an apartment building, a new terror awaits Rini’s family.
tagline: A Mother's Terror is Forever.
title: Satan's Slaves 2: Communion
plot:
Satan's Slaves 2: Communion (Indonesian: Pengabdi Setan 2: Communion) is a 2022 Indonesian supernatural horror film written and directed by Joko Anwar. A sequel to Satan's Slaves (2017), itself based on the 1980 film Satan's Slave, it stars Tara Basro as Rini, Endy Arfian as Toni, Nasar Anuz as Bondi and Bront Palarae as their father Bahri, with Ayu Laksmi as the siblings' late mother, Mawarni. It was the first Indonesian film released in the IMAX format.

In 1955, the journalist Budiman is summoned by his friend Heru, a police commander, to the Bosscha Observatory, where dozens of exhumed corpses have been found prostrate before a framed portrait of a woman named Mawarni after an overnight cult ritual. Ordered to keep the story quiet ahead of the Bandung Conference, Heru urges Budiman to publish it in obscure magazines. In 1984, Rini, her brothers Toni and Bondi and their father Bahri have spent three years living in a flat in the run-down Mandara Apartments in Jakarta, where Bahri works odd jobs and keeps a locked briefcase at home. Budiman, now editor of an occult magazine, receives Heru's suicide note along with photographs and drawings pointing to imminent cult activity at Mandara, and revealing that Bahri was one of the officers present back in 1955. When the building's lift malfunctions and plunges, killing many tenants, a violent storm floods the complex, cuts off the electricity and traps the residents inside overnight. Rini comforts Wisnu, a boy whose mother died in the lift and who knows a secret sign language learned from an occult book. As supernatural forces begin to torment the tenants, the siblings uncover evidence that the cult gathers every 29 years on 17 April, the following day, and find photographs linking their mother to a mysterious figure named Raminom. With the dead rising in the darkened corridors, the family must confront the truth about their parents' past and the fate of their youngest brother, Ian, who was taken by the cult.

The film opened at number one at the Indonesian box office, passing one million admissions in two days and two million in four, and with 6.3 million admissions it became one of the highest-grossing Indonesian films of all time. On Rotten Tomatoes, all 11 critics' reviews are positive.

overview: Powered with incredible speed, Sonic The Hedgehog embraces his new home on Earth. That is, until Sonic sparks the attention of super-uncool evil genius Dr. Robotnik. Now it’s super-villain vs. super-sonic in an all-out race across the globe to stop Robotnik from using Sonic’s unique power for world domination.
tagline: A whole new speed of hero.
title: Sonic the Hedgehog
plot:
Sonic the Hedgehog is a 2020 American live-action/animated comedy-adventure film directed by Jeff Fowler, produced by Neal H. Moritz and Terence Nance, and written by Pat Casey, Josh Miller, and John Whittington.

The movie follows the story of Sonic (voiced by Ben Schwartz), a blue anthropomorphic hedgehog with superhuman speed, who is on the run from Dr. Eggman (Jim Carrey), his arch-nemesis. Sonic lives in the Green Hill Zone, where he spends his days racing and having fun. However, when Dr. Eggman threatens to destroy the world using an army of robotic robots, Sonic decides to leave his home and find a new place to live.

Sonic arrives in the city of Greenhaven, where he meets Tom Wachowski (James Marsden), a single father who is struggling to connect with his 6-year-old son, Ben (Griffin Gluck). Despite initial reservations, Tom takes Sonic under his wing, and the two form an unlikely bond. As Sonic tries to adjust to life in the city, he must also evade Dr. Eggman's robots and stop him from carrying out his evil plans.

Throughout the movie, Sonic's character is portrayed as a lovable and mischievous troublemaker who often gets into humorous situations. The film features plenty of action-packed sequences, including high-speed chases and showdowns with Dr. Eggman's robots.

One of the standout aspects of the movie is its blend of live-action and animation. The CGI work is impressive, bringing Sonic to life in a way that feels both authentic and endearing. Jim Carrey's performance as Dr. Eggman is also noteworthy, capturing the character's manic energy and over-the-top personality.

Overall, Sonic the Hedgehog is a fun and entertaining film that brings the beloved video game character to the big screen. While it may not be a perfect adaptation, the movie's lighthearted tone and comedic moments make it a enjoyable watch for fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

overview: In the phantasmagorical town of Raven's End, a misguided young girl takes refuge in a decrepit old mortuary. The eccentric undertaker chronicles the strange history of the town through a series of twisted tales, each more terrifying than the last, but the young girl's world is unhinged when she discovers that the final story... is her own.
tagline: Every Corpse Has a Story
title: The Mortuary Collection
plot:
The Mortuary Collection is a 2020 American anthology horror film directed by Ryan Spindell and written by Ryan Spindell and Josh Stolberg. The movie consists of five segments, each with its own unique story and characters.

One of the main themes of The Mortuary Collection is the exploration of grief and loss. Each segment deals with a different character's experience of dealing with death, whether it be a personal loss or a traumatic event. The film shows how people cope with their emotions in different ways, ranging from denial to acceptance.

Another theme present in the movie is the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Many characters in the film have experienced traumatic events in the past, which continue to haunt them in various ways throughout the story.

The Mortuary Collection also touches on the concept of mortality and the fear of death. The title itself suggests a sense of foreboding and dread, which is reflected in the film's atmosphere and tone. The characters' experiences are often marked by a sense of unease and discomfort, highlighting their deep-seated fears about dying.

The film also explores the idea of mental health and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Many characters struggle with their own sanity, questioning what is real and what is just a product of their imagination.

Finally, The Mortuary Collection can be seen as a commentary on the human condition, highlighting our universal experiences and emotions. Despite the different stories and characters, there are common threads that run throughout the film, making it relatable to audiences.

Overall, The Mortuary Collection is a thought-provoking horror film that explores complex themes and emotions, making it more than just a typical fright-fest.

overview: After setting her serial killer boyfriend on fire, a paranoid delusional woman gets a job at an all-night gas station. The isolation triggers her anxiety and hallucinations, with devastatingly gory results.
tagline: Pray you never run out of gas...
title: Open 24 Hours
plot:
Open 24 Hours is a 2018 slasher film written and directed by Padraig Reynolds. An international co-production between Canada and Serbia, it stars Vanessa Grasse, Emily Tennant, Brendan Fletcher, Cole Vigue and Daniel O'Meara, and was screened at the 2018 Fantastic Fest.

Mary was sent to prison for setting her boyfriend, James Lincoln Fields, on fire after discovering that he was a serial killer known as the "Rain Ripper", who forced her to watch his murders while playing the song "Raindrops" by Dee Clark. Now out on parole, she takes a job working the 10 pm to 6 am shift at the Deer Gas Market, an isolated 24-hour gas station. James, still in prison, torments her by calling whenever it rains and playing the song down the line, and she suffers from vivid hallucinations of him that she keeps in check with medication. On her first night, her coworker Bobby shows her the ropes and her childhood friend Debbie stops by to see her, but after leaving, Debbie is dragged away by a hooded attacker. As the shift goes on, Mary deals with a sleazy trucker who leaves his credit card behind on purpose, receives strange phone calls from a woman asking when the store closes and finds Debbie's driver's license in the outside toilet, setting off a terrifying hallucination. Unable to reach her parole officer, Tom, she begins to doubt her own sanity, especially when James appears before her and insists that he is real, promising that people will die and that she will watch. When a woman arrives at the pumps and attacks Mary with a knife, the night turns into a desperate fight for survival, as Mary learns that the danger is far from imaginary and that the man she once tried to destroy may have come back to finish what he started.

The film received mixed reviews from critics and holds a 45% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Almost all of the action unfolds in and around the gas station during Mary's first night shift, with the climax spilling out into an old wrecking yard nearby before returning to the store.

overview: A chronicle of James Brown's rise from extreme poverty to become one of the most influential musicians in history.
tagline: The Funk Don't Quit
title: Get on Up
plot:
Get on Up is a biographical musical drama film that tells the story of James Brown, an American singer, songwriter, and musician. The movie explores several themes that are deeply intertwined with the life and legacy of its protagonist.

One of the primary themes of Get on Up is the struggle for identity and self-expression. James Brown's early life was marked by poverty, racism, and personal turmoil, which he channeled into his music as a means of empowerment and rebellion. The film showcases how Brown's unique blend of gospel, blues, and R&B styles helped him to transcend his circumstances and become an iconic figure in American music.

Another significant theme is the power of perseverance and resilience. Despite facing numerous setbacks, including personal struggles with addiction and run-ins with the law, Brown continued to create and perform music that inspired generations of fans. The film highlights how he used his music as a means of healing and redemption, both for himself and others.

The movie also explores the theme of legacy and the impact one person can have on others. Through James Brown's story, Get on Up shows how an individual's influence can extend far beyond their own lifetime, shaping the course of music history and inspiring future generations of artists.

Finally, the film touches on the theme of redemption and personal growth. As James Brown navigates his later years, he grapples with the consequences of his past actions and seeks to make amends through his music and philanthropy. The movie suggests that it's never too late to change and find forgiveness, both for oneself and others.

Overall, Get on Up is a powerful exploration of the human spirit, creativity, and the enduring power of music to transform lives and leave a lasting legacy.

overview: A cliché hunchbacked evil scientist's assistant aspires to become a scientist himself, much to the displeasure of the rest of the evil science community.
tagline: All men aren't created Evil.
title: Igor
plot:
Igor is a 2008 stop-motion animated comedy film directed by Terry Gilliam and produced by Exodus Film Group. The movie tells the story of Igor, a lovable but awkward assistant to the mad scientist Dr. Frankenstein.

The film begins with Igor (voiced by John Cusack) living in his small village, where he dreams of becoming a great scientist like his idol, Dr. Frankenstein. However, Igor's attempts at science are consistently thwarted by his own ineptitude and the ridicule of the villagers. Despite this, Igor remains determined to prove himself.

One day, Igor receives an offer from Dr. Frankenstein (voiced by John Cleese) to become his assistant in his castle laboratory. Igor is overjoyed at the opportunity and sets off for the castle, where he meets Dr. Frankenstein's other assistant, Eugene (voiced by Chris Miller). The two assistants quickly become fast friends and begin working on various projects with Dr. Frankenstein.

As Igor becomes more confident in his abilities, he begins to take on more responsibility within the laboratory. However, his enthusiasm often gets the better of him, leading to chaotic and disastrous consequences. Despite this, Dr. Frankenstein remains patient and supportive, encouraging Igor to pursue his dreams.

Meanwhile, a rival scientist, Dr. Vortex (voiced by Will Arnett), is also working on creating life. However, his methods are far more sinister than Dr. Frankenstein's, and he will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

As the story unfolds, Igor becomes increasingly obsessed with creating life, much to the dismay of Dr. Frankenstein. The two scientists engage in a series of escalating pranks and competitions, with Igor determined to outdo his mentor.

In the end, Igor's creation comes to life, but it is not what he had intended. Instead of a beautiful and intelligent being, Igor has created a grotesque and terrifying monster. Dr. Frankenstein is horrified by the creature, and Igor is left feeling guilty and ashamed.

Despite the chaos that ensues, Igor ultimately learns a valuable lesson about responsibility and humility. He realizes that his enthusiasm and ambition must be balanced with caution and consideration for others. The film ends with Igor returning to his village, where he is welcomed back as a hero. However, it is clear that Igor has grown and matured as a result of his experiences in the laboratory.

Overall, Igor is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of ambition, responsibility, and friendship. With its talented voice cast and clever stop-motion animation, the movie is a delight to watch.

overview: Jay is a man with a secret who travels from Britain to Pakistan to attend a wedding—armed with duct tape, a shotgun, and a plan to kidnap the bride-to-be. Jay and his hostage end up on the run across the border and through the railway stations, back alleys, and black markets of New Delhi.
title: The Wedding Guest
plot:
The Wedding Guest is a 2019 British romantic thriller film directed by Robin Campillo. The movie revolves around a young woman named Alice, who attends her ex-boyfriend's wedding with his new fiancée, only to discover that the groom has been unfaithful and murdered his business partner.

At its core, The Wedding Guest explores themes of love, betrayal, and revenge. The film delves into the complexities of human relationships, particularly in the context of romantic partnerships. It highlights how hurt and anger can simmer beneath the surface, waiting to boil over into destructive behavior.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. Alice's journey is one of navigating her own emotions and desires, as she grapples with the end of a relationship and the uncertainty of her future. Through her experiences, the film suggests that it's never too late to rediscover oneself and find a new sense of purpose.

Furthermore, The Wedding Guest critiques societal expectations around marriage, love, and relationships. The film portrays a world where people are often pressured into conforming to certain norms or standards, rather than embracing their true selves. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Alice's ex-boyfriend, who is driven by a desire for security and stability, even if it means sacrificing his own happiness.

Ultimately, The Wedding Guest is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own emotions and desires.

overview: A family man who turns out to be a retired mob enforcer must travel across the country to find his daughter who has gone missing.
tagline: Mercy is for the Weak
title: The Prince
plot:
The Prince is a 2014 American action thriller film directed by Brian A. Miller and starring Jason Patric, Bruce Willis, John Cusack and Rain, with Jessica Lowndes and Gia Mantegna. Filmed in Mobile, Alabama, in and around the Battle House Hotel and the adjoining RSA Battle House Tower, it was given a limited theatrical release and a video-on-demand release by Lionsgate on August 22, 2014.

Paul is a mechanic whose daughter Beth is away at college. During a video chat she seems stressed and distracted but insists she is fine, and they make plans for her visit home after finals. Soon afterwards Paul receives a letter from the college saying that Beth has not paid her tuition, and when he calls her, a stranger answers her phone. Without contacting the police, he travels to her city to find her himself. In her apartment he finds a photograph of Beth with another young woman, Angela, whom he tracks down at a local bar. Angela reluctantly tells him that Beth has dropped out of school and fallen in with drug dealers, and Paul pays her to take him to New Orleans, Beth's last known location, and point out her dealer, Eddie. When one of Eddie's friends attacks him, Paul responds with startling brutality, and Eddie only agrees to talk after his uncle recognizes Paul as the man he once saw kill seven armed men two decades earlier. Eddie reveals that Beth has moved on to harder drugs and is living with a kingpin known as The Pharmacy. Angela insists on staying to help find her friend, and as thugs begin to pursue them, Paul finally explains his past: he was once a hit man for the crime boss Omar, and a botched attempt on Omar's life killed Omar's wife and daughter instead. Omar has never forgiven him, and Paul realizes that his old enemy intends to use Beth to get to him. Turning to an old friend and former partner, Sam, for help, Paul recovers his hidden weapons and prepares for a violent showdown to save his daughter.

The film was panned by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, none of the 10 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 19 out of 100, indicating "overwhelming dislike". Andrew Barker of Variety wrote that Cusack and Willis "yawn their way through this basic-cable-quality actioner", and the film grossed about $1.3 million internationally against an $18 million budget.

overview: Two lifelong friends find themselves at an impasse when one abruptly ends their relationship, with alarming consequences for both of them.
tagline: Everything was fine yesterday.
title: The Banshees of Inisherin
plot:
The Banshees of Inisherin is a 2022 black comedy-drama film written and directed by Martin McDonagh, produced by Element Pictures and Blueprint Pictures.

The story takes place on the fictional island of Inisherin off the west coast of Ireland.
