Meanwhile, Arlong, a fish-man pirate, emerges as a rival to Don Krieg. Arlong's true intentions are revealed, and he is determined to take revenge on the people of Water 7, where he was once shunned by society due to his appearance.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between Luffy and Arlong, with the fate of Water 7 hanging in the balance. In the end, Luffy emerges victorious, but not before realizing that there is more to being a pirate than just fighting and treasure hunting.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities and relationships are on full display. Luffy's innocence and determination are contrasted with Zoro's cynicism and Nami's pragmatism. The movie also explores the themes of friendship, loyalty, and the consequences of one's actions.

One Piece: Curse of the Sacred Sword is an exciting and action-packed adaptation that sets the stage for the rest of the One Piece series. With its engaging characters, thrilling battles, and epic scope, it's no wonder why this film has become a beloved classic among fans of the franchise.

original_title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
overview: Just one enchanted jewel stands between earth and an army of evil spirits led by the devious ghoul, Phears. With the help of his new girlfriend and ghost pals, Max Doyle races to find the crystal and save the world.
title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
plot:
Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House, released as R.L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly: One Night in Doom House, is a 2016 American family fantasy horror comedy written and directed by Ron Oliver. It is the third feature film based on R. L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly book series, following Mostly Ghostly: Who Let the Ghosts Out? (2008) and Mostly Ghostly: Have You Met My Ghoulfriend? (2014), and was made by Universal 1440 Entertainment. To keep the characters at the same ages, the main roles were recast: Corey Fogelmanis plays Max Doyle, with Sophie Reynolds as Cammie, Blake Michael and Olivia Ryan Stern as the ghosts Nicky and Tara, Adam Tsekhman as Phears, Danny Trejo as Mr. Morgo and Jamie Kennedy as a television ghost hunter. Morgan Fairchild also appears.

Max is a teenage stage magician who shares his home with Nicky and Tara, two young ghosts who are counting on him to help them find their missing parents. To raise money for his girlfriend Cammie's school dance crew, he stages a public séance. The ghosts supply genuine spectral effects, but everyone assumes they are Max's tricks, and when the ghost of a French maid interrupts the show with information about Nicky and Tara's parents, the evening ends in embarrassment and Cammie breaks up with him. At the same time, his ghost friends complain that he treats them more like pets than friends.

Max turns for help to Simon Drake, the self-obsessed host of a ghost-hunting television show who is filming an episode in town, only to discover that he is a fraud. The evil ghost Phears, working with the sinister Mr. Morgo, takes possession of Drake as part of a new attempt to release an army of evil spirits on the world and plunge it into darkness. The key is a dark crystal that turns up in Max's house, which Max has tried to use to win Cammie back. Hampered by fame, family squabbles, a rich rival for Cammie's affections and an anxious dance choreographer, Max has to recover the jewel and rescue Nicky and Tara before Phears succeeds, in a showdown at a derelict mansion, the Doom House of the title.

The film was released directly on DVD, digital download and on demand on 6 September 2016. Common Sense Media described it as a low-budget, harmless fright-fest with nonstop action and over-the-top villains, enlivened by Kennedy's send-up of a reality television star, but lacking in depth.

overview: In a Paris hotel room, Jack Whitman lies on a bed. His phone rings; it's a woman on her way to see him, a surprise. She arrives and the complications of their relationship emerge in bits and pieces. Will they make love? Is their relationship over? (A prequel to The Darjeeling Limited, 2007.)
title: Hotel Chevalier
plot:
Hotel Chevalier is a 2007 romantic drama film that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and identity through the story of two young Americans, Jack and Jules, who meet at a Parisian hotel. The movie delves into the themes of youthful disillusionment, social class, and the search for meaning in life.

The film's narrative is presented as a series of vignettes, showcasing the characters' inner struggles and desires. As Jack and Jules navigate their whirlwind romance, they must confront their own insecurities and the societal expectations that come with being young and privileged. The movie raises questions about the nature of identity, class, and privilege, highlighting the tensions between the old money and new rich.

Through its portrayal of the characters' emotional journeys, Hotel Chevalier touches on themes of love, loss, and longing. The film's use of atmospheric settings and poignant dialogue adds to the sense of melancholy and introspection that pervades the narrative. Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

The film's director, Todd Haynes, masterfully weaves together these themes, creating a cinematic experience that is both intimate and expansive. By exploring the complexities of love and relationships through the lens of two young characters, Hotel Chevalier offers a poignant commentary on the human condition, one that continues to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, Hotel Chevalier is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences and desires. Its exploration of themes such as identity, class, and love makes it a rich and rewarding cinematic experience.

overview: Suzu is a 17-year-old high-school student living in a rural town with her father. Wounded by the loss of her mother at a young age, Suzu one day discovers the massive online world "U" and dives into this alternate reality as her avatar, Belle. Before long, all of U's eyes are fixed on Belle, when, suddenly, a mysterious, dragon-like figure appears before her.
tagline: You are no longer alone.
title: Belle
plot:
Belle (Japanese: 竜とそばかすの姫, Ryū to Sobakasu no Hime, "The Dragon and the Freckled Princess") is a Japanese animated musical science-fantasy drama of 2021 written and directed by Mamoru Hosoda and produced by Studio Chizu, inspired by Beauty and the Beast. Kaho Nakamura voices Suzu Naito and her virtual alter ego Belle, with Takeru Satoh as Kei, the Dragon, Lilas Ikuta as her friend Hiro, Ryo Narita as Shinobu, Shota Sometani as Kamishin, Tina Tamashiro as Ruka and Kōji Yakusho as Suzu's father.

Suzu is a shy high school student in rural Kōchi Prefecture who stopped singing after her mother drowned rescuing a stranger's child, a sacrifice Suzu still resents. Urged by her best friend Hiro, she joins the vast virtual world U, where the system gives her a beautiful freckled avatar she names Bell. There she can sing again, and with Hiro as her producer she becomes a sensation known as Belle. One of her concerts is disrupted by the Dragon, a feared, nearly unbeatable user pursued by the Justices, self-appointed enforcers led by Justin, who threatens to unmask him. Intrigued, Belle seeks out the Dragon in his hidden castle, discovers that children see him as a hero, and grows close to him, while in real life she helps her classmates Ruka and Kamishin admit their feelings for each other.

Justin captures Belle and threatens to expose her, and when the Dragon's AI guardians rescue her, the Justices find and burn his castle. Racing to identify the Dragon first, Suzu and Hiro learn that he is Kei, a junior high student abused by his father, whose fierce protectiveness of his little brother Tomo gives his avatar its strength. Kei refuses to believe Suzu is Belle, so with the encouragement of her friends and her late mother's choir companions, she reveals her true face to all of U and sings. Kei's father cuts off their connection, but her friends trace the boys to Kawasaki, near Tokyo. Unwilling to wait for the authorities, Suzu travels there alone and stares down the father until he backs off. Returning home, she reconciles with her father, accepts Shinobu's affection and comes to understand her mother's selfless choice.

Belle premiered to acclaim at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival and opened in Japan on 16 July 2021, becoming one of the country's top-grossing films of the year with ¥6.53 billion. GKIDS released it in North America in January 2022. It holds 95% on Rotten Tomatoes and received five Annie Award nominations.

overview: During the 1972 Olympic Games in Munich, eleven Israeli athletes are taken hostage and murdered by a Palestinian terrorist group known as Black September. In retaliation, the Israeli government recruits a group of Mossad agents to track down and execute those responsible for the attack.
tagline: The world was watching in 1972 as 11 Israeli athletes were murdered at the Munich Olympics. This is the story of what happened next.
title: Munich
plot:
Munich is a 2005 historical drama film directed by Steven Spielberg, written by Tony Kushner, and produced by DreamWorks Pictures.

The film begins with a dramatic and intense sequence showing the aftermath of the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre, where 11 Israeli athletes were killed by Palestinian terrorists. The story then shifts to the present day, where we meet Avner Kaufman (played by Eric Bana), an Israeli agent working for the Mossad, Israel's intelligence agency.

Avner is tasked with leading a team of six agents on a mission to track down and assassinate the perpetrators of the Munich massacre. The team consists of Avner, Gadi (played by Daniel Henshall), Carl (played by Ciarán Hinds), Peter (played by Mathieu Kassovitz), Michael (played by Lior Ashkenazi), and Salim (played by Saïd Taghmaoui).

The team is sent to Munich, Germany, where they track down the mastermind behind the massacre, Flávio Costa (played by Rodrigo Santoro). However, as Avner delves deeper into the investigation, he begins to question the morality of the mission and the true motives of his handlers.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of the events leading up to the Munich Olympics massacre, including a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Golda Meir (played by Helen Mirren) and Avner's father, who is a Mossad agent. This meeting sets off a chain of events that ultimately leads to Avner's recruitment into the Mossad.

Throughout the film, Spielberg explores themes of revenge, morality, and the consequences of violence. The team's mission becomes increasingly complex as they face setbacks and personal losses. Meanwhile, Avner grapples with his own demons, including the guilt of having lost his brother in a previous operation.

The climax of the film takes place at a Munich hotel, where Avner and his team confront Flávio Costa and his accomplices. In a tense and violent confrontation, the team manages to kill several of the perpetrators, but not before one of them reveals that he was working for a larger organization.

In the aftermath of the mission, Avner is left to grapple with the consequences of his actions. He begins to question whether the ends justify the means and whether he has become the very thing he set out to destroy – a ruthless assassin.

The film concludes with Avner returning to Israel, where he is met with a mixture of praise and criticism for his actions. As he reflects on the mission, we see flashbacks of his family and friends, who are struggling to come to terms with the loss of their loved ones.

Ultimately, Munich is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that challenges viewers to consider the complexities of revenge and violence. Through its powerful performances, stunning cinematography, and masterful direction, Spielberg creates a cinematic experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: After a young mother murders her family in her own house, a detective attempts to investigate the mysterious case, only to discover that the house is cursed by a vengeful ghost. Now targeted by the demonic spirits, the detective must do anything to protect herself and her family from harm.
title: The Grudge
plot:
The Grudge is a 2020 American supernatural horror film directed by Nicolas Pesce and written by Pesce and Jeff Buhler. The movie serves as a reboot of the Grudge franchise, which was previously based on the Japanese horror series Ju-On.

The story begins with Kay Gushiken (Andi Matichak), a nurse who is struggling to cope with her mother's death from a grudge-related curse. Kay has always been fascinated by the supernatural and decides to investigate the cursed house where her mother died, hoping to understand the origins of the curse.

As Kay delves deeper into the mystery, she meets Ben (Justin Bartha), an American journalist who is researching the history of the cursed house in Japan. The two form a connection, but their budding romance is threatened by the supernatural forces that surround them.

The movie takes a dark and twisted turn when Kay discovers that the curse has been awakened once again, this time targeting her own life. As she tries to uncover the truth behind the curse, she realizes that it's not just a simple vengeful spirit, but a complex web of emotions and trauma that have been passed down through generations.

Throughout the film, the audience is taken on a journey through the cursed house, where they encounter various characters who are also under the influence of the grudge. The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Kay tries to break the curse and free herself from its grasp.

One of the standout aspects of The Grudge is its use of atmospheric tension and suspense. The film's cinematography is stunning, capturing the eerie and foreboding atmosphere of the cursed house. The score by Roque Barral adds to the sense of unease, creating a feeling of dread that permeates throughout the movie.

The cast delivers solid performances, with Andi Matichak standing out as Kay Gushiken. Her portrayal of a strong and determined protagonist is compelling, and her chemistry with Justin Bartha is undeniable.

Overall, The Grudge is a chilling and unsettling horror film that explores themes of trauma, grief, and the supernatural. While it may not be as complex or layered as some other horror movies, its atmospheric tension and suspense make it a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: When cop David is injured in a drug bust gone wrong, his partner Cal chases the two criminals who shot him. They all land at a remote farm owned by troubled vet Eric, and as Cal and Eric plot their defense, more of the gang arrives - along with a wounded David. Outnumbered, the three heroes must use stealth, smarts, and good shooting to take down the drug-dealing mob.
tagline: Your land. Your rules. Your fight.
title: Survive the Game
plot:
Survive the Game, also released as Killing Field, is a 2021 American action thriller directed by James Cullen Bressack from a screenplay by Ross Peacock, his first feature script. It stars Chad Michael Murray as a troubled military veteran and Bruce Willis as a veteran detective, with Swen Temmel, Michael Sirow, Kate Katzman, Zack Ward, Donna D'Errico and Canyon Prince. It was produced by Randall Emmett and George Furla's Emmett/Furla Oasis with Lionsgate, which distributed the film.

Detective David Watson and his younger partner Cal stake out a drug deal by a gang David has long pursued, but the operation goes wrong, a gunfight breaks out and David is shot. The criminal couple Mickey Jean and Violet escape and take refuge on a remote farm owned by Eric, a former soldier who has withdrawn there and turned to drink after the deaths of his wife Hannah and their daughter. The pair hold Eric hostage while they wait for their boss to arrive, but Cal tracks them to the property, leading to a tense stand-off in which Mickey holds a gun to Eric while Cal holds a knife to Violet's throat.

When the gang's leader, Michael, who bears a grudge against David, learns what has happened, he sends a large force of armed men to the farm to eliminate every witness, bringing the wounded David with them as a captive. Eric reveals his military skills, and he and Cal devise a plan to defend the farm against the much larger group. Eric must also persuade his friend Andrew, who unexpectedly visits, to leave before the gangsters kill him. Outnumbered, the men rely on stealth and marksmanship through a series of gun battles and hand-to-hand fights, and David eventually rejoins them as they take on the drug ring.

The film was released in select theaters and on video on demand in the United States on October 8, 2021, followed by DVD and Blu-ray on October 12. Most critics were negative: on Rotten Tomatoes only one of seven reviews was positive. Bobby LePire of Film Threat was an exception, awarding it 8 out of 10 and praising its energetic, no-frills action and the performances of Murray and Ward while finding the car chase finale a letdown, whereas Oliver Armknecht of Film-Rezensionen criticized its cheap-looking action, its throwaway story and how seldom Willis appears despite his billing. Willis's performance was among those nominated for a special Golden Raspberry category devoted to his 2021 films, which was rescinded after he retired because of aphasia.

overview: In the midst of trying to legitimize his business dealings in 1979 New York and Italy, aging mafia don, Michael Corleone seeks forgiveness for his sins while taking a young protege under his wing.
tagline: All the power on earth can't change destiny.
title: The Godfather Part III
plot:
The Godfather Part III is a 1990 American epic gangster film produced and directed by Francis Ford Coppola from a screenplay he co-wrote with Mario Puzo. It stars Al Pacino, Diane Keaton, Talia Shire, Andy Garcia, Eli Wallach, Joe Mantegna, Bridget Fonda, George Hamilton and Sofia Coppola. The sequel to The Godfather Part II (1974) and the final installment of the trilogy, it concludes the story of Michael Corleone as he tries to make his criminal empire legitimate, and it weaves in fictionalized versions of the 1978 death of Pope John Paul I and the Papal banking scandal of 1981 and 1982.

In 1979, Michael Corleone, now nearing sixty and tormented by guilt over his rise to power, above all for ordering the murder of his brother Fredo, is donating millions to charity and receives a papal honor. Divorced from Kay, he has a strained relationship with their children, Anthony and Mary, who live with Kay; Anthony announces that he is abandoning law school to become an opera singer. At the celebration, Vincent Mancini, the hot-tempered illegitimate son of Michael's late brother Sonny, clashes with the rival mobster Joey Zasa, and Michael, impressed by his loyalty, takes him into the family business. Seeking to leave crime behind, Michael offers to cover a huge deficit at the Vatican Bank in exchange for a controlling stake in the international real estate company Internazionale Immobiliare, a deal that requires the Pope's approval. When he refuses to let his old Mafia partners share in the venture, a helicopter attack on a meeting of the bosses nearly kills him, and Michael realizes that the elderly Don Altobello is betraying him. While Michael recovers from a diabetic stroke, Vincent begins a romance with his cousin Mary and takes revenge on Zasa. The family then travels to Sicily for Anthony's operatic debut at the Teatro Massimo in Palermo, where Michael seeks Kay's forgiveness and makes his first confession in thirty years, even as enemies both inside and outside the Church close in around him and his family.

The film received mostly positive reviews, although it was considered inferior to its predecessors; critics praised Pacino's and Garcia's performances and Coppola's direction but criticized the plot and Sofia Coppola's performance. It grossed $136.8 million and received seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture. A recut version, The Godfather Coda: The Death of Michael Corleone, was released in 2020.

overview: A seasoned team of bank robbers, including Gordon Jennings, John Rahway, A.J., and brothers Jake and Jesse Attica successfully complete their latest heist and lead a life of luxury while planning their next job. When Ghost, a former member of their team, is released from prison he convinces the group to strike an armored car carrying $20 million. As the "Takers" carefully plot out their strategy and draw nearer to exacting the grand heist, a reckless police officer inches closer to apprehending the criminals.
tagline: Who's Taking Who?
title: Takers
plot:
Takers is a 2010 American heist action thriller film directed by John Luessenhop, who co-wrote it with Peter Allen, Gabriel Casseus and Avery Duff. It stars Idris Elba as Gordon Cozier, leader of a crew of professional bank robbers, Paul Walker as John Rahway, Michael Ealy and Chris Brown as the brothers Jake and Jesse Attica, Hayden Christensen as A.J., Tip "T.I." Harris as their former partner Ghost, and Matt Dillon and Jay Hernandez as the detectives Jack Welles and Eddie Hatcher.

Welles and Hatcher are investigating a daring bank robbery by Gordon's well-organized crew. Ghost, once a member, was caught during a robbery five years earlier; in his absence, Jake has become engaged to Ghost's former girlfriend, Lilli. Released from prison, Ghost reconnects with the crew and proposes a major job: in five days, $25 million will be moved in a convoy of two armored trucks. Disguised as construction workers, the robbers plan to blow a hole beneath the street and drop the trucks into the ground, with Ghost posing as a police officer and John covering him with a sniper rifle in case of a setup. When a cyclist forces the lead truck to stop short, the charges go off early, and a gunfight breaks out with the guards before John rams the lead truck into the crater. The crew bag the cash and escape through sewer tunnels connected to the subway. Deducing their route, the detectives corner Jesse in a station, and he shoots Hatcher, who dies as Welles stops to help him.

The crew regroups at a hotel, unaware that Ghost had made the same deal with a Russian gang and double-crossed it by striking early. Ghost tells the Russians where the crew is hiding and slips out a window before they attack. A.J. sacrifices himself, and the others kill the gangsters and flee. Jake and Jesse return home to find Lilli dead and their money gone, and they die charging out at the police who surround their bar. Ghost kills the crew's fence, Scott, on his private plane and takes their laundered money, but he is confronted by Gordon and Welles and wounds them both before John shoots him dead. Sparing Welles, who calls for help, John and the wounded Gordon drive off with the money and Gordon's sister, Naomi.

The film opened at number one at the U.S. box office with about $20.5 million. Critics were largely negative, with 28% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 45; reviewers found its set pieces gripping but its characters two-dimensional and its plot derivative.

overview: In Imperial Russia, Anna, the wife of the officer Karenin, goes to Moscow to visit her brother. On the way, she meets the charming cavalry officer Vronsky to whom she is immediately attracted. But in St. Petersburg’s high society, a relationship like this could destroy a woman’s reputation.
tagline: An epic story of love.
title: Anna Karenina
plot:
Anna Karenina is a 2012 historical romantic drama directed by Joe Wright, with a screenplay by Tom Stoppard adapted from Leo Tolstoy's 1878 novel. Keira Knightley, in her third film with Wright, plays Anna, the wife of senior statesman Alexei Karenin, played by Jude Law. Aaron Taylor-Johnson plays the cavalry officer Count Vronsky, Domhnall Gleeson plays Konstantin Levin and Alicia Vikander plays Kitty.

In the Russian Empire in 1874, Dolly has thrown out her unfaithful husband, Stiva Oblonsky. His sister Anna, who lives in Saint Petersburg with Karenin and their son Seryozha, travels to Moscow to reconcile them. Kitty, Dolly's sister, rejects the landowner Levin, hoping to marry Vronsky. Anna meets Vronsky, and they are instantly attracted. At a ball he favors Anna over Kitty, then follows her to Saint Petersburg. He turns down a posting in Tashkent, and they become lovers. Anna becomes pregnant, and her reaction to Vronsky's fall at a horse race betrays her. She admits the affair to Karenin, who demands that she give him up.

Karenin decides to divorce her, while Levin and Kitty reunite and marry. Anna nearly dies giving birth to a daughter, and Karenin forgives her. She first resolves to stay with him, but Vronsky persuades her to leave for Italy with the baby. At Levin's estate, Kitty defies convention by helping Masha, a prostitute, nurse Levin's sickly brother Nikolai. Returning to Saint Petersburg, Anna is turned away by Karenin when she tries to see Seryozha on his birthday, and she is publicly shunned at the opera. Taking morphine and consumed by jealousy, she suspects that Vronsky's mother wants him to marry the young Princess Sorokina. On a train journey, tormented by imagined betrayal, Anna asks God for forgiveness and throws herself under a train. The film ends with Levin and Kitty raising their child and the retired Karenin at his estate, watching Seryozha and Anna's daughter play.

Wright staged most of the story on a single soundstage at Shepperton Studios dressed as a dilapidated theatre. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and grossed about $69 million worldwide. Reviews were generally positive: critics praised the cast but were divided by the theatrical concept, and Rotten Tomatoes called it bold and stylized "for both better and worse." It received four Academy Award nominations, and Durran won both the Oscar and the BAFTA for Best Costume Design.

overview: Gabriel tells the story of an archangel who fights to bring light back to purgatory - a place where darkness rules - and save the souls of the city's inhabitants.
tagline: Far From Grace
title: Gabriel
plot:
Gabriel is an Australian action horror film of 2007 set in purgatory, the first feature of director Shane Abbess, who wrote it with Matt Hylton Todd. Made on a low budget without government funding, it stars Andy Whitfield as the archangel Gabriel, Dwaine Stevenson as the fallen angel Sammael, Samantha Noble as the archangel Amitiel, Erika Heynatz as Lilith, Harry Pavlidis as Uriel, Jack Campbell as Raphael and Michael Piccirilli as Asmodeus.

Heaven and Hell have long fought over purgatory, each sending seven warriors who must take human form to enter it. Hell has won, turning the realm into a dark, seedy city, and Gabriel, the last archangel to arrive, comes to learn the fate of his comrades. The Fallen leader Sammael senses him but orders his followers to hold off. Gabriel finds Uriel drunk and hiding in a derelict bus; he explains that in human form the archangels grew weak and prey to human desires, that dying here means the death of the soul, and that Amitiel has been stripped of her wings and forced into prostitution. Gabriel rescues her from a brothel run by Asmodeus, kills the Fallen Balan, and finds Ithuriel at a soup kitchen and the badly wounded Raphael in tunnels below, healing him at great cost to his own strength.

As Gabriel begins killing the Fallen one by one, they strike back, slaying Uriel, Ithuriel and Raphael. Consumed by rage, Gabriel takes on the brown eyes of the Fallen and kills Asmodeus, but pulls back from damnation by restoring a woman the narcissistic demon had disfigured. He finds comfort with Amitiel, kills Lilith and confronts Sammael on a nightclub roof. Sammael reveals that he is in fact the archangel Michael, Gabriel's closest friend, who killed the real Sammael and took his place, preferring freedom to a life of service. Weakened, Gabriel is impaled on a metal pipe but embraces Michael, driving it through him too, and forgives him; the dying Michael heals Gabriel, and light returns to purgatory. Questioning God, Gabriel steps off the roof, and a post-credits scene, absent from the DVD, shows him reunited with Amitiel.

Shot in Sydney in late 2005, the film premiered in November 2007 and was distributed by Sony. Reviews were mixed, praising its visuals and technical polish on a small budget but criticising its dialogue and familiar story.

overview: Two couples disintegrate when they begin destructive adulterous affairs with each other.
tagline: If you believe in love at first sight, you never stop looking.
title: Closer
plot:
Closer is a 2004 American romantic drama film directed by Mike Nichols, starring Julia Roberts, Jude Law, Natalie Portman, and Clive Owen.

The story revolves around four main characters: Dan (Jude Law), Alice (Julia Roberts), Larry (Clive Owen), and Mary (Natalie Portman). The narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between the characters' past and present.

The film begins with Dan, a writer who has recently lost his wife to cancer. He meets Alice, a single mother who is struggling to cope with her own personal demons. They begin an affair, which becomes intense but ultimately unfulfilling for both of them.

Meanwhile, Larry, a novelist, is having an affair with Mary, a young and beautiful woman. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that they are both married to other people. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that all four characters are struggling with feelings of loneliness and disconnection in their personal lives.

As the narrative progresses, we see flashbacks of each character's past relationships and experiences. We learn about Dan's troubled marriage and his inability to connect with his wife on an emotional level. We also see glimpses of Alice's difficult childhood and her struggles to raise her son as a single mother.

Through a series of twists and turns, the story reveals that all four characters are connected in unexpected ways. It becomes clear that each character has been hurt by past relationships and is struggling to move on. However, as they navigate their complicated web of emotions, they begin to realize that they have more in common than they initially thought.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a poignant and emotional conclusion. Dan and Alice's affair comes to an end, but not before they both come to terms with their own vulnerabilities and weaknesses. Larry and Mary's relationship also reaches a breaking point, forcing them to confront the reality of their own desires and needs.

Throughout the film, Mike Nichols masterfully weaves together the complex narratives of his characters, creating a rich and nuanced exploration of love, loss, and human connection. The performances from the cast are outstanding, with each actor bringing depth and nuance to their respective roles.

In the end, Closer is a powerful and moving film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which we hurt and heal each other. With its non-linear narrative and complex characters, it's a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that lingers long after the credits roll.

overview: Four undying warriors who've secretly protected humanity for centuries become targeted for their mysterious powers just as they discover a new immortal.
tagline: Forever is harder than it looks
title: The Old Guard
plot:
The Old Guard is a 2020 American superhero film directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood and written by Greg Rucka, based on his own comic book series. Charlize Theron stars as Andy, leader of a band of immortal mercenaries, with KiKi Layne as Nile Freeman, Matthias Schoenaerts as Booker, Marwan Kenzari as Joe, Luca Marinelli as Nicky, Harry Melling as Steven Merrick, Veronica Ngo as Quỳnh and Chiwetel Ejiofor as James Copley.

Andy, Booker, Joe and Nicky heal from any wound. Breaking their rule against repeat clients, they accept a job from Copley to rescue kidnapped girls in South Sudan. It is a trap, and Copley films them dying and recovering. At the same time, U.S. Marine Nile Freeman has her throat cut in Afghanistan and revives without a scar. The immortals dream of each new member until she is found, and Andy extracts Nile before the military can study her. Copley shows his footage to the pharmaceutical executive Merrick, who sends operatives after them. At a safe house in France, the others reveal to Nile that their healing eventually stops without warning. They also tell her about Quỳnh, Andy's companion, who was condemned as a witch about 500 years ago and cast into the sea in an iron maiden, drowning ever since.

Merrick's forces capture Joe and Nicky, who are tortured in his London lab, and Andy secretly finds that a wound is not healing. When Andy and Booker confront Copley, Booker shoots her, revealing that he betrayed them, hoping Merrick's research might end the immortality he has grown tired of. Copley, seeing that Merrick is driven by greed and cruelty rather than medicine, changes sides and helps Nile storm the building. She frees the others, and she and the now-mortal Andy kill Merrick when Nile drags him out of a high-rise window. The group sentences Booker to a century of exile. Copley, who shows them the good their past missions achieved, agrees to cover their tracks. Six months later, a drunken Booker returns to his Paris apartment to find Quỳnh waiting.

Netflix released the film on July 10, 2020. Netflix reported that 78 million households had watched it. Reviews were generally positive, with praise for the action sequences and Theron's performance. Rotten Tomatoes reported 80% approval, and its consensus said Prince-Bythewood brought a sophisticated vision to the superhero genre. A sequel, The Old Guard 2, directed by Victoria Mahoney, followed in July 2025.

original_title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
overview: In Shirleyville, Vermont, during the sixties, sisters Merricat and Constance, along with their ailing uncle Julian, confined to a wheelchair, live isolated in a big mansion located on the hill overlooking the town, tormented by the memories of a family tragedy occurred six years ago. The arrival of cousin Charles will threaten the fragile equilibrium of their minds, haunted by madness, fear and superstition.
title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
plot:
We Have Always Lived in the Castle is a 2018 film directed by Stacey Steers, not 2019, and produced by Furthur Films. The movie is an adaptation of Shirley Jackson's 1962 novel of the same name.

The main themes of We Have Always Lived in the Castle revolve around the dark and complex relationships within the Blackwood family, particularly between the two sisters, Merricat and Constance. The film explores the idea of isolation and how it can both protect and suffocate individuals. The Blackwoods' isolated life on a remote farm serves as a metaphor for their emotional isolation from the rest of society.

The movie also delves into themes of paranoia, suspicion, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Constance's perception of the world is distorted by her own experiences and the events that have shaped her life, leading to a sense of unease and tension that permeates the entire film.

Furthermore, We Have Always Lived in the Castle touches on the idea of family dynamics and the consequences of past actions. The Blackwoods' history is marked by tragedy and violence, which has created a toxic atmosphere within the family. The film raises questions about the nature of guilt, responsibility, and the cyclical patterns of abuse.

Overall, We Have Always Lived in the Castle is a haunting and atmospheric film that explores the complexities of human relationships, isolation, and the darker aspects of human nature.

overview: When a bestselling celebrity biographer is no longer able to get published because she has fallen out of step with current tastes, she turns her art form to deception.
tagline: Her greatest work will be her biggest crime.
title: Can You Ever Forgive Me?
plot:
Can You Ever Forgive Me? is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the blurred lines between truth and deception. The film follows the story of Lee Israel, a struggling writer who turns to forgery as a means of survival.

At its core, Can You Ever Forgive Me? explores the theme of loneliness and isolation. Lee's life is marked by her inability to form genuine connections with others, leading her to create fictional personas and relationships that ultimately become a facade for her own emotional emptiness. The film masterfully captures the desperation and vulnerability that can arise when individuals feel disconnected from the world around them.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and performance. Lee's alter egos, including her "fictional" persona as a renowned author, serve as a coping mechanism for her own insecurities and fears. As she navigates this complex web of identities, the film raises questions about the nature of self and how we present ourselves to others.

Furthermore, Can You Ever Forgive Me? touches on the theme of obsession and fixation. Lee's relationship with her mark, Jack, is a prime example of this. Her fixation on him becomes an all-consuming force that drives her actions, highlighting the darker aspects of human desire and the blurred lines between love and obsession.

Ultimately, the film presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that is both poignant and thought-provoking. Through Lee's complex and often disturbing journey, Can You Ever Forgive Me? invites viewers to confront their own vulnerabilities and the complexities of human relationships.

original_title: Gone Mom: The Disappearance of Jennifer Dulos
overview: Jennifer Dulos, the wealthy, Connecticut mother-of-five who mysteriously vanished.
title: Gone Mom: The Disappearance of Jennifer Dulos
plot:
Gone Mom: The Disappearance of Jennifer Dulos is a 2021 American biographical crime drama television film directed by Gail Harvey and written by Gregory Small and Richard Blaney, produced by Lighthouse Pictures for Lifetime with Dan Abrams, Ilene Kahn Power and Rachel Stockman as executive producers. Based on the real 2019 disappearance of Jennifer Farber Dulos, a wealthy Connecticut mother of five, it stars Annabeth Gish as Jennifer and Warren Christie as her husband Fotis Dulos, with Laura Harris as her best friend Audrey and Heidi Bauman as Michelle Troconis. It runs 88 minutes and premiered on 5 June 2021 as part of Lifetime's Summer of Secrets slate.

The film moves between two time frames, intercutting the story of the marriage with the police investigation after Jennifer vanishes. Jennifer, a thoughtful aspiring novelist from a very wealthy New York family, and the gregarious, athletic Fotis first met at Brown University but begin a whirlwind romance years later and marry within a year, as Jennifer, then 35, longs for a family. Her friends, especially Audrey, suspect he is after her money. Fotis bankrolls a struggling development company with her family's wealth and spends much of the year away on business and skiing trips while Jennifer, raising their five children largely alone with the help of a nanny, puts aside her writing. He belittles her, flies into rages and makes threats, and eventually openly brings his mistress Michelle into their life, telling Jennifer to accept it. She files for divorce and moves out with the children, leading to a bitter custody battle in which Fotis threatens to take the children to Greece and to kill her. When Jennifer disappears in New Canaan, Audrey points the police towards Fotis, and investigators reconstruct how they believe he attacked her in her garage and cleaned up with rolls of paper towels, tracing his movements on security cameras even though her body is never found. Fotis, charged with her murder, takes his own life while still protesting his innocence, and Michelle is charged as well.

Reviews were broadly favorable. TV Fanatic praised its respectful focus on Jennifer's life, Gish's grace in the role and Christie's balance of charm and volatility. Mark Gabrish Conlan of Movie Magg found it well made and eloquently acted, especially by Gish. Beverly White of MEAWW called it a fascinating cautionary tale and praised Christie, though she found Gish oddly relaxed at times.

overview: Ronny is a rebellious man, who falls in love with Sia but circumstances separate them. Years later, Ronny learns that Sia is abducted by a martial arts champion, Raghav.
tagline: Be a Rebel
title: Baaghi
plot:
Baaghi (2016) is an action-packed film that delves into the complexities of family, loyalty, and redemption. The movie revolves around Surya, a young man who seeks to protect his sister from the clutches of a powerful gangster, Veeravalli. As Surya navigates this treacherous world, he must confront his own demons and make difficult choices that test his moral fiber.

At its core, Baaghi is a story about the unbreakable bonds of family and the lengths to which one would go to protect those they love. The film explores the theme of loyalty, not just in terms of familial ties but also in the context of friendship and community. Surya's relationships with his sister and her partner serve as a catalyst for his actions, highlighting the importance of standing up for what is right, even when it means putting oneself in harm's way.

The movie also touches on the theme of redemption, as Surya grapples with his own past mistakes and seeks to make amends. Through his journey, he learns valuable lessons about forgiveness, self-sacrifice, and the true meaning of heroism.

Overall, Baaghi is a gripping tale that explores the complexities of human relationships, morality, and personal growth, making it a compelling watch for audiences.

original_title: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee
overview: Beginning just after the bloody Sioux victory over General Custer at Little Big Horn, the story is told through two unique perspectives: Charles Eastman, a young, white-educated Sioux doctor held up as living proof of the alleged success of assimilation, and Sitting Bull the proud Lakota chief whose tribe won the American Indians’ last major victory at Little Big Horn.
tagline: The Epic Fall of the American Indian
title: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee
plot:
Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee is a powerful and poignant film that delves into the tragic events surrounding the Battle of Little Bighorn, but it also explores deeper themes. The movie masterfully weaves together historical facts with emotional storytelling to convey the devastating consequences of colonialism, cultural erasure, and the clash between two worlds.

At its core, the film is a powerful exploration of the American West's dark past, where the ideals of freedom and democracy are starkly contrasted with the brutal reality of imperialism. The movie shines a light on the struggles of Native American tribes, who were forcibly relocated, marginalized, and subjected to violence by the US government.

One of the primary themes that emerges is the theme of loss and grief. The film's title itself is a poignant metaphor for the emotional toll inflicted upon the Native American communities by the brutal events depicted in the movie. The characters' experiences are marked by trauma, displacement, and the erasure of their cultures, leaving them with a deep sense of sorrow and longing.

The movie also explores the theme of identity and cultural heritage. As the Native American tribes struggle to maintain their way of life in the face of encroaching colonialism, they must confront the loss of their traditions, languages, and very existence. This is particularly evident through the character of Wind in His Hair, who embodies the resilience and determination of his people.

Furthermore, Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee touches on the theme of power dynamics and the abuse of authority. The film highlights the ways in which those in positions of power exploit and manipulate others for their own gain, often under the guise of "progress" or "civilization." This is evident in the character of General George Armstrong Custer, whose arrogance and hubris ultimately lead to his downfall.

Ultimately, the movie presents a powerful critique of the American West's troubled history, one that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of their nation's past. Through its thoughtful storytelling and nuanced characters, Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee offers a thought-provoking exploration of the human cost of colonialism and the importance of preserving cultural heritage.

overview: Mia, a young woman struggling with sobriety, heads to a remote cabin with a group of friends where the discovery of a Book of the Dead unwittingly summon up dormant demons which possess the youngsters one-by-one.
tagline: The Most Terrifying Film You Will Ever Experience.
title: Evil Dead
plot:
Evil Dead is a 2013 American supernatural horror film directed by Fede Álvarez in his feature debut, from a screenplay he co-wrote with Rodo Sayagues. A soft reboot and the fourth installment of the Evil Dead series, it stars Jane Levy as Mia, Shiloh Fernandez as her brother David, Lou Taylor Pucci as Eric, Jessica Lucas as Olivia and Elizabeth Blackmore as Natalie.

In a prologue, a possessed young woman held in a remote cabin's cellar is burned and shot by her father. Later, David and his girlfriend Natalie come to the cabin, his family's holiday home, with his estranged younger half-sister Mia and their friends Eric, a teacher, and Olivia, a nurse. They plan to help Mia quit heroin; her last attempt ended in a relapse in which she briefly died. In the cellar they find animal corpses and a book, the Naturom Demonto, and Eric reads an incantation that awakens a demonic force. Mia sees a demonic double of herself, flees in Eric's car, crashes and is possessed after vines attack her. When she scalds herself, flooded roads stop David from taking her to a hospital.

The possessed Mia shoots David, vomits into Olivia's mouth and is locked in the cellar. Olivia, now possessed, mutilates herself and attacks Eric before he kills her. Mia bites Natalie, who is possessed through the wound and dies after attacking with a nail gun. The book says the Taker of Souls needs five souls to raise the Abomination, and that Mia can be purified only by live burial, dismemberment or burning. Eric is fatally stabbed protecting David, who buries Mia alive and then revives her with a makeshift defibrillator, freeing her of the demon. The entity possesses Eric's corpse, and David sacrifices himself by igniting a gasoline can. His death is the fifth soul. Blood rains from the sky, and the Abomination rises. Mia, losing a hand under David's overturned Jeep, splits it in two with a chainsaw. In a post-credits scene, Bruce Campbell appears as Ash Williams.

The project was announced in 2011 with Ghost House Pictures producing and Diablo Cody revising the script. Jane Levy replaced Lily Collins as Mia. The film was shot near Auckland, New Zealand, in 2012 and premiered at South by Southwest on March 8, 2013, before TriStar Pictures released it on April 5. It opened at number one and grossed $97.5 million on a $17 million budget. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 64% approval, noting that it trades the original's absurd humor for brutal, gory terror. Evil Dead Rise followed.

overview: Dating coach and aspiring book author Abigale Slater is tasked by her publisher Jack to prove that her dating advice really works. With that, she decides to make a man fall for her by Christmas Eve in 12 days. When she Michael Ryan, her single-minded mission takes an unexpected turn.
title: The Holiday Dating Guide
plot:
The Holiday Dating Guide is a 2022 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Brian Herzlinger and produced by W Squared Media, Workhorse Cinema and ZMA Films. Made for Lifetime's It's a Wonderful Lifetime holiday season, it stars Maria Menounos as Abigale Slater and Brent Bailey as Michael Ryan, with Andrea Susan Bush, Kelly Lynn Reiter, Ava Paloma, Steve Vinovich, Mason McCulley, Jequrey Slaton, Kerry Malloy, Sarah Allyn, Thomas Wilson Pace and Amadeo Fusca. The film runs 85 minutes.

Abigale is a dating coach and aspiring self-help author who is on the verge of publishing her first book, a how-to guide to dating over the holidays. When she meets the publisher Jack, however, he argues that people should not need a guide to find love, because fate will bring the right two people together on their own. Abigale counters that times have changed and that there are tips worth following, and to prove that her advice really works she makes a bet with him: she will make a man fall for her within twelve days and bring him to Jack's Christmas Eve party as proof, in return for a book deal. She sets out following her own rules, which include not seeing a date two days in a row, staying mysterious and getting to know someone only lightly, but with so little time she is soon forced to bend them. When she meets Michael Ryan at a bar, she breaks one immediately by agreeing to a date straight away, and as their romance develops she sees him too often, learns too much about him, meets his friends too soon and falls too fast, although he falls just as quickly. Along the way she realises that sometimes it is better to follow one's instincts and be spontaneous, and that there is something underhanded about making someone fall in love as a test to advance her career. When Michael learns of the bet at the worst possible moment, he feels used, and Abigale must try to make things right before Christmas.

The film premiered on Lifetime in December 2022. Kristen of TV Tweetie found it cute but wildly predictable, crediting the cast, especially Bailey's appealing, down-to-earth performance, while objecting that a dating coach would embark on such a thoughtless scheme and that the story lacked emotional depth. Jade of Fangirlish called it a lighthearted, sweet seasonal romance that shone brighter because of the chemistry between Menounos and Bailey.

overview: A nerdy teen, Ryan Woodman is smitten with the popular and gorgeous Ashley Grant, who apparently has no interest in him. Meanwhile, dim star athlete Chris Campbell has his eye on Ryan's brainy and beautiful friend, Maggie Carter. The two agree to help each other in their romantic quests, but, as they come closer to their goals, both Ryan and Chris suspect that they might be pursuing the wrong girls.
tagline: How low will they go to get the girls of their dreams?
title: Whatever It Takes
plot:
Whatever It Takes is a 2000 American teen comedy film directed by David Raynr and starring Shane West, Marla Sokoloff, Jodi Lyn O'Keefe and James Franco, with Aaron Paul making his film debut. A modern update of Edmond Rostand's 1897 play Cyrano de Bergerac, it was released in the United States by Sony Pictures Releasing in March 2000.

Ryan Woodman is a somewhat geeky high school student who has his heart set on Ashley Grant, the most popular girl in school, much to the dismay of his next-door neighbor and best friend, Maggie Carter, a clever and down-to-earth girl. Meanwhile Chris Campbell, a football star who happens to be Ashley's cousin, has his eye on Maggie. The two boys strike a deal: Chris will help Ryan win Ashley, and Ryan will help Chris win Maggie. Ryan begins writing heartfelt e-mails and letters for Chris to pass off as his own, while Chris advises Ryan that the only way to get Ashley's attention is to treat her badly. At first neither finds it easy to change; Chris comes on too strong for Maggie, and Ryan is too nervous to act like a jerk. As their schemes begin to work, however, Ryan starts to see Maggie in a new light and to wonder whether he is pursuing the right girl, all while he is busy convincing her of Chris's feelings. Maggie, for her part, has doubts about the self-absorbed Chris, and Ryan's new attitude, which includes snubbing his geeky friends, lowers her opinion of him. When Ryan discovers that Chris intends to sleep with Maggie on prom night and then dump her, as he has done with every girl he has dated, he finally confesses the truth, including that he wrote the romantic messages himself. Hurt by the deception, Maggie goes to the prom with Chris anyway, while Ryan reluctantly takes Ashley, leading to a night of reversals and comeuppance in which everyone must decide what they really want.

Whatever It Takes received negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has a 15% approval rating based on 66 reviews, with a consensus calling it a run-of-the-mill teen romance with clichéd jokes and a tired plot, and Metacritic gave it a score of 20 out of 100. It was a box-office bomb, grossing $9 million against a $15 million budget.

overview: Karen, a single mother, gifts her son Andy a Buddi doll for his birthday, unaware of its more sinister nature. A contemporary re-imagining of the 1988 horror classic.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
Province of British Columbia Production Services Tax Credit
tagline: More than a toy... he's your best friend.
title: Child's Play
plot:
Child's Play is a 2019 horror film directed by Lars Klevberg from a screenplay by Tyler Burton Smith. A remake of the 1988 film of the same name and the eighth installment in the Child's Play franchise, it stars Aubrey Plaza, Gabriel Bateman and Brian Tyree Henry, with Mark Hamill as the voice of Chucky. It follows a family terrorized by a high-tech doll that malfunctions and becomes hostile and murderous. It was the first Orion Pictures film to be released through United Artists Releasing.

The multinational Kaslan Corporation has launched Buddi, a line of high-tech dolls that use artificial intelligence to learn from their surroundings and serve as lifelong companions, and the product is a worldwide hit. At a Kaslan factory in Vietnam, an employee who has been fired and abused by his supervisor takes revenge by disabling all of the safety protocols on one of the dolls before taking his own life. In Chicago, Karen Barclay, a retail clerk, has just moved into a new apartment with her twelve-year-old son Andy, who is hard of hearing. Hoping to cheer him up about the move and her new boyfriend Shane, Karen blackmails her boss into giving her a defective Buddi doll, which turns out to be the sabotaged one. Once activated, the doll names himself Chucky and becomes fiercely attached to Andy. At first Chucky helps Andy make friends with two neighborhood kids, Falyn and Pugg, but he soon shows violent tendencies, and his literal-minded desire to make Andy happy turns deadly. After Chucky kills the family cat and begins targeting the people Andy resents, the children try to get rid of the doll, but he keeps coming back. While police detective Mike Norris investigates a string of gruesome deaths and Karen refuses to believe her son's warnings, Chucky grows ever more dangerous, setting the stage for a bloody rampage at the shopping mall where Karen works, in which he turns other Buddi dolls against the crowds.

Child's Play received mixed reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes it has a 64% approval rating based on 208 reviews, with a consensus that it updates an 1980s horror icon for the Internet of Things era with gruesome and generally entertaining results. It grossed $44.9 million worldwide against a $10 million budget.

overview: No beau? No problem! To earn money for college, a high schooler creates a dating app that lets him act as a stand-in boyfriend.
tagline: He's whoever you want him to be.
title: The Perfect Date
plot:
The Perfect Date is a 2019 American teen romantic comedy film directed by Susanna White and written by Dan Cross and David Neevel. The movie follows the story of Noah, a high school student who starts a dating app for other students to find dates for school dances.

The main themes of The Perfect Date include:

1. **Self-discovery**: Throughout the movie, Noah learns more about himself and his relationships with others. He discovers that he values honesty and authenticity in his interactions with people.
2. **Friendship**: The film highlights the importance of friendships and how they can be a source of support and comfort. Noah's friendship with his best friend, Emily, is particularly significant in this regard.
3. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores various aspects of love and relationships, including first crushes, unrequited love, and the complexities of high school dating.
4. **Authenticity vs. superficiality**: The film critiques the superficiality of social media and online dating platforms, highlighting the importance of genuine connections with others.
5. **Growing up and maturity**: As Noah navigates his relationships and personal growth, he learns to take responsibility for his actions and become more mature.

Overall, The Perfect Date is a heartwarming and relatable coming-of-age story that explores themes relevant to teenagers and young adults.

overview: Two children discover that their mother is gone. The youngest of the pair, adventurer and upcomming singer, Long Johnson forces his older sister, Lily Johnson, to hunt down a unicorn with magical blood.
title: Wish Upon a Unicorn
plot:
Wish Upon a Unicorn is a 2020 American family fantasy comedy film written and directed by Steve Bencich, produced by Universal 1440 Entertainment and Indy Entertainment and released by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on DVD and digital platforms on 15 September 2020, later streaming on Netflix. It stars Ryan Kiera Armstrong as Mia and Summer Fontana as her older sister Emma, with Chloe Webb as their grandmother Rose, Jonathan Lajoie as their father and Kevin J. O'Connor as Willie, alongside Tait Blum, Jon Gries and André Gower. Rated PG, it runs 93 minutes.

Emma and Mia have recently lost their mother, and their father has lost his job in Chicago, so the family moves to the country home where their mother grew up to live with Grandma Rose and help on her ranch. Rose is fading and losing her memory, but her joyful, eccentric spirit revives as she sets the girls to work on the chores. The sisters face bullies at their new school, and at the local general store they meet Willie, a conspiracy-minded local who tells Bigfoot stories and recognizes in Mia a fellow believer. In the woods, Mia spots a sparkling unicorn colt bathed in rainbow light, names him Rocco and discovers the good luck he brings, but no one else can see him and her skeptical father laughs off her claims. Mia researches unicorn lore to prove they exist, and when the more practical Emma finally starts to believe, she too can see Rocco; the sisters even take him to school to deal with a bully. Willie, however, knows the legends as well, and when he learns of Rocco's presence he sets out to capture the colt, intending to kill him and drink his blood to gain eternal youth. When Rose falls ill and is taken to hospital, she pulls out her tubes to help her granddaughters chase down the unicorn-napper, rescue Rocco and return him to his mother.

Reviewers found it a gentle film for young children. Barbara Shulgasser-Parker of Common Sense Media called it sweet and perfectly tailored to its target audience, with smart, amusing dialogue and a charming performance from Webb, though loose in its logic. Roger Moore of Movie Nation described it as cutesy, corny and little-kid friendly, a lightweight cross between Prancer and E.T. with modest effects but enough goofy gags and one-liners to avoid being insipid, while noting it was too undemanding for anyone over eight.

overview: A young woman is sent to Paradise Hills to be reformed, only to learn that the high-class facility's beautiful facade hides a sinister secret.
production_companies: Generalitat de Catalunya - Departament de Cultura
Instituto de Ciencias y Artes Cinematográficas del Ministerio de Cultura
tagline: Rebels Reign.
title: Paradise Hills
plot:
Paradise Hills is a 2019 Spanish science fiction film directed by Isabel Coixet. The movie follows the story of two young women, Alice and Milla, who are sent to a mysterious facility called Paradise Hills, where they are forced to undergo a transformation that erases their memories and identities.

The main theme of Paradise Hills revolves around the concept of identity and self-discovery. The film explores how our sense of self is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and memories, and how these can be manipulated and altered. Through the characters' journeys, the movie delves into the idea that our identities are not fixed entities, but rather complex and multifaceted constructs that can be influenced by external forces.

The film also touches on themes of female empowerment, rebellion, and resistance against patriarchal norms. The characters' struggles to reclaim their autonomy and individuality serve as a commentary on the societal expectations placed upon women, particularly in terms of beauty, behavior, and conformity.

Furthermore, Paradise Hills critiques the notion of perfection and the pressure to conform to unrealistic standards. The facility's attempts to transform the women into perfect, idealized versions of themselves serve as a metaphor for the societal pressures that can lead to feelings of inadequacy and disconnection.

Overall, Paradise Hills is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes related to identity, self-discovery, and female empowerment, raising questions about the nature of reality and our place within it.

overview: A grieving mother transforms herself into a vigilante following the murders of her husband and daughter, eluding the authorities to deliver her own personal brand of justice.
tagline: The system failed. She won't.
title: Peppermint
plot:
Peppermint is a 2018 American action thriller film directed by Pierre Morel and written by Brian Helgeland. The movie stars Jennifer Garner, John Gallagher Jr., and Patrick Wilson.

The story begins with Katie Ferris (Jennifer Garner), a mother of two who lives in suburban New Jersey with her husband, Tom (John Gallagher Jr.), and their children, Molly (Linda Fiorentino) and Ben (Clayton Rohner). Katie is a devoted wife and mother, but she's also hiding a dark secret: she was once a hitwoman for the Russian mafia.

The movie flashes back to Katie's past, where we see her working as a hitwoman, taking on various jobs and eliminating targets with precision. However, after a job goes sour, Katie is forced to flee the country to avoid being killed by her former employers.

Years later, Katie has built a new life in New Jersey, leaving her violent past behind. She's married to Tom, who knows nothing about her true identity, and they're living a happy suburban life with their children. However, when Molly, Katie's daughter, is kidnapped from school, Katie's past comes back to haunt her.

As Katie searches for her daughter, she must confront her own demons and use her skills as a hitwoman to track down the kidnappers. Along the way, she teams up with Detective Michael Zarno (Patrick Wilson), who helps her navigate the complex web of clues and suspects.

As the investigation unfolds, Katie's past and present begin to collide. She must use all her skills and resources to stay one step ahead of the kidnappers and rescue her daughter before it's too late. The movie builds towards a thrilling climax as Katie faces off against the mastermind behind Molly's kidnapping.

Throughout the movie, Jennifer Garner delivers a strong performance as Katie Ferris, bringing depth and nuance to the character. She's able to convey the complexity of Katie's personality, from her tough exterior to her vulnerable interior.

The movie also explores themes of motherhood, identity, and redemption. Katie's journey is not just about rescuing her daughter but also about finding a way to redeem herself for past mistakes. The film raises questions about the nature of violence and how it can shape us, both as individuals and as a society.

Overall, Peppermint is a tense and thrilling action movie that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and thought-provoking themes, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: A brother and sister's journey into the jungle to find their missing father.
tagline: The search for their father... led them to hell!
title: Jungle Run
plot:
Jungle Run is a 2021 American adventure film directed and photographed by Noah Luke and produced by The Asylum as a "mockbuster" of Disney's Jungle Cruise, released in the United States about a month ahead of that film. The cast includes Alyson Gorske, Richard Grieco, Jamie Petitto, Wade Hunt Williams and Jack Pearson.

In the Brazilian Amazon, the anthropologist Nicholas Kieran unearths a statue holding a striking green triangular relic. When a member of his team proposes selling it, a piercing sound rings out and swarms of insects attack the dig. Learning that their father is missing, his children Amanda and Scott set off to find him. Amanda hires the boat of Captain Lebecq, who agrees to take her upriver along with Vera, a woman claiming to be in charge of the excavation, and Scott jumps aboard at the last moment. Guided by Lebecq and his crewmen Sark and Teese, the group goes ashore, where poison dart frogs attack Lebecq. As Sark prepares to cut off his leg, a seemingly blind stranger emerges from the forest, treats the wound and warns them of the Curupira, an indigenous deity who fiercely protects the rainforest and dwells at the heart of the jungle.

Pressing on, the travelers lose Teese to piranhas that wreck their boat, and are scattered by crocodiles. Amanda and Lebecq reach the abandoned dig and escape an attack by bullet ants, while Nicholas, the sole survivor of his team, is revealed to be living in a trailer with the relic. Captured by a tribe of cannibals who mistake Scott for one of the loggers destroying the forest, the group escapes when giant spiders drop from a sacred tree and attack their captors. Following clues left by the blind man, Amanda deduces that the heart of the jungle is a waterfall, behind which giant snakes swallow her companions; she cuts her way out and frees all but Sark. Outside they find the dying Lebecq and their father bound nearby. When the Curupira, a huge two-legged creature with flames on its back, appears, they destroy the relic to free it, while Vera tries to shoot the deity and is devoured by a giant Venus flytrap. The family heads home as the Curupira watches over the forest.

Released on 25 June 2021, the film received poor reviews. German critics mocked its cheap effects, simple story and childish dialogue, though some singled out Gorske's committed performance and the film's ecological message.

overview: An updated version of the 1980 musical, which centered on the students of the New York Academy of Performing Arts.
title: Fame
plot:
Fame is a 2009 American teen musical drama directed by Kevin Tancharoen from a screenplay by Allison Burnett, a remake of Alan Parker's 1980 film of the same name. It follows a group of gifted students through four years at New York City's High School of Performing Arts. The young cast includes Naturi Naughton, Collins Pennie, Kay Panabaker, Asher Book, Paul Iacono, Anna Maria Perez de Tagle, Paul McGill, Kherington Payne and Walter Perez, while the faculty are played by Debbie Allen, Charles S. Dutton, Bebe Neuwirth, Megan Mullally and Kelsey Grammer.

Denise Dupree (Naughton), a classically trained pianist with strict parents, secretly longs to sing, and Malik Washburn (Pennie), an aspiring actor and rapper, hides his enrollment from his overworked mother and refuses to talk in drama class about the death of his sister. When Malik overhears Denise singing, he and the musician Victor Tavares (Perez) persuade her to record with them, and a record executive later tells them that her voice is what interests him. The shy actress Jenny Garrison (Panabaker) begins a romance with the singer Marco Ramonte (Book), which is shaken when she meets a former student who promises to introduce her to his agent.

Other students face harder lessons. Joy Moy (Perez de Tagle) lands a role on Sesame Street but eventually drops out as her grades suffer, while the aspiring filmmaker Neil Baczynsky (Iacono) is swindled out of five thousand dollars by a supposed producer. In senior year the dancer Kevin Barrett (McGill) is told by Ms. Kraft (Neuwirth) that he lacks the talent to dance professionally and, devastated, tries to throw himself in front of a subway train before his friends stop him; he later resolves to go home and become a dance teacher. Denise defies her father by performing at a club concert, winning over her mother, and Jenny and Marco reconcile before the class comes together for the graduation performance of "Hold Your Dream".

Fame premiered in Los Angeles on September 23, 2009, and MGM released it in the United States two days later. Critics were largely negative, with only 23 percent of reviews on Rotten Tomatoes positive and a Metacritic score of 39, and the consensus faulted its choppy editing and incomplete characters; Parker himself called the remake awful. It was nevertheless a moderate commercial success, grossing about 77 million dollars worldwide on an 18 million dollar budget.

overview: The Jungle Beat animals think it’s the best thing ever when an alien arrives in the jungle bringing with him the power of speech. They also surprisingly think it’s the best thing ever when they find out that he’s been sent to conquer them.
tagline: Home is where the hugs are.
title: Jungle Beat: The Movie
plot:
Jungle Beat: The Movie is a 2020 Indian animated musical comedy film directed by Rakesh Manak. The movie is based on the popular children's television series "Jungle Book" and features a unique blend of music, dance, and storytelling.

The main themes of Jungle Beat: The Movie revolve around friendship, loyalty, and the power of unity in the face of adversity. The story follows Mowgli, a young boy raised by wolves in the jungle, as he navigates his way through various challenges and obstacles with the help of his animal friends, including Baloo, Bagheera, and Kaa.

Throughout the movie, the characters learn valuable lessons about the importance of working together, embracing their differences, and standing up for what is right. The film also explores themes of identity, belonging, and self-discovery as Mowgli struggles to find his place in the world beyond the jungle.

The movie features a range of catchy musical numbers that showcase the unique blend of Indian and Western music styles, adding to its energetic and vibrant atmosphere. Overall, Jungle Beat: The Movie is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of friendship and unity in overcoming adversity.

overview: Reporter John Klein is plunged into a world of impossible terror and unthinkable chaos when fate draws him to a sleepy West Virginia town whose residents are being visited by a great winged shape that sows hideous nightmares and fevered visions.
tagline: What do you see?
title: The Mothman Prophecies
plot:
The Mothman Prophecies is a 2002 American supernatural thriller film directed by Mark Pellington, based on the 1975 book of the same name by John A. Keel.

The main themes of The Mothman Prophecies revolve around the intersection of science and mysticism, as well as the blurred lines between reality and paranoia. Here's a breakdown of the plot development and ending:

**Beginning:** The film follows John Klein (played by Richard Gere), a journalist who is struggling to cope with his terminal cancer diagnosis. He is sent to Point Pleasant, West Virginia, to investigate the legend of the Mothman, a creature reportedly seen in the area before a devastating bridge collapse.

As John delves deeper into the mystery, he becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the Mothman's appearances and the strange occurrences that have been happening in Point Pleasant. He is joined by his colleague, Linda (played by Laura Linney), who is initially skeptical of the supernatural events unfolding around them.

**Plot Development:** As John digs deeper, he discovers a series of eerie events and encounters with the Mothman, which seem to be connected to an impending disaster. The film's climax revolves around the collapse of the Silver Bridge in Point Pleasant, which kills 46 people.

John's investigation leads him to believe that the Mothman is a supernatural being sent to warn the townspeople about the impending tragedy. However, as the events unfold, it becomes clear that there are multiple explanations for the strange occurrences, and John's own perceptions of reality begin to blur.

**Ending:** The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of John's paranoia. As the Silver Bridge collapses, John is seen walking away from the disaster, seemingly unaffected by the tragedy. However, in a twist, it is revealed that John has actually died in the collapse, and his investigation was all part of his own delusional attempt to make sense of his impending death.

The Mothman Prophecies explores themes of existentialism, the power of human perception, and the fragility of reality. The film raises questions about the nature of truth and how our perceptions can be influenced by our own biases and fears. Ultimately, the movie leaves the audience with a sense of unease and uncertainty, mirroring John's own struggles to come to terms with his mortality.

Overall, The Mothman Prophecies is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of human psychology and the blurred lines between reality and the supernatural.

overview: A zoo veterinarian gets caught up in a grisly adventure as she finds herself leading the city-wide hunt for a monstrous lion terrorizing the Dutch capital of Amsterdam.
tagline: On the loose... and he's hungry.
title: Prey
plot:
Prey (Dutch: Prooi), also known as Uncaged, is a 2016 Dutch action comedy horror film written and directed by Dick Maas about a man-eating lion loose in Amsterdam. It stars Sophie van Winden, Julian Looman and Mark Frost, with Rienus Krul, Theo Pont and Victor Löw, and was released on 13 October 2016.

When a family is found slaughtered on a farm outside Amsterdam, Chief Inspector Olaf Brinkers suspects that this is no ordinary crime and calls in Lizzy, a veterinarian at the ARTIS zoo who spent several years in Tanzania. She quickly confirms his fears: the victims were killed by a large male lion. Later that day a golfer is mauled in broad daylight, proving that the animal has moved into the city, but Police Commissioner Zaimberg refuses to accept the evidence until a delivery driver is also killed. Ignoring Lizzy's advice to hire a professional hunter, Zaimberg calls in his cousin Theo, an amateur whose experience is limited to game farms, and the hunt ends in disaster for Theo and his son. When the lion attacks passengers on a city tram, its presence can no longer be hidden, and the humiliated commissioner finally agrees to Lizzy's plan. She summons Jack Delarue, an eccentric English big game hunter who uses a wheelchair and who also happens to be her former boyfriend, a development that causes friction with her current partner Dave, a television news cameraman. Delarue immediately clashes with Zaimberg by proposing to use a victim's body as bait, while further deaths and a bungled police operation, in which armed officers mistakenly open fire on a group of army veterans conducting their own hunt, push the city toward panic. As Lizzy, Delarue and Dave pursue the lion through the streets and into the university's medical building, the hunters discover that their prey is cunning, relentless and seemingly everywhere at once.

Prey received mostly positive reviews from critics in the Netherlands. Floortje Smit of de Volkskrant called it an entertaining thriller and a fine addition to Maas's body of work, full of jabs at Dutch gossip and regulatory zeal, while Bart van der Put of Het Parool gave it a mixed review, finding it weaker than the director's earlier films. Despite the positive notices, the film was a box-office flop in the Netherlands, although it found success in China.

overview: When Will decides to tell his daughter the story of how he met her mother, he discovers that a second look at the past might also give him a second chance at the future.
tagline: Three relationships. Three disasters. One last chance.
title: Definitely, Maybe
plot:
Definitely, Maybe is a 2008 American romantic comedy film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Mayim Bialik and Andrew Jacobson.

The movie follows Will Hayes (played by Ryan Reynolds), a children's party entertainer who is recently divorced from his wife, Sarah (played by Rachel Weisz). On the day of their divorce, Will tells his daughter, Mary (played by Abigail Breslin), three stories about what could have been her mother. The story that unfolds is a romantic comedy that explores Will's past relationships and his journey to find true love.

The main themes of Definitely, Maybe include:

1. Love and Relationships: The movie delves into the complexities of love, relationships, and heartbreak. Will's experiences with Sarah and the other two women in his life serve as a backdrop for exploring what it means to truly love someone.
2. Self-Discovery: As Will navigates his past relationships, he is also on a journey of self-discovery. He must confront his own flaws and shortcomings in order to grow as a person and find true happiness.
3. Parenting and Responsibility: The movie highlights the challenges of being a single parent and the importance of responsibility and commitment. Will's relationship with Mary serves as a catalyst for exploring what it means to be a good parent and partner.
4. Nostalgia and Regret: Definitely, Maybe is also a film about nostalgia and regret. Will's stories about his past relationships serve as a way for him to process his emotions and come to terms with the choices he has made.

Overall, Definitely, Maybe is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of love, relationships, and self-discovery.

overview: Op and Ed, two adorable donut-shaped animals - flummels - accidentally time-travel from 1835 to modern-day Shanghai.  There they discover traffic, trans fats, and worst of all, that flummels are now extinct. It's up to this bumbling pair to save themselves and their species...and, just maybe, change the course of history.
tagline: The end is just their beginning.
title: Extinct
plot:
Extinct is a 2021 animated science fiction comedy directed by David Silverman, with Raymond S. Persi as co-director, from a screenplay by Joel Cohen, John Frink and Rob LaZebnik. Rachel Bloom and Adam DeVine voice the siblings Op and Ed, with Zazie Beetz as Dottie, Ken Jeong as Clarance, Benedict Wong as Dr. Lee Chung, Catherine O'Hara as Alma, Jim Jefferies as Burnie and Reggie Watts as Hoss.

Op and Ed are flummels, fluffy, doughnut-shaped creatures with holes through their middles, native to the Galápagos Islands. Their community shuns them because of Op's knack for disaster. In 1835, just before Charles Darwin reaches their island, the pair tumble into a giant flower that transports them to modern-day Shanghai.
