They befriend Clarance, a white poodle, and learn that their species died out when a volcano destroyed the island. At the Time Terminal, where his owner Dr. Chung studied the time-traveling flowers and seeds, Op knocks seeds loose, and Clarance is flung to 1915 Antarctica, where Ernest Shackleton's expedition captures him, along with the seed that leads home.

The flummels team up with the Extinctables, a group of extinct animals Dr. Chung rescued: Dottie the dodo, Burnie the thylacine, Alma the Macrauchenia and Hoss the Triceratops. Together they hop through time from seed to seed. After a quarrel with Ed, Op returns to 1835 to warn the flummels about the volcano, only to be imprisoned by Clarance. He reveals that he resented the adorable flummels for winning over Dr. Chung, so he pushed his owner into one of the flowers, destroyed the seed that would bring him back and planted a drone bomb to wipe out the flummels. Ed arrives after seeing a video message from Op, and after several failed attempts to stop the bomb, they use a seed to move the entire island into the present. Dr. Chung returns and banishes Clarance to 1915 Antarctica. A year later, the flummels finally accept Op and Ed, and Dottie, Ed's love interest, surprises him with a mysterious egg shaped like a flummel.

It opened theatrically in Russia on February 11, 2021, was released by Sky Cinema in the United Kingdom on August 20, 2021, and debuted worldwide on Netflix on November 19, 2021. Reviews were largely negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 43% positive reviews from a small sample, and The Guardian's Steve Rose, giving it two stars, called it an evolutionary dead end in children's entertainment.

overview: When innocent civilians begin committing unthinkable crimes across Metropolis, Gotham City and beyond, Batman must call upon mystical counterparts to eradicate this demonic threat to the planet; enter Justice League Dark. This team of Dark Arts specialists must unravel the mystery of Earth's supernatural plague and contend with the rising, powerful villainous forces behind the siege—before it's too late for all of mankind.
title: Justice League Dark
plot:
Justice League Dark is a 2017 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics series of the same name. The movie follows the story of a group of supernatural heroes, known as the Justice League Dark, who are tasked with protecting the world from magical threats.

The main themes of Justice League Dark include:

1. **Balance between Light and Darkness**: The film explores the idea that there is no clear distinction between good and evil, and that even the most well-intentioned individuals can be driven by darkness within themselves. This theme is reflected in the character of John Constantine, who struggles with his own demons and grapples with the morality of his actions.
2. **The Power of Friendship and Unity**: The Justice League Dark team is formed when their individual interests and goals are brought together to form a cohesive unit. Through their interactions and relationships, they learn to trust and rely on each other, demonstrating that even the most unlikely heroes can become a powerful force for good.
3. **The Importance of Self-Sacrifice**: Many characters in the film, including Constantine and Deadman, demonstrate selfless acts of sacrifice in order to protect others. This theme highlights the value of putting the needs of others before one's own interests and desires.
4. **The Blurred Lines between Reality and Fantasy**: The movie explores the idea that reality is not always what it seems, and that there are forces beyond human understanding at work in the world. This theme is reflected in the supernatural elements of the story, which challenge the characters' perceptions of reality.

Overall, Justice League Dark offers a unique take on the superhero genre by exploring themes that are often overlooked in more traditional superhero films.

overview: When Cecilia's abusive ex takes his own life and leaves her his fortune, she suspects his death was a hoax. As a series of coincidences turn lethal, Cecilia works to prove that she is being hunted by someone nobody can see.
tagline: What You Can't See Can Hurt You
title: The Invisible Man
plot:
The Invisible Man is a 2020 psychological horror film directed by Leigh Whannell, based on the 1933 novel of the same name by H.G. Wells.

The story begins with Cecilia Kass (Elisabeth Moss), a young woman who escapes from an emotionally and physically abusive relationship with her boyfriend, Adrian Griffin (Oliver Jackson-Cohen). After a violent incident, Cecilia flees to Boston, where she meets a therapist named Dr. Bernard Rose (David Strathairn).

Cecilia begins to experience strange occurrences, including hearing whispers in her ear and seeing apparitions around her. She becomes convinced that Adrian is stalking her from beyond the grave, using his wealth and influence to manipulate those around him.

As Cecilia delves deeper into her past, she discovers a dark secret: Adrian was involved in a sinister experiment at his family's estate, where he used a revolutionary technology to become invisible. The experiment went horribly wrong, leaving Adrian with severe psychological trauma and a deep-seated need for control.

Cecilia becomes determined to expose the truth about Adrian's past and bring him to justice. She enlists the help of Dr. Rose, who is initially hesitant but eventually becomes her ally.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Adrian has become increasingly unstable and paranoid, using his wealth and influence to manipulate those around him. He begins to stalk Cecilia again, this time using his technology to make himself invisible.

The film's tension builds as Cecilia tries to evade Adrian's attacks and uncover the truth about his past. Along the way, she discovers a series of cryptic messages and clues that suggest Adrian's experiment has had far-reaching consequences, including the creation of an army of mindless drones who are loyal only to him.

In the film's climax, Cecilia confronts Adrian at his family's estate, where she discovers the full extent of his plan. Adrian has created a network of invisible drones who are programmed to do his bidding, and he plans to use them to take over the world.

Cecilia manages to outsmart Adrian and destroy his technology, but not before he reveals that he has been manipulating her entire life, including her relationships and her career. The film ends with Cecilia, finally free from Adrian's control, setting out on a new journey of self-discovery and empowerment.

Throughout the film, Whannell explores themes of trauma, abuse, and the dangers of unchecked power. The Invisible Man is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling film that challenges viewers to confront their own fears and vulnerabilities.

overview: Two siblings begin to develop special talents after they find a mysterious box of toys, and soon their parents and even their teacher are drawn into a strange new world – and find a task ahead of them that is far more important than any of them could imagine.
tagline: The future is trying to tell us something.
title: The Last Mimzy
plot:
The Last Mimzy is a 2007 American fantasy drama film directed by Paul McGuigan. The story revolves around a young boy named Josh Baskin, who discovers that he has inherited a mysterious toy from his recently deceased grandmother.

As Josh delves deeper into the world of the toy, known as "Mimzy," he learns about its incredible powers and the responsibility that comes with it. Through his journey, Josh must navigate the complexities of growing up, family secrets, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

At its core, The Last Mimzy explores themes of identity, belonging, and the struggle to find one's place in the world. As Josh grapples with the weight of his newfound powers, he is forced to confront the challenges of adolescence, including self-discovery, peer pressure, and the desire for independence.

The film also touches on the idea of legacy and the importance of understanding where we come from. Through Josh's connection to his grandmother, the story highlights the significance of family history and the lessons that are passed down through generations.

Ultimately, The Last Mimzy is a heartwarming and thought-provoking tale about a young boy's journey towards self-discovery, growth, and acceptance.

overview: Mankind must fight to survive as Earth is invaded by hostile UFOs bent on destroying the planet. As the epic battle wages on, astronauts sneak aboard the mothership where they discover a portal to the aliens' home world. They manage to alert Earth before they are brutally murdered. Left with no other choice, Earth sends an elite military team of science and combat specialists through the portal where they attempt to stop the invasion from the inside out.
tagline: Extinction Has Arrived
title: Age of Tomorrow
plot:
Age of Tomorrow, also released as Alien Extinction, is a 2014 American science fiction action film produced by The Asylum. It was directed by James Kondelik from a screenplay by Jacob Cooney, based on a story by Bill Hanstock, and produced by David Michael Latt, with cinematography by Ben Demaree, music by Chris Cano and visual effects supervised by Joseph J. Lawson. Like many of the studio's "mockbusters", it was released just days after a major Hollywood film with a similar title, in this case the Tom Cruise vehicle Edge of Tomorrow, although the two share little beyond an alien invasion. The cast includes Anthony Marks, Lane Townsend, Kelly Hu, Robert Picardo, Morgan West, Taylor Coliee, Nick Stellate and Mitchell Carpenter.

NASA warns General Magowan (Picardo) that a gigantic asteroid, about a quarter of the size of the Moon, is on a collision course with Earth. The headstrong shuttle pilot James Wheeler (Marks) is sent with a crew of rough-edged specialists, joined by the NASA scientist Dr. Gordon (Hu), to plant nuclear weapons that will push it off course. After landing they discover that the asteroid is not natural at all but a hostile alien vessel. Exploring its tunnels, they come under fire from its occupants, and in desperation leap through a teleportation device that carries them to the aliens' home world. There they learn that the invaders are moving people through portals en masse to use them as experimental subjects, and they manage to radio a warning back to Earth before deciding to fight back from the inside.

Meanwhile, hundreds of spheres are launched from the asteroid and begin attacking anything that moves on Earth. In Los Angeles, the firefighter Chris Meher (Townsend) and his crew battle through the devastation, fending off the flying machines, as he searches for his daughter Lindsay (Coliee). The two storylines run largely in parallel and meet only near the end, which closes on an open cliffhanger.

The film was released on home video in June 2014 and received poor reviews. Moria Reviews gave it one and a half stars, finding the alien planet unconvincing, with exteriors that looked like a manicured park, criticising its two disconnected plot strands and pointing out scientific blunders, although it found some of the effects for the flying spheres competent. Other critics similarly dismissed it as incoherent, low-budget B-movie fare, while noting that Hu and Picardo, the best-known names in the cast, have only secondary roles.

overview: Alex Rider thinks he is a normal school boy, until his uncle is killed. He discovers that his uncle was actually spy on a mission, when he was killed. Alex is recruited by Alan Blunt to continue the mission. He is sent to Cornwall to investigate a new computer system, which Darrius Sayle has created. He plans to give the new computer systems to every school in the country, but Mr. Blunt has other ideas and Alex must find out what it is.
tagline: Rule the school. Save the world.
title: Stormbreaker
plot:
Stormbreaker, also known as Alex Rider: Operation Stormbreaker, is a 2006 action spy film directed by Geoffrey Sax from a screenplay by Anthony Horowitz, based on his 2000 novel, the first book in the Alex Rider series. Alex Pettyfer stars as the teenage Alex, with Ewan McGregor as his uncle Ian, Mickey Rourke as the billionaire Darrius Sayle, Bill Nighy as MI6 chief Alan Blunt, Sophie Okonedo as Mrs. Jones, Alicia Silverstone as Jack Starbright, Andy Serkis as Mr. Grin, Damian Lewis as the assassin Yassen Gregorovich, Stephen Fry as Smithers and Robbie Coltrane as the Prime Minister. It was an international co-production between the United Kingdom, the United States and Germany.

Fourteen-year-old orphan Alex Rider lives in London with his uncle Ian, supposedly a bank manager who is often away, and their American housekeeper, Jack. When Ian is reported killed in a car crash, Alex quickly discovers that his uncle was in fact an MI6 spy who was murdered on a mission, and that Ian had been quietly training him for the same work all his life. Alan Blunt and Mrs. Jones of MI6's Special Operations Division recruit Alex, and when he refuses they threaten to have Jack deported. After a tough crash course at a Special Air Service training camp in the Brecon Beacons, where the soldiers come to respect him despite his age, Alex is equipped with gadgets by the armorer Smithers and sent undercover in Cornwall. His target is Darrius Sayle, a billionaire who is donating his advanced Stormbreaker computer system to every school in the country. Posing as a competition winner, Alex meets Sayle and his sinister assistants, Mr. Grin and Nadia Vole, while Vole investigates his true identity and gets into a fight with Jack back in London. Alex discovers that Sayle's generosity hides a monstrous plan involving the computers and the nation's schoolchildren, and he must use his wits, his training and Smithers's gadgets to stop the launch before Sayle can strike.

Intended as the first entry in a franchise, Stormbreaker received mixed reviews from critics, who found it lacking in originality and believability; it holds a 35% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a consensus calling it strictly children's fare. It grossed between $20.7 and $23.9 million against a $40 million budget, and The Weinstein Company eventually cancelled plans for a sequel.

original_title: The Best Years of Our Lives
overview: It's the hope that sustains the spirit of every GI: the dream of the day when he will finally return home. For three WWII veterans, the day has arrived. But for each man, the dream is about to become a nightmare.
tagline: Three wonderful loves in the best picture of the year!
title: The Best Years of Our Lives
plot:
The Best Years of Our Lives is a poignant and powerful film that explores the complexities of post-war America through the eyes of three World War II veterans, Burt "Bud" Schulberg, Al Stephenson, and Fred Derry. The movie delves into the struggles of readjusting to civilian life, as these characters navigate the challenges of finding employment, rebuilding their lives, and coping with the trauma of war.

At its core, the film is a nuanced portrayal of the human spirit's capacity for resilience, hope, and redemption in the face of adversity. The movie masterfully captures the sense of disillusionment and frustration that many veterans felt as they struggled to find their place in a rapidly changing world.

Through the characters' experiences, the film highlights the importance of community, friendship, and support in overcoming the difficulties of readjusting to civilian life. The relationships between Bud, Al, and Fred serve as a powerful reminder of the enduring bonds that can form between people who have shared a common experience.

The Best Years of Our Lives also explores themes of identity, purpose, and the search for meaning in a post-war world. As the characters grapple with their own sense of self-worth and direction, they must confront the harsh realities of a society that is rapidly changing and often unforgiving.

Ultimately, the film presents a hopeful and optimistic vision of America's future, one that is built on the principles of hard work, determination, and the power of human connection. Through its powerful storytelling and memorable characters, The Best Years of Our Lives continues to resonate with audiences today, offering a timeless and thought-provoking exploration of the human experience.

overview: Bud Clay races motorcycles in the 250cc Formula II class of road racing. After a race in New Hampshire, he has five days to get to his next race in California. During his road trip, he is haunted by memories of the last time he saw Daisy, his true love.
tagline: I'm not going to be okay, Bud.
title: The Brown Bunny
plot:
The Brown Bunny is a 2003 film, not 2004, directed by Vincent Gallo and produced by Wild Bunch.

The Brown Bunny is a surrealist drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, desire, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film follows the story of a struggling actor, played by Vincent Gallo, who embarks on a road trip with his girlfriend, played by Chloë Sevigny. As they journey through the American Southwest, their relationship is put to the test, and the boundaries between intimacy and violence become increasingly ambiguous.

Throughout the film, Gallo's character grapples with feelings of inadequacy, insecurity, and frustration, which are exacerbated by his own ego and sense of entitlement. The Brown Bunny is a deeply personal and introspective work that probes the darker aspects of human nature, revealing a world where desire can be both alluring and destructive.

The film's use of long takes, static shots, and deliberate pacing creates a sense of unease and tension, mirroring the characters' inner turmoil. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the lines between reality and fantasy are constantly shifting.

Ultimately, The Brown Bunny is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges its audience to confront the complexities and nuances of desire, relationships, and the self.

overview: A teacher opens a time capsule that has been dug up at his son's elementary school; in it are some chilling predictions -- some that have already occurred and others that are about to -- that lead him to believe his family plays a role in the events that are about to unfold.
tagline: What happens when the numbers run out?
title: Knowing
plot:
Knowing is a 2009 science fiction thriller film directed by Alex Proyas and written by Grady Stiles Jr. The movie stars Nicolas Cage, Aaron Eckhart, and Hilary Swank.

The story begins with Dr. John Koestler (Nicolas Cage), a professor of mathematics at Columbia University who has lost his wife, Lea (Rose Byrne), in a tragic accident 10 years ago. On the day of Lea's death, John receives a mysterious manuscript that contains a cryptic code and a series of numbers.

As John delves deeper into the code, he discovers that it is actually a message from an unknown sender who claims to have knowledge about the future. The message reveals that on December 21, 2012, a catastrophic event will occur, causing widespread destruction and chaos.

John becomes obsessed with deciphering the code and understanding its significance. He teams up with his colleague, Dr. Emma Sheehan (Hilary Swank), who helps him unravel the mystery. As they dig deeper, they realize that the message is not just a prediction but also a warning from someone who has knowledge of the future.

As the release date of December 21, 2012, approaches, John and Emma become increasingly concerned about the impending disaster. They try to warn people, but their efforts are met with skepticism and ridicule.

Meanwhile, John's son, Max (Lily Rabe), is struggling to cope with her mother's death. She becomes entangled in her father's investigation and helps him decipher the code.

As the clock ticks down to December 21, John and Emma realize that they have only a few days left to prevent the catastrophe. They work tirelessly to understand the message and find a way to stop it.

The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as John and Emma finally uncover the truth behind the code. In a desperate bid to save humanity, John uses his knowledge of mathematics to create a device that can manipulate time itself.

On December 21, 2012, the predicted event occurs, but instead of destruction, the world is saved by John's device. The movie ends with John reflecting on the experience and realizing that he has been given a rare gift – the ability to see into the future.

Throughout the movie, Nicolas Cage delivers a powerful performance as John Koestler, bringing depth and nuance to his character. The supporting cast, including Aaron Eckhart and Hilary Swank, adds to the tension and suspense.

Overall, Knowing is a thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that explores themes of fate, free will, and the power of human ingenuity. While some critics have panned the movie for its convoluted plot and lack of scientific accuracy, it remains a compelling watch for fans of the genre.

overview: At an isolated frontier outpost, a colonial magistrate suffers a crisis of conscience when an army colonel arrives looking to interrogate the locals about an impending uprising, using cruel tactics that horrify the magistrate.
title: Waiting for the Barbarians
plot:
Waiting for the Barbarians is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of colonialism, power dynamics, and the human condition. The movie is set in a fictional African colony during the 19th century and follows the story of Colonel Joll (played by Johnny Depp), a ruthless and cunning military officer who serves as the commander of the outpost.

At its core, Waiting for the Barbarians explores the themes of imperialism, oppression, and the dehumanizing effects of colonialism. The film portrays a society where the ruling elite exploit and manipulate the native population, stripping them of their culture, identity, and dignity. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Colonel Joll is not only a symbol of colonial power but also a complex character with his own motivations and desires.

One of the main themes of the film is the blurring of lines between good and evil. Colonel Joll's actions are morally ambiguous, and he is willing to do whatever it takes to maintain his power and control over the colony. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that he is also a product of his environment and the system he serves. This nuanced portrayal of morality raises questions about the nature of humanity and whether individuals can be redeemed or if they are forever trapped by their circumstances.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by power dynamics. The native characters in the film, particularly the young girl who becomes embroiled in Colonel Joll's plans, struggle to maintain their sense of self amidst the oppressive forces that surround them. Their experiences serve as a powerful commentary on the ways in which colonialism erases cultural identities and reduces individuals to mere objects.

Furthermore, Waiting for the Barbarians is a film about the fragility of human relationships and the devastating consequences of violence and oppression. The movie's title, "Waiting for the Barbarians," refers to the idea that the native population is seen as barbaric and uncivilized by the colonial powers. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this perception is a product of fear, ignorance, and prejudice.

Ultimately, Waiting for the Barbarians is a powerful critique of colonialism and its ongoing impact on our world today. The film's themes of oppression, power dynamics, and the human condition serve as a reminder of the importance of empathy, understanding, and social justice.

overview: The film contains five stories set on desolate stretches of a desert highway. Two men on the run from their past, a band on its way to a gig, a man struggling to get home, a brother in search of his long-lost sister and a family on vacation are forced to confront their worst fears and darkest secrets in these interwoven tales.
tagline: One way in, no way out.
title: Southbound
plot:
Southbound is a 2015 American horror anthology made by the directing collective Radio Silence with Roxanne Benjamin, David Bruckner and Patrick Horvath, whose five linked stories unfold along a lonely desert highway watched over by mysterious floating creatures. The cast includes Fabianne Therese, Larry Fessenden, Kate Beahan, Zoe Cooper and Gerald Downey.

In "The Way Out", two men, Mitch and Jack, flee the creatures but keep returning to the same gas station; Jack is killed, and Mitch, convinced he deserves his fate, enters a motel room that becomes his own home, where an apparition of his daughter, Katherine, forever slips away from him. In "Siren", Sadie, Ava and Kim, members of a touring band, break down in the desert and accept a ride from an eccentric couple, whose dinner, prayers and strange medicine draw Sadie's friends into a cult ritual; still haunted by the death of a former bandmate, Sadie escapes and runs into the road, where she is struck by a car.

In "The Accident", the driver, Lucas, distracted by a phone call, calls 911 but cannot say where he is. Voices on the line guide him to an abandoned hospital and talk him through gruesome surgery that kills Sadie, then mock him before letting him leave with clean clothes and a new car. In "Jailbreak", Danny storms a bar called The Trap with a shotgun, searching for his sister, Jesse; its regulars are demons, and he forces the bartender to lead him to Jesse, who is working as a tattoo artist and insists she stays by choice. Danny drags her away into the desert, where she admits that she killed their parents, abandons him to the demons and drives off. In "The Way In", a family spends a last weekend together before their daughter, Jem, leaves for college, when three masked men break in. They kill the mother after revealing a secret about the father, Daryl, and then Daryl himself, showing him a photograph of Katherine; unmasked, they are Mitch and Jack. Jem fights back but is killed, and as the ground opens and the creatures rise, Mitch and Jack escape onto the highway, closing the loop.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 16, 2015, and The Orchard released it in U.S. theaters on February 5, 2016. It drew 81% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 58.

overview: Over a weekend in the High Atlas Mountains of Morocco, a random accident reverberates through the lives of both the local Muslims and Western visitors to a house party in a grand villa.
tagline: Everything must be faced.
title: The Forgiven
plot:
The Forgiven is a 2022 drama film directed by Michael Winterbottom, starring Jesse Eisenberg, Mia Goth, and Timothée Chalamet. The movie takes place on a luxury safari in Botswana and follows the story of John Russell (Jesse Eisenberg), a wealthy American businessman who has just been released from prison after serving time for insider trading.

John is accompanied by his girlfriend, Lucy (Mia Goth), and her brother, Nick (Timothée Chalamet). The group is on a luxury safari to celebrate Lucy's birthday. However, their trip quickly turns into a nightmare when John gets drunk and accidentally kills the driver of their safari vehicle.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that John's past mistakes have caught up with him, and he must confront the consequences of his actions. The group is forced to navigate the complexities of John's situation, while also dealing with their own personal demons.

Throughout the film, Michael Winterbottom employs his signature style of non-linear storytelling, jumping back and forth in time to reveal the events leading up to the accident. This narrative structure adds to the sense of tension and unease, as the audience is left wondering what will happen next.

One of the standout aspects of The Forgiven is its exploration of themes such as privilege, class, and redemption. John's character is a complex and nuanced one, driven by a desire to escape his past mistakes and start anew. However, his actions are also rooted in a deep-seated sense of entitlement and arrogance.

The cast delivers strong performances across the board, with Jesse Eisenberg bringing a sense of vulnerability and desperation to his portrayal of John. Mia Goth and Timothée Chalamet also shine as Lucy and Nick, respectively, adding depth and complexity to their characters.

Overall, The Forgiven is a thought-provoking and unsettling drama that explores the darker aspects of human nature. With its non-linear narrative and complex themes, it's a film that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

overview: Just when his time under house arrest is about to end, Scott Lang once again puts his freedom at risk to help Hope van Dyne and Dr. Hank Pym dive into the quantum realm and try to accomplish, against time and any chance of success, a very dangerous rescue mission.
tagline: Real heroes. Not actual size.
title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
plot:
Ant-Man and the Wasp is a 2018 American superhero film directed by Peyton Reed and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie is the sequel to Ant-Man (2015) and follows Scott Lang (played by Paul Rudd) as he navigates his life with his family while also dealing with his responsibilities as a superhero.

The story begins with Scott Lang, who has been under house arrest for violating his parole after stealing the Pym Particle technology from Hank Pym (Michael Douglas). However, when Hank's daughter Hope van Dyne (Evangeline Lilly) and her friend Janet van Dyne (Michelle Pfeiffer) discover that Hank is missing, they set out to find him. Scott, who has been keeping in touch with Hope, agrees to help them.

As they search for Hank, the trio discovers that he has been kidnapped by Ghost (Hannah John-Kamen), a former S.H.I.E.L.D. agent turned thief. Ghost plans to use Hank's technology to break into the Quantum Realm, a subatomic world where matter can be manipulated and energy is limitless. The team soon realizes that they need Scott's help to rescue Hank and stop Ghost.

Meanwhile, Scott struggles with his responsibilities as a superhero and his life with his family. He tries to balance his duties as Ant-Man with being a husband and father, but it becomes increasingly difficult. His wife Maggie (Judy Greer) is worried about the risks he takes as a superhero, and their daughter Cassie (Abby Ryder Fortson) is struggling to cope with her father's absence.

As the team navigates the Quantum Realm, they encounter various obstacles and challenges. They also discover that Janet van Dyne has been trapped in the Quantum Realm for decades, and Scott must find a way to rescue her. Along the way, Scott and Hope grow closer, and their relationship becomes more intimate.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between the team and Ghost's minions. Scott uses his Ant-Man suit to outsmart and outmaneuver his enemies, while Hope and Hank work together to stop Ghost's plans. In the end, they succeed in rescuing Hank and stopping Ghost, but not before she reveals that she has been working for a mysterious organization known as the Ghost Division.

The movie concludes with Scott returning home to his family, where he is welcomed back with open arms. However, it also sets up the stage for future movies, as Hope and Hank begin to work together as a team, and Scott's role in the Marvel Cinematic Universe becomes more established.

Overall, Ant-Man and the Wasp is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of family, responsibility, and teamwork. The movie features impressive visuals, witty humor, and memorable performances from its cast.

original_title: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
overview: A timid magazine photo manager who lives life vicariously through daydreams embarks on a true-life adventure when a negative goes missing.
tagline: Stop Dreaming, Start Living
title: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
plot:
The Secret Life of Walter Mitty is an American adventure comedy-drama of 2013 directed and co-produced by Ben Stiller, who also plays the title role, from a screenplay by Steve Conrad. Adapted from James Thurber's 1939 short story, and closer to a remake of the 1947 film version, it co-stars Kristen Wiig as Cheryl Melhoff, Sean Penn as the photojournalist Sean O'Connell, Shirley MacLaine as Walter's mother Edna, Adam Scott as Ted Hendricks, Kathryn Hahn as his sister Odessa and Patton Oswalt as Todd Maher.

Walter manages photo negatives at Life magazine in New York and escapes his uneventful life through vivid daydreams. He is too shy to approach his co-worker Cheryl, and his online dating profile is blank where it asks about places visited and things done. When the magazine prepares its final print issue before going online, the legendary Sean O'Connell, who still shoots on film, sends Walter a roll of negatives and a wallet as a gift, saying that frame 25 captures the "quintessence" of life and should be the last cover. But negative 25 is missing, and Walter stalls the smug transition manager Hendricks. Using the other frames as clues, he sets off for Greenland, jumps from a helicopter flown by a drunken pilot into frigid, shark-infested waters to reach a ship, and follows Sean's trail to Iceland, racing across the countryside by bike and skateboard only to miss him as Eyjafjallajökull erupts.

Back home, Walter is fired and throws away Sean's wallet. Recognising his mother's piano in one of the negatives, he learns that she had met Sean and baked the clementine cake whose wrapper bore his notes, which lead Walter to the Himalayas in Afghanistan, where he finds Sean photographing a rare snow leopard. Sean reveals that he had tucked the negative inside the wallet. Detained at Los Angeles airport on his return, Walter is vouched for by Todd, the dating-site representative who has followed his adventures. His mother has rescued the wallet; Walter delivers the negative without looking at it and tells Hendricks off for his treatment of the staff. Reconciled with Cheryl, he finds the final issue on a newsstand: its cover shows Walter himself at work outside the Life building, a tribute to the magazine's staff.

After two decades of development, it premiered as the Centerpiece Gala of the New York Film Festival in October 2013 and opened in December. Reviews were mixed, with 52% on Rotten Tomatoes, critics finding it ambitious but short on substance.

overview: A version of Shakespeare's play, set in the world of warring indoor and outdoor gnomes. Garden gnomes Gnomeo and Juliet have as many obstacles to overcome as their quasi namesakes when they are caught up in a feud between neighbors. But with plastic pink flamingos and lawnmower races in the mix, can this young couple find lasting happiness?
tagline: A LITTLE ADVENTURE GOES A LAWN WAY.
title: Gnomeo & Juliet
plot:
Gnomeo & Juliet is a 3D animated comedy film released in 2011, produced by Reliance Entertainment and Miramax Films. The movie is an adaptation of William Shakespeare's classic tragic love story Romeo and Juliet, set in a world of garden gnomes.

In the beginning, we are introduced to Gnomeo (voiced by James McAvoy), a red gnome who lives in a beautiful garden filled with other colorful gnomes. Gnomeo is a bit of an oddball, as he loves to play video games and watch TV instead of engaging in traditional gnome activities like gardening.

One day, while out on a walk, Gnomeo meets Juliet (voiced by Emily Blunt), a lovely white gnome who lives in the neighboring garden. The two gnomes immediately fall in love at first sight, but their families have been feuding for years due to a long-standing dispute over a prized red rose.

The evil garden gnome, Lord Redbrick (voiced by Michael Caine), is determined to keep the red rose for himself and will stop at nothing to prevent Gnomeo and Juliet from being together. Meanwhile, Juliet's family, led by her father, King Verminus (voiced by Jim Broadbent), also wants to keep the red rose for themselves.

As Gnomeo and Juliet try to navigate their forbidden love, they must also contend with the rivalry between their families. The two gnomes come up with a plan to outsmart Lord Redbrick and his minions, but things don't go according to plan.

The plot development takes a dramatic turn when Gnomeo and Juliet's families engage in an all-out war, resulting in the destruction of both gardens. In the chaos, Gnomeo is captured by Lord Redbrick and forced to participate in a series of challenges to prove his worth as a gnome warrior.

Meanwhile, Juliet fakes her own death to avoid marrying another gnome, but Gnomeo believes she is really dead and sets out on a quest to find her. Along the way, he meets a wise old badger named Benny (voiced by Patrick Stewart) who helps him on his journey.

In the end, Gnomeo and Juliet finally reunite, but their happiness is short-lived. Lord Redbrick reveals that he has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, and the two gnomes are forced to confront each other in a final showdown.

The ending is a heartwarming and humorous take on the classic Romeo and Juliet story, with plenty of action, adventure, and witty banter. In the end, Gnomeo and Juliet's love prevails, and they are able to live happily ever after in their own little garden paradise.

Overall, Gnomeo & Juliet is a fun and lighthearted adaptation of Romeo and Juliet that is sure to delight audiences of all ages. With its colorful characters, witty dialogue, and exciting plot twists, this movie is a must-see for anyone who loves animation, comedy, or classic literature.

overview: Best pals Jason and Daniel indulge in casual flings and revel in their carefree, unattached lives. After learning that the marriage of their friend Mikey is over, they gladly welcome him back into their circle. The three young men make a pact to have fun and avoid commitment. However, when all three find themselves involved in serious relationships, they must keep their romances secret from one another.
tagline: When you realize getting some means wanting more.
title: That Awkward Moment
plot:
That Awkward Moment (released as Are We Officially Dating? in Australia, New Zealand and Indonesia) is an American romantic comedy-drama of 2014 written and directed by Tom Gormican in his debut. Zac Efron, Miles Teller and Michael B. Jordan star as the friends Jason, Daniel and Mikey, with Imogen Poots as Ellie, Mackenzie Davis as Chelsea and Jessica Lucas as Mikey's wife Vera.

Waiting on a bench in New York, Jason explains in voice-over that every relationship reaches the "So..." moment, when one partner wants to get serious, and that for him it marks the end. He and Daniel design book covers at a publishing house. When their friend Mikey, a young doctor married since college, learns that Vera wants a divorce, the three head out to celebrate his freedom with Daniel's wingwoman, Chelsea. Jason charms Ellie but, mistakenly concluding that she is a prostitute, flees her apartment in the morning, only to discover the next day that she is a new author whose book cover he is pitching. The friends vow to stay single together.

Each promptly breaks the pact in secret. Jason wins Ellie back with an apology drawn as a comic strip and begins seeing her, even getting along well with her father; Daniel falls for Chelsea; and Mikey rekindles his marriage after Vera complains that he lacks spontaneity. Everything unravels at Thanksgiving. When Ellie's father dies, Jason, unwilling to commit, skips the funeral and loses her; Vera admits she no longer loves Mikey; and Daniel, caught out, denies that he is dating Chelsea, ending that romance too. The friends quarrel over their secrecy and then patch things up. Mikey calls a woman he met on the first night, and Daniel reunites with Chelsea after being hit by a taxi. Two months later, at one of Ellie's book readings, Jason makes a public scene, recalling how they met and asking her to start over in Gramercy Park, where he once gave her a stolen key. After four hours on the bench, Ellie sits down beside him and he begins, "So..."

The script appeared on the 2010 Black List of the best unproduced screenplays under its original title. Released by Focus Features on 31 January 2014, the film drew largely negative reviews, scoring 23% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Efron won the MTV Movie Award for Best Shirtless Performance.

overview: Set in the Mayan civilization, when a man's idyllic presence is brutally disrupted by a violent invading force, he is taken on a perilous journey to a world ruled by fear and oppression where a harrowing end awaits him. Through a twist of fate and spurred by the power of his love for his woman and his family he will make a desperate break to return home and to ultimately save his way of life.
tagline: No one can outrun their destiny.
title: Apocalypto
plot:
Apocalypto is a 2006 epic adventure film directed by Mel Gibson, written by Gibson and Farrelly brothers, and produced by Gibson's Icon Productions. The film is set in Mesoamerica during the Mayan civilization's decline.

The story begins with our protagonist, Jaguar Paw (played by Rudy Younger), a young Mayan warrior who lives with his tribe in a lush jungle environment. However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when they are attacked by a rival tribe, led by the ruthless and cunning Chief Black Deer (played by Clancy Brown). The attack leaves many of the tribe's men dead or injured, including Jaguar Paw's father.

As a result, Jaguar Paw is forced to flee into the jungle with his mother, Ixchel (played by Daliah Zohar), and younger brother, Chilichin (played by Juan Carlos Villalobos). They are pursued by Chief Black Deer and his men, who seek to capture or kill them.

As they journey deeper into the jungle, Jaguar Paw and his family encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and rival tribes. Along the way, he meets a young woman named Chel (played by Sienna Guillory), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

The group eventually reaches a Mayan city, where they are captured and sold into slavery. Jaguar Paw is forced to participate in human sacrifices, which he witnesses firsthand. He also discovers that the city is being destroyed by a deadly plague, which has been brought on by the city's corrupt leaders.

As the story unfolds, Jaguar Paw becomes embroiled in a rebellion against the city's rulers, led by a wise and just leader named Kanaq (played by Cliff Curtis). Kanaq seeks to overthrow the corrupt leaders and restore balance to the city.

Throughout the film, Gibson explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption. The action sequences are intense and visceral, with a focus on practical effects and stunts. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the lush beauty of the jungle environment.

Ultimately, Jaguar Paw plays a key role in the rebellion's success, using his skills and cunning to help Kanaq defeat the corrupt leaders. In the end, the city is saved, and Jaguar Paw finds a sense of purpose and belonging among its people.

Overall, Apocalypto is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption in a richly detailed and immersive world.

overview: Young and disenchanted Sam meets a mysterious and beautiful woman who's swimming in his building's pool one night. When she suddenly vanishes the next morning, Sam embarks on a surreal quest across Los Angeles to decode the secret behind her disappearance, leading him into the murkiest depths of mystery, scandal and conspiracy.
tagline: What are they hiding?
title: Under the Silver Lake
plot:
Under the Silver Lake is a 2018 American neo-noir mystery film written and directed by David Robert Mitchell. The movie stars Andrew Garfield, Riley Keough, and Riz Ahmed.

The main themes of Under the Silver Lake include:

1. **Paranoia and Conspiracy**: The film's protagonist, Sam (played by Andrew Garfield), becomes increasingly paranoid as he delves deeper into a mysterious case involving a woman named Sarah (Riley Keough) who has gone missing. As he digs deeper, he uncovers a web of conspiracy that leads him to question the truth about his own life and the world around him.

2. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: Throughout the film, Sam's search for answers forces him to confront his own identity and sense of self. He is a man who feels disconnected from his life and struggles to find meaning in his relationships and work.

3. **Love and Connection**: The movie explores the theme of love and connection through Sam's relationship with Sarah. Their romance serves as a catalyst for Sam's investigation, but it also highlights the fragility and impermanence of human connections.

4. **The Power of Perception**: Under the Silver Lake is known for its non-linear narrative structure and multiple plot twists, which challenge the viewer's perception of reality. The film blurs the lines between truth and fiction, leaving the audience to question what is real and what is just a product of Sam's paranoid imagination.

5. **The American Dream**: The movie critiques the idea of the American Dream, which promises success, happiness, and fulfillment to those who work hard enough. Instead, Under the Silver Lake presents a darker vision of America, where the pursuit of wealth and status can lead to disillusionment and despair.

Overall, Under the Silver Lake is a complex and thought-provoking film that explores themes of paranoia, identity, love, perception, and the American Dream.

original_title: Monster High: Why Do Ghouls Fall in Love?
overview: Draculaura’s Sweet 1600th birthday is an extra special occasion to party at Monster High! But her high expectations lead to deadly results when she’s faced with the choice between practical boyfriend Clawd, and new vampire heartthrob, Valentine, a romantic blast from her past. Her ghoulfriends find it odd that Valentine created a holiday in her honor, but oddly named it after himself (how romantic?) and have to stop him before he steals her heart… literally. Draculaura must decide which boy is right for her before the party! Will she find out about Valentine’s sinister plan? Will her best ghoulfriends be able to help her in time? And most importantly… will Draculaura pass her driving test?
title: Monster High: Why Do Ghouls Fall in Love?
plot:
"Monster High: Why Do Ghouls Fall in Love?" is a 2012 animated film produced by Mattel Playground Productions. The movie revolves around the story of Frankie Stein, a young ghoul who struggles to understand her feelings for her crush, Deuce Gorgon.

The main themes of the film include:

1. Self-discovery: Frankie's journey is centered around finding her place in the world and understanding her unique identity as a half-ghoul, half-human hybrid. She must navigate her emotions and learn to accept herself for who she is.
2. Friendship and acceptance: The movie highlights the importance of having supportive friends who accept you for your differences. Frankie's friendships with Cleo de Nile, Clawdeen Wolf, and other characters help her feel more confident and secure in her identity.
3. Love and relationships: The film explores the complexities of love and relationships, particularly in the context of a monster high school setting. Frankie must navigate her feelings for Deuce while also dealing with the challenges of being a ghoul in a human-dominated world.
4. Individuality and diversity: "Why Do Ghouls Fall in Love?" celebrates the diversity of its characters, showcasing their unique personalities, interests, and backgrounds. The movie promotes the idea that everyone is special and deserves to be loved for who they are.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together with a mix of humor, adventure, and heart, making "Why Do Ghouls Fall in Love?" an entertaining and engaging watch for both kids and adults.

original_title: 映画ドラえもん のび太の宝島
overview: Doraemon, Nobita, Shizuka, Gian, and Suneo set out on an adventure in the Caribbean Sea. Nobita is the captain of a ship and fights his enemies on board. Shizuka gets kidnapped, and a storm impedes their journey. Mini-Dora help Nobita and friends on their journey. When the adventurers finally find the mysterious Treasure Island, they discover it is more than just an ordinary island.
title: Doraemon: Nobita's Treasure Island
plot:
Doraemon: Nobita's Treasure Island is a 2018 Japanese animated adventure film based on the popular manga series Doraemon created by Fujiko F. Fujio.

The main theme of Doraemon: Nobita's Treasure Island revolves around friendship, teamwork, and the importance of believing in oneself. The story follows Nobita Nobi, a young boy who is struggling to find his place in the world, as he embarks on an adventure with his robotic cat friend Doraemon.

The plot begins with Nobita discovering a mysterious treasure map that supposedly leads to a hidden treasure. Believing this will change his life for the better, Nobita sets out on a journey with Doraemon and their friends to find the treasure. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles and challenges that test their courage, wit, and determination.

As the story unfolds, Nobita learns valuable lessons about perseverance, self-confidence, and the power of friendship. Through his experiences, he comes to realize that true wealth lies not in material possessions but in the relationships and memories we create with others.

The film's climax features an exciting treasure hunt, where Nobita and his friends use their combined skills and ingenuity to overcome the challenges and reach the treasure. Ultimately, they discover that the real treasure was the friendship and adventures they shared along the way.

Throughout the film, Fujio F. Fujio's signature blend of humor, action, and heartwarming moments is on full display, making Doraemon: Nobita's Treasure Island a delightful and entertaining adventure for audiences of all ages.

overview: A bullied teenage girl forms an unlikely friendship with a mysterious young man who protects her from her assailants, while she copes with the pressures of her final examinations.
production_companies: He Nan Dian Ying Dian Shi Zhi Zuo Ji Tuan
tagline: You protect the world. I'll protect you.
title: Better Days
plot:
Better Days is a 2019 Chinese drama film directed by Han Yan. The movie follows the story of a young woman named Li Xia, who returns to her hometown after being away for several years and becomes involved in a local labor dispute.

The main themes of Better Days include:

1. Class struggle: The film highlights the stark contrast between the wealthy elite and the working class, showcasing the struggles faced by the latter.
2. Social inequality: The movie exposes the deep-seated social inequalities that exist in Chinese society, particularly in rural areas where the divide between the rich and the poor is more pronounced.
3. Labor rights: The film focuses on the plight of migrant workers who are exploited and mistreated by their employers, highlighting the need for better labor protections and working conditions.
4. Identity: Li Xia's journey is also a metaphorical exploration of her own identity and sense of belonging, as she navigates between her past and present selves.

The movie features a strong ensemble cast, including Wang Kai, Wang Qianyuan, and Yu Nan, among others. The cinematography is also noteworthy, capturing the stark beauty of rural China's landscapes and the gritty realities of life in the countryside.

Overall, Better Days is a powerful and thought-provoking film that sheds light on some of the most pressing social issues facing China today.

overview: On his way out of the wilderness, Jesus struggles with the Devil over the fate of a family in crisis, setting himself up for a dramatic test.
title: Last Days in the Desert
plot:
"Last Days in the Desert" is a 2016 American Western drama film directed by James Gray. The movie stars Nick Nolte as Henry, a former preacher who has lost his faith and is now a drifter.

The main themes of "Last Days in the Desert" include:

1. **Spiritual Crisis**: The film explores Henry's spiritual crisis, as he grapples with feelings of guilt, shame, and disillusionment with his past life as a preacher. His journey is a metaphor for the search for meaning and purpose in life.

2. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Henry's character is marked by loneliness and isolation, which serves as a backdrop to explore themes of human connection and community. The film highlights the difficulties of forming meaningful relationships in a world that often seems hostile or unforgiving.

3. **Redemption and Forgiveness**: Throughout the movie, Henry seeks redemption for past mistakes and grapples with the idea of forgiveness – both from himself and others. His journey is one of self-discovery and acceptance, as he comes to terms with his own flaws and weaknesses.

4. **The Search for Meaning**: The film's narrative is interwoven with biblical references and allusions, which serve to underscore Henry's spiritual quest. The movie explores the idea that meaning can be found in the simplest moments of life, such as a conversation with a stranger or a moment of introspection.

5. **Human Nature**: Gray's direction and Nolte's performance bring to light the complexities of human nature, revealing both the darkness and the beauty within us all. The film is a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that encourages empathy and understanding.

Overall, "Last Days in the Desert" is a thought-provoking drama that explores themes of spirituality, loneliness, redemption, and the search for meaning in life.

overview: The true and infamous story of Australia's notorious criminal Mark 'Chopper' Read and his years of crime, interest in violence, drugs and prostitutes.
tagline: Never let the truth get in the way of a good yarn.
title: Chopper
plot:
Chopper is a 2000 Australian crime drama film written and directed by Andrew Dominik in his feature debut, based on the autobiographical books of the criminal turned author Mark "Chopper" Read. It stars Eric Bana as Read, with Vince Colosimo, Simon Lyndon and Kate Beahan. Read himself suggested Bana for the role after seeing him on the sketch comedy series Full Frontal.

In 1978, Read is an inmate at Pentridge Prison in Victoria, serving a sixteen-and-a-half-year sentence for attempting to abduct a judge in a bid to free his friend Jimmy Loughnan. When a fellow prisoner, Keithy George, warns him not to cross a line in the yard marking the territory of the Painters and Dockers gang, Read crosses it the next day and stabs him repeatedly. The gang puts a $10,000 contract on his life. Read recruits Bluey Barnes and Jimmy to help him wage war on the gang, but Jimmy, wanting no part in the suicidal plan, stabs Read and cuts his own arm to claim self-defense. Read recovers and is moved to a separate cell. When the prison board refuses to transfer him for his safety, he has his ears cut off so that he will be sent to a psychiatric wing, where he finishes his sentence.

Released, Read reunites with his girlfriend, Tanya. At a nightclub he flies into a jealous rage and fires a handgun, and when he later catches Tanya on the phone with Neville Bartos, played by Colosimo, he beats both her and her mother. Learning that Neville is a wealthy supplier of amphetamines to Melbourne's western suburbs, Read demands money and shoots him in the stomach when he refuses. He then visits Jimmy, who lives with his pregnant fiancée, Mandy, and their young daughter, claims that the police have given him a green light to shoot criminals, and confronts Jimmy at gunpoint about the contracts on his life before apologizing and giving him money. In the Bojangles car park, an associate called Sammy the Turk says he wants to show Read something, and after an argument, Read shoots him in the eye with a sawn-off shotgun. Mandy, who witnessed the killing, becomes a Crown witness. It emerges that Sammy had been leading Read into a trap for Jimmy to collect the contract but chose the wrong car park. Read is acquitted of murder but convicted of wounding Neville and sentenced to five years.

The film opened at number one in Australia in August 2000. It grossed A$5.9 million locally and received positive reviews, with critics singling out Bana's performance; it has since gained a cult following.

overview: When the kingdom's most wanted-and most charming-bandit Flynn Rider hides out in a mysterious tower, he's taken hostage by Rapunzel, a beautiful and feisty tower-bound teen with 70 feet of magical, golden hair. Flynn's curious captor, who's looking for her ticket out of the tower where she's been locked away for years, strikes a deal with the handsome thief and the unlikely duo sets off on an action-packed escapade, complete with a super-cop horse, an over-protective chameleon and a gruff gang of pub thugs.
tagline: They're taking adventure to new lengths.
title: Tangled
plot:
Tangled is a 2010 animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie is a modern retelling of the classic fairy tale Rapunzel, with a few twists and creative liberties.

The story follows Princess Rapunzel (voiced by Mandy Moore), a young woman with long, magical hair that has healing properties. She lives in a tower in the kingdom of Corona, guarded by Mother Gothel (voiced by Donna Murphy), who claims to be Rapunzel's mother. However, it is revealed that Gothel has been using Rapunzel's hair to stay young and beautiful.

One day, thief Flynn Rider (voiced by Zachary Levi) stumbles upon the tower while on the run from the law. He convinces Rapunzel to join him on a journey to see the floating lights in the sky, which she believes are her only connection to the outside world. As they travel together, they develop feelings for each other and become embroiled in a plot by Gothel to use Rapunzel's hair to gain control over the kingdom.

Throughout their adventure, Rapunzel discovers her true identity and the secrets of her past. She also learns about her royal heritage and the prophecy that foretells her destiny as the queen of Corona. Meanwhile, Flynn must confront his own troubled past and learn to trust himself and others.

The movie features a range of memorable characters, including Maximus (voiced by Donal Logue), a loyal and lovable horse who becomes Rapunzel's companion, and Pascal (voiced by Jeffrey Tambor), a chatty and endearing pet chameleon. The film's soundtrack, featuring songs like "When Will My Life Begin" and "I've Got a Dream," is also noteworthy for its catchy melodies and heartfelt lyrics.

Overall, Tangled offers a fresh take on the classic Rapunzel story, with engaging characters, witty humor, and stunning animation. The movie's themes of self-discovery, friendship, and embracing one's true identity make it a delightful and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

overview: Queen Ramonda, Shuri, M’Baku, Okoye and the Dora Milaje fight to protect their nation from intervening world powers in the wake of King T’Challa’s death. As the Wakandans strive to embrace their next chapter, the heroes must band together with the help of War Dog Nakia and Everett Ross and forge a new path for the kingdom of Wakanda.
tagline: Forever.
title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
plot:
Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is a 2022 superhero film directed by Ryan Coogler, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics character Black Panther. The movie takes place after the events of Avengers: Endgame.

The story begins with the death of King T'Challa (played by Chadwick Boseman), who had assumed the mantle of Black Panther to protect his nation Wakanda from threats both within and outside its borders. The film follows Shuri (Letitia Wright), T'Challa's sister, as she navigates her new role as queen and tries to find a way to honor her brother's legacy.

As Shuri delves deeper into the mysteries of her brother's death, she discovers that it was not a natural occurrence but rather a result of a catastrophic event known as the "Heart-Shaped Herb" being destroyed. This herb is a powerful plant that gives Black Panther his powers and allows him to heal from injuries.

Shuri soon learns that the destruction of the Heart-Shaped Herb has caused a ripple effect, leading to the return of Namor (played by Tenoch Huerta), the long-lost king of Atlantis. Namor seeks revenge against Wakanda for its role in the destruction of his homeland and its people.

Meanwhile, Shuri is joined by a new generation of heroes, including Riri Williams (Dominique Thorne), a brilliant inventor who creates a suit inspired by Iron Man's armor, and M'Baku (Winston Duke), the leader of the Jabari Land tribe. Together, they form a team to protect Wakanda from Namor's attacks.

Throughout the film, Shuri grapples with her own identity and sense of purpose as she tries to balance her desire for revenge against Namor with her duty to protect her people. Along the way, she discovers that her brother's legacy is not just about power but also about love, family, and community.

The movie features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a powerful performance from Letitia Wright as Shuri. While it may not have the same level of emotional resonance as its predecessor, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is a worthy sequel that expands on the world and characters introduced in the first film.

Overall, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of grief, identity, and community. With its richly detailed world-building and strong performances, it's a must-see for fans of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

overview: A man who lost his family in the September 11 attack on New York City runs into his old college roommate. Rekindling the friendship is the one thing that appears able to help the man recover from his grief.
tagline: Let in the unexpected.
title: Reign Over Me
plot:
Reign Over Me is a poignant and powerful drama that delves into the complexities of grief, loss, and redemption. The film tells the story of Charlie Fineman, a man who lost his entire family in the 9/11 attacks, and his journey to come to terms with his past and find a new sense of purpose.

At its core, Reign Over Me is a movie about the devastating effects of trauma and the struggle to heal. Charlie's character is a complex and nuanced portrayal of a man who has been shattered by tragedy, and his story serves as a powerful exploration of the human capacity for resilience and survival in the face of unimaginable pain.

The film also explores themes of guilt, anger, and regret, as Charlie grapples with the what-ifs and maybes that haunt him. His relationship with Norman, a fellow survivor who has found a way to move on from his trauma, serves as a catalyst for Charlie's own journey towards healing and redemption.

Through its thoughtful and introspective portrayal of its characters, Reign Over Me raises important questions about the nature of grief, the power of human connection, and the possibility of finding meaning and purpose in the midst of unimaginable loss. Ultimately, the film is a powerful exploration of the human spirit's capacity for hope, forgiveness, and transformation.

overview: The dark secrets of a seemingly peaceful island threaten to swallow up an orphaned student when he grows close to a mysterious new teacher.
title: Black Island
plot:
Black Island (German: Schwarze Insel) is a 2021 German psychological thriller made for Netflix, directed by Miguel Alexandre from a screenplay he wrote with Lisa Carline Hofer. Philip Froissant stars as the student Jonas Hansen, with Alice Dwyer as the teacher Helena Jung, Hanns Zischler as Jonas's grandfather Friedrich and Mercedes Müller as his classmate Nina Cohrs. It was filmed on the North Frisian island of Amrum, with shooting completed in November 2020.

A year after his parents were killed when their car left the road and hit a tree, and after the death of his grandmother, Jonas, who is about to finish school, lives on a remote, picturesque island with his cold, recently widowed grandfather. He dreams of becoming a writer, and he is drifting into a romance with Nina. When the class's regular German teacher is injured in an accident abroad, the young substitute Helena arrives. She recognises Jonas's talent, encourages his writing and soon seduces him, drawing him into an intense, secret relationship.

The audience already knows that Helena caused the crash that killed Jonas's parents by driving straight at their car on the wrong side of the road. Nina grows suspicious of the newcomer, suspects she had a hand in the teacher's injury and finds a photograph in an old yearbook of a teacher called Maria Roth who looks exactly like Helena, but before she can learn more, Helena kills her. Shortly afterward Friedrich suffers a seizure that leaves him partly paralysed and unable to speak. At his hospital bed, Helena reveals the truth: she is Maria's daughter by Friedrich, and therefore Jonas's aunt, and after he abandoned her pregnant mother, Maria took her own life. Helena admits killing his wife and Jonas's parents and vows to kill Jonas too. Bringing Friedrich home to watch, she drugs Jonas and tries to drown him in the pond, but he breaks free, and when she tries to strangle him he stabs her with a shard of glass. Friedrich gives Jonas Maria's farewell letter, which confirms the story, and Jonas leaves the island on the ferry.

Netflix released the film worldwide in August 2021. Reviews were mostly unfavourable. Decider called it a half-baked slow burn whose revelations come too late and feel rushed, though it praised Müller, and German critics, including kino-zeit.de and the RedaktionsNetzwerk Deutschland, found it predictable or lacking tension while admiring Dwyer's performance and the rugged island setting.

overview: Eric and Kurt Sloane are the descendants of a well-known Venice, California-based family of martial artists. Kurt has always been in older brother, Eric's shadow, as he lacks the instincts needed to become a champion. Against Kurt's concerns, Eric accepts a paid offer and travels to Thailand to challenge the Muay Thai champion Tong Po and fails with dire consequences. Kurt sets out for revenge. He trains with his brother's mentor, Master Durand, for a Muay Thai fight against the merciless champion, Tong Po. Durand first thinks Kurt is impossible to train, but through a series of spiritual exercises and tests, Durand discovers that Kurt has a deeper strength that will carry him through his final showdown with Tong Po.
title: Kickboxer: Vengeance
plot:
Kickboxer: Vengeance is a 2016 martial arts film directed by Yuen Woo-ping and starring Tony Jaa, Muay Thai fighter and actor. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1989 film Kickboxer.

The main themes of Kickboxer: Vengeance revolve around revenge, redemption, and self-discovery. The protagonist, Jay Kuan (played by Tony Jaa), is a young man seeking vengeance against Tong Po (played by Hafþór Júlíus Björnsson), the man responsible for his brother's death.

As Jay navigates the world of Muay Thai, he must confront his own demons and learn to control his temper in order to achieve his goal. Along the way, he meets a new ally, Tong's sister, Ling (played by Katheryn Winnick), who helps him on his quest for revenge.

Throughout the film, Jay faces various challenges and obstacles that test his skills and resolve. He must confront his own personal struggles with anger and aggression in order to find redemption and move forward from his past traumas.

The movie also explores themes of cultural identity and the importance of family. Jay's journey is not just about seeking revenge but also about finding a sense of belonging and purpose in his life.

Ultimately, Kickboxer: Vengeance is a story about the power of forgiveness, redemption, and self-discovery. Through its action-packed sequences and emotional character development, the film delivers a thrilling and satisfying ride for audiences.

overview: France asleep in the nineteenth century, governed by steam and Napoleon VI, where scientists vanish mysteriously, a girl, Avril, goes in search of her missing scientist parents.
tagline: A Film By Christian Desmares And Franck Ekinci
title: April and the Extraordinary World
plot:
April and the Extraordinary World is a French animated science fiction film that tells the story of a young girl named April who lives in a post-apocalyptic world where humans have been wiped out by an alien invasion. The movie follows her journey as she embarks on a quest to find her father, a renowned scientist who may hold the key to humanity's survival.

The main theme of April and the Extraordinary World is the resilience of human spirit in the face of catastrophic loss and destruction. Despite the desolate landscape and the absence of humans, the film suggests that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope for a better future. The movie also explores the idea of identity and belonging, as April struggles to find her place in a world that no longer makes sense.

The film's portrayal of a futuristic society that has been ravaged by war and environmental disaster serves as a commentary on our own world's relationship with technology and the environment. The movie highlights the consequences of unchecked technological advancement and the importance of preserving human connection and community in the face of rapid progress.

Through April's journey, the film also touches on themes of love, loss, and sacrifice, as she navigates her complicated relationships with her father and the world around her. Ultimately, the movie offers a message of hope and renewal, suggesting that even in the most desperate of circumstances, there is always the possibility for transformation and rebirth.

Overall, April and the Extraordinary World is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its unique blend of science fiction and coming-of-age storytelling.

overview: In the not-too-distant future, two drifters traveling through the desert stumble across the biggest gold nugget ever found and the dream of immense wealth and greed takes hold. They hatch a plan to excavate their bounty, with one man leaving to secure the necessary tools while the other remains with the gold. The man who remains must endure harsh desert elements, ravenous wild dogs, and mysterious intruders, while battling the sinking suspicion that he has been abandoned to his fate.
tagline: Survive at any cost
title: Gold
plot:
Gold is a 2022 Australian survival thriller film directed by Anthony Hayes, who co-stars alongside Zac Efron and Susie Porter. It was released internationally on 13 January 2022 before debuting on the streaming service Stan on 26 January, and a limited theatrical and video-on-demand release followed on 11 March 2022.

In a dystopian near future, a lone traveller named Virgil arrives at a remote outpost and pays a local man, Keith, to drive him across an inhospitable desert to a place known as the Compound. During the journey the car overheats, and while stopped the two men stumble on an enormous gold nugget buried in the ground. Unable to dig it out with their basic tools, they agree that one of them must stay to guard the find while the other leaves to fetch an excavator. Keith suggests that Virgil does not have what it takes to survive alone, but Virgil insists on staying, since he was the one who found the gold. Keith leaves him with the remaining supplies and promises to return in five days. As the days pass under the scorching sun, Virgil's body and mind begin to deteriorate, and paranoia sets in. He builds a shelter from the wreckage of a crashed plane, fends off wild dogs, and loses precious water in a clumsy encounter with a snake. When a woman appears in the desert, suspicious of his reasons for being there and contemptuous of people fleeing the cities for the resources of her land, accuses him of hiding something, the encounter ends in violence. A sandstorm then destroys his camp and leaves him badly wounded, and as he drifts between consciousness and delirium, haunted by visions and visited by another mysterious scavenger, he clings to his radio and to the hope that Keith will return before the desert claims him.

On Rotten Tomatoes, 65% of 51 critics' reviews of Gold are positive, with a consensus that Efron's committed central performance makes the film worth watching even when the film as a whole struggles to match it. It grossed about $230,000 worldwide in theaters.

overview: When an IMF mission ends badly, the world is faced with dire consequences. As Ethan Hunt takes it upon himself to fulfill his original briefing, the CIA begin to question his loyalty and his motives. The IMF team find themselves in a race against time, hunted by assassins while trying to prevent a global catastrophe.
tagline: Some missions are not a choice.
title: Mission: Impossible - Fallout
plot:
Mission: Impossible - Fallout is a 2018 action spy film directed by Christopher McQuarrie and produced by Paramount Pictures. The movie marks the sixth installment in the Mission: Impossible film series.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and his team, including Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg), Luther Stickell (Ving Rhames), and Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson), on a mission to neutralize a threat from the terrorist group, The Apostles. However, things take a turn when they discover that the Apostles are actually working for August Walker (Henry Cavill), an American CIA operative.

As Ethan delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a plot by August to sell nuclear materials to the highest bidder. Meanwhile, Ilsa is revealed to be working undercover as a double agent, feeding information to The Apostles while secretly working with Ethan's team.

The stakes escalate when Ethan and his team are ambushed by The Apostles in Paris, resulting in Luther being killed. The team then flees to Istanbul, where they discover that August has stolen the plutonium from the nuclear facility, intending to sell it to a terrorist organization.

Ethan and Ilsa embark on a perilous journey across Europe, following a trail of clues and encountering various obstacles along the way. They visit Morocco, Austria, and Norway, all while being pursued by The Apostles and August's henchmen.

As the story unfolds, Ethan and Ilsa grow closer, but their relationship is complicated by Ilsa's loyalty to her country and her allegiance to Ethan's team. Meanwhile, August's true intentions are revealed, and Ethan must confront him in a thrilling showdown.

The film's climax features an intense sequence of action-packed set pieces, including a HALO (high-altitude, low-opening) skydive jump by Ethan and Ilsa, as well as a high-speed car chase through the streets of Paris. The final confrontation between Ethan and August takes place at a nuclear facility in Norway, where Ethan must use his skills to disable the plutonium's delivery system.

In the end, Ethan successfully prevents the sale of the plutonium, but not before Ilsa is mortally wounded by one of August's henchmen. As Ethan holds her dying body, he realizes that their relationship has become a central part of his mission. The film concludes with Ethan and his team escaping, while Ilsa passes away in Ethan's arms.

Throughout the movie, Tom Cruise performs many of his own stunts, which adds to the film's sense of realism and authenticity. The action sequences are expertly choreographed, and the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the beauty of various locations around the world.

Overall, Mission: Impossible - Fallout is a thrilling and entertaining spy thriller that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and suspenseful storytelling.

overview: A mysterious place, an indescribable prison, a deep hole. An unknown number of levels. Two inmates living on each level. A descending platform containing food for all of them. An inhuman fight for survival, but also an opportunity for solidarity.
title: The Platform
plot:
The Platform is a Spanish science fiction film written and directed by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia, released in 2019. The movie premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and received critical acclaim for its unique concept, social commentary, and tense atmosphere.

In a dystopian future, humanity has been reduced to a single, massive spaceship, where the ruling class lives in luxury while the lower classes are forced to survive on a vertical platform that descends into the depths of the ship. The platform is divided into 200 levels, each with its own unique environment and inhabitants. The upper levels are opulent and extravagant, with lavish parties and excesses, while the lower levels are cramped, dirty, and poverty-stricken.

The story follows Daphne (played by Zorion Eguileor), a young man who is one of the lowest-ranking members on the platform. He lives in Level 1, where he struggles to survive amidst the squalid conditions. The platform's strict rules dictate that each level must consume all its food and resources before moving up, ensuring that no one can ascend to a higher level.

As the story unfolds, Daphne becomes aware of the cruel system that governs the platform. He witnesses the brutal treatment of those who are deemed "undesirable" by the ruling class, including the elderly, the disabled, and those who are deemed "unproductive." The platform's inhabitants are forced to fight for survival, often resorting to cannibalism when resources become scarce.

One day, a new prisoner is brought to Level 1, which sets off a chain of events that challenges Daphne's perception of the world. This prisoner, known only as "The Boy" (played by Ivan Massagué), is from a higher level and possesses skills and knowledge that could potentially disrupt the status quo.

As the platform continues its descent into chaos, Daphne finds himself at the center of a rebellion against the ruling class. With The Boy's help, he begins to question the morality of the system and the true nature of those who govern the platform. Along the way, he must confront his own demons and make difficult choices that will determine his fate.

Throughout the film, Gaztelu-Urrutia explores themes of social inequality, class struggle, and the human condition. The Platform is a thought-provoking commentary on our society's obsession with wealth and power, as well as the consequences of unchecked capitalism.

The film's tension builds towards its climax, where Daphne and The Boy must confront the ruling class in a desperate bid for survival. In the end, only one can ascend to the top level, and the true cost of their victory is revealed.

Overall, The Platform is a gripping and unsettling film that challenges viewers to think critically about the world we live in. With its unique concept, strong performances, and thought-provoking themes, it has become a modern classic of science fiction cinema.

overview: Although theorised, no one is really ready when a mountain pass above the scenic and narrow Geiranger fjord in Norway collapses and creates a tsunami over 300 feet high. A geologist is one of those caught in the middle of it.
tagline: It was only a matter of time.
title: The Wave
plot:
The Wave is a 2015 Swedish drama film directed by Roine Ehnmark, produced by Film i Väst, and released on October 16, 2015.
