The story revolves around a group of high school students who are struggling to find their place in the world. The main character, Elias (played by Gustaf Skarsgård), is an outsider who feels disconnected from his peers. He is fascinated by the concept of the "wave" and its potential to bring people together.

Elias becomes obsessed with the idea of creating a wave that will unite everyone and make them feel part of something bigger than themselves. He starts to recruit like-minded students, including his best friend, Marcus (played by Malte Gårdinger), and a new student, Sofia (played by Maja Johansson).

As Elias's enthusiasm grows, so does the group's momentum. They start to organize events and activities that are designed to create a sense of community and belonging among their peers. However, as time goes on, it becomes clear that Elias's vision is not just about creating a wave, but also about exerting control over his fellow students.

Elias's behavior becomes increasingly authoritarian, and he starts to manipulate the group into doing his bidding. He uses tactics such as peer pressure, guilt trips, and emotional manipulation to keep everyone in line. The group begins to feel trapped and suffocated by Elias's demands, but they are also drawn to him because of his charisma and conviction.

As tensions rise within the group, it becomes clear that Elias's vision for a wave is not just about creating a sense of community, but also about exerting power over others. The film takes a dark turn as Elias's behavior becomes more and more extreme, and the group begins to realize that they are trapped in his web.

The Wave explores themes of teenage angst, peer pressure, and the dangers of unchecked ambition. It is a thought-provoking commentary on the ways in which young people can be manipulated and exploited by charismatic leaders.

In the end, the film builds towards a tragic confrontation between Elias and his followers. The wave that Elias has created ultimately proves to be a destructive force that consumes everyone involved. The film ends with a sense of devastation and loss, as the survivors are left to pick up the pieces and try to make sense of what happened.

Overall, The Wave is a gripping and thought-provoking drama that explores the complexities of teenage relationships and the dangers of unchecked ambition.

overview: Five friends go for a break at a remote cabin, where they get more than they bargained for, discovering the truth behind the cabin in the woods.
tagline: You think you know the story.
title: The Cabin in the Woods
plot:
The Cabin in the Woods is a 2012 American horror film directed by Drew Goddard and produced by Lionsgate. The movie takes place in a remote cabin in the woods, where five college students go to spend their spring break.

The story begins with Dana Polk (Kristen Connolly), Jules Louden (Frances O'Connor), Curt Vaughan (Chris Hemsworth), Holden McCrea (Jesse Williams), and Marty Mikalski (Richard Jenkins) - who is actually an older man, not a college student - arriving at the cabin. They are all excited to spend their break together, but things take a dark turn when they discover that the cabin has a mind of its own.

As the group settles in, they begin to experience strange occurrences and supernatural events, which seem to be connected to an ancient ritual. The group soon realizes that they are part of a larger experiment, designed by a secret organization known as the Order of the Garter.

The Order, led by Gary Sitterson (Bradley Whitford) and Wendy Linowski (Amy Acker), has been manipulating the students' actions from behind the scenes. They have set up a complex system to control the group's behavior, using a combination of psychological manipulation, technology, and supernatural forces.

As the night wears on, the group is forced to participate in the ritual, which involves sacrificing one of their own to an ancient deity known as the "Tribal Elder." The students are unaware that they are part of a larger experiment, designed to appease the deity and ensure the continuation of human life.

Throughout the movie, the characters' actions are influenced by the Order's manipulation. However, as the night progresses, the group begins to realize what is happening and starts to fight back against their captors. The movie takes a dark and unexpected turn when Marty, who is actually an older man with a hidden agenda, reveals his true intentions.

In the end, the group manages to subvert the Order's plan and sacrifice themselves to the deity, but not in the way that was expected. Instead of sacrificing one of their own, they use the ritual to destroy the cabin and kill the Order members. The movie ends with a twist: Marty is revealed to be an older man who has been manipulating the group all along, and he is actually the one who has been controlling the experiment.

The Cabin in the Woods is a clever subversion of traditional horror movie tropes, using humor, satire, and social commentary to critique the genre. The movie's twist ending adds a layer of complexity to the story, making it a thought-provoking and entertaining watch.

overview: A brother and sister driving home through an isolated countryside from college encounter a flesh-eating creature in the midst of its ritualistic eating spree.
tagline: Jeepers Creepers
title: Jeepers Creepers
plot:
Jeepers Creepers is a 2001 American horror film directed by Victor Salva and produced by United Artists. The movie follows the story of Darry Jenner (Justin Long) and his brother Travis (Gina Philips) as they embark on a road trip across the country to visit their father's grave.

The story begins with the introduction of the Creeper, a monstrous creature that is said to appear every 23 years to feast on human flesh. The Creeper is an ancient being with supernatural powers, and it is said to be able to control the minds of humans, forcing them to do its bidding.

As Darry and Travis drive through the desert, they come across a mysterious truck stop where they meet a local named John Smith (Jonathan Breck), who claims to have information about their father's grave. However, things take a dark turn when the Creeper appears, and John is revealed to be possessed by the creature.

The Creeper begins to terrorize Darry and Travis, forcing them to flee from its wrath. Along the way, they meet a local woman named Dr. Tendler (Patricia Belcher), who helps them understand the legend of the Creeper and how it can be defeated.

As the story unfolds, Darry and Travis discover that their father's grave is actually a trap set by an ancient cult to contain the Creeper. The brothers soon realize that they are in grave danger and must find a way to defeat the creature before it's too late.

The climax of the movie features an intense showdown between Darry and Travis, who use a combination of ingenuity and bravery to outsmart the Creeper. In the end, they manage to trap the creature in a tomb, saving themselves and their father's grave from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds as the Creeper becomes increasingly menacing, forcing Darry and Travis to confront their deepest fears. The film's climax is both intense and satisfying, providing a sense of closure for the characters.

Overall, Jeepers Creepers is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of family, sacrifice, and the supernatural. With its blend of action, horror, and humor, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

original_title: Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel
overview: Pop sensations Alvin, Simon and Theodore end up in the care of Dave Seville's twenty-something nephew Toby. The boys must put aside music super stardom to return to school, and are tasked with saving the school's music program by winning the $25,000 prize in a battle of the bands. But the Chipmunks unexpectedly meet their match in three singing chipmunks known as The Chipettes - Brittany, Eleanor and Jeanette. Romantic and musical sparks are ignited when the Chipmunks and Chipettes square off.
tagline: The Boys are back in town... and they have competition.
title: Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel
plot:
Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel is a 2009 American musical comedy film directed by Brian Levant, produced by Ross Bagdasarian Jr., and written by Ross Bagdasarian Jr. and Ross Schwartz.

The movie begins with Alvin (voiced by Jason Lee), Simon (voiced by David Cross), Theodore (voiced by Matthew Gray Gubler), and their manager Dave Seville (voiced by Justin Long) preparing for the Chipmunks' upcoming concert at the Hollywood Bowl. However, things take a turn when the Chipmunks discover that they are being sued by Ian Hawke (voiced by Jesse McCartney), a young singer who claims to be the original owner of the Chipmunks' music.

As the lawsuit progresses, Alvin and his brothers begin to experience a series of strange occurrences, including mysterious messages from an unknown sender. They soon realize that the messages are coming from a rival group called The Chipettes (voiced by Amy Poehler, Christina Aguilera, and Jessica Alba), who were created by Ian Hawke's father.

The Chipmunks and The Chipettes engage in a series of competitions to prove their musical superiority, with the winner earning the rights to their music. Meanwhile, Dave becomes increasingly stressed as he tries to manage the Chipmunks' schedules and deal with the lawsuit.

As the competition heats up, Alvin begins to develop feelings for Jeanette (voiced by Amy Poehler), one of The Chipettes. However, Simon is smitten with Brittany (voiced by Christina Aguilera) and Theodore becomes infatuated with Eleanor (voiced by Jessica Alba).

In the end, the Chipmunks and The Chipettes come together to perform a joint concert at the Hollywood Bowl, which showcases their musical talents and helps to resolve the lawsuit. In the process, Ian Hawke learns that his father was not the original owner of the Chipmunks' music, and he drops the lawsuit.

The movie ends with the Chipmunks and The Chipettes performing together as a single group, with Alvin and Jeanette sharing a romantic moment. Dave is relieved to have resolved the lawsuit and can finally focus on managing his beloved chipmunk friends.

Overall, Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel is a lighthearted and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, music, and competition. With its catchy musical numbers and lovable characters, it's no wonder this movie became a hit with both children and adults alike.

overview: During transport from the Philippines to South Korea, a group of dangerous criminals unites to stage a coordinated escape attempt. As the jailbreak escalates into a bloody, all-out riot, the fugitives and their allies from the outside exact a brutal terror campaign against the special agents onboard the ship.
title: Project Wolf Hunting
plot:
Project Wolf Hunting, released in Korea as Neukdae Sanyang ("Wolf Hunt"), is a 2022 South Korean science fiction action horror film directed by Kim Hong-sun. Seo In-guk plays the tattooed gang leader Park Jong-doo and Jang Dong-yoon the withdrawn prisoner Lee Do-il, with Park Ho-san, Jung So-min, Sung Dong-il and Choi Gwi-hwa. Almost all of its blood-soaked action takes place aboard the cargo ship Frontier Titan as it carries fugitives from the Philippines to Korea.

After an earlier attempt to fly Korean criminals home from the Philippines ends in a deadly bombing at the airport, the authorities move a new group of fugitives by sea under heavy police guard. Jong-doo, a violent and sadistic killer, earns an early beating from the tough detective Lee Seok-woo, but he has planned an escape in advance. Meanwhile a doctor repeatedly slips down into the hold with medical supplies, where a secret passenger is kept in a drugged sleep: Alpha, a genetically engineered super soldier being smuggled to Korea, linked to a pharmaceutical company's anti-aging research.

Once the ship is at sea, Jong-doo slips his handcuffs, accomplices kill the guards and seize the bridge to cut off communications, and the freed prisoners launch a bloody riot against their police escorts. The carnage wakes Alpha, a near-invulnerable berserker of enormous strength, who begins tearing through criminals and officers alike. A small band of survivors, including the determined officer Lee Da-yeon and Do-il, joins forces against him. Do-il proves to be far more than a prisoner: he was himself an unwilling subject of the company's experiments, which gave him superhuman abilities, and after he tried to escape, its agents killed his wife and took his son. He has quietly followed Alpha's trail to find the people responsible, and the film's final stretch pits him against Alpha and the company's other enhanced soldiers.

The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival on September 16, 2022, and opened in South Korea on September 21. It grossed about $3.9 million worldwide on a budget of roughly $9.1 million. It earned 88% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 53, critics relishing its extreme gore and spectacle while faulting thin characters and a convoluted backstory.

original_title: All the Money in the World
overview: The story of the kidnapping of 16-year-old John Paul Getty III and the desperate attempt by his devoted mother to convince his billionaire grandfather Jean Paul Getty to pay the ransom.
tagline: J. Paul Getty had a fortune. Everyone else paid the price.
title: All the Money in the World
plot:
All the Money in the World is a 2017 biographical crime drama film directed by Ridley Scott, based on John Pearson's 1995 book "Painfully Rich: The Outrageous Fortune and Misfortunes of the Heirs of J. Paul Getty". 

The main themes of All the Money in the World include:

1. Family dynamics and power struggles: The film explores the complex relationships within the Getty family, particularly between J. Paul Getty (played by Christopher Plummer) and his grandson John Paul Getty III (played by Mark Wahlberg). The tension between them is palpable as they clash over the management of the family's vast fortune.

2. Greed and materialism: The film critiques the excesses of wealth and privilege, highlighting the Getty family's ruthless pursuit of power and wealth at any cost. This theme is exemplified through John Paul Getty III's kidnapping and the subsequent negotiations with his kidnappers.

3. Class and social status: The movie portrays the stark contrast between the wealthy elite and those on the fringes of society. The kidnappers, who are portrayed as desperate and marginalized individuals, serve as a foil to the Getty family's opulence and entitlement.

4. Corruption and exploitation: The film exposes the dark underbelly of wealth and power, revealing how the Getty family exploited their wealth and influence to silence their critics and avoid accountability for their actions.

5. Redemption and sacrifice: Through John Paul Getty III's character, the film explores the theme of redemption and personal growth. Despite being trapped in a life of privilege and entitlement, he begins to question his values and ultimately makes a heroic sacrifice to save his family from further exploitation.

Overall, All the Money in the World is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on the darker aspects of wealth and power, while also exploring themes of family, class, and redemption.

overview: Three friends try to save their mummified friend, Harold, from greedy criminals by returning him to his resting place before midnight on Halloween.
title: Under Wraps
plot:
Under Wraps is an American family horror comedy made for television in 2021, directed by Alex Zamm, who wrote it with William Robertson, as a remake of the 1997 film of the same name, the first Disney Channel Original Movie. Produced by MarVista Entertainment and Brightlight Pictures, it features Malachi Barton in the role of Marshall, with Christian J. Simon as Gilbert, Sophia Hammons as Amy and Phil Wright as the mummy Harold, plus Melanie Brook as Buzzy, Brent Stait as the villain Kubot and Karin Konoval as the collector Ravensworth.

Twelve-year-old Marshall loves horror films, unlike his timid best friend Gilbert, and is struggling to accept Ted, the man his divorced mother is dating. The boys see a body being carried into the house of their creepy neighbour, Mr. Kubot. On a museum trip they team up with Amy, a newcomer who shares Marshall's taste for horror, and hear of an Egyptian mummy couple, one of whom has mysteriously gone missing. Sneaking into Kubot's house, the three find the mummy, which comes to life and follows them home. Marshall hides him in his bedroom, names him Harold and introduces him to pizza and hot sauce, and the kids plan to make a mummy film with him for a school project. When Harold wanders off to the museum where his beloved's sarcophagus lies, they discover that his amulet is what brought him to life.

Their monster-expert friend Buzzy translates the amulet: unless both mummies are back in their sarcophagi by the third day, Harold will crumble to dust. Meanwhile, Amy tells Marshall how she came to accept her stepfather, encouraging him to give Ted a chance. Kubot, realising that a living mummy could make him rich, snatches the amulet from Harold at the school's Halloween carnival and delivers him to Ravensworth at an abandoned ice cream factory. Gilbert loses his nerve but returns to retrieve the amulet, revived Harold fights off the henchmen, and Buzzy's trap knocks out Kubot and Ravensworth. The friends break into the museum to reunite Harold with his love before he returns to his sarcophagus, and Gilbert admits that his fear of losing his friends drove him back.

Shot in and around Vancouver, the film premiered on Disney Channel on 1 October 2021 and on Disney+ a week later. Reviews were mixed, though Common Sense Media gave it four out of five stars for its diversity, spookiness and humour.

overview: A former Marine races against time to save a group of hostages -- including his young daughter and a congressman — when armed militants take over his stepfather's store.
tagline: Free the hostages. Or everyone dies.
title: Rogue Hostage
plot:
Rogue Hostage is an American action thriller of 2021 directed by Jon Keeyes. Tyrese Gibson stars as Kyle Snowden, a former Marine, with John Malkovich as his stepfather, Congressman Sam Nelson, Christopher Backus as the mercenary leader Eagan Raize, Michael Jai White as Sparks, Holly Taylor as Mikki, Luna Lauren Velez as Sunshine, Carlos Sanchez as the boy Manny and Brandi Bravo as Kyle's colleague Clove Martinez.

Haunted by nightmares of the battlefield, Kyle left the military after accidentally shooting and killing his own partner, an incident that left him unable to pick up a gun again. He now works for Child Protective Services in a rural American town and is raising his young daughter, Angel, alone since his wife walked out. Meanwhile a band of rogue mercenaries led by Eagan Raize is plotting against Congressman Nelson. Eagan's father, Luther, was once Nelson's business partner and spent eighteen years in prison for fraud, and Eagan is convinced that Nelson destroyed his father's life in order to seize control of their business.

Eagan's crew plants a bomb and takes over Nelson's store while Kyle, Angel and many others are inside, holding them hostage. Intending to ruin Nelson and make an example of him before the town, Eagan instead ends up looting the store's money and taking Sunshine at gunpoint because he is infatuated with her. When the gunmen kill Clove, Kyle's CPS colleague, he finds himself responsible for Manny, a young boy in her care. Forced to take up arms again, Kyle conquers his fear, storms the store and defeats the mercenaries. In the aftermath Nelson tries to persuade the police that the siege was a robbery rather than an act of terrorism, in order to claim the insurance money, but his scheme collapses when Mikki makes off with his money for herself and Sunshine. Kyle prepares to ask the court for temporary custody of Manny, and he and his stepfather finally make their peace.

Originally titled Red 48, the film completed shooting in September 2020 and was released in the United States on 11 June 2021 by Vertical Entertainment and Redbox Entertainment. Critics were unimpressed, giving it a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from ten reviews, though The Guardian's Leslie Felperin, awarding two stars, found the bloody, cheesy action decent fun.

original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- 大興奮!みかづき島のアニマル騒動だってばよ
overview: Naruto Uzumaki, Kakashi Hatake, Sakura Haruno, and Rock Lee are assigned to protect the prince of the Land of the Moon, Michiru, during his world trip; other escorts had been hired, but quit due to being treated poorly. The Land of the Moon is a very wealthy nation, so Michiru tends to buy whatever he wants, and has a very materialistic worldview. His Hikaru, also acts in much the same manner.
title: Naruto: Guardians of the Crescent Moon Kingdom
plot:
Naruto the Movie: Guardians of the Crescent Moon Kingdom (Japanese title literally "Great Excitement! The Animal Panic of Crescent Moon Island!") is a Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure of 2006 written and directed by Toshiyuki Tsuru and produced by Studio Pierrot, based on Masashi Kishimoto's manga. The third and last film of the series' first part, it features the voices of Junko Takeuchi as Naruto Uzumaki, Chie Nakamura as Sakura Haruno, Yōichi Masukawa as Rock Lee, Kazuhiko Inoue as Kakashi Hatake, Kyōsuke Ikeda as Prince Hikaru and Akio Ōtsuka as his father Michiru.

Naruto, Kakashi, Sakura and Lee are assigned to escort Michiru, heir to the fabulously rich Land of the Moon, and his spoiled son Hikaru home. Michiru casually buys an entire circus so that Hikaru can befriend its star sabre-toothed cat, Chamū, and its monkey partner Kiki, but Chamū attacks the boy. Michiru's former wife, Amayo, rejects his hopes of reconciliation, saying he does not understand what really matters. During a storm at sea, Naruto rebukes Hikaru for not caring about the animals, and Hikaru helps save Chamū and Kiki, winning their friendship and Naruto's.

On arrival they find that the greedy minister Shabadaba has overthrown King Kakeru, Michiru's father. Loyal soldiers under Captain Korega help the group flee to a mountain refuge, where the dying Kakeru, turned partly to stone by the gauntlet of the hired ninja Ishidate, tells his son that wealth is not happiness and names him king. Ishidate's mercenaries poison the team, kill Korega and capture Michiru. Shabadaba reveals that he seized power to keep the kingdom's riches for himself, whereas Kakeru wanted to spend them on his people. Rallied by Naruto, the group sneaks into the palace with help from the circus, Kakashi leads a surprise attack, and Lee and Sakura defeat Ishidate's henchmen Karenbana and Kongō. Hikaru saves his father from hanging with an arrow, and, carried by father and son, Naruto finishes Ishidate and Shabadaba with a Rasengan strengthened by the island's moonlight. While Kakashi recovers, the team enjoy two weeks on the island and see Michiru and Hikaru inaugurated as king and prince, and Michiru resolves to win back Amayo.

Distributed by Toho, the film opened in Japan on 5 August 2006 and grossed about $3.2 million.

overview: Christopher Robin, the boy who had countless adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, has grown up and lost his way. Now it’s up to his spirited and loveable stuffed animals, Winnie The Pooh, Tigger, Piglet, and the rest of the gang, to rekindle their friendship and remind him of endless days of childlike wonder and make-believe, when doing nothing was the very best something.
tagline: Don't underestimate the value of doing nothing.
title: Christopher Robin
plot:
Christopher Robin is a 2018 American fantasy drama film directed by Marc Forster and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is based on the Winnie-the-Pooh stories created by A.A. Milne.

The story begins with Christopher Robin (played by Ewan McGregor), now a grown man, who has lost touch with his childhood imagination and the magical world of Winnie-the-Pooh. He is struggling to find meaning in his life as a successful businessman, but feels unfulfilled and disconnected from his past.

One day, while on vacation at the Hundred Acre Wood, Christopher Robin reunites with his old friends Pooh (voiced by Jim Cummings), Piglet (voiced by Nick Mohammed), Eeyore (voiced by Brad Garrett), Tigger (voiced by Jim Cummings), Rabbit (voiced by Peter Capaldi), Owl (voiced by Toby Jones), and Kanga (voiced by Nicole Scherzinger). The friends are delighted to see Christopher Robin again, but they also sense that he has lost his way.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Christopher Robin's adult life is marked by stress, anxiety, and a lack of creativity. He feels like he's losing himself in the process of becoming a successful businessman. Meanwhile, Pooh and the other animals are struggling to cope with the changing world around them, including the loss of their home due to urban development.

Through his interactions with his friends, Christopher Robin begins to rediscover the joys of childhood imagination and creativity. He starts to see the world through the eyes of a child again, and finds inspiration in the simple pleasures of life. The movie features stunning animation, bringing the beloved characters to life in a way that is both nostalgic and fresh.

As the story reaches its climax, Christopher Robin must confront his own fears and doubts in order to find his true purpose in life. With the help of his friends, he learns to let go of his adult responsibilities and rediscover the magic of childhood. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Christopher Robin returning home to his family, but this time with a renewed sense of wonder and imagination.

Throughout the film, there are also flashbacks that show Christopher Robin's childhood adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, which serve as a reminder of the power of imagination and friendship. The movie features a talented voice cast, including Emily Blunt as Christopher Robin's wife, Jane, and Hayley Atwell as his mother.

Overall, Christopher Robin is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the importance of childhood imagination and creativity. It's a story about finding one's true purpose in life and rediscovering the magic of childhood through the power of friendship and imagination.

overview: Cinderella, an orphaned girl with an evil stepmother, has big dreams and with the help of her Fabulous Godmother, she perseveres to make them come true.
tagline: One shoe to rule them all.
title: Cinderella
plot:
Cinderella is a 2021 jukebox musical romantic comedy film written and directed by Kay Cannon, based on Charles Perrault's fairy tale. Singer Camila Cabello makes her acting debut in the title role, alongside Nicholas Galitzine as Prince Robert, Idina Menzel as Cinderella's stepmother, Billy Porter as her fairy godparent, Minnie Driver and Pierce Brosnan. The idea of reinterpreting the story came from James Corden, who produced the film through Fulwell 73. Filming began at Pinewood Studios in February 2020 but was suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic, resuming in August 2020. It mixes pop and rock hits with several original songs.

Ella is an ambitious young woman whose dream is to open her own shop, Dresses by Ella. Prince Robert catches sight of her in passing, disguises himself as a commoner and finds her trying to sell one of her creations at the market, where after some playful banter he buys the dress for three times its price. He invites her to the royal ball, promising that she will meet guests from around the world who might buy her designs. On the night of the ball, Vivian, who has arranged for Ella to marry a vegetable merchant named Thomas, ruins her dress with ink so that only her own daughters, Malvolia and Narissa, can attend. Ella's fairy godparent, Fab G, comes to the rescue, dressing her in a gown of her own design and a pair of glass shoes and turning mice into footmen and a crate into a carriage. At the ball Ella meets Robert's sister, Princess Gwen, who is wearing the dress he bought, and a visiting queen, Tatiana, who offers to take her around the world as her personal dressmaker. When Robert proposes, Ella hesitates, fearing that marriage will mean giving up a dream that is finally within reach, while Robert, whose lifelong ambition has been to assume the throne, struggles with her answer. As midnight strikes and Ella flees, leaving a glass shoe behind, both of them must decide whether love and personal ambition can coexist.

Cinderella was released in select theaters and on Amazon Prime Video on September 3, 2021, to mixed reviews; it holds a 41% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. According to Screen Engine, it was the most-watched streaming film of its opening weekend.

overview: French drama based on the 1996 kidnapping and killing of seven monks in Algeria. A group of Trappist monks reside in the monastery of Tibhirine in Algeria, where they live in harmony with the largely muslim population. When a bloody conflict between Algeria's army and Muslim Jihadi insurgents disrupts the peace, they are forced to consider fleeing the monastery and deserting the villagers they have ministered to. In the face of deadly violence the monks wrestle with their faith and their convictions, eventually deciding to stay and help their neighbours keep the army and the insurgents at bay.
tagline: In the face of terror, their greatest weapon was faith...
title: Of Gods and Men
plot:
Of Gods and Men is a 2010 French drama film directed by Xavier Beauvois, produced by Wild Bunch and Why Not Productions.

The movie is based on the true story of a group of Trappist monks who were killed in Algeria in 1996. The main themes of the film revolve around the clash between faith and violence, as embodied by the character of Jacques Hamel, a French monk who becomes embroiled in the conflict between the Algerian government and Islamist militants.

The film explores the tension between the desire for peace and the need to protect one's community. The characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the limits of their faith in the face of violence and extremism. Through the story, the movie highlights the complexities of human nature and the difficulties of making moral choices in the midst of chaos.

The film also touches on the theme of cultural identity and the struggle for self-discovery, as embodied by the character of Jacques Hamel's friend, a young Algerian man who is torn between his loyalty to his community and his desire to connect with the outside world.

overview: Chanel, Dorinda, and Aqua, are off to India to star in a Bollywood movie. But when there they discover that they will have to compete against each other to get the role in the movie. Will the Cheetah's break up again?
tagline: What if only one star can shine?
title: The Cheetah Girls: One World
plot: Chanel, Dorinda, and Aqua are off to India to star in a Bollywood movie. But when they discover that they will have to compete against each other to get the role in the movie, will the Cheetahs break up again?

overview: Mary Lennox is born in India to wealthy British parents who never wanted her. When her parents suddenly die, she is sent back to England to live with her uncle. She meets her sickly cousin, and the two children find a wondrous secret garden lost in the grounds of Misselthwaite Manor.
title: The Secret Garden
plot:
The Secret Garden is a 2020 British fantasy drama film directed by Marc Munden and adapted by Jack Thorne from Frances Hodgson Burnett's 1911 novel, of which it is the fourth film adaptation. It stars Dixie Egerickx as Mary Lennox, with Colin Firth as Archibald Craven and Julie Walters as Mrs Medlock, and moves the story to England in 1947. STXfilms released it on premium video on demand in the United States in August 2020, and Sky released it in British cinemas and on its Sky Cinema channels on 23 October 2020.

In 1947, Mary Lennox is found alone in her home in British India, her parents having died of cholera and the girl having been forgotten in the turmoil of Partition. She is sent to live with her uncle, Archibald Craven, at Misselthwaite Manor in Yorkshire. Sullen and unkind after a childhood in which she learned to suppress her feelings, Mary is received by the strict housekeeper, Mrs Medlock, who forbids her to explore the house and confines her to her room at night, and she quickly unsettles the young maid Martha with her demands. Allowed to wander the grounds, Mary befriends a stray dog she names Jemima, and at night she follows mysterious cries through the corridors to discover her bedridden cousin Colin, who believes he has a hunched back and will never walk. After freeing Jemima from a trap, Mary follows the runaway dog, climbs a wall and tumbles into a hidden, overgrown garden, where a robin leads her to a key concealed in a statue. With Dickon, a local boy who helps nurse the injured dog, she begins to visit the garden in secret, and the two plan to bring Colin there in the hope that its magic will heal him. Meanwhile Mary finds pictures of her own mother and of Colin's late mother, Grace, and uncovers letters exchanged between the two women, whose memory still haunts the grieving Mr Craven, and the three children find in the garden a place where their own sorrows can begin to mend.

On Rotten Tomatoes, 68% of 96 reviews of the film are positive, with a consensus praising it as faithful in spirit while putting its own spin on the source material, and Metacritic gave it a score of 59 out of 100, indicating mixed or average reviews. In the United States it debuted as the top rental on Amazon Prime.

overview: 20 years since their first adventure, Lloyd and Harry go on a road trip to find Harry's newly discovered daughter, who was given up for adoption.
tagline: The average person uses 10% of their brain capacity. Imagine what he could do with 1%.
title: Dumb and Dumber To
plot:
Dumb and Dumber To is a 2014 American comedy film directed by the Farrelly brothers and starring Jim Carrey, Jeff Daniels, and Steve Carell. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1994 film Dumb and Dumber.

The story begins with Lloyd Christmas (Jim Carrey) and Harry Dunne (Jeff Daniels), two dim-witted but lovable friends who have been inseparable since childhood. After years of drifting from one get-rich-quick scheme to another, they are now in their mid-40s, still living in the same apartment in Providence, Rhode Island.

The movie starts with Lloyd and Harry receiving an invitation from Mary Swanson (Lauren Holly), a woman who was once Lloyd's love interest. She is now married to a wealthy man named Tim (Terence Stamp) and has two children. The invitation is for her 40th birthday party in Aspen, Colorado, where she plans to reunite with Lloyd.

Lloyd becomes obsessed with the idea of reuniting with Mary and sets out on a road trip from Providence to Aspen with Harry by his side. Along the way, they encounter various misadventures, including a run-in with a group of bikers, a wild goose chase through a casino, and a disastrous attempt at getting a tattoo.

As Lloyd and Harry arrive in Aspen, they discover that Mary is now married and has two children. However, Lloyd becomes convinced that she still has feelings for him and sets out to win her back. The movie follows their antics as they try to get close to Mary and her family, often with hilarious results.

Meanwhile, Tim (Terence Stamp) is revealed to be a wealthy and ruthless businessman who will stop at nothing to protect his interests. He becomes the main antagonist of the movie, and Lloyd and Harry must use all their wits (or lack thereof) to outsmart him and win Mary back.

Throughout the movie, Lloyd and Harry's friendship is put to the test as they navigate their way through various challenges. Despite their dim-wittedness, they always manage to find a way to help each other out, often in unexpected ways.

In the end, Lloyd and Harry succeed in winning over Mary and her family, but not before facing off against Tim in an epic battle of wits. The movie ends with Lloyd and Harry returning home to Providence, where they are greeted as heroes by their friends and neighbors.

Overall, Dumb and Dumber To is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that follows the misadventures of two lovable but dim-witted friends as they try to win back an old flame. The movie features plenty of slapstick humor, witty one-liners, and hilarious performances from its cast.

overview: The film takes place in Paris, where two cops are competing for the vacant seat of chief of police while in the middle of a search for a gang of violent thieves. The movie is directed by Olivier Marchal, a former police officer who spent 12 years with the French police before creating this story, which is taken in part from real facts that happened during the 1980s in France.
title: 36th Precinct
plot:
36th Precinct (French: 36 Quai des Orfèvres), also known as The 36, is a 2004 French crime film directed by Olivier Marchal, a former police officer. Named after the historic address of the Paris Judicial Police headquarters on the Île de la Cité, it stars Daniel Auteuil as Léo Vrinks and Gérard Depardieu as Denis Klein, rival police commanders competing for the post of chief of the Paris criminal police, with Roschdy Zem and Valeria Golino. It is loosely based on real 1980s events.

Vrinks, head of the BRI, and Klein, head of the BRB, both hope to succeed their chief, Robert Mancini, who is being promoted, and the job will likely go to whoever catches a violent gang of armored-car robbers. Vrinks's wife, Camille, was once Klein's lover. Vrinks is an effective detective with loyal officers and shady informants, while the heavy-drinking Klein is less capable and less scrupulous. Vrinks's methods backfire when an informant on weekend release, Hugo Silien, tricks him into driving the getaway car while he kills a gangster who once testified against him. In exchange for Vrinks's silence and alibi, Silien gives up the gang's members and hideout. During the stakeout, a drunken Klein breaks procedure and alerts the robbers; most are arrested, but Vrinks's best friend is killed in the gunfire.

Learning from a prostitute who witnessed Silien's crime that Vrinks was involved, Klein ensures that his rival is prosecuted, making Vrinks's evidence inadmissible and clearing himself of blame. When Silien later meets Camille to offer her money, Klein, tapping her phone, orders his men to force her car off the road despite the danger, and both die in the crash. Klein then fires Silien's gun into Camille's body and his own into Silien's to make it appear he acted in self-defense. Seven years later, Vrinks leaves prison and reunites with his daughter. Klein now heads the criminal police. A former colleague, Titi, is beaten into a coma by Bruno, a thug Vrinks's team once humiliated in a mock execution. Vrinks confronts Klein at a police ball and urges him to kill himself, but when Klein follows him out shouting threats, Bruno, lying in wait, shoots Klein dead, apparently having been given Klein's name by Titi. Vrinks and his daughter leave to start a new life abroad.

Marchal named the informant Silien in tribute to the character in the classic French crime film Le Doulos. The film received eight César Award nominations and was remade in South Korea in 2019 as The Beast.

overview: A young woman becomes trapped in her car after a hitchhiker causes her to have an automobile accident.
title: Curve
plot:
Curve is a 2015 American horror thriller film directed by Iain Softley from a screenplay by Kimberly Lofstrom Johnson, later rewritten by Lee Patterson. Julianne Hough stars as Mallory Rutledge, a bride-to-be trapped in her car on a deserted highway, and Teddy Sears plays Christian Laughton, the charming but predatory hitchhiker who puts her there, with Penelope Mitchell as Mallory's sister Ella and Madalyn Horcher as a girl named Katie. The film was produced by Jason Blum through Blumhouse Productions together with Ombra Films and LBI Entertainment, and Universal Pictures acquired its worldwide distribution rights.

Mallory is driving to Denver for her wedding rehearsal when she video chats with Ella, who admits she has delayed buying her plane ticket because she doubts Mallory is truly happy about the marriage; Mallory insists she is and ends the call. Soon afterwards her car breaks down in an area without phone service, and a stranger named Christian gets it running again. Feeling guilty for driving off, Mallory turns back and offers him a ride, but his behavior grows increasingly unsettling as he talks about fate having brought them together. When she orders him out, he pulls a knife and forces her to keep driving. Noticing that he is not wearing a seat belt, Mallory deliberately swerves toward a guardrail on a curve, and the car crashes violently and lands upside down. She survives with her leg pinned inside the wreck, while Christian walks away, telling her she must get herself out of this. Over the following days he returns to taunt her, eating and drinking in front of her, telling her he is holding a family hostage, and finally handing her a saw with the suggestion that she cut off her own leg if she wants to live. Weakened and desperate, Mallory resorts to eating a rat and drinking her own urine. When a rainstorm begins to flood the wrecked car and a passing police officer drives away with Christian, Mallory must find a way to free herself and stop him before he harms the captive family.

The film had its world premiere at the Film4 FrightFest on August 31, 2015, and was released through video on demand on January 19, 2016, followed by a home media release on February 2, 2016. Principal photography had begun on October 22, 2013.

overview: Hard-nosed liberal lawyer Roman J. Israel has been fighting the good fight forever while others take the credit. When his partner – the firm's frontman – has a heart attack, Israel suddenly takes on that role. He soon discovers some unsettling truths about the firm – truths that conflict with his values of helping the poor and dispossessed – and finds himself in an existential crisis that leads to extreme actions.
production_companies: Culture China - Image Nation Abu Dhabi Fund
tagline: All rise.
title: Roman J. Israel, Esq.
plot:
Roman J. Israel, Esq. is a 2017 American drama film directed by Dan Gilroy, starring Denzel Washington as the titular character.

The main themes of Roman J. Israel, Esq. include:

1. **Moral Ambiguity**: The film explores the complexities of moral decision-making in a world where right and wrong are often blurred. Roman's rigid adherence to his principles is contrasted with the more pragmatic approach of his colleague, Dr. Abraham Cole (Colin Trevorrow).
2. **Identity Crisis**: As Roman navigates the changing landscape of law firms and societal expectations, he struggles to reconcile his personal values with the demands of a rapidly evolving world.
3. **Loneliness and Isolation**: Despite being surrounded by colleagues and acquaintances, Roman feels increasingly disconnected from others, highlighting the tension between his desire for human connection and his need for solitude.
4. **The Corrupting Influence of Power**: The film critiques the ways in which power and privilege can lead individuals to compromise their values and principles, as seen in the character of Arthur Edens (Denzel Washington's alter ego).
5. **Redemption and Self-Discovery**: Through his journey, Roman comes to realize that he must adapt and evolve in order to find a new sense of purpose and belonging.

The film received critical acclaim for its thought-provoking themes, nuanced performances, and sharp commentary on the human condition.

overview: In a sleepy town, one man, a wannabe horror film director is about to have his life and the world he knows change forever. Finally, he gets the big break he has been waiting a lifetime for, but its not Hollywood knocking on his door.
tagline: Make America hungry again
title: Fat Ass Zombies
plot:
Fat Ass Zombies, also released as American Zombieland, is a 2020 American low-budget zombie comedy directed by George J. Bennett, who wrote the screenplay with Christopher De Maria and Brave Matthews. Produced by Magicbullet Media and Summertown Productions, it stars Dave Mussen as Sam Pentergrass, Johnny Dowers as Popper, Samantha Walker as Pam, Brave Matthews as Pistol, Kristen Renton as Tiffany Taylor, Sondra Currie, Bryan Handy and Robert Johnson. It runs 88 minutes and was promoted with the tagline "Make America hungry again."

In the sleepy town of Corsicana, Texas, Sam is a clueless wannabe horror director whose previous efforts include titles such as Zombie Abortion Apocalypse. The townspeople throw a party in anticipation of his big break, the expected acceptance of his latest film, Deadbeat Zombie Dad, into a film festival. Sam cannot bring himself to tell them that the festival has rejected it with a brutally insulting letter, and he becomes the joke of the town. The party, however, is soon interrupted when most of the citizens turn into zombies after eating "Freedom Cakes," and the town is overrun by the undead. Seeing that this is not Hollywood knocking on his door but an opportunity of another kind, Sam gathers his buddies and assorted locals, grabs a camera and sets out to make the most realistic found-footage horror film ever produced, a zombie apocalypse movie that he intends to call Fat Ass Zombies. The film leans heavily on gross-out and raunchy humour, and its ending turns into a fantasy of success in which Sam's film wins acclaim and Hollywood stardom.

The film was released on DVD in the United States by Mill Creek Entertainment under the title American Zombieland, a play on the horror comedy Zombieland. B.J. Burgess of Ramblings of a Coffee-Addicted Writer found it not nearly as stupid as it should have been, describing a raunchy B-comedy with decent direction and production values for its shoestring budget, passable to laughable acting, a few laugh-out-loud moments and little character development, and warning that it takes nearly thirty minutes for any zombies to appear and that the gore is mostly tame. Moria was far harsher, giving it one star and calling it painfully bad on all accounts, criticizing its self-consciously bad-taste humour and noting that, despite the title, most of the zombies are of regular size; the site listed it among its worst films of 2020.

overview: It's Senior year at East Great Falls. Annie, Kayla, Michelle, and Stephanie decide to harness their girl power and band together to get what they want their last year of high school.
title: American Pie Presents: Girls' Rules
plot:
American Pie Presents: Girls' Rules is a 2020 American sex comedy film directed by Mike Elliott. The ninth installment overall in the American Pie franchise and the fifth in its American Pie Presents spin-off series, it is a standalone sequel centered on Stephanie, a relative of Steve Stifler, played by Lizze Broadway, and her friends. The cast also includes Madison Pettis, Piper Curda, Natasha Behnam and Darren Barnet. It is the first film in the franchise without Eugene Levy and the first to contain no nudity. The project grew out of a script for a male-centered film called American Pie Presents: East Great Falls, which writer David H. Steinberg had been hired to write in 2010; in 2017 Universal brought in new writers who flipped the genders of all the characters.

At the start of their senior year, four friends, Annie, Kayla, Michelle and Stephanie, make a pact to help one another get what they want before graduation. Annie hopes to lose her virginity to her college boyfriend, Jason; Stephanie, a confident lacrosse player, is blackmailing the school's lecherous principal into retiring; Kayla is obsessed with the idea that her boyfriend Tim is cheating on her; and Michelle prides herself on her expertise in sex toys. Their plans are thrown into disarray by the arrival of Grant, a handsome new student whose mother Ellen moves in next door to Annie and her single father. Michelle and Stephanie both set out to win Grant's affection, with Stephanie paying her estranged old friend Emmett to help, while Grant offers to help Kayla make Tim jealous after their breakup and studies with Annie in the library, where the two slowly fall for each other. When the girls discover at a party that they all have feelings for the same boy, the pact begins to strain, though new romances emerge, including Stephanie's with Emmett and Michelle's with the nerdy assistant Oliver, who shares her admiration for John F. Kennedy. After Annie catches Jason cheating, she realizes her heart lies with Grant, only for a misunderstanding about the pact to threaten everything ahead of the pajama prom.

Released on demand and on DVD by Universal Pictures on October 6, 2020, followed by a Blu-ray release in September 2021, the film received generally negative reviews and holds a 33% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on nine critics.

overview: Fed up with the cruelty and stupidity of American culture, an unlikely duo goes on a killing spree, killing reality TV stars, bigots and others they find repugnant.
tagline: Taking out the trash, one jerk at a time.
title: God Bless America
plot:
God Bless America is a 2011 American black comedy film written and directed by Bobcat Goldthwait. Blending political satire with dark humor, it stars Joel Murray as Frank Murdoch, a middle-aged man, and Tara Lynne Barr as Roxy, a teenage girl, who embark on a killing spree after bonding over their shared disgust with what American culture has become in the years after 9/11. The cast also includes Alexie Gilmore, Mackenzie Brooke Smith and Travis Wester.

Frank is an insurance salesman who is sickened by the cruelty and vapidity he sees in television, talk radio and the internet. Divorced, he is kept awake by his neighbors' screaming baby, while his spoiled young daughter Ava lives with his ex-wife. In a single stretch he is fired from his job and told by an indifferent doctor that he has a terminal brain tumor. Watching television that night, he sees a talent show mocking a disabled contestant named Steven Clark and then a reality program about Chloe, a monstrously spoiled teenager. On the verge of suicide, Frank instead steals his neighbor's car, drives to Chloe's school and shoots her. Her classmate Roxanne "Roxy" Harmon witnesses the killing, applauds it and follows Frank to his motel, where she talks him out of killing himself. Insisting that only genuinely awful people should die, the pair go on to murder Chloe's parents and then roam the country targeting rude moviegoers, a man who double-parks, extremist protesters and a right-wing political commentator, while Roxy dreams of escaping with Frank to France. Frank's world shifts when his doctor calls to say the tumor diagnosis was a mix-up with another patient, and again when he learns that Roxy has lied about her troubled home life; her parents are in fact respectable and worried about her. After the two part ways, Frank arms himself with an assault rifle and storms the studio of the talent show, where he takes the audience hostage and delivers a speech about the state of American society as police surround the building.

God Bless America premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 9, 2011, and also screened at South by Southwest, before a video-on-demand release in April 2012 and a theatrical release in May. It holds a 65% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it uneven and somewhat thin but with ideas of primal appeal, and a Metacritic score of 56.

overview: Mike Sullivan works as a hit man for crime boss John Rooney. Sullivan views Rooney as a father figure, however after his son is witness to a killing, Mike Sullivan finds himself on the run in attempt to save the life of his son and at the same time looking for revenge on those who wronged him.
tagline: Pray for Michael Sullivan.
title: Road to Perdition
plot:
"Road to Perdition" is a 2002 American crime drama film directed by Sam Mendes, produced by DreamWorks Pictures, and written by David Self.

The main themes of "Road to Perdition" include:

1. **Family and Loyalty**: The film explores the complex relationships within the Murphy family, particularly between Michael (Tyler Hoechlin) and his father, John (Tom Hanks). As Michael navigates the treacherous world of organized crime, he must confront the harsh realities of loyalty, duty, and sacrifice.
2. **Redemption and Guilt**: The story delves into the themes of guilt, redemption, and personal responsibility. John Murphy's past mistakes come back to haunt him, forcing him to make amends with his son and find a way to redeem himself.
3. **Mortality and Loss**: The film grapples with the inevitability of death and loss, as embodied by the character of Big Jim Caffrey (Paul Newman). His demise serves as a catalyst for Michael's journey, highlighting the fragility of life and the importance of cherishing time with loved ones.
4. **Coming of Age**: Through Michael's experiences, the film explores themes of adolescence, self-discovery, and growing up. As he navigates the dark world of organized crime, Michael must confront his own vulnerabilities and learn to rely on himself.

The movie's narrative is marked by a series of tragic events, including the brutal murder of Michael's family members, which sets him on a path of revenge against those responsible. Along the way, he forms an unlikely alliance with Big Jim Caffrey, who becomes a mentor and guide in his quest for justice.

Ultimately, "Road to Perdition" is a powerful exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of family, loyalty, guilt, and redemption. The film's themes are both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving audiences with a lasting impression long after the credits roll.

overview: In 1930s France, two sisters who are thought to be able to communicate with ghosts meet a visionary producer while performing in Paris.
tagline: You never know what's about to change...
title: Planetarium
plot:
Planetarium is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the search for meaning in life.

At its core, the movie delves into the theme of female empowerment and the struggle for independence. The protagonist, Sophie, played by Golshifteh Farahani, is a young Iranian woman who defies societal expectations to pursue her dreams and forge her own path. Her journey is marked by a series of encounters with men who embody different aspects of patriarchal oppression, forcing her to confront the constraints placed upon her.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and belonging. Sophie's experiences as an Iranian woman in Europe serve as a metaphor for the complexities of cultural heritage and the search for one's place in the world. Her relationships with others are shaped by her own sense of self, which is constantly evolving as she navigates different social contexts.

Furthermore, Planetarium explores the tension between individual desire and societal responsibility. Sophie's choices are often driven by a desire to break free from the constraints of her past, but she must also confront the consequences of her actions on those around her. This internal conflict serves as a powerful reminder of the complexities of human relationships and the need for empathy and understanding.

Ultimately, Planetarium is a movie about finding one's own voice and forging a path that is true to oneself, even in the face of adversity. The film's themes are both deeply personal and universally relatable, making it a powerful and thought-provoking watch.

overview: Heidi, who initially left her small town of Pleasant Valley with the dream of one day becoming a successful painter, has put her own art on hold to excel as an art gallery curator. Now, a week before the gallery’s big Christmas party, she must return home to watch her niece and nephew. She comes face to face with her high school love, Chris, now a teacher, and offers to help him find a new last-minute location for the Christmas dance.
title: Christmas Wonderland
plot:
Christmas Wonderland is a heartwarming holiday romance film that explores the transformative power of love and second chances. The story revolves around Holly, a successful businesswoman who has lost touch with her Christmas spirit, and Nick, a widowed father who is struggling to balance his work and family life.

As Holly and Nick's paths cross, they embark on a journey of self-discovery and healing, learning to let go of their past heartaches and rediscover the magic of Christmas. Through their blossoming romance, the film highlights the importance of human connection, forgiveness, and the redemptive power of love.

The movie also touches on themes of grief, loss, and the challenges of single parenthood, showcasing Nick's unwavering dedication to his daughter and his own journey towards healing and finding happiness again. As Holly and Nick navigate their feelings for each other, they must confront their own emotional baggage and learn to trust themselves and others.

Ultimately, Christmas Wonderland is a feel-good film that celebrates the joy, hope, and renewal of the holiday season, reminding viewers that it's never too late to rediscover the magic of love and Christmas.

overview: A young and unskilled fairy godmother that ventures out on her own to prove her worth by tracking down a young girl whose request for help was ignored. What she discovers is that the girl has now become a grown woman in need of something very different than a "prince charming."
tagline: Be careful who you wish for.
title: Godmothered
plot:
Godmothered is a 2020 American fantasy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a young witch named Meredith, played by Jillian Bell, who is struggling to find her place in the world.

The story begins with Meredith, a talented but awkward young witch, who has been searching for her godmother for years. According to tradition, every young witch needs a godmother to guide and mentor them on their magical journey. However, Meredith's search has been unsuccessful, and she is starting to lose hope.

One day, while out on a job as a maid, Meredith meets a kind-hearted but slightly eccentric woman named Godmother Agnes, played by Isla Fisher. Agnes is a retired witch who has lost her own goddaughter and is now searching for a new one to take her place. Despite their initial differences, the two women form an unlikely bond, and Agnes agrees to become Meredith's godmother.

As Meredith begins to learn from Agnes, she discovers that being a witch is not just about casting spells and wearing fancy hats, but also about understanding the importance of family, friendship, and community. Through her adventures with Agnes, Meredith learns valuable lessons about embracing her uniqueness and finding her own path in life.

However, their relationship is put to the test when a rival godmother, Godmother Barbara, played by Rachel Bloom, appears on the scene. Barbara is a ruthless and cunning witch who will stop at nothing to become the most powerful godmother in the land. She sees Agnes as a threat to her own power and sets out to sabotage their relationship.

As Meredith and Agnes work together to thwart Barbara's plans, they discover that being a good godmother is not just about magic and spells, but also about love, kindness, and selflessness. In the end, Meredith learns that she has found not only a godmother but also a true friend in Agnes, and that their bond will last a lifetime.

The movie ends with Meredith and Agnes standing together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way. Meredith has finally found her place in the world, and Agnes has found a new purpose in life. The film is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of what it means to be a good friend, family member, and godmother.

Overall, Godmothered is a delightful and entertaining movie that celebrates the power of female friendship and the importance of embracing one's uniqueness. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and magical storyline, this film is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

overview: Homer is an orphan who was never adopted, becoming the favorite of orphanage director Dr. Larch. Dr. Larch imparts his full medical knowledge on Homer, who becomes a skilled, albeit unlicensed, physician. But Homer yearns for a self-chosen life outside the orphanage. What will Homer learn about life and love in the cider house? What of the destiny that Dr. Larch has planned for him?
tagline: A story about how far we must travel to find the place where we belong.
title: The Cider House Rules
plot:
The Cider House Rules is a 1999 American drama film directed by Lasse Hallström, based on the 1991 novel of the same name by John Irving. The movie stars Tobey Maguire, Charlize Theron, and Michael Caine.

The main themes of The Cider House Rules can be summarized as follows:

1. **Coming of Age**: The film explores the journey of Homer Wells (Tobey Maguire), a young orphan who grows up in an orphanage run by Dr. William Novich (Michael Caine). As Homer navigates his way through adolescence, he grapples with complex moral and philosophical questions that shape his understanding of himself and the world around him.
2. **Morality and Ethics**: The movie delves into the gray areas between right and wrong, as Homer is forced to confront the harsh realities of life in a rural community. He must navigate the complexities of human relationships, medical ethics, and personal responsibility, all while struggling with his own sense of morality.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: Throughout the film, Homer searches for a sense of belonging and identity, which is often elusive due to his unconventional upbringing. His experiences in the orphanage and later as an apprentice to Dr. Novich challenge his perceptions of himself and his place in the world.
4. **Love and Human Connection**: The Cider House Rules explores the power of human relationships and love in shaping our lives. Homer's connections with various characters, including Abby (Charlize Theron) and Hannah (Sacramento), demonstrate the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding in building meaningful relationships.
5. **Social Commentary**: The film offers commentary on social issues such as abortion, euthanasia, and the treatment of orphans. Dr. Novich's character, in particular, serves as a foil to the societal norms of his time, highlighting the complexities and nuances of medical ethics.

The Cider House Rules is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and moral dilemmas through Homer's journey. The movie features outstanding performances from its cast, including Tobey Maguire, Charlize Theron, and Michael Caine.

overview: When Queen Elizabeth's reign is threatened by ruthless familial betrayal and Spain's invading army, she and her shrewd adviser must act to safeguard the lives of her people.
tagline: Woman. Warrior. Queen.
title: Elizabeth: The Golden Age
plot:
Elizabeth: The Golden Age is a historical drama film directed by Shekhar Kapur, released in 2007 by Columbia Pictures and Universal Pictures.

The main themes of Elizabeth: The Golden Age revolve around power, politics, identity, and the complexities of female leadership. Here's a breakdown of the plot development and ending:

Beginning:
The film begins with Queen Elizabeth I (played by Cate Blanchett) facing challenges from her advisors, particularly Sir Francis Walsingham (played by Clive Owen), who is trying to manipulate her for his own gain. The story also explores Elizabeth's relationships with her sister Mary (played by Abbie Cornish) and her cousin Lady Jane Grey (played by Saoirse Ronan).

Plot Development:
As the film progresses, Elizabeth must navigate the treacherous waters of European politics, including the threat posed by Spanish Armada leader Don Carlos (played by Jordi Mollà). She also faces opposition from her own advisors, who are divided on how to deal with Spain. Meanwhile, Elizabeth's personal life is marked by romance and heartbreak, particularly with Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex (played by Geoffrey Rush).

Ending:
The film culminates in the defeat of the Spanish Armada and Elizabeth's emergence as a strong and confident leader. The ending also marks a turning point in Elizabeth's personal life, as she must confront her feelings for Essex and make difficult choices about her future.

Main Themes:

1. Power: The film explores the complexities of power and how it can be both empowering and suffocating.
2. Politics: The story delves into the intricate world of European politics, highlighting the machinations of advisors and the challenges faced by a female leader.
3. Identity: Elizabeth's journey is also one of self-discovery, as she navigates her relationships with others and grapples with her own identity.
4. Female Leadership: The film celebrates Elizabeth's strength and resilience as a leader, while also acknowledging the challenges she faces as a woman in a male-dominated world.

Overall, Elizabeth: The Golden Age is a rich and complex film that explores themes of power, politics, identity, and female leadership, set against the backdrop of one of history's most fascinating monarchs.

overview: After her lousy stepfather steals her savings to buy a vicious tiger, Kelly loses all hope of going to college. But Kelly's situation worsens when a hurricane leaves her and her autistic brother boarded up in their house with the man-eating beast. This edge-of-your-seat thriller follows the gutsy heroine and her younger sibling as they struggle to outwit the ravenous predator and find a way to survive.
tagline: His Feeding. Your Frenzy.
title: Burning Bright
plot:
Burning Bright is an American horror thriller of 2010 directed by Carlos Brooks. Briana Evigan stars as Kelly Taylor, a young woman trapped with her autistic younger brother Tom, played by Charlie Tahan, and a starving tiger inside their boarded-up house during a hurricane, with Garret Dillahunt as their stepfather John Gaveneau, Mary Rachel Dudley as their mother Catherine and Meat Loaf in an uncredited role.

Planning to open a safari attraction, John buys a Bengal tiger named Lucifer from a travelling circus. When Kelly tries to place Tom in a care facility before she leaves for college, her payment bounces, and she learns that John has spent the money, which their late mother intended for Tom's care, on the tiger. John refuses to give it back, arguing that there was no will, and has the house boarded up against an approaching hurricane. Kelly is warned that she will lose her scholarship if she defers college yet again. That night someone frees Lucifer inside the house and nails the front door shut.

In the morning Kelly finds a note saying John has gone to the store, spots the tiger prowling the foyer and discovers that Tom is missing from his bed. With the house sealed and emergency lines jammed by the storm, she escapes the tiger by climbing a laundry chute, finds Tom and struggles to keep him safe through his sensory meltdowns. They hide under a bed doused in perfume, in a cupboard from which Kelly smashes an escape route through the wall, and Lucifer wounds her leg. In John's study she discovers life insurance policies on both siblings and a gun, but the first chamber is empty. Kelly breaks out through a window and reaches her car, then returns for Tom, promising never to leave him. Fending Lucifer off with a makeshift torch, she hides Tom in an empty chest freezer and lulls him to sleep. At dawn John returns to unseal the door, and Kelly realises he trapped them; he confesses that he murdered their mother when she planned to leave him. Lucifer then mauls him to death, and Kelly and Tom slip out into the storm-wrecked landscape, hand in hand.

Shot in Florida from July 2008, the film was released straight to DVD by Lionsgate on 17 August 2010. Retrospective reviews were warmer: Bloody Disgusting praised its solid direction and performances, and CHUD called it entertaining and at times surprisingly good.

overview: An ex-cop and his family are the target of an evil force that is using mirrors as a gateway into their home.
tagline: There is evil...On the other side.
title: Mirrors
plot:
Mirrors is a 2008 supernatural horror film directed by David Twohy and produced by Regency Enterprises.

The movie follows Nick Morton (played by Chris Hemsworth), an American soldier who, along with his team, discovers a mysterious ancient artifact in Iraq. Unbeknownst to them, the artifact is actually a magical mirror that has been used for centuries to trap evil spirits from other dimensions.

As soon as Nick touches the mirror, he is transported to a mystical realm where he encounters a seductive and alluring woman named Bo (played by Rachel Nichols). However, it becomes clear that Bo is not what she seems, and she is actually a malevolent spirit who has been trapped in the mirror for centuries.

Throughout the film, Nick must navigate this supernatural world and confront his own dark past in order to survive. Along the way, he discovers that the mirror is a portal to other dimensions, and that it is being used by an ancient cult to summon evil spirits.

The main themes of Mirrors include:

* The power of temptation: Bo's seductive nature serves as a catalyst for Nick's downfall, highlighting the dangers of giving in to one's desires.
* The danger of playing with forces beyond human control: The mirror's supernatural powers serve as a metaphor for the unpredictable consequences of meddling with forces we don't fully understand.
* Redemption and personal growth: Through his experiences, Nick is forced to confront his own dark past and make amends, ultimately emerging stronger and wiser.

Overall, Mirrors is a thrilling supernatural horror film that explores themes of temptation, control, and redemption.

original_title: 名探偵コナン 緋色の弾丸
overview: At the opening ceremony of the WSG (World Sports Games) Tokyo Games, a sports festival held once every four years, it is announced that the world's first vacuum superconducting maglev with a maximum speed of 1,000 kilometers per hour will open. While attracting attention from around the world, top executives of large companies are kidnapped from the party venue where WSG tournament sponsors gather. Conan moves toward a solution and eventually finds a connection with the WSG abduction case that occurred 15 years ago in Boston, USA.
title: Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet
plot:
Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet is a 2021 Japanese mystery film directed by Kiyosumi Kojima and produced by Toho. 

The movie revolves around the story of a mysterious woman named Eri Kisaragi, who possesses supernatural abilities that allow her to see into the future. She becomes entangled in a complex web of events involving a series of murders and conspiracies.

At its core, Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet explores themes of identity, trauma, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Eri's character, in particular, is a fascinating study of how past traumas can shape one's perception of themselves and the world around them.

Throughout the film, the main characters grapple with their own dark pasts and the consequences of their actions, leading to a thrilling cat-and-mouse game that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. The movie also touches on the theme of obsession, as Eri becomes increasingly fixated on uncovering the truth behind a series of murders.

The film's use of mystery and suspense creates an atmosphere of tension and unease, mirroring the characters' inner turmoil and emotional struggles. Ultimately, Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet is a gripping whodunit that keeps viewers guessing until the very end, while also exploring deeper themes about identity, trauma, and the human condition.

The movie's portrayal of Eri's character, in particular, raises questions about the nature of reality and how our perceptions can be influenced by our experiences. Her abilities serve as a metaphor for the ways in which our past traumas can shape us, making it difficult to distinguish between what is real and what is imagined.

Overall, Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet is a thought-provoking mystery that delves into complex themes of identity, trauma, and reality, keeping viewers engaged until the very end.

overview: A bohemian artist travels from London to Italy with his estranged son to sell the house they inherited from his late wife.
title: Made in Italy
plot:
Made in Italy is a 2020 comedy-drama film written and directed by James D'Arcy in his feature directorial debut. It stars Liam Neeson as Robert Foster, a once-famous artist, and Neeson's son Micheál Richardson as Robert's estranged son, Jack, who travel together to restore a dilapidated Tuscan villa years after the death of Jack's mother, with Valeria Bilello as Natalia and Lindsay Duncan as the estate agent Kate.

Jack, a gallery manager, is reeling because his wife, Ruth, wants a divorce and her family plans to sell the gallery he has run for years. Hoping to buy it, he decides to sell the Italian house he co-owns with Robert, which had belonged to his mother, an Italian woman killed in a car crash years earlier. In Italy they find the house derelict. Kate advises that some work would raise its value, and although Jack is ready to sell it as it is, Robert, overwhelmed by memories of his wife, decides to help renovate. They befriend locals, including Natalia, a divorced restaurant owner who shares custody of her young daughter. As Natalia and her daughter help paint, Robert explains that after his wife's death he sent Jack to boarding school to shield him from reminders of her, and that he has neither painted nor driven since.

Jack and Natalia grow close, and he confides how Ruth has taken everything from him and how Robert never supported his career. Finding Robert's workspace full of paintings of his mother and of himself as a child, Jack confronts his father for shutting him out and begins wrecking it until Robert holds him. They finally share memories of her, and Robert tearfully blames himself for her death, as he was too absorbed in painting on the day of the accident. When a couple who want to buy the house treat it with contempt, Robert refuses to sell, and Jack returns angrily to England. Robert follows, having sold his London home to buy Jack's share of the villa so that Jack can buy the gallery, and plans to host painting holidays in Italy. When Ruth refuses to sell after all, Jack hands her the signed divorce papers and returns to Italy, telling his father that he only ever wanted him. He reconciles with Natalia, and the film ends with father and son painting a wall together.

IFC Films acquired U.S. rights and released the film in theaters and on video on demand on 7 August 2020. Reviews were mixed, with 44% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44; critics praised the performances and setting but found the story slight.

overview: When his dysfunctional family clashes over the holidays, young Max is disillusioned and turns his back on Christmas.  Little does he know, this lack of festive spirit has unleashed the wrath of Krampus: a demonic force of ancient evil intent on punishing non-believers.
tagline: You don't want to be on his list.
title: Krampus
plot:
Krampus is a 2015 American Christmas horror-comedy film directed by Michael Dougherty and written by Dougherty and Todd Farmer. The movie stars Adam Scott, Toni Collette, David Koechner, and Krista Stadler.

The story begins with a family, the Smiths, who are struggling to cope with the recent death of their son, Max, in a car accident. The family is still grieving, and tensions are running high between the parents, Howard (Scott) and Mary (Collette), as well as their daughter, Blair (Stadler). To make matters worse, they receive an eviction notice from their landlord, which forces them to spend Christmas with their eccentric and reclusive aunt, Eliza (Stadler).

As Christmas Eve approaches, the family is visited by a mysterious figure in a red suit, who claims to be Krampus, the half-goat, half-demon creature from Alpine folklore. According to legend, Krampus punishes naughty children during the holiday season, while his companion, Saint Nicholas, rewards the well-behaved ones.

As the night progresses, strange and terrifying events begin to occur around the Smiths' house. Blair starts acting out in increasingly disturbing ways, and her parents are forced to confront their own dark past and the true nature of Krampus. Meanwhile, a series of gruesome and supernatural events unfold, including the appearance of a demonic creature that seems to be connected to Krampus.

As the night wears on, the family is forced to face the consequences of their own actions and the true meaning of Christmas. In the end, they must make a choice between embracing the darkness and chaos brought by Krampus or finding redemption and forgiveness through love and sacrifice.

Throughout the movie, Dougherty expertly weaves together elements of horror, comedy, and family drama, creating a unique and unsettling viewing experience. The film's use of atmospheric tension, clever plot twists, and memorable performances make it a standout in the holiday horror genre.

Overall, Krampus is a dark and twisted take on traditional Christmas folklore, offering a fresh and frightening perspective on the holiday season. With its blend of humor, horror, and heart, this movie is sure to leave audiences feeling uneasy and entertained until the very end.

overview: A group of friends reunite ten years after their high-school graduation.
tagline: Who Got Fat? Who Didn't Change? Who Got Rich? Who Got Hot?
title: 10 Years
plot:
10 Years is a 2011 American independent romantic comedy film written and directed by Jamie Linden in his directorial debut. Set over a single night at a ten-year high school reunion, it features an ensemble cast including Channing Tatum, Jenna Dewan, Justin Long, Kate Mara, Rosario Dawson, Oscar Isaac, Chris Pratt, Aubrey Plaza and Anthony Mackie.

On the day of the reunion, Jake and his girlfriend, Jess, arrive at the home of his old friends Cully and Sam, now married. Others gather, including best friends Marty and AJ, the famous musician Reeves, and the adventurous Scott with his wife, Suki, and at the reunion they meet up with Garrity, his wife, Olivia, and his best friend, Andre. Elise, a reclusive classmate, arrives alone and is ignored by the organizer, former prom queen Anna. Jake shows his friends an engagement ring he has long meant to give Jess, but he is thrown when he meets his high school sweetheart, Mary, and her husband, Paul. Reeves reminisces with Elise after spotting an old photo of her in bright yellow shoes. Cully drunkenly attempts to apologize to classmates he bullied, and Marty and AJ compete for Anna. Jake and Mary recall the prom they never attended because her father had a heart attack that night.

The group moves on to a karaoke bar. Noticing Jake's behavior around Mary, Jess returns to the hotel, as does Paul.
