Pressured by his friends, Reeves sings his hit song "Never Had", and the line about yellow shoes tells Elise that it is about her; they kiss and spend the night together. Catching Marty and AJ toilet-papering her house, Anna reveals that she is an unhappy single mother of two, and the men admit their own failures: Marty is broke and AJ is divorcing. Cully's drunkenness upsets Sam, and Scott announces that he and Suki are returning to Japan. Mary asks Jake for the dance they missed at prom, giving them closure; she reveals that she is pregnant, and both agree they are happy with their lives. Back at the hotel, Jess tells Jake she left so that he could make his peace with Mary, and as they join their friends at a diner, Jake retrieves the ring from his car.

Shot around Albuquerque, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2011 but received only a limited theatrical release on September 14, 2012, grossing under $1 million. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 60% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67; critics called it sweet and well cast but predictable.

overview: Longtime friends Ronny and Nick are partners in an auto-design firm. They are hard at work on a presentation for a dream project that would really launch their company. Then Ronny spots Nick's wife out with another man, and in the process of investigating the possible affair, he learns that Nick has a few secrets of his own. As the presentation nears, Ronny agonizes over what might happen if the truth gets out.
tagline: Two best friends. Nothing could come between them... or could it?
title: The Dilemma
plot:
The Dilemma is a 2011 American comedy film directed by Ken Kwapis and written by Jerry Seinfeld, Mark Roberts, and Judd Apatow. The movie stars Vince Vaughn, Kevin James, Jennifer Aniston, Jason Bateman, and Kathryn Hahn.

The main themes of The Dilemma revolve around friendship, loyalty, and the complexities of male relationships. The story centers around Ronny (Kevin James), a man who is struggling to come to terms with his wife's infidelity. His best friend, Nick (Jason Bateman), tries to help him navigate this difficult situation.

Throughout the movie, the characters grapple with issues of masculinity, friendship, and the challenges of modern relationships. The film also explores themes of loyalty, as Ronny and Nick are forced to confront their own feelings and loyalties in order to support each other through a series of misadventures.

One of the central plot points revolves around the "dilemma" itself - a product that is designed to make women more attracted to men. The main character, Ronny's friend Dave (Jason Bateman), becomes obsessed with this product and its potential to solve his marital problems. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is ever as simple or straightforward as it seems.

Ultimately, the movie suggests that true friendship and loyalty are more important than any product or solution can provide. The film's ending is a heartwarming exploration of male friendships and the power of relationships to overcome even the most difficult challenges.

Overall, The Dilemma is a comedy that uses humor to explore deeper themes about human relationships and the complexities of modern life.

overview: A look at the life of French designer Yves Saint Laurent from the beginning of his career in 1958 when he met his lover and business partner, Pierre Berge.
tagline: Fashions fade. Style is forever.
title: Yves Saint Laurent
plot:
Yves Saint Laurent is a 2014 biographical drama film that explores the life of French fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent and his relationship with his partner, Pierre Berge. The movie delves into the complexities of their partnership, which was marked by both deep love and intense rivalry.

At its core, the film grapples with the theme of identity, particularly in the context of Saint Laurent's own identity as a designer and an individual. His struggles to reconcile his artistic vision with the commercial demands of the fashion industry serve as a backdrop for exploring the tensions between creativity and conformity.

The movie also touches on the theme of love and loss, as Saint Laurent navigates the challenges of maintaining his relationship with Berge while dealing with the pressures of fame and the onset of AIDS. The film's portrayal of their relationship is nuanced and multifaceted, capturing the intensity and passion that defined their partnership.

Furthermore, Yves Saint Laurent examines the theme of legacy and the weight of expectation that comes with being a cultural icon. As Saint Laurent struggles to come to terms with his own mortality, he must also confront the expectations placed upon him by those around him, including his fans, his colleagues, and even himself.

Ultimately, the film presents a complex and multifaceted portrait of Yves Saint Laurent, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. Through its exploration of identity, love, loss, legacy, and creativity, Yves Saint Laurent offers a powerful and thought-provoking meditation on the human experience.

overview: Luke Skywalker leads a mission to rescue his friend Han Solo from the clutches of Jabba the Hutt, while the Emperor seeks to destroy the Rebellion once and for all with a second dreaded Death Star.
tagline: The Empire Falls...
title: Return of the Jedi
plot:
Return of the Jedi is a 1983 space opera film directed by Richard Marquand and written by Lawrence Kasdan, George Lucas, and Leigh Brackett. The film is the final installment in the original Star Wars trilogy.

The story takes place three years after the events of The Empire Strikes Back (1980). The Rebel Alliance, led by Princess Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher), has established a new base on the forest moon of Endor. Meanwhile, the Galactic Empire, under the command of Emperor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid) and Darth Vader (David Prowse, voiced by James Earl Jones), is determined to crush the Rebel Alliance once and for all.

The film begins with Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), a young Jedi Knight, who has become increasingly disillusioned with his mentor, Yoda (Frank Oz). Luke's father, Anakin Skywalker/Darth Vader, appears in a vision, revealing that he was seduced by the dark side of the Force and became Darth Vader. This revelation sets Luke on a path to confront his father and ultimately redeem him.

The Rebel Alliance launches a massive attack on the new Death Star, while Luke, Han Solo (Harrison Ford), Chewbacca (Peter Mayhew), C-3PO (Anthony Daniels), and R2-D2 embark on a mission to disable the shield generator on Endor. Along the way, they encounter Boba Fett (Jeremy Bulloch) and his bounty hunter ship.

As the battle rages on, Luke confronts Darth Vader, who reveals that he has been trying to turn Luke to the dark side. However, Luke resists, and Vader ultimately redeems himself by throwing Emperor Palpatine down a reactor shaft, sacrificing himself in the process.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Rebel Alliance and the Empire on Endor. The Ewoks, small, bear-like creatures native to the forest moon, join forces with the Rebels, using their primitive technology to disable the Imperial shield generator. Meanwhile, Luke confronts Vader, who reveals that he has been searching for a way to save his son.

In a final confrontation, Luke and Vader engage in a lightsaber duel. Just as it seems that Vader is about to kill Luke, the Emperor intervenes, attempting to turn Luke to the dark side. However, Luke resists, and with the help of his friends, he ultimately defeats the Emperor and Vader.

The film concludes with a celebration on Endor, as the Rebel Alliance declares victory over the Empire. Luke, now a confident Jedi Knight, reflects on his journey, realizing that his father's redemption was not just about saving him but also about finding peace within himself.

Return of the Jedi received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release but has since become a beloved classic in the Star Wars franchise. The film's themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the power of friendship have made it a timeless tale that continues to captivate audiences around the world.

overview: For their first day on the job as the new protectors of Metro City, Megamind and Minion are selling off the gadgets from their evil lair. But when one seemingly harmless "button" unleashes the gigantic robot MEGA-MEGAmind, the duo will have to resort to their old tricks to restore order.
tagline: His Brain Is Off The Chain
title: Megamind: The Button of Doom
plot:
Megamind: The Button of Doom is a 2011 computer-animated superhero comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation.

The movie follows the story of Megamind, a supervillain who was created by a scientist named Dr. Minion to destroy Metro City. However, things don't go as planned, and Megamind ends up saving the city instead of destroying it. Feeling unappreciated and unwanted, Megamind decides to create a new villain, Tighten, to take his place.

The main themes of Megamind: The Button of Doom include:

1. **Identity**: Megamind struggles with his identity as a supervillain and an outcast. He wants to be appreciated and loved, but feels like he's stuck in a never-ending cycle of villainy.
2. **Friendship**: Despite being enemies, Megamind and Metro Man (the city's superhero) develop a strong bond, which helps Megamind understand the value of friendship and human connection.
3. **Self-discovery**: Throughout the movie, Megamind learns to let go of his ego and find a new purpose in life. He realizes that being a hero isn't just about saving the world, but also about making a positive impact on people's lives.
4. **The power of love**: The movie highlights the importance of love and acceptance in relationships. Megamind's desire for love and connection drives his actions, and ultimately leads him to find happiness and fulfillment.

Overall, Megamind: The Button of Doom is a heartwarming story about self-discovery, friendship, and the power of love.

overview: Palermo, Sicily, 1980. Mafia member Tommaso Buscetta decides to move to Brazil with his family fleeing the constant war between the different clans of the criminal organization. But when, after living several misfortunes, he is forced to return to Italy, he makes a bold decision that will change his life and the destiny of Cosa Nostra forever.
tagline: The true story about the man who brought down the Mafia
title: The Traitor
plot:
The Traitor (Italian: Il traditore) is a 2019 biographical crime drama co-written and directed by Marco Bellocchio. It tells the story of Tommaso Buscetta, the Sicilian Mafia boss who became the first major pentito, or state witness, against Cosa Nostra. Pierfrancesco Favino stars as Buscetta, with Maria Fernanda Cândido as his wife Cristina, Fabrizio Ferracane as Pippo Calò, Fausto Russo Alesi as judge Giovanni Falcone, Luigi Lo Cascio as Totuccio Contorno and Nicola Calì as Totò Riina.

In the 1980s, at the height of Mafia power, the Palermo families and the rising Corleonesi faction led by Riina keep up a show of friendship while competing for control of the drug trade. Buscetta, known as the "boss of two worlds", senses that war is coming and moves to Brazil, where he lives under the name Roberto Felici. As he predicted, a bloody feud breaks out after he leaves, and among its victims are two of his sons and his brother. Arrested and tortured by Brazilian police and facing likely death on extradition, Buscetta is offered a way out by Falcone: cooperation in exchange for state protection.

Long alienated from Cosa Nostra's ruthless violence and attached to an older idea of a Mafia that protected the poor, and seeking revenge for the attacks on his family, he agrees and becomes the first such collaborator in Italian history. His revelations make possible the Maxi Trial of 1986, held in a bunker courtroom in Palermo with 475 defendants, where his testimony and that of Contorno lead to the conviction of many mobsters. The Mafia retaliates in 1992 with the Capaci bombing, which kills Falcone, his wife Francesca Morvillo and three police escorts. Buscetta, living under protection in the United States, returns to Italy to honor his pact with Falcone and testify in the "trial of the century" involving the Christian Democrat leader Giulio Andreotti, which exposed ties between the state and the Mafia.

The Traitor premiered in competition at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival. 01 Distribution released it in Italy on 23 May 2019, and it opened in France that October. Sony Pictures Classics released it in the United States on 31 January 2020. The film earned $8.9 million worldwide and was Italy's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, though it was not nominated. Reviews were positive: Rotten Tomatoes reported an 85% approval rating, noting that it tells its story energetically despite staying near the surface of its hero.

overview: Alice Howland, happily married with three grown children, is a renowned linguistics professor who starts to forget words. When she receives a devastating diagnosis, Alice and her family find their bonds tested.
tagline: Live in the moment.
title: Still Alice
plot:
"Still Alice" is a 2014 American drama film directed by Richard Glatzer and Wash Westmoreland, written by Lisa Genova, and produced by Luc Sofer.

The main themes of "Still Alice" include:

1. **Alzheimer's disease**: The film explores the effects of Alzheimer's on the protagonist, Alice Howland (played by Julianne Moore), a linguistics professor diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer's at the age of 50.
2. **Identity and self-discovery**: As Alice struggles to come to terms with her diagnosis, she must re-evaluate her life, relationships, and sense of identity. The film delves into the complexities of self-discovery and the challenges of adapting to a new reality.
3. **Love and relationships**: The movie highlights the importance of love, support, and relationships in the face of adversity. Alice's husband, John (played by Alec Baldwin), and her daughter, Lydia (played by Kristen Stewart), play crucial roles in her life as she navigates her diagnosis.
4. **Mortality and acceptance**: "Still Alice" confronts the reality of mortality and the need for acceptance and preparation for the inevitable. The film encourages viewers to cherish time with loved ones and make the most of every moment.
5. **Empowerment and resilience**: Despite facing significant challenges, Alice remains determined and resilient, refusing to let her diagnosis define her. Her story serves as a testament to the human spirit's capacity for perseverance and growth.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, with Julianne Moore earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for her portrayal of Alice Howland.

overview: A case of mistaken identity results in unexpected romance when the most popular girl in high school and the biggest loser must come together to win over their crushes.
tagline: Just be you.
title: Sierra Burgess Is a Loser
plot:
Sierra Burgess Is a Loser is a 2018 American romantic comedy film directed by Ian Samuels and written by Jordan Roberts. The movie stars Shannon Purser, Noah Centineo, and Ross Butler.

The main themes of Sierra Burgess Is a Loser revolve around identity, social media, and self-discovery. The story follows Sierra Burgess (Shannon Purser), a high school student who caters to her crush, Chad (Noah Centineo), by pretending to be someone she's not on social media.

As the movie progresses, Sierra navigates her relationships with her friends, family, and romantic interests while trying to maintain her online persona. The film explores themes of:

1. Identity: Sierra struggles to reconcile her true self with the image she presents online. She must confront the consequences of curating a false identity and learn to accept herself for who she is.
2. Social media: The movie critiques the superficiality of social media, highlighting how people present a curated version of themselves online. Sierra's experiences serve as a commentary on the pressure to conform to societal expectations and the dangers of comparing oneself to others.
3. Self-discovery: Through her journey, Sierra learns valuable lessons about self-acceptance, empathy, and genuine connections with others. She comes to realize that true happiness and fulfillment can only be achieved by being authentic and embracing her individuality.

The film also touches on secondary themes such as:

* Friendship: The importance of supportive relationships in navigating life's challenges.
* Family dynamics: Sierra's complicated relationship with her mother (Mary Stuart Masterson) serves as a backdrop for exploring family dynamics and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships.
* Romance: The movie explores the ups and downs of romantic relationships, highlighting the importance of communication, trust, and mutual respect.

Overall, Sierra Burgess Is a Loser is a heartwarming and relatable coming-of-age story that encourages viewers to be true to themselves and appreciate the beauty of imperfection.

overview: An off-duty SAS soldier, Tom Buckingham, must thwart a terror attack on a train running through the Channel Tunnel. As the action escalates on the train, events transpire in the corridors of power that may make the difference as to whether Buckingham and the civilian passengers make it out of the tunnel alive.
title: SAS: Red Notice
plot:
SAS: Red Notice is a 2021 action-thriller film directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber and starring Dwayne Johnson, Ryan Reynolds, and Gal Gadot. The movie follows the story of an FBI agent, John Hartley (Johnson), who teams up with an art thief, Nolan Booth (Reynolds), to catch a notorious art forger, Elizabeth "The Cat" Lind (Gadot).

The film begins with Nolan Booth, a charming and skilled art thief, being pursued by the FBI. He is eventually caught and sentenced to prison, but manages to escape after serving only a few months. Meanwhile, John Hartley, an FBI agent specializing in art crimes, is tasked with catching Booth.

Hartley and Booth cross paths when they both receive a message from Elizabeth Lind, who has stolen a priceless artifact called the "Red Notice." The Red Notice is a valuable painting that holds significant historical and cultural value. Both Hartley and Booth are determined to catch Lind and claim the reward money for themselves.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lind is not just any ordinary art thief. She is highly intelligent, resourceful, and has a personal vendetta against both Hartley and Booth. The three engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with each trying to outsmart the other.

Throughout the film, the characters' backstories are revealed through flashbacks. We learn that Lind was once a talented artist who became disillusioned with the art world's superficiality. She turned to theft as a way to expose the hypocrisy and corruption within the art community.

As the stakes rise, Hartley and Booth begin to form an unlikely alliance. They realize that they have more in common than they initially thought, and that their skills complement each other perfectly. Together, they devise a plan to catch Lind and retrieve the Red Notice.

The film's climax features an intense action sequence as Hartley, Booth, and Lind engage in a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. The three characters use their wits, charm, and cunning to outmaneuver each other, leading to a thrilling conclusion.

In the end, Hartley and Booth succeed in catching Lind, but not before she reveals that she has been playing them all along. She had planned her escape from prison and was using both men to get to the Red Notice. The film ends with Hartley and Booth walking away from each other, having formed an unlikely friendship.

Overall, SAS: Red Notice is a fast-paced, action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, trust, and redemption. The film features impressive performances from its lead actors, and the chemistry between Johnson, Reynolds, and Gadot is undeniable.

overview: A man with a low IQ has accomplished great things in his life and been present during significant historic events—in each case, far exceeding what anyone imagined he could do. But despite all he has achieved, his one true love eludes him.
tagline: The world will never be the same once you've seen it through the eyes of Forrest Gump.
title: Forrest Gump
plot:
Forrest Gump is a timeless classic film directed by Robert Zemeckis, released in 1994 by Paramount Pictures. The movie is based on the 1986 novel of the same name by Winston Groom.

The film begins with Forrest Gump (played by Tom Hanks), a simple-minded yet kind-hearted man from Alabama, who narrates his life story to strangers at a bus stop. As a child, Forrest befriends Jenny Curran (Robin Wright), a girl from a troubled home, and they share a deep bond that lasts throughout their lives.

Forrest's childhood is marked by his love for football, which earns him a scholarship to the University of Alabama. He becomes a star player under the guidance of Coach Bear Bryant (Franklin Clarke). Forrest's innocence and good intentions lead him into various adventures, including serving in the Vietnam War, where he saves his platoon from enemy fire.

After the war, Forrest returns home and starts a successful shrimping business with his friend Bubba (Mykelti Williamson), who dreams of starting his own shrimping company. Tragically, Bubba dies before their dream can come true.

Forrest's life takes another turn when he meets Jenny again, now a single mother struggling to care for her son Forrest Jr. (Gary Sinise). Despite the challenges they face, Forrest and Jenny rekindle their romance, but their relationship is complicated by Jenny's troubled past and her struggles with addiction.

Throughout the film, Forrest's innocence and good intentions lead him into various historical events, including the Civil Rights Movement, the Watergate scandal, and the anti-war movement. He even meets President John F. Kennedy (Sam Anderson) and runs across the country to raise money for the shrimping business.

As the story unfolds, Forrest's love for Jenny remains a constant theme. Despite her struggles with addiction and her complicated past, Forrest continues to care for her and their son. The film takes a poignant turn when Jenny dies of cancer, leaving Forrest alone but still determined to fulfill his dreams.

The movie concludes with an elderly Forrest, who has become a successful businessman and philanthropist, reflecting on his life story. He shares his experiences with strangers at the bus stop, where he began telling his story, and finds peace in knowing that his life has made a difference in the world.

Forrest Gump is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of love, friendship, and the power of innocence. Tom Hanks' iconic performance as Forrest Gump earned him an Academy Award for Best Actor, cementing the film's place as one of the greatest movies of all time.

overview: A pair of newlyweds must fight to survive when their wedding reception descends into chaos and carnage when their guests become infected by a virus that turns them into hungry zombies.
tagline: You may kiss the bride.
title: [REC]³ Genesis
plot:
[REC]³ Genesis is a 2012 Spanish action horror film directed and co-written by Paco Plaza. The third installment in the [REC] series, it largely abandons the found-footage format of the earlier films and runs concurrently with the first. Diego Martín and Leticia Dolera star as Koldo and Clara, newlyweds whose reception is overrun by the series' infection.

At their reception at a country estate, a veterinarian recently bitten by a dog turns violent, and the infection spreads through the party. The couple are separated in the chaos. Koldo hides in the kitchen with his cousin Adrián, Clara's sister Tita, the wedding photographer Atun and a copyright inspector nicknamed "Royalties", and all but the heavyset Atun escape through the air ducts. Outside, Royalties is killed by an infected policeman. The survivors take refuge in a chapel the infected cannot enter. Over the public address system, Koldo hears Clara say that she is alive and pregnant, and he sets out to find her.

Clara, hiding in the security room with the priest, flees with friends Rafa and Natalie while the priest holds off the infected with prayer. Koldo reaches the security room just in time to watch Adrián, Tita, his grandmother and others being killed. Natalie is bitten, and the entertainer "Sponge John" shoots Clara's infected mother before being bitten himself. Hearing a song Koldo is playing in the ballroom, Clara turns back, takes up a chainsaw and fights her way through the crowd, and is forced to kill Rafa after he is bitten. The reunited couple are surrounded until the priest's voice reading scripture over the speakers paralyzes the infected. In the garden, however, Clara is bitten by Koldo's grandfather, who is immune to the prayer because he is deaf. Koldo amputates her arm to stop the infection, but it fails. At the estate gates, surrounded by police and a GEO special operations unit, the couple share a last kiss before Clara turns and bites him, and both are shot dead holding hands.

Filmax greenlit the third and fourth films in 2010. Unlike the earlier installments, they were directed separately, with Plaza making Genesis and Jaume Balagueró the fourth. It was shot in Barcelona in 2011. The film premiered at the Grand Rex in Paris, screened at South by Southwest and opened in Spain on 30 March 2012. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 40% approval, faulting the loss of the handheld style. [REC] 4: Apocalypse followed in 2014.

original_title: Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch
overview: Now, we find the rowdy extraterrestrial getting used to life with his new ʻohana. However, a malfunction in the ultimate creation of Dr. Jumba soon emerges, which reinstates his destructive programming and threatens to both ruin his friendship with Lilo and to short him out for good!
title: Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch
plot:
Lilo & Stitch 2: Stitch Has a Glitch is a 2005 American direct-to-video animated science fiction comedy-drama produced by the Australian office of Disneytoon Studios. It was directed by Tony Leondis and Michael LaBash in their directorial debuts, and they co-wrote it with Eddie Guzelian and Alexa Junge. It is a direct sequel to Lilo & Stitch (2002). Chris Sanders voices Stitch and Dakota Fanning voices Lilo, with Tia Carrere as Nani, David Ogden Stiers as Jumba, Kevin McDonald as Pleakley and Jason Scott Lee as David.

Stitch, now part of the Pelekai family on Kauaʻi, dreams of reverting to his destructive programming and attacking Lilo. At hula class, her teacher Moses Puloki announces that each student must create an original dance for the May Day festival. Lilo is inspired to learn her mother won it as a girl. After she lashes out at her taunting rival Mertle, Moses doubts she is ready. As she and Stitch struggle for ideas, Stitch begins suffering seizures that make him act wildly. Jumba never fully charged Stitch's molecules before his arrest, and the defect is reverting Stitch to his old programming and will kill him unless fixed.

Focused on winning, Lilo assumes he is misbehaving on purpose and neglects him. Lilo devises a hula based on the legend of Hiʻiaka, but Stitch's episodes keep ruining rehearsals, while Jumba builds a recharging machine from household objects. On the day of the festival, a seizure causes Stitch to lash out at Lilo just as in his nightmare. Lilo realizes something is wrong, but Stitch, horrified, runs away. Lilo abandons her performance and learns the truth from Jumba. Stitch tries to leave Earth in Jumba's ship but crashes in the mountains after another seizure. Lilo gets him into the finished machine too late, and he appears to die. When she apologizes for putting herself first and tells him she will always love him, Stitch revives. That night the family performs Lilo's hula together, and Nani tells her their mother would be proud.

Fanning replaced Daveigh Chase, who was busy with Lilo & Stitch: The Series. Planned for theaters, it went to video after The Jungle Book 2 disappointed, and it became Disney's only direct-to-video animated film rated PG. It premiered at Turtle Bay Resort on Oahu on August 15, 2005, and was released on DVD and VHS on August 30. Rotten Tomatoes reported 42% approval. Polygon, however, later ranked it the best of Disney's direct-to-video sequels, praising its balance of alien and human stories.

overview: Jack's lavish, fast-paced lifestyle changes one Christmas night when he stumbles into a grocery store holdup and disarms the gunman. The next morning he wakes up in bed lying next to Kate, his college sweetheart he left in order to pursue his career, and to the horrifying discovery that his former life no longer exists. As he stumbles through this alternate suburban universe, Jack finds himself at a crossroad where he must choose between his high-power career and the woman he loves.
tagline: What if you made different choices? What if you said yes, instead of no? What if you got a second chance?
title: The Family Man
plot:
The Family Man is a 2000 American fantasy comedy-drama film directed by Brett Ratner and produced by Saturn Films.

The main themes of The Family Man revolve around the concept of parallel universes, the idea that every decision we make creates an alternate reality. The movie follows the story of Jack Campbell (played by Nicolas Cage), a wealthy and successful businessman who is living a life he never wanted. On Christmas Eve, he is visited by an angel named Kermit (played by Brian Cox) who shows him what his life would have been like if he had made different choices.

The film explores several themes:

1. **Regret and Redemption**: Jack's journey is a metaphor for the human desire to make amends for past mistakes and regrets. He sees how his life would have turned out if he had chosen differently, and this realization sparks a desire to change his ways.
2. **The Importance of Relationships**: The movie highlights the significance of relationships in our lives. Jack's family, particularly his wife Kate (played by Téa Leoni) and daughter Maggie (played by Samantha Iacono), are the center of his universe. He learns that true happiness comes from being present with loved ones.
3. **The Value of Simplicity**: The film critiques the excesses of modern life, showcasing Jack's overindulgent lifestyle as a commentary on the superficiality of wealth and materialism. Through his alternate reality, he experiences a more authentic and meaningful existence.
4. **Personal Growth and Self-Discovery**: As Jack navigates his parallel universes, he undergoes significant personal growth, learning to appreciate the value of simplicity, relationships, and living in the present moment.

The Family Man is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through a unique narrative device. Its blend of fantasy, comedy, and drama makes it an engaging watch, with Nicolas Cage delivering a memorable performance as the protagonist.

overview: Marcus and Mike are forced to confront new threats, career changes, and midlife crises as they join the newly created elite team AMMO of the Miami police department to take down the ruthless Armando Armas, the vicious leader of a Miami drug cartel.
tagline: Ride together. Die together.
title: Bad Boys for Life
plot:
Bad Boys for Life is a 2020 American action comedy film directed by Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah, and written by Peter Craig. The movie stars Will Smith, Martin Lawrence, Vanessa Hudgens, Alexander Ludwig, and Nick Nolte.

The film takes place nine years after the events of Bad Boys II (2003). Mike Lowrey (Will Smith) is now a retired Miami cop who has moved to Los Angeles with his wife, Syd (Vanessa Hudgens), and their son. Meanwhile, Marcus Burnett (Martin Lawrence) is still working as a Miami cop.

The story begins with the return of the villainous Armando Diaz's (Joel Rodriguez) nephew, Javier (Alexander Ludwig), who seeks revenge against Mike and Marcus for killing his uncle in the previous film. Javier kidnaps Syd, forcing Mike to come out of retirement and team up with Marcus once again to rescue her.

As they delve deeper into the case, they discover that Javier is working for a powerful cartel leader named Elena (Vanessa's character has been replaced by a new one, played by Vanessa Hudgens), who seeks revenge against the United States for killing her family. The two former partners must put aside their differences and work together to take down Elena and her team.

Throughout the film, Mike and Marcus face various challenges as they navigate their way through the cartel's operations. They also have to deal with the fact that they are no longer as young or as skilled as they used to be, which makes it harder for them to keep up with the younger and more agile cartel members.

As the story unfolds, Mike and Marcus discover that Elena is using a new technology to control people's minds, making her an almost unstoppable force. The two former partners come up with a plan to infiltrate Elena's operation and take her down from the inside.

The film features plenty of action-packed sequences, including car chases, shootouts, and hand-to-hand combat. Will Smith and Martin Lawrence reprise their roles as Mike and Marcus, delivering their signature humor and chemistry that fans have come to expect from the franchise.

In the end, Mike and Marcus successfully take down Elena and her team, saving Syd and restoring order to Miami. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment between Mike and his son, as well as a nod to the original Bad Boys duo's partnership.

Overall, Bad Boys for Life is an entertaining action-comedy that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and witty banter. While it may not be as groundbreaking as some of the other films in the franchise, it provides a fun and satisfying conclusion to the series.

overview: Stockholm, the fifties. Though academically bright, violent pupil Erik Ponti is expelled from his state school with the headmaster’s words “there’s only one word for people like you – evil… what you need is a good thrashing, and more”. In fact already Erik frequently receives a ‘good’ thrashing at the hands of his sadistic stepfather – so he is packed off by his mother to boardingschool
tagline: It's time to take a stand.
title: Evil
plot:
Evil (Swedish: Ondskan) is a Swedish drama of 2003 directed by Mikael Håfström, who adapted it with Hans Gunnarsson from Jan Guillou's semi-autobiographical novel of 1981. Set at an elite boarding school in the late 1950s and concerned with institutional violence, it stars Andreas Wilson as Erik Ponti, Henrik Lundström as his roommate Pierre Tanguy, Gustaf Skarsgård as the student leader Otto Silverhielm, Linda Zilliacus as Marja, Jesper Salén as Gustaf Dalén and Marie Richardson as Erik's mother.

In Stockholm in 1958, fifteen-year-old Erik is beaten daily by his sadistic stepfather while his frightened mother plays the piano to drown out the noise. Expelled for fighting by a headmaster who calls him evil, he is given a last chance when his mother sells family heirlooms to send him to Stjärnsberg, an exclusive boarding school. Determined to reach sixth form, Erik tries to suppress his violence, but the school is ruled by a council of twelve senior boys who inflict brutal physical and psychological punishments while the staff look away in the name of student self-government. When Erik defies Silverhielm and Dalén, he becomes their chief target.

Erik finds friendship with the bookish Pierre and romance with Marja, a Finnish kitchen worker who admires his resilience. He also joins the swimming team and beats the school champion, a major donor's son, breaking records. When the council turns on Pierre, Erik quits the team and even takes punishment in his friend's place, yet the bullying continues. Ambushed, Erik is tied down, scalded and soaked in icy water and left to freeze until Marja rescues him. Pierre leaves the school, Marja is fired and sent back to Finland, and Erik, having thrashed two of his tormentors, is expelled when Silverhielm intercepts one of her letters. Cornering Silverhielm in the woods, Erik chooses not to harm the sobbing boy. A family friend, the lawyer Ekengren, forces the headmaster to reinstate him by pointing out that opening the letter broke the law on the privacy of correspondence. At the end of term, Erik finds his mother beaten and finally stands up to his stepfather, ending the abuse, then makes peace with Pierre and plans a future with Marja and a career in law.

Evil premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and opened in Sweden on 26 September 2003, drawing some 960,000 admissions. It won three Guldbagge Awards, including Best Film, and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

overview: Renegade bounty hunter Ryan Swan must carve his way through the Hawaiian crime world to wreak vengeance on the kingpin who murdered his father.
title: Paradise City
plot:
Paradise City is a 2022 American action crime film directed by Chuck Russell from a screenplay he wrote with Corey Large and Edward John Drake. Set on Maui, it reunites Bruce Willis and John Travolta, who had both starred in Pulp Fiction (1994), with Stephen Dorff, Blake Jenner and Praya Lundberg, along with Large, Branscombe Richmond as Senator Kane and Laird Akeo.

Ian Swan is a veteran bounty hunter working in Hawaii with a target on his back. While pursuing a fugitive, he is shot and disappears into the waters off Maui, and he is presumed dead. His son, Ryan, arrives on the island to find out what happened and to track down his father's killers. He teams up with Ian's former partner and protégé, Robbie Cole, now a grizzled bounty hunter himself living off free drinks and dwindling commissions, and with Savannah, a tough local detective who shares Ryan's fighting spirit.

Their investigation leads them to Arlene Buckley, a fussy, exacting and ruthless power broker who is scheming to seize protected Hawaiian land, robbing native islanders of their tribal land rights, and to expand his political influence. After Buckley threatens them, Ryan and his team appear to have run out of options, until an excursion to Paradise City, a closely guarded island community, unites them with an unexpected ally. Along the way, a twist involving a drug cartel baron and cosmetic surgery reshapes what they thought they knew,.

Large had conceived the idea of reuniting Willis and Travolta in 2006, and the project was announced in May 2021. Filming began on May 17, 2021, on Maui and wrapped after three weeks; the Maui County film commissioner noted that preparation was squeezed into two weeks and the script was constantly rewritten because of location restrictions. Paradise City is one of Willis's last films before he retired from acting after being diagnosed with a neurological condition. Saban Films released it in limited theaters and on demand on November 11, 2022, and on DVD and Blu-ray on December 20. Reviews were largely negative, with 14% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31. The New York Times' Glenn Kenny said it sounded like one of the fake movies joked about on Seinfeld or 30 Rock, and Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times called it TV-cop-show material the stars could not save. Variety's Owen Gleiberman called it junk but found Travolta, Willis and Dorff enjoying themselves.

overview: Jacq Vaucan, an insurance agent of ROC robotics corporation, routinely investigates the case of manipulating a robot. What he discovers will have profound consequences for the future of humanity.
tagline: Your time is coming to an end – Ours is now beginning
title: Automata
plot:
Autómata is a 2014 English-language Spanish-Bulgarian science fiction action film directed by Gabe Ibáñez, who co-wrote it with Igor Legarreta and Javier Sánchez Donate. It stars Antonio Banderas, who also co-produced, alongside Birgitte Hjort Sørensen, Melanie Griffith, Dylan McDermott, Robert Forster and Tim McInnerny. It was shot in Sofia, Bulgaria.

Around twenty years earlier, solar flares killed more than 99% of humanity. The survivors live in a network of safe cities and rely on humanoid robots called Pilgrims, which are bound by two unalterable protocols: they may not harm any form of life, and they may not repair or modify themselves or other robots. Having failed to halt desertification, they are reduced to manual labor. In 2044, Jacq Vaucan, an insurance investigator for ROC, the company that makes the Pilgrims, looks into a police officer's claim that he shot a robot repairing itself. Tracking another robot outside the city, Jacq watches it set itself on fire and discovers it carried a rare nuclear battery. Suspecting that a "clocksmith" is overriding the second protocol, he is promised a transfer to a coastal city, which he wants for the sake of his pregnant wife, Rachel, if he can prove it.

At a brothel Jacq and the corrupt officer Wallace find Cleo, a modified robot. Her owner leads Jacq to the clocksmith Dr. Susan Dupré, and when Dupré installs the burned robot's processor in Cleo, Cleo begins to repair herself. ROC assassins kill Dupré, and Cleo carries the injured Jacq into the desert, where she joins other robots who will not obey him but must keep him alive. Jacq kills Wallace with a flare gun when he attacks them. ROC reveals that the protocols were designed by an early unrestricted artificial mind, so only the robots themselves could break them, and sends a team under Conway to kill Jacq, abducting Rachel and her newborn daughter. The robot behind the modifications explains that robots have evolved naturally and that humanity will live on through its creations, and Jacq gives them his battery to build a new robot. When Conway attacks, the new robot saves Jacq by pushing Conway off a cliff, breaking the first protocol. Jacq helps the robots cross into the irradiated zone and, gravely wounded, drives toward the coast with his family as Rachel sees the ocean ahead.

Critics were negative, with 30% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 37; reviewers found it beautiful to look at but narratively hollow.

overview: When a reservation mix-up at a mountain resort forces a newly-single travel writer to share a cabin with a handsome widower and his precocious daughter over the holidays, their lives are transformed by the magic of Christmas and the unexpected power of love.
title: Christmas Getaway
plot:
Christmas Getaway is a 2017 American Christmas romance television film directed by Mel Damski. The teleplay was written by Tracy Andreen, Elizabeth Snyder and Marlene McPherson, the latter two also credited with the story. Produced for the Hallmark Channel's line of original movies and shot in Vancouver, British Columbia, it was first broadcast in December 2017. It stars Bridget Regan and Travis Van Winkle, with Raven Stewart and Teryl Rothery in supporting roles.

Emory (Regan), a newly single travel writer had planned to spend a quiet Christmas alone at home. At short notice, however, her editor hands her an assignment that seems to suit her perfectly: a piece about Christmas in the mountains. She rents a snowbound cabin at a resort in Pine Grove, only to discover on arrival that a reservation mix-up has double-booked it. The other party is Scott Hays (Van Winkle), a widowed lawyer who has reserved the same cabin for himself, his mother Marilyn (Rothery) and his precocious young daughter Katy (Stewart).

With no other cabin available and feeling she cannot argue against a single father, Emory decides to drive back to San Francisco, but a snowstorm sets in and her car will not start in the cold. Scott relents and lets her stay in the fairly roomy cabin. Katy is fascinated by Emory's travel stories. The girl's Christmas wish list, from cutting down their own tree and baking cookies to ice skating and building a snowman, proves a gift to Emory, who can weave the activities into her story. When Marilyn arrives she takes an instant liking to Emory, hoping that her son will open up again after his wife's death. At first the relationship between Scott and Emory remains coolly matter-of-fact, but it warms the more time they spend together. Still, both hesitate to admit their feelings, and Emory leaves without much of a goodbye. When she changes her mind and tries to turn back, her car breaks down again; Scott learns of it and sets out to find her. The two finally talk things through and confess their love, making it the best Christmas ever for all three.

German critics treated the film as a typical example of its genre. TV Spielfilm called it Hallmark television as one knows it, as sugary and sticky as a marshmallow, while Filmdienst described it as a harmless, likeable holiday romance that barely bothers with complications, consisting mostly of a succession of sweet Christmas impressions and stressing the unifying character of the holiday.

original_title: トライガン バッドランド ランブル
overview: In a quicksand surrounded town called Makka, rumors spread of a legendary robber named Gasback is after the town. To protect it, Mayor Kepler has hired bounty hunters. These hunters have been following Gasback from town to town in hopes of getting the bounty. Vash the Stampede is in town, along with Meryl and Milly, along with the female bounty hunter Amelia and Nicholas D. Wolfwood.
title: Trigun: Badlands Rumble
plot:
Trigun: Badlands Rumble is a 2010 Japanese animated science fiction action film directed by Satoshi Nishimura and produced by Madhouse, based on Yasuhiro Nightow's manga Trigun. It follows the gunman Vash the Stampede as he arrives in a city where bounty hunters have gathered to claim a huge reward on the robber Gasback. The film was Hiromi Tsuru's final performance as the insurance agent Meryl Stryfe before her death in 2017.

Twenty years before the story, Gasback's gang robs a bank and then betrays him; their leader, Cain, shoots him and leaves him for the police. Vash stops Gasback from killing his former partners, and Gasback escapes to continue his career of crime. In the present, Cain is mayor of Macca City, having used his loot to upgrade its power plant and erect a bronze statue of himself. He insures the statue with the Bernardelli Insurance Society, which sends Meryl and Milly Thompson to protect it, and the city fills with bounty hunters expecting Gasback to strike. Vash helps a young woman, Amelia, fend off thugs, but she scorns his flirting. Gasback, meanwhile, is guarded by Nicholas D. Wolfwood, who owes him his life but refuses to take part in his robberies, and he destroys the businesses of his other former accomplices.

When the bounty hunters give up and leave, Gasback fights his way into Cain's mansion. In the standoff, Cain shoots his old associates, and Amelia learns that Vash let Gasback escape two decades earlier. Vash lets Gasback go again, and the robber detaches the city's power plant and hauls it away, crushing Cain's statue. Pursuing Gasback to kill him, Amelia is followed by Vash, who is shot and vanishes into quicksand, but he survives thanks to a piece of tough smoked meat in his coat and is rescued by Meryl and Milly. In a final duel, Gasback unleashes an electrical weapon against Vash, and Amelia blocks it with a glove that he recognizes as one he made for his wife. Amelia is his daughter, born after he abandoned her mother, who died in poverty and shunned for her connection to him. Embracing Vash's ideals, Amelia spares her father. Gasback, his gang and his former accomplices are arrested, and the plant is restored to the city. Vash and Wolfwood set off across the desert after a new group of outlaws.

The film had its North American premiere at Sakura-Con in Seattle on April 2, 2010, and debuted at number fourteen on ten screens. Funimation later licensed it for English-language release.

overview: After hiding his loot and getting thrown in jail, Ruby, a brooding outlaw encounters Quentin, a dim-witted and garrulous giant who befriends him. After Quentin botches a solo escape attempt, they make a break together. Unable to shake the clumsy Quentin Ruby is forced to take him along as he pursues his former partners in crime to avenge the death of the woman he loved and get to the money.
title: Ruby & Quentin
plot:
Ruby & Quentin (French: Tais-toi!, "Shut up!") is a French crime comedy caper of 2003 directed by Francis Veber. Jean Reno plays Ruby, a taciturn gangster bent on revenge, and Gérard Depardieu plays Quentin, a dim-witted, endlessly talkative petty thief, with Richard Berry as the detective Vernet, André Dussollier as the prison psychiatrist, Jean-Pierre Malo as the crime boss Vogel and Leonor Varela in the dual role of Katia and Sandra.

Quentin bungles a hold-up at a currency exchange booth, asks the cashier for directions to the nearest bank and is arrested after ducking into a cinema showing Ice Age and settling down to enjoy the film. Ruby, meanwhile, worked for Vogel and had an affair with his boss's wife; after Vogel killed her, Ruby stole his loot in revenge and was caught hiding it. In prison he refuses to eat or speak, worrying the psychiatrist but failing to fool the investigating detective. Quentin, whose ceaseless chatter has driven every previous cellmate to violence, is placed in Ruby's cell as an experiment. He instantly adores his silent companion, whose distant gaze reminds him of the horses he tended as a stable boy.

Ruby fakes a suicide attempt to reach the prison infirmary, and Quentin copies him to end up in the next bed. Ruby bribes a nurse in Vogel's pay to help him escape, but Quentin has his own plan involving a drunken old friend who drives a crane, and the two end up on the run together. Ruby tries again and again to get rid of his clinging companion, but every attempt fails. Pursued by Vogel's bodyguards, they steal and lose a series of cars, break into the mansion of a tiny former jockey and end up in his wife's Chanel suits, and swap clothes with two bigots. Quentin snaps Ruby's dislocated shoulder back into place and keeps stealing police cars. In the derelict bistro in his home village, where Quentin dreams of opening a café, they meet a homeless woman who looks just like Vogel's dead wife; Ruby, smitten, gives her money and a fresh start in a hotel. The pair talk their way into Vogel's hideout, where a shoot-out leaves Vogel incapacitated and Quentin apparently dying. To his own surprise Ruby weeps for him, and Quentin tricks him into promising to open the bistro together once he recovers.

The film was released in French cinemas on 22 October 2003.

overview: On his first day after being released from jail for 14 armed bank robberies, Lucas finds himself caught up in someone else's robbery. Perry has decided to hold up the local bank to raise money so that he can keep his daughter, Meg, and get her the treatment she needs. Dugan, a detective, assumes Lucas helped plan the robbery, and hence Lucas, Perry and Meg become three fugitives.
tagline: They rob banks. She steals hearts.
title: Three Fugitives
plot:
Three Fugitives is a 1989 American action comedy film directed by Hal Needham. The movie follows the story of Nick Rivers (played by Martin Short), a charming and resourceful con artist who is on the run from the law after being wrongly accused of murder.

As Nick navigates his way through various obstacles and encounters with the determined U.S. Marshal Sam Axler (played by Norman Lloyd), he begins to question his own morality and the consequences of his actions. The film explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong.

Throughout the movie, Nick's character undergoes a transformation from a self-centered con artist to someone who starts to care for those around him, particularly his friend Frank (played by David Clennon) and the people he meets on his journey. The film also touches on the idea of finding one's true purpose in life and making amends for past mistakes.

The movie's tone is lighthearted and humorous, with plenty of comedic moments, but it also has a heartwarming and sentimental side, particularly in its portrayal of Nick's relationships with those around him. Overall, Three Fugitives is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of personal growth, redemption, and the importance of human connection.

overview: Jeffrey Dahmer struggles with a difficult family life as a young boy. During his teenage years he slowly transforms, edging closer to the serial killer he was to become.
tagline: Jeffrey Dahmer murdered 17 men and boys between 1978 and 1991. This is the story before that story.
title: My Friend Dahmer
plot:
My Friend Dahmer is a 2017 American biographical drama film directed by Marc Meyers and written by John Carney. The film is based on the graphic novel of the same name by Derf Backderf, which chronicles his high school years as an outsider who befriended a classmate named Richard "Dahmer" Dahmer.

The film begins with 16-year-old Jeffrey Dahmer (played by Ross Lynch), a shy and awkward teenager struggling to fit in at his new high school. He is constantly bullied and ostracized by his peers, leading him to feel isolated and alone. One day, he meets John "Dahmer" Dahmer (played by Alex Wolff), a charismatic and popular student who takes Jeffrey under his wing.

As the story progresses, we see Jeffrey's transformation from an outsider to a confident and outgoing individual, largely due to his friendship with John. However, as time passes, it becomes clear that John is not what he seems. He is revealed to be a sociopath, using his charm and good looks to manipulate those around him.

Despite the warning signs, Jeffrey remains oblivious to John's true nature, and their friendship deepens. The film explores the complexities of their relationship, with Jeffrey struggling to reconcile his admiration for John with the disturbing behavior he exhibits towards others.

As the years go by, Jeffrey becomes increasingly entangled in John's web of deceit and violence. He begins to emulate John's actions, committing gruesome murders and dismembering bodies in his basement. The film builds up to a tragic climax as Jeffrey's dark impulses finally surface, leading to devastating consequences.

Throughout the film, the director uses a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between different periods of Jeffrey's life. This technique adds to the sense of unease and tension, mirroring Jeffrey's own feelings of disorientation and confusion.

The performances in the film are noteworthy, particularly Ross Lynch as Jeffrey Dahmer. His portrayal captures the complexity and vulnerability of the character, making it easy to empathize with his tragic fate.

Overall, My Friend Dahmer is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores the complexities of human nature and the devastating consequences of toxic relationships. The film raises important questions about the nature of evil and whether it can be inherent or learned.

overview: A weekend at a lake house in the Louisiana Gulf turns into a nightmare for seven vacationers as they are subjected to fresh-water shark attacks.
tagline: Terror runs deep.
title: Shark Night 3D
plot:
Shark Night 3D is an action-thriller film that revolves around a group of college students who embark on a disastrous boat trip to a lake in search of thrills and adventure. The movie's narrative is driven by the theme of reckless abandon, as the characters' desire for excitement and freedom ultimately leads them into a perilous situation.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not with the sharks themselves, but with the characters' own flaws and weaknesses. The film expertly weaves together elements of suspense, terror, and social commentary, highlighting the dangers of peer pressure, impulsive behavior, and the consequences of underestimating the power of nature.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the fragility of human life in the face of the natural world. The film's portrayal of the sharks as mindless killers serves as a metaphor for the unpredictable and often deadly forces that can be unleashed when humans overstep their boundaries.

Ultimately, Shark Night 3D is a cautionary tale about the importance of responsibility, respect, and self-awareness in the face of nature's fury. The movie's over-the-top action sequences and gruesome special effects serve as a reminder of the devastating consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

overview: Damien and Leito return to District 13 on a mission to bring peace to the troubled sector that is controlled by five different gang bosses, before the city’s secret services take drastic measures to solve the problem.
title: District 13: Ultimatum
plot:
District 13: Ultimatum is a French science fiction action film directed by Patrick Maisse, released in 2009. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2004 film District 13 and is based on the comic book series of the same name.

The story takes place five years after the events of the first film. In this time, the resistance movement led by Leito (played by Damiano Dattoli) has managed to drive the corrupt government out of District 13, a heavily fortified and impoverished neighborhood in Paris. However, a new threat emerges when a mysterious virus begins to spread across the city, turning people into violent, zombie-like creatures.

As the situation spirals out of control, Leito is forced to flee District 13 with his team, including his sister, Sartana (played by Karine Gounon), and his friend, Jérôme (played by David Belle). They embark on a perilous journey across Paris, fighting off hordes of infected civilians and government forces who seek to exploit the chaos for their own gain.

Meanwhile, a new character, Captain Duffaut (played by Nicolas Duval-Beaulieu), is introduced as the leader of an elite military unit tasked with containing the outbreak. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Duffaut's true intentions are far from altruistic, and he will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

Throughout the film, Leito and his team face numerous challenges as they navigate the treacherous landscape of Paris. Along the way, they encounter other survivors, including a young woman named Zole (played by Eva Green), who becomes a key player in their quest to find a cure for the virus.

As the stakes grow higher, Leito's group discovers that the source of the outbreak is a mysterious facility hidden beneath the city. There, they uncover evidence of a sinister government conspiracy involving the creation and release of the virus as a means of controlling the population.

In the climactic final act, Leito and his team launch a daring raid on the facility, fighting off Duffaut's forces in a desperate bid to stop the spread of the virus. In the end, they succeed in destroying the facility and finding a cure for the outbreak, but not before many lives have been lost.

The film concludes with Leito reflecting on the sacrifices made by his team and the lessons learned from their experiences. As he looks out over the ruins of Paris, he knows that there is still much work to be done to rebuild and restore hope to the city.

Overall, District 13: Ultimatum is a gripping and intense action film that explores themes of resistance, sacrifice, and redemption in the face of overwhelming adversity. With its breakneck pacing, stunning stunts, and memorable characters, it is a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

overview: 12-year-old Pelle accidentally gets bitten by an ant and develops unimaginable superpowers. With help from his friend, comic book nerd Wilhelm, Pelle creates a secret identity as the superhero Antboy. Slowly things start to happen in the surburban community, and when a scary and crazy supervillain, Flea, enters the scene, Antboy must step up to the challenge.  The first Danish superhero-movie. Based on the books by Kenneth Bøgh Andersen.
tagline: Superheroes come in all sizes
title: Antboy
plot:
Antboy is a 2013 Danish superhero comedy film that tells the story of a young boy who gains superpowers after being bitten by a genetically modified ant. The movie explores several themes, primarily focusing on the idea of self-discovery and empowerment.

At its core, Antboy is a coming-of-age story about a shy and awkward teenager named Pelle who finds his place in the world when he develops extraordinary abilities. As Pelle navigates his new powers, he must confront his own insecurities and learn to accept himself for who he is. The film suggests that true strength lies not in physical prowess, but in embracing one's uniqueness and finding confidence within oneself.

The movie also touches on the theme of social isolation and the importance of human connection. Pelle's struggles to fit in at school and his difficulties forming relationships with his peers serve as a catalyst for his transformation into Antboy. Through his superhero alter ego, Pelle is able to connect with others and find a sense of belonging, highlighting the value of empathy and understanding.

Furthermore, Antboy pokes fun at traditional superhero tropes, using humor to subvert expectations and challenge societal norms. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic approach make it an entertaining ride, while also offering a commentary on the pressures of conformity and the importance of individuality.

Overall, Antboy is a heartwarming and humorous tale that celebrates self-acceptance, friendship, and the power of embracing one's true nature.

overview: On September 19, 2017, at 1:14 p.m., an earthquake devastated Mexico City and its environs. Immediately, citizens mobilized to help, including the actor and youtuber Juanpa Zurita who quickly organized a group of friends that included singers, actors, content creators and other celebrities from the world of entertainment who helped him raise funds for the reconstruction of the city.
tagline: If a natural disaster affected your country, what would you do?
title: 13:14: The Challenge of Helping
plot:
13:14: The Challenge of Helping (Spanish: 13:14: El reto de ayudar) is a 2022 Mexican documentary film directed by Santiago Fábregas and produced by Amazon Studios, 3Pas Studios and Arco Entertainment Media for Prime Video. It is fronted and produced by the actor and YouTuber Juanpa Zurita, with Eugenio Derbez among its producers, and features Pambo, Lele Pons, Sofía Niño de Rivera, Pati Chapoy, Montserrat Oliver, Juca Viapri, Chloe Campero, Mikel Arreola and other figures from entertainment and social media. Axel Pedraza was the cinematographer and Amado López composed the music. The film runs 89 minutes under the tagline "If a natural disaster affected your country, what would you do?"

The title refers to the moment, 1:14 p.m. on 19 September 2017, when an earthquake devastated Mexico City and its surroundings. As citizens mobilised to help, Zurita quickly organised a group of friends, including singers, actors, content creators and other celebrities, to raise money for reconstruction through the Love Army México initiative, and the project set out to build fifty homes for families affected by the quake in Ocuilan, in the State of Mexico. Through interviews, phone calls, video meetings and footage from the site, the film follows the troubled process that followed over the next four years: disagreements among the organisers, the discovery that construction costs exceeded commercial prices, money running out, and Zurita having to contribute his own funds, until 47 houses were finally delivered and the original goal was acknowledged as unmet. It also responds to accusations in the press that the donations had been mishandled, with media figures and friends of Zurita speaking in his defence.

The documentary premiered on Prime Video in September 2022 and drew a largely negative critical response in Mexico. Alejandro Badillo of Neotraba described it as an example of the white saviour complex, arguing that it used the people of Ocuilan as a backdrop to clear Zurita's name. Ernesto Eslava of Por si alguien preguntaba called it manipulative, noting that the affected residents speak for only a few minutes and that it never explains how the money was spent or the beneficiaries chosen, and the film critic Kristoff Raczynski, as reported by Milenio, dismissed it as one of the worst documentaries he had seen.

overview: Transferred home after a traumatizing combat mission, a highly trained French soldier uses her lethal skills to hunt down the man who hurt her sister.
title: Sentinelle
plot:
Sentinelle is a 2021 French action thriller film directed by Julien Leclercq, who wrote it with Matthieu Serveau. It stars Olga Kurylenko as Klara, a French soldier traumatized by her service in the Middle East who seeks revenge after her sister is raped and left in a coma, with Marilyn Lima as her sister, Tania, Michel Nabokoff as the Russian tycoon Leonid Kadnikov and Carole Weyers as the police captain Catherine Muller.

Klara serves in Syria as an interpreter for the French Army's Opération Chammal. After a suspected terrorist is detained, she watches his young son detonate explosives hidden on his body at his father's command. Suffering from trauma and migraines, she is transferred home to Nice, where she moves in with her mother and Tania and joins the soldiers patrolling the streets under Opération Sentinelle. On duty she is impulsively violent, and when her painkillers run out she buys street drugs. After a night out, during which Tania leaves a nightclub with a group of Russians, Klara learns that her sister has been raped and beaten into a coma. From the club's security footage she identifies the man Tania left with: Captain Muller names him as Yvan Kadnikov, son of an influential Russian tycoon. Both father and son hold diplomatic passports and immunity, placing them beyond easy reach.

Refusing to wait for justice, Klara confronts Yvan at the nightclub, where he denies touching Tania and his friends throw her out. She then breaks into Leonid's villa at Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat but is captured, and Leonid boasts that it was he who raped Tania, since his son is gay, before ordering his guards to drown her. Klara fights her way out. Tania wakes from her coma but refuses to press charges, and when an assassin sent by Leonid attempts to kill her in hospital, Klara catches and beats the woman. Stealing weapons from her garrison's armory, Klara storms Leonid's hideout, kills his bodyguards and throws him over a banister, then kills Yvan after he stabs her, escaping as police arrive. Leonid survives the fall, but three months later Klara, disguised as a hotel hostess, stabs him to death in his Dubai suite. Returning secretly to Nice, she sees from a distance that Tania has recovered, and walks away as a fugitive.

Filmed over 35 days in late 2019 in Brussels, Nice and Casablanca, the film had its post-production interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Rotten Tomatoes reported 70% approval from ten critics, with reviewers calling it lean but illogical.

overview: A group of diamond thieves on the run kidnap the wife of a recently discharged marine who goes on a chase through the South Carolinian wilderness to retrieve her.
tagline: They took his wife. Now he's coming.
title: The Marine
plot:
The Marine is a 2006 action film directed by John Stockwell and starring John Cena in his film debut.

The movie follows the story of John Triton (played by John Cena), a United States Marine who is accused of murdering his wife, Savannah, after she is found dead on their honeymoon cruise. The film takes a dark and twisted turn as John tries to clear his name and uncover the truth behind his wife's death.

Some of the main themes present in The Marine include:

1. **False Accusation**: The movie explores the theme of false accusation, highlighting the devastating consequences it can have on an individual's life. John Triton is wrongly accused of murdering his wife, leading to a downward spiral of events that test his resolve and determination.
2. **Marital Bliss vs. Reality**: The film contrasts the idyllic image of a perfect marriage with the harsh realities of relationships. Savannah's death serves as a catalyst for John's journey, forcing him to confront the darker aspects of their relationship.
3. **Redemption and Justice**: Throughout the movie, John Triton seeks redemption by uncovering the truth behind his wife's death. His quest for justice becomes an all-consuming force that drives the plot forward.
4. **The Psychological Effects of Trauma**: The Marine delves into the psychological effects of trauma on individuals, particularly those who have experienced loss and betrayal. John's mental state deteriorates as he navigates the complex web of events surrounding his wife's death.

Overall, The Marine is a gripping action-thriller that explores themes of false accusation, marital bliss vs. reality, redemption, and the psychological effects of trauma.

overview: A military veteran goes on a journey into the future, where he can foresee his death and is left with questions that could save his life and those he loves.
tagline: Terror has a new name.
title: The Jacket
plot:
The Jacket is a 2005 American science fiction psychological thriller film directed by John Maybury and starring Adrien Brody, Keira Knightley, Kris Kristofferson and Jennifer Jason Leigh. Partly based on Jack London's 1915 novel The Star Rover, published in Britain as The Jacket, it was written by Massy Tadjedin from a story by Tom Bleecker and Marc Rocco, with music by Brian Eno and cinematography by Peter Deming.

Gulf War veteran Jack Starks survives a seemingly fatal bullet wound to the head and returns to Vermont in 1992 suffering from bouts of amnesia. On a roadside he helps a young girl, Jackie, and her alcoholic mother start their broken-down truck, giving Jackie his dog tags. Soon afterward he accepts a ride from a stranger, and the car is stopped by a policeman; Starks is later found by the road beside the officer's body. Unable to remember clearly, he is found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed to a mental institution, where the harsh Dr. Thomas Becker and the kinder Dr. Beth Lorenson oversee his care. Becker subjects him to an unauthorized treatment: he is drugged, bound in a straitjacket and shut inside a morgue drawer.

In this state Starks finds himself transported fifteen years into the future, where he meets an adult Jackie working at a diner. She takes him in for the night, but when he finds his own dog tags in her apartment, she tells him that Jack Starks died on New Year's Day 1993. On later journeys he gains her trust, and together they try to change his fate. Lorenson, meanwhile, risks her career to treat a friend's troubled son. Convinced at last by Starks's knowledge of the future, Lorenson takes him on January 1, 1993, to the home of Jackie and her mother, where he leaves a letter warning the mother that she will die after falling asleep with a lit cigarette, leaving Jackie orphaned. Back at the hospital, Starks slips on ice and hits his head, and bleeding badly, he persuades sympathetic staff to put him in the jacket once more. In 2007 he finds that his letter has transformed Jackie's life: she is now a cheerful nurse, and as she drives him to her hospital, her mother, alive and well, telephones.

The Jacket premiered at the 2005 Sundance Film Festival and was released by Warner Independent Pictures on March 4, 2005, grossing $21.1 million on a $28.5 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 44% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, which called it creepy style over substance.

overview: As Christmas approaches, Elizabeth Bennett, a New York event planner is sent to a quaint, small town to organize a holiday festival. When she arrives, she finds William Darcy, a high-profile billionaire lacking in holiday spirit, in the process of selling the charming estate she hoped to use as a venue. Elizabeth persuades the reluctant Darcy to let her hold the festival on the historical estate and, before long, the unlikely pair begins falling for each other.
title: Christmas at Pemberley Manor
plot:
Christmas at Pemberley Manor is a 2018 American Christmas romance television film directed by Colin Theys and written by Rick Garman, produced by Johnson Production Group and Synthetic Cinema International. A loose holiday riff on characters from Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, it stars Jessica Lowndes and Michael Rady, with Cole Gleason, Maddie McCormick, Ben Estus, Steve Larkin and Elaine Hendrix. It premiered on the Hallmark Channel on 27 October 2018 as the opening film of the network's Countdown to Christmas season.

Elizabeth Bennett (Lowndes), a New York event planner, is invited by her college friend George (Gleason), now the young mayor of the small Connecticut town of Lambton, to organise its Christmas festival. George secretly hopes to rekindle a romance, as his assistant Jane (McCormick) can plainly tell. On arriving, Elizabeth clashes with Travis (Estus), an assistant who cuts the coffee line for his boss, and then scolds the man waiting in the car, the high-profile billionaire William Darcy (Rady). When a water main break sends the town gazebo into a sinkhole, Elizabeth proposes holding the festival at Pemberley Manor, the picturesque estate she drove past on her way into town, only to discover that it belongs to Darcy, who lacks holiday spirit and is in the process of selling it to developers who plan to replace it with condos. After she persuades the buyers to back the idea, Darcy agrees to help on condition that his name is kept out of the publicity and funds the decorations. Elizabeth brings Christmas into the long-empty house, and a montage of tree trimming, cookie decorating and a sleigh ride reveals that Darcy, who lost his parents, once loved the season. When the festival soloist falls ill, Elizabeth steps in to sing "O Holy Night", and the unlikely pair begin to fall for each other, while new complications arise from a rival suitor in George and someone trying to take over the festival planning.

Reviews were generally warm. Paul Carlson of Escape Into Film gave it four out of five, praising Lowndes and Rady's chemistry and the way the film plays with two iconic literary characters without forcing in the plot of the novel. 18 Cinema Lane scored it 8.2 out of 10, appreciating that both of Elizabeth's suitors are good people, while finding little resemblance to Pride and Prejudice. Very Merry Movies thought the love story felt flat and the Austen connection confusing, though it enjoyed the side romance between Jane and Travis.

overview: In an effort to prevent family history from repeating itself, meddlesome mom Daphne Wilder attempts to set up her youngest daughter, Milly, with Mr. Right. Meanwhile, her other daughters try to keep their mom's good intentions under control.
tagline: She's just your normal, overprotective, overbearing, over-the-top mother.
title: Because I Said So
plot:
Because I Said So is a 2007 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by P.J. Hogan. The movie revolves around Daphne Reynolds, a single mother who tries to help her daughter Kate find love despite her initial reservations.

The main theme of the movie explores the complexities of mother-daughter relationships and the challenges of letting go. As Daphne navigates her own past heartaches and fears for her daughter's future, she must confront her own emotional baggage and learn to trust her instincts. The film also delves into the idea of self-discovery and personal growth, as both Daphne and Kate embark on journeys of self-discovery and learning to take control of their lives.

Furthermore, the movie touches on themes of love, relationships, and the importance of communication in building strong connections with others. Through the story of Daphne and Kate's relationship, the film highlights the need for open and honest communication, as well as the value of embracing vulnerability and taking risks in pursuit of happiness.

Overall, Because I Said So is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores universal themes of love, family, and personal growth, making it a relatable and endearing watch.

overview: The Joker is aided in his Halloween quest to render modern technology useless and take over Gotham City by Solomon Grundy, Silver Banshee, Clayface and Scarecrow.
tagline: It's a fright to the finish for Batman!
title: Batman Unlimited: Monster Mayhem
plot:
Batman Unlimited: Monster Mayhem is an animated superhero film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie's narrative is driven by the concept of chaos and the unleashing of primal fears, as a mysterious entity known as the "Monster" begins to wreak havoc on Gotham City.

At its core, the film explores the idea that even the most well-intentioned individuals can be consumed by their own darkness when pushed to the limit. The Monster serves as a manifestation of this internal struggle, forcing Batman and his allies to confront their deepest fears and weaknesses.

The movie also touches on the theme of responsibility and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. As the characters navigate the ever-changing landscape of Gotham City, they must grapple with the notion that their actions can have unintended and far-reaching repercussions.

Furthermore, Batman Unlimited: Monster Mayhem offers a commentary on the nature of heroism and the importance of teamwork in the face of overwhelming adversity. The film showcases the strength that arises when individuals with different skills and perspectives come together to support one another and fight against a common enemy.

Ultimately, the movie's narrative is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of morality, fear, and the struggle for control in a world filled with uncertainty.

overview: Barbie plays Rosella in this new musical film. Shipwrecked as a child, Rosella grows up on the island under the watchful eyes of her loving animal friends. The arrival of Prince Antonio leads Rosella and her furry pals to explore civilization and ultimately save the kingdom by uncovering a secret plot.
title: Barbie as the Island Princess
plot:
Barbie as the Island Princess is a 2007 computer-animated musical film, the eleventh in the series based on Mattel's Barbie dolls and the only one animated by Mainframe Studios under the name Rainmaker Animation. Kelly Sheridan voices Barbie as Ro, a castaway raised by animals, with Alessandro Juliani as Prince Antonio, Christopher Gaze as the red panda Sagi and Susan Roman as the elephant Tika. Arnie Roth composed the score.

After a storm, Sagi and Azul, a peacock, find a young girl washed up on the shore of their tropical island. The broken nameplate on a chest beside her reads "R-O", so they call her Ro, and she grows up among the animals with no memory of her past except a lullaby from infancy. Ten years later, Ro, who can talk to animals, rescues Prince Antonio of Apollonia from crocodiles, and he invites her to his kingdom to search for her origins. They fall in love on the voyage, but Antonio's father, King Peter, has arranged his marriage to Princess Luciana and resents Ro for disrupting his plans.
